children.text: Chapter 1
agnir vai devānām avamo viṣṇuḥ paramas tadantareṇa sarvā anyā devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> indeed is the lowest of the gods, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the highest; between them are all the other deities.

children.text: āgnāvaiṣṇavam puroﾱāśaṃ nirvapanti dīkṣaṇīyam ekādaśakapālam ||
children.translated_text: They set out, as the consecration offering, an Āgnāvaiṣṇava <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) on eleven potsherds.

children.text: sarvābhya evainaṃ tad devatābhyo 'nantarāyaṃ nirvapanti ||
children.translated_text: Thereby they set it out for all the deities without interruption.

children.text: agnir vai sarvā devatā viṣṇuḥ sarvā devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> indeed is all the deities; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is all the deities.

children.text: ete vai yajñasyāntye tanvau yad agniś ca viṣṇuś ca tad yad āgnāvaiṣṇavam puroﾱāśaṃ nirvapanty antata eva tad devān ṛdhnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: These two, <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, are the two terminal bodies of the sacrifice; therefore, when they set out the Āgnāvaiṣṇava <s>puroḍāśa</s>, they prosper among the gods precisely from the two ends.

children.text: tad āhur yad ekādaśakapālaḥ puroﾱāśo dvāv agnāviṣṇū kainayos tatra kﾱptiḥ kā vibhaktir iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'Since the <s>puroḍāśa</s> is on eleven potsherds, while <s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> are two, what arrangement and what division is there for these two?'

children.text: aṣṭākapāla āgneyo 'ṣṭākṣarā vai gāyatrī gāyatram agneś chandas trikapālo vaiṣṇavas trir hīdaṃ viṣṇur vyakramata sainayos tatra kﾱptiḥ sā vibhaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Agneya cake is on eight potsherds, for the Gāyatrī has eight syllables and the Gāyatra meter belongs to <s>Agni</s>; the Vaiṣṇava cake is on three potsherds, for <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode through this world three times. That is the arrangement for these two; that is the division.

children.text: ghṛte caruṃ nirvapeta yo 'pratiṣṭhito manyeta ||
children.translated_text: One who thinks himself unestablished should set out a <s>caru</s> (porridge-offering) in ghee.

children.text: asyāṃ vāva sa na pratitiṣṭhati yo na pratitiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: For one who is unestablished is, in truth, not established upon this earth.

children.text: tad yad ghṛtaṃ tat striyai payo ye taṇḍulās te puṃsas tan mithunam mithunenaivainaṃ tat prajayā paśubhiḥ prajanayati prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: What is ghee is the milk of the female, and what are rice grains are the male; that is a pair. By means of a pair he thereby causes him to generate with offspring and cattle, for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this is propagated with offspring and cattle.

children.text: ārabdhayajño vā eṣa ārabdhadevato yo darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajata āmāvāsyena vā haviṣeṣṭvā paurṇamāsena vā tasminn eva haviṣi tasmin barhiṣi dīkṣetaiṣo ekā dīkṣā ||
children.translated_text: One who sacrifices with the new- and full-moon rites has begun the sacrifice and has begun with the deities. Having sacrificed either with the new-moon oblation or with the full-moon oblation, he should be consecrated in that very oblation and on that very sacrificial grass. This is one form of <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration).

children.text: saptadaśa sāmidhenīr anubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should recite seventeen <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses.

children.text: saptadaśo vai prajāpatir dvādaśa māsāḥ pañcartavo hemantaśiśirayoḥ samāsena tāvān saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> is seventeen: there are twelve months and five seasons, with winter and the cool season counted together; so great is the year. The year is <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: prajāpatyāyatanābhir evābhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: By rites whose basis is <s>Prajāpati</s>, he prospers in these things, he who knows this.

children.text: Chapter 2
yajño vai devebhya udakrāmat tam iṣṭibhiḥ praiṣam aicchan yad iṣṭibhiḥ praiṣam aicchaṃs tad iṣṭīnām iṣṭitvaṃ tam anvavindan ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice went away from the gods. They sought an impelling summons to it by means of <s>iṣṭi</s> offerings. Because they sought an impelling summons by means of <s>iṣṭi</s> offerings, that is the <s>iṣṭi</s>-nature of the <s>iṣṭi</s> offerings. They found it again.

children.text: anuvittayajño rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: One whose sacrifice has been found again prospers, he who knows this.

children.text: āhūtayo vai nāmaitā yad āhutaya etābhir vai devān yajamāno hvayati tad āhutīnām āhutitvam ||
children.translated_text: These are called <s>āhūtayaḥ</s>, namely the oblations; by these the sacrificer calls the gods. That is the <s>āhuti</s>-nature of the oblations.

children.text: ūtayaḥ khalu vai tā nāma yābhir devā yajamānasya havam āyanti ye vai panthāno yāḥ srutayas tā vā ūtayas ta u evaitat svargayāṇā yajamānasya bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: They are, in fact, called <s>ūtayaḥ</s>, by which the gods come to the sacrificer's call. The paths and the streams are the <s>ūtayaḥ</s>; they thus become the sacrificer's roads leading to heaven.

children.text: tad āhur yad anyo juhoty atha yo 'nu cāha yajati ca kasmāt taṃ hotety ācakṣata iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'When one man pours the oblation, while the one who follows with the recitation and performs the sacrifice is another, why do they call him the <s>hotṛ</s>?'

children.text: yad vāva sa tatra yathābhājanaṃ devatā amum āvahāmum āvahety āvāhayati tad eva hotur hotṛtvam ||
children.translated_text: Because there he calls the deities according to their proper portions, saying, 'Bring this one here, bring that one here'; that very act is the <s>hotṛ</s>-function of the <s>hotṛ</s>.

children.text: hotā bhavati hotety enamācakṣate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He becomes a <s>hotā</s>; they call him '<s>hotṛ</s>,' he who knows this.

children.text: Chapter 3
punar vā etam ṛtvijo garbhaṃ kurvanti yaṃ dīkṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: The officiating priests make again into an embryo the man whom they consecrate.

children.text: adbhir abhiṣiñcanti ||
children.translated_text: They sprinkle him with waters.

children.text: reto vā āpaḥ saretasam evainaṃ tat kṛtvā dīkṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: The waters are seed; having thus made him possessed of seed, they consecrate him.

children.text: navanītenābhyañjanti ||
children.translated_text: They anoint him with fresh butter.

children.text: ājyaṃ vai devānāṃ surabhi ghṛtam manuṣyāṇām āyutam pitṝṇāṃ navanītaṃ garbhāṇāṃ tad yan navanītenābhyañjanti svenaivainaṃ tad bhāgadheyena samardhayanti ||
children.translated_text: Clarified butter is the fragrant substance of the gods, ghee that of human beings, the prepared portion that of the fathers, and fresh butter that of embryos. Therefore, when they anoint him with fresh butter, they make him prosper by his own allotted share.

children.text: āñjanty enam ||
children.translated_text: They apply collyrium to him.

children.text: tejo vā etad akṣyor yad āñjanaṃ satejasam evainaṃ tat kṛtvā dīkṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: This brightness of the eyes is collyrium; having thus made him possessed of brightness, they consecrate him.

children.text: ekaviṃśatyā darbhapiñjūlaiḥ pāvayanti ||
children.translated_text: They purify him with twenty-one bundles of darbha grass.

children.text: śuddham evainaṃ tat pūtaṃ dīkṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: They thereby consecrate him as clean and purified.

children.text: dīkṣitavimitam prapādayanti ||
children.translated_text: They lead him into the <s>dīkṣita-vimita</s>, the consecrated man's enclosure.

children.text: yonir vā eṣā dīkṣitasya yad dīkṣitavimitaṃ yonim evainaṃ tat svām prapādayanti ||
children.translated_text: This, namely the <s>dīkṣita-vimita</s>, is the womb of the consecrated man; they thereby lead him into his own womb.

children.text: tasmād dhruvād yoner āste ca carati ca ||
children.translated_text: Therefore from a fixed womb he both sits and moves.

children.text: tasmād dhruvād yoner garbhā dhīyante ca pra ca jāyante ||
children.translated_text: Therefore embryos are placed in a fixed womb and are born forth from it.

children.text: tasmād dīkṣitaṃ nānyatra dīkṣitavimitād ādityo 'bhyudiyād vābhyastamiyād vāpi vābhyāśrāvayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the sun should not rise upon, set upon, or even be made to call near a consecrated man anywhere other than in the <s>dīkṣita-vimita</s>.

children.text: vāsasā prorṇuvanti ||
children.translated_text: They wrap him with a garment.

children.text: ulbaṃ vā etad dīkṣitasya yad vāsa ulbenaivainaṃ tat prorṇuvanti ||
children.translated_text: The garment is the fetal membrane of the consecrated man; with the membrane itself they thereby wrap him.

children.text: kṛṣṇājinam uttaram bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The black antelope skin is the upper covering.

children.text: uttaraṃ vā ulbāj jarāyu jarāyuṇaivainaṃ tat prorṇuvanti ||
children.translated_text: Above the membrane is the afterbirth; with the afterbirth itself they thereby wrap him.

children.text: muṣṭī kurute ||
children.translated_text: He makes his fists.

children.text: muṣṭī vai kṛtvā garbho 'ntaḥ śete muṣṭī kṛtvā kumāro jāyate tadyan muṣṭī kurute yajñaṃ caiva tat sarvāś ca devatā muṣṭyoḥ kurute ||
children.translated_text: An embryo lies inside with its fists made, and a boy is born with his fists made. Therefore, when he makes his fists, he thereby places both the sacrifice and all the deities in his fists.

children.text: tad āhur na pūrvadīkṣiṇaḥ saṃsavo 'sti parigṛhīto vā etasya yajñaḥ parigṛhītā devatā naitasyārtir asty aparadīkṣiṇa eva yathā tatheti ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'There is no shared pressing for one consecrated earlier; his sacrifice is enclosed, and the deities are enclosed. There is no harm for him. For one consecrated later, it is just the opposite.'

children.text: unmucya kṛṣṇājinam avabhṛtham abhyavaiti tasmān muktā garbhā jarāyor jāyante ||
children.translated_text: Having untied the black antelope skin, he goes down to the <s>avabhṛtha</s> bath; therefore embryos are born freed from the afterbirth.

children.text: sahaiva vāsasābhyavaiti tasmāt sahaivolbena kumāro jāyate ||
children.translated_text: He goes down together with the garment; therefore a child is born together with the fetal membrane.

children.text: Chapter 4
tvam agne saprathā asi soma yās te mayobhuva ity ājyabhāgayoḥ puronuvākye anubrūyād yaḥ pūrvam anījānaḥ syāt tasmai ||
children.translated_text: For a man who has not sacrificed before, he should recite as the two preliminary verses for the two <s>ājyabhāga</s> portions, 'You, <s>Agni</s>, are wide-extending,' and 'O <s>Soma</s>, those of yours that bring refreshment.'

children.text: tvayā yajñaṃ vi tanvata iti yajñam evāsmā etad vitanoti ||
children.translated_text: 'With you they stretch out the sacrifice': by this he stretches out the sacrifice for him.

children.text: agniḥ pratnena manmanā soma gīrbhiṣ ṭvā vayam iti yaḥ pūrvam ījānaḥ syāt tasmai ||
children.translated_text: For one who has sacrificed previously, he should use, "O <s>Agni</s>, with ancient thought," and "O <s>Soma</s>, with songs we [approach] you."

children.text: pratnam iti pūrvaṃ karmābhivadati ||
children.translated_text: "Ancient" here refers to the earlier ritual act.

children.text: tattan nādṛtyam ||
children.translated_text: That is not to be disregarded.

children.text: agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat tvaṃ somāsi satpatir iti vārtraghnāv eva kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Rather, he should make them <s>Vritra</s>-slaying verses: "<s>Agni</s> has struck down the <s>Vritras</s>," and "You, <s>Soma</s>, are the true lord."

children.text: vṛtraṃ vā eṣa hanti yaṃ yajña upanamati tasmād vārtraghnāv eva kartavyau ||
children.translated_text: For he slays <s>Vritra</s>, toward whom the sacrifice inclines; therefore the verses must indeed be <s>Vritra</s>-slaying ones.

children.text: agnir mukham prathamo devatānām agniś ca viṣṇo tapa uttamam maha ity āgnāvaiṣṇavasya haviṣo yājyānuvākye bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Agni</s>, the mouth, the first of the deities," and "<s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>, highest heat, greatness" are the offering verse and invitatory verse for the oblation to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>.

children.text: āgnāvaiṣṇavyau rūpasamṛddhe etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: They are verses belonging to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>, complete in form. For this is the prosperity of a sacrifice, namely that it is complete in form, when a recited verse states the ritual action that is being performed.

children.text: agniś ca ha vai viṣṇuś ca devānāṃ dīkṣāpālau tau dīkṣāyā īśāte tad yad āgnāvaiṣṇavaṃ havir bhavati yau dīkṣāyā īśāte tau prītau dīkṣām prayacchatāṃ yau dīkṣayitārau tau dīkṣayetām iti ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s> are the guardians of consecration among the gods; they have power over <s>diksa</s> (consecration). Therefore, when the oblation belongs to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vishnu</s>, the meaning is: "May those who have power over consecration, being pleased, grant consecration; may those who consecrate perform the consecration."

children.text: triṣṭubhau bhavataḥ sendriyatvāya ||
children.translated_text: The two verses are in the <s>tristubh</s> meter, for the sake of possessing Indra-like power.

children.text: Chapter 5
gāyatryau sviṣṭakṛtaḥ saṃyājye kurvīta tejaskāmo brahmavarcasakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who desires brilliance and sacred radiance should make the Svishtakrit concluding offering verses two <s>gayatri</s> verses.

children.text: tejo vai brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī ||
children.translated_text: For brilliance and sacred radiance are the <s>gayatri</s>.

children.text: tejasvī brahmavarcasī bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān gāyatryau kurute ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this and makes them two <s>gayatri</s> verses becomes brilliant and endowed with sacred radiance.

children.text: uṣṇihāv āyuṣkāmaḥ kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: One who desires long life should make them two <s>usnih</s> verses.

children.text: āyur vā uṣṇik ||
children.translated_text: For long life is the <s>usnih</s>.

children.text: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ vidvān uṣṇihau kurute ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this and makes them two <s>usnih</s> verses reaches a full lifespan.

children.text: anuṣṭubhau svargakāmaḥ kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: One who desires heaven should make them two <s>anustubh</s> verses.

children.text: dvayor vā anuṣṭubhoś catuḥṣaṣṭir akṣarāṇi traya ima ūrdhvā ekaviṃśā lokā ekaviṃśatyaikaviṃśatyaivemāṃllokān rohati svarga eva loke catuḥṣaṣṭitamena pratitiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: For in two <s>anustubh</s> verses there are sixty-four syllables. These three worlds above here are each twenty-one; by twenty-one and twenty-one he ascends these worlds, and in the heavenly world he stands firm by the sixty-fourth.

children.text: pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ vidvān anuṣṭubhau kurute ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this and makes them two <s>anustubh</s> verses stands firm.

children.text: bṛhatyau śrīkāmo yaśaskāmaḥ kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: One who desires prosperity and fame should make them two <s>brhati</s> verses.

children.text: śrīr vai yaśaś chandasām bṛhatī ||
children.translated_text: For prosperity and fame among the meters are the <s>brhati</s>.

children.text: śriyam eva yaśa ātman dhatte ya evaṃ vidvān bṛhatyau kurute ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this and makes them two <s>brhati</s> verses places prosperity and fame in himself.

children.text: paṅktī yajñakāmaḥ kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: One who desires sacrifice should make them two <s>pankti</s> verses.

children.text: pāṅkto vai yajñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the sacrifice is <s>pankti</s>-formed.

children.text: upainaṃ yajño namati ya evaṃ vidvān paṅktī kurute ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice inclines toward one who knows this and makes them two <s>pankti</s> verses.

children.text: triṣṭubhau vīryakāmaḥ kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: One who desires vigor should make them two <s>tristubh</s> verses.

children.text: ojo vā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ triṣṭubhau ||
children.translated_text: For strength, power, and vigor are the two <s>tristubh</s> verses.

children.text: ojasvīndriyavān vīryavān bhavati ya evaṃ vidvāṃs triṣṭubhau kurute ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this and makes them two <s>tristubh</s> verses becomes strong, powerful, and vigorous.

children.text: jagatyau paśukāmaḥ kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: One who desires cattle should make them two <s>jagati</s> verses.

children.text: jāgatā vai paśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For cattle are <s>jagati</s>-formed.

children.text: paśumān bhavati ya evaṃ vidvāñ jagatyau kurute ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this and makes them two <s>jagati</s> verses becomes possessed of cattle.

children.text: virājāv annādyakāmaḥ kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: One who desires food to eat should make them two <s>viraj</s> verses.

children.text: annaṃ vai virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: For food is the <s>viraj</s>.

children.text: tasmād yasyaiveha bhūyiṣṭham annam bhavati sa eva bhūyiṣṭhaṃ loke virājati tad virājo virāṭtvam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the one here who has the most food shines most in the world. That is the being-<s>viraj</s> of the <s>viraj</s>.

children.text: vi sveṣu rājati śreṣṭhaḥ svānām bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He rules among all his own people and becomes the best of them, who knows this.

children.text: Chapter 6
atho pañcavīryaṃ vā etacchando yad virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, this meter which is <s>viraj</s> has fivefold vigor.

children.text: yat tripadā tenoṣṇihāgāyatryau yad asyā ekādaśākṣarāṇi padāni tena triṣṭub yat trayastriṃśadakṣarā tenānuṣṭum na vā ekenākṣareṇa chandāṃsi viyanti na dvābhyāṃ yad virāṭ tat pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: Because it has three feet, it is the <s>usnih</s> and the <s>gayatri</s>; because its feet have eleven syllables, it is the <s>tristubh</s>; because it has thirty-three syllables, it is the <s>anustubh</s>. The meters do not differ by one syllable, nor by two. Because it is <s>viraj</s>, that is the fifth.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ chandasāṃ vīryam avarunddhe sarveṣāṃ chandasāṃ vīryam aśnute sarveṣāṃ chandasāṃ sāyujyaṃ sarūpatāṃ salokatām aśnute 'nnādo 'nnapatir bhavaty aśnute prajayānnādyaṃ ya evaṃ vidvān virājau kurute ||
children.translated_text: He secures the vigor of all the meters; he obtains the vigor of all the meters; he obtains union, likeness of form, and the same world with all the meters. He becomes an eater of food and lord of food, and by offspring he obtains food to eat, who knows this and makes them two <s>viraj</s> verses.

children.text: tasmād virājāv eva kartavye ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the two <s>viraj</s> verses should indeed be made.

children.text: preddho agna imo agna ity ete ||
children.translated_text: These are the verses "Kindled beforehand, O <s>Agni</s>" and "These, O <s>Agni</s>."

children.text: ṛtaṃ vāva dīkṣā satyam dīkṣā tasmād dīkṣitena satyam eva vaditavyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Diksa</s> (consecration) is indeed order; consecration is truth. Therefore one who is consecrated must speak only the truth.

children.text: atho khalv āhuḥ ko 'rhati manuṣyaḥ sarvaṃ satyaṃ vadituṃ satyasaṃhitā vai devā anṛtasaṃhitā manuṣyā iti ||
children.translated_text: But they also say, "What human being is able to speak the whole truth? The gods are joined to truth, while human beings are joined to untruth."

children.text: vicakṣaṇavatīṃ vācam vadet ||
children.translated_text: He should speak speech that has clear seeing.

children.text: cakṣur vai vicakṣaṇaṃ vi hy enena paśyatīti ||
children.translated_text: For the eye is clear-seeing, since by it one sees distinctly.

children.text: etaddha vai manuṣyeṣu satyaṃ nihitaṃ yac cakṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, this truth is deposited among human beings: the eye.

children.text: tasmād ācakṣāṇam āhur adrāg iti sa yady adarśam ity āhāthāsya śraddadhati yady u vai svayam paśyati na bahūnāṃ canānyeṣāṃ śraddadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they say of one who is reporting, "He saw." If he says, "I saw," then they believe him. But if he himself sees, he does not trust even many others.

children.text: tasmād vicakṣaṇavatīm eva vācaṃ vadet satyottarā haivāsya vāg uditā bhavati bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he should speak only speech that has clear seeing. His speech, once uttered, becomes grounded in truth; it becomes so.

children.text: Chapter 7
svargaṃ vā etena lokam upa prayanti yat prāyaṇīyas tat prāyaṇīyasya prāyaṇīyatvam ||
children.translated_text: By this they approach the heavenly world, namely by the Prayaniya offering; that is the reason it is called Prayaniya.

children.text: prāṇo vai prāyaṇīya udāna udayanīyaḥ samāno hotā bhavati samānau hi prāṇodānau prāṇānāṃ kﾱptyai prāṇānām pratiprajñātyai ||
children.translated_text: Breath is the Prayaniya, upward breath is the Udayaniya, and the Hotr is the equalizing breath; for breath and upward breath are equal, for the ordering of the breaths and for the recognition of the breaths.

children.text: yajño vai devebhya udakrāmat te devā na kiṃcanāśaknuvan kartuṃ na prājānaṃs te 'bruvann aditiṃ tvayemaṃ yajñam prajānāmeti sā tathety abravīt sā vai vo varaṃ vṛṇā iti vṛṇīṣveti saitam eva varam avṛṇīta matprāyaṇā yajñāḥ santu madudayanā iti tatheti tasmād ādityaś caruḥ prāyaṇīyo bhavaty āditya udayanīyo varavṛto hy asyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice went away from the gods. The gods could not do anything, nor did they understand it. They said to <s>Aditi</s>, "Through you may we understand this sacrifice." She said, "So be it." She said, "Let me choose a boon from you." "Choose," they replied. She chose this very boon: "Let sacrifices have me as their beginning and me as their ending." "So be it," they said. Therefore the <s>Aditya</s> rice-pap is the Prayaniya, and the <s>Aditya</s> rice-pap is the Udayaniya, for her boon was chosen.

children.text: atho etaṃ varam avṛṇīta mayaiva prācīṃ diśam prajānāthāgninā dakṣiṇāṃ somena pratīcīṃ savitrodīcīm iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he chose this boon: "Let them know the eastern quarter through me, the southern through <s>Agni</s>, the western through <s>Soma</s>, and the northern through <s>Savitṛ</s>."

children.text: pathyāṃ yajati ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices to <s>Pathyā</s>.

children.text: yat pathyāṃ yajati tasmād asau pura udeti paścāstam eti pathyāṃ hy eṣo 'nusaṃcarati ||
children.translated_text: Because he sacrifices to <s>Pathyā</s>, therefore that one rises in front and sets behind; for this one moves along <s>Pathyā</s>.

children.text: agniṃ yajati ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yad agniṃ yajati tasmād dakṣiṇato 'gra oṣadhayaḥ pacyamānā āyanty āgneyyo hy oṣadhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because he sacrifices to <s>Agni</s>, therefore plants, ripening first from the south, come forth; for plants belong to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: somaṃ yajati ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices to <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: yat somaṃ yajati tasmāt pratīcyo 'py āpo bahvyaḥ syandante saumyā hy āpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because he sacrifices to <s>Soma</s>, therefore many waters flow down toward the west; for the waters belong to <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: savitāram yajati ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices to <s>Savitṛ</s>.

children.text: yat savitāraṃ yajati tasmād uttarataḥ paścād ayam bhūyiṣṭham pavamānaḥ pavate savitṛprasūto hy eṣa etat pavate ||
children.translated_text: Because he sacrifices to <s>Savitṛ</s>, therefore from the north, behind, this purifying wind blows most abundantly; for, impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, it blows there.

children.text: uttamām aditiṃ yajati ||
children.translated_text: As the last, he sacrifices to <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: yad uttamām aditiṃ yajati tasmād asāv imāṃ vṛṣṭyābhyunatty abhijighrati ||
children.translated_text: Because, as the last, he sacrifices to <s>Aditi</s>, therefore that one moistens this earth with rain and smells upon it.

children.text: pañca devatā yajati pāṅkto yajñaḥ sarvā diśaḥ kalpante kalpate yajño 'pi ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices to five deities. The sacrifice is fivefold; all the quarters are made fit, and the sacrifice too is made fit.

children.text: tasyai janatāyai kalpate yatraivaṃ vidvān hotā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: It is made fit for that people among whom there is a <s>hotṛ</s> who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 8
yas tejo brahmavarcasam icchet prayājāhutibhiḥ prāṅ sa iyāt tejo vai brahmavarcasam prācī dik ||
children.translated_text: One who desires brilliance and brahminical lustre should go eastward with the fore-offerings; brilliance and brahminical lustre are the eastern quarter.

children.text: tejasvī brahmavarcasī bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān prāṅ eti ||
children.translated_text: He becomes brilliant and possessed of brahminical lustre, who, knowing thus, goes eastward.

children.text: yo 'nnādyam icchet prayājāhutibhir dakṣiṇā sa iyād annādo vā eṣo 'nnapatir yad agniḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who desires the eating of food should go southward with the fore-offerings; for that which is <s>Agni</s> is the eater of food and the lord of food.

children.text: annādo 'nnapatir bhavaty aśnute prajayānnādyaṃ ya evaṃ vidvān dakṣiṇaiti ||
children.translated_text: He becomes an eater of food and a lord of food; he attains the eating of food through offspring, who, knowing thus, goes southward.

children.text: yaḥ paśūn icchet prayājāhutibhiḥ pratyaṅ sa iyāt paśavo vā ete yad āpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who desires cattle should go westward with the fore-offerings; for these waters are cattle.

children.text: paśumān bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān pratyaṅṅ eti ||
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of cattle, who, knowing thus, goes westward.

children.text: yaḥ somapītham icchet prayājāhutibhir udaṅ sa iyād uttarā ha vai somo rājā ||
children.translated_text: One who desires the draught of <s>Soma</s> should go northward with the fore-offerings; for king <s>Soma</s> is indeed in the north.

children.text: pra somapītham āpnoti ya evaṃ vidvān udaṅṅ eti ||
children.translated_text: He obtains the draught of <s>Soma</s>, who, knowing thus, goes northward.

children.text: svargyaivordhvā dik sarvāsu dikṣu rādhnoti ||
children.translated_text: The upward quarter is precisely heavenly; he prospers in all the quarters.

children.text: samyañco vā ime lokāḥ samyañco 'smā ime lokāḥ śriyai dīdyati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: These worlds are concordant; these worlds shine for him in concord for prosperity, who knows thus.

children.text: pathyāṃ yajati yat pathyāṃ yajati vācam eva tad yajñamukhe saṃbharati ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices to <s>Pathyā</s>. In that he sacrifices to <s>Pathyā</s>, he gathers speech itself at the mouth of the sacrifice.

children.text: prāṇāpānāv agnīṣomau prasavāya savitā pratiṣṭhityā aditiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> are the in-breath and out-breath, <s>Savitṛ</s> is for impulsion, and <s>Aditi</s> is for establishment.

children.text: pathyām eva yajati yat pathyām eva yajati vācaiva tad yajñam panthām apinayati ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices to <s>Pathyā</s> alone. In that he sacrifices to <s>Pathyā</s> alone, by speech itself he leads the sacrifice onto the path.

children.text: cakṣuṣī evāgnīṣomau prasavāya savitā pratiṣṭhityā aditiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> are the two eyes, <s>Savitṛ</s> is for impulsion, and <s>Aditi</s> is for establishment.

children.text: cakṣuṣā vai devā yajñam prājānaṃś cakṣuṣā vā etat prajñāyate yad aprajñeyaṃ tasmād api mugdhaś caritvā yadaivānuṣṭhyā cakṣuṣā prajānāty atha prajānāti ||
children.translated_text: By sight the gods discerned the sacrifice; by sight indeed that is discerned which is otherwise not discernible. Therefore even a confused man, after moving about, when he recognizes it with the eye following after, then he understands.

children.text: yad vai tad devā yajñam prājānann asyāṃ vāva tat prājānann asyāṃ samabharann asyai vai yajñas tāyate 'syai kriyate 'syai saṃbhriyata iyaṃ hy aditis tad uttamām aditiṃ yajati yad uttamām aditiṃ yajati yajñasya prajñātyai svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai ||
children.translated_text: When the gods discerned that sacrifice, they discerned it here in this earth; they gathered it here in this earth. For this earth the sacrifice is stretched out, for this earth it is performed, for this earth it is gathered; for this earth is <s>Aditi</s>. Therefore, as the last, he sacrifices to <s>Aditi</s>. In that, as the last, he sacrifices to <s>Aditi</s>, it is for the discerning of the sacrifice and for the beholding of the heavenly world.

children.text: Chapter 9
devaviśaḥ kalpayitavyā ity āhus tāḥ kalpamānā anu manuṣyaviśaḥ kalpanta iti sarvā viśaḥ kalpante kalpate yajño 'pi ||
children.translated_text: They say, "The clans of the gods must be made fit; when they are being made fit, the clans of men are made fit after them." All the clans are made fit, and the sacrifice too is made fit.

children.text: tasyai janatāyai kalpate yatraivaṃ vidvān hotā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: It is made fit for that people among whom there is a <s>hotṛ</s> who knows thus.

children.text: svasti naḥ pathyāsu dhanvasv ity anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites after it, "May there be well-being for us on the paths, in the dry lands."

children.text: svasty apsu vṛjane svarvati svasti naḥ putrakṛtheṣu yoniṣu svasti rāye maruto dadhātaneti ||
children.translated_text: "Well-being in the waters, in the enclosure rich in light; may the <s>Maruts</s> grant us well-being in wombs that produce sons, well-being for wealth."

children.text: maruto vai devānāṃ viśas tā evaitad yajñamukhe 'cīkﾱpat ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maruts</s> are the clans of the gods; them he thereby sets in order at the mouth of the sacrifice.

children.text: sarvaiś chandobhir yajed ity āhuḥ sarvair vai chandobhir iṣṭvā devāḥ svargaṃ lokam ajayaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānaḥ sarvaiś chandobhir iṣṭvā svargaṃ lokaṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: They say, "One should sacrifice with all the metres." Having sacrificed with all the metres, the gods won the heavenly world; in just the same way the sacrificer, having sacrificed with all the metres, wins the heavenly world.

children.text: svasti naḥ pathyāsu dhanvasu svastir iddhi prapathe śreṣṭheti pathyāyāḥ svastes triṣṭubhāv agne naya supathā rāye asmān ā devānām api panthām aganmety agnes triṣṭubhau tvaṃ soma pra cikito manīṣā yā te dhāmāni divi yā pṛthivyām iti somasya triṣṭubhāv ā viśvadevaṃ satpatiṃ ya imā viśvā jātānīti savitur gāyatryau sutrāmāṇam pṛthivīṃ dyām anehasam mahīm ū ṣu mātaraṃ suvratānām ity aditer jagatyau ||
children.translated_text: "May there be well-being for us on the paths, in the dry lands; well-being indeed on the best high road"--these are the two <s>triṣṭubh</s> verses of <s>Pathyā Svasti</s>. "<s>Agni</s>, lead us by a good path to wealth" and "We have come upon the path of the gods"--these are the two <s>triṣṭubh</s> verses of <s>Agni</s>. "You, <s>Soma</s>, have perceived through wisdom" and "Those stations of yours that are in heaven and on earth"--these are the two <s>triṣṭubh</s> verses of <s>Soma</s>. "To the lord of beings, the All-god" and "He who is all these born things"--these are the two <s>gāyatrī</s> verses of <s>Savitṛ</s>. "The well-protecting earth and heaven, free from harm" and "The great mother of good ordinances"--these are the two <s>jagatī</s> verses of <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: etāni vāva sarvāṇi chandāṃsi gāyatraṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ jāgatam anv anyāny etāni hi yajñe pratamām iva kriyante ||
children.translated_text: These indeed are all the metres: the <s>gāyatra</s>, the <s>traiṣṭubha</s>, and the <s>jāgata</s>; the others follow after them, for these are performed as foremost in the sacrifice.

children.text: etair ha vā asya chandobhir yajataḥ sarvaiś chandobhir iṣṭam bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For him who sacrifices with these metres, the sacrifice has been performed with all the metres, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 10
tā vā etāḥ pravatyo netṛmatyaḥ pathimatyaḥ svastimatya etasya haviṣo yājyānuvākyā etābhir vā iṣṭvā devāḥ svargaṃ lokam ajayaṃs tathaivaitad yajamāna etābhir iṣṭvā svargaṃ lokaṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: These, then, are the invitatory and offering verses of this oblation: flowing onward, possessing a leader, possessing a path, and possessing well-being. Having sacrificed with these, the gods won the heavenly world; in just the same way the sacrificer, having sacrificed with these, wins the heavenly world.

children.text: tāsu padam asti svasti rāye maruto dadhātaneti maruto ha vai devaviśo 'ntarikṣabhājanās tebhyo ha yo 'nivedya svargaṃ lokam etīśvarā hainaṃ ni vā roddhor vi vā mathitoḥ sa yad āha svasti rāye maruto dadhātaneti tam marudbhyo devaviḍbhyo yajamānaṃ nivedayati na ha vā enam maruto devaviśaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yantaṃ nirundhate na vimathnate ||
children.translated_text: Among them there is this pada: "May the <s>Maruts</s> bestow well-being for wealth." The <s>Maruts</s> are indeed the divine clansmen, whose share is the midspace. If someone goes to the heavenly world without first announcing himself to them, they are able either to stop him or to tear him apart. Therefore, when he says, "May the <s>Maruts</s> bestow well-being for wealth," he announces the sacrificer to the <s>Maruts</s>, the divine clansmen. The <s>Maruts</s>, the divine clansmen, do not obstruct him as he goes to the heavenly world, nor do they tear him apart.

children.text: svasti hainam atyarjanti svargaṃ lokam abhi ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: They let him pass safely on toward the heavenly world, he who knows thus.

children.text: virājāv etasya haviṣaḥ sviṣṭakṛtaḥ saṃyājye syātāṃ ye trayastriṃśadakṣare ||
children.translated_text: For this oblation the two saṃyājya verses of the sviṣṭakṛt should be two <s>Virāj</s> verses, those which have thirty-three syllables.

children.text: sed agnir agnīṃr aty astv anyān sed agnir yo vanuṣyato nipātīty ete ||
children.translated_text: "May this <s>Agni</s> surpass the other fires; may this <s>Agni</s> strike down the one who attacks," these are the two.

children.text: virāḍbhyāṃ vā iṣṭvā devāḥ svargaṃ lokam ajayaṃs tathaivaitad yajamāno virāḍbhyām iṣṭvā svargaṃ lokaṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: Having sacrificed with the two <s>Virāj</s> verses, the gods won the heavenly world. In just the same way, after sacrificing with the two <s>Virāj</s> verses, the sacrificer wins the heavenly world.

children.text: te trayastriṃśadakṣare bhavatas trayastriṃśad vai devā aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāḥ prajāpatiś ca vaṣaṭkāraś ca tat prathame yajñamukhe devatā akṣarabhājaḥ karoty akṣareṇākṣareṇaiva tad devatām prīṇāti devapātreṇaiva tad devatās tarpayati ||
children.translated_text: They are thirty-three-syllabled. There are indeed thirty-three gods: eight <s>Vasus</s>, eleven <s>Rudras</s>, twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>. Thus, at the first opening of the sacrifice, he makes the deities sharers in syllables; with each syllable he pleases a deity, and with a divine vessel he satisfies the deities.

children.text: Chapter 11
prayājavad ananuyājaṃ kartavyam prāyaṇīyam ity āhur hīnam iva vā etad īṅkhitam iva yat prāyaṇīyasyānuyājā iti ||
children.translated_text: It should be performed with prayājas but without anuyājas, because it is the prāyaṇīya, they say. For the anuyājas of the prāyaṇīya are, as it were, deficient and, as it were, unsteady.

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyam ||
children.translated_text: But that is not to be accepted.

children.text: prayājavad evānuyājavat kartavyam prāṇā vai prayājāḥ prajānuyājā yat prayājān antariyāt prāṇāṃs tad yajamānasyāntariyād yad anuyājān antariyāt prajāṃ tad yajamānasyāntariyāt ||
children.translated_text: It should be performed with prayājas and also with anuyājas. The prayājas are the breaths; the anuyājas are offspring. If he were to omit the prayājas, he would omit the sacrificer's breaths; if he were to omit the anuyājas, he would omit the sacrificer's offspring.

children.text: tasmāt prayājavad evānuyājavat kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it should indeed be performed with prayājas and with anuyājas.

children.text: patnīr na saṃyājayet saṃsthitayajur na juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not perform the wife-related saṃyājas; he should not offer the concluding yajus.

children.text: tāvataiva yajño 'saṃsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By just so much the sacrifice remains unconcluded.

children.text: prāyaṇīyasya niṣkāsaṃ nidadhyāt tam udayanīyenābhinirvaped yajñasya saṃtatyai yajñasyāvyavachedāya ||
children.translated_text: He should set aside the residue of the prāyaṇīya and offer it together with the udayanīya, for the continuity of the sacrifice and for the non-interruption of the sacrifice.

children.text: atho khalu yasyām eva sthālyām prāyaṇīyaṃ nirvapet tasyām udayanīyaṃ nirvapet tāvataiva yajñaḥ saṃtato 'vyavachinno bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, in the very bowl in which he prepares the prāyaṇīya, in that same one he should prepare the udayanīya. By just that much the sacrifice becomes continuous and uninterrupted.

children.text: amuṣmin vā etena loke rādhnuvanti nāsminn ity āhur yat prāyaṇīyam iti prāyaṇīyam iti nirvapanti prāyaṇīyam iti caranti prayanty evāsmāl lokād yajamānā iti ||
children.translated_text: By this, they say, people prosper in yonder world, not in this one: because they prepare the prāyaṇīya as "the departure offering" and proceed with it as "the departure offering," the sacrificers depart from this world.

children.text: avidyayaiva tad āhur vyatiṣajed yājyānuvākyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say that only through ignorance. He should interweave the yājyā and anuvākyā verses.

children.text: yāḥ prāyaṇīyasya puronuvākyās tā udayanīyasya yājyāḥ kuryād yā udayanīyasya puronuvākyās tāḥ prāyaṇīyasya yājyāḥ kuryāt tad vyatiṣajaty ubhayor lokayor ṛddhyā ubhayor lokayoḥ pratiṣṭhityā ubhayor lokayor ṛdhnoty ubhayor lokayoḥ pratitiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: The puronuvākyā verses of the prāyaṇīya he should make the yājyā verses of the udayanīya, and the puronuvākyā verses of the udayanīya he should make the yājyā verses of the prāyaṇīya. Thus he interweaves them, for success in both worlds and for firm standing in both worlds. He prospers in both worlds and stands firm in both worlds.

children.text: pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He stands firm, he who knows thus.

children.text: ādityaś caruḥ prāyaṇīyo bhavaty āditya udayanīyo yajñasya dhṛtyai yajñasya barsanaddhyai yajñasyāprasraṃsāya ||
children.translated_text: The prāyaṇīya is an <s>Āditya</s> caru, and the udayanīya is for <s>Āditya</s>, for the support of the sacrifice, for the binding-fast of the sacrifice, and so that the sacrifice does not slip away.

children.text: tad yathaivāda iti ha smāha tejanyā ubhayato 'ntayor aprasraṃsāya barsau nahyaty evam evaitad yajñasyobhayato 'ntayor aprasraṃsāya barsau nahyati yad ādityaś caruḥ prāyaṇīyo bhavaty āditya udayanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is just as, he used to say, one ties the two fastening-bands at both ends of a bowstring so that it may not slip away. In the same way he ties the two fastening-bands at both ends of the sacrifice so that it may not slip away, when the prāyaṇīya is an <s>Āditya</s> caru and the udayanīya is for <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: pathyayaivetaḥ svastyā prayanti pathyāṃ svastim abhy udyanti svasty evetaḥ prayanti svasty udyanti svasty udyanti ||
children.translated_text: By the auspicious path they set forth from here; they rise toward the auspicious path of well-being. With well-being they depart from here; with well-being they rise; with well-being they rise.

children.text: Chapter 12
prācyāṃ vai diśi devāḥ somaṃ rājānam akrīṇaṃs tasmāt prācyāṃ diśi krīyate ||
children.translated_text: In the eastern direction the gods bought King <s>Soma</s>; therefore he is bought in the eastern direction.

children.text: taṃ trayodaśān māsād akrīṇaṃs tasmāt trayodaśo māso nānuvidyate na vai somavikrayy anuvidyate pāpo hi somavikrayī ||
children.translated_text: They bought him from a thirteenth month; therefore a thirteenth month is not recognized. The Soma-seller is not recognized, for the Soma-seller is sinful.

children.text: tasya krītasya manuṣyān abhy upāvartamānasya diśo vīryāṇīndriyāṇi vyudasīdaṃs tāny ekayarcāvārurutsanta tāni nāśaknuvaṃs tāni dvābhyāṃ tāni tisṛbhis tāni catasṛbhis tāni pañcabhis tāni ṣaḍbhis tāni saptabhir naivāvārundhata tāny aṣṭābhir avārundhatāṣṭābhir āśnuvata yad aṣṭābhir avārundhatāṣṭābhir āśnuvata tad aṣṭānām aṣṭatvam ||
children.translated_text: When he had been bought and was turning back toward human beings, the directions, powers, and faculties withdrew from him. They wished to secure them with one ṛc, but could not; then with two, then with three, then with four, then with five, then with six, then with seven, but they still did not secure them. With eight they secured them; with eight they attained them. Because they secured them with eight and attained them with eight, that is the eightness of the eights.

children.text: aśnute yad yat kāmayate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He attains whatever he desires, he who knows thus.

children.text: tasmād eteṣu karmasv aṣṭāvaṣṭāv anūcyanta indriyāṇāṃ vīryāṇām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in these rites, eight verses at a time are recited, for the securing of the faculties and powers.

children.text: Chapter 13
somāya krītāya prohyamāṇāyānubrūhīty āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The adhvaryu says, "Recite for <s>Soma</s>, who has been bought and is being carried forth."

children.text: bhadrād abhi śreyaḥ prehīty anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "From the good go forward toward the better."

children.text: ayaṃ vāva loko bhadras tasmād asāv eva lokaḥ śreyān svargam eva tallokaṃ yajamānaṃ gamayati ||
children.translated_text: This world is indeed the good; therefore that other world is the better. Thus he causes the sacrificer to go to that heavenly world.

children.text: bṛhaspatiḥ puraetā te astv iti brahma vai bṛhaspatir brahmaivāsmā etat purogavam akaḥ na vai brahmaṇvad riṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "Let <s>Bṛhaspati</s> be your forerunner." <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the brahman; thus he has made the brahman his forerunner. One possessed of brahman does not come to harm.

children.text: athem ava sya vara ā pṛthivyā iti devayajanaṃ vai varam pṛthivyai devayajana evainaṃ tad avasāyayaty āre śatrūn kṛṇuhi sarvavīra iti dviṣantam evāsmai tatpāpmānam bhrātṛvyam apabādhate 'dharam pādayati ||
children.translated_text: Then, with the words, "Settle this excellent one upon the earth," the sacrificial ground is indeed the excellent part of the earth; thereby he settles him precisely in the sacrificial ground. With "Drive the enemies far away, O one with all heroes," he thereby repels for him the hater, the evil, the rival, and sets him lower.

children.text: soma yās te mayobhuva iti tṛcaṃ saumyaṃ gāyatram anvāha some rājani prohyamāṇe svayaivainaṃ tad devatayā svena chandasā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the three-verse Somic Gāyatrī hymn, "O <s>Soma</s>, those of yours that bring delight," while King <s>Soma</s> is being brought forward; thereby he prospers him with his own deity and with his own meter.

children.text: sarve nandanti yaśasāgatenety anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "All rejoice when fame has come."

children.text: yaśo vai somo rājā sarvo ha vā etena krīyamāṇena nandati yaś ca yajñe lapsyamāno bhavati yaś ca na ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Soma</s> is fame. When he is being bought, everyone rejoices: both the one who is to gain something in the sacrifice and the one who is not.

children.text: sabhāsāhena sakhyā sakhāya ity eṣa vai brāhmaṇānāṃ sabhāsāhaḥ sakhā yat somo rājā ||
children.translated_text: With "a friend, together with a friend who conquers assemblies," this King <s>Soma</s> is indeed the assembly-conquering friend of the brahmins.

children.text: kilbiṣaspṛd ity eṣa u eva kilbiṣaspṛt ||
children.translated_text: With "touching guilt," he is indeed precisely the one who touches or removes guilt.

children.text: yo vai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭhatām aśnute sa kilbiṣam bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Whoever becomes important, whoever attains preeminence, becomes involved with guilt.

children.text: tasmād āhur mānuvoco mā pracārīḥ kilbiṣaṃ nu mā yātayann iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they say, "Do not speak; do not go forward. Surely you are driving me into guilt."

children.text: pituṣaṇir ity annaṃ vai pitu dakṣiṇā vai pitu tām enena sanoty annasanim evainaṃ tat karoti ||
children.translated_text: With "winning nourishment," nourishment is food, and the priestly fee is food; he wins that through him. Thereby he makes him a winner of food.

children.text: araṃ hito bhavati vājināyetīndriyaṃ vai vīryaṃ vājinam ||
children.translated_text: With "he becomes suitably placed for the vigorous one," the vigorous one is power and heroic strength.

children.text: ājarasaṃ hāsmai vājinaṃ nāpacchidyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For the one who knows thus, the vigorous power is not cut off until old age.

children.text: āgan deva ity anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "The god has come."

children.text: āgato hi sa tarhi bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For at that time he has indeed come.

children.text: ṛtubhir vardhatu kṣayam ity ṛtavo vai somasya rājño rājabhrātaro yathā manuṣyasya tair evainaṃ tat sahāgamayati ||
children.translated_text: With "may he increase the dwelling with the seasons," the seasons are the royal brothers of King <s>Soma</s>, as they are of a human king; by those very seasons he makes him come together with them.

children.text: dadhātu naḥ savitā suprajām iṣam ity āśiṣam āśāste ||
children.translated_text: With "may <s>Savitṛ</s> bestow on us good offspring and refreshment," he seeks a blessing.

children.text: sa naḥ kṣapābhir ahabhiś ca jinvatv ity ahāni vā ahāni rātrayaḥ kṣapā ahorātrair evāsmā etām āśiṣam āśāste prajāvantaṃ rayim asme sam invatv ity āśiṣam evāśāste ||
children.translated_text: With "may he enliven us by nights and by days," days are days and nights are kṣapās; by days and nights he seeks this blessing for him. With "may he bring together for us wealth rich in offspring," he again seeks a blessing.

children.text: yā te dhāmāni haviṣā yajantīty anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Those abodes of yours which they worship with oblation."

children.text: tā te viśvā paribhūr astu yajñaṃ ||
children.translated_text: "May all those of yours encompass the sacrifice."

children.text: gayasphānaḥ prataraṇaḥ suvīra iti gavāṃ naḥ sphāvayitā pratārayitaidhīty eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: With "increaser of cattle, carrier across, rich in heroes," he says just this: "Be the increaser of our cattle and the one who carries us across."

children.text: avīrahā pra carā soma duryān iti gṛhā vai duryā bibhyati vai somād rājña āyato yajamānasya gṛhāḥ sa yad etām anvāha śāntyaivainaṃ tacchamayati so 'sya śānto na prajāṃ na paśūn hinasti ||
children.translated_text: With "Move through the houses, <s>Soma</s>, not harming heroes," houses are the dwellings. The houses of the sacrificer fear King <s>Soma</s> as he approaches. Because he recites this verse, he quiets him by appeasement; being appeased, he harms neither his offspring nor his cattle.

children.text: imāṃ dhiyaṃ śikṣamāṇasya deveti vāruṇyā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the verse to <s>Varuṇa</s>, "This thought of the one who is learning, O god," he encloses him.

children.text: varuṇadevatyo vā eṣa tāvad yāvad upanaddho yāvat pariśritāni prapadyate svayaivainaṃ tad devatayā svena chandasā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: For so long as he is bound, until he enters the enclosing screens, he has <s>Varuṇa</s> as his deity; thereby he prospers him with his own deity and with his own meter.

children.text: śikṣamāṇasya deveti śikṣate vā eṣa yo yajate ||
children.translated_text: With "of the one who is learning, O god," one who sacrifices is indeed learning.

children.text: kratuṃ dakṣaṃ varuṇa saṃ śiśādhīti vīryam prajñānaṃ varuṇa saṃ śiśādhīty eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: With "<s>Varuṇa</s>, sharpen together resolve and skill," he says just this: "<s>Varuṇa</s>, sharpen together strength and understanding."

children.text: yayāti viśvā duritā tarema sutarmāṇam adhi nāvaṃ ruhemeti yajño vai sutarmā nauḥ kṛṣṇājinaṃ vai sutarmā naur vāg vai sutarmā naur vācam eva tad āruhya tayā svargaṃ lokam abhi saṃtarati ||
children.translated_text: With "by which we may cross over all difficulties; may we mount the well-crossing boat," the sacrifice is the well-crossing boat; the black antelope skin is the well-crossing boat; speech is the well-crossing boat. Having mounted speech itself, by it he crosses over to the heavenly world.

children.text: tā etā aṣṭāvanvāha rūpasamṛddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites these eight verses, complete in their form.

children.text: etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: That in the sacrifice is truly complete which is complete in form, when a ṛc addresses the action that is being performed.

children.text: tāsāṃ triḥ prathamām anvāha trir uttamām ||
children.translated_text: Of them he recites the first three times and the last three times.

children.text: tā dvādaśa sampadyante dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They amount to twelve; the year has twelve months, and the year is <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: prajāpatyāyatanābhir evābhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: By means whose foundation is <s>Prajāpati</s> he succeeds in them, the one who knows thus.

children.text: triḥ prathamāṃ trir uttamām anvāha yajñasyaiva tad barsau nahyati sthemne balāyāvisraṃsāya ||
children.translated_text: He recites the first three times and the last three times; thereby he fastens the two flanks of the sacrifice for firmness, for strength, and so that it does not fall apart.

children.text: Chapter 14
anyataro 'naḍvān yuktaḥ syād anyataro vimukto 'tha rājānam upāvahareyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: One draught ox should be yoked and the other unyoked; then they should bring the king forward.

children.text: yad ubhayor vimuktayor upāvahareyuḥ pitṛdevatyaṃ rājānaṃ kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If they were to bring the king forward when both were unyoked, they would make the king belong to the Fathers.

children.text: yad yuktayor ayogakṣemaḥ prajā vindet tāḥ prajāḥ pariplaveran ||
children.translated_text: If they were to bring him when both were yoked, insecurity would overtake the offspring; those offspring would drift away.

children.text: yo 'naḍvān vimuktas tacchālāsadām prajānāṃ rūpaṃ yo yuktas tac cakriyāṇāṃ te ye yukte 'nye vimukte 'nya upāvaharanty ubhāveva te kṣemayogau kalpayanti ||
children.translated_text: The draught ox that is unyoked is the form of the people sitting in the hall; the one that is yoked is the form of those who are active. Therefore, when some bring him forward with one yoked and another unyoked, they arrange both security and active acquisition.

children.text: devāsurā vā eṣu lokeṣu samayatanta ta etasyām prācyāṃ diśy ayatanta tāṃs tato 'surā ajayaṃs te dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśy ayatanta tāṃs tato 'surā ajayaṃs te pratīcyāṃ diśy ayatanta tāṃs tato 'surā ajayaṃs ta udīcyāṃ diśy ayatanta tāṃs tato 'surā ajayaṃs ta udīcyām prācyāṃ diśy ayatanta te tato na parājayanta saiṣā dig aparājitā tasmād etasyāṃ diśi yateta vā yātayed veśvaro hānṛṇākartoḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods and the Asuras contended in these worlds. They contended in this eastern direction, and from there the Asuras defeated them. They contended in the southern direction, and from there the Asuras defeated them. They contended in the western direction, and from there the Asuras defeated them. They contended in the northern direction, and from there the Asuras defeated them. They contended in the north-eastern direction, and from there they were not defeated. This is the unconquered direction. Therefore one should strive in this direction, or should cause another to set out in it; it is indeed capable of making one free from debt.

children.text: te devā abruvann arājatayā vai no jayanti rājānaṃ karavāmahā iti tatheti te somaṃ rājānam akurvaṃs te somena rājnā sarvā diśo 'jayann eṣa vai somarājā yo yajate prāci tiṣṭhaty ādadhati tena prācīṃ diśaṃ jayati taṃ dakṣiṇā parivahanti tena dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ jayati tam pratyañcam āvartayanti tena pratīcīṃ diśaṃ jayati tam udīcas tiṣṭhata upāvaharanti tenodīcīṃ diśaṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: The gods said, "Because we have no king, they conquer us; let us make a king." "So be it," they said. They made <s>Soma</s> king. With <s>Soma</s> as king they conquered all the quarters. He who sacrifices has <s>Soma</s> as king. They set him down while he stands facing east; by that he conquers the eastern quarter. They carry him around to the south; by that he conquers the southern quarter. They turn him westward; by that he conquers the western quarter. Those standing to the north bring him up; by that he conquers the northern quarter.

children.text: somena rājñā sarvā diśo jayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: With <s>Soma</s> as king he conquers all the quarters, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 15
havir ātithyaṃ nirupyate some rājany āgate ||
children.translated_text: The guest-offering is set out when King <s>Soma</s> has arrived.

children.text: somo vai rājā yajamānasya gṛhān āgacchati tasmā etaddhavir ātithyaṃ nirupyate tad ātithyasyātithyatvam ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Soma</s> comes to the sacrificer's houses. For him this guest-offering is set out; that is the guesthood of the guest-offering.

children.text: navakapālo bhavati nava vai prāṇāḥ prāṇānāṃ kﾱptyai prāṇānām pratiprajñātyai ||
children.translated_text: It consists of nine potsherds. There are nine breaths, for the fitting of the breaths and for the recognition of the breaths.

children.text: vaiṣṇavo bhavati viṣṇur vai yajñaḥ svayaivainaṃ tad devatayā svena chandasā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: It belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the sacrifice; thereby he makes it prosper with its own deity and with its own metre.

children.text: sarvāṇi vāva chandāṃsi ca pṛṣṭhāni ca somaṃ rājānaṃ krītam anv āyanti yāvantaḥ khalu vai rājānam anuyanti tebhyaḥ sarvebhya ātithyaṃ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: All the metres and the pṛṣṭha-stotras follow King <s>Soma</s> when he has been bought. Indeed, however many follow a king, for all of them hospitality is performed.

children.text: agnim manthanti some rājany āgate tad yathaivādo manuṣyarāja āgate 'nyasmin vārhaty ukṣāṇaṃ vā vehataṃ vā kṣadanta evam evāsmā etat kṣadante yad agnim manthanty agnir hi devānām paśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They churn <s>Agni</s> when King <s>Soma</s> has arrived. Just as, when a human king has arrived, people cut up for him another worthy bull or steer, so they cut this up for him when they churn <s>Agni</s>; for <s>Agni</s> is the animal of the gods.

children.text: Chapter 16
agnaye mathyamānāyānubrūhīty āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>adhvaryu</s> says, "Recite for <s>Agni</s> as he is being churned."

children.text: abhi tvā devā savitar iti sāvitrīm anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Sāvitrī</s> verse, "The gods toward you, O <s>Savitṛ</s>."

children.text: tad āhur yad agnaye mathyamānāyānu vācāhātha kasmāt sāvitrīm anvāheti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If he has called for a recitation for <s>Agni</s> as he is being churned, then why does he recite a <s>Sāvitrī</s> verse?"

children.text: savitā vai prasavānām īśe savitṛprasūtā evainaṃ tan manthanti tasmāt sāvitrīm anvāha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Savitṛ</s> is lord of impulsions. Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, they thereby churn him; therefore he recites a <s>Sāvitrī</s> verse.

children.text: mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivīyām anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites the verse addressed to Heaven and Earth, "Great heaven and earth for us."

children.text: tad āhur yad agnaye mathyamānāyānu vācāhātha kasmād dyāvāpṛthivīyām anvāheti dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ vā etaṃ jātaṃ devāḥ paryagṛhṇaṃs tābhyām evādyāpi parigṛhītas tasmād dyāvāpṛthivīyām anvāha ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If he has called for a recitation for <s>Agni</s> as he is being churned, then why does he recite a verse addressed to Heaven and Earth?" The gods enclosed him when born with Heaven and Earth; by them he is still enclosed today. Therefore he recites a verse addressed to Heaven and Earth.

children.text: tvām agne puṣkarād adhīti tṛcam āgneyaṃ gāyatram anvāhāgnau mathyamāne svayaivainaṃ tad devatayā svena chandasā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the three-verse <s>gāyatrī</s> hymn to <s>Agni</s>, "You, O <s>Agni</s>, from the lotus." While <s>Agni</s> is being churned, he thereby makes him prosper with his own deity and with his own metre.

children.text: atharvā nir amanthateti rūpasamṛddhaṃ etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Atharvan</s> churned you forth" is successful in form. This is the success of the sacrifice: when a verse speaks directly of the ritual action that is being performed, that is success in form.

children.text: sa yadi na jāyeta yadi ciraṃ jāyeta rākṣoghnyo gāyatryo 'nūcyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he should not be born, or if he should be long in being born, <s>gāyatrī</s> verses that repel demons should be recited.

children.text: agne haṃsi ny atriṇam ity etāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are the verses, "O <s>Agni</s>, you strike down the devourer."

children.text: rakṣasām apahatyai ||
children.translated_text: They are for the driving away of demons.

children.text: rakṣāṃsi vā enaṃ tarhy ālabhante yarhi na jāyate yarhi ciraṃ jāyate ||
children.translated_text: For demons seize him at that time, when he is not born or when he is long in being born.

children.text: sa yady ekasyām evānūktāyāṃ jāyeta yadi dvayor atho ta bruvantu jantava iti jātāya jātavatīm abhirūpām anubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he should be born after just one verse has been recited, or if after two, then to him once born he should recite the birth-speaking, corresponding verse, "And let the creatures speak."

children.text: yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: What is corresponding in form in the sacrifice is successful.

children.text: ā yaṃ haste na khādinam iti ||
children.translated_text: "To this one as to a biter in the hand."

children.text: hastābhyāṃ hy enam manthanti ||
children.translated_text: For they churn him with the two hands.

children.text: śiśuṃ jātam iti śiśur iva vā eṣa prathamajāto yad agniḥ ||
children.translated_text: "A child born"; for this one is like a child when first born, namely <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: na bibhrati viśām agniṃ svadhvaram iti ||
children.translated_text: "They do not bear <s>Agni</s> of the clans, good for sacrifice."

children.text: yad vai devānāṃ neti tad eṣām om iti ||
children.translated_text: What is "no" among the gods is "om" for them.

children.text: pra devaṃ devavītaye bharatā vasuvittamam iti prahriyamāṇāyābhirūpā ||
children.translated_text: "Bring forward the god for the god-loving, the best finder of wealth" is corresponding in form for him as he is being carried forward.

children.text: yad yajñe'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: What is corresponding in form in the sacrifice is successful.

children.text: ā sve yonau ni ṣīdatv iti ||
children.translated_text: "Let him sit down in his own womb."

children.text: eṣa ha vā asya svo yonir yad agnir agneḥ ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is his own womb, namely the fire that belongs to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: ā jātaṃ jātavedasīti ||
children.translated_text: "Come to the one born, O <s>Jātavedas</s>."

children.text: jāta itaro jātavedā itaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The one is born; the other is <s>Jātavedas</s>.

children.text: priyaṃ śiśītātithim ity eṣa ha vā asya priyo 'tithir yad agnir agneḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Sharpen the dear guest"; this indeed is his dear guest, namely the fire that belongs to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: syona ā gṛhapatim iti śāntyām evainaṃ tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: "Kindly come to the householder"; thereby he places him in peacefulness.

children.text: agnināgniḥ sam idhyate kavir gṛhapatir yuvā havyavāḍ juhvāsya ity abhirūpā ||
children.translated_text: "By <s>Agni</s>, <s>Agni</s> is kindled, the seer, the young householder, the carrier of oblations, with the ladle as his mouth" is corresponding in form.

children.text: yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: What is corresponding in form in the sacrifice is successful.

children.text: tvaṃ hy agne agninā vipro vipreṇa san sateti ||
children.translated_text: "For you, O <s>Agni</s>, are kindled by <s>Agni</s>, a sage by a sage, being by what is."

children.text: vipra itaro vipra itaraḥ sann itaraḥ sann itaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The one is a sage, the other is a sage; the one is being, the other is being.

children.text: sakhā sakhyā samidhyasa ity eṣa ha vā asya svaḥ sakhā yad agnir agneḥ ||
children.translated_text: "You are kindled as friend by friend"; this indeed is his own friend, namely the fire that belongs to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: tam marjayanta sukratum puroyāvānam ājiṣu sveṣu kṣayeṣu vājinam iti ||
children.translated_text: "They cleanse that one of good skill, going before in battles, the steed in his own abodes."

children.text: eṣa ha vā asya svaḥ kṣayo yad agnir agneḥ ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is his own abode, namely the fire that belongs to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yajñena yajñam ayajanta devā ity uttamayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse, "By sacrifice the gods sacrificed the sacrifice," he encloses it.

children.text: yajñena vai tad devā yajñam ayajanta yad agnināgnim ayajanta te svargaṃ lokam āyan ||
children.translated_text: For by sacrifice the gods sacrificed the sacrifice when they sacrificed <s>Agni</s> with <s>Agni</s>; they went to the heavenly world.

children.text: tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan te ha nākam mahimānaḥ sacanta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devā iti ||
children.translated_text: "Those were the first <s>dharmas</s>; those powers reached the firmament, where the former <s>Sādhya</s> gods are."

children.text: chandāṃsi vai sādhyā devās te 'gre 'gnināgnim ayajanta te svargaṃ lokam āyan ||
children.translated_text: The metres are the <s>Sādhya</s> gods. In the beginning they sacrificed <s>Agni</s> with <s>Agni</s>; they went to the heavenly world.

children.text: ādityāś caivehāsann aṅgirasaś ca te 'gre 'gnināgnim ayajanta te svargaṃ lokam āyan ||
children.translated_text: And the <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Aṅgirases</s> were here. In the beginning they sacrificed <s>Agni</s> with <s>Agni</s>; they went to the heavenly world.

children.text: saiṣā svargyāhutir yad agnyāhutir yadi ha vā apy abrāhmaṇokto yadi duruktokto yajate 'tha haiṣāhutir gacchaty eva devān na pāpmanā saṃsṛjyate ||
children.translated_text: This is a heavenly oblation, namely the oblation to <s>Agni</s>. If one sacrifices even when it has been uttered by one not instructed as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or if it has been badly uttered, then this oblation still goes to the gods and is not joined with evil.

children.text: gacchaty asyāhutir devān nāsyāhutiḥ pāpmanā saṃsṛjyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: His oblation goes to the gods; his oblation is not joined with evil, who knows thus.

children.text: tā etās trayodaśānvāha rūpasamṛddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These thirteen he recites after; they are complete in form.

children.text: etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: For this is the prosperity of the sacrifice: that it is complete in form, when a verse speaks in accord with the rite that is being performed.

children.text: tāsāṃ triḥ prathamām anvāha trir uttamāṃ tāḥ saptadaśa sampadyante saptadaśo vai prajāpatir dvādaśa māsāḥ pañcartavas tāvān saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of them he recites the first three times and the last three times; they amount to seventeen. <s>Prajāpati</s> is seventeenfold: twelve months and five seasons; such is the year. The year is <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: prajāpatyāyatanābhir evābhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: With supports belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s> he prospers in these, who knows thus.

children.text: triḥ prathamāṃ trir uttamām anvāha yajñasyaiva tad barsau nahyati sthemne balāyāvisraṃsāya ||
children.translated_text: He recites the first three times and the last three times; thereby he binds the two flanks of the sacrifice itself, for firmness, strength, and non-collapse.

children.text: Chapter 17
samidhāgniṃ duvasyat ā pyāyasva sam etu ta ity ājyabhāgayoḥ puronuvākye bhavata ātithyavatyau rūpasamṛddhe ||
children.translated_text: "Attend upon <s>Agni</s> with fuel" and "Swell up; let them come together" are the invitatory verses for the two <s>ājyabhāga</s> portions. They have the character of hospitality and are complete in form.

children.text: etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yadrūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: For this is the prosperity of the sacrifice: that it is complete in form, when a verse speaks in accord with the rite that is being performed.

children.text: saiṣāgneyy atithimatī na saumyātithimaty asti yat saumyātithimatī syācchaśvat sā syāt ||
children.translated_text: This verse to <s>Agni</s> has the character of a guest; there is no Soma-verse that has the character of a guest. If there were one to <s>Soma</s> with the character of a guest, it would be permanent.

children.text: etat tv evaiṣātithimatī yad āpīnavatī ||
children.translated_text: But this one here has the character of a guest precisely because it contains the idea of being filled up.

children.text: yadā vā atithim pariveviṣaty āpīna iva vai sa tarhi bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For when one wishes to wait upon a guest, at that time he becomes, as it were, filled up.

children.text: tayor juṣāṇenaiva yajati ||
children.translated_text: For those two he sacrifices with the verse containing "being well pleased."

children.text: idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame tad asya priyam abhi pātho aśyām iti vaiṣṇavyau ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Viṣṇu</s> strode out this world" and "May we attain that dear path of his" are the two verses to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tripadām anūcya catuṣpadayā yajati ||
children.translated_text: After reciting a three-footed verse, he sacrifices with a four-footed one.

children.text: sapta padāni bhavanti śiro vā etad yajñasya yad ātithyaṃ sapta vai śīrṣan prāṇāḥ śīrṣann eva tat prāṇān dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: There are seven feet. This Ātithya offering is the head of the sacrifice, and there are seven breaths in the head; thereby he places the breaths in the head.

children.text: hotāraṃ citraratham adhvarasya pra prāyam agnir bharatasya śṛṇva iti sviṣṭakṛtaḥ saṃyājye bhavata ātithyavatyau rūpasamṛddhe etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: "The <s>hotṛ</s>, the bright-charioted one of the rite" and "May <s>Agni</s> hear the advance of <s>Bharata</s>" are the two <s>saṃyājya</s> verses for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. They have the character of hospitality and are complete in form. This indeed is the prosperity of the sacrifice: that it is complete in form, when a verse speaks in accord with the rite that is being performed.

children.text: triṣṭubhau bhavataḥ sendriyatvāya ||
children.translated_text: They are two <s>triṣṭubh</s> verses, for possession of Indra-like power.

children.text: iﾱāntam bhavatīﾱāntena vā etena devā arādhnuvan yad ātithyaṃ tasmād iﾱāntam eva kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: It ends with <s>Iḍā</s>; for by this ending with <s>Iḍā</s> the gods prospered, namely by the Ātithya offering. Therefore it should indeed be made to end with <s>Iḍā</s>.

children.text: prayājān evātra yajanti nānuyājān ||
children.translated_text: Here they sacrifice only the fore-offerings; they do not sacrifice the after-offerings.

children.text: prāṇā vai prayājānuyājās te ya ime śīrṣan prāṇās te prayājā ye 'vāñcas te 'nuyājāḥ sa yo 'trānuyājān yajed yathemān prāṇān ālupya śīrṣan dhitset tādṛk tat ||
children.translated_text: The fore-offerings and after-offerings are breaths. Those breaths that are here in the head are the fore-offerings; those that are downward are the after-offerings. If one were to sacrifice the after-offerings here, it would be as if he tore out these breaths and set them in the head.

children.text: atiriktaṃ tat sam u vā ime prāṇā vidre ye ceme ye ceme ||
children.translated_text: That would be excessive; moreover these breaths would be scattered, both these and those.

children.text: tad yad evātra prayājān yajanti nānuyājāṃs tatra sa kāma upāpto yo 'nuyājeṣu yo 'nuyājeṣu ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in that they sacrifice only the fore-offerings here and not the after-offerings, that desire is attained here which belongs to the after-offerings, which belongs to the after-offerings.

children.text: Chapter 18

yajño vai devebhya udakrāman na vo 'ham annam bhaviṣyāmīti neti devā abruvann annam eva no bhaviṣyasīti taṃ devā vimethire sa haibhyo vihṛto na prababhūva te hocur devā na vai na itthaṃ vihṛto 'lam bhaviṣyati hantemaṃ yajñaṃ saṃbharāmeti tatheti taṃ saṃjabhruḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice went away from the gods, saying, "I will not be food for you." "No," said the gods, "you shall indeed be food for us." The gods divided it up; when divided up, it did not suffice for them. The gods said, "Divided in this way, it will not be enough for us. Come, let us gather this sacrifice together." "So be it," they said, and they gathered it together.

children.text: taṃ saṃbhṛtyocur aśvināv imam bhiṣajyatam ity aśvinau vai devānām bhiṣajāv aśvināv adhvaryū tasmād adhvaryū gharmaṃ saṃbharataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having gathered it together, they said, "O <s>Aśvins</s>, heal this." The <s>Aśvins</s> are the physicians of the gods, and the <s>adhvaryu</s>s are the <s>Aśvins</s>; therefore the <s>adhvaryu</s>s gather together the <s>gharma</s>.

children.text: taṃ saṃbhṛtyāhatur brahman pravargyeṇa pracariṣyāmo hotar abhiṣṭuhīti ||
children.translated_text: Having gathered it together, they said, "O <s>brahman</s>, we will proceed with the <s>Pravargya</s>; O <s>hotṛ</s>, praise it."

children.text: Chapter 19
brahma jajñānam prathamam purastād iti pratipadyate brahma vai bṛhaspatir brahmaṇaivainaṃ tad bhiṣajyati ||
children.translated_text: He begins with "Brahman was born first in the east." <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is brahman; by brahman itself he thereby heals it.

children.text: iyaṃ vai pitre rāṣṭry ety agra iti vāgvai rāṣṭrī vācam evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: "This sovereign one goes first to her father": speech is the sovereign one; thereby he places speech in it.

children.text: mahān mahī astabhāyad vi jāta iti brāhmaṇaspatyā brahma vai bṛhaspatir brahmaṇaivainaṃ tad bhiṣajyati ||
children.translated_text: "The great one has propped up the great one as it was born" is a verse belonging to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is brahman; by brahman itself he thereby heals it.

children.text: abhi tyaṃ devaṃ savitāram oṇyor iti sāvitrī prāṇo vai savitā prāṇam evāsmiṃstad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: "Toward that god <s>Savitṛ</s> between the two laps" is a verse to <s>Savitṛ</s>. <s>Savitṛ</s> is breath; thereby he places breath in it.

children.text: saṃ sīdasva mahāṁ asīty evainaṃ samasādayan ||
children.translated_text: With "Sit down together; you are great," they set it together in just this way.

children.text: añjanti yam prathayanto na viprā ity ajyamānāyābhirūpā yad yajñe 'bhirūpam tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: "They anoint him, spreading him out like inspired priests" is suitable for it as it is being anointed. What is suitable in the sacrifice is prosperous.

children.text: pataṃgam aktam asurasya māyayā yo naḥ sanutyo abhidāsad agne bhavā no agne sumanā upetāv iti dve dve abhirūpe yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: "The bird anointed by the power of the <s>Asura</s>," "Whoever in secret plots against us, O <s>Agni</s>," and "Be gracious to us, O <s>Agni</s>, when approached" are two and two suitable verses. What is suitable in the sacrifice is prosperous.

children.text: kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ prasitiṃ na pṛthvīm iti pañca rākṣoghnyo rakṣasām apahatyai ||
children.translated_text: "Make your force like a snare over the earth" comprises five demon-slaying verses, for driving away the <s>rakṣas</s>es.

children.text: pari tvā girvaṇo giro 'dhi dvayor adadhā ukthyaṃ vacaḥ śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te anyad apaśyaṃ gopām anipadyamānam iti catasra ekapātinyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Around you, O lover of song, the songs," "Upon the two I placed the laudatory word," "Bright is one of your forms, worshipful the other," and "I saw the herdsman who does not fall away" are four single-footed verses.

children.text: tā ekaviṃśatir bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: They become twenty-one.

children.text: ekaviṃśo 'yam puruṣo daśa hastyā aṅgulayo daśa pādyā ātmaikaviṃśas tam imam ātmānam ekaviṃśaṃ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: This person here is twenty-onefold: ten fingers on the hands, ten on the feet, and the self as the twenty-first. Thus he prepares this very self as twenty-onefold.

children.text: Chapter 20
srakve drapsasya dhamataḥ sam asvarann iti nava pāvamānyo nava vai prāṇāḥ prāṇān evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the verse, "The two srakvas sounded together as the drop was blown," there are nine <s>Pāvamānī</s> verses. The breaths are indeed nine; thereby he places the breaths in him.

children.text: ayaṃ venaś codayat pṛśnigarbhā iti ||
children.translated_text: With the verse, "This <s>Vena</s> has impelled the dappled-wombed ones."

children.text: ayaṃ vai veno 'smād vā ūrdhvā anye prāṇā venanty avāñco 'nye tasmād venaḥ prāṇo vā ayaṃ san nābher iti tasmān nābhis tan nābher nābhitvaṃ prāṇam evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: This one is indeed <s>Vena</s>. From this one some breaths go upward, and others downward; therefore he is <s>Vena</s>. Since this, being breath, is said to be "from the navel," therefore there is the navel; that is the navelhood of the navel. Thereby he places breath in him.

children.text: pavitraṃ te vitatam brahmaṇaspate tapoṣ pavitraṃ vitataṃ divas pade vi yat pavitraṃ dhiṣaṇā atanvateti pūtavantaḥ prāṇās ta ime 'vāñco retasyo mūtryaḥ purīṣya ity etān evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With "Your purifier is stretched out, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>; the purifier born of heat is stretched in heaven's station; the purifier which <s>Dhiṣaṇā</s> stretched out," the breaths are purified. These downward ones, namely the seminal, urinary, and fecal ones, he thereby places in him.

children.text: Chapter 21
gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ havāmaha iti brāhmaṇaspatyam brahma vai bṛhaspatir brahmaṇaivainam tad bhiṣajyati ||
children.translated_text: With "We invoke you as lord of the groups, lord of groups," the verse is addressed to <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the <s>brahman</s> (sacred formulation); by the <s>brahman</s> itself he heals him.

children.text: prathaś ca yasya saprathaś ca nāmeti gharmatanvaḥ satanum evainaṃ tat sarūpaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: With "Of whom Expansion and Wide-extension are the names," the bodies of the <s>gharma</s> are meant; thereby he makes him embodied and of corresponding form.

children.text: rathaṃtaram ājabhārā vasiṣṭhaḥ bharadvājo bṛhad ā cakre agner iti bṛhadrathantaravantam evainaṃ tat karoti ||
children.translated_text: With "<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> brought the <s>Rathantara</s>; <s>Bharadvāja</s> fashioned the <s>Bṛhat</s> from <s>Agni</s>," he thereby makes him possessed of both the <s>Bṛhat</s> and the <s>Rathantara</s>.

children.text: apaśyaṃ tvā manasā cekitānam iti prajāvān prājāpatyaḥ prajām evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With "I saw you with my mind, discerning," it is possessed of offspring and belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>; thereby he places offspring in him.

children.text: kā rādhaddhotrāśvinā vām iti nava vichandasas tad etad yajñasyāntastyaṃ vikṣudram iva vā antastyam aṇīya iva ca sthavīya iva ca tasmād etā vichandaso bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: With "Which priestly office has prospered for you two, O <s>Aśvins</s>?" there are nine verses in irregular meters. This is the inner part of the sacrifice. The inner part is as though minute, both more slender and more massive; therefore these verses are in irregular meters.

children.text: etābhir hāśvinoḥ kakṣīvān priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchat sa paramaṃ lokam ajayat ||
children.translated_text: With these verses <s>Kakṣīvān</s> approached the dear abode of the two <s>Aśvins</s>, and he won the highest world.

children.text: upāśvinoḥ priyaṃ dhāma gacchati jayati paramaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He approaches the dear abode of the two <s>Aśvins</s> and wins the highest world, he who knows thus.

children.text: ābhāti agnir uṣasām anīkam iti sūktam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn begins, "<s>Agni</s> shines forth, the face of the dawns."

children.text: pīpivāṃsam aśvinā gharmam acchety abhirūpaṃ yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: With "O <s>Aśvins</s>, come to the swollen <s>gharma</s>," it is appropriate in form; what is appropriate in form in the sacrifice is successful.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ vīryaṃ vai triṣṭub vīryam evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is vigor; thereby he places vigor in him.

children.text: grāvāṇeva tad id arthaṃ jarethe iti sūktam akṣī iva karṇāv iva nāsevety aṅgasamākhyāyam evāsmiṃs tad indriyāṇi dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: The hymn begins, "Like two pressing stones you two grow old for this purpose." With expressions such as "like the eyes, like the ears, like the nose," by the naming of the limbs he thereby places the faculties in him.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ vīryaṃ vai triṣṭub vīryam evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
