children.translated_text: That, moreover, is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is vigor; thereby he places vigor in him.

children.text: īﾱe dyāvāpṛthivī pūrvacittaya iti sūktam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn begins, "I praise Heaven and Earth, foreknowing from of old."

children.text: agniṃ gharmaṃ surucaṃ yāmann iṣṭaya ity abhirūpaṃ yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: With "<s>Agni</s>, the <s>gharma</s>, bright, at the courses for the offerings," it is appropriate in form; what is appropriate in form in the sacrifice is successful.

children.text: tad u jāgataṃ jāgatā vai paśavaḥ paśūn evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is in the <s>Jagatī</s> meter. Animals are connected with the <s>Jagatī</s>; thereby he places cattle in him.

children.text: yābhir amum āvataṃ yābhir amum āvatam ity etāvato hātrāśvinau kāmān dadṛśatus tān evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti tair evainaṃ tat samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: With "By those powers with which you aided that one, by those with which you aided that one," the two <s>Aśvins</s> saw just so many desires. Those very desires he places in him; with those he prospers him.

children.text: arūrucad uṣasaḥ pṛśnir agriya iti rucitavatī rucam evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With "The foremost dappled one has made the dawns shine," it contains shining; thereby he places radiance in him.

children.text: dyubhir aktubhiḥ pari pātam asmān ity uttamayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse, "With days and nights protect us all around," he encloses him.

children.text: ariṣṭebhir aśvinā saubhagebhiḥ tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyaur ity etair evainaṃ tat kāmaiḥ samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: With "With unharmed good fortunes, O <s>Aśvins</s>; may <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, Earth, and Heaven not injure us," he thereby prospers him with these desires.

children.text: iti nu pūrvam paṭalam ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the preceding <s>paṭala</s>.

children.text: Chapter 22
athottaram ||
children.translated_text: Now the following one begins.

children.text: upa hvaye sudughāṃ dhenum etāṃ hiṃkṛṇvatī vasupatnī vasūnām abhi tvā deva savitaḥ sam ī vatsaṃ na mātṛbhiḥ saṃ vatsa iva mātṛbhir yas te stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūr gaur amīmed anu vatsam miṣantaṃ namased upa sīdata saṃjānānā upa sīdann abhijñv ā daśabhir vivasvato duhanti saptaikāṃ samiddho agnir aśvinā samiddho agnir vṛṣaṇāratir divas tad u prayakṣatamam asya karmātmanvan nabho duhyate ghṛtam paya ut tiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate 'dhukṣat pipyuṣīm iṣam upa dravapayasā godhug oṣam ā sute siñcata śriyam ā nūnam aśvinor ṛṣiḥ sam u tye mahatīr apa ity ekaviṃśatir abhirūpā yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: The twenty-one appropriate verses are: "I call near this good-milking cow"; "lowing, mistress of goods among goods"; "toward you, O god <s>Savitṛ</s>"; "together, like a calf with its mothers"; "together, like a calf with its mothers"; "that breast of yours which lies ready, which brings delight"; "the cow bellowed after the blinking calf"; "sit near with homage"; "coming to know, they sat near, bending the knee"; "with ten the seven milk the one belonging to <s>Vivasvat</s>"; "<s>Agni</s> has been kindled, O <s>Aśvins</s>"; "<s>Agni</s> has been kindled, the bull-like gift of heaven"; "that indeed is the most fit offering of this rite"; "from the cloud are milked ghee and milk"; "rise up, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>"; "he has milked the swelling refreshment"; "come near with flowing milk, O milker of cows, swiftly"; "pour splendor upon the pressed draught"; "now the seer of the two <s>Aśvins</s>"; and "together those great waters." What is appropriate in form in the sacrifice is successful.

children.text: ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayety anūttiṣṭhati praitu brahmaṇaspatir ity anupraiti gandharva itthā padam asya rakṣatīti kharam avekṣate nāke suparṇam upa yat patantam ity upaviśati tapto vāṃ gharmo nakṣati svahotobhā pibatam aśvineti pūrvāhṇe yajati ||
children.translated_text: After "Up has risen that god <s>Savitṛ</s> with his golden one," he stands up. After "Let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forward," he goes forward. With "The <s>Gandharva</s> thus guards his track," he looks at the <s>khara</s> mound. With "As the eagle flying up to the firmament," he sits down. With "The heated <s>gharma</s> reaches you, well-offered; drink, both of you, O <s>Aśvins</s>," he sacrifices in the forenoon.

children.text: agne vīhīty anuvaṣaṭkaroti sviṣṭakṛdbhājanam ||
children.translated_text: With "O <s>Agni</s>, go," he makes the subsequent <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call; it is the portion for <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.

children.text: yad usriyāsv āhutaṃ ghṛtam payo 'sya pibatam aśvinety aparāhṇe yajaty agne vīhīty anuvaṣaṭkaroti sviṣṭakṛdbhājanam ||
children.translated_text: With "Drink the ghee and milk that has been offered among the cows, O <s>Aśvins</s>," he sacrifices in the afternoon. With "O <s>Agni</s>, go," he makes the subsequent <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call; it is the portion for <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.

children.text: trayāṇāṃ ha vai haviṣāṃ sviṣṭakṛte na samavadyanti somasya gharmasya vājinasyeti sa yad anuvaṣaṭkaroty agner eva sviṣṭakṛto 'nantarityai ||
children.translated_text: For three oblations they do not cut out a share for <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>: for <s>Soma</s>, for the <s>gharma</s>, and for the <s>vājina</s>. When he makes the subsequent <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call, it is for unbroken continuity with <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.

children.text: viśvā āśā dakṣiṇasād iti brahmā japati ||
children.translated_text: With "All the quarters, sitting on the southern side," the <s>brahman</s> priest mutters.

children.text: svāhākṛtaḥ śucir deveṣu gharmaḥ samudrād ūrmim ud iyarti veno drapsaḥ samudram abhi yaj jigāti sakhe sakhāyam abhy ā vavṛtsvordhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaya ūrdhvo naḥ pāhy aṃhasas taṃ ghem itthā namasvina ity abhirūpā yad yajñe'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: "Offered with svāhā, pure among the gods is the <s>gharma</s> (hot offering). From the ocean <s>Vena</s> sends up the wave; the drop goes toward the ocean. O friend, turn toward your friend. Stand upright now for our aids; standing upright protect us from distress. Thus may we have him, reverent." These verses are suited in form; whatever in the sacrifice is suited in form is thereby successful.

children.text: pāvakaśoce tava hi kṣayam parīti bhakṣam ākāṅkṣate ||
children.translated_text: With "O you of purifying flame, for your dwelling is round about," he looks forward to the portion to be consumed.

children.text: hutaṃ havir madhu havir indratame 'gnāv aśyāma te deva gharma madhumataḥ pitumato vājavato 'ṅgirasvato namas te astu mā mā hiṃsīr iti gharmasya bhakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: With "The oblation has been offered; honey is the oblation. O most <s>Indra</s>-like one, in <s>Agni</s> may we partake of you, O divine <s>gharma</s>, rich in honey, rich in milk, rich in vigor, rich in <s>Aṅgirases</s>. Homage be to you; do not harm me," he consumes the <s>gharma</s>.

children.text: śyeno na yoniṃ sadanaṃ dhiyā kṛtam ā yasmin sapta vāsavā iti saṃsādyamānāyānvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites over it as it is being placed, "Like an eagle to the womb, to the seat made by thought, in which are the seven <s>Vasus</s>."

children.text: havir haviṣmo mahi sadma daivyam iti yad ahar utsādayiṣyanto bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: When they are about to raise it on that day, he recites, "The oblation-bearing one, the great divine seat."

children.text: sūyavasād bhagavatī hi bhūyā ity uttamayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse, "May she become rich in good pasture, for she is blessed," he encloses it.

children.text: tad etad devamithunaṃ yad gharmaḥ sa yo gharmas tacchiśnaṃ yau śaphau tau śaphau yopayamanī te śroṇikapāle yat payas tad retas tad idam agnau devayonyām prajanane retaḥ sicyate 'gnir vai devayoniḥ so 'gner devayonyā āhutibhyaḥ sambhavati ||
children.translated_text: This <s>gharma</s> is a divine pair. The <s>gharma</s> is the penis; the two śaphas are the two śaphas; the two upayamanī vessels are the two hip-bowls; the milk is semen. This semen is poured into <s>Agni</s>, the divine womb, the place of generation. <s>Agni</s> is the divine womb; therefore it comes into being from <s>Agni</s>'s divine womb, from the oblations.

children.text: ṛṅmayo yajurmayaḥ sāmamayo vedamayo brahmamayo 'mṛtamayaḥ sambhūya devatā apyeti ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvānetena yajñakratunā yajate ||
children.translated_text: Made of ṛc-verses, made of yajus-formulas, made of sāmans, made of the Veda, made of brahman, made of immortality, it comes into being and goes to the deities: he who knows thus, and who, knowing thus, sacrifices with this sacrificial rite.

children.text: Chapter 23

devāsurā vā eṣu lokeṣu samayatanta te vā asurā imān eva lokān puro 'kurvata yathaujīyāṃso balīyāṃsa evaṃ te vā ayasmayīm evemām akurvata rajatām antarikṣaṃ hariṇīṃ divaṃ te tathemāṃllokān puro 'kurvata te devā abruvan puro vā ime 'surā imāṃllokān akrata pura imāṃllokān pratikaravāmahā iti tatheti te sada evāsyāḥ pratyakurvatāgnīdhram antarikṣāddhavirdhāne divas te tathemāṃllokān puraḥ pratyakurvata ||
children.translated_text: The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> contended in these worlds. The <s>Asuras</s> made these very worlds into forts, as the stronger and more powerful would do: they made this earth of iron, the midspace of silver, and heaven golden. Thus they made these worlds into forts. The gods said, "The <s>Asuras</s> have made these worlds into forts. Let us make counter-forts against these worlds." "So be it," they said. From the earth they made the sadas as a counter-fort, from the midspace the agnīdhra, and from heaven the havirdhāna. Thus they made counter-forts against these worlds.

children.text: te devā abruvann upasada upāyāmopasadā vai mahāpuraṃ jayantīti tatheti te yām eva prathamām upasadam upāyaṃs tayaivainān asmāllokād anudanta yāṃ dvitīyāṃ tayāntarikṣād yāṃ tṛtīyāṃ tayā divas tāṃstathaibhyo lokebhyo 'nudanta ||
children.translated_text: The gods said, "Let us approach the <s>upasads</s>; by an <s>upasad</s> one conquers a great fort." "So be it," they said. With the first <s>upasad</s> that they approached, they drove them out from this world; with the second, from the midspace; with the third, from heaven. Thus they drove them out from these worlds.

children.text: te vā ebhyo lokebhyo nuttā asurā ṛtūn aśrayanta te devā abruvann upasada evopāyāmeti tatheti ta imās tisraḥ satīr upasado dvir dvir ekaikām upāyaṃs tāḥ ṣaṭ samapadyanta ṣaḍ vā ṛtavas tān vā ṛtubhyo 'nudanta ||
children.translated_text: Driven out from these worlds, the <s>Asuras</s> resorted to the seasons. The gods said, "Let us approach the <s>upasads</s> again." "So be it," they said. Though these <s>upasads</s> were three, they approached each one twice; they became six. There are six seasons, and they drove them out from the seasons.

children.text: te vā ṛtubhyo nuttā asurā māsān aśrayanta te devā abruvann upasada evopāyāmeti tatheti ta imāḥ ṣaṭ satīrupasado dvir dvir ekaikām upāyaṃs tā dvādaśa samapadyanta dvādaśa vai māsas tān vai māsebhyo 'nudanta ||
children.translated_text: Driven out from the seasons, the <s>Asuras</s> resorted to the months. The gods said, "Let us approach the <s>upasads</s> again." "So be it," they said. Though these <s>upasads</s> were six, they approached each one twice; they became twelve. There are twelve months, and they drove them out from the months.

children.text: te vai māsebhyo nuttā asurā ardhamāsān aśrayanta te devā abruvann upasada evopāyāmeti tatheti ta imā dvādaśa satīr upasado dvir dvir ekaikām upāyaṃs tāś caturviṃśatiḥ samapadyanta caturviṃśatir vā ardhamāsās tān vā ardhamāsebhyo 'nudanta ||
children.translated_text: Driven out from the months, the <s>Asuras</s> resorted to the half-months. The gods said, "Let us approach the <s>upasads</s> again." "So be it," they said. Though these <s>upasads</s> were twelve, they approached each one twice; they became twenty-four. There are twenty-four half-months, and they drove them out from the half-months.

children.text: te vā ardhamāsebhyo nuttā asurā ahorātre aśrayanta te devā abruvann upasadāv evopāyāmeti tatheti te yām eva pūrvāhṇa upasadam upāyaṃs tayaivainān ahno 'nudanta yām aparāhṇe tayā rātres tāṃstathobhābhyām antarāyan ||
children.translated_text: Driven out from the half-months, the <s>Asuras</s> resorted to day and night. The gods said, "Let us approach the two <s>upasads</s>." "So be it," they said. With the <s>upasad</s> that they approached in the forenoon, they drove them out from the day; with the one in the afternoon, from the night. Thus they kept them away from both.

children.text: tasmāt supūrvāhṇa eva pūrvayopasadā pracaritavyaṃ svaparāhṇe 'parayā tāvantameva tad dviṣate lokam pariśinaṣṭi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the first <s>upasad</s> should be performed in a good forenoon, and the later one in a good afternoon. By that he fences off just that much world from the hating rival.

children.text: Chapter 24
jitayo vai nāmaitā yad upasado 'sapatnāṃ vā etābhir devā vijitiṃ vyajayanta ||
children.translated_text: These are indeed called "victories," namely the <s>upasads</s>. With them the gods won an unrivaled conquest.

children.text: asapatnāṃ vijitiṃ vijayate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He wins an unrivaled conquest who knows thus.

children.text: yāṃ devā eṣu lokeṣu yām ṛtuṣu yām māseṣu yām ardhamāseṣu yām ahorātrayor vijitiṃ vyajayanta tāṃ vijitiṃ vijayate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The conquest that the gods won in these worlds, in the seasons, in the months, in the half-months, and in day and night: that conquest he wins who knows thus.

children.text: te devā abibhayur asmākaṃ vipremāṇam anvidam asurā ābhaviṣyantīti te vyutkramyāmantrayantāgnir vasubhir udakrāmad indro rudrair varuṇa ādityair bṛhaspatir viśvair devaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods were afraid: "The <s>Asuras</s>, discovering our separation, will overcome us." Going apart, they took counsel: <s>Agni</s> went out with the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s> with the <s>Ādityas</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> with the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>.

children.text: te tathā vyutkramyāmantrayanta te 'bruvan hanta yā eva na imāḥ priyatamās tanvas tā asya varuṇasya rājño gṛhe saṃnidadhāmahai tābhir eva naḥ sa na saṃgacchātai yo na etad atikrāmād ya ālulobhayiṣād iti tatheti te varuṇasya rājño gṛhe tanūḥ saṃnyadadhata ||
children.translated_text: Having gone apart in this way, they took counsel. They said, "Come, let us deposit in the house of this king <s>Varuṇa</s> those bodies of ours that are dearest. By means of them let him not have fellowship with us, whoever should transgress this agreement of ours, whoever should try to entice us." "So be it," they said, and they deposited their bodies in the house of king <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: te yad varuṇasya rājño gṛhe tanūḥ saṃnyadadhata tat tānūnaptram abhavat tat tānūnaptrasya tānūnaptratvam ||
children.translated_text: Because they deposited their bodies in the house of king <s>Varuṇa</s>, that became the <s>Tānūnaptra</s>. That is the <s>Tānūnaptra</s>-ness of the <s>Tānūnaptra</s>.

children.text: tasmād āhur na satānūnaptriṇe drogdhavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they say, "One must not deal treacherously with one who shares the <s>Tānūnaptra</s> covenant."

children.text: tasmād v idam asurā nānvābhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Asuras</s> do not come to share in this.

children.text: Chapter 25
śiro vā etad yajñasya yad ātithyaṃ grīvā upasadaḥ samānabarhiṣī bhavataḥ samānaṃ hi śirogrīvam ||
children.translated_text: The ātithya (guest-offering) is the head of the sacrifice, and the <s>upasad</s> rites are the neck. They have the same barhis, for head and neck are joined together.

children.text: iṣuṃ vā etāṃ devāḥ samaskurvata yad upasadas tasyā agnir anīkam āsīt somaḥ śalyo viṣṇus tejanaṃ varuṇaḥ parṇāni tām ājyadhanvāno vyasṛjaṃs tayā puro bhindanta āyan ||
children.translated_text: The gods fashioned this arrow, namely the <s>upasad</s> rites: <s>Agni</s> was its point, <s>Soma</s> its barb, <s>Viṣṇu</s> its shaft, and <s>Varuṇa</s> its feathers. They released it with ghee as its bow; with it they went on breaking the strongholds.

children.text: tasmād etā ājyahaviṣo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore these are oblations of ghee.

children.text: caturo 'gre stanān vratam upaity upasatsu catuḥsaṃdhir hīṣur anīkaṃ śalyas tejanam parṇāni ||
children.translated_text: At first he enters upon the vrata (milk-vow) of four teats during the <s>upasad</s> rites; for an arrow has four joints: point, barb, shaft, and feathers.

children.text: trīn stanān vratam upaity upasatsu triṣaṃdhir hīṣur anīkaṃ śalyas tejanaṃ dvau stanau vratam upaity upasatsu dviṣaṃdhir hīṣuḥ śalyaś ca hy eva tejanaṃ caikaṃ stanaṃ vratam upaity upasatsv ekā hy eveṣur ity ākhyāyata ekayā vīryam kriyate ||
children.translated_text: He enters upon the vrata of three teats during the <s>upasad</s> rites, for an arrow has three joints: point, barb, and shaft. He enters upon the vrata of two teats during the <s>upasad</s> rites, for an arrow has two joints, since there are only barb and shaft. He enters upon the vrata of one teat during the <s>upasad</s> rites, for an arrow is said to be one; by one, heroic power is produced.

children.text: paro varīyāṃso vā ime lokā arvāg aṃhīyaṃsaḥ parastād arvācīr upasada upaity eṣām eva lokānām abhijityā ||
children.translated_text: These worlds farther away are broader, and those nearer are narrower. He proceeds through the <s>upasad</s> rites from the far side toward the near side, for the conquest of these very worlds.

children.text: upasadyāya mīﾱhuṣa imām me agne samidham imām upasadaṃ vaner iti tisras tisraḥ sāmidhenyo rūpasamṛddhā etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: For the approachable, bounteous one: This fuel-stick of mine, O <s>Agni</s>, this <s>upasad</s>, may you win. Thus there are three and three sāmidhenī verses, complete in form. That in the sacrifice is indeed successful which is complete in form, when a ṛc addresses the action that is being performed.

children.text: jaghnivatīr yājyānuvākyāḥ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: He should make the yājyā and anuvākyā verses ones that speak of smiting.

children.text: agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanad ya ugra iva śaryahā tvaṃ somāsi satpatir gayasphāno amīvahedaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame trīṇi padā vicakrama ity etāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The verses are these: <s>Agni</s> shall smite the Vṛtras; he who is fierce like an archer; you, <s>Soma</s>, are the true lord, increaser of wealth, remover of disease; this <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode out, he strode out in three steps.

children.text: viparyastābhir aparāhṇe yajati ||
children.translated_text: In the afternoon he sacrifices with them in reversed order.

children.text: ghnanto vā etābhir devāḥ puro bhindanta āyan yad upasadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For with these, while smiting, the gods went on breaking the strongholds, namely with the <s>upasad</s> rites.

children.text: sachandasaḥ kartavyā na vichandasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should be made metrical, not unmetrical.

children.text: yad vichandasaḥ kuryād grīvāsu tad gaṇḍaṃ dadhyād īśvaro glāvo janitoḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he were to make them unmetrical, he would set a swelling upon the necks; a tumor would be liable to arise.

children.text: tasmāt sachandasa eva kartavyā na vichandasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they should be made metrical, not unmetrical.

children.text: tad u ha smāhopāvir jānaśruteya upasadāṃ kila vai tad brāhmaṇe yasmād apy aślīlasya śrotriyasya mukhaṃ vy eva jñāyate tṛptam iva rebhatīvety ājyahaviṣo hy upasado grīvāsu mukhamadhyāhitaṃ tasmāddha sma tad āha ||
children.translated_text: Concerning this, <s>Upāvir Jānaśruteya</s> used to say: It is indeed stated in the brāhmaṇa of the <s>upasad</s> rites why even the face of an indecorous śrotriya is clearly recognized, as if satisfied and bleating. For the <s>upasad</s> rites are oblations of ghee, and the face is placed in the middle of the necks; therefore he used to say this.

children.text: Chapter 26
devavarma vā etad yat prayājāś cānuyājāś cāprayājam ananuyājam bhavatīṣvai saṃśityā apratiśarāya ||
children.translated_text: This is divine armor, namely the prayājas and anuyājas. It is without prayāja and without anuyāja for the sharpening of the arrow and so that there may be no opposing missile.

children.text: sakṛd atikramyāśrāvayati yajñasyābhikrāntyā anapakramāya ||
children.translated_text: Having stepped past once, he has the call to hear made, for the advance of the sacrifice and so that there may be no retreat.

children.text: tad āhuḥ krūram iva vā etat somasya rājño 'nte caranti yad asya ghṛtenānte caranti ghṛtena hi vajreṇendro vṛtram ahan ||
children.translated_text: They say: This is rather cruel treatment at the end of King <s>Soma</s>, that they act at his end with ghee; for with ghee as the thunderbolt <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>.

children.text: tad yad aṃśur aṃśuṣ ṭe deva somāpyāyatām indrāyaikadhanavida ā tubhyam indraḥ pyāyatām ā tvam indrāya pyāyasvā pyāyayāsmān sakhīn sanyā medhayā svasti te deva soma sutyām udṛcam aśīyeti rājānam āpyāyayanti yad evāsya tat krūram ivānte caranti tad evāsyaitenāpyāyayanty atho enaṃ vardhayanty eva ||
children.translated_text: When they say, O shoot, may your shoot, O god <s>Soma</s>, swell for <s>Indra</s>, finder of the single treasure; may <s>Indra</s> swell for you; may you swell for <s>Indra</s>; make us, your companions, swell together with insight; welfare to you, god <s>Soma</s>; may I attain the end of the pressing, they cause the king to swell. Whatever cruel treatment they perform at his end, by this they cause just that in him to swell; and they also increase him.

children.text: dyāvāpṛthivyor vā eṣa garbho yat somo rājā tad yad eṣṭā rāya eṣṭā vāmāni preṣe bhagāya ṛtam ṛtavādibhyo namo dive namaḥ pṛthivyā iti prastare nihnavate dyāvāpṛthivībhyām eva tan namaskurvanty atho ene vardhayanty eva vardhayanty eva ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Soma</s> is the embryo of heaven and earth. When, on the prastara grass, they bow down with the words, You are the seeker of wealth, the seeker of desirable things; at the sending for <s>Bhaga</s>; homage to truth and to the speakers of truth; homage to heaven, homage to earth, they thereby pay homage to heaven and earth, and they also increase them; they increase them indeed.

children.text: Chapter 27

somo vai rājā gandharveṣv āsīt taṃ devāś ca ṛṣayaś cābhyadhyāyan katham ayam asmān somo rājā gacched iti sā vāg abravīt strīkāmā vai gandharvā mayaiva striyā bhūtayā paṇadhvam iti neti devā abruvan kathaṃ vayaṃ tvad ṛte syāmeti sābravīt krīṇītaiva yarhi vāva vo mayārtho bhavitā tarhyeva vo 'ham punar āgantāsmīti tatheti tayā mahānagnyā bhūtayā somaṃ rājānam akrīṇan ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Soma</s> was among the Gandharvas. The gods and the seers pondered him, asking how this King <s>Soma</s> might come to them. Then <s>Vāc</s> said: The Gandharvas desire women; bargain with me when I have become a woman. No, said the gods, how could we be without you? She said: Buy him; whenever you have need of me, then I shall come back to you. So be it, they said. With her, when she had become a great naked woman, they bought King <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: tām anukṛtim askannāṃ vatsatarīm ājanti somakrayaṇīṃ tayā somaṃ rājānāṃ krīṇanti ||
children.translated_text: In imitation of her they anoint an unspilled young cow, the soma-purchase cow; with her they buy King <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: tām punar niṣkrīṇīyāt punar hi sā tān āgacchat ||
children.translated_text: He should buy her back again, for she did come back to them.

children.text: tasmād upāṃśu vācā caritavyaṃ some rājani krīte gandharveṣu hi tarhi vāg bhavati sāgnāv eva praṇīyamāne punar āgacchati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should move with speech kept low after King <s>Soma</s> has been bought; for at that time <s>Vāc</s> is among the Gandharvas. She comes back only when <s>Agni</s> is being led forward.

children.text: Chapter 28
agnaye praṇīyamānāyānubrūhīty āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The adhvaryu says: Recite for <s>Agni</s> as he is being led forward.

children.text: pra devaṃ devyā dhiyā bharatā jātavedasam havyā no vakṣad ānuṣag iti gāyatrīm brāhmaṇasyānubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: For a brāhmaṇa he should recite the Gāyatrī: Bring forth the god <s>Jātavedas</s> with divine thought; he shall carry our oblations continually.

children.text: gāyatro vai brāhmaṇas tejo vai brahmavarcasaṃ gāyatrī tejasaivainaṃ tad brahmavarcasena samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: The brāhmaṇa is Gāyatrī-metrical; Gāyatrī is brilliance and brahmavarcasa (sacred lustre). By brilliance and by brahmavarcasa he prospers him.

children.text: imam mahe vidathyāya śūṣam iti triṣṭubhaṃ rājanyasyānubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: For a rājanya he should recite the Triṣṭubh: This mighty praise for the great assembly.

children.text: traiṣṭubho vai rājanya ojo vā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ triṣṭub ojasaivainaṃ tad indriyeṇa vīryeṇa samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: The rājanya is Triṣṭubh-metrical; strength, faculty, and heroic power are Triṣṭubh. By strength, faculty, and heroic power he prospers him.

children.text: śaśvat kṛtva īḍyāya pra jabhruriti ||
children.translated_text: Again and again they have borne him forth for the praiseworthy one.

children.text: svānām evainaṃ tacchraiṣṭhyaṃ gamayati ||
children.translated_text: By that he brings him to preeminence among his own people.

children.text: śṛṇotu no damyebhir anīkaiḥ śṛṇotv agnir divyair ajasra iti ||
children.translated_text: "May he hear us with the domestic fronts; may <s>Agni</s> hear with the heavenly, unceasing ones."

children.text: ājarasaṃ hāsminn ajasro dīdāya ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For the one who knows thus, the unceasing one shines in him until old age.

children.text: ayam iha prathamo dhāyi dhātṛbhir iti jagatīṃ vaiśyasyānubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: For a <s>Vaiśya</s> he should recite the <s>jagatī</s> verse, "This one here was set down first by the establishers."

children.text: jāgato vai vaiśyo jāgatāḥ paśavaḥ paśubhir evainaṃ tat samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśya</s> is connected with the <s>jagatī</s>; cattle are connected with the <s>jagatī</s>. By cattle he thereby makes him prosper.

children.text: vaneṣu citraṃ vibhvaṃ viśe viśa ity abhirūpā yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: "Bright in the forests, wide-spreading, for clan after clan" is corresponding in form. What is corresponding in form in the sacrifice is successful.

children.text: ayam u ṣya pra devayur iti ||
children.translated_text: "This one here, going forth godward."

children.text: anuṣṭubhi vācaṃ visṛjate ||
children.translated_text: With an <s>anuṣṭubh</s> verse he releases speech.

children.text: vāg vā anuṣṭub vācyeva tad vācaṃ visṛjate ||
children.translated_text: For speech is the <s>anuṣṭubh</s>; in speech itself he thereby releases speech.

children.text: ayam u ṣya iti yad āhāyam u syāgamaṃ yā purā gandharveṣv avāksam ity eva tad vāk prabrūte ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "This one here," speech thereby declares, "I have come to this one here, I who formerly spoke among the <s>Gandharvas</s>."

children.text: ayam agnir uruṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: "This <s>Agni</s> protects broadly."

children.text: ayaṃ vā agnir uruṣyati ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Agni</s> indeed protects broadly.

children.text: amṛtād iva janmana ity amṛtatvam evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: By "as if from an immortal birth" he thereby places immortality in him.

children.text: sahasaś cit sahīyān devo jīvātave kṛta iti ||
children.translated_text: "A god, stronger even than force, made for living."

children.text: devo hy eṣa etaj jīvātave kṛto yad agniḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this god, namely <s>Agni</s>, is made for living.

children.text: iﾱāyās tvā pade vayaṃ nābhā pṛthivyā adhīti ||
children.translated_text: "At the place of <s>Iḍā</s>, at the navel of the earth, we set you down."

children.text: etad vā iﾱāyās padaṃ yad uttaravedīnābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That indeed is the place of <s>Iḍā</s>, namely the navel of the northern altar.

children.text: jātavedo ni dhīmahīti nidhāsyanto hy enaṃ bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: By "O <s>Jātavedas</s>, we set you down," for they are about to set him down.

children.text: agne havyāya voﾱhava iti havyaṃ hi vakṣyan bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By "O <s>Agni</s>, to carry the oblations," for he is about to carry the oblation.

children.text: agne viśvebhiḥ svanīka devair ūrṇāvantam prathamaḥ sīda yonim iti ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Agni</s> of fair front, with all the gods, sit first in the woolly womb."

children.text: viśvair evainaṃ taddevaiḥ sahāsādayati ||
children.translated_text: With all the gods he thereby makes him sit down together.

children.text: kulāyinaṃ ghṛtavantaṃ savitra iti kulāyam iva hy etad yajñe kriyate yat paitudāravāḥ paridhayo gulgulūrṇāstukāḥ sugandhitejanānīti yajñaṃ naya yajamānāya sādhv iti yajñam eva tad ṛjudhā pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: By "nest-holding, ghee-filled, of <s>Savitṛ</s>," for this is made in the sacrifice like a nest: the enclosing sticks of paitudāru wood, the lumps of gulgulu and wool, and the fragrant kindling sticks. By "Lead the sacrifice rightly for the sacrificer to success," he thereby establishes the sacrifice straightly.

children.text: sīda hotaḥ sva u loke cikitvān ity agnir vai devānāṃ hotā tasyaiṣa svo loko yad uttaravedīnābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: By "Sit, O <s>hotṛ</s>, in your own place, knowing," for <s>Agni</s> is the <s>hotṛ</s> of the gods, and this is his own place, namely the navel of the northern altar.

children.text: sādayā yajñaṃ sukṛtasya yonāv iti yajamāno vai yajño yajamānāyaivaitām āśiṣam āśāste ||
children.translated_text: By "Set the sacrifice in the womb of what is well done," for the sacrificer is the sacrifice; he thereby invokes this blessing for the sacrificer himself.

children.text: devāvīr devān haviṣā yajāsy agne bṛhad yajamāne vayo dhā iti prāṇo vai vayaḥ prāṇam eva tad yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: By "Serving the gods, you will worship the gods with oblation; O <s>Agni</s>, place great vitality in the sacrificer," for vitality is breath; he thereby places breath in the sacrificer.

children.text: ni hotā hotṛṣadane vidāna ity agnir vai devānāṃ hotā tasyaitaddhotṛṣadanaṃ yad uttaravedīnābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: By "The <s>hotṛ</s> has sat in the seat of the <s>hotṛ</s>, knowing," for <s>Agni</s> is the <s>hotṛ</s> of the gods, and this is his seat of the <s>hotṛ</s>, namely the navel of the northern altar.

children.text: tveṣo dīdivāṁ asadat sudakṣa ity āsanno hi sa tarhi bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By "Blazing, shining, very skillful, he has sat," for he is then sitting close by.

children.text: adabdhavratapramatir vasiṣṭha ity agnir vai devānāṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By "Of unbroken vow, not negligent, the best dweller," for <s>Agni</s> is the best dweller among the gods.

children.text: sahasrambharaḥ śucijihvo agnir ity eṣā ha vā asya sahasrambharatā yad enam ekaṃ santam bahudhā viharanti ||
children.translated_text: By "<s>Agni</s>, bearing a thousand, with bright tongue," this indeed is his thousand-bearing nature: that, though he is one, they distribute him in many ways.

children.text: pra ha vai sāhasram poṣam āpnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows thus obtains thousandfold nourishment.

children.text: tvaṃ dūtas tvam u naḥ paraspā ityuttamayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse, "You are the messenger; you indeed are our protector from afar," he encloses him.

children.text: tvaṃ vasya ā vṛṣabha praṇetā agne tokasya nas tane tanūnām aprayucchan dīdyad bodhi gopā iti ||
children.translated_text: "You are the leader of wealth, O bull; O <s>Agni</s>, not neglecting the child, our offspring, and our bodies, shine and be a guardian."

children.text: agnir vai devānāṃ gopā agnim eva tatsarvato goptāram paridatta ātmane ca yajamānāya ca yatraivaṃ vidvān etayā paridadhāty atho saṃvatsarīṇām evaitāṃ svastiṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is the guardian of the gods. He thereby entrusts <s>Agni</s> on every side as guardian for himself and for the sacrificer, when, knowing thus, he encloses with this verse. Moreover, he thereby makes this welfare last for a year.

children.text: tā etā aṣṭāv anvāha rūpasamṛddhā etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: These eight he recites after; they are complete in form. This indeed is the success of the sacrifice: that it is complete in form, when a verse speaks in accord with the rite that is being performed.

children.text: tāsāṃ triḥ prathamām anvāha trir uttamāṃ tā dvādaśa sampadyante dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatyāyatanābhir evābhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda triḥ prathamāṃ trir uttamām anvāha yajñasyaiva tad barsau nahyati sthemne balāyāvisraṃsāya ||
children.translated_text: Of these he recites the first three times and the last three times; they amount to twelve. There are twelve months; the year is <s>Prajāpati</s>. With supports belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s> he succeeds in these, who knows thus. He recites the first three times and the last three times; thereby he binds the two flanks of the sacrifice itself, for firmness, strength, and non-collapse.

children.text: Chapter 29
havirdhānābhyām prohyamāṇābhyām anubrūhīty āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>adhvaryu</s> says, "Recite as the two <s>havirdhāna</s> carts are being driven forward."

children.text: yuje vām brahma pūrvyaṃ namobhir ity anvāha brahmaṇā vā ete devā ayuñjata yaddhavirdhāne brahmaṇaivaine etad yuṅkte na vai brahmaṇvad riṣyati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "I yoke for you two the ancient <s>brahman</s> with reverences." With <s>brahman</s> these gods yoked the <s>havirdhāna</s> carts; by <s>brahman</s> itself he thereby yokes them. What possesses <s>brahman</s> does not come to harm.

children.text: pretāṃ yajñasya śaṃbhuveti tṛcaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīyam anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites the three-verse hymn addressed to Heaven and Earth, "Go forward for the welfare of the sacrifice."

children.text: tad āhur yaddhavirdhānābhyām prohyamāṇābhyām anu vācāhātha kasmāt tṛcaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīyam anvāheti dyāvāpṛthivī vai devānāṃ havirdhāne āstāṃ te u evādyāpi havirdhāne te hīdam antareṇa sarvaṃ havir yadidaṃ kiṃca tasmāt tṛcaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīyam anvāha ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If he recites an accompanying utterance for the two <s>havirdhāna</s> carts as they are being driven forward, then why does he recite a three-verse hymn addressed to Heaven and Earth?" Heaven and Earth were the <s>havirdhāna</s> carts of the gods, and they are still today the <s>havirdhāna</s> carts. For all this oblation, whatever there is, is within them. Therefore he recites a three-verse hymn addressed to Heaven and Earth.

children.text: yame iva yatamāne yad aitam iti yame iva hy ete yatamāne prabāhug itaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Like two <s>Yamas</s> striving, when you two went"; for these two, like two striving <s>Yamas</s>, have gone forward from here with arms outstretched.

children.text: pra vāṃ bharan mānuṣā devayanta iti devayanto hy ene mānuṣāḥ prabharanti ||
children.translated_text: "Human beings, seeking the gods, bear you two forward"; for human beings seeking the gods do bear these two forward.

children.text: ā sīdataṃ svam u lokaṃ vidāne svāsasthe bhavatam indave na iti somo vai rājenduḥ somāyaivaine etad rājña āsade 'cīkﾱpat ||
children.translated_text: "Sit in your own place, knowing; be in your own seat for <s>Indu</s>." <s>Soma</s> is the king <s>Indu</s>; for king <s>Soma</s> he thereby prepared these two for sitting.

children.text: adhi dvayor adadhā ukthyaṃ vaca iti ||
children.translated_text: "Upon the two he set the laudatory word."

children.text: dvayor hy etat tṛtīyaṃ chadir adhinidhīyata ||
children.translated_text: For this third covering is set upon the two.

children.text: ukthyaṃ vaca iti yad āha yajñiyaṃ vai karmokthyaṃ vaco yajñamevaitena samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "<s>ukthya</s> speech," the sacrificial act is indeed <s>ukthya</s> speech; by this he prospers the sacrifice itself.

children.text: yatasrucā mithunā yā saparyataḥ asaṃyatto vrate te kṣeti puṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: "With the ladle, the pair who serve, unbound, in the vow, may it dwell and prosper for you."

children.text: yad evādaḥ pūrvaṃ yattavat padam āha tad evaitena śāntyā śamayati ||
children.translated_text: Whatever word of that earlier passage he uttered as bound or constrained, that very thing he pacifies by this pacifying formula.

children.text: bhadrā śaktir yajamānāya sunvata ity āśiṣam āśāste ||
children.translated_text: With "Auspicious power for the pressing sacrificer," he seeks a blessing.

children.text: viśvā rūpāṇi prati muñcate kavir iti viśvarūpām anvāha ||
children.translated_text: With "The sage puts on all forms," he recites a verse that has all forms.

children.text: sa rarāṭyām īkṣamāṇo 'nubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should recite while looking at the <s>rarāṭī</s> mark.

children.text: viśvam iva hi rūpaṃ rarāṭyāḥ śuklam iva ca kṛṣṇam iva ca ||
children.translated_text: For the form of the <s>rarāṭī</s> is, as it were, all-variegated, both white, as it were, and black, as it were.

children.text: viśvaṃ rūpam avarunddha ātmane ca yajamānāya ca yatraivaṃ vidvān etāṃ rarāṭyām īkṣamāṇo 'nvāha ||
children.translated_text: He secures every form for himself and for the sacrificer when, knowing thus, he recites this while looking at the <s>rarāṭī</s> mark.

children.text: pari tvā girvaṇo gira ity uttamayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse, "Around you, O lover of song, the songs," he encloses it.

children.text: sa yadaiva havirdhāne saṃpariśrite manyetātha paridadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: When he thinks the two <s>havirdhāna</s> sheds have been completely enclosed, then he should enclose it.

children.text: anagnambhāvukā ha hotuś ca yajamānasya ca bhāryā bhavanti yatraivaṃ vidvān etayā havirdhānayoḥ saṃpariśritayoḥ paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: The wives of the <s>hotṛ</s> and of the sacrificer do not become deprived of fire when, knowing thus, he encloses with this verse after the two <s>havirdhānas</s> have been completely enclosed.

children.text: yajuṣā vā ete pariśrīyete yaddhavirdhāne yajuṣaivaine etat pariśrayanti ||
children.translated_text: These two, namely the <s>havirdhānas</s>, are enclosed with a <s>yajus</s>; with a <s>yajus</s> they thus enclose them.

children.text: tau yadaivādhvaryuś ca pratiprasthātā cobhayato methyau nihanyātām atha paridadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>adhvaryu</s> and the <s>pratiprasthātṛ</s> have driven in the two pegs on both sides, then he should enclose it.

children.text: atra hi te saṃpariśrite bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For at that point they have been completely enclosed.

children.text: tā etā aṣṭāv anvāha rūpasamṛddhā etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati tāsāṃ triḥ prathamām anvāha trir uttamāṃ tā dvādaśa sampadyante dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatyāyatanābhir evābhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda triḥ prathamāṃ trir uttamām anvāha yajñasyaiva tad barsau nahyati sthemne balāyāvisraṃsāya ||
children.translated_text: These eight he recites, complete in form. For that in the sacrifice is successful which is complete in form, when a <s>ṛc</s> addresses the action that is being performed. Of these he recites the first three times and the last three times; they become twelve. There are twelve months; the year is <s>Prajāpati</s>. By abodes belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s> he thereby succeeds with them, he who knows thus. He recites the first three times and the last three times; thereby he ties the two sides of the sacrifice itself, for firmness, strength, and freedom from slipping apart.

children.text: Chapter 30
agnīṣomābhyām praṇīyamānābhyām anubrūhīty āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>adhvaryu</s> says, "Recite for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> as they are being led forward."

children.text: sāvīr hi deva prathamāya pitra iti sāvitrīm anvāha ||
children.translated_text: With "For you are mighty, O god, for the first father," he recites a verse belonging to <s>Savitṛ</s>.

children.text: tad āhur yad agnīṣomābhyām praṇīyamānābhyām anu vācāhātha kasmāt sāvitrīm anvāheti savitā vai prasavānām īśe savitṛprasūtā evainau tat praṇayanti tasmāt sāvitrīm anvāha ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If the verbal direction is for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> as they are being led forward, then why does he recite a verse belonging to <s>Savitṛ</s>?" <s>Savitṛ</s> is indeed lord of impellings. Thus they lead those two forward impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>. Therefore he recites a verse belonging to <s>Savitṛ</s>.

children.text: praitu brahmaṇaspatir iti brāhmaṇaspatyām anvāha ||
children.translated_text: With "Let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth," he recites a verse belonging to <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>.

children.text: tad āhur yad agnīṣomābhyām praṇīyamānābhyām anu vācāhātha kasmād brāhmaṇaspatyām anvāheti brahma vai bṛhaspatir brahmaivābhyām etat purogavam akaḥ na vai brahmaṇvad riṣyati ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If the verbal direction is for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> as they are being led forward, then why does he recite a verse belonging to <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>?" <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is <s>brahman</s> (sacred formulation). Thus he has made <s>brahman</s> go before them; one endowed with <s>brahman</s> does not come to harm.

children.text: pra devy etu sūnṛteti sasūnṛtam eva tad yajñaṃ karoti tasmād brāhmaṇaspatyām anvāha ||
children.translated_text: With "Let the goddess kindly speech go forth," he thereby makes the sacrifice possessed of kindly speech. Therefore he recites a verse belonging to <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>.

children.text: hotā devo amartya iti tṛcam āgneyaṃ gāyatram anvāha some rājani praṇīyamāne ||
children.translated_text: With "The divine <s>hotṛ</s>, immortal," he recites an Agni triplet in the Gāyatrī meter while King <s>Soma</s> is being led forward.

children.text: somaṃ vai rājānam praṇīyamānam antareṇaiva sadohavirdhānāny asurā rakṣāṃsy ajighāṃsaṃs tam agnir māyayātyanayat ||
children.translated_text: As King <s>Soma</s> was being led forward, the <s>Asuras</s> and <s>Rakṣases</s> sought to strike him precisely between the <s>sadas</s> and the <s>havirdhānas</s>; <s>Agni</s> led him beyond them by <s>māyā</s> (powerful stratagem).

children.text: purastād eti māyayeti māyayā hi sa tam atyanayat tasmād v asyāgnim purastād dharanti ||
children.translated_text: With "He goes in front by <s>māyā</s>," for by <s>māyā</s> he led him beyond them. Therefore they carry <s>Agni</s> in front of him.

children.text: upa tvāgne dive diva upa priyam panipnatam iti tisraś caikāṃ cānvāha ||
children.translated_text: With "To you, O <s>Agni</s>, day by day; to the dear one, the most delightful," he recites three verses and one additional verse.

children.text: īśvarau ha vā etau saṃyantau yajamānaṃ hiṃsitor yaś cāsau pūrva uddhṛto bhavati yam u cainam aparam praṇayanti tad yat tisraś caikāṃ cānvāha saṃjānānāv evainau tat saṃgamayati pratiṣṭhāyām evainau tat pratiṣṭhāpayaty ātmanaś ca yajamānasya cāhiṃsāyai ||
children.translated_text: These two, when coming together, are liable to injure the sacrificer: the one that has previously been taken out and the other which they are now leading forward. Because he recites three verses and one, he thereby makes them come together in mutual understanding; he thereby establishes them on a firm foundation, so that neither he himself nor the sacrificer may be injured.

children.text: agne juṣasva prati harya tad vaca ity āhutyāṃ hūyamānāyām anvāha ||
children.translated_text: With "O <s>Agni</s>, accept; receive that speech," he recites while the oblation is being offered.

children.text: agnaya eva taj juṣṭim āhutiṃ gamayati ||
children.translated_text: He thereby causes the oblation to go to <s>Agni</s> as something acceptable.

children.text: somo jigāti gātuvid iti tṛcaṃ saumyaṃ gāyatram anvāha some rājani praṇīyamāne svayaivainaṃ taddevatayā svena chandasā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: With "<s>Soma</s> goes, knowing the path," he recites a Soma triplet in the Gāyatrī meter while King <s>Soma</s> is being led forward; by his own deity and his own meter he thereby prospers him.

children.text: somaḥ sadhastham āsadad ity āsatsyan hi sa tarhi bhavati ||
children.translated_text: With "<s>Soma</s> has taken his seat in the common place," for at that time he is about to sit down.

children.text: tad atikramyaivānubrūyāt pṛṣṭhata ivāgnīdhraṃ kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: Having just passed beyond that, he should recite, as though making the <s>agnīdhra</s> stand behind him.

children.text: tam asya rājā varuṇas tam aśvineti vaiṣṇavīm anvāha ||
children.translated_text: With "Him, king <s>Varuṇa</s>; him, the <s>Aśvins</s>," he recites a verse belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: kratuṃ sacanta mārutasya vedhasaḥ dādhāra dakṣam uttamam aharvidaṃ vrajaṃ ca viṣṇuḥ sakhivāṁ aporṇuta iti ||
children.translated_text: "They attend the resolve of the Marut-like sage; <s>Viṣṇu</s>, companionable, upheld the highest skill, the day-knowing pen, and opened it."

children.text: viṣṇur vai devānāṃ dvārapaḥ sa evāsmā etad dvāraṃ vivṛṇoti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the doorkeeper of the gods; he himself thereby opens this door for him.

children.text: antaś ca prāgā aditir bhavāsīti prapādyamāne 'nvāha ||
children.translated_text: With "You have gone inside; be <s>Aditi</s>," he recites as he is being brought in.

children.text: śyeno na yoniṃ sadanaṃ dhiyākṛtam ity āsanne ||
children.translated_text: With "Like an eagle to the womb, to the seat made by thought," he recites when he is seated.

children.text: hiraṇyayam āsadaṃ deva eṣatīti ||
children.translated_text: With "The god shall go to the golden seat."

children.text: hiraṇmayam iva ha vā eṣa etad devebhyaś chadayati yat kṛṣṇājinam ||
children.translated_text: For this black antelope skin is, as it were, what he spreads as golden for the gods.

children.text: tasmād etām anvāha ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he recites this verse.

children.text: astabhnād dyām asuro viśvavedā iti vāruṇyā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the Varuṇa verse, "The all-knowing <s>Asura</s> propped up heaven," he encloses it.

children.text: varuṇadevatyo vā eṣa tāvad yāvad upanaddho yāvat pariśritāni prapadyate svayaivainaṃ tad devatayā svena chandasā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: This is connected with <s>Varuṇa</s> as its deity for just so long as it is bound, for so long as it enters the enclosures. Thereby he prospers him by his own deity and by his own meter.

children.text: taṃ yady upa vā dhāveyur abhayaṃ veccherann evā vandasva varuṇam bṛhantam ity etayā paridadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: If they should run toward him, or should desire safety, he should enclose him with this verse: "Praise <s>Varuṇa</s> the lofty one."

children.text: yāvadbhyo hābhayam icchati yāvadbhyo hābhayaṃ dhyāyati tāvadbhyo hābhayam bhavati yatraivaṃ vidvān etayā paridadhāti tasmād evaṃ vidvān etayaiva paridadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: From as many as he desires safety, from as many as he thinks of safety, from that many safety comes to him, when one who knows thus encloses with this verse. Therefore one who knows thus should enclose with this very verse.

children.text: tā etāḥ saptadaśānvāha rūpasamṛddhā etadvai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati tāsāṃ triḥ prathamām anvāha trir uttamāṃ tā ekaviṃśatiḥ sampadyanta ekaviṃśo vai prajāpatir dvādaśa māsāḥ pañcartavas traya ime lokā asāv āditya ekaviṃśa uttamā pratiṣṭhā ||
children.translated_text: These seventeen he recites after; they are complete in form. This indeed is the success of the sacrifice: that it is complete in form, when a verse speaks in accord with the rite that is being performed. Of them he recites the first three times and the last three times; they amount to twenty-one. <s>Prajāpati</s> is the twenty-first: the twelve months, the five seasons, these three worlds, and that sun as the twenty-first. The last is the foundation.

children.text: tad daivaṃ kṣatraṃ sā śrīs tad ādhipatyaṃ tad bradhnasya viṣṭapaṃ tat prajāpater āyatanaṃ tat svārājyam ||
children.translated_text: That is the divine ruling power; that is splendor; that is overlordship; that is the summit of <s>Bradhna</s>; that is the abode of <s>Prajāpati</s>; that is self-rule.

children.text: ṛdhnoty etam evaitābhir ekaviṃśatyaikaviṃśatyā ||
children.translated_text: He prospers him with these twenty-one, precisely by means of twenty-one.

children.text: Chapter 31

yajñena vai devā ūrdhvāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs te 'bibhayur imaṃ no dṛṣṭvā manuṣyāś ca ṛṣayaś cānuprajñāsyantīti taṃ vai yūpenaivāyopayaṃs taṃ yad yūpenaivāyopayaṃs tad yūpasya yūpatvaṃ tam avācīnāgraṃ nimityordhvā udāyaṃs tato vai manuṣyāś ca ṛṣayaś ca devānāṃ yajñavāstv abhyāyan yajñasya kiṃcid eṣiṣyāmaḥ prajñātyā iti te vai yūpam evāvindann avācīnāgraṃ nimitaṃ te 'vidur anena vai devā yajñam ayūyupann iti tam utkhāyordhvaṃ nyaminvaṃs tato vai te pra yajñam ajānan pra svargaṃ lokam ||
children.translated_text: By the sacrifice the gods went upward to the heavenly world. They became afraid, thinking, "Having seen this, human beings and seers will understand it after us." They obstructed it with the <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post) itself. Because they obstructed it with the <s>yūpa</s>, that is the <s>yūpa</s>'s nature as yūpa. Setting it with its point downward, they went upward. Then human beings and seers came upon the sacrificial ground of the gods, saying, "Let us seek to understand something of the sacrifice." They found the <s>yūpa</s> alone, set with its point downward. They knew, "With this the gods obstructed the sacrifice." Uprooting it, they set it upright; then they understood the sacrifice and the heavenly world.

children.text: tad yad yūpa ūrdhvo nimīyate yajñasya prajñātyai svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>yūpa</s> is set upright, for the recognition of the sacrifice and for the manifestation of the heavenly world.

children.text: vajro vā eṣa yad yūpaḥ so 'ṣṭāśriḥ kartavyo 'ṣṭāśrir vai vajras taṃ tam praharati dviṣate bhrātṛvyāya vadhaṃ yo 'sya stṛtyas tasmai startavai ||
children.translated_text: This, namely the <s>yūpa</s>, is a <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt). It should be made eight-cornered, for the <s>vajra</s> is eight-cornered. With it he strikes the hated rival, the hostile kinsman, for the killing of the one whom he is to bring down.

children.text: vajro vai yūpaḥ sa eṣa dviṣato vadha udyatas tiṣṭhati tasmāddhāpy etarhi yo dveṣṭi tasyāpriyam bhavaty amuṣyāyaṃ yūpo 'muṣyāyaṃ yūpa iti dṛṣṭvā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>yūpa</s> is a <s>vajra</s>; it stands raised as death for the hater. Therefore even now, when a man sees the <s>yūpa</s> of someone whom he hates, it becomes displeasing to him: "This is that man's <s>yūpa</s>, this is that man's <s>yūpa</s>."

children.text: khādiraṃ yūpaṃ kurvīta svargakāmaḥ khādireṇa vai yūpena devāḥ svargaṃ lokam ajayaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānaḥ khādireṇa yūpena svargaṃ lokaṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: One who desires the heavenly world should make a <s>yūpa</s> of khadira wood. With a khadira <s>yūpa</s> the gods won the heavenly world; in just the same way the sacrificer wins the heavenly world with a khadira <s>yūpa</s>.

children.text: bailvaṃ yūpaṃ kurvītānnādyakāmaḥ puṣṭikāmaḥ samāṃ samāṃ vai bilvo gṛbhītas tad annādyasya rūpam ā mūlācchākhābhir anucitas tat puṣṭeḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who desires food to eat, one who desires prosperity, should make a <s>yūpa</s> of bilva wood. The bilva is grasped year by year; that is the form of food to be eaten. It is furnished with branches from the root upward; that is the form of prosperity.

children.text: puṣyati prajāṃ ca paśūṃś ca ya evaṃ vidvān bailvaṃ yūpaṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: He prospers in offspring and cattle, who, knowing thus, makes a <s>yūpa</s> of bilva wood.

children.text: yad eva bailvāṃ bilvaṃ jyotir iti vā ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: And as to what belongs to bilva: people call the bilva "light."

children.text: jyotiḥ sveṣu bhavati śreṣṭhaḥ svānām bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He becomes a light among his own people; he becomes the best of his own people, who knows thus.

children.text: pālāśaṃ yūpaṃ kurvīta tejaskāmo brahmavarcasakāmas tejo vai brahmavarcasaṃ vanaspatīnām palāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who desires brilliance, one who desires <s>brahmavarcasa</s> (sacred lustre), should make a <s>yūpa</s> of palāśa wood. Among trees the palāśa is brilliance and <s>brahmavarcasa</s>.

children.text: tejasvī brahmavarcasī bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān pālāśaṃ yūpaṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: He becomes brilliant and possessed of <s>brahmavarcasa</s>, who, knowing thus, makes a <s>yūpa</s> of palāśa wood.

children.text: yad eva pālāśāṃ sarveṣāṃ vā eṣa vanaspatīnāṃ yonir yat palāśas tasmāt palāśasyaiva palāśenācakṣate 'muṣya palāśam amuṣya palāśam iti ||
children.translated_text: And as to the palāśa: this, namely the palāśa, is the womb of all forest trees. Therefore they designate the leaf of the palāśa itself as palāśa, saying, "The palāśa of this one, the palāśa of that one."

children.text: sarveṣāṃ hāsya vanaspatīnāṃ kāma upāpto bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The desire connected with all forest trees becomes attained for him, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 32
añjmo yūpam anubrūhīty āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>adhvaryu</s> says, "Recite for the <s>yūpa</s> as it is being anointed."

children.text: añjanti tvām adhvare devayanta ity anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Those seeking the gods anoint you in the sacrifice."

children.text: adhvare hy enaṃ devayanto 'ñjanti ||
children.translated_text: For those seeking the gods do anoint it in the sacrifice.

children.text: vanaspate madhunā daivyenety etad vai madhu daivyaṃ yad ājyam ||
children.translated_text: "O forest-lord, with divine honey": this indeed is the divine honey, namely the clarified butter.

children.text: yad ūrdhvas tiṣṭhā draviṇeha dhattād yad vā kṣayo mātur asyā upastha iti yadi ca tiṣṭhāsi yadi ca śayāsai draviṇam evāsmāsu dhattād ity eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: "If, standing upright, you would place wealth here, or if lying in the lap of this mother": whether you stand or whether you lie, place wealth among us; that is what it says.

children.text: ucchrayasva vanaspata ity ucchrīyamāṇāyābhirūpā yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: "Rise up, O forest-lord": this is fitting for one being raised. What is fitting in the sacrifice is successful.

children.text: varṣman pṛthivyā adhīty etad vai varṣma pṛthivyai yatra yūpam unminvanti ||
children.translated_text: "Upon the height of the earth": this indeed is the height of the earth, the place where they set up the <s>yūpa</s>.

children.text: sumitī mīyamāno varco dhā yajñavāhasa ity āśiṣam āśāste ||
children.translated_text: "Being measured with good measure, place radiance, O bearer of the sacrifice": he thereby seeks a blessing.

children.text: samiddhasya śrayamāṇaḥ purastād iti ||
children.translated_text: "Resting in front of the kindled one," it says.

children.text: samiddhasya hyeṣa etat purastācchrayate ||
children.translated_text: For this indeed rests there in front of the kindled one.

children.text: brahma vanvāno ajaraṃ suvīram ity āśiṣam evāśāste ||
children.translated_text: "Winning <s>brahman</s>, undecaying, rich in heroes": he thereby seeks a blessing.

children.text: āre asmad amatim bādhamāna ity aśanāyā vai pāpmāmatis tām eva tad ārān nudate yajñāc ca yajamānāc ca ||
children.translated_text: "Driving far away from us want of thought": hunger is evil and want of thought; that very thing he drives far away from the sacrifice and from the sacrificer.

children.text: ucchrayasva mahate saubhagāyety āśiṣam evāśāste ||
children.translated_text: "Rise up for great good fortune": he thereby seeks a blessing.

children.text: ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaye tiṣṭhā devo na saviteti ||
children.translated_text: "Stand upright indeed for our aid, like the god <s>Savitṛ</s>."

children.text: yad vai devānāṃ neti tad eṣām om iti tiṣṭha deva iva savitety eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: What among the gods is expressed by "na," that for them is assent; thus it says, "Stand for aid, O god, like <s>Savitṛ</s>."

children.text: ūrdhvo vājasya saniteti vājasanim evainaṃ tad dhanasāṃ sanoti ||
children.translated_text: By the words, "upright, winner of the prize," he thereby wins him prize-winning possession among riches.

children.text: yad añjibhir vāghadbhir vihvayāmaha iti chandāṃsi vā añjayo vāghatas tair etad devān yajamānā vihvayante mama yajñam āgacchata mama yajñam iti ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "with the adorned, resounding ones we call hither," the metres are the adornments and resounding ones; with them the sacrificers call the gods hither: "Come to my sacrifice, to my sacrifice."

children.text: yadi ha vā api bahava iva yajante 'tha hāsya devā yajñam aiva gacchanti yatraivaṃ vidvān etām anvāha ||
children.translated_text: Even if many, as it were, are sacrificing, the gods go to his sacrifice alone, when one who knows thus recites this verse after.

children.text: ūrdhvo naḥ pāhy aṃhaso ni ketunā viśvaṃ sam atriṇaṃ daheti ||
children.translated_text: "Protect us upward from distress; with your sign burn up every devourer."

children.text: rakṣāṃsi vai pāpmātriṇo rakṣāṃsi pāpmānaṃ dahety eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: The devourers are the <s>rakṣases</s>, the evils; he thereby says, "Burn up the <s>rakṣases</s>, the evil."

children.text: kṛdhī na ūrdhvāñcarathāya jīvasa iti yad āha kṛdhī na ūrdhvāñcaraṇāya jīvasa ity eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "Make us move upward for the course, for life," he thereby says, "Make us move upward, for life."

children.text: yadi ha vā api nīta iva yajamāno bhavati pari haivainaṃ tat saṃvatsarāya dadāti ||
children.translated_text: Even if the <s>yajamāna</s> is as though led away, by that he allots him round about for a year.

children.text: vidā deveṣu no duva ity āśiṣam evāśāste ||
children.translated_text: By "know our service among the gods," he simply invokes a blessing.

children.text: jāto jāyate sudinatve ahnām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Born, he is born in the good-day-ness of the days."

children.text: jāto hy eṣa etāj jāyate ||
children.translated_text: For this one, having been born, is born from these.

children.text: samarya ā vidathe vardhamāna iti vardhayanty evainaṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: By "growing in the gathering, at the rite," they thereby make him grow.

children.text: punanti dhīrā apaso manīṣeti punanty evainaṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: By "the wise purify the waters with insight," they thereby purify him.

children.text: devayā vipra ud iyarti vācam iti devebhya evainaṃ tan nivedayati ||
children.translated_text: By "the inspired priest sends up speech for the gods," he thereby announces him to the gods.

children.text: yuvā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgād ity uttamayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse, "young, well-clothed, wrapped about, he has come," he wraps him around.

children.text: prāṇo vai yuvā suvāsāḥ so 'yaṃ śarīraiḥ parivṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Breath is the young, well-clothed one; this breath is wrapped about by bodies.

children.text: sa u śreyān bhavati jāyamāna iti śreyāñchreyān hy eṣa etad bhavati jāyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By "he becomes better as he is being born," for this one, as he is being born, becomes better and better.

children.text: taṃ dhīrāsaḥ kavaya un nayanti svādhyo manasā devayanta iti ye vā anūcānās te kavayas ta evainaṃ tad unnayanti ||
children.translated_text: By "the wise poets raise him up, worshipping the gods with a well-directed mind," those who are learned are the poets; they thereby raise him up.

children.text: tā etāḥ saptānvāha rūpasamṛddhā etad vai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yad rūpasamṛddhaṃ yat karma kriyamāṇam ṛg abhivadati tāsāṃ triḥ prathamām anvāha trir uttamāṃ tā ekādaśa sampadyanta ekādaśākṣarā vai triṣṭup triṣṭub indrasya vajra indrāyatanābhir evābhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda triḥ prathamāṃ trir uttamām anvāha yajñasyaiva tad barsau nahyati sthemne balāyāvisraṃsāya ||
children.translated_text: These seven he recites after; they are complete in form. This indeed is the success of the sacrifice: that it is complete in form, when a verse speaks in accord with the rite being performed. Of them he recites the first three times and the last three times; they amount to eleven. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> has eleven syllables; the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt. With supports belonging to <s>Indra</s> he succeeds in these, who knows thus. He recites the first three times and the last three times; thereby he binds the two flanks of the sacrifice itself, for steadiness, strength, and non-collapse.

children.text: Chapter 33
tiṣṭhed yūpāḥ anupraharait ity āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Should the <s>yūpa</s> stand, or should one cast after it?"

children.text: tiṣṭhet paśukāmasya ||
children.translated_text: It should stand for one who desires cattle.

children.text: devebhyo vai paśavo 'nnādyāyālambhāya nātiṣṭhanta te 'pakramya prativāvadato 'tiṣṭhan nāsmān ālapsyadhve nāsmān iti tato vai devā etaṃ yūpam vajram apaśyaṃs tam ebhya udaśrayaṃs tasmād bibhyata upāvartanta tam evādyāpy upāvṛttās tato vai devebhyaḥ paśavo 'nnādyāyālambhāyatiṣṭhanta ||
children.translated_text: The animals did not stand still for the gods to be taken for food. Having gone away, they stood protesting, "You shall not take us, not us." Then the gods saw this <s>yūpa</s> as a thunderbolt and raised it up against them. In fear of it they turned back toward it. From then on the animals stood still for the gods to be taken for food.

children.text: tiṣṭhante 'smai paśavo 'nnādyāyālambhāya ya evaṃ veda yasya caivaṃ viduṣo yūpas tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Animals stand still for him, to be taken for food, who knows thus, and for the one who, knowing thus, has a <s>yūpa</s> standing.

children.text: anupraharet svargakāmasya ||
children.translated_text: He should cast after it for one who desires heaven.

children.text: tam u ha smaitam pūrve 'nv eva praharanti ||
children.translated_text: The people of old used to cast this very one after it.

children.text: yajamāno vai yūpo yajamānaḥ prastaro 'gnir vai devayoniḥ so 'gner devayonyā āhutibhyaḥ sambhūya hiraṇyaśarīra ūrdhvaḥ svargaṃ lokam eṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>yajamāna</s> is the <s>yūpa</s>; the <s>yajamāna</s> is the <s>prastara</s>; <s>Agni</s> is the divine womb. Having come into being from <s>Agni</s>, the divine womb, from the oblations, he will go upward, with a golden body, to the heavenly world.

children.text: atha ye tebhyo 'vara āsaṃs ta etaṃ svarum apaśyan yūpaśakalaṃ taṃ tasmin kāle 'nupraharet tatra sa kāma upāpto yo 'nupraharaṇe tatra sa kāma upāpto yaḥ sthāne ||
children.translated_text: Then those who were later than them saw this <s>svaru</s>, a chip of the <s>yūpa</s>. He should cast it after at that time. There the desire connected with casting after is attained; there the desire connected with its standing is attained.

children.text: sarvābhyo vā eṣa devatābhya ātmānam ālabhate yo dīkṣate 'gniḥ sarvā devatāḥ somaḥ sarvā devatāḥ sa yad agnīṣomīyam paśum ālabhate sarvābhya eva tad devatābhyo yajamāna ātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīte ||
children.translated_text: Whoever is consecrated offers himself to all the deities. <s>Agni</s> is all the deities; <s>Soma</s> is all the deities. When he offers the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal, the <s>yajamāna</s> thereby buys himself back from all the deities.

children.text: tad āhur dvirūpo 'gnīṣomīyaḥ kartavyo dvidevatyo hīti tat tan nādṛtyam pīva iva kartavyaḥ pīvorūpā vai paśavaḥ kṛśita iva khalu vai yajamāno bhavati tad yat pīvā paśur bhavati yajamānam eva tat svena medhena samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: They say, "The <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> should be made two-formed, since it has two deities." That is not to be heeded. It should be made as if plump. Animals are plump in form, while the <s>yajamāna</s> indeed is as if emaciated. When the animal is plump, he thereby prospers the <s>yajamāna</s> with its own sacrificial fatness.

children.text: tad āhur nāgnīṣomīyasya paśor aśnīyāt puruṣasya vā eṣo 'śnāti yo 'gnīṣomīyasya paśor aśnāti yajamāno hy etenātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīta iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "One should not eat from the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal. Whoever eats from the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> animal eats from a man, since with it the <s>yajamāna</s> buys himself back."

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyaṃ vārtraghnaṃ vā etaddhavir yad agnīṣomīyo 'gnīṣomābhyāṃ vā indro vṛtram ahaṃs tāv enam abrūtām āvābhyāṃ vai vṛtram avadhīr varaṃ te vṛṇāvahā iti vṛṇāthām iti tāv etam eva varam avṛṇātāṃ śvaḥsutyāyām paśuṃ sa enayor eṣo 'cyuto varavṛto hy enayos tasmāt tasyāśitavyaṃ caiva līpsitavyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: That is not to be heeded. The <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> is an oblation that slays <s>Vṛtra</s>. By <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>. The two said to him, "By us you have slain <s>Vṛtra</s>; let us choose a boon from you." He said, "Choose." They chose this very boon: an animal at the next-day Soma-pressing. This animal has not fallen away from them, for it is the boon chosen by them. Therefore it should both be eaten and desired.

children.text: Chapter 34
āprībhir āprīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: He propitiates with the <s>āprī</s> verses.

children.text: tejo vai brahmavarcasam āpriyas tejasaivainaṃ tad brahmavarcasena samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>āprī</s> verses are brilliance and <s>brahmavarcasa</s> (sacred lustre). With brilliance and <s>brahmavarcasa</s> he thereby prospers him.

children.text: samidho yajati ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices the kindling-sticks.

children.text: prāṇā vai samidhaḥ prāṇā hīdaṃ sarvaṃ samindhate yad idaṃ kiṃca prāṇān eva tat prīṇāti prāṇān yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: The kindling-sticks are the breaths, for breaths kindle all this, whatever there is here. He thereby satisfies the breaths and places breaths in the <s>yajamāna</s>.

children.text: tanūnapātaṃ yajati prāṇo vai tanūnapāt sa hi tanvaḥ pāti prāṇam eva tat prīṇāti prāṇaṃ yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships <s>Tanūnapāt</s>. Breath indeed is <s>Tanūnapāt</s>, for it protects the body. Thus he gratifies breath itself; he places breath in the sacrificer.

children.text: narāśaṃsaṃ yajati prajā vai naro vāk śaṃsaḥ prajāṃ caiva tad vācaṃ ca prīṇāti prajāṃ ca vācaṃ ca yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>. Offspring indeed are the men, and speech is the praise. Thus he gratifies offspring and speech; he places offspring and speech in the sacrificer.

children.text: iﾱo yajaty annaṃ vā iﾱo 'nnam eva tat prīṇāty annaṃ yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships <s>Iḍā</s>. Food indeed is <s>Iḍā</s>. Thus he gratifies food itself; he places food in the sacrificer.

children.text: barhir yajati paśavo vai barhiḥ paśūn eva tat prīṇāti paśūn yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass). Animals indeed are the <s>barhis</s>. Thus he gratifies animals themselves; he places animals in the sacrificer.

children.text: duro yajati vṛṣṭir vai duro vṛṣṭim eva tat prīṇāti vṛṣṭim annādyaṃ yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships the <s>Doors</s>. Rain indeed is the <s>Doors</s>. Thus he gratifies rain itself; he places rain and edible food in the sacrificer.

children.text: uṣāsānaktā yajaty ahorātre vā uṣāsānaktāhorātre eva tat prīṇāty ahorātrayor yajamānaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships <s>Uṣāsānaktā</s>, Dawn and Night. Day and night indeed are <s>Uṣāsānaktā</s>. Thus he gratifies day and night themselves; he places the sacrificer in day and night.

children.text: daivyā hotārā yajati prāṇāpānau vai daivyā hotārā prāṇāpānāv eva tat prīṇāti prāṇāpānau yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships the two divine <s>hotṛ</s>s. The in-breath and the out-breath indeed are the two divine <s>hotṛ</s>s. Thus he gratifies the in-breath and the out-breath themselves; he places the in-breath and the out-breath in the sacrificer.

children.text: tisro devīr yajati prāṇo vā apāno vyānas tisro devyas tā eva tat prīṇāti tā yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships the three goddesses. Breath, out-breath, and diffused breath indeed are the three goddesses. Thus he gratifies them themselves; he places them in the sacrificer.

children.text: tvaṣṭāraṃ yajati vāg vai tvaṣṭā vāgghīdaṃ sarvaṃ tāṣṭīva vācam eva tat prīṇāti vācaṃ yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>. Speech indeed is <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, for speech fashions all this, as it were. Thus he gratifies speech itself; he places speech in the sacrificer.

children.text: vanaspatiṃ yajati prāṇo vai vanaspatiḥ prāṇam eva tat prīṇāti prāṇaṃ yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He worships <s>Vanaspati</s>. Breath indeed is <s>Vanaspati</s>. Thus he gratifies breath itself; he places breath in the sacrificer.

children.text: svāhākṛtīr yajati pratiṣṭhā vai svāhākṛtayaḥ pratiṣṭhāyām eva tad yajñam antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He worships the <s>svāhākṛti</s>s. The <s>svāhākṛti</s>s are a firm foundation. Thus, at the end, he establishes the sacrifice upon a firm foundation.

children.text: tābhir yathaṛṣy āprīṇīyād yad yathaṛṣy āprīṇāti yajamānam eva tad bandhutāyā notsṛjati ||
children.translated_text: With these he should make the āprī offerings according to the seer. When he makes the āprī offerings according to the seer, he does not release the sacrificer from kinship.

children.text: Chapter 35
paryagnaye kriyamāṇāyānubrūhīty āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>adhvaryu</s> says, "Recite as the fire is being carried around."

children.text: agnir hotā no adhvara iti tṛcam āgneyaṃ gāyatram anvāha paryagni kriyamāṇe svayaivainaṃ tad devatayā svena chandasā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the three-verse hymn addressed to <s>Agni</s>, in the Gāyatrī meter, beginning "<s>Agni</s> is our <s>hotṛ</s> at the rite," while the carrying-around of the fire is being performed. By his own deity and his own meter he thereby makes him prosper.

children.text: vājī san pari ṇīyata iti vājinam iva hy enaṃ santam pariṇayanti ||
children.translated_text: "Being a steed, he is led around," for they lead him around as one who is like a steed.

children.text: pari triviṣṭy adhvaraṃ yāty agnī rathīr ivety eṣa hi rathīr ivādhvaram pariyāti ||
children.translated_text: "Around the threefold rite <s>Agni</s> goes like a charioteer," for he goes around the rite like a charioteer.

children.text: pari vājapatiḥ kavir ity eṣa hi vājānām patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Around goes the inspired lord of prizes," for he indeed is lord of prizes.

children.text: ata upapreṣya hotar havyā devebhya ity āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>adhvaryu</s>, having given the secondary summons, says, "<s>Hotṛ</s>, the oblations for the gods."

children.text: ajaid agnir asanad vājam iti maitrāvaruṇa upapraiṣam pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> takes up the secondary summons, "<s>Agni</s> has conquered; he has won the prize."

children.text: tad āhur yad adhvaryur hotāram upapreṣyaty atha kasmān maitrāvaruṇa upapraiṣam pratipadyata iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If the <s>adhvaryu</s> gives the secondary summons to the <s>hotṛ</s>, then why does the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> take up the secondary summons?"

children.text: mano vai yajñasya maitrāvaruṇo vāg yajñasya hotā manasā vā iṣita vāg vadati yāṃ hy anyamanā vācaṃ vadaty asuryā vai sā vāg adevajuṣṭā tad yan maitrāvaruṇa upapraiṣam pratipadyate manasaiva tad vācam īrayati tan manaseritayā vācā devebhyo havyaṃ sampādayati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is the mind of the sacrifice; the <s>hotṛ</s> is the speech of the sacrifice. Speech speaks when impelled by mind. For speech that one utters with another mind is demonic speech, not enjoyed by the gods. Therefore, when the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> takes up the secondary summons, by mind itself he sets speech in motion; with speech set in motion by mind he prepares the oblation for the gods.

children.text: Chapter 36
daivyāḥ śamitāra ārabhadhvam uta manuṣyā ity āha ||
children.translated_text: He says, "Divine slaughterers, begin, and also the human ones."

children.text: ye caiva devānāṃ śamitāro ye ca manuṣyāṇāṃ tān eva tat saṃśāsti ||
children.translated_text: Those who are slaughterers among the gods and those who are slaughterers among human beings, he thereby instructs just them.

children.text: upanayata medhyā dura āśāsānā medhapatibhyām medham iti ||
children.translated_text: "Lead up the fit victim at the doors, desiring the offering for the two lords of the offering."

children.text: paśur vai medho yajamāno medhapatir yajamānam eva tat svena medhena samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: The animal indeed is the offering, and the sacrificer is the lord of the offering. Thus he makes the sacrificer prosper through his own offering.

children.text: atho khalv āhur yasyai vāva kasyai ca devatāyai paśur ālabhyate saiva medhapatir iti ||
children.translated_text: But then they say, "For whatever deity an animal is seized, that very deity is the lord of the offering."

children.text: sa yady ekadevatyaḥ paśuḥ syān medhapataya iti brūyād yadi dvidevatyo medhapatibhyām iti yadi bahudevatyo medhapatibhya ity etad eva sthitam ||
children.translated_text: If the animal is for one deity, he should say, "For the lord of the offering"; if it is for two deities, "For the two lords of the offering"; if it is for many deities, "For the lords of the offering." This is the settled rule.

children.text: prāsmā agnim bharateti ||
children.translated_text: "Bring <s>Agni</s> forward for him."

children.text: paśur vai nīyamānaḥ sa mṛtyum prāpaśyat sa devān nānvakāmayataituṃ taṃ devā abruvann ehi svargaṃ vai tvā lokaṃ gamayiṣyāma iti sa tathety abravīt tasya vai me yuṣmākam ekaḥ purastād aitv iti tatheti tasyāgniḥ purastād ait so 'gnim anuprācyavata ||
children.translated_text: The animal, being led, saw death and did not wish to go after the gods. The gods said to it, "Come; we will make you go to the heavenly world." It said, "So be it. But let one of you go before me." "So be it," they said. <s>Agni</s> went before it, and it followed after <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: tasmād āhur āgneyo vāva sarvaḥ paśur agniṃ hi so 'nuprācyavateti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they say, "Every animal is really connected with <s>Agni</s>, for it followed after <s>Agni</s>."

children.text: tasmād v asyāgnim purastāddharanti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they carry <s>Agni</s> before it.

children.text: stṛṇīta barhir ity oṣadhyātmā vai paśuḥ paśum eva tat sarvātmānaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: "Spread the <s>barhis</s>." The animal indeed has the plants as its self. Thus he makes the animal whole in self.

children.text: anv enam mātā manyatām anu pitānu bhrātā sagarbhyo 'nu sakhā sayūthya iti janitrair evainaṃ tat samanumatam ālabhante ||
children.translated_text: "Let its mother consent to it; let its father consent, its brother, its womb-mate, its friend, its herd-companion." Thus they seize it as one consented to by those who produced it.

children.text: udīcīnāṁ asya pado ni dhattāt sūryaṃ cakṣur gamayatād vātam prāṇam anvavasṛjatād antarikṣam asuṃ diśaḥ śrotram pṛthivīṃ śarīram ity eṣv evainaṃ tal lokeṣv ādadhāti ||
children.translated_text: "Set its feet northward; make its eye go to the sun; release its breath to the wind, its life-breath to the atmosphere, its hearing to the quarters, its body to the earth." Thus he places it in these very worlds.

children.text: ekadhāsya tvacam āchyatāt purā nābhyā apiśaso vapām utkhidatād antar evoṣmāṇaṃ vārayadhvād iti paśuṣv eva tat prāṇān dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: "Cut its skin in one piece; before the navel, without tearing, pull out the omentum; keep the warmth inside." Thus he places the breaths in the animals.

children.text: śyenam asya vakṣaḥ kṛṇutāt praśasā bāhū śalā doṣaṇī kaśyapevāṃsāchidre śroṇī kavaṣorū srekaparṇāṣṭhīvantā ṣaḍviṃśatir asya vaṅkrayas tā anuṣṭhyoccyāvayatād gātraṃ gātram asyānūnaṃ kṛṇutād ity aṅgāny evāsya tad gātrāṇi prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: "May he make its breast an eagle; its two arms with the praśasā, its two forearms with the śalā; its shoulders like those of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, its hips without a gap; its thighs like kavasa, its ankle-bones like srekaparṇa; its ribs are twenty-six. Having followed them, let him loosen each limb; let him make each of its limbs complete." By this he gratifies its limbs and members.

children.text: ūvadhyagoham pārthivaṃ khanatād ity āhauṣadhaṃ vā ūvadhyam iyaṃ vā oṣadhīnām pratiṣṭhā tad enat svāyām eva pratiṣṭhāyām antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He says, "Let him dig the earth-born ūvadhya down into the earth." The ūvadhya is a plant, and this earth is the foundation of plants. Thus in the end he establishes it in its own foundation.

children.text: Chapter 37

asnā rakṣaḥ saṃsṛjatād ity āha tuṣair vai phalīkaraṇair devā haviryajñebhyo rakṣāṃsi nirabhajann asnā mahāyajñāt sa yad asnā rakṣaḥ saṃsṛjatād ity āha rakṣāṃsy eva tat svena bhāgadheyena yajñān niravadayate ||
children.translated_text: He says, "Let him mix the rakṣas with blood." With husks and broken grains the gods excluded the rakṣases from the havir-sacrifices, and with blood from the great sacrifice. When he says, "Let him mix the rakṣas with blood," he thereby cuts the rakṣases off from the sacrifice with their own allotted share.

children.text: tad āhur na yajñe rakṣasāṃ kīrtayet kāni rakṣāṃsy ṛterakṣā vai yajña iti ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, "He should not mention the rakṣases in the sacrifice. What have rakṣases to do with it? The sacrifice is free from rakṣases."

children.text: tad u vā āhuḥ kīrtayed eva ||
children.translated_text: But others say, "He should indeed mention them."

children.text: yo vai bhāginam bhāgān nudate cayate vainaṃ sa yadi vainaṃ na cayate 'tha putram atha pautraṃ cayate tv evainam iti ||
