children.translated_text: For one who drives a sharer away from his shares harms him; and if he does not harm him, then he harms his son or his grandson. He certainly harms him.

children.text: sa yadi kīrtayed upāṃśu kīrtayet tira iva vā etad vāco yad upāṃśu tira ivaitad yad rakṣāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: If he should mention them, he should mention them in a low voice. What is spoken in a low voice is, as it were, beyond speech, and the rakṣases are, as it were, beyond sight.

children.text: atha yad uccaiḥ kīrtayed īśvaro hāsya vāco rakṣobhāṣo janitoḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if he should mention them aloud, he is liable to produce rakṣas-speech in his own speech.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ rākṣasīṃ vācaṃ vadati sa ||
children.translated_text: The man who speaks this rākṣasī speech is such a one.

children.text: yāṃ vai dṛpto vadati yām unmattaḥ sā vai rākṣasī vāk ||
children.translated_text: For the speech which an arrogant man speaks, and which a madman speaks, is rākṣasī speech.

children.text: nātmanā dṛpyati nāsya prajāyāṃ dṛpta ājāyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He himself does not become arrogant, nor is an arrogant man born among his offspring, who knows thus.

children.text: vaniṣṭhum asya mā rāviṣṭorūkam manyamānā ned vas toke tanaye ravitā ravacchamitāra iti ye caiva devānāṃ śamitāro ye ca manuṣyāṇāṃ tebhya evainaṃ tat paridadāti ||
children.translated_text: "Do not let its vaniṣṭhu cry out, thinking it a wound; lest a crier cry among your children and descendants, O slaughterers." Both the slaughterers of the gods and the slaughterers of men are meant; to them he thereby hands it over.

children.text: adhrigo śamīdhvaṃ suśami śamīdhvaṃ śamīdhvaṃ adhrigo iti trir brūyād apāpeti cādhrigur vai devānāṃ śamitāpāpo nigrabhītā śamitṛbhyaś caivainaṃ tan nigrabhītṛbhyaś ca samprayacchati ||
children.translated_text: He should say three times, "O <s>Adhrigu</s>, slaughter well; slaughter with good slaughter; slaughter, O <s>Adhrigu</s>," and also, "O <s>Apāpa</s>." For <s>Adhrigu</s> is the slaughterer of the gods, and <s>Apāpa</s> is the holder. He thereby delivers it to the slaughterers and to the holders.

children.text: śamitāro yad atra sukṛtaṃ kṛṇavathāsmāsu tad yad duṣkṛtam anyatra tad ity āhāgnir vai devānāṃ hotāsīt sa enaṃ vācā vyaśād vācā vā enaṃ hotā viśāsti tad yad arvāg yat paraḥ kṛntanti yad ulbaṇaṃ yad vithuraṃ kriyate śamitṛbhyaś caivainat tan nigrabhītṛbhyaś ca samanudiśati svasty eva hotonmucyate sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya ||
children.translated_text: He says, "O slaughterers, whatever well-done thing you do here, let that be with us; whatever ill-done thing, let that be elsewhere." <s>Agni</s> was the hotṛ of the gods; he cut it up with speech. With speech indeed the hotṛ cuts it up. Whatever they cut on this side or beyond, whatever excessive or irregular thing is done, he thereby assigns that to the slaughterers and to the holders. The hotṛ is released in welfare, for the sake of full life and full lifetime.

children.text: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus reaches the whole span of life.

children.text: Chapter 38
puruṣaṃ vai devāḥ paśum ālabhanta tasmād ālabdhān medha udakrāmat so 'śvam prāviśat tasmād aśvo medhyo 'bhavad athainam utkrāntamedham atyārjanta sa kimpuruṣo 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: The gods once took a man as the sacrificial animal. From him, when he had been taken, the <s>medha</s> (sacrificial essence) went out. It entered the horse; therefore the horse became fit for sacrifice. Then, when the <s>medha</s> had gone out from him, they rejected him, and he became a <s>kiṃpuruṣa</s>.

children.text: te 'śvam ālabhanta so 'śvād ālabdhād udakrāmat sa gām prāviśat tasmād gaur medhyo 'bhavad athainam utkrāntamedham atyārjanta sa gauramṛgo 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: They took the horse as the sacrificial animal. From the horse, when it had been taken, it went out. It entered the cow; therefore the cow became fit for sacrifice. Then, when the <s>medha</s> had gone out from him, they rejected him, and he became a gauramṛga.

children.text: te gām ālabhanta sa gor ālabdhād udakrāmat so 'vim prāviśat tasmād avir medhyo 'bhavad athainam utkrāntamedham atyārjanta sa gavayo 'bhavat te 'vim ālabhanta so 'ver ālabdhād udakrāmat so 'jam prāviśat tasmād ajo medhyo 'bhavad athainam utkrāntamedham atyārjanta sa uṣṭro 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: They took the cow as the sacrificial animal. From the cow, when it had been taken, it went out. It entered the sheep; therefore the sheep became fit for sacrifice. Then, when the <s>medha</s> had gone out from it, they rejected it, and it became a gavaya. They took the sheep as the sacrificial animal. From the sheep, when it had been taken, it went out. It entered the goat; therefore the goat became fit for sacrifice. Then, when the <s>medha</s> had gone out from it, they rejected it, and it became a camel.

children.text: so 'je jyoktamām ivāramata tasmād eṣa eteṣām paśūnām prayuktatamo yad ajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the goat it remained for a very long time, as it were. Therefore, among these animals, the goat is the one most commonly employed.

children.text: te 'jam ālabhanta so 'jād ālabdhād udakrāmat sa imām prāviśat tasmād iyam medhyābhavad athainam utkrāntamedham atyārjanta sa śarabho 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: They took the goat as the sacrificial animal. From the goat, when it had been taken, it went out. It entered this earth; therefore this earth became fit for sacrifice. Then, when the <s>medha</s> had gone out from it, they rejected it, and it became a <s>śarabha</s>.

children.text: ta eta utkrāntamedhā amedhyāḥ paśavas tasmād eteṣāṃ nāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: These animals from which the <s>medha</s> has gone out are unfit for sacrifice. Therefore one should not eat them.

children.text: tam asyām anvagacchan so 'nugato vrīhir abhavat tad yat paśau puroﾱāśam anunirvapanti samedhena naḥ paśuneṣṭam asat kevalena naḥ paśuneṣṭam asad iti ||
children.translated_text: They pursued it in this earth. When it was followed, it became rice. Therefore, when they offer the puroḍāśa cake after the animal, they do so thinking, "May our offering with the animal be with the <s>medha</s>; may our offering with the animal be complete for us."

children.text: samedhena hāsya paśuneṣṭam bhavati kevalena hāsya paśuneṣṭam bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For him who knows thus, the offering with the animal is indeed with the <s>medha</s>, and the offering with the animal is complete.

children.text: Chapter 39
sa vā eṣa paśur evālabhyate yat puroﾱāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this puroḍāśa cake is itself the sacrificial animal that is taken.

children.text: tasya yāni kiṃśārūṇi tāni romāṇi ye tuṣāḥ sā tvag ye phalīkaraṇās tad asṛg yat piṣṭaṃ kiknasās tan māṃsaṃ yat kiṃcitkaṃ sāraṃ tad asthi ||
children.translated_text: Its awns are the hairs; the husks are the skin; the broken grains are the blood; the flour is the kiknasa; that is the flesh; whatever little solid essence there is, that is the bone.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vā eṣa paśūnām medhena yajate yaḥ puroﾱāśena yajate ||
children.translated_text: Whoever sacrifices with the puroḍāśa sacrifices with the <s>medha</s> of all animals.

children.text: tasmād āhuḥ puroﾱāśasatraṃ lokyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they say, "The puroḍāśa-satra is suitable for attaining the world."

children.text: yuvam etāni divi rocanāny agniś ca soma sakratū adhattam yuvaṃ sindhūṃr abhiśaster avadyād agnīṣomāv amuñcataṃ gṛbhītān iti vapāyai yajati ||
children.translated_text: "You two, <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, of one resolve, placed these shining realms in heaven. You two, <s>Agni-Soma</s>, released those seized from curse and blame among the rivers." With this he sacrifices for the omentum.

children.text: sarvābhir vā eṣa devatābhir ālabdho bhavati yo dīkṣito bhavati tasmād āhur na dīkṣitasyāśnīyād iti sa yad agnīṣomāv amuñcataṃ gṛbhītān iti vapāyai yajati sarvābhya eva tad devatābhyo yajamānam pramuñcati tasmād āhur aśitavyaṃ vapāyāṃ hutāyāṃ yajamāno hi sa tarhi bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: One who has been consecrated is taken hold of by all the deities. Therefore they say, "One should not eat what belongs to the consecrated one." So when he sacrifices for the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) with, "<s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> released those who were seized," he thereby releases the sacrificer from all the deities. Therefore they say, "It is to be eaten when the omentum has been offered, for then he becomes the sacrificer."

children.text: ānyaṃ divo mātariśvā jabhāreti puroﾱāśasya yajati ||
children.translated_text: With, "<s>Mātariśvan</s> brought the other one from heaven," he sacrifices with the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake).

children.text: amathnād anyam pari śyeno 'drer itīta iva ca hy eṣa ita iva ca medhaḥ samāhṛto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: With, "The eagle churned the other one from the rock," for this sacrificial essence has been gathered together, as it were, from there and, as it were, from here.

children.text: svadasva havyā sam iṣo didīhīti puroﾱāśasviṣṭakṛto yajati ||
children.translated_text: With, "Make the oblations savory; kindle the refreshments together," he sacrifices for the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> of the <s>puroḍāśa</s>.

children.text: havir evāsmā etat svadayatīṣam ūrjam ātman dhatte ||
children.translated_text: He thereby makes this oblation savory for him and places food and vigor in himself.

children.text: iﾱām upahvayate paśavo vā iﾱā paśūn eva tad upahvayate paśūn yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He invokes <s>Iḍā</s>. <s>Iḍā</s> is cattle; he thereby invokes cattle, and he places cattle in the sacrificer.

children.text: Chapter 40
manotāyai haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānubrūhīty āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>adhvaryu</s> says, "Recite for <s>Manotā</s> as portions of the oblation are being cut off."

children.text: tvaṃ hy agne prathamo manoteti sūktam anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites the hymn, "For you, O <s>Agni</s>, are the first <s>manotā</s>."

children.text: tad āhur yad anyadevatya uta paśur bhavaty atha kasmād āgneyīr eva manotāyai haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānvāheti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since the animal may belong to another deity, why does he recite only Agni-verses for <s>Manotā</s> as portions of the oblation are being cut off?"

children.text: tisro vai devānām manotās tāsu hi teṣām manāṃsy otāni vāg vai devānām manotā tasyāṃ hi teṣām manāṃsy otāni gaur vai devānām manotā tasyāṃ hi teṣām manāṃsy otāny agnir vai devānām manotā tasmin hi teṣām manāṃsy otāny agniḥ sarvā manotā agnau manotāḥ saṃgacchante tasmād āgneyīr eva manotāyai haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānvāha ||
children.translated_text: There are three <s>manotās</s> of the gods, for in them their minds are woven. Speech is the <s>manotā</s> of the gods, for in it their minds are woven. The cow is the <s>manotā</s> of the gods, for in it their minds are woven. <s>Agni</s> is the <s>manotā</s> of the gods, for in him their minds are woven. <s>Agni</s> is all the <s>manotās</s>; the <s>manotās</s> come together in <s>Agni</s>. Therefore he recites only Agni-verses for <s>Manotā</s> as portions of the oblation are being cut off.

children.text: agnīṣomā haviṣaḥ prasthitasyeti haviṣo yajati ||
children.translated_text: With, "<s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, when the oblation has set forth," he sacrifices for the oblation.

children.text: haviṣa iti rūpasamṛddha prasthitasyeti rūpasamṛddhā ||
children.translated_text: "For the oblation" is fullness of form; "when it has set forth" is fullness of form.

children.text: sarvābhir hāsya samṛddhibhiḥ samṛddhaṃ havyaṃ devān apyeti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For one who knows thus, the oblation, complete with all its completions, goes to the gods.

children.text: vanaspatiṃ yajati prāṇo vai vanaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices to <s>Vanaspati</s>; <s>Vanaspati</s> is breath.

children.text: jīvaṃ hāsya havyaṃ devān apyeti yatraivaṃ vidvān vanaspatiṃ yajati ||
children.translated_text: A living oblation goes to the gods for him when one who knows thus sacrifices to <s>Vanaspati</s>.

children.text: sviṣṭakṛtaṃ yajati pratiṣṭhā vai sviṣṭakṛt pratiṣṭhāyām eva tad yajñam antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices to the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. The <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> is a firm foundation; at the end he thereby establishes the sacrifice upon a firm foundation.

children.text: iﾱām upahvayate paśavo vā iﾱā paśūn eva tad upahvayate paśūn yajamāne dadhāti dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He invokes <s>Iḍā</s>. <s>Iḍā</s> is cattle; he thereby invokes cattle, and he places cattle in the sacrificer; he places them indeed.

children.text: Chapter 41

devā vai yajñam atanvata tāṃs tanvānān asurā abhyāyan yajñaveśasam eṣāṃ kariṣyāma iti tān āprīte paśau pura iva paryagner yūpam prati purastād upāyaṃs te devāḥ pratibudhyāgnimayīḥ puras tripuram paryāsyanta yajñasya cātmanaś ca guptyai tā eṣām imā agnimayyaḥ puro dīpyamānā bhrājamānā atiṣṭhaṃs tā asurā anapadhṛṣyaivāpādravaṃs te 'gninaiva purastād asurarakṣāṃsy apāghnatāgninā paścāt ||
children.translated_text: The gods once stretched out the sacrifice. As they were stretching it out, the <s>Asuras</s> came upon them, thinking, "We shall make ruin of their sacrifice." At the prepared animal, as if at a fortress, they approached the sacrificial post from the front. The gods, becoming aware, cast fiery strongholds, a triple stronghold, around themselves for the protection of the sacrifice and of themselves. These fiery strongholds of theirs stood blazing and shining. The <s>Asuras</s>, unable to assail them, ran away. With <s>Agni</s> they drove away the <s>Asuras</s> and <s>Rakṣases</s> from the front, and with <s>Agni</s> from behind.

children.text: tathaivaitad yajamānā yat paryagni kurvanty agnimayīr eva tat puras tripuram paryasyante yajñasya cātmanaś ca guptyai tasmāt paryagni kurvanti tasmāt paryagnaye 'nvāha ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, when sacrificers perform the <s>paryagni</s>, they cast fiery strongholds, a triple stronghold, around themselves for the protection of the sacrifice and of themselves. Therefore they perform the <s>paryagni</s>; therefore he recites for the <s>paryagni</s>.

children.text: taṃ vā etam paśum āprītaṃ santam paryagnikṛtam udañcaṃ nayanti ||
children.translated_text: They lead this animal, when it has been prepared and had the <s>paryagni</s> performed around it, northward.

children.text: tasyolmukam purastād dharanti ||
children.translated_text: They carry a firebrand in front of it.

children.text: yajamāno vā eṣa nidānena yat paśur anena jyotiṣā yajamānaḥ purojyotiḥ svargaṃ lokam eṣyatīti tena jyotiṣā yajamānaḥ purojyotiḥ svargaṃ lokam eti ||
children.translated_text: This animal is the sacrificer by means of the tether. With this light the sacrificer, having light in front, will go to the heavenly world; by that light the sacrificer, having light in front, does go to the heavenly world.

children.text: taṃ yatra nihaniṣyanto bhavanti tad adhvaryur barhir adhastād upāsyati ||
children.translated_text: Where they are about to kill it, there the <s>adhvaryu</s> spreads the <s>barhis</s> beneath.

children.text: yad evainam ada āprītaṃ santam paryagnikṛtam bahirvedi nayanti barhiṣadam evainaṃ tat kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Since, after it has been prepared and had the <s>paryagni</s> performed around it, they lead it outside the altar, they thereby make it seated on the <s>barhis</s>.

children.text: tasyovadhyagohaṃ khananti ||
children.translated_text: They dig a pit for concealing its entrails.

children.text: auṣadhaṃ vā ūvadhyam iyaṃ vā oṣadhīnām pratiṣṭhā tad enat svāyām eva pratiṣṭhāyām antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayanti ||
children.translated_text: The entrails are vegetable matter, and this earth is the foundation of plants. Thus at the end they establish it in its own foundation.

children.text: tad āhur yad eṣa havir eva yat paśur athāsya bahv apaiti lomāni tvag asṛk kuṣṭhikāḥ śaphā viṣāṇe skandati piśitaṃ kenāsya tad āpūryata iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since this animal is itself an oblation, why does much of it go away: the hairs, the skin, the blood, the hoofs, the horns, the excrement, and the flesh fall away. By what is that part of it filled up?"

children.text: yad evaitat paśau puroﾱāśam anunirvapanti tenaivāsya tad āpūryate ||
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>puroḍāśa</s> they offer additionally with the animal, by that this part of it is filled up.

children.text: paśubhyo vai medhā udakrāmaṃs tau vrīhiś caiva yavaś ca bhūtāv ajāyetāṃ tad yat paśau puroﾱāśam anunirvapanti samedhena naḥ paśuneṣṭam asat kevalena naḥ paśuneṣṭam asad iti ||
children.translated_text: The sacrificial essence went out from the animals; having become rice and barley, the two were born. Therefore, when they offer a <s>puroḍāśa</s> additionally with the animal, it is so that, "Our animal-offering may be with sacrificial essence; our animal-offering may be complete."

children.text: samedhena hāsya paśuneṣṭam bhavati kevalena hāsya paśuneṣṭam bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For one who knows thus, his animal-offering is with sacrificial essence; his animal-offering is complete.

children.text: Chapter 42
tasya vapām utkhidyāharanti tām adhvaryuḥ sruveṇābhighārayann āha stokebhyo 'nubrūhīti ||
children.translated_text: They tear out its omentum and bring it. The <s>adhvaryu</s>, sprinkling it with the <s>sruva</s> (offering spoon), says, "Recite for the drops."

children.text: tad yat stokāḥ ścotanti sarvadevatyā vai stokā nen ma ime 'nabhiprītā devān gacchān iti ||
children.translated_text: When the drops trickle, the drops belong to all the deities. He does this thinking, "Let these of mine not go to the gods unpropitiated."

children.text: juṣasva saprathastamam ity anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Accept what is most widely extended."

children.text: vaco devapsarastamam havyājuhvāna āsanīti ||
children.translated_text: "Speech, most possessed of divine nymphs, sat offering oblations with the oblation-tongue."

children.text: agner evaināṃs tad āsye juhoti ||
children.translated_text: He thereby offers them into the mouth of <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: imaṃ no yajñam amṛteṣu dhehīti sūktam anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites the hymn, "Place this sacrifice of ours among the immortals."

children.text: imā havyā jātavedo juṣasveti havyajuṣṭim āśāste ||
children.translated_text: With "Accept these oblations, O <s>Jātavedas</s>," he seeks the enjoyment of the oblations.

children.text: stokānām agne medaso ghṛtasyeti medasaś ca hi ghṛtasya ca bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: With "Of the drops, O <s>Agni</s>, of the fat, of the ghee," for they are indeed of both fat and ghee.

children.text: hotaḥ prāśāna prathamo niṣadyety agnir vai devānāṃ hotāgne prāśāna prathamo niṣadyety eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: With "O <s>hotṛ</s>, eat first, having sat down": <s>Agni</s> is indeed the <s>hotṛ</s> of the gods; thus he says just this, "O <s>Agni</s>, eat first, having sat down."

children.text: ghṛtavantaḥ pāvaka te stokā ścotanti medasa iti medasaś ca hy eva hi ghṛtasya ca bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: With "Rich in ghee, O purifier, your drops of fat drip," for they are indeed of both fat and ghee.

children.text: svadharman devavītaye śreṣṭhaṃ no dhehi vāryam ity āśiṣam āśāste ||
children.translated_text: With "According to your own law, for the divine course, place the best desirable good for us," he seeks a blessing.

children.text: tubhyaṃ stokā ghṛtaścuto 'gne viprāya santyeti ghṛtaścuto hi bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: With "For you, O <s>Agni</s>, inspired one, there are drops flowing with ghee," for they are indeed flowing with ghee.

children.text: ṛṣiḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sam idhyase yajñasya prāvitā bhaveti yajñasamṛddhim āśāste ||
children.translated_text: With "As the best seer you are kindled; be the furtherer of the sacrifice," he seeks the success of the sacrifice.

children.text: tubhyaṃ ścotanty adhrigo śacīva stokāso agne medaso ghṛtasyeti medasaś ca hy eva hi ghṛtasya ca bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: With "For you, O uninjured <s>Agni</s>, with power, the drops of fat and ghee drip," for they are indeed of both fat and ghee.

children.text: kaviśasto bṛhatā bhānunāgā havyā juṣasva medhireti havyajuṣṭim evāśāste ||
children.translated_text: With "Praised by poets, with great radiance, come; accept the oblations, O wise one," he seeks precisely the enjoyment of the oblations.

children.text: ojiṣṭhaṃ te madhyato meda udbhṛtam pra te vayaṃ dadāmahe ścotanti te vaso stokā adhi tvaci prati tān devaśo vihīti ||
children.translated_text: With "The strongest fat, taken from your middle, we present to you; your drops drip upon the skin, O good one; distribute them among the gods."

children.text: abhy evaināṃs tad vaṣaṭkaroti yathā somasyāgne vīhīti ||
children.translated_text: With that he pronounces the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-call over them, just as with "O <s>Agni</s>, partake of the Soma."

children.text: tad yat stokāḥ ścotanti sarvadevatyā vai stokās tasmād iyaṃ stokaśo vṛṣṭir vibhaktopācarati ||
children.translated_text: As to the fact that the drops drip: the drops belong to all the gods. Therefore this rain comes forth distributed drop by drop.

children.text: Chapter 43
tad āhuḥ kā svāhākṛtīnām puronuvākyāḥ kaḥ praiṣaḥ kā yājyeti ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, "What are the preliminary verses of the <s>svāhā</s>-offerings? What is the summons? What is the offering-verse?"

children.text: yā evaitā anvāhaitāḥ puronuvākyā yaḥ praiṣaḥ sa praiṣo yā yājyā sā yājyā ||
children.translated_text: Those very verses which he recites are the preliminary verses; that which is the summons is the summons; that which is the offering-verse is the offering-verse.

children.text: tad āhuḥ kā devatāḥ svāhākṛtaya iti ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, "What deities are the <s>svāhā</s>-offerings?"

children.text: viśve devā iti brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should say, "The <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>."

children.text: tasmāt svāhākṛtaṃ havir adantu devā iti yajantīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they sacrifice with "Let the gods eat the oblation made with <s>svāhā</s>."

children.text: devā vai yajñena śrameṇa tapasāhutibhiḥ svargaṃ lokam ajayaṃs teṣāṃ vapāyām eva hutāyāṃ svargo lokaḥ prākhyāyata te vapām eva hutvānādṛtyetarāṇi karmāṇy ūrdhvāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs tato vai manuṣyāś ca ṛṣayaś ca devānāṃ yajñavāstv abhyāyan yajñasya kiṃcid eṣiṣyāmaḥ prajñātyā iti te 'bhitaḥ paricaranta et paśum eva nirāntraṃ śayānaṃ te vidur iyān vāva kila paśur yāvatī vapeti ||
children.translated_text: The gods, by sacrifice, toil, austerity, and oblations, won the heavenly world. When the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) alone had been offered for them, the heavenly world appeared. Having offered only the <s>vapā</s>, and disregarding the other rites, they went upward to the heavenly world. Then humans and seers approached the sacrificial site of the gods, thinking, "Perhaps we shall find some trace of the sacrifice." Going about on all sides, they found the animal lying with only its entrails removed. They understood, "The animal is really only as much as the <s>vapā</s>."

children.text: sa etāvān eva paśur yāvatī vapā ||
children.translated_text: The animal is only as much as the <s>vapā</s>.

children.text: atha yad enaṃ tṛtīyasavane śrapayitvā juhvati bhūyasībhir na āhutibhir iṣṭam asat kevalena naḥ paśuneṣṭam asad iti ||
children.translated_text: Now when, after cooking it at the third pressing, they offer it, they do so thinking, "May our sacrifice be performed with many oblations; may our sacrifice be performed with the animal alone."

children.text: bhūyasībhir hāsyāhutibhir iṣṭaṃ bhavati kevalena hāsya paśuneṣṭaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For him who knows thus, the sacrifice is performed with many oblations, and his sacrifice is performed with the animal alone.

children.text: Chapter 44
sā vā eṣāmṛtāhutir eva yad vapāhutir amṛtāhutir agnyāhutir amṛtāhutir ājyāhutir amṛtāhutiḥ somāhutir etā vā aśarīrā āhutayo yā vai kāścāśarīrā āhutayo 'mṛtatvam eva tābhir yajamāno jayati ||
children.translated_text: That <s>vapā</s>-offering is indeed an immortal oblation. An <s>Agni</s>-offering is an immortal oblation; a ghee-offering is an immortal oblation; a Soma-offering is an immortal oblation. These are bodiless oblations. Whatever oblations are bodiless, by them the sacrificer wins immortality.

children.text: sā vā eṣā reta eva yad vapā preva vai reto līyate preva vapā līyate śuklaṃ vai retaḥ śuklā vapāśarīraṃ vai reto 'śarīrā vapā yad vai lohitaṃ yan māṃsaṃ taccharīraṃ tasmād brūyād yāvad alohitaṃ tāvat parivāsayeti ||
children.translated_text: That <s>vapā</s> is indeed seed. Seed dissolves away, and the <s>vapā</s> dissolves away. Seed is white, and the <s>vapā</s> is white. Seed is bodiless, and the <s>vapā</s> is bodiless. Whatever is blood and whatever is flesh, that is body. Therefore he should say, "Let him keep it covered for as long as it is without blood."

children.text: sā pañcāvattā bhavati yady api caturavattī yajamānaḥ syād atha pañcāvattaiva vapā ||
children.translated_text: It is divided into five portions, even if the sacrificer is one whose offerings are divided into four; still the <s>vapā</s> is divided into five portions.

children.text: ājyasyopastṛṇāti hiraṇyaśalko vapā hiraṇyaśalka ājyasyopariṣṭād abhighārayati ||
children.translated_text: He spreads ghee beneath it. The <s>vapā</s> has a gold flake. He pours ghee over it from above, with a gold flake.

children.text: tad āhur yaddhiraṇyaṃ na vidyeta kathaṃ syād iti dvir ājyasyopastīrya vapām avadāya dvir upariṣṭād abhighārayati ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, "If gold were not available, how would it be?" Having spread ghee twice beneath, having cut off the <s>vapā</s>, he pours ghee over it twice from above.

children.text: amṛtaṃ vā ājyam amṛtaṃ hiraṇyaṃ tatra sa kāma upāpto ya ājye tatra sa kāma upāpto yo hiraṇye tatpañca sampadyante ||
children.translated_text: Ghee is immortality; gold is immortality. In that case, the same desire is attained which is attained in ghee, and the same desire is attained which is attained in gold. That makes five in all.

children.text: pāṅkto 'yam puruṣaḥ pañcadhā vihito lomāni tvaṅ māṃsam asthi majjā sa yāvān eva puruṣas tāvantaṃ yajamānaṃ saṃskṛtyāgnau devayonyāṃ juhoty agnir vai devayoniḥ so 'gner devayonyā āhutibhyaḥ sambhūya hiraṇyaśarīra ūrdhvaḥ svargaṃ lokam eti ||
children.translated_text: This person is fivefold, arranged in five parts: hairs, skin, flesh, bone, and marrow. Having prepared the sacrificer to the full extent of a person, he offers him into the fire, the womb of the gods. <s>Agni</s> is indeed the womb of the gods. Coming into being from <s>Agni</s>, the womb of the gods, from the oblations, he rises upward with a golden body and goes to the heavenly world.

children.text: Chapter 45
devebhyaḥ prātaryāvabhyo hotar anubrūhīty āhādhvaryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>adhvaryu</s> says, "O <s>hotṛ</s>, recite for the gods who go in the morning."

children.text: ete vāva devāḥ prātaryāvāṇo yad agnir uṣā aśvinau ta ete saptabhiḥ saptabhiś chandobhir āgacchanti ||
children.translated_text: These indeed are the gods who go in the morning, namely <s>Agni</s>, <s>Uṣas</s>, and the <s>Aśvins</s>. They come with seven meters each.

children.text: āsya devāḥ prātaryāvāṇo havaṃ gacchanti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The gods who go in the morning come to the call of the one who knows thus.

children.text: prajāpatau vai svayaṃ hotari prātaranuvākam anuvakṣyaty ubhaye devāsurā yajñam upāvasann asmabhyam anuvakṣyaty asmabhyam iti sa vai devebhya evānvabravīt ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Prajāpati</s> himself, as <s>hotṛ</s>, was about to recite the morning litany, both the gods and the asuras sat near the sacrifice, saying, "He will recite for us; he will recite for us." He recited only for the gods.

children.text: tato vai devā abhavan parāsurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the gods came into being, and the asuras were defeated.

children.text: bhavaty ātmanā parāsya dviṣan pāpmā bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus comes into being in himself, while his hating evil, his enemy, is defeated.

children.text: prātar vai sa taṃ devebhyo 'nvabravīd yat prātar anvabravīt tat prātaranuvākasya prātaranuvākatvam ||
children.translated_text: In the morning he recited it to the gods. Because he recited it in the morning, that is why the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> has the character of a morning recitation.

children.text: mahati rātryā anūcyaḥ sarvasyai vācaḥ sarvasya brahmaṇaḥ parigṛhītyai yo vai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭhatām aśnute tasya vācam proditām anupravadanti tasmān mahati rātryā anūcyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be recited in the great night, for the grasping of all speech and all <s>brahman</s>. For when someone becomes eminent and attains superiority, people speak after the speech uttered by him. Therefore it should be recited in the great night.

children.text: purā vācaḥ pravaditor anūcyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be recited before the speaker of speech has spoken.

children.text: yad vāci proditāyām anubrūyād anyasyaivainam uditānuvādinaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: If he were to recite after speech had been uttered, he would make him merely one who repeats what another has said.

children.text: tasmān mahati rātryā anūcyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it should be recited in the great night.

children.text: purā śakunivādād anubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should recite before the cry of birds.

children.text: nirṛter vā etan mukhaṃ yad vayāṃsi yacchakunayas tad yat purā śakunivādād anubrūyān māyajñiyāṃ vācam proditām anupravadiṣmeti tasmān mahati rātryā anūcyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this is the mouth of <s>Nirṛti</s>, namely flying creatures, birds. Therefore, if he recites before the cry of birds, he does so thinking, "May we not speak after speech unfit for sacrifice has been uttered." Therefore it should be recited in the great night.

children.text: atho khalu yadaivādhvaryur upākuryād athānubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: But also, just when the <s>adhvaryu</s> has begun, then he should recite.

children.text: yadā vā adhvaryur upākaroti vācaivopākaroti vācā hotānvāha vāgghi brahma tatra sa kāma upāpto yo vāci ca brahmaṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: For when the <s>adhvaryu</s> begins, he begins with speech. With speech the <s>hotṛ</s> recites after him, for speech indeed is <s>brahman</s>. There that desire is attained which is in speech and in <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: Chapter 46

prajāpatau vai svayam hotari prātaranuvākam anuvakṣyati sarvā devatā āśaṃsanta mām abhi pratipatsyati mām abhīti sa prajāpatir aikṣata yady ekāṃ devatām ādiṣṭāmabhi pratipatsyāmītarā me kena devatā upāptā bhaviṣyantīti sa etām ṛcam apaśyad āpo revatīr ity āpo vai sarvā devatā revatyaḥ sarvā devatāḥ sa etayarcā prātaranuvākam pratyapadyata tāḥ sarvā devatāḥ prāmodanta mām abhi pratyapādi mām abhīti ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Prajāpati</s> himself was the <s>hotṛ</s> and was about to recite the <s>prātaranuvāka</s>, all the deities hoped, "He will turn toward me, toward me." Then <s>Prajāpati</s> considered, "If I turn toward one specified deity, by what means will the other deities be attained for me?" He saw this verse, "Āpo revatīḥ." The waters are all deities, and the rich ones are all deities. With this verse he entered upon the <s>prātaranuvāka</s>. All those deities rejoiced, saying, "He has turned toward me, toward me."

children.text: sarvā hāsmin devatāḥ prātaranuvākam anubruvati pramodante ||
children.translated_text: All the deities rejoice in him when he recites the <s>prātaranuvāka</s>.

children.text: sarvābhir hāsya devatābhiḥ prātaranuvākaḥ pratipanno bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For him who knows thus, the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> has been entered upon with all the deities.

children.text: te devā abibhayur ādātāro vai na imam prātaryajñam asurā yathaujīyāṃso balīyāṃsa evam iti tān abravīd indro mā bibhīta triṣamṛddham ebhyo 'ham prātar vajram prahartāsmīty etāṃ vāva tad ṛcam abravīd vajras tena yad aponaptrīyā vajras tena yat triṣṭub vajras tena yad vāk tam ebhyaḥ prāharat tenainān ahaṃs tato vai devā abhavan parā asurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods were afraid: "The <s>Asuras</s>, being stronger and more powerful, will surely seize this morning sacrifice from us." <s>Indra</s> said to them, "Do not be afraid. In the morning I shall hurl against them a triply complete <s>vajra</s>." That very verse was what he called a <s>vajra</s>: a <s>vajra</s> because it belongs to <s>Apāṃ Napāt</s>, a <s>vajra</s> because it is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, and a <s>vajra</s> because it is speech. He hurled it against them; with it he struck them down. Then the gods prevailed and the <s>Asuras</s> were defeated.

children.text: bhavaty ātmanā parāsya dviṣan pāpmā bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers in his own person, and his hateful evil, his rival, is defeated, who knows thus.

children.text: tad āhuḥ sa vai hotā syād ya etasyām ṛci sarvāṇi chandāṃsi prajanayed ity eṣā vāva trir anūktā sarvāṇi chandāṃsi bhavaty eṣā chandasām prajātiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "He indeed would be a <s>hotṛ</s> who could generate all the meters in this verse." This verse, recited three times, indeed becomes all the meters; this is the generation of the meters.

children.text: Chapter 47
śatam anūcyam āyuṣkāmasya śatāyur vai puruṣaḥ śatavīryaḥ śatendriya āyuṣy evainaṃ tad vīrya indriye dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: One hundred should be recited for one who desires long life. A man indeed has a hundred years of life, a hundredfold vigor, and a hundredfold power of the senses. Thereby he places him in life, vigor, and sensory power.

children.text: trīṇi ca śatāni ṣaṣṭiś cānūcyāni yajñakāmasya trīṇi ca vai śatāni ṣaṣṭiś ca saṃvatsarasyāhāni tāvān saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatir yajñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Three hundred and sixty should be recited for one who desires sacrifice. For three hundred and sixty are the days of the year; so great is the year. The year is <s>Prajāpati</s>, and <s>Prajāpati</s> is the sacrifice.

children.text: upainaṃ yajño namati yasyaivaṃ vidvāṃs trīṇi ca śatāni ṣaṣṭiṃ cānvāha ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice bows toward the one for whom a man who knows thus recites three hundred and sixty.

children.text: sapta ca śatāni viṃśatiś cānūcyāni prajāpaśukāmasya sapta ca vai śatāni viṃśatiś ca saṃvatsarasyāhorātrās tāvān saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatir yam prajāyamānaṃ viśvaṃ rūpam idaṃ anuprajāyate prajāpatim eva tat prajāyamānam prajayā paśubhir anuprajāyate prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: Seven hundred and twenty should be recited for one who desires offspring and cattle. For seven hundred and twenty are the days and nights of the year; so great is the year. The year is <s>Prajāpati</s>. This whole form follows after <s>Prajāpati</s> as he is being born; thereby he follows after <s>Prajāpati</s>, as he is being born, with offspring and cattle, for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is born with offspring and cattle, who knows thus.

children.text: aṣṭau śatāny anūcyāny abrāhmaṇoktasya yo vā duruktoktaḥ śamalagṛhīto yajetāṣṭākṣarā vai gāyatrī gāyatryā vai devāḥ pāpmānaṃ śamalam apāghnata gāyatryaivāsya tat pāpmānaṃ śamalam apahanti ||
children.translated_text: Eight hundred should be recited for one who has been called non-Brahman, or for one who, having been spoken of with bad words and seized by impurity, should sacrifice. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> indeed has eight syllables; with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> the gods drove away evil and impurity. With the <s>Gāyatrī</s> he thereby drives away his evil and impurity.

children.text: apa pāpmānaṃ hate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He drives evil away, who knows thus.

children.text: sahasram anūcyaṃ svargakāmasya sahasrāśvīne vā itaḥ svargo lokaḥ svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai sampattyai saṃgatyai ||
children.translated_text: A thousand should be recited for one who desires the heavenly world. From here the heavenly world is a thousand <s>aśvina</s>-measures away; this is for reaching, attaining, and joining the heavenly world.

children.text: aparimitam anūcyam aparimito vai prajāpatiḥ prajāpater vā etad ukthaṃ yat prātaranuvākas tasmin sarve kāmā avarudhyante sa yad aparimitam anvāha sarveṣāṃ kāmānām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: An unlimited number should be recited. <s>Prajāpati</s> is unlimited, and this <s>uktha</s> of <s>Prajāpati</s> is the <s>prātaranuvāka</s>. In it all desires are secured. When he recites without limit, it is for the securing of all desires.

children.text: sarvān kāmān avarunddhe ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He secures all desires, who knows thus.

children.text: tasmād aparimitam evānūcyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore an unlimited number should indeed be recited.

children.text: saptāgneyāni chandāṃsy anvāha sapta vai devalokāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites seven meters belonging to <s>Agni</s>; seven indeed are the worlds of the gods.

children.text: sarveṣu devalokeṣu rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers in all the worlds of the gods, who knows thus.

children.text: saptoṣasyāni chandāṃsy anvāha sapta vai grāmyāḥ paśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites seven meters belonging to <s>Uṣas</s>; seven indeed are the domestic animals.

children.text: ava grāmyān paśūn runddhe ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He secures the domestic animals, who knows thus.

children.text: saptāśvināni chandāṃsy anvāha saptadhā vai vāg avadat tāvad vai vāg avadat sarvasyai vācaḥ sarvasya brahmaṇaḥ parigṛhītyai ||
children.translated_text: He recites seven meters belonging to the <s>Aśvins</s>. Speech spoke in seven ways; speech spoke to that extent, for the grasping of all speech and all <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tisro devatā anvāha trayo vā ime trivṛto lokā eṣām eva lokānām abhijityai ||
children.translated_text: He recites three deities. These three worlds are indeed threefold; this is for the conquest of these very worlds.

children.text: Chapter 48
tad āhuḥ katham anūcyaḥ prātaranuvāka iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "How should the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> be recited?"

children.text: yathāchandasam anūcyaḥ prātaranuvākāḥ prajāpater vā etāny aṅgāni yac chandāṃsy eṣa u eva prajāpatir yo yajate tad yajamānāya hitam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>prātaranuvāka</s> should be recited according to the meters. For the meters are these limbs of <s>Prajāpati</s>; and he who sacrifices is this very <s>Prajāpati</s>. That is beneficial for the sacrificer.

children.text: paccho 'nūcyaḥ prātaranuvākaś catuṣpādā vai paśavaḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: The <s>prātaranuvāka</s> should be recited by quarters. Animals are four-footed; this is for securing animals.

children.text: ardharcaśa evānūcyo yathaivainam etad anvāha pratiṣṭhāyā eva dvipratiṣṭho vai puruṣaś catuṣpādāḥ paśavo yajamānam eva tad dvipratiṣṭhaṃ catuṣpātsu paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati tasmād ardharcaśa evānūcyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be recited in half-verses, just as he recites it for him in this way, for the sake of firm establishment. For man stands on two supports, and animals are four-footed; he thereby establishes the sacrificer, who stands on two supports, among four-footed animals. Therefore it should be recited in half-verses.

children.text: tad āhur yad vyūﾱhaḥ prātaranuvākaḥ katham avyūﾱho bhavatīti yad evāsya bṛhatī madhyān naitīti brūyāt teneti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since the <s>prātaranuvāka</s> is expanded, how does it become unexpanded?" He should say, "By the fact that its Bṛhatī does not depart from the middle."

children.text: āhutibhāgā vā anyā devatā anyāḥ stomabhāgāś chandobhāgās tā yā agnāv āhutayo hūyante tābhir āhutibhāgāḥ prīṇāty atha yat stuvanti ca śaṃsanti ca tena stomabhāgāś chandobhāgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some deities are sharers in oblations, while others are sharers in <s>stoma</s> chants and sharers in meters. The oblations that are offered in the fire: with them he pleases the oblation-sharers. But by the fact that they chant and recite, he pleases the <s>stoma</s>-sharers and the meter-sharers.

children.text: ubhayyo hāsyaitā devatāḥ prītā abhīṣṭā bhavanti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Both groups of these deities become pleased and gratified for him who knows thus.

children.text: trayastriṃśad vai devāḥ somapās trayastriṃśad asomapā aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāḥ prajāpatiś ca vaṣaṭkāraś caite devā somapā ekādaśa prayājā ekādaśānuyājā ekādaśopayājā ete 'somapāḥ paśubhājanāḥ somena somapān prīṇāti paśunāsomapān ||
children.translated_text: Thirty-three gods are Soma-drinkers, and thirty-three are non-Soma-drinkers. The eight <s>Vasus</s>, the eleven <s>Rudras</s>, the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the <s>Vaṣaṭkāra</s>: these gods are Soma-drinkers. The eleven <s>prayājas</s>, the eleven <s>anuyājas</s>, and the eleven <s>upayājas</s>: these are non-Soma-drinkers, having the animal as their portion. With Soma he pleases the Soma-drinkers; with the animal he pleases the non-Soma-drinkers.

children.text: ubhayyo hāsyaitā devatāḥ prītā abhīṣṭā bhavanti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Both groups of these deities become pleased and gratified for him who knows thus.

children.text: abhūd uṣā ruśatpaśur ity uttamayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He concludes with the last verse, "Dawn has appeared, with shining cattle."

children.text: tad āhur yat trīn kratūn anvāhāgneyam uṣasyam āśvinaṃ katham asyaikayarcā paridadhataḥ sarve trayaḥ kratavaḥ parihitā bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since he recites three rites, the one for <s>Agni</s>, the one for <s>Uṣas</s>, and the one for the <s>Aśvins</s>, how, when he concludes with a single verse, are all three rites enclosed?"

children.text: abhūd uṣā ruśatpaśur ity uṣaso rūpam āgnir adhāyy ṛtviya ity agner ayoji vāṃ vṛṣaṇvasū ratho dasrāv amartyo mādhvī mama śrutaṃ havam ity aśvinor evam u hāsyaikayarcā paridadhataḥ sarve trayaḥ kratavaḥ parihitā bhavanti bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: "Dawn has appeared, with shining cattle" is the form of <s>Uṣas</s>; "<s>Agni</s> has been kindled at the proper time" is that of <s>Agni</s>; "Your chariot has been yoked, O two rich in bulls, O wonder-working immortals; hear my honeyed call" is that of the <s>Aśvins</s>. Thus, when he concludes with a single verse, all three rites are enclosed for him.

children.text: Chapter 49

ṛṣayo vai sarasvatyāṃ satram āsata te kavaṣam ailūṣaṃ somād anayan dāsyāḥ putraḥ kitavo 'brāhmaṇaḥ kathaṃ no madhye 'dīkṣiṣṭeti tam bahir dhanvodavahann atrainam pipāsā hantu sarasvatyā udakam mā pād iti sa bahir dhanvodūﾱhaḥ pipāsayā vitta etad aponaptrīyam apaśyat pra devatrā brahmaṇe gātur etv iti tenāpām priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchat tam āpo 'nūdāyaṃs taṃ sarasvatī samantam paryadhāvat ||
children.translated_text: The seers once held a <s>sattra</s> on the <s>Sarasvatī</s>. They drove <s>Kavaṣa Ailūṣa</s> away from the Soma, saying, "He is the son of a slave-woman, a gambler, not a Brahmin. How has he been consecrated among us?" They carried him outside into the desert, saying, "Let thirst kill him here; may he not obtain the water of <s>Sarasvatī</s>." Carried outside into the desert and afflicted by thirst, he saw this hymn to <s>Apāṃ Napāt</s>, "Let a path go forth to the gods for the sacred formulation." With it he reached the dear abode of the waters. The waters flowed after him, and <s>Sarasvatī</s> ran all around him.

children.text: tasmāddhāpy etarhi parisārakam ity ācakṣate yad enaṃ sarasvatī samantam parisasāra ||
children.translated_text: Therefore even now they call it the <s>Parisāraka</s>, because <s>Sarasvatī</s> flowed all around him.

children.text: te vā ṛṣayo 'bruvan vidur vā imaṃ devā upemaṃ hvayāmahā iti tatheti tam upāhvayanta tam upahūyaitad aponaptrīyam akurvata pra devatrā brahmaṇe gātur etv iti tenāpām priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchann upa devānām ||
children.translated_text: Those seers said, "The gods know this man. Let us call him to us." "So be it," they said. They called him to them; and after calling him, they performed this rite of <s>Apāṃ Napāt</s>, "Let a path go forth to the gods for the sacred formulation." With it they reached the dear abode of the waters, and the nearness of the gods.

children.text: upāpām priyaṃ dhāma gacchaty upa devānāṃ jayati paramaṃ lokaṃ ya evam veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān etad aponaptrīyaṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: He reaches the dear abode of the waters and wins the highest world of the gods, who knows thus, and who, knowing thus, performs this rite of <s>Apāṃ Napāt</s>.

children.text: tat saṃtatam anubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should recite it continuously.

children.text: saṃtatavarṣī ha prajābhyaḥ parjanyo bhavati yatraivaṃ vidvān etat saṃtatam anvāha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Parjanya</s> becomes one who rains continuously for the creatures wherever one who knows thus recites this continuously.

children.text: yad avagrāham anubrūyāj jīmūtavarṣī ha prajābhyaḥ parjanyaḥ syāt tasmāt tat saṃtatam evānūcyam ||
children.translated_text: If he were to recite it with breaks, <s>Parjanya</s> would rain only from clouds for the creatures. Therefore it should be recited continuously.

children.text: tasya triḥ prathamāṃ saṃtatam anvāha tenaiva tat sarvaṃ saṃtatam anūktam bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Of it he recites the first verse three times continuously. By that, all of it becomes recited continuously.

children.text: Chapter 50
tā etā navānantarāyam anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites these nine without interruption.

children.text: hinotā no adhvaraṃ devayajyeti daśamīm ||
children.translated_text: As the tenth, he recites, "Set our rite in motion, O divine worship."

children.text: āvarvṛtatīr adha nu dvidhārā ity avṛttāsv ekadhanāsu ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Turning back, now with two streams," while the <s>ekadhanā</s> waters have not yet turned back.

children.text: pratiyad āpo adṛśram āyatīr iti pratidṛśyamānāsu ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "When the approaching waters came into view," while they are being seen approaching.

children.text: ā dhenavaḥ payasā tūrṇyarthā ity upāyatīṣu ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "The milch cows, with milk, swiftly seeking their goal," while they are approaching.

children.text: sam anyā yanty upa yanty anyā iti samāyatīṣu ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Some go together; others come near," while they are coming together.

children.text: āpo vā aspardhanta vayam pūrvaṃ yajñaṃ vakṣyāmo vayam iti yāś cemāḥ pūrvedyur vasatīvaryo gṛhyante yāś ca prātar ekadhanās tā bhṛgur apaśyad āpo vai spardhanta iti tā etayarcā samajñapayat sam anyā yanty upa yanty anyā iti tāḥ samajānata ||
children.translated_text: The waters once contended, saying, "We shall carry the sacrifice first; we shall." Those <s>Vasatīvarī</s> waters that are taken on the previous day and those <s>ekadhanā</s> waters that are taken in the morning: <s>Bhṛgu</s> saw them contending, thinking, "The waters are contending." With this verse he brought them to agreement, "Some go together; others come near." They came to agreement.

children.text: saṃjānānā hāsyāpo yajñaṃ vahanti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The waters, being in agreement, carry the sacrifice for him who knows thus.

children.text: āpo na devīr upa yanti hotriyam iti hotṛcamase samavanīyamānāsv anvāha vasatīvarīṣv ekadhanāsu ca ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "The divine waters come to the <s>hotṛ</s>'s portion," when the <s>Vasatīvarī</s> and <s>ekadhanā</s> waters are being poured together into the <s>hotṛ</s>'s cup.

children.text: aver apo 'dhvaryāu iti hotādhvaryum pṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: "Have you found the waters, O <s>adhvaryu</s>?" the <s>hotṛ</s> asks the <s>adhvaryu</s>.

children.text: āpo vai yajño 'vido yajñam ity eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: The waters are the sacrifice; he thereby says, "Have you found the sacrifice?"

children.text: utem anannamur ity adhvaryuḥ pratyāha ||
children.translated_text: "And these have not sunk away," the <s>adhvaryu</s> answers.

children.text: utemāḥ paśyety eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: He thereby says, "And look at these."

children.text: tāsv adhvaryo indrāya somaṃ sotā madhumantam vṛṣṭivaniṃ tīvrāntam bahuramadhyaṃ vasumate rudravata ādityavata ṛbhumate vibhumate vājavate bṛhaspativate viśvadevyāvate yasyendraḥ pītvā vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat pra sa janyāni tāriṣaum iti pratyuttiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: At these waters he rises toward them, saying, "O <s>adhvaryu</s>, press for <s>Indra</s> the <s>soma</s> that is honeyed, winning rain, ending in sharp strength, rich in the middle, possessed of the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, the <s>Vibhus</s>, the <s>Vājas</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and all the gods; after drinking it may <s>Indra</s> smash the <s>Vṛtras</s> and carry us beyond hostile powers."

children.text: pratyuttheyā vā āpaḥ prati vai śreyāṃsam āyantam uttiṣṭhanti tasmāt pratyuttheyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The waters are indeed to be risen to. People rise to meet a superior as he approaches; therefore the waters are to be risen to.

children.text: anuparyāvṛtyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are to be approached after turning around.

children.text: anu vai śreyāṃsam paryāvartante tasmād anuparyāvṛtyā anubruvataivānuprapattavyam ||
children.translated_text: For people turn around after a superior; therefore they are to be approached after turning around. One should approach after them only while reciting.

children.text: īśvaro ha yady apy anyo yajetātha hotāraṃ yaśo 'rtos tasmād anubruvataivānuprapattavyam ||
children.translated_text: For even if another should sacrifice, he might take fame away from the <s>hotṛ</s>; therefore one should approach after them only while reciting.

children.text: ambayo yanty adhvabhir ity etām anubruvann anuprapadyeta ||
children.translated_text: While reciting this verse, "The mothers go along the paths," he should approach after them.

children.text: jāmayo adhvarīyatām pṛñcatīr madhunā paya iti ||
children.translated_text: "Sisters, mingle for those performing the rite, with honey, with milk."

children.text: yo 'madhavyo yaśo 'rtor bubhūṣet ||
children.translated_text: This is for one who, lacking sweetness, would wish to become a winner of fame.

children.text: amūr yā upa sūrye yābhir vā sūryaḥ saheti tejaskāmo brahmavarcasakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Those waters up by the sun, those with which the sun is together" is for one who desires brilliance and the luster of sacred knowledge.

children.text: apo devīr upa hvaye yatra gāvaḥ pibanti na iti paśukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I call upon the divine waters, where the cows drink" is for one who desires cattle.

children.text: tā etāḥ sarvā evānubruvann anuprapadyetaiteṣāṃ kāmānām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: He should approach after them reciting all these verses, for the securing of these desires.

children.text: etān kāmān avarunddhe ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He secures these desires who knows thus.

children.text: emā agman revatīr jīvadhanyā iti sādyamānāsv anvāha vasatīvarīṣv ekadhanāsu ca ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>vasatīvarī</s> waters and the <s>ekadhanā</s> waters are being set down, he recites over them, "These rich, life-sustaining ones have come here."

children.text: agmann āpa uśatīr barhir edam iti sannāsu sa etayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: When they have been set down, he encloses them with this verse: "The eager waters have come to this <s>barhis</s>."

children.text: Chapter 51
śiro vā etad yajñasya yat prātaranuvākaḥ prāṇāpānā upāṃśvantaryāmau vajra eva vāṅ nāhutayor upāṃśvantaryāmayor hotā vācaṃ visṛjeta ||
children.translated_text: The morning recitation is the head of the sacrifice. The <s>upāṃśu</s> and <s>antaryāma</s> offerings are the in-breath and out-breath. Speech is a thunderbolt; therefore the <s>hotṛ</s> should not release speech before the <s>upāṃśu</s> and <s>antaryāma</s> have been offered.

children.text: yad ahutayor upāṃśvantaryāmayor hotā vācaṃ visṛjeta vācā vajreṇa yajamānasya prāṇān vīyāt ya enaṃ tatra brūyād vācā vajreṇa yajamānasya prāṇān vyagāt prāṇa enaṃ hāsyatīti śaśvat tathā syāt tasmān nāhutayor upāṃśvantaryāmayor hotā vācaṃ visṛjeta ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>hotṛ</s> were to release speech before the <s>upāṃśu</s> and <s>antaryāma</s> had been offered, with speech as a thunderbolt he would sever the sacrificer's breaths. If someone there were to say of him, "With speech, the thunderbolt, he has made the sacrificer's breaths go away; breath will abandon him," it would surely be so. Therefore the <s>hotṛ</s> should not release speech before the <s>upāṃśu</s> and <s>antaryāma</s> have been offered.

children.text: prāṇaṃ yaccha svāhā tvā suhava sūryāyety upāṃśum anumantrayeta tam abhiprānet prāṇa prāṇam me yacchety apānaṃ yaccha svāhā tvā suhava sūryāyety antaryāmam anumantrayeta tam abhyapāned apānāpānam me yaccheti vyānāya tvety upāṃśusavanaṃ grāvāṇam abhimṛśya vācaṃ visṛjate ||
children.translated_text: He should mutter over the <s>upāṃśu</s>, "Restrain the breath; svāhā to you, well-invoked one, for <s>Sūrya</s>." He should breathe upon it, saying, "Breath, give me breath." He should mutter over the <s>antaryāma</s>, "Restrain the out-breath; svāhā to you, well-invoked one, for <s>Sūrya</s>." He should breathe downward upon it, saying, "Out-breath, give me out-breath." Having touched the <s>upāṃśusavana</s> pressing-stone with "For the diffused breath I touch you," he releases speech.

children.text: ātmā vā upāṃśusavana ātmany eva taddhotā prāṇān pratidhāya vācaṃ visṛjate sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya ||
children.translated_text: The <s>upāṃśusavana</s> is the self. There, having placed the breaths in the self itself, the <s>hotṛ</s> releases speech, for the sake of full life and full lifetime.

children.text: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus reaches the whole span of life.

children.text: Chapter 52
tad āhuḥ sarpet na sarpet iti sarped iti haika āhur ubhayeṣāṃ vā eṣa devamanuṣyāṇām bhakṣo yad bahiṣpavamānas tasmād enam abhisaṃgacchanta iti vadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say about this, "Should he creep forward, or should he not creep forward?" Some say, "He should creep forward; for the <s>bahiṣpavamāna</s> is the share of both gods and men, and therefore they say that they come together toward it."

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyam ||
children.translated_text: That should not be regarded.

children.text: yat sarped ṛcam eva tat sāmno 'nuvartmānaṃ kuryād ya enaṃ tatra brūyād anuvartmā nvā ayaṃ hotā sāmagasyābhūd udgātari yaśo'dhād acyoṣṭāyatanāc cyoṣyata āyatanād iti śaśvat tathā syāt ||
children.translated_text: If he were to creep forward, he would make the ṛc follow the track of the sāman. If someone there were to say of him, "This <s>hotṛ</s> has become a follower of the sāman-singer; he has placed fame in the <s>udgātṛ</s>; he has fallen from his place; he will fall from his place," it would surely be so.

children.text: tasmāt tatraivāsīno 'numantrayeta ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, seated right there, he should mutter the formula over it.

children.text: yo devānām iha somapītho yajñe barhiṣi vedyām tasyāpi bhakṣayāmasīti ||
children.translated_text: "Whatever Soma-drinking of the gods is here in the sacrifice, on the <s>barhis</s>, on the altar, of that too we partake."

children.text: evam u hāsyātmā somapīthād anantarito bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed his self is not separated from the Soma-drinking.

children.text: atho brūyān mukham asi mukham bhūyāsam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he should say, "You are the mouth; may I become the mouth."

children.text: mukhaṃ vā etad yajñasya yad bahiṣpavamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bahiṣpavamāna</s> is the mouth of the sacrifice.

children.text: mukhaṃ sveṣu bhavati śreṣṭhaḥ svānām bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He becomes the mouth among his own people; he becomes the best of his own people, who knows thus.

children.text: asurī vai dīrghajihvī devānām prātaḥsavanam avāleṭ tad vyamādyat te devāḥ prājijñāsanta te mitrāvaruṇāv abruvan yuvam idaṃ niṣkurutam iti tau tathety abrūtāṃ tau vai vo varaṃ vṛṇāvahā iti vṛṇāthām iti tāv etam eva varam avṛṇātām prātaḥsavane payasyāṃ sainayor eṣācyutā varavṛtā hy enayos tad yad asyai vimattam iva tad asyai samṛddhaṃ vimattam iva hi tau tayā nirakurutām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dīrghajihvī</s>, an Asurī, licked up the gods' morning pressing. It became disordered. The gods perceived this, and they said to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, "You two set this right." They said, "So be it. Let us choose a boon from you." "Choose," they said. They chose this very boon: a <s>payasyā</s> at the morning pressing. This has not slipped away from those two, for it was chosen by them as a boon. Whatever of it seems disordered is its successful form, for those two set her right by means of it while she was, as it were, disordered.

children.text: Chapter 53
devānāṃ vai savanāni nādhriyanta ta etān puroﾱāśān apaśyaṃs tān anusavanaṃ niravapan savanānāṃ dhṛtyai tato vai tāni teṣām adhriyanta ||
children.translated_text: The gods' pressings did not hold firm. They saw these <s>puroḍāśa</s> cakes and offered them at each pressing for the firmness of the pressings. From then on those pressings held firm for them.

children.text: tad yad anusavanam puroﾱāśā nirupyante savanānām eva dhṛtyai tathā hi tāni teṣām adhriyanta ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when <s>puroḍāśa</s> cakes are offered at each pressing, it is for the firmness of the pressings; for in that way those pressings held firm for them.

children.text: puro vā etān devā akrata yat puroﾱāśās tat puroﾱāśānām puroﾱāśatvam ||
children.translated_text: The gods placed these in front, namely the <s>puroḍāśa</s> cakes; that is why the <s>puroḍāśa</s> cakes have the name <s>puroḍāśa</s>.

children.text: tad āhur anusavanam puroﾱāśān nirvaped aṣṭākapālam prātaḥsavana ekādaśakapālam mādhyaṃdine savane dvādaśakapālaṃ tṛtīyasavane tathā hi savanānāṃ rūpaṃ tathā chandasām iti ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, "One should offer <s>puroḍāśa</s> cakes at each pressing: an eight-potsherd cake at the morning pressing, an eleven-potsherd cake at the midday pressing, and a twelve-potsherd cake at the third pressing. For thus there is the form of the pressings, and thus the form of the meters."

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyam aindrā vā ete sarve nirupyante yad anusavanam puroﾱāśās tasmāt tān ekādaśakapālān eva nirvapet ||
children.translated_text: That should not be regarded. All these <s>puroḍāśa</s> cakes offered at each pressing are for <s>Indra</s>; therefore he should offer them only as eleven-potsherd cakes.

children.text: tad āhur yato ghṛtenānaktaṃ syāt tataḥ puroﾱāśasya prāśnīyāt somapīthasya guptyai ghṛtena hi vajreṇendro vṛtram ahann iti ||
children.translated_text: They say: from whatever part of the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) is anointed with ghee, from there one should eat, for the protection of the soma-drinking; for with ghee, as with a thunderbolt, <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>.

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyaṃ havir vā etad yad utpūtaṃ somapītho vā eṣa yadutpūtaṃ tasmāt tasya yata eva kutaś ca prāśnīyāt sarvato vā etāḥ svadhā yajamānam upakṣaranti yad etāni havīṃṣy ājyaṃ dhānāḥ karambhaḥ parivāpaḥ puroﾱāśaḥ payasyeti ||
children.translated_text: That should not be disregarded. This, namely what has been purified, is an oblation; what has been purified is the soma-drinking. Therefore one should eat of it from wherever at all. From every side these <s>svadhās</s> (nourishing ritual powers) flow toward the sacrificer: ghee, parched grains, <s>karambha</s> (groats), <s>parivāpa</s>, <s>puroḍāśa</s>, and <s>payasyā</s>.

children.text: sarvata evainaṃ svadhā upakṣaranti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: From every side the <s>svadhās</s> flow toward one who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 54
yo vai yajñaṃ haviṣpaṅktiṃ veda haviṣpaṅktinā yajñena rādhnoti dhānāḥ karambhaḥ parivāpaḥ puroﾱāśaḥ payasyety eṣa vai yajño haviṣpaṅktir haviṣpaṅktinā yajñena rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows the sacrifice as the oblation-pentad prospers by a sacrifice that is an oblation-pentad. Parched grains, <s>karambha</s>, <s>parivāpa</s>, <s>puroḍāśa</s>, and <s>payasyā</s>: this indeed is the sacrifice as the oblation-pentad. By a sacrifice that is an oblation-pentad he prospers, who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai yajñam akṣarapaṅktiṃ vedākṣarapaṅktinā yajñena rādhnoti su mat pad vag da ity eṣa vai yajño 'kṣarapaṅktir akṣarapaṅktinā yajñena rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows the sacrifice as the syllable-pentad prospers by a sacrifice that is a syllable-pentad. Su, mat, pad, vag, da: this indeed is the sacrifice as the syllable-pentad. By a sacrifice that is a syllable-pentad he prospers, who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai yajñaṃ narāśaṃsapaṅktiṃ veda narāśaṃsapaṅktinā yajñena rādhnoti dvinārāśaṃsam prātaḥsavanaṃ dvinārāśaṃsaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ sakṛnnārāśaṃsaṃ tṛtīyasavanam eṣa vai yajño narāśaṃsapaṅktir narāśaṃsapaṅktinā yajñena rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows the sacrifice as the <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>-pentad prospers by a sacrifice that is a <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>-pentad. The morning pressing has two <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> portions, the midday pressing has two <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> portions, and the third pressing has one <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> portion: this indeed is the sacrifice as the <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>-pentad. By a sacrifice that is a <s>Narāśaṃsa</s>-pentad he prospers, who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai yajñaṃ savanapaṅktiṃ veda savanapaṅktinā yajñena rādhnoti paśur upavasathe trīṇi savanāni paśur anūbandhya ity eṣa vai yajñaḥ savanapaṅktiḥ savanapaṅktinā yajñena rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows the sacrifice as the savana-pentad prospers by a sacrifice that is a savana-pentad. The animal on the fast-day, the three savanas, and the following animal-offering: this indeed is the sacrifice as the savana-pentad. By a sacrifice that is a savana-pentad he prospers, who knows thus.

children.text: harivāṁ indro dhānā attu pūṣaṇvān karambhaṃ sarasvatīvān bhāratīvān parivāpa indrasyāpūpa iti haviṣpaṅktyā yajati ||
children.translated_text: With the oblation-pentad he sacrifices, saying, "Let <s>Indra</s>, accompanied by his bay steeds, eat the parched grains; let the one accompanied by <s>Pūṣan</s> eat the <s>karambha</s>; let the one accompanied by <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Bhāratī</s> eat the <s>parivāpa</s>; the cake is <s>Indra</s>'s."

children.text: ṛksāme vā indrasya harī ||
children.translated_text: The ṛc and the sāman are <s>Indra</s>'s two bay steeds.

children.text: paśavaḥ pūṣānnaṃ karambhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūṣan</s> is cattle; <s>karambha</s> is food.

children.text: sarasvatīvān bhāratīvān iti vāg eva sarasvatī prāṇo bharataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it says, "accompanied by <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Bhāratī</s>," speech itself is <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and breath is <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: parivāpa indrasyāpūpa ity annam eva parivāpa indriyam apūpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it says, "the <s>parivāpa</s>, <s>Indra</s>'s cake," the <s>parivāpa</s> is food itself, and the cake is vital power.

children.text: etāsām eva tad devatānāṃ yajamānaṃ sāyujyaṃ sarūpatāṃ salokatāṃ gamayati gacchati śreyasaḥ sāyujyaṃ gacchati śreṣṭhatāṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Thereby he leads the sacrificer to union, likeness, and dwelling in the same world with these very deities. He attains union with what is better; he attains superiority, who knows thus.

children.text: havir agne vīhīty anusasavanam puroﾱāśasviṣṭakṛto yajati ||
children.translated_text: With "O <s>Agni</s>, go to the oblation," at each savana he sacrifices to the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of what is well offered) of the <s>puroḍāśa</s>.

children.text: avatsāro vā etenāgneḥ priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchat sa paramaṃ lokam ajayat ||
children.translated_text: With this, <s>Avatsāra</s> approached the dear abode of <s>Agni</s> and won the highest world.

children.text: upāgneḥ priyaṃ dhāma gacchati jayati paramaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān etayā haviṣpaṅktyā yajate yajatīti ca yajatīti ca ||
children.translated_text: He approaches the dear abode of <s>Agni</s> and wins the highest world, who knows thus and who, knowing thus, sacrifices with this oblation-pentad. He sacrifices, indeed; he sacrifices, indeed.

children.text: Chapter 55

devā vai somasya rājño 'grapeye na samapādayann aham prathamaḥ pibeyam aham prathamaḥ pibeyam ity evākāmayanta te sampādayanto 'bruvan hantājim āyāma sa yo na ujjeṣyati sa prathamaḥ somasya pāsyatīti tatheti ta ājim āyus teṣām ājiṃ yatām abhisṛṣṭānāṃ vāyur mukham prathamaḥ pratyapadyatāthendro 'tha mitrāvaruṇāv athāśvinau ||
children.translated_text: The gods could not settle the first drinking of king <s>Soma</s>. Each desired, "May I drink first, may I drink first." While arranging it they said, "Come, let us run a race. Whichever of us wins out shall drink first of the soma." "So be it," they said. They ran the race. As they were running the race, once they had been released, <s>Vāyu</s> first reached the front; then <s>Indra</s>, then <s>Mitra-Varuṇa</s>, then the <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: so 'ved indro vāyum ud vai jayatīti tam anuparāpatat saha nāv athojjayāveti sa nety abravīd aham evojjeṣyāmīti tṛtīyam me 'thojjayāveti neti haivābravīd aham evojjeṣyāmīti turīyam me 'thojjayāveti tatheti taṃ turīye 'tyārjata tat turīyabhāg indro 'bhavat tribhāg vāyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> knew, "<s>Vāyu</s> will indeed win out." He ran after him: "Let the two of us win out together." He said, "No; I alone will win out." "Let a third share be mine, and then let us win out together." Still he said no: "I alone will win out." "Let a fourth share be mine, and then let us win out together." "So be it," he said. At the fourth share he overtook him. Therefore <s>Indra</s> became the one with a fourth share, while <s>Vāyu</s> had three shares.

children.text: tau sahaivendravāyū udajayatāṃ saha mitrāvaruṇau sahāśvinau ta eṣām ete yathojjitam bhakṣā indravāyvoḥ prathamo 'tha mitrāvaruṇayor athāśvinoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> won out, together <s>Mitra-Varuṇa</s>, and together the <s>Aśvins</s>. These are their portions according to the way they won: first that of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, then that of <s>Mitra-Varuṇa</s>, then that of the <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: sa eṣa indraturīyo graho gṛhyate yad aindravāyavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This cup is taken as one in which <s>Indra</s> has the fourth share, namely the <s>Aindravāyava</s>.

children.text: tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann abhyanūvāca niyutvāṁ indrasārathir iti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the seer uttered over it, "Possessed of teams, with <s>Indra</s> as charioteer."

children.text: tasmāddhāpyetarhi bharatāḥ satvanāṃ vittim prayanti turīye haiva saṃgrahītāro vadante 'munaivānūkāśena yad ada indraḥ sārathir iva bhūtvodajayat ||
children.translated_text: Therefore even now the <s>Bharatas</s> go to the wealth of the <s>Satvans</s>; at the fourth share the chariot-holders say, "By just this indication," because <s>Indra</s>, becoming as it were the charioteer, won out.

children.text: Chapter 56
te vā ete prāṇā eva yad dvidevatyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These dual-deity cups are in fact the vital functions.

children.text: vāk ca prāṇaś caindravāyavaś cakṣuś ca manaś ca maitrāvaruṇaḥ śrotraṃ cātmā cāśvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Speech and breath are the <s>Aindravāyava</s>; sight and mind are the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; hearing and self are the <s>Āśvina</s>.

children.text: tasya haitasyaindravāyavasyāpy eke 'nuṣṭubhau puronuvākye kurvanti gāyatryau yājye ||
children.translated_text: For this <s>Aindravāyava</s>, some make the preliminary offering-verses anuṣṭubh verses and the offering-verses gāyatrī verses.

children.text: vāk ca vā eṣa prāṇaś ca graho yad aindravāyavas tad api chandobhyāṃ yathāyathaṃ klapsyete iti ||
children.translated_text: This cup, namely the <s>Aindravāyava</s>, is speech and breath; therefore these two will fit the metres respectively.

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyaṃ vyṛddhaṃ vā etad yajñe kriyate yatra puronuvākyā jyāyasī yājyāyai yatra vai yājyā jyāyasī tat samṛddham atho yatra same yasyo tat kāmāya tathā kuryāt prāṇasya ca vācaś cātraiva tad upāptam ||
children.translated_text: That should not be followed. Something deficient is done in the sacrifice where the preliminary verse is greater than the offering-verse. Where the offering-verse is greater, that is prosperous; likewise where the two are equal. If one were to do it in that way for someone's desire, then breath and speech are obtained right here.

children.text: vāyavyā pūrvā puronuvākyaindravāyavy uttaraivaṃ yājyayoḥ sā yā vāyavyā tayā prāṇaṃ kalpayati vāyurhi prāṇo 'tha yaindravāyavī tasyai yad aindram padaṃ tena vācaṃ kalpayati vāgghyaindry upo taṃ kāmam āpnoti yaḥ prāṇe ca vāci ca na yajñe viṣamaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: The earlier preliminary recitation is addressed to <s>Vāyu</s>, and the later one to <s>Indra-Vāyu</s>; so too with the two offering verses. By the one addressed to <s>Vāyu</s> he prepares the breath, for <s>Vāyu</s> is breath. Then by the one addressed to <s>Indra-Vāyu</s>, by whatever word in it belongs to <s>Indra</s>, he prepares speech, for speech belongs to <s>Indra</s>. He obtains that desire who does not create an imbalance in the sacrifice with respect to both breath and speech.

children.text: Chapter 57
prāṇā vai dvidevatyā ekapātrā gṛhyante tasmāt prāṇā ekanāmāno dvipātrā hūyante tasmāt prāṇā dvandvam ||
children.translated_text: The two-deity cups are indeed breaths. They are drawn in one vessel; therefore the breaths have one name. They are offered in two vessels; therefore the breaths are paired.

children.text: yenaivādhvaryur yajuṣā prayacchati tena hotā pratigṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: With the very <s>yajus</s> by which the <s>adhvaryu</s> hands it over, the <s>hotṛ</s> receives it.

children.text: eṣa vasuḥ purūvasur iha vasuḥ purūvasur mayi vasuḥ purūvasur vākpā vācam me pāhīty aindravāyavam bhakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "This is <s>Vasu Purūvasu</s>; here is <s>Vasu Purūvasu</s>; in me is <s>Vasu Purūvasu</s>. Guardian of speech, protect my speech," he consumes the <s>Aindravāyava</s> cup.

children.text: upahūtā vāk saha prāṇenopa māṃ vāksaha prāṇena hvayatām upahūtā ṛṣayo daivyāsas tanūpāvānas tanvas tapojā upa mām ṛṣayo daivyāso hvayantāṃ tanūpāvānas tanvas tapojā iti ||
children.translated_text: "Speech has been invited together with breath. May speech together with breath invite me. The divine seers, protectors of the body, born of austerity for the body, have been invited. May the divine seers, protectors of the body, born of austerity for the body, invite me"; so he says.

children.text: prāṇā vā ṛṣayo daivyāsas tanūpāvānas tanvas tapojās tān eva tad upahvayate ||
children.translated_text: The breaths are indeed the divine seers, protectors of the body, born of austerity for the body. It is precisely them that he thereby invites.

children.text: eṣa vasur vidadvasur iha vasur vidadvasur mayi vasur vidadvasuś cakṣuṣpāś cakṣur me pāhīti maitrāvaruṇam bhakṣayaty upahūtaṃ cakṣuḥ saha manasopa māṃ cakṣuḥ saha manasā hvayatām upahūtā ṛṣayo daivyāsas tanūpāvānas tanvas tapojā upa mām ṛṣayo daivyāso hvayantāṃ tanūpāvānas tanvas tapojā iti prāṇā vā ṛṣayo daivyāsas tanūpāvānas tanvas tapojās tān eva tad upahvayate ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "This is <s>Vasu Vidadvasu</s>; here is <s>Vasu Vidadvasu</s>; in me is <s>Vasu Vidadvasu</s>. Guardian of sight, protect my sight," he consumes the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> cup. "Sight has been invited together with mind. May sight together with mind invite me. The divine seers, protectors of the body, born of austerity for the body, have been invited. May the divine seers, protectors of the body, born of austerity for the body, invite me." The breaths are indeed the divine seers, protectors of the body, born of austerity for the body. It is precisely them that he thereby invites.

children.text: eṣa vasuḥ saṃyadvasur iha vasuḥ saṃyadvasur mayi vasuḥ saṃyadvasuḥ śrotrapāḥ śrotram me pāhīty āśvinam bhakṣayaty upahūtaṃ śrotraṃ sahātmanopa māṃ śrotraṃ sahātmanā hvayatām upahūtā ṛṣayo daivyāsas tanūpāvānas tanvas tapojā upa mām ṛṣayo daivyāso hvayantāṃ tanūpāvānas tanvas tapojā iti prāṇā vā ṛṣayo daivyāsas tanūpāvānas tanvas tapojās tān eva tad upahvayate ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "This is <s>Vasu Saṃyadvasu</s>; here is <s>Vasu Saṃyadvasu</s>; in me is <s>Vasu Saṃyadvasu</s>. Guardian of hearing, protect my hearing," he consumes the <s>Āśvina</s> cup. "Hearing has been invited together with the self. May hearing together with the self invite me. The divine seers, protectors of the body, born of austerity for the body, have been invited. May the divine seers, protectors of the body, born of austerity for the body, invite me." The breaths are indeed the divine seers, protectors of the body, born of austerity for the body. It is precisely them that he thereby invites.

children.text: purastāt pratyañcam aindravāyavam bhakṣayati tasmāt purastāt prāṇāpānau purastāt pratyañcam maitrāvaruṇam bhakṣayati tasmāt purastāccakṣuṣī sarvataḥ parihāram āśvinam bhakṣayati tasmān manuṣyāś ca paśavaś ca sarvato vācaṃ vadantīṃ śṛṇvanti ||
children.translated_text: He consumes the <s>Aindravāyava</s> cup in front, facing backward; therefore the in-breath and out-breath are in front. He consumes the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> cup in front, facing backward; therefore the two eyes are in front. He consumes the <s>Āśvina</s> cup with movement around on every side; therefore human beings and animals hear speech being spoken from every side.

children.text: Chapter 58
prāṇā vai dvidevatyā anavānaṃ dvidevatyān yajet prāṇānāṃ saṃtatyai prāṇānām avyavacchedāya ||
children.translated_text: The two-deity cups are indeed breaths. He should sacrifice with the two-deity cups without taking a break in breathing, for the continuity of the breaths and for the non-interruption of the breaths.

children.text: prāṇā vai dvidevatyā na dvidevatyānām anuvaṣaṭkuryāt ||
children.translated_text: The two-deity cups are indeed breaths. He should not make an <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> for the two-deity cups.

children.text: yad dvidevatyānām anuvaṣaṭkuryād asaṃsthitān prāṇān saṃsthāpayet saṃsthā vā eṣā yad anuvaṣaṭkāro ya enaṃ tatra brūyād asaṃsthitān prāṇān samatiṣṭhipat prāṇa enam hāsyatīti śaśvat tathā syāt tasmān na dvidevatyānām anuvaṣaṭkuryāt ||
children.translated_text: If he were to make an <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> for the two-deity cups, he would bring to completion breaths that have not reached completion. For completion is precisely what the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> is. If someone were then to say of him, "He has brought to completion breaths that had not reached completion; breath will abandon him," it would surely be so. Therefore he should not make an <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> for the two-deity cups.

children.text: tad āhur dvir āgūrya maitrāvaruṇo dviḥ preṣyati sakṛd āgūrya hotā dvir vaṣaṭkaroti kā hoturāgūr iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, having made the <s>āgūr</s> twice, gives the prompt twice; the <s>hotṛ</s>, having made the <s>āgūr</s> once, utters the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> twice. What, then, is the <s>hotṛ</s>'s <s>āgūr</s>?"

children.text: prāṇā vai dvidevatyā āgūr vajras tad yaddhotāntareṇāguretāgurā vajreṇa yajamānasya prāṇān vīyād ya enaṃ tatra brūyād āgurā vajreṇa yajamānasya prāṇān vyagāt prāṇa enaṃ hāsyatīti śaśvat tathā syāt tasmāt tatra hotāntareṇa nāgureta ||
children.translated_text: The two-deity cups are indeed breaths, and the <s>āgūr</s> is a thunderbolt. If the <s>hotṛ</s> were to make an intervening <s>āgūr</s> there, with the <s>āgūr</s> as a thunderbolt he would cut apart the sacrificer's breaths. If someone were then to say of him, "With the <s>āgūr</s> as a thunderbolt he has severed the sacrificer's breaths; breath will abandon him," it would surely be so. Therefore the <s>hotṛ</s> should not make an intervening <s>āgūr</s> there.

children.text: atho mano vai yajñasya maitrāvaruṇo vāg yajñasya hotā manasā vā iṣitā vāg vadati yāṃ hy anyamanā vācaṃ vadaty asuryā vai sā vāg adevajuṣṭā tad yad evātra maitrāvaruṇo dvir āgurate saiva hotur āgūḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is the mind of the sacrifice, and the <s>hotṛ</s> is the speech of the sacrifice. Speech speaks when impelled by mind. For the speech that one speaks while one's mind is elsewhere is demonic speech, not pleasing to the gods. Therefore the fact that the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> makes the <s>āgūr</s> twice here is itself the <s>hotṛ</s>'s <s>āgūr</s>.

children.text: Chapter 59
prāṇā vā ṛtuyājās tad yad ṛtuyājaiścaranti prāṇān eva tad yajamāne dadhati ||
children.translated_text: The seasonal offerings are indeed breaths. When they proceed with the seasonal offerings, they thereby place the breaths in the sacrificer.

children.text: ṣaﾱ ṛtuneti yajanti prāṇam eva tad yajamāne dadhati ||
children.translated_text: They sacrifice six times with the formula "with the season"; thereby they place the in-breath in the sacrificer.

children.text: catvāra ṛtubhir iti yajanty apānam eva tad yajamāne dadhati ||
children.translated_text: They sacrifice four times with the formula "with the seasons"; thereby they place the out-breath in the sacrificer.

children.text: dvir ṛtunety upariṣṭād vyānam eva tad yajamāne dadhati ||
children.translated_text: They sacrifice twice afterward with the formula "with the season"; thereby they place the diffused breath in the sacrificer.

children.text: sa vā ayam prāṇas tredhā vihitaḥ prāṇo 'pāno vyāna iti tad yad ṛtunartubhir ṛtuneti yajanti prāṇānāṃ saṃtatyai prāṇānām avyavacchedāya ||
children.translated_text: This breath is thus arranged in three ways, as in-breath, out-breath, and diffused breath. Since they sacrifice with "with the season," "with the seasons," and "with the season," it is for the continuity of the breaths and for the non-interruption of the breaths.

children.text: prāṇā vā ṛtuyājā nartuyājānām anuvaṣaṭkuryād asaṃsthitā vā ṛtava ekaika eva ||
children.translated_text: The seasonal offerings are indeed breaths. He should not make an <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> for the seasonal offerings, for the seasons, each one by itself, have not reached completion.
