children.text: yad ṛtuyājānām anuvaṣaṭkuryād asaṃsthitān ṛtūn saṃsthāpayet saṃsthā vā eṣā yad anuvaṣaṭkāro ya enaṃ tatra brūyād asaṃsthitān ṛtūn samatiṣṭhipad duṣṣamam bhaviṣyatīti śaśvat tathā syāt tasmān nartuyājānām anuvaṣaṭkuryāt ||
children.translated_text: If he were to make an <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> for the seasonal offerings, he would bring to completion seasons that have not reached completion. For completion is precisely what the <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> is. If someone were then to say of him, "He has brought to completion seasons that had not reached completion; there will be a bad year," it would surely be so. Therefore he should not make an <s>anuvaṣaṭkāra</s> for the seasonal offerings.

children.text: Chapter 60
prāṇā vai dvidevatyāḥ paśava iﾱā dvidevatyān bhakṣayitveﾱām upahvayate paśavo vā iﾱā paśūn eva tad upahvayate paśūn yajamāne dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: The two-deity cups are indeed breaths, and <s>Iḍā</s> is cattle. Having consumed the two-deity cups, he invites <s>Iḍā</s>. For <s>Iḍā</s> is cattle. It is cattle that he thereby invites; he places cattle in the sacrificer.

children.text: tad āhur avāntareﾱām pūrvām prāśnīyāt hotṛcamasam bhakṣayet iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "One should first eat of the avāntareḍā portions, and then partake of the <s>hotṛcamas</s> (the hotṛ's cup)."

children.text: avāntareﾱām eva pūrvām prāśnīyād atha hotṛcamasam bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: One should indeed first eat of the avāntareḍā portions, and then partake of the <s>hotṛcamas</s>.

children.text: yad vāva dvidevatyān pūrvān bhakṣayati tenāsya somapīthaḥ pūrvo bhakṣito bhavati tasmād avāntareﾱām eva pūrvām prāśnīyād atha hotṛcamasam bhakṣayet tad ubhayato 'nnādyam parigṛhṇāti somapīthābhyām annādyasya parigṛhītyai ||
children.translated_text: For when he first partakes of the cups belonging to two deities, his Soma-drinking has thereby already been partaken of first. Therefore he should first eat of the avāntareḍā portions, and then partake of the <s>hotṛcamas</s>. Thus he takes hold of food on both sides, between the two Soma-drinkings, for the taking hold of food.

children.text: prāṇā vai dvidevatyā ātmā hotṛcamaso dvidevatyānāṃ saṃsravān hotṛcamase samavanayaty ātmany eva taddhotā prāṇān samavanayate sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya ||
children.translated_text: The cups belonging to two deities are the breaths; the <s>hotṛcamas</s> is the self. He pours together the runnings from the cups belonging to two deities into the <s>hotṛcamas</s>; thereby the <s>hotṛ</s> pours the breaths together into the self, for full length of life and for the state of having full length of life.

children.text: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He reaches the whole length of life, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 61
devā vai yad eva yajñe 'kurvaṃs tad asurā akurvaṃs te samāvadvīryā evāsan na vyāvartanta tato vai devā etaṃ tūṣṇīṃśaṃsam apaśyaṃs tam eṣām asurā nānvavāyaṃs tūṣṇīṃsāro vā eṣa yat tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever the gods did in the sacrifice, the Asuras did the same; they were equal in strength and were not distinguished. Then the gods saw this <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> (silent recitation). The Asuras did not follow them in it. For this <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> is silent in essence.

children.text: devā vai yaṃ yam eva vajram asurebhya udayacchaṃs taṃ tam eṣām asurāḥ pratyabudhyanta tato vai devā etaṃ tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ vajram apaśyaṃs tam ebhya udayacchaṃs tam eṣām asurā na pratyabudhyanta tam ebhyaḥ prāharaṃs tenainān apratibuddhenāghnaṃs tato vai devā abhavan parāsurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever thunderbolt the gods raised against the Asuras, the Asuras perceived it. Then the gods saw this <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> as a thunderbolt. They raised it against them, and the Asuras did not perceive it. They struck them with it; with that unperceived weapon they slew them. Then the gods prevailed, and the Asuras were defeated.

children.text: bhavaty ātmanā parāsya dviṣan pāpmā bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prevails in himself, and his hateful evil, his rival, is defeated, who knows thus.

children.text: te vai devā vijitino manyamānā yajñam atanvata tam eṣām asurā abhyāyan yajñaveśasam eṣāṃ kariṣyāma iti tān samantam evodārān pariyattān udapaśyaṃs te 'bruvan saṃsthāpayāmemaṃ yajñaṃ yajñaṃ no 'surā mā vadhiṣur iti tatheti taṃ tūṣṇīṃśaṃse saṃsthāpayan bhūr agnir jyotir jyotir agnir ity ājyaprauge saṃsthāpayann indro jyotir bhuvo jyotir indra iti niṣkevalyamarutvatīye saṃsthāpayan sūryo jyotir jyotiḥ svaḥ sūrya iti vaiśvadevāgnimārute saṃsthāpayaṃs tam evaṃ tūṣṇīṃśaṃse saṃsthāpayaṃs tam evaṃ tūṣṇīṃśaṃse saṃsthāpya tenāriṣṭenodṛcam āśnuvata ||
children.translated_text: Those gods, thinking themselves victorious, extended the sacrifice. The Asuras came against it, saying, "We shall make their sacrifice collapse." The gods saw them on every side, uplifted and arrayed. They said, "Let us bring this sacrifice to completion, lest the Asuras destroy our sacrifice." "So be it," they said. They brought it to completion in the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s>: in the ājyaprauga they completed it with "bhūr, Agni, light; light, Agni"; in the niṣkevalya-marutvatīya they completed it with "Indra, light; bhuvas, light, Indra"; in the vaiśvadeva-agnimāruta they completed it with "Sūrya, light; light, svaḥ, Sūrya." Thus they completed it in the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s>; having thus completed it in the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s>, through that uninjured rite they attained the final verse.

children.text: sa tadā vāva yajñaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate yadā hotā tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: Only then does the sacrifice truly come to completion, when the <s>hotṛ</s> recites the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s>.

children.text: sa ya enaṃ śaste tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa upa vā vaded anu vā vyāharet tam brūyād eṣa evaitām ārtim āriṣyati prātar vāva vayam adyemaṃ śaste tūṣṇīṃśaṃse saṃsthāpayāmas taṃ yathā gṛhān itaṃ karmaṇānusamiyād evam evainam idam anusamima iti so ha vāva tām ārtim ṛcchati ya evaṃ vidvān saṃśaste tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa upa vā vadaty anu vā vyāharati tasmād evaṃ vidvān saṃśaste tūṣṇīṃśaṃse nopavaden nānuvyāharet ||
children.translated_text: If, while this <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> is being recited, someone should speak up against it or make an utterance after it, one should say to him, "This man will incur that very injury. This morning, while this <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> was being recited, we brought the sacrifice to completion. Just as one might follow after a man who has gone home with some business, so this has followed after him." He indeed incurs that injury who, knowing thus, speaks up against the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> while it is being jointly recited, or makes an utterance after it. Therefore one who knows thus should not speak up against the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> while it is being jointly recited, nor make an utterance after it.

children.text: Chapter 62

cakṣūṃṣi vā etāni savanānāṃ yat tūṣṇīṃśaṃso bhūr agnir jyotir jyotir agnir iti prātaḥsavanasya cakṣuṣī indro jyotir bhuvo jyotir indra iti mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya cakṣuṣī sūryo jyotir jyotiḥ svaḥ sūrya iti tṛtīyasavanasya cakṣuṣī ||
children.translated_text: These <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> formulas are the eyes of the pressings: "bhūr, Agni, light; light, Agni" are the two eyes of the morning pressing; "Indra, light; bhuvas, light, Indra" are the two eyes of the midday pressing; "Sūrya, light; light, svaḥ, Sūrya" are the two eyes of the third pressing.

children.text: cakṣuṣmadbhiḥ savanai rādhnoti cakṣuṣmadbhiḥ savanaiḥ svargaṃ lokam eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: With pressings that have eyes he prospers; with pressings that have eyes he reaches the heavenly world, who knows thus.

children.text: cakṣur vā etad yajñasya yat tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa ekā satī vyāhṛtir dvedhocyate tasmād ekaṃ sac cakṣur dvedhā ||
children.translated_text: This <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> is the eye of the sacrifice. Though the utterance is one, it is pronounced in two ways; therefore the eye, though one, is twofold.

children.text: mūlaṃ vā etad yajñasya yat tūṣṇīṃśaṃso yaṃ kāmayetānāyatanavān syād iti nāsya yajñe tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ śaṃsed unmūlam eva tad yajñam parābhavantam anu parābhavati ||
children.translated_text: This <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> is the root of the sacrifice. If he should desire of someone, "May he be without a foundation," he should not recite the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s> for him in the sacrifice. Following after a sacrifice that is rootless and failing, he himself fails.

children.text: tad u vā āhuḥ śaṃsed evāpi vai tad ṛtvije 'hitaṃ yaddhotā tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ na śaṃsaty ṛtviji hi sarvo yajñaḥ pratiṣṭhito yajñe yajamānas tasmācchaṃstavyaḥ śaṃstavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But they also say, "He should recite it nevertheless. For that is harmful to the officiating priest, when the <s>hotṛ</s> does not recite the <s>tūṣṇīṃśaṃsa</s>. For the whole sacrifice is established in the officiating priest, and the sacrificer is established in the sacrifice. Therefore it must be recited; it must be recited."

children.text: Chapter 63

brahma vā āhāvaḥ kṣatraṃ nivid viṭ sūktam āhvayate 'tha nividaṃ dadhāti brahmaṇy eva tat kṣatram anuniyunakti nividaṃ śastvā sūktaṃ śaṃsati kṣatraṃ vai nivid viṭ sūktaṃ kṣatra eva tad viśam anuniyunakti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>āhāva</s> (summons) is <s>brahman</s>; the <s>nivid</s> is <s>kṣatra</s> (royal power); the <s>sūkta</s> is the <s>viś</s> (people). He gives the summons and then places the <s>nivid</s>; thereby he joins the royal power to the priestly power. Having recited the <s>nivid</s>, he recites the <s>sūkta</s>; the <s>nivid</s> is royal power and the <s>sūkta</s> is the people, so thereby he joins the people to royal power.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta kṣatreṇainaṃ vyardhayānīti madhya etasyai nividaḥ sūktaṃ śaṃset kṣatraṃ vai nivid viṭ sūktaṃ kṣatreṇaivainaṃ tad vyardhayati ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire of someone, "May I deprive him of royal power," he should recite the <s>sūkta</s> in the middle of that <s>nivid</s>. The <s>nivid</s> is royal power and the <s>sūkta</s> is the people; thereby he deprives him of royal power through royal power itself.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta viśainaṃ vyardhayānīti madhya etasya sūktasya nividaṃ śaṃset kṣatraṃ vai nividviṭ sūktaṃ viśaivainaṃ tad vyardhayati ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire of someone, "May I deprive him of the people," he should recite the <s>nivid</s> in the middle of that <s>sūkta</s>. The <s>nivid</s> is royal power and the <s>sūkta</s> is the people; thereby he deprives him of the people through the people itself.

children.text: yam u kāmayeta sarvam evāsya yathāpūrvam ṛju kﾱptaṃ syād ity āhvayetātha nividaṃ dadhyād atha sūktaṃ śaṃset so sarvasya kﾱptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if he should desire of someone, "May everything of his be set straight and arranged according to the former order," he should give the summons, then place the <s>nivid</s>, and then recite the <s>sūkta</s>. That is the arrangement of everything.

children.text: prajāpatir vā idam eka evāgra āsa so 'kāmayata prajāyeya bhūyān syām iti sa tapo 'tapyata sa vācam ayacchat sa saṃvatsarasya parastād vyāharad dvādaśakṛtvo dvādaśapadā vā eṣā nivid etāṃ vāva tāṃ nividaṃ vyāharat tām sarvāṇi bhūtāny anvasṛjyanta ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> alone was this in the beginning. He desired, "May I generate offspring; may I become more numerous." He performed austerity. He summoned speech. After a year he uttered aloud twelve times. This <s>nivid</s> has twelve feet; that indeed was the <s>nivid</s> which he uttered. All beings were created in accordance with it.

children.text: tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann abhyanūvāca sa pūrvayā nividā kavyatāyor imāḥ prajā ajanayan manūnām iti ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the seer recited over it: "With the former <s>nivid</s>, in their inspired wisdom, they generated these offspring of the Manus."

children.text: tad yad etām purastāt sūktasya nividaṃ dadhāti prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when he places this <s>nivid</s> before the hymn, it is for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is propagated with offspring and cattle who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 64
agnir deveddha iti śaṃsaty asau vā agnir deveddha etaṃ hi devā indhata etam eva tad etasmiṃlloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "<s>Agni</s>, kindled by the gods." That yonder one is <s>Agni</s> kindled by the gods, for the gods kindle him. Thereby he makes that very one come to this world.

children.text: agnir manviddha iti śaṃsaty ayaṃ vā agnir manviddha imaṃ hi manuṣyā indhate 'gnim eva tad asmiṃlloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "<s>Agni</s>, kindled by men." This one here is <s>Agni</s> kindled by men, for men kindle this one. Thereby he makes <s>Agni</s> himself come to this world.

children.text: agniḥ suṣamid iti śaṃsati vāyur vā agniḥ suṣamid vāyur hi svayam ātmānaṃ saminddhe svayam idaṃ sarvaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃca vāyum eva tad antarikṣaloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "<s>Agni</s>, well kindled." <s>Vāyu</s> is <s>Agni</s> well kindled, for <s>Vāyu</s> kindles himself by himself, and by himself all this, whatever there is. Thereby he makes <s>Vāyu</s> himself come to the mid-space world.

children.text: hotā devavṛta iti śaṃsaty asau vai hotā devavṛta eṣa hi sarvato devair vṛta etam eva tad etasmiṃlloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "The <s>hotṛ</s>, chosen by the gods." That yonder one is the <s>hotṛ</s> chosen by the gods, for he is chosen by the gods from every side. Thereby he makes that very one come to this world.

children.text: hotā manuvṛta iti śaṃsaty ayaṃ vā agnir hotā manuvṛto 'yaṃ hi sarvato manuṣyair vṛto 'gnim eva tad asmiṃlloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "The <s>hotṛ</s>, chosen by men." This <s>Agni</s> here is the <s>hotṛ</s> chosen by men, for this one is chosen by men from every side. Thereby he makes <s>Agni</s> himself come to this world.

children.text: praṇīr yajñānām iti śaṃsati vāyur vai praṇīr yajñānāṃ yadā hi prāṇity atha yajño 'thāgnihotraṃ vāyum eva tad antarikṣaloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "The leader of sacrifices." <s>Vāyu</s> is the leader of sacrifices; for when one breathes, then there is the sacrifice, and then the <s>Agnihotra</s>. Thereby he makes <s>Vāyu</s> himself come to the mid-space world.

children.text: rathīr adhvarāṇām iti śaṃsaty asau vai rathīr adhvarāṇām eṣa hi yathaitac carati rathīr ivaitam eva tad etasmiṃlloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "The charioteer of the rites." That yonder one is the charioteer of the rites, for as he moves in this way, he is like a charioteer. Thereby he makes that very one come to this world.

children.text: atūrto hoteti śaṃsaty ayaṃ vā agnir atūrto hotemaṃ ha na kaścana tiryañcaṃ taraty agnim eva tad asmiṃlloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "The <s>hotṛ</s> who is not overcome." This <s>Agni</s> here is the <s>hotṛ</s> who is not overcome; no one crosses over this one sideways. Thereby he makes <s>Agni</s> himself come to this world.

children.text: tūrṇir havyavāﾱ iti śaṃsati vāyur vai tūrṇir havyavāḍ vāyur hīdaṃ sarvam sadyas tarati yad idaṃ kiṃca vāyur devebhyo havyaṃ vahati vāyum eva tad antarikṣaloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "The swift carrier of oblations." <s>Vāyu</s> is the swift carrier of oblations, for <s>Vāyu</s> immediately crosses all this, whatever there is; <s>Vāyu</s> carries the oblation to the gods. Thereby he makes <s>Vāyu</s> himself come to the mid-space world.

children.text: ā devo devān vakṣad iti śaṃsaty asau vai devo devān āvahaty etam eva tad etasmiṃlloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "May the god bring the gods here." That yonder god brings the gods here. Thereby he makes that very one come to this world.

children.text: yakṣad agnir devo devān iti śaṃsaty ayaṃ vā agnir devo devān yajaty agnim eva tad asmiṃlloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "May <s>Agni</s>, the god, sacrifice to the gods." This <s>Agni</s> here, the god, sacrifices to the gods. Thereby he makes <s>Agni</s> himself come to this world.

children.text: so 'dhvarā karati jātavedā iti śaṃsati vāyur vai jātavedā vāyur hīdaṃ sarvaṃ karoti yad idaṃ kiṃca vāyum eva tad antarikṣaloka āyātayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "So <s>Jātavedas</s> performs the rites." <s>Vāyu</s> is <s>Jātavedas</s>, for <s>Vāyu</s> performs all this, whatever there is. Thereby he makes <s>Vāyu</s> himself come to the mid-space world.

children.text: Chapter 65
pra vo devāyāgnaya ity anuṣṭubhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Forth for you, O fires, to the god" are anuṣṭubh verses.

children.text: prathame pade viharati tasmāt stry ūrū viharati ||
children.translated_text: He separates the first pāda; therefore a woman separates her thighs.

children.text: samasyaty uttare pade tasmāt pumān ūrū samasyati tan mithunam mithunam eva tad ukthamukhe karoti prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: He joins together the following pādas; therefore a man joins his thighs. That is a pair. Thus he makes a pair at the mouth of the <s>uktha</s>, for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is propagated with offspring and cattle who knows thus.

children.text: pra vo devāyāgnaya ity evānuṣṭubhaḥ prathame pade viharati vajram eva tat parovarīyāṃsaṃ karoti samasyaty evottare pade ārambhaṇato vai vajrasyāṇimātho daṇḍasyātho paraśor vajram eva tat praharati dviṣate bhrātṛvyāya vadhaṃ yo'sya stṛtyas tasmai startavai ||
children.translated_text: "Forth for you, O fires, to the god" are indeed anuṣṭubh verses. He separates the first pāda; thereby he makes the thunderbolt ever more superior. He joins together the following pādas. From the grip comes the sharp edge of the thunderbolt, and also of the staff, and also of the axe. Thus he hurls the thunderbolt as a blow against the hateful rival who is to be laid low by him, in order to lay him low.

children.text: Chapter 66

devāsurā vā eṣu lokeṣu samayatanta te vai devāḥ sada evāyatanam akurvata tān sadaso 'jayaṃs ta āgnīdhraṃ samprāpadyanta te tato na parājayanta tasmād āgnīdhra upavasanti na sadasy āgnīdhre hy adhārayanta yad āgnīdhre 'dhārayanta tad āgnīdhrasyāgnīdhratvam ||
children.translated_text: The gods and the Asuras contended in these worlds. The gods made the <s>sadas</s> itself their abode. The Asuras defeated them from the <s>sadas</s>. They resorted to the <s>āgnīdhra</s>, and from there they were not defeated. Therefore they sit near the <s>āgnīdhra</s>, not in the <s>sadas</s>; for in the <s>āgnīdhra</s> they held firm. Because they held firm in the <s>āgnīdhra</s>, that is the <s>āgnīdhra</s>'s character as <s>āgnīdhra</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ vai devānām asurāḥ sadasyān agnīn nirvāpayāṃcakrus te devā āgnīdhrād eva sadasyān agnīn viharanta tair asurarakṣāṃsy apāghnata tathaivaitad yajamānā āgnīdhrād eva sadasyān agnīn viharanty asurarakṣāṃsy eva tad apaghnate ||
children.translated_text: The Asuras put out the fires of those gods in the <s>sadas</s>. The gods carried the fires from the <s>āgnīdhra</s> to the <s>sadas</s>; with them they drove away the Asuras and Rakṣases. In just the same way, sacrificers carry the fires from the <s>āgnīdhra</s> to the <s>sadas</s>; thereby they drive away the Asuras and Rakṣases.

children.text: te vai prātar ājyair evājayanta āyan yad ājyair evājayanta āyaṃs tad ājyānām ājyatvam ||
children.translated_text: In the morning they advanced and conquered by means of the <s>ājya</s> verses. Because they advanced and conquered by means of the <s>ājya</s> verses, that is the <s>ājya</s> character of the <s>ājya</s> verses.

children.text: tāsāṃ vai hotrāṇām āyatīnām ājayantīnām achāvākīyāhīyata tasyām indrāgnī adhyāstām indrāgnī vai devānām ojiṣṭhau baliṣṭhau sahiṣṭhau sattamau pārayiṣṇutamau tasmād aindrāgnam achāvākaḥ prātaḥsavane śaṃsatīndrāgnī hi tasyām adhyāstām ||
children.translated_text: Of those <s>hotṛ</s> recitations, as they advanced and conquered, the <s>achāvākīyā</s> was left behind. <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> sat upon it. <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are the strongest, most powerful, most overcoming, most excellent, and most capable of carrying across among the gods. Therefore the <s>achāvāka</s> recites an <s>Aindrāgna</s> hymn at the morning pressing, for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> sat upon that recitation.

children.text: tasmād u purastād anye hotrakāḥ sadaḥ prasarpanti paścāchāvākaḥ paśceva hi hīno 'nusaṃjigamiṣati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the other assistant <s>hotṛ</s> priests creep forward to the <s>sadas</s> first, and the <s>achāvāka</s> afterward; for one who has been left behind wishes to catch up afterward.

children.text: tasmād yo brāhmaṇo bahvṛco vīryavān syāt so 'syāchāvākīyāṃ kuryāt tenaiva sāhīnā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> versed in many ṛcs and possessed of vigor there may be, he should perform this <s>achāvākīyā</s> for him. Thereby that recitation is not left behind.

children.text: Chapter 67
devaratho vā eṣa yad yajñas tasyaitāv antarau raśmī yad ājyaprauge tad yad ājyena pavamānam anuśaṃsati praugeṇājyaṃ devarathasyaiva tad antarau raśmī viharaty alobhāya ||
children.translated_text: This, namely the sacrifice, is the gods' chariot. Its two inner reins are the <s>ājya</s> and the <s>prauga</s>. Thus, when he recites the <s>pavamāna</s> with the <s>ājya</s> and the <s>ājya</s> with the <s>prauga</s>, he arranges the two inner reins of the gods' chariot, so that it may not become confused.

children.text: tām anukṛtim manuṣyarathasyaivāntarau raśmī viharantyalobhāya ||
children.translated_text: In imitation of that, they arrange the two inner reins of a human chariot too, so that it may not become confused.

children.text: nāsya devaratho lubhyati na manuṣyaratho ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: His divine chariot does not become confused, nor his human chariot, who knows thus.

children.text: tad āhur yathā vāva stotram evaṃ śastram pāvamānīṣu sāmagāḥ stuvata āgneyaṃ hotājyaṃ śaṃsati katham asya pāvamānyo 'nuśastā bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, "As the <s>stotra</s> is, so should the <s>śastra</s> be. The <s>sāmaga</s>s chant among the <s>pāvamānī</s> verses, while the <s>hotṛ</s> recites the <s>āgneya</s> <s>ājya</s>. How, then, do the <s>pāvamānī</s> verses become recited for him?"

children.text: yo vā agniḥ sa pavamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is <s>Agni</s> is the <s>Pavamāna</s>.

children.text: tad apy etad ṛṣiṇoktam agnir ṛṣiḥ pavamāna iti ||
children.translated_text: And this too has been said by the seer: "<s>Agni</s>, the seer, is <s>Pavamāna</s>."

children.text: evam u hāsyāgneyībhir eva pratipadyamānasya pāvamānyo 'nuśastā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for him who begins with verses belonging to <s>Agni</s>, the <s>pāvamānī</s> verses have indeed been recited.

children.text: tad āhur yathā vāva stotram evaṃ śastraṃ gāyatrīṣu sāmagāḥ stuvata ānuṣṭubhaṃ hotājyaṃ śaṃsati katham asya gāyatryo 'nuśastā bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, "As the <s>stotra</s> is, so should the <s>śastra</s> be. The <s>sāmaga</s>s chant in <s>gāyatrī</s> verses, while the <s>hotṛ</s> recites the <s>ājya</s> in <s>anuṣṭubh</s> verses. How, then, do the <s>gāyatrī</s> verses become recited for him?"

children.text: sampadeti brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should say, "By equivalence."

children.text: saptaitā anuṣṭubhas tās triḥ prathamayā trir uttamayaikādaśa bhavanti virāḍ yājyā dvādaśī na vā ekenākṣareṇa chandāṃsi viyanti na dvābhyāṃ tāḥ ṣoﾱaśa gāyatryo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: These <s>anuṣṭubh</s> verses are seven. With the first repeated three times and the last repeated three times, they become eleven; the <s>virāj</s> offering-verse is the twelfth. The metres do not fall apart because of one syllable, nor because of two. They become sixteen <s>gāyatrī</s> verses.

children.text: evam u hāsyānuṣṭubbhir eva pratipadyamānasya gāyatryo 'nuśastā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for him who begins with <s>anuṣṭubh</s> verses, the <s>gāyatrī</s> verses have indeed been recited.

children.text: agna indraś ca dāśuṣo duroṇa ity āgnendryā yajati ||
children.translated_text: With "O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Indra</s>, from the worshipper's house," he sacrifices with an <s>Āgnendra</s> verse.

children.text: na vā etāv indrāgnī santau vyajayetām āgnendrau vā etau santau vyajayetāṃ tad yad āgnendryā yajati vijityā eva ||
children.translated_text: These two, if they were <s>Indra</s>-and-<s>Agni</s>, would not win out separately; rather, as <s>Agni</s>-and-<s>Indra</s> they win out. Therefore, when he sacrifices with the <s>āgnendrī</s>, it is precisely for victory.

children.text: sā virāṭ trayastriṃśadakṣarā bhavati trayastriṃśad vai devā aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāḥ prajāpatiś ca vaṣaṭkāraś ca tat prathama ukthamukhe devatā akṣarabhājaḥ karoty akṣaram akṣaram eva tad devatā anuprapibanti devapātreṇaiva tad devatās tṛpyanti ||
children.translated_text: It is a <s>virāj</s> of thirty-three syllables. There are thirty-three gods: eight <s>Vasu</s>s, eleven <s>Rudra</s>s, twelve <s>Āditya</s>s, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>. Thus, at the first opening of the <s>uktha</s>, he makes the deities sharers in the syllables. Syllable by syllable the deities drink after it; with a divine vessel the deities are satisfied.

children.text: tad āhur yathā vāva śastram evaṃ yājyāgneyaṃ hotājyaṃ śaṃsaty atha kasmād āgnendryā yajatīti ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, "As the <s>śastra</s> is, so should the offering-verse be. The <s>hotṛ</s> recites an <s>āgneya</s> <s>ājya</s>; then why does he sacrifice with an <s>āgnendrī</s>?"

children.text: yā vā āgnendry aindrāgnī vai sā sendrāgnam etad ukthaṃ graheṇa ca tūṣṇīṃśaṃsena ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>āgnendrī</s> is indeed <s>aindrāgnī</s>. This <s>uktha</s> is accompanied by <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, through the cup and through the silent recitation.

children.text: indrāgnī ā gataṃ sutaṃ gīrbhir nabho vareṇyam asya pātaṃ dhiyeṣitety aindrāgnam adhvaryur grāhaṃ gṛhṇāti bhūr agnir jyotir jyotir agnir indro jyotir bhuvo jyotir indraḥ sūryo jyotir jyotiḥ svaḥ sūrya iti hotā tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ śaṃsati tad yathaiva śastram evaṃ yājyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>adhvaryu</s> takes the <s>aindrāgna</s> cup with "O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, come to the pressed Soma; with songs, drink this excellent one, impelled by thought." The <s>hotṛ</s> recites the silent recitation: "<s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Agni</s> is light; light is <s>Agni</s>. <s>Indra</s> is light; the light of <s>bhuvas</s> is <s>Indra</s>. <s>Sūrya</s> is light; light is <s>svar</s>; <s>Sūrya</s>." Thus the offering-verses are just as the <s>śastra</s> is.

children.text: Chapter 68
hotṛjapaṃ japati retas tat siñcati ||
children.translated_text: He mutters the <s>hotṛjapa</s> (hotṛ's muttering); thereby he pours seed.

children.text: upāṃśu japaty upāṃśv iva vai retasaḥ siktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He mutters under his breath; for the pouring of seed is, as it were, under one's breath.

children.text: purāhāvājjapati yad vai kiṃcordhvam āhāvācchastrasyaiva tat ||
children.translated_text: He mutters before the summons. Whatever is after the summons belongs to the <s>śastra</s> itself.

children.text: parāñcaṃ catuṣpady āsīnam abhyāhvayate tasmāt parāñco bhūtvā catuṣpādo retaḥ siñcanti ||
children.translated_text: He calls upon one sitting turned away, as a quadruped; therefore quadrupeds, having turned away, pour seed.

children.text: samyaṅ dvipād bhavati tasmāt samyañco bhūtvā dvipādo retaḥ siñcanti ||
children.translated_text: The biped is facing straight forward; therefore bipeds, facing straight forward, pour seed.

children.text: pitā mātariśvety āha prāṇo vai pitā prāṇo mātariśvā prāṇo reto retas tat siñcati ||
children.translated_text: He says, "The father is <s>Mātariśvan</s>." Breath is the father; breath is <s>Mātariśvan</s>; breath is seed. Thereby he pours seed.

children.text: achidrā padā dhā iti reto vā achidram ato hyachidraḥ sambhavati ||
children.translated_text: With "Set it down with unbroken feet," for seed is unbroken; from it, indeed, an unbroken being is born.

children.text: achidrokthā kavayaḥ śaṃsann iti ye vā anūcānās te kavayas ta idam achidraṃ retaḥ prajanayann ity eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: With "The poets, reciting unbroken <s>uktha</s>s," for those who have studied are the poets. Thereby he says just this: "They generated this unbroken seed."

children.text: somo viśvavin nīthāni neṣad bṛhaspatir ukthāmadāni śaṃsiṣad iti brahma vai bṛhaspatiḥ kṣatraṃ somaḥ stutaśastrāṇi nīthāni cokthamadāni ca daivena caivaitad brahmaṇā prasūto daivena ca kṣatreṇokthāni śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: With "May <s>Soma</s>, knower of all, lead the guiding ways; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> recite the delights of the <s>uktha</s>," for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is priestly power and <s>Soma</s> is royal power. The praised recitations are the guiding ways and the delights of the <s>uktha</s>. Thus, impelled by divine priestly power and by divine royal power, he recites the <s>uktha</s>s.

children.text: etau ha vā asya sarvasya prasavasyeśāte yad idaṃ kiṃca ||
children.translated_text: These two are the lords of all this bringing-forth, whatever there is here.

children.text: tad yad etābhyām aprasūtaḥ karoty akṛtaṃ tad akṛtam akar iti vai nindanti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever he does without being impelled by these two is not done. People blame it, saying, "He has made the undone remain undone."

children.text: kṛtam asya kṛtam bhavati nāsyākṛtaṃ kṛtam bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: What has been done by him becomes done; what has not been done by him does not become done, who knows thus.

children.text: vāg āyur viśvāyur viśvam āyur ity āha prāṇo vā āyuḥ prāṇo reto vāg yonir yoniṃ tad upasaṃdhāya retaḥ siñcati ||
children.translated_text: He says, "Speech is life, universal life, the life of all." Breath is life; breath is seed; speech is the womb. Having joined the womb, he thereby pours seed.

children.text: ka idaṃ śaṃsiṣyati sa idaṃ śaṃsiṣyatīty āha prajāpatir vai kaḥ prajāpatiḥ prajanayiṣyatīty eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: He says, "Who will recite this? He will recite this." <s>Ka</s> is <s>Prajāpati</s>. Thereby he says just this: "<s>Prajāpati</s> will generate."

children.text: Chapter 69
āhūya tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ śaṃsati retas tat siktam vikaroti siktir vā agre 'tha vikṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having called, he recites the silent recitation; thereby he transforms the seed that has been poured. First there is pouring, and then transformation.

children.text: upāṃśu tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ śaṃsaty upāṃśv iva vai retasaḥ siktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites the silent recitation under his breath; for the pouring of seed is, as it were, under one's breath.

children.text: tira iva tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ śaṃsati tira iva vai retāṃsi vikriyante ||
children.translated_text: He recites the silent recitation as if across and hidden; for seeds are transformed as if across and hidden.

children.text: ṣaṭpadaṃ tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ śaṃsati ṣaḍvidho vai puruṣaḥ ṣaﾱaṅga ātmānam eva tat ṣaḍvidhaṃ ṣaﾱaṅgaṃ vikaroti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the silent recitation as six-footed. The person is sixfold; the self is six-limbed. Thereby he transforms his own self as sixfold and six-limbed.

children.text: tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ śastvā purorucaṃ śaṃsati retas tad vikṛtam prajanayati vikṛtir vā agre 'tha jātiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having recited the silent recitation, he recites the <s>puroruc</s>; thereby he generates the seed that has been transformed. First there is transformation, and then birth.

children.text: uccaiḥ purorucaṃ śaṃsaty uccair evainaṃ tat prajanayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>puroruc</s> aloud; thereby, quite aloud, he causes him to be born.

children.text: dvādaśapadām purorucāṃ śaṃsati dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ so 'sya sarvasya prajanayitā sa yo 'sya sarvasya prajanayitā sa evainaṃ tat prajayā paśubhiḥ prajanayati prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: He recites a twelve-footed <s>puroruc</s>. The year is twelve months; the year is <s>Prajāpati</s>; he is the begetter of all this. Therefore he who is the begetter of all this thereby begets him with offspring and cattle, for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is born with offspring and cattle who knows thus.

children.text: jātavedasyām purorucaṃ śaṃsati jātavedonyaṅgām ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>puroruc</s> in the hymn to <s>Jātavedas</s>, the one beginning with <s>Jātavedas</s>.

children.text: tad āhur yat tṛtīyasavanam eva jātavedasa āyatanam atha kasmāt prātaḥsavane jātavedasyām purorucaṃ śaṃsatīti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If the third pressing is the proper place of <s>Jātavedas</s>, then why does he recite the <s>puroruc</s> to <s>Jātavedas</s> at the morning pressing?"

children.text: prāṇo vai jātavedāḥ sa hi jātānāṃ veda yāvatāṃ vai sa jātānāṃ veda te bhavanti yeṣām u na veda kim u te syur yo vā ājya ātmasaṃskṛtiṃ veda tat suviditam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jātavedas</s> is <s>prāṇa</s> (breath). For he knows those that are born. As many of those born as he knows, they exist; but those whom he does not know, what would they be? Whoever knows the self-preparation in the <s>ājya</s> has it well known.

children.text: Chapter 70
pra vo devāyāgnaya iti śaṃsati prāṇo vai pra prāṇaṃ hīmāni sarvāṇi bhūtāny anuprayanti prāṇam eva tat saṃbhāvayati prāṇaṃ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Pra vo devāyāgnaye." The syllable "pra" is <s>prāṇa</s>; for all these beings follow after <s>prāṇa</s>. Thereby he makes <s>prāṇa</s> present; he prepares <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: dīdivāṃsam apūrvyam iti śaṃsati mano vai dīdāya manaso hi na kiṃcana pūrvam asti mana eva tat saṃbhāvayati manaḥ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Dīdivāṃsam apūrvyam." Mind indeed shines forth; for nothing is prior to mind. Thereby he makes mind present; he prepares mind.

children.text: sa naḥ śarmāṇi vītaya iti śaṃsati vāg vai śarma tasmād vācānuvadantam āha śarmavad āsmā ayāṃsīti vācam eva tat saṃbhāvayati vācaṃ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Sa naḥ śarmāṇi vītaye." Speech is protection; therefore, when a man approves one who has spoken, he says, "You have come to him with protection." Thereby he makes speech present; he prepares speech.

children.text: uta no brahmann aviṣa iti śaṃsati śrotraṃ vai brahma śrotreṇa hi brahma śṛṇoti śrotre brahma pratiṣṭhitaṃ śrotram eva tat saṃbhāvayati śrotraṃ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Uta no brahmann aviṣa." Hearing is <s>brahman</s>; for by hearing one hears the <s>brahman</s>, and the <s>brahman</s> is established in hearing. Thereby he makes hearing present; he prepares hearing.

children.text: sa yantā vipra eṣām iti śaṃsaty apāno vai yantāpānena hyayaṃ yataḥ prāṇo na parāṅ bhavaty apānam eva tat saṃbhāvayaty apānaṃ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Sa yantā vipra eṣām." The <s>apāna</s> is the guide; for by the <s>apāna</s> this restrained <s>prāṇa</s> does not turn away. Thereby he makes <s>apāna</s> present; he prepares <s>apāna</s>.

children.text: ṛtāvā yasya rodasī iti śaṃsati cakṣur vā ṛtaṃ tasmād yataro vivadamānayor āhāham anuṣṭhyā cakṣuṣādarśam iti tasya śraddadhati cakṣur eva tat saṃbhāvayati cakṣuḥ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Ṛtāvā yasya rodasī." Sight is <s>ṛta</s> (truthful order); therefore, when one of two disputants says, "I have seen it with my own eyes in accordance with fact," they trust him. Thereby he makes sight present; he prepares sight.

children.text: nū no rāsva sahasravat tokavat puṣṭimad vasv ity uttamayā paridadhāty ātmā vai samastaḥ sahasravāṃs tokavān puṣṭimān ātmānam eva tat samastaṃ saṃbhāvayaty ātmānaṃ samastaṃ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse he encloses it: "Nū no rāsva sahasravat tokavat puṣṭimad vasu." The self is complete, thousandfold, rich in offspring, and rich in nourishment. Thereby he makes the complete self present; he prepares the complete self.

children.text: yājyayā yajati prattir vai yājyā puṇyaiva lakṣmīḥ puṇyām eva tallakṣmīṃ saṃbhāvayati puṇyāṃ lakṣmīṃ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices with the <s>yājyā</s>. The <s>yājyā</s> is giving; it is blessed prosperity. Thereby he makes blessed prosperity present; he prepares blessed prosperity.

children.text: sa evaṃ vidvāṃś chandomayo devatāmayo brahmamayo 'mṛtamayaḥ sambhūya devatā apyeti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Thus, knowing in this way, having become made of metres, made of deities, made of <s>brahman</s>, and made of immortality, he reaches the deities, who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai tad veda yathā chandomayo devatāmayo brahmamayo 'mṛtamayaḥ sambhūya devatā apyeti tat suviditam ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows how, having become made of metres, made of deities, made of <s>brahman</s>, and made of immortality, one reaches the deities: that is well known.

children.text: ity adhyātmam athādhidaivatam ||
children.translated_text: So much with reference to the self; now with reference to the deities.

children.text: Chapter 71
ṣaṭpadaṃ tūṣṇīṃśaṃsaṃ śaṃsati ṣaḍ vā ṛtava ṛtūn eva tat kalpayaty ṛtūn apyeti ||
children.translated_text: He recites a six-footed silent recitation. There are six seasons; thereby he sets the seasons in order, and he reaches the seasons.

children.text: dvādaśapadām purorucaṃ śaṃsati dvādaśa vai māsā māsān eva tat kalpayati māsān apyeti ||
children.translated_text: He recites a twelve-footed <s>puroruc</s>. There are twelve months; thereby he sets the months in order, and he reaches the months.

children.text: pra vo devāyāgnaya iti śaṃsaty antarikṣaṃ vai prāntarikṣaṃ hīmāni sarvāṇi bhūtāny anuprayanty antarikṣam eva tat kalpayaty antarikṣamapyeti ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Pra vo devāyāgnaye." The midspace is "pra"; for all these beings follow after the midspace. Thereby he sets the midspace in order, and he reaches the midspace.

children.text: dīdivāṃsam apūrvyam iti śaṃsaty asau vai dīdāya yo 'sau tapaty etasmāddhi na kiṃcana pūrvam asty etam eva tat kalpayaty etam apyeti ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Dīdivāṃsam apūrvyam." That one yonder who gives heat is the one who shines forth; for nothing is prior to him. Thereby he sets that one in order, and he reaches that one.

children.text: sa naḥ śarmāṇi vītaya iti śaṃsaty agnir vai śarmāny annādyāni yacchaty agnim eva tat kalpayaty agnim apyeti ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Sa naḥ śarmāṇi vītaye." <s>Agni</s> gives protections, foods, and means of eating. Thereby he sets <s>Agni</s> in order, and he reaches <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: uta no brahmann aviṣa iti śaṃsati candramā vai brahma candramasam eva tat kalpayati candramasam apyeti ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Uta no brahmann aviṣa." The moon is <s>brahman</s>. Thereby he sets the moon in order, and he reaches the moon.

children.text: sa yantā vipra eṣām iti śaṃsati vāyur vai yantā vāyunā hīdaṃ yatam antarikṣaṃ na samṛcchati vāyum eva tat kalpayati vāyum apyeti ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Sa yantā vipra eṣām." <s>Vāyu</s> is the guide; for this midspace, held by <s>Vāyu</s>, does not collapse. Thereby he sets <s>Vāyu</s> in order, and he reaches <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: ṛtāvā yasya rodasī iti śaṃsati dyāvāpṛthivī vai rodasī dyāvāpṛthivī eva tat kalpayati dyāvāpṛthivī apyeti ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "Ṛtāvā yasya rodasī." Heaven and earth are the two <s>rodasī</s>. Thereby he sets heaven and earth in order, and he reaches heaven and earth.

children.text: nū no rāsva sahasravat tokavat puṣṭimad vasv ity uttamayā paridadhāti saṃvatsaro vai samastaḥ sahasravāṃs tokavān puṣṭimān saṃvatsaram eva tat samastaṃ kalpayati saṃvatsaraṃ samastam apyeti ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse he encloses it: "Nū no rāsva sahasravat tokavat puṣṭimad vasu." The year is complete, thousandfold, rich in offspring, and rich in nourishment. Thereby he sets the complete year in order, and he reaches the complete year.

children.text: yājyayā yajati vṛṣṭir vai yājyā vidyud eva vidyuddhīdaṃ vṛṣṭim annādyaṃ samprayacchati vidyutam eva tat kalpayati vidyutam apyeti ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices with the <s>yājyā</s>. The <s>yājyā</s> is rain, indeed lightning; for lightning bestows this rain as food and nourishment. Thereby he sets lightning in order, and he reaches lightning.

children.text: sa evaṃ vidvān etanmayo devatāmayo bhavati bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, knowing in this way, he becomes made of that, made of the deities; he becomes, he becomes.

children.text: Chapter 72
grahokthaṃ vā etad yat praugaṃ nava prātar grahā gṛhyante navabhir bahiṣpavamāne stuvate stute stome daśamaṃ gṛhṇāti hiṃkāra itarāsāṃ daśamaḥ so sā sammā ||
children.translated_text: This <s>prauga</s> is indeed a <s>grahoktha</s>. Nine morning cups are taken; with nine verses they sing the <s>bahiṣpavamāna</s>. When the <s>stoma</s> has been sung, he takes the tenth. The <s>hiṃkāra</s> is the tenth of the others. That is its proper correspondence.

children.text: vāyavyaṃ śaṃsati tena vāyavya ukthavān ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Vāyavya</s>; by that the <s>Vāyavya</s> has an <s>uktha</s>.

children.text: aindravāyavaṃ śaṃsati tenaindravāyava ukthavān ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Aindravāyava</s>; by that the <s>Aindravāyava</s> is furnished with an <s>uktha</s>.

children.text: maitrāvaruṇaṃ śaṃsati tena maitrāvaruṇa ukthavān ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; by that the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is furnished with an <s>uktha</s>.

children.text: āśvinaṃ śaṃsati tenāśvina ukthavān ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Āśvina</s>; by that the <s>Āśvina</s> is furnished with an <s>uktha</s>.

children.text: aindraṃ śaṃsati tena śukrāmanthinā ukthavantau ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Aindra</s>; by that the <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Manthin</s> are furnished with an <s>uktha</s>.

children.text: vaiśvadevaṃ śaṃsati tenāgrayaṇa ukthavān ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>; by that the <s>Agrayaṇa</s> is furnished with an <s>uktha</s>.

children.text: sārasvataṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Sārasvata</s>.

children.text: na sārasvato graho 'sti ||
children.translated_text: There is no <s>Sārasvata</s> cup.

children.text: vāk tu sarasvatī ye tu keca vācā grahā gṛhyante te 'sya sarve śastokthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But speech is <s>Sarasvatī</s>; whatever cups are drawn with speech, all of those have been praised and furnished with <s>uktha</s> for him.

children.text: ukthino bhavanti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: They become possessed of <s>uktha</s>, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 73
annādyaṃ vā etenāvarunddhe yat praugam anyānyā devatā prauge śasyate 'nyad anyad uktham prauge kriyate ||
children.translated_text: By this he secures food for eating, namely the <s>prauga</s>: one deity after another is praised in the <s>prauga</s>, and one <s>uktha</s> after another is performed in the <s>prauga</s>.

children.text: anyad anyad asyānnādyaṃ graheṣu dhriyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: One kind of food after another is placed for him among the cups, who knows thus.

children.text: etaddha vai yajamānasyādhyātmatamam ivokthaṃ yat praugaṃ tasmād enainaitad upekṣyatamam ivety āhur etena hy enaṃ hotā saṃskarotīti ||
children.translated_text: This <s>prauga</s> is indeed, as it were, the sacrificer's most inward <s>uktha</s>. Therefore they say that this is, as it were, the thing most to be carefully observed for him, for by this the <s>hotṛ</s> prepares him.

children.text: vāyavyaṃ śaṃsati tasmād āhur vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇo reto retaḥ puruṣasya prathamaṃ sambhavataḥ sambhavatīti yad vāyavyaṃ śaṃsati prāṇam evāsya tat saṃskaroti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Vāyavya</s>. Therefore they say, '<s>Vāyu</s> is breath; breath is seed; seed is the first thing that comes into being in a man as he comes into being.' Since he recites the <s>Vāyavya</s>, he thereby prepares his breath.

children.text: aindravāyavaṃ śaṃsati yatra vāva prāṇas tad apāno yad aindravāyavaṃ śaṃsati prāṇāpānāv evāsya tat saṃskaroti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Aindravāyava</s>. Wherever there is in-breath, there also is out-breath. Since he recites the <s>Aindravāyava</s>, he thereby prepares his in-breath and out-breath.

children.text: maitrāvaruṇaṃ śaṃsati tasmād āhuś cakṣuḥ puruṣasya prathamaṃ sambhavataḥ sambhavatīti yan maitrāvaruṇaṃ śaṃsati cakṣur evāsya tat saṃskaroti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>. Therefore they say, 'The eye is the first thing that comes into being in a man as he comes into being.' Since he recites the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, he thereby prepares his sight.

children.text: āśvinaṃ śaṃsati tasmāt kumāraṃ jātaṃ saṃvadanta upa vai śuśrūṣate ni vai dhyāyatīti yad āśvinaṃ śaṃsati śrotram evāsya tat saṃskaroti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Āśvina</s>. Therefore, when people speak to a newborn child, it listens attentively and contemplates. Since he recites the <s>Āśvina</s>, he thereby prepares his hearing.

children.text: aindraṃ śaṃsati tasmāt kumāraṃ jātaṃ saṃvadante pratidhārayati vai grīvā atho śira iti yad aindraṃ śaṃsati vīryam evāsya tat saṃskaroti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Aindra</s>. Therefore, when people speak to a newborn child, they say, 'The neck indeed holds up, and then the head.' Since he recites the <s>Aindra</s>, he thereby prepares his strength.

children.text: vaiśvadevaṃ śaṃsati tasmāt kumāro jātaḥ paśceva pracarati vaiśvadevāni hy aṅgāni yad vaiśvadevaṃ śaṃsaty aṅgāny evāsya tat saṃskaroti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. Therefore a newborn child moves about afterward, as it were; for the limbs are connected with the <s>All-gods</s>. Since he recites the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, he thereby prepares his limbs.

children.text: sārasvataṃ śaṃsati tasmāt kumāraṃ jātaṃ jaghanyā vāg āviśati vāgghi sarasvatī yat sārasvataṃ śaṃsati vācam evāsya tat saṃskaroti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Sārasvata</s>. Therefore speech enters a newborn child last, for speech is <s>Sarasvatī</s>. Since he recites the <s>Sārasvata</s>, he thereby prepares his speech.

children.text: eṣa vai jāto jāyate sarvābhya etābhyo devatābhyaḥ sarvebhya ukthebhyaḥ sarvebhyaś chandobhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ praugebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ savanebhyo ya evaṃ veda yasya caivaṃ viduṣa etacchaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus, and he for whom those who know thus recite this, is born as truly born from all these deities, from all the <s>ukthas</s>, from all the metres, from all the <s>praugas</s>, and from all the pressings.

children.text: Chapter 74
prāṇānāṃ vā etad ukthaṃ yat praugaṃ sapta devatāḥ śaṃsati sapta vai śīrṣan prāṇāḥ śīrṣann eva tat prāṇān dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: This <s>prauga</s> is the <s>uktha</s> of the vital breaths. He recites seven deities; there are seven vital breaths in the head. Thus he places the vital breaths in the head itself.

children.text: kiṃ sa yajamānasya pāpabhadram ādriyeteti ha smāha yo 'sya hotā syād ity atraivainaṃ yathā kāmayeta tathā kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: 'Why should he care about harm or benefit for the sacrificer,' so one who was his <s>hotṛ</s> used to say; right here he may do to him just as he desires.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta prāṇenainaṃ vyardhayānīti vāyavyam asya lubdhaṃ śaṃsed ṛcaṃ vā padaṃ vātīyāt tenaiva tal lubdham prāṇenaivainaṃ tad vyardhayati ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire, 'May I deprive him of breath,' he should recite his <s>Vāyavya</s> in a spoiled way, or skip over a verse or a word. By that very spoiled element he deprives him of breath itself.

children.text: yam kāmayeta prāṇāpānābhyām enaṃ vyardhayānīty aindravāyavam asya lubdhaṃ śaṃsed ṛcaṃ vā padaṃ vātīyāt tenaiva tallubdham prāṇāpānābhyām evainaṃ tad vyardhayati ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire, 'May I deprive him of in-breath and out-breath,' he should recite his <s>Aindravāyava</s> in a spoiled way, or skip over a verse or a word. By that very spoiled element he deprives him of in-breath and out-breath themselves.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta cakṣuṣainaṃ vyardhayānīti maitrāvaruṇam asya lubdhaṃ śaṃsed ṛcam vā padaṃ vātīyāt tenaiva tallubdhaṃ cakṣuṣaivainam tad vyardhayati ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire, 'May I deprive him of sight,' he should recite his <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> in a spoiled way, or skip over a verse or a word. By that very spoiled element he deprives him of sight itself.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta śrotreṇainaṃ vyardhayānīty āśvinam asya lubdhaṃ śaṃsed ṛcaṃ vā padaṃ vātīyāt tenaiva tallubdhaṃ śrotreṇaivainaṃ tad vyardhayati ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire, 'May I deprive him of hearing,' he should recite his <s>Āśvina</s> in a spoiled way, or skip over a verse or a word. By that very spoiled element he deprives him of hearing itself.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta vīryeṇainaṃ vyardhayānīty aindram asya lubdhaṃ śaṃsed ṛcaṃ vā padaṃ vātīyāt tenaiva tallubdhaṃ vīryenaivainaṃ tad vyardhayati ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire, 'May I deprive him of strength,' he should recite his <s>Aindra</s> in a spoiled way, or skip over a verse or a word. By that very spoiled element he deprives him of strength itself.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayetāṅgair enaṃ vyardhayānīti vaiśvadevam asya lubdhaṃ śaṃsed ṛcaṃ vā padaṃ vātīyāt tenaiva tallubdham aṅgair evainaṃ tadvyardhayati ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire, 'May I deprive him of his limbs,' he should recite his <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> in a spoiled way, or skip over a verse or a word. By that very spoiled element he deprives him of his limbs themselves.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta vācainaṃ vyardhayānīti sārasvatam asya lubdhaṃ śaṃsed ṛcaṃ vā padaṃ vātīyāt tenaiva tallubdhaṃ vācaivainaṃ tad vyardhayati ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire, 'May I deprive him of speech,' he should recite his <s>Sārasvata</s> in a spoiled way, or skip over a verse or a word. By that very spoiled element he deprives him of speech itself.

children.text: yam u kāmayeta sarvair enam aṅgaiḥ sarveṇātmanā samardhayānīty etad evāsya yathāpūrvam ṛju kﾱptaṃ śaṃset sarvair evainaṃ tad aṅgaiḥ sarveṇātmanā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: But if he should desire, 'May I make him prosper with all his limbs and with his whole self,' he should recite that same series for him in its former order, straight and properly arranged. By that he makes him prosper with all his limbs and with his whole self.

children.text: sarvair aṅgaiḥ sarveṇātmanā samṛdhyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers with all his limbs and with his whole self, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 75
tad āhur yathā vāva stotram evaṃ śastram āgneyīṣu sāmagāḥ stuvate vāyavyayā hotā pratipadyate katham asya āgneyyo 'nuśastā bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: Then they say, 'As is the chant, so is the recitation. The <s>sāman</s>-singers chant among the <s>Āgneyī</s> verses, while the <s>hotṛ</s> begins with a <s>Vāyavya</s> verse. How, then, do the <s>Āgneyī</s> verses come to have been recited for him?'

children.text: agner vā etāḥ sarvās tanvo yad etā devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For all these deities are forms of <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: sa yad agniḥ pravān iva dahati tad asya vāyavyaṃ rūpaṃ tad asya tenānuśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Agni</s> burns as though driven forward, that is his form belonging to <s>Vāyu</s>; with that form of his he thereby receives praise.

children.text: atha yad dvaidham iva kṛtvā dahati dvau vā indravāyū tad asyaindravāyavaṃ rūpaṃ tad asya tenānuśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And when he burns as though making a division in two, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> are two; that is his <s>Aindravāyava</s> form, and with that form of his he thereby receives praise.

children.text: atha yad uc ca hṛṣyati ni ca hṛṣyati tad asya maitrāvaruṇaṃ rūpaṃ tad asya tenānuśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And when he both bristles upward and bristles downward, that is his <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> form; with that form of his he thereby receives praise.

children.text: sa yad agnir ghorasaṃsparśas tad asya vāruṇaṃ rūpaṃ taṃ yad ghorasaṃsparśaṃ santam mitrakṛtyevopāsate tad asya maitraṃ rūpaṃ tad asya tenānuśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Agni</s> is terrible to the touch, that is his form belonging to <s>Varuṇa</s>. When, though he is terrible to the touch, they attend upon him as if with a friendly act, that is his <s>Maitra</s> form; with that form of his he thereby receives praise.

children.text: atha yad enaṃ dvābhyām bāhubhyāṃ dvābhyām araṇībhyāṃ manthanti dvau vā aśvinau tad asyāśvinaṃ rūpaṃ tad asya tenānuśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And when they churn him with two arms and with two kindling-sticks, the <s>Aśvins</s> are two; that is his <s>Āśvina</s> form, and with that form of his he thereby receives praise.

children.text: atha yad uccairghoṣaḥ stanayan bababākurvann iva dahati yasmād bhūtāni vijante tad asyaindraṃ rūpaṃ tad asya tenānuśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And when he burns with a loud noise, thundering and as if crying 'bababā,' so that beings tremble from him, that is his form belonging to <s>Indra</s>; with that form of his he thereby receives praise.

children.text: atha yad enam ekaṃ santaṃ bahudhā viharanti tad asya vaiśvadevaṃ rūpaṃ tad asya tenānuśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And when, though he is one, they distribute him in many ways, that is his <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> form; with that form of his he thereby receives praise.

children.text: atha yat sphūrjayan vācam iva vadan dahati tad asya sārasvataṃ rūpaṃ tad asya tenānuśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And when he burns while crackling and as if speaking with speech, that is his form belonging to <s>Sarasvatī</s>; with that form of his he thereby receives praise.

children.text: evam u hāsya vāyavyayaiva pratipadyamānasya tṛcena tṛcenaivaitābhir devatābhiḥ stotriyo 'nuśasto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for him who begins with the <s>Vāyavya</s> set, with each triad of verses the stotriya has been praised by these very deities.

children.text: viśvebhiḥ somyam madhv agna indreṇa vāyunā pibā mitrasya dhāmabhir iti vaiśvadevam ukthaṃ śastvā vaiśvadevyā yajati yathābhāgaṃ tad devatāḥ prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: Having recited the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> uktha, 'O <s>Agni</s>, drink the Soma-honey with all the gods, with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, with the abodes of <s>Mitra</s>,' he sacrifices with a <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse; in accordance with their shares he thereby pleases the deities.

children.text: Chapter 76
devapātraṃ vā etad yad vaṣaṭkāro vaṣaṭkaroti devapātreṇaiva tad devatās tarpayati ||
children.translated_text: The vaṣaṭ call is a vessel of the gods. When he utters vaṣaṭ, with the vessel of the gods he thereby satisfies the deities.

children.text: anuvaṣaṭkaroti tad yathādo 'śvān vā gā vā punarabhyākāraṃ tarpayanty evam evaitad devatāḥ punarabhyākāraṃ tarpayanti yad anuvaṣaṭkaroti ||
children.translated_text: He makes the anuvaṣaṭ call. Just as here they satisfy horses or cows again by a repeated summoning, so in just this way they satisfy the deities again by a repeated summoning when he makes the anuvaṣaṭ call.

children.text: imān evāgnīn upāsata ity āhur dhiṣṇyān atha kasmāt pūrvasminn eva juhvati pūrvasmin vaṣaṭkurvantīti ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'They attend upon these fires here, the dhiṣṇya hearths; then why do they sacrifice only in the former fire, why do they utter vaṣaṭ in the former fire?'

children.text: yad eva somasyāgne vīhīty anuvaṣaṭkaroti tena dhiṣṇyān prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: In that he makes the anuvaṣaṭ call with 'O <s>Agni</s>, go to the Soma,' by that he pleases the dhiṣṇya hearths.

children.text: asaṃsthitān somān bhakṣayantīty āhur yeṣāṃ nānuvaṣaṭkaroti ko nu somasya sviṣṭakṛdbhāga iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'They consume Soma portions that have not been brought to completion, for which he does not make the anuvaṣaṭ call. What, then, is the sviṣṭakṛt share of the Soma?'

children.text: yad vāva somasyāgne vīhīty anuvaṣaṭkaroti tenaiva saṃsthitān somān bhakṣayanti sa u eva somasya sviṣṭakṛdbhāgo vaṣaṭkaroti ||
children.translated_text: In fact, when he makes the anuvaṣaṭ call with 'O <s>Agni</s>, go to the Soma,' by that alone they consume Soma portions that have been brought to completion. That very call is the sviṣṭakṛt share of the Soma; he utters vaṣaṭ.

children.text: Chapter 77
vajro vā eṣa yad vaṣaṭkāro yaṃ dviṣyāt taṃ dhyāyed vaṣaṭkariṣyaṃs tasminn eva taṃ vajram āsthāpayati ||
children.translated_text: This vaṣaṭ call is a thunderbolt. Whomever he should hate, he should think of him when about to utter vaṣaṭ; upon that very man he sets that thunderbolt.

children.text: ṣaﾱ iti vaṣaṭkaroti ṣaḍ vā ṛtava ṛtūn eva tat kalpayaty ṛtūn pratiṣṭhāpayaty ṛtūn vai pratitiṣṭhata idaṃ sarvam anupratitiṣṭhati yad idaṃ kiṃca ||
children.translated_text: He utters vaṣaṭ with 'ṣaṭ.' The seasons are six; thereby he arranges the seasons, establishes the seasons. For when the seasons are established, all this, whatever exists here, is established after them.

children.text: pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is established who knows thus.

children.text: tad u ha smāha hiraṇyadan baida etāni vā etena ṣaṭ pratiṣṭhāpayati dyaur antarikṣe pratiṣṭhitāntarikṣam pṛthivyām pṛthivy apsv āpaḥ satye satyam brahmaṇi brahma tapasīty etā eva tat pratiṣṭhāḥ pratitiṣṭhantīr idaṃ sarvam anupratitiṣṭhati yad idaṃ kiṃca pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: On this point <s>Hiraṇyadan Baida</s> used to say: 'By this he establishes these six. Heaven is established in the midspace, the midspace in the earth, the earth in the waters, the waters in truth, truth in brahman, and brahman in austerity.' Thus these very foundations, as they become established, all this, whatever exists here, becomes established after them. He is established who knows thus.

children.text: vauṣaﾱ iti vaṣaṭkaroty asau vāva vāv ṛtavaḥ ṣaﾱ etam eva tad ṛtuṣv ādadhāty ṛtuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati yādṛg iva vai devebhyaḥ karoti tādṛg ivāsmai devāḥ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: He utters vaṣaṭ with 'vauṣaṭ.' That one yonder, indeed, is the 'vau,' and the seasons are the 'ṣaṭ.' Thereby he places that one in the seasons and establishes him in the seasons. As one does for the gods, so the gods do for him.

children.text: Chapter 78
trayo vai vaṣaṭkārā vajro dhāmachad riktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are three vaṣaṭ calls: the thunderbolt, the support-covering one, and the empty one.

children.text: sa yam evoccair bali vaṣaṭkaroti sa vajraḥ ||
children.translated_text: That one which he utters loudly and forcefully as vaṣaṭ is the thunderbolt.

children.text: taṃ tam praharati dviṣate bhrātṛvyāya vadhaṃ yo 'sya stṛtyas tasmai startavai tasmāt sa bhrātṛvyavatā vaṣaṭkṛtyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He hurls it at the hateful rival, as a blow against the one who is to be struck by him, in order to strike him down. Therefore that vaṣaṭ should be uttered by one who has a rival.

children.text: atha yaḥ samaḥ saṃtato nirhāṇarcaḥ sa dhāmachat ||
children.translated_text: But the one that is even, continuous, and accompanied by the concluding verse is the support-covering one.

children.text: taṃ tam prajāś ca paśavaś cānūpatiṣṭhante tasmāt sa prajākāmena paśukāmena vaṣaṭkṛtyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On that one, offspring and cattle attend. Therefore that vaṣaṭ should be uttered by one who desires offspring and desires cattle.

children.text: atha yenaiva ṣaﾱ avarādhnoti sa riktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the one by which he misses the mark at the very syllable 'ṣaṭ' is the empty one.

children.text: riṇakty ātmānaṃ riṇakti yajamānam pāpīyān vaṣaṭkartā bhavati pāpīyān yasmai vaṣaṭkaroti tasmāt tasyāśāṃ neyāt ||
children.translated_text: He empties himself; he empties the sacrificer. The utterer of vaṣaṭ becomes worse, and the one for whom he utters vaṣaṭ becomes worse. Therefore one should not enter into expectation of that one.

children.text: kiṃ sa yajamānasya pāpabhadram ādriyeteti ha smāha yo 'sya hotā syād ity atraivainaṃ yathā kāmayeta tathā kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: 'Why should he care about the sacrificer's evil or good fortune?' so he used to say, 'the man who is his <s>hotṛ</s>.' Right there he should do with him as he wishes.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta yathaivānījāno 'bhūt tathaivejānaḥ syād iti yathaivāsya ṛcam brūyāt tathaivāsya vaṣaṭkuryāt sadṛśam evainaṃ tat karoti ||
children.translated_text: Of the man of whom he should wish, 'May he be just as he was when he had not sacrificed, even after he has sacrificed,' he should utter the vaṣaṭ for him just as he recites the verse for him. Thereby he makes him just the same.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta pāpīyān syād ity uccaistarām asya ṛcam uktvā śanaistarāṃ vaṣaṭkuryāt pāpīyāṃsam evainaṃ tat karoti ||
children.translated_text: Of the man of whom he should wish, 'May he become worse,' he should recite his verse more loudly and utter the vaṣaṭ more softly; thereby he makes him worse.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta śreyān syād iti śanaistarām asya ṛcam uktvoccaistarāṃ vaṣaṭkuryāc chriya evainaṃ tacchriyām ādadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Of the man of whom he should wish, 'May he become better,' he should recite his verse more softly and utter the vaṣaṭ more loudly; thereby he places prosperity, indeed prosperity, upon him.

children.text: saṃtatam ṛcā vaṣaṭkṛtyaṃ saṃtatyai ||
children.translated_text: The vaṣaṭ should be uttered continuously with the verse, for continuity.

children.text: saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is joined with offspring and cattle who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 79
yasyai devatāyai havir gṛhītaṃ syāt tāṃ dhyāyed vaṣaṭkariṣyan sākṣād eva tad devatām prīṇāti pratyakṣād devatāṃ yajati ||
children.translated_text: For whatever deity the oblation has been taken, he should meditate on that deity when he is about to make the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call. Thereby he directly gratifies that deity; he sacrifices to the deity as present before him.

children.text: vajro vai vaṣaṭkāraḥ sa eṣa prahṛto 'śānto dīdāya tasya haitasya na sarva iva śāntiṃ veda na pratiṣṭhāṃ tasmāddhāpy etarhi bhūyān iva mṛtyus tasya haiṣaiva śāntir eṣā pratiṣṭhā vāg ity eva tasmād vaṣaṭkṛtya vaṣaṭkṛtya vāg ity anumantrayeta sa enaṃ śānto na hinasti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> is a thunderbolt. Once hurled, unappeased, it blazes. Not everyone knows its appeasement or its establishment; therefore even now death is, as it were, greater. This alone is its appeasement, this its establishment: speech. Therefore, after each <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call, he should mutter after it, "Speech." When appeased, it does not harm him.

children.text: vaṣaṭkāra mā mām pramṛkṣo māhaṃ tvām pramṛkṣam bṛhatā mana upahvaye vyānena śarīram pratiṣṭhāsi pratiṣṭhāṃ gaccha pratiṣṭhām mā gamayeti vaṣaṭkāram anumantrayeta ||
children.translated_text: He should mutter after the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>: "O <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>, do not wipe me away; may I not wipe you away. With the great one I call upon mind; with the out-breathing I call upon the body. You are established; go to establishment; lead me to establishment."

children.text: tad u ha smāha dīrgham etat sad aprabhv ojaḥ saha ojaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On this point, they say, he used to declare, "This is long: being present, not mastering; vigor, strength, vigor."

children.text: ity eva vaṣaṭkāram anumantrayeta ||
children.translated_text: With these very words he should mutter after the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>.

children.text: ojaś ca ha vai sahaś ca vaṣaṭkārasya priyatame tanvau ||
children.translated_text: For vigor and strength are the two dearest bodies of the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>.

children.text: priyeṇaivainaṃ tad dhāmnā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: Thereby he prospers it with its own dear dwelling.

children.text: priyeṇa dhāmnā samṛdhyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers by the dear dwelling who knows thus.

children.text: vāk ca vai prāṇāpānau ca vaṣaṭkāras ta ete vaṣaṭkṛte vaṣaṭkṛte vyutkrāmanti tān anumantrayeta vāg ojaḥ saha ojo mayi prāṇāpānāv ity ātmany eva taddhotā vācaṃ ca prāṇāpānau ca pratiṣṭhāpayati sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya ||
children.translated_text: Speech, the in-breath and out-breath, and the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> are these. At each <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call they pass out. He should mutter after them, "Speech, vigor, strength, vigor; may the in-breath and out-breath be in me." Thereby the <s>hotṛ</s> establishes speech and the in-breath and out-breath within himself, for the whole span of life, for attaining the whole span of life.

children.text: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He reaches the whole span of life who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 80
yajño vai devebhya udakrāmat taṃ praiṣaiḥ praiṣam aicchan yat praiṣaiḥ praiṣam aicchaṃs tat praiṣāṇām praiṣatvam ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice went away from the gods. By summons after summons they sought to summon it. Because they sought to summon it by summonses, that is the summonhood of the <s>praiṣa</s>s.

children.text: taṃ purorugbhiḥ prārocayan yat purorugbhiḥ prārocayaṃs tat purorucām puroruktvam ||
children.translated_text: They made it shine forth with the <s>puroruc</s> verses. Because they made it shine forth with the <s>puroruc</s> verses, that is the prior-uttered nature of the <s>puroruc</s> verses.

children.text: taṃ vedyām anvavindan yad vedyām anvavindaṃs tad veder veditvam ||
children.translated_text: They found it upon the altar. Because they found it upon the altar, that is the altar's being a finding-place.

children.text: taṃ vittaṃ grahair vyagṛhṇata yadvittaṃ grahair vyagṛhṇata tad grahāṇāṃ grahatvam ||
children.translated_text: When they had found it, they seized it with the cups. Because, once found, they seized it with the cups, that is the cuphood of the <s>graha</s>s.

children.text: taṃ vittvā nividbhir nyavedayan yad vittvā nividbhir nyavedayaṃs tan nividāṃ nivittvam ||
children.translated_text: When they had found it, they announced it with the <s>nivid</s>s. Because, once found, they announced it with the <s>nivid</s>s, that is the announcing nature of the <s>nivid</s>s.

children.text: mahad vāva naṣṭaiṣy abhy alpaṃ vecchati yataro vāva tayor jyāya ivābhīcchati sa eva tayoḥ sādhīya icchati ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, one who is seeking something great that has been lost may also seek a little thing; and whichever of the two seeks the greater thing, he is the one who seeks the better of the two.

children.text: ya u eva praiṣān varṣīyaso varṣīyaso veda sa u eva tān sādhīyo veda naṣṭaiṣyaṃ hy etad yat praiṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the <s>praiṣa</s>s as greater and greater, he knows them better; for what the <s>praiṣa</s>s are is a seeking for what has been lost.

children.text: tasmāt prahvas tiṣṭhan preṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he gives the summons while standing bent forward.

children.text: Chapter 81
garbhā vā eta ukthānāṃ yan nividas tad yat purastād ukthānām prātaḥsavane dhīyante tasmāt parāñco garbhā dhīyante parāñcaḥ sambhavanti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nivid</s>s are the embryos of the <s>uktha</s>s. Since they are placed before the <s>uktha</s>s at the morning pressing, therefore embryos are placed turned outward and come into being turned outward.

children.text: yan madhyato madhyaṃdine dhīyante tasmān madhye garbhā dhṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since they are placed in the middle at the midday pressing, therefore embryos are held in the middle.

children.text: yad antatas tṛtīyasavane dhīyante tasmād amuto 'rvāñco garbhāḥ prajāyante prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: Since they are placed at the end at the third pressing, therefore embryos are born from there hither, for birth.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is born with offspring and cattle who knows thus.

children.text: peśā vā eta ukthānāṃ yan nividas tad yat purastād ukthānām prātaḥsavane dhīyante yathaiva pravayaṇataḥ peśaḥ kuryāt tādṛk tad yan madhyato madhyaṃdine dhīyante yathaiva madhyataḥ peśaḥ kuryāt tādṛk tad yad antatas tṛtīyasavane dhīyante yathaivāvaprajjanataḥ peśaḥ kuryāt tādṛk tat ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nivid</s>s are the ornamentation of the <s>uktha</s>s. Since they are placed before the <s>uktha</s>s at the morning pressing, it is as if one were to make the ornamentation from the beginning. Since they are placed in the middle at the midday pressing, it is as if one were to make the ornamentation from the middle. Since they are placed at the end at the third pressing, it is as if one were to make the ornamentation from the finishing end.

children.text: sarvato yajñasya peśasā śobhate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice shines with ornamentation on every side for one who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 82
sauryā vā etā devatā yan nividas tad yat purastād ukthānām prātaḥsavane dhīyante madhyato madhyaṃdine 'ntatas tṛtīyasavana ādityasyaiva tad vratam anuparyāvartante ||
children.translated_text: These <s>nivid</s>s are solar deities. Since they are placed before the <s>uktha</s>s at the morning pressing, in the middle at the midday pressing, and at the end at the third pressing, they follow all around the observance of <s>Āditya</s> himself.

children.text: paccho vai devā yajñaṃ samabharaṃs tasmāt paccho nividaḥ śasyante ||
children.translated_text: The gods gathered the sacrifice together word by word; therefore the <s>nivid</s>s are recited word by word.

children.text: yad vai tad devā yajñaṃ samabharaṃs tasmād aśvaḥ samabhavat tasmād āhur aśvaṃ nividāṃ śaṃstre dadyād iti tad u khalu varam eva dadati ||
children.translated_text: From that sacrifice which the gods gathered together, the horse came into being. Therefore they say, "One should give a horse at the recitation of the <s>nivid</s>s." But in fact they give only an excellent gift.

children.text: na nividaḥ padam atīyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not pass over a word of the <s>nivid</s>s.

children.text: yan nividaḥ padam atīyād yajñasya tacchidraṃ kuryād yajñasya vai chidraṃ sravad yajamāno 'nu pāpīyān bhavati tasmān na nividaḥ padam atīyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he were to pass over a word of the <s>nivid</s>s, he would make a breach in the sacrifice. When a breach in the sacrifice leaks, the <s>yajamāna</s> becomes worse after it. Therefore he should not pass over a word of the <s>nivid</s>s.

children.text: na nividaḥ pade viparihared yan nividaḥ pade vipariharen mohayed yajñam mugdho yajamānaḥ syāt tasmān na nividaḥ pade vipariharet ||
children.translated_text: He should not transpose anything in a word of the <s>nivid</s>s. If he were to transpose anything in a word of the <s>nivid</s>s, he would bewilder the sacrifice; the <s>yajamāna</s> would be bewildered. Therefore he should not transpose anything in a word of the <s>nivid</s>s.

children.text: na nividaḥ pade samasyed yan nividaḥ pade samasyed yajñasya tad āyuḥ saṃharet pramāyuko yajamānaḥ syāt tasmān na nividaḥ pade samasyet ||
children.translated_text: He should not contract anything in a word of the <s>nivid</s>s. If he were to contract anything in a word of the <s>nivid</s>s, he would contract the life of the sacrifice; the <s>yajamāna</s> would be short-lived. Therefore he should not contract anything in a word of the <s>nivid</s>s.

children.text: predam brahma predaṃ kṣatram ity ete eva samasyed brahmakṣatrayoḥ saṃśrityai tasmād brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca saṃśrite ||
children.translated_text: Only these two he should combine: "Forward this <s>brahman</s>; forward this <s>kṣatra</s>," for the union of priestly power and royal power. Therefore <s>brahman</s> and <s>kṣatra</s> are joined together.

children.text: na tṛcaṃ na caturṛcam ati manyeta nividdhānam ekaikaṃ vai nividaḥ padam ṛcaṃ sūktam prati tasmān na tṛcaṃ na caturṛcam ati manyeta nividdhānaṃ nividā hy eva stotram atiśastam bhavati ||
children.translated_text: One should not disregard a triplet of verses, nor a set of four verses, when placing the <s>nivid</s>. For each single word of the <s>nivid</s> corresponds to a verse, to a hymn. Therefore one should not disregard a triplet or a set of four verses when placing the <s>nivid</s>; for by the <s>nivid</s> the chant becomes fully praised.

children.text: ekām pariśiṣya tṛtīyasavane nividaṃ dadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: At the third pressing he should place the <s>nivid</s>, leaving one verse remaining.

children.text: yad dve pariśiṣya dadhyāt prajananaṃ tad upahanyād garbhais tat prajā vyardhayet tasmād ekām eva pariśiṣya tṛtīyasavane nividaṃ dadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he were to place it leaving two verses remaining, he would injure procreation; with embryos he would deprive offspring of prosperity. Therefore he should place the <s>nivid</s> at the third pressing leaving just one verse remaining.

children.text: na sūktena nividam atipadyeta ||
children.translated_text: He should not pass beyond the <s>nivid</s> with the hymn.

children.text: yena sūktena nividam atipadyeta na tat punar upanivarteta vāstuham eva tat ||
children.translated_text: With whatever hymn he passes beyond the <s>nivid</s>, that does not return again; that is indeed destructive of the dwelling.

children.text: anyat taddaivataṃ tacchandasaṃ sūktam āhṛtya tasmin nividaṃ dadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having brought another hymn of the same deity and the same metre, he should place the <s>nivid</s> in that.

children.text: mā pra gāma patho vayam iti purastāt sūktasya śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites before the hymn, 'May we not go forth from the path.'

children.text: patho vā eṣa praiti yo yajñe muhyati mā yajñād indra somina iti yajñād eva tan na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: For one who becomes confused in the sacrifice goes forth from the path. With 'May we not fall away from the sacrifice, O <s>Indra</s>, we Soma-pressers,' he thereby does not fall away from the sacrifice.

children.text: mānta sthur no arātaya ity arātīyata eva tad apahanti ||
children.translated_text: With 'May hostile powers not stand around us,' he thereby drives away hostility itself.

children.text: yo yajñasya prasādhanas tantur deveṣv ātataḥ tam āhutaṃ naśīmahīti ||
children.translated_text: With 'The thread of the sacrifice, its accomplisher, stretched among the gods, may we obtain that invoked one.'

children.text: prajā vai tantuḥ prajām evāsmā etat saṃtanoti ||
children.translated_text: Offspring, indeed, is the thread; by this he extends offspring for him.

children.text: mano nv ā huvāmahe nārāśaṃsena someneti ||
children.translated_text: With 'Now we call upon the mind with <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s> Soma.'

children.text: manasā vai yajñas tāyate manasā kriyate ||
children.translated_text: For sacrifice is stretched out by the mind; it is performed by the mind.

children.text: saiva tatra prāyaścittiḥ prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That, there, is the expiation, the expiation.

children.text: Chapter 83

devaviśaḥ kalpayitavyā ity āhuś chandaś chandasi pratiṣṭhāpyam iti śoṃsāvom ity āhvayate prātaḥsavane tryakṣareṇa śaṃsāmodaivom ity adhvaryuḥ pratigṛṇāti pañcākṣareṇa tad aṣṭākṣaraṃ sampadyate 'ṣṭākṣarā vai gāyatrī gāyatrīm eva tat purastāt prātaḥsavane 'cīkﾱpatām ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'The divine hosts are to be arranged; metre is to be established in metre.' At the morning pressing he calls out '<s>śoṃsāvom</s>' with three syllables; the <s>adhvaryu</s> responds '<s>śaṃsāmodaivom</s>' with five syllables. That makes eight syllables; <s>Gāyatrī</s> is eight-syllabled. Thus they fitted <s>Gāyatrī</s> in front at the morning pressing.

children.text: ukthaṃ vācīty āha śastvā caturakṣaram om ukthaśā ity adhvaryuś caturakṣaraṃ tad aṣṭākṣaraṃ sampadyate 'ṣṭākṣarā vai gāyatrī gāyatrīm eva tad ubhayataḥ prātaḥsavane 'cīkﾱpatām ||
children.translated_text: After reciting, he says, '<s>ukthaṃ vāci</s>,' four syllables; the <s>adhvaryu</s> says, '<s>om ukthaśāḥ</s>,' four syllables. That makes eight syllables; <s>Gāyatrī</s> is eight-syllabled. Thus they fitted <s>Gāyatrī</s> on both sides at the morning pressing.

children.text: adhvaryo śoṃsāvom ity āhvayate madhyaṃdine ṣaﾱakṣareṇa śaṃsāmodaivom ity adhvaryuḥ pratigṛṇāti pañcākṣareṇa tad ekādaśākṣaraṃ sampadyata ekādaśākṣarā vai triṣṭup triṣṭubham eva tat purastān madhyaṃdine 'cīkﾱpatām ukthaṃ vācīndrāyety āha śastvā saptākṣaram om ukthaśā ity adhvaryuś caturakṣaraṃ tad ekādaśākṣaraṃ sampadyata ekādaśākṣarā vai triṣṭup triṣṭubham eva tad ubhayato madhyaṃdine 'cīkﾱpatām ||
children.translated_text: At midday he calls out, 'O <s>adhvaryu</s>, <s>śoṃsāvom</s>,' with six syllables; the <s>adhvaryu</s> responds '<s>śaṃsāmodaivom</s>' with five syllables. That makes eleven syllables; <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is eleven-syllabled. Thus they fitted <s>Triṣṭubh</s> in front at midday. After reciting, he says, '<s>ukthaṃ vāci indrāya</s>,' seven syllables; the <s>adhvaryu</s> says, '<s>om ukthaśāḥ</s>,' four syllables. That makes eleven syllables; <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is eleven-syllabled. Thus they fitted <s>Triṣṭubh</s> on both sides at midday.

children.text: adhvaryo śośoṃsāvom ity āhvayate tṛtīyasavane saptākṣareṇa śaṃsāmodaivom ity adhvaryuḥ pratigṛṇāti pañcākṣareṇa tad dvādaśākṣaraṃ sampadyate dvādaśākṣarā vai jagatī jagatīm eva tat purastāt tṛtīyasavane 'cīkﾱpatām ukthaṃ vācīndrāya devebhya ity āha śastvaikādaśākṣaram om ity adhvaryur ekākṣaraṃ tad dvādaśākṣaraṃ sampadyate dvādaśākṣarā vai jagatī jagatīm eva tad ubhayatas tṛtīyasavane 'cīkﾱpatām ||
children.translated_text: At the third pressing he calls out, 'O <s>adhvaryu</s>, <s>śośoṃsāvom</s>,' with seven syllables; the <s>adhvaryu</s> responds '<s>śaṃsāmodaivom</s>' with five syllables. That makes twelve syllables; <s>Jagatī</s> is twelve-syllabled. Thus they fitted <s>Jagatī</s> in front at the third pressing. After reciting, he says, '<s>ukthaṃ vāci indrāya devebhyaḥ</s>,' eleven syllables; the <s>adhvaryu</s> says '<s>om</s>,' one syllable. That makes twelve syllables; <s>Jagatī</s> is twelve-syllabled. Thus they fitted <s>Jagatī</s> on both sides at the third pressing.

children.text: tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann abhyanūvāca ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the seer uttered this in response:

children.text: yad gāyatre adhi gāyatram āhitaṃ traiṣṭubhād vā traiṣṭubhaṃ niratakṣata yad vā jagaj jagaty āhitam padaṃ ya it tad vidus te amṛtatvam ānaśur iti ||
children.translated_text: 'What <s>Gāyatra</s> has been set upon <s>Gāyatra</s>, or what <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> they have fashioned from <s>Traiṣṭubha</s>, or what <s>Jagat</s> foot has been set in <s>Jagatī</s>: those who know that have attained immortality.'
