children.text: etad vai tac chandaś chandasi pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: This, indeed, is that by which he establishes metre in metre.

children.text: kalpayati devaviśo ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus arranges the <s>devaviś</s>, the divine hosts.

children.text: Chapter 84

prajāpatir vai yajñaṃ chandāṃsi devebhyo bhāgadheyāni vyabhajat sa gāyatrīm evāgnaye vasubhyaḥ prātaḥsavane 'bhajat triṣṭubham indrāya rudrebhyo madhyaṃdine jagatīṃ viśvebhyo devebhya ādityebhyas tṛtīyasavane ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> divided the sacrifice and the metres as shares among the gods. He allotted <s>Gāyatrī</s> to <s>Agni</s> and the <s>Vasus</s> at the morning pressing, <s>Triṣṭubh</s> to <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Rudras</s> at midday, and <s>Jagatī</s> to the <s>Viśve Devas</s> and the <s>Ādityas</s> at the third pressing.

children.text: athāsya yat svaṃ chanda āsīd anuṣṭup tām udantam abhy udauhad achāvākīyām abhi sainam abravīd anuṣṭup tvaṃ nv eva devānām pāpiṣṭho 'si yasya te 'haṃ svaṃ chando 'smi yāṃ modantam abhy udauhīr achāvākīyām abhīti tad ajānāt sa svaṃ somam āharat sa sve some 'gram mukham abhi paryāharad anuṣṭubhaṃ tasmād v anuṣṭub agriyā mukhyā yujyate sarveṣāṃ savanānām ||
children.translated_text: Then the metre that was his own, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, he carried upward toward the end, toward the <s>Acchāvāka</s>'s portion. She said to him, '<s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, surely you are now the worst of the gods, since I am your own metre and you have carried me upward toward the delighted end, toward the <s>Acchāvāka</s>'s portion.' He recognized that. He brought his own Soma; at his own Soma he carried the foremost mouth around to the front. Therefore <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is joined as foremost and chief among all the pressings.

children.text: agriyo mukhyo bhavati śreṣṭhatām aśnute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He becomes foremost and chief; he attains preeminence, who knows thus.

children.text: sve vai sa tat some 'kalpayat tasmād yatra kva ca yajamānavaśo bhavati kalpata eva yajño 'pi ||
children.translated_text: He arranged it at his own Soma. Therefore, wherever the sacrifice is under the sacrificer's control, the sacrifice itself comes into proper order.

children.text: tasyai janatāyai kalpate yatraivaṃ vidvān yajamāno vaśī yajate ||
children.translated_text: That community comes into proper order where a sacrificer who knows thus sacrifices while having control.

children.text: Chapter 85
agnir vai devānāṃ hotāsīt taṃ mṛtyur bahiṣpavamāne 'sīdat so 'nuṣṭubhājyam pratyapadyata mṛtyum eva tat paryakrāmat tam ājye 'sīdat sa praugeṇa pratyapadyata mṛtyum eva tat paryakrāmat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> was the <s>hotṛ</s> of the gods. Death settled upon him at the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s>; he resorted to the <s>Ājya</s> with <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, and by that he went around Death. Death settled upon him at the <s>Ājya</s>; he resorted to the <s>Praüga</s>, and by that he went around Death.

children.text: tam mādhyaṃdine pavamāne 'sīdat so 'nuṣṭubhā marutvatīyam pratyapadyata mṛtyum eva tat paryakrāmat taṃ mādhyaṃdine bṛhatīṣu nāśaknot sattum prāṇā vai bṛhatyaḥ prāṇān eva tan nāśaknod vyavaituṃ tasmān mādhyaṃdine hotā bṛhatīṣu stotriyeṇaiva pratipadyate prāṇā vai bṛhatyaḥ prāṇān eva tad abhi pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: He sat down in the midday <s>pavamāna</s>. With an <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> he entered upon the <s>Marutvatīya</s>; thereby he just went around Death. In the midday pressing he was not able to sit down among the <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses. The <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses are the vital breaths; thereby he was not able to separate himself from the vital breaths. Therefore, at the midday pressing the <s>hotṛ</s> begins among the <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses with the <s>stotriya</s> itself. The <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses are the vital breaths; thereby he enters upon the vital breaths themselves.

children.text: taṃ tṛtīyapavamāne 'sīdat so 'nuṣṭubhā vaiśvadevam pratyapadyata mṛtyum eva tat paryakrāmat taṃ yajñāyajñīye 'sīdat sa vaiśvānarīyeṇāgnimārutam pratyapadyata mṛtyum eva tat paryakrāmad vajro vai vaiśvānarīyam pratiṣṭhā yajñāyajñīyaṃ vajreṇaiva tat pratiṣṭhāyā mṛtyuṃ nudate sa sarvān pāśān sarvān sthāṇūn mṛtyor atimucya svasty evodamucyata svasty eva hotonmucyate sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya ||
children.translated_text: He sat down in the third <s>pavamāna</s>. With an <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> he entered upon the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>; thereby he just went around Death. He sat down in the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s>. With the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> he entered upon the <s>Agnimāruta</s>; thereby he just went around Death. The <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> is a thunderbolt, and the <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> is a foundation. With the thunderbolt, from the foundation, he drives Death away. Having been released beyond all the nooses and all the posts of Death, he came out safely. In just this way the <s>hotṛ</s> comes out safely, for the whole span of life, for attaining the whole span of life.

children.text: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He goes to the whole span of life, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 86

indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā nāstṛṣīti manyamānaḥ parāḥ parāvato 'gacchat sa paramām eva parāvatam agacchad anuṣṭub vai paramā parāvad vāg vā anuṣṭup sa vācam praviśyāśayat taṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni vibhajyānvaicchaṃs tam pūrvedyuḥ pitaro 'vindann uttaram ahar devās tasmāt pūrvedyuḥ pitṛbhyaḥ kriyata uttaram ahar devān yajante ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, after killing <s>Vṛtra</s>, thinking, 'I have not escaped,' went away to far distances. He went to the farthest distance. The <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is indeed the farthest distance, and speech is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. He entered speech and lay there. All beings searched for him, each in its own division. The Fathers found him on the previous day, and the gods on the following day. Therefore on the previous day the rite is performed for the Fathers, and on the following day they sacrifice to the gods.

children.text: te 'bruvann abhiṣuṇavāmaiva tathā vāva na āśiṣṭham āgamiṣyatīti tatheti te 'bhyaṣuṇvaṃs ta ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaya ity evainam āvartayann idaṃ vaso sutam andha ity evaibhyaḥ sutakīrtyām āvir abhavad indra nedīya ed ihīty evainam madhyam prāpādayanta ||
children.translated_text: They said, 'Let us press Soma; in that way, surely, what is most desired by us will come to us.' 'So be it,' they said, and they pressed. With 'as supports bring you to the chariot' they turned him back; with 'this, O good one, is the pressed Soma-drink' he became manifest to them in the praise of the pressed Soma; with 'O <s>Indra</s>, come nearer here' they brought him to the middle.

children.text: āgatendreṇa yajñena yajate sendreṇa yajñena rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Indra</s> has come, he sacrifices with a sacrifice that has <s>Indra</s>; he prospers with a sacrifice that has <s>Indra</s>, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 87

indraṃ vai vṛtraṃ jaghnivāṃsaṃ nāstṛteti manyamānāḥ sarvā devatā ajahus tam maruta eva svāpayo nājahuḥ prāṇā vai marutaḥ svāpayaḥ prāṇā haivainam tan nājahus tasmād eṣo 'cyutaḥ svāpimān pragāthaḥ śasyata ā svāpe svāpibhir iti ||
children.translated_text: All the deities abandoned <s>Indra</s>, who had killed <s>Vṛtra</s>, thinking, 'He has not escaped.' The <s>Maruts</s> alone, his close companions, did not abandon him. The <s>Maruts</s>, the close companions, are the vital breaths; thereby the vital breaths themselves did not abandon him. Therefore this unfailing <s>pragātha</s>, possessing close companionship, is recited: 'to the companion, with the companions.'

children.text: api ha yady aindram evāta ūrdhvaṃ chandaḥ śasyate taddha sarvam marutvatīyam bhavaty eṣa ced acyutaḥ svāpimān pragāthaḥ śasyata ā svāpe svāpibhir iti ||
children.translated_text: And even if, from this point onward, only an <s>Aindra</s> metre is recited, all that becomes <s>Marutvatīya</s>, provided that this unfailing <s>pragātha</s>, possessing close companionship, is recited: 'to the companion, with the companions.'

children.text: Chapter 88
brāhmaṇaspatyam pragāthaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Brāhmaṇaspatya</s> <s>pragātha</s>.

children.text: bṛhaspatipurohitā vai devā ajayan svargaṃ lokaṃ vy asmiṃlloke 'jayanta tathaivaitad yajamāno bṛhaspatipurohita eva jayati svargaṃ lokaṃ vy asmiṃlloke jayate ||
children.translated_text: With <s>Bṛhaspati</s> as their priest the gods conquered the heavenly world and won distinction in this world. In the same way this sacrificer, with <s>Bṛhaspati</s> as his priest, conquers the heavenly world and wins distinction in this world.

children.text: tau vā etau pragāthāv astutau santau punarādāyaṃ śasyete tad āhur yan na kiṃcanāstutaṃ sat punarādāyaṃ śasyate 'tha kasmād etau pragāthāv astutau santau punarādāyaṃ śasyete iti ||
children.translated_text: These two <s>pragāthas</s>, though they have not been chanted, are recited by being taken up again. They ask, 'Since nothing that has not been chanted is recited by being taken up again, why then are these two <s>pragāthas</s>, though they have not been chanted, recited by being taken up again?'

children.text: pavamānokthaṃ vā etad yan marutvatīyaṃ ṣaṭsu vā atra gāyatrīṣu stuvate ṣaṭsu bṛhatīṣu tisṛṣu triṣṭupsu sa vā eṣa trichandāḥ pañcadaśo mādhyaṃdinaḥ pavamānas tad āhuḥ kathaṃ ta eṣa trichandāḥ pañcadaśo mādhyaṃdinaḥ pavamāno 'nuśasto bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Marutvatīya</s> is a <s>pavamāna-uktha</s>. Here they chant on six <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, on six <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses, and on three <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses. Thus this midday <s>pavamāna</s> is three-metred and fifteenfold. They ask, 'How then does this three-metred, fifteenfold midday <s>pavamāna</s> come to have been recited for him?'

children.text: ye eva gāyatryā uttare pratipado yo gāyatro 'nucaras tābhir evāsya gāyatryo 'nuśastā bhavanty etābhyām evāsya pragāthābhyām bṛhatyo 'nuśastā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: The later opening verses in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre and the <s>Gāyatra</s> follower: by those his <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses come to have been recited. By these two <s>pragāthas</s> his <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses come to have been recited.

children.text: tāsu vā etāsu bṛhatīṣu sāmagā rauravayaudhājayābhyām punarādāyaṃ stuvate tasmād etau pragāthāvastutau santau punarādāyaṃ śasyete tac chastreṇa stotram anvaiti ||
children.translated_text: Among these <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses the <s>sāman</s>-singers chant by taking up again with the <s>Raurava</s> and the <s>Yaudhājaya</s>. Therefore these two <s>pragāthas</s>, though not chanted, are recited by being taken up again. Thus the recitation follows the chant.

children.text: ye eva triṣṭubhau dhāyye yat traiṣṭubhaṃ nividdhānam tābhir evāsya triṣṭubho 'nuśastā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: The two <s>Triṣṭubh</s> <s>dhāyyā</s> verses, and whatever <s>nivid</s>-placing is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> metre: by those his <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses come to have been recited.

children.text: evam u hāsyaiṣa trichandāḥ pañcadaśo mādhyaṃdinaḥ pavamāno 'nuśasto bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed this three-metred, fifteenfold midday <s>pavamāna</s> comes to have been recited for him, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 89
dhāyyāḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.

children.text: dhāyyābhir vai prajāpatir imāṃllokān adhayad yaṃ yaṃ kāmam akāmayata ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses <s>Prajāpati</s> milked these worlds for whatever desire he desired.

children.text: tathaivaitad yajamāno dhāyyābhir evemāṃllokān dhayati yaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate ya evaṃ veda yad eva dhāyyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way this sacrificer, with the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses, milks these worlds for whatever desire he desires, who knows thus, as to why they are <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.

children.text: yatra yatra vai devā yajñasya chidraṃ nirajānaṃs tad dhāyyābhir apidadhus tad dhāyyānāṃ dhāyyātvam ||
children.translated_text: Wherever the gods perceived a gap, an unjoined place, in the sacrifice, they covered it with the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses. That is the <s>dhāyyā</s>-nature of the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.

children.text: achidreṇa hāsya yajñeneṣṭam bhavati ya evaṃ veda yad v eva dhāyyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For him the sacrifice has been performed with no gap, who knows thus, as to why they are <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.

children.text: syūma haitad yajñasya yad dhāyyās tad yathā sūcyā vāsaḥ saṃdadhad iyād evam evaitābhir yajñasya chidraṃ saṃdadhad eti ya evaṃ veda yad v eva dhāyyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These <s>dhāyyā</s> verses are the stitching of the sacrifice. Just as one might go along joining a garment with a needle, so with these he goes along joining the gap in the sacrifice, who knows thus, as to why they are <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.

children.text: tāny u vā etāny upasadām evokthāni yad dhāyyā agnir netety āgneyī prathamopasat tasyā etad ukthaṃ tvaṃ soma kratubhir iti saumyā dvitīyopasat tasyā etad ukthaṃ pinvanty apa iti vaiṣṇavī tṛtīyopasat tasyā etad uktham ||
children.translated_text: These, indeed, are precisely the <s>uktha</s> (recitations) of the <s>upasads</s>, namely the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses. 'Agnir neti' is the <s>Āgneyī</s>, the first <s>upasad</s>; its <s>uktha</s> is this: 'tvaṃ soma kratubhir iti.' The <s>Saumyā</s> is the second <s>upasad</s>; its <s>uktha</s> is this: 'pinvanty apa iti.' The <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> is the third <s>upasad</s>; its <s>uktha</s> is this.

children.text: yāvantaṃ ha vai saumyenādhvareṇeṣṭvā lokaṃ jayati tam ata ekaikayopasadā jayati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān dhāyyāḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: As much of a world as one wins after sacrificing with the Soma rite, that world he wins from here by each single <s>upasad</s>, who knows thus and who, knowing thus, recites the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.

children.text: taddhaika āhus tān vo maha iti śaṃsed etāṃ vāva vayam bharateṣu śasyamānām abhivyajānīma iti vadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On this point some say, 'He should recite "tān vo maha iti"; for we recognize this very verse as being recited among the <s>Bharatas</s>,' so they say.

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyam ||
children.translated_text: That is not to be heeded.

children.text: yad etāṃ śaṃsed īśvaraḥ parjanyo 'varṣṭoḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he were to recite that verse, <s>Parjanya</s> might fail to rain.

children.text: pinvanty apa ity eva śaṃset ||
children.translated_text: He should recite only 'pinvanty apa iti.'

children.text: vṛṣṭivani padaṃ maruta iti mārutam atyaṃ na mihe vi nayantīti vinītavad yad vinītavat tad vikrāntavad yad vikrāntavat tad vaiṣṇavaṃ vājinam itīndro vai vājī tasyāṃ vā etasyāṃ catvāri padāni vṛṣṭivani mārutaṃ vaiṣṇavam aindram ||
children.translated_text: 'Vṛṣṭivani' is a word; 'marutaḥ' makes it <s>Māruta</s>. 'Atyaṃ na mihe vi nayanti' has the sense of leading apart; what has leading apart has striding forth; what has striding forth is <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>. 'Vājinam' is <s>Aindra</s>, for <s>Indra</s> is indeed the vājī. In that verse there are four elements: rain-winning, <s>Māruta</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, and <s>Aindra</s>.

children.text: sā vā eṣā tṛtīyasavanabhājanā satī madhyaṃdine śasyate tasmāddhedaṃ bharatānām paśavaḥ sāyaṃgoṣṭhāḥ santo madhyaṃdine saṃgavinīm āyanti so jagatī jāgatā hi paśava ātmā yajamānasya madhyaṃdinas tad yajamāne paśūn dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Although this verse belongs to the vessel of the third pressing, it is recited at midday. Therefore the cattle of the <s>Bharatas</s>, though they have their stalls in the evening, come to the midday cattle-gathering. It is a <s>jagatī</s>, for cattle belong to the <s>jagatī</s>; midday is the self of the sacrificer. Thereby he places cattle in the sacrificer.

children.text: Chapter 90
marutvatīyam pragāthaṃ śaṃsati paśavo vai marutaḥ paśavaḥ pragāthaḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>pragātha</s>. The <s>Maruts</s> are cattle, and the <s>pragātha</s> is cattle; this is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāyeti sūktam śaṃsati tad vā etad yajamānajananam eva sūktaṃ yajamānaṃ ha vā etena yajñād devayonyai prajanayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>sūkta</s> beginning 'janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāya.' That <s>sūkta</s> is indeed a begetting of the sacrificer: by means of it he brings the sacrificer forth from the sacrifice for a divine birth.

children.text: tat saṃjayam bhavati saṃ ca jayati vi ca jayate ||
children.translated_text: It becomes a complete conquest: he conquers together, and he is victorious separately.

children.text: etad gaurivītaṃ gaurivītir ha vai śāktyo nediṣṭhaṃ svargasya lokasyāgacchat sa etat sūktam apaśyat tena svargaṃ lokam ajayat tathaivaitad yajamāna etena sūktena svargaṃ lokaṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Gaurivīta</s>. <s>Gaurivīti Śāktya</s> came nearest to the heavenly world; he saw this <s>sūkta</s>, and with it he won the heavenly world. In just the same way, by means of this <s>sūkta</s>, the sacrificer wins the heavenly world.

children.text: tasyārdhāḥ śastvārdhāḥ pariśiṣya madhye nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: After reciting half of it and leaving half remaining, he places the <s>nivid</s> in the middle.

children.text: svargasya haiṣa lokasya roho yan nivit ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nivid</s> is the ascent to the heavenly world.

children.text: svargasya haital lokasyākramaṇaṃ yan nivit tām ākramamāṇa iva śaṃsed upaiva yajamānaṃ nigṛhṇīta yo 'sya priyaḥ syād iti nu svargakāmasya ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nivid</s> is the step onto the heavenly world. He should recite it as if stepping upon it; he should thereby hold the sacrificer close, if the sacrificer is dear to him. This, then, is for one who desires heaven.

children.text: athābhicarato yaḥ kāmayeta kṣatreṇa viśaṃ hanyām iti tris tarhi nividā sūktaṃ viśaṃset kṣatraṃ vai nivid viṭ sūktaṃ kṣatreṇaiva tad viśaṃ hanti ||
children.translated_text: But in the case of one practicing hostile rites, if he should desire, 'May I strike the people with royal power,' then he should break up the <s>sūkta</s> three times with the <s>nivid</s>. Royal power is the <s>nivid</s>, and the people are the <s>sūkta</s>; thus he strikes the people with royal power itself.

children.text: yaḥ kāmayeta viśā kṣatraṃ hanyām iti tris tarhi sūktena nividaṃ viśaṃset kṣatraṃ vai nivid viṭ sūktaṃ viśaiva tat kṣatraṃ hanti ||
children.translated_text: If he should desire, 'May I strike royal power with the people,' then he should break up the <s>nivid</s> three times with the <s>sūkta</s>. Royal power is the <s>nivid</s>, and the people are the <s>sūkta</s>; thus he strikes royal power with the people themselves.

children.text: ya u kāmayetobhayata enaṃ viśaḥ paryavacchinadānīty ubhayatas tarhi nividaṃ vyāhvayītobhayata evainaṃ tad viśaḥ paryavacchinatti ||
children.translated_text: And if he should desire, 'May the people cut him off on both sides,' then he should call out the <s>nivid</s> on both sides; thereby the people cut him off on both sides.

children.text: iti nv abhicarata itarathā tv eva svargakāmasya ||
children.translated_text: So much for one practicing hostile rites; otherwise it is for one who desires heaven.

children.text: vayaḥ suparṇā upa sedur indram ity uttamayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He encloses it with the final verse, 'vayaḥ suparṇā upa sedur indram iti.'

children.text: priyamedhā ṛṣayo nādhamānāḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Priyamedha</s> seers, seeking help.'

children.text: apa dhvāntam ūrṇuhīti yena tamasā prāvṛto manyeta tan manasā gacched apa haivāsmāt tal lupyate ||
children.translated_text: 'Apa dhvāntam ūrṇuhi': whatever darkness he thinks he is covered by, he should go to that with his mind; it is thereby stripped away from him.

children.text: pūrdhi cakṣur iti cakṣuṣī marīmṛjyeta ||
children.translated_text: At 'pūrdhi cakṣur,' he should wipe his two eyes.

children.text: ājarasaṃ ha cakṣuṣmān bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of sight until old age, who knows thus.

children.text: mumugdhy asmān nidhayeva baddhān iti pāśā vai nidhā mumugdhy asmān pāśād iva baddhān ity eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: 'Mumugdhy asmān nidhayeva baddhān': the <s>nidhā</s> are nooses. 'Release us as if bound from a noose' is just what he thereby says.

children.text: Chapter 91

indro vai vṛtraṃ haniṣyan sarvā devatā abravīd anu mopatiṣṭhadhvam upa mā hvayadhvam iti tatheti taṃ haniṣyanta ādravan so 'ven māṃ vai haniṣyanta ādravanti hantemān bhīṣayā iti tān abhi prāśvasīt tasya śvasathād īṣamāṇā viśve devā adravan maruto hainaṃ nājahuḥ prahara bhagavo jahi vīrayasvety evainam etāṃ vācaṃ vadanta upātiṣṭhanta tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann abhyanūvāca vṛtrasya tvā śvasathād īṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahur ye sakhāyaḥ marudbhir indra sakhyaṃ te astv athemā viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāsīti so 'ved ime vai kila me sacivā ime mākāmayanta hantemān asminn uktha ābhajā iti tān etasminn uktha ābhajad atha haite tarhy ubhe eva niṣkevalye ukthe āsatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, intending to slay <s>Vṛtra</s>, said to all the deities, 'Stand beside me; call upon me.' 'So be it,' they said. As he was about to slay him, they ran toward him. He realized, 'They are running at me in order to slay me. Come, I shall frighten them.' He breathed upon them. From his breath all the gods ran away in terror; the <s>Maruts</s> did not abandon him. Saying to him, 'Strike, blessed one; slay; show your manhood,' they stood beside him with this speech. Seeing this, the seer repeated after it: 'From <s>Vṛtra</s>'s breath, trembling, all the gods who were your companions abandoned you. Let there be friendship for you with the <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Indra</s>; then may you conquer all these battles.' He realized, 'These indeed are my helpers; these desired me. Come, I shall give them a share in this <s>uktha</s>.' He gave them a share in this <s>uktha</s>. At that time, then, these two <s>niṣkevalya</s> <s>ukthas</s> existed.

children.text: marutvatīyaṃ grahaṃ gṛhṇāti marutvatīyam pragāthaṃ śaṃsati marutvatīyaṃ sūktaṃ śaṃsati marutvatīyām nividaṃ dadhāti marutāṃ sā bhaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He takes the <s>Marutvatīya</s> cup, recites the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>pragātha</s>, recites the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>sūkta</s>, and places the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>nivid</s>; that is the share of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: marutvatīyam ukthaṃ śastvā marutvatīyayā yajati yathābhāgaṃ tad devatāḥ prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: Having recited the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>uktha</s>, he sacrifices with the <s>Marutvatīya</s> verse. Thereby he pleases the deities according to their shares.

children.text: ye tvāhihatye maghavann avardhan ye śāmbare harivo ye gaviṣṭau ye tvā nūnam anumadanti viprāḥ pibendra somaṃ sagaṇo marudbhir iti ||
children.translated_text: Those who strengthened you, O <s>Maghavan</s>, in the slaying of <s>Ahi</s>, those at <s>Śambara</s>, O <s>Harivat</s>, those in the quest for cows, the inspired priests who now approve you: drink the <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, together with the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: yatra yatraivaibhir vyajayata yatra yatra vīryam akarot tad evaitat samanuvedyendreṇainān sasomapīthān karoti ||
children.translated_text: Wherever with these he conquered, wherever he performed a heroic deed, just that is here recounted in order; having connected them with <s>Indra</s>, he makes them sharers in the drinking of <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: Chapter 92

indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā sarvā vijitīr vijityābravīt prajāpatim aham etad asāni yat tvam aham mahān asānīti sa prajāpatir abravīd atha ko 'ham iti yad evaitad avoca ity abravīt tato vai ko nāma prajāpatir abhavat ko vai nāma prajāpatir yan mahān indro 'bhavat tan mahendrasya mahendratvam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, having slain <s>Vṛtra</s> and won all victories, said to <s>Prajāpati</s>, 'I will be this which you are; I will be great.' <s>Prajāpati</s> said, 'Then who am I?' He replied, 'Just what you have said.' From that, <s>Prajāpati</s> became named <s>Ka</s>; for <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed named <s>Ka</s>. Because <s>Indra</s> became great, that is the great-Indrahood of <s>Mahendra</s>.

children.text: sa mahān bhūtvā devatā abravīd uddhāram ma uddharateti yathāpy etarhīcchati yo vai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭhatām aśnute sa mahān bhavati taṃ devā abruvan svayam eva brūṣva yat te bhaviṣyatīti sa etam māhendraṃ graham abrūta mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanānāṃ niṣkevalyam ukthānāṃ triṣṭubhaṃ chandasām pṛṣṭhaṃ sāmnāṃ tam asmā uddhāram udaharan ||
children.translated_text: Having become great, he said to the deities, 'Lift out an exceptional portion for me.' As even now, whoever becomes somebody, whoever reaches preeminence, becomes great. The gods said to him, 'Tell us yourself what is to be yours.' He declared this <s>Māhendra</s> graha: the midday pressing among the pressings, the exclusive <s>uktha</s> among the <s>ukthas</s>, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> among the metres, and the <s>pṛṣṭha</s> among the <s>sāmans</s>. That they lifted out for him as his exceptional portion.

children.text: ud asmā uddhāraṃ haranti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: They lift up an exceptional portion for the one who knows thus.

children.text: taṃ devā abruvan sarvaṃ vā avocathā api no 'trāstv iti sa nety abravīt kathaṃ vo 'pisyād iti tam abruvann apy eva no 'stu maghavann iti tān īkṣataiva ||
children.translated_text: The gods said to him, 'You have named everything; let there be a share for us here too.' He said, 'No.' 'How could there be a share for you?' They said to him, 'Let there indeed be one for us too, O <s>Maghavan</s>.' He merely looked at them.

children.text: Chapter 93

te devā abruvann iyaṃ vā indrasya priyā jāyā vāvātā prāsahā nāmāsyām evecchāmahā iti tatheti tasyām aicchanta sainān abravīt prātar vaḥ prativaktāsmīti tasmāt striyaḥ patyāvicchante tasmād u stryanurātram patyāvicchate tām prātar upāyan saitad eva pratyapadyata ||
children.translated_text: The gods said, 'This dear wife of <s>Indra</s>, his favorite, is named <s>Prāsahā</s>; in her we wish to have our share.' 'So be it.' In her they sought it. She said to them, 'In the morning I will answer you.' Therefore women are not desired by the husband; therefore, moreover, the woman desires the husband at night. In the morning they approached her. She came to this very answer:

children.text: yad vāvāna purutamam purāṣāﾱ ā vṛtrahendro nāmāny aprāḥ aceti prāsahas patis tuviṣmān iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Since he has desired the very most, the ancient one, <s>Indra</s>, slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, has filled the names; <s>Prāsahā</s>'s lord is mighty,' so it says.

children.text: indro vai prāsahas patis tuviṣmān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> is indeed <s>Prāsahā</s>'s lord, the mighty one.

children.text: yadīm uśmasi kartave karat tad iti yad evaitad avocāmākarat tad ity evaināṃs tad abravīt ||
children.translated_text: 'If we wish it to be done, may he do it,' so it says. 'Just what we have spoken, he has done,' she thereby said to them.

children.text: te devā abruvann apy asyā ihāstu yā no 'smin na vai kam avidad iti tatheti tasyā apy atrākurvan ||
children.translated_text: The gods said, 'Let her too have a share here, since she found no favor for us in this matter.' 'So be it.' They made a share for her there too.

children.text: tasmād eṣātrāpi śasyate yad vāvāna purutamam purāṣāﾱ iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this verse too is recited there: 'Since he has desired the very most, the ancient one,' and so on.

children.text: senā vā indrasya priyā jāyā vāvātā prāsahā nāma ko nāma prajāpatiḥ śvaśuras tad yāsya kāme senā jayet tasyā ardhāt tiṣṭhaṃs tṛṇam ubhayataḥ paricchidyetarāṃ senām abhy asyet prāsahe kas tvā paśyatīti tad yathaivādaḥ snuṣā śvaśurāllajjamānā nilīyamānaity evam eva sā senā bhajyamānā nilīyamānaiti yatraivaṃ vidvāṃs tṛṇam ubhayataḥ paricchidyetarāṃ senāṃ abhy asyati prāsahe kas tvā paśyatīti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Senā</s>, the dear wife of <s>Indra</s>, his favorite, is named <s>Prāsahā</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s>, named <s>Ka</s>, is her father-in-law. Therefore, when he wishes that an army should conquer, he should stand at half of it, cut off a blade of grass at both ends, and throw it against the other army, saying, 'O <s>Prāsahā</s>, who sees you?' Just as a daughter-in-law, ashamed before her father-in-law, goes hiding herself, so that army, being broken, goes hiding itself when one who knows thus cuts off a blade of grass at both ends and throws it against the other army, saying, 'O <s>Prāsahā</s>, who sees you?'

children.text: tān indra uvācāpi vo 'trāstv iti te devā abruvan virāḍ yājyāstu niṣkevalyasya yā trayastriṃśadakṣarā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> said to them, 'Let there be a share for you here too.' The gods said, 'Let the <s>Virāj</s> be the offering verse of the exclusive rite, the one that has thirty-three syllables.'

children.text: trayastriṃśad vai devā aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāḥ prajāpatiś ca vaṣaṭkāraś ca devatā akṣarabhājaḥ karoty akṣaram akṣaram eva tad devatā anuprapibanti devapātreṇaiva tad devatās tṛpyanti ||
children.translated_text: There are indeed thirty-three gods: eight <s>Vasus</s>, eleven <s>Rudras</s>, twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, and <s>Prajāpati</s> and the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>. He makes the deities share in the syllables. Then the deities drink after every syllable; with the vessel of the gods he thereby satisfies the deities.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayetānāyatanavān syād ity avirājāsya yajed gāyatryā vā triṣṭubhā vānyena vā chandasā vaṣaṭkuryād anāyatanavantam evainaṃ tat karoti ||
children.translated_text: Of the man of whom he should wish, 'May he be without a support,' he should sacrifice for him without a <s>Virāj</s>, or should utter the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> with a <s>Gāyatrī</s>, a <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, or some other metre. Thereby he makes him without a support.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayetāyatanavān syād iti virājāsya yajet pibā somam indra mandatu tvety etayāyatanavantam evainaṃ tat karoti ||
children.translated_text: Of the man of whom he should wish, 'May he have a support,' he should sacrifice for him with a <s>Virāj</s>, with this verse, 'Drink the <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>; let it gladden you.' Thereby he makes him have a support.

children.text: Chapter 94

ṛk ca vā idam agre sāma cāstāṃ saiva nāma ṛg āsīd amo nāma sāma sā vā ṛk sāmopāvadan mithunaṃ saṃbhavāva prajātyā iti nety abravīt sāma jyāyān vā ato mama mahimeti te dve bhūtvopāvadatāṃ te na prati cana samavadata tās tisro bhūtvopāvadaṃs tat tisṛbhiḥ samabhavad yat tisṛbhiḥ samabhavat tasmāt tisṛbhiḥ stuvanti tisṛbhir udgāyanti tisṛbhir hi sāma saṃmitaṃ tasmād ekasya bahvyo jāyā bhavanti naikasyai bahavaḥ saha patayo yad vai tat sā cāmaś ca samabhavatāṃ tat sāmābhavat tat sāmnaḥ sāmatvam ||
children.translated_text: In the beginning there were this <s>ṛc</s> and <s>sāman</s>. The <s>ṛc</s> was named <s>Sā</s>, and the <s>sāman</s> was named <s>Ama</s>. The <s>ṛc</s> approached the <s>sāman</s>, saying, 'Let us two unite as a pair for procreation.' It said, 'No; I am greater than you in greatness.' They became two each and approached; they still did not come together. They became three each and approached; with three they came together. Because it came together with three, therefore they praise with three, they sing with three, for the <s>sāman</s> is measured by three. Therefore many wives belong to one man, but many husbands do not belong to one woman at the same time. What came together as that <s>Sā</s> and <s>Ama</s>, that became <s>sāman</s>; that is the sāmanhood of the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: sāman bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of <s>sāman</s> who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭhatām aśnute sa sāman bhavaty asāmanya iti hi nindanti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever becomes somebody, whoever reaches preeminence, becomes <s>sāman</s>; for people censure a man by saying, 'He is without <s>sāman</s>.'

children.text: te vai pañcānyad bhūtvā pañcānyad bhūtvākalpetām āhāvāś ca hiṃkāraś ca prastāvaś ca prathamā ca ṛg udgīthaś ca madhyamā ca pratihāraś cottamā ca nidhanaṃ ca vaṣaṭkāraś ca ||
children.translated_text: They, becoming five in one way and five in another way, arranged themselves: the <s>āhāva</s> and the <s>hiṃkāra</s>, the <s>prastāva</s> and the first <s>ṛc</s>, the <s>udgītha</s> and the middle one, the <s>pratihāra</s> and the last one, the <s>nidhana</s> and the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>.

children.text: te yat pañcānyad bhūtvā pañcānyad bhūtvākalpetāṃ tasmād āhuḥ pāṅkto yajñaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśava iti ||
children.translated_text: Because those two, becoming five on one side and five on the other, were fitted together, therefore they say, "The sacrifice is fivefold; the animals are fivefold."

children.text: yad u virājaṃ daśinīm abhisamapadyetāṃ tasmād āhur virāji yajño daśinyām pratiṣṭhita iti ||
children.translated_text: And because those two together came up to the <s>Virāj</s> as a tenfold one, therefore they say, "The sacrifice is established in the tenfold <s>Virāj</s>."

children.text: ātmā vai stotriyaḥ prajānurūpaḥ patnī dhāyyā paśavaḥ pragātho gṛhāḥ sūktam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>stotriya</s> is the self, the <s>anurūpa</s> is offspring, the <s>dhāyyā</s> is the wife, the <s>pragātha</s> is cattle, and the <s>sūkta</s> is the household.

children.text: sa vā asmiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca prajayā ca paśubhiś ca gṛheṣu vasati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He lives in this world and in yonder world, with offspring and cattle in his households, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 95
stotriyaṃ śaṃsaty ātmā vai stotriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>stotriya</s>; the <s>stotriya</s> is the self.

children.text: tam madhyamayā vācā śaṃsaty ātmānam eva tat saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: He recites it with a middle voice; thereby he refines the self itself.

children.text: anurūpaṃ śaṃsati prajā vā anurūpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>anurūpa</s>; offspring, indeed, are the <s>anurūpa</s>.

children.text: sa uccaistarām ivānurūpaḥ śaṃstavyaḥ prajām eva tacchreyasīm ātmanaḥ kurute ||
children.translated_text: That <s>anurūpa</s> should be recited rather more loudly; thereby he makes offspring superior to himself.

children.text: dhāyyāṃ śaṃsati patnī vai dhāyyā ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>dhāyyā</s>; the <s>dhāyyā</s> is the wife.

children.text: sā nīcaistarām iva dhāyyā śaṃstavyā ||
children.translated_text: That <s>dhāyyā</s> should be recited rather more softly.

children.text: prativādinī hāsya gṛheṣu patnī bhavati yatraivaṃ vidvān nīcaistarāṃ dhāyyāṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: A responsive wife comes to be in the house of the man who, knowing thus, recites the <s>dhāyyā</s> more softly.

children.text: pragāthaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>pragātha</s>.

children.text: sa svaravatyā vācā śaṃstavyaḥ paśavo vai svaraḥ paśavaḥ pragāthaḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: It should be recited with a voice possessing tone; tone is cattle, and the <s>pragātha</s> is cattle, for the securing of cattle.

children.text: indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam iti sūktaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>sūkta</s>, "Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>."

children.text: tad vā etat priyam indrasya sūktaṃ niṣkevalyaṃ hairaṇyastūpam etena vai sūktena hiraṇyastūpa āṅgirasa indrasya priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchat sa paramaṃ lokam ajayat ||
children.translated_text: This, indeed, is that <s>sūkta</s> dear to <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Niṣkevalya</s>, the <s>Hairaṇyastūpa</s>. By this very <s>sūkta</s>, <s>Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa</s> approached <s>Indra</s>'s dear abode; he won the highest world.

children.text: upendrasya priyaṃ dhāma gacchati jayati paramaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He approaches <s>Indra</s>'s dear abode and wins the highest world who knows thus.

children.text: gṛhā vai pratiṣṭhā sūktaṃ tat pratiṣṭhitatamayā vācā śaṃstavyaṃ tasmād yady api dūra iva paśūṃllabhate gṛhān evainān ājigamiṣati gṛhā hi paśūnām pratiṣṭhā pratiṣṭhā ||
children.translated_text: Households are the foundation; the <s>sūkta</s> is the household. Therefore it should be recited with the most firmly established voice. Therefore, even if he obtains cattle as though far away, he will desire to bring them home; for households are the foundation, the foundation of cattle.

children.text: Chapter 96

somo vai rājāmuṣmiṃlloka āsīt taṃ devāś carṣayaś cābhyadhyāyan katham ayam asmān somo rājāgacched iti te 'bruvaṃś chandāṃsi yūyaṃ na imaṃ somaṃ rājānam āharateti tatheti te suparṇā bhūtvodapataṃs te yat suparṇā bhūtvodapataṃs tad etat sauparṇam ity ākhyānavida ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Soma</s> was in yonder world. The gods and the seers longed for him, thinking, "How might this king <s>Soma</s> come to us?" They said, "O meters, bring us this king <s>Soma</s>." "So be it," they said. Becoming well-winged birds, they flew up. Because they flew up after becoming well-winged birds, those who know the tale call this the <s>Sauparṇa</s>.

children.text: chandāṃsi vai tat somaṃ rājānam acchācaraṃs tāni ha tarhi caturakṣarāṇi caturakṣarāṇy eva chandāṃsy āsan sā jagatī caturakṣarā prathamodapatat sā patitvārdham adhvano gatvāśrāmyat sā parāsya trīṇy akṣarāṇy ekākṣarā bhūtvā dīkṣāṃ ca tapaś ca harantī punar abhyavāpatat tasmāt tasya vittā dīkṣā vittaṃ tapo yasya paśavaḥ santi jāgatā hi paśavo jagatī hi tān āharat ||
children.translated_text: The meters went toward that king <s>Soma</s>. At that time the meters were only four syllables each. <s>Jagatī</s>, four-syllabled, flew up first. After flying and going half the road, she grew weary. Casting off three syllables, she became one-syllabled and fell back again, bringing consecration and austerity. Therefore consecration is acquired and austerity is acquired for one who has cattle; for cattle belong to <s>Jagatī</s>, and <s>Jagatī</s> brought them.

children.text: atha triṣṭub udapatat sā patitvā bhūyo 'rdhād adhvano gatvāśrāmyat sā parāsyaikam akṣaraṃ tryakṣarā bhūtvā dakṣiṇā harantī punar abhyavāpatat tasmān madhyaṃdine dakṣiṇā nīyante triṣṭubho loke triṣṭubbhi tā āharat ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Triṣṭubh</s> flew up. After flying and going more than half the road, she grew weary. Casting off one syllable, she became three-syllabled and fell back again, bringing the sacrificial gift. Therefore gifts are led forth at midday, in the world of <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; <s>Triṣṭubh</s> brought them.

children.text: Chapter 97

te devā abruvan gāyatrīṃ tvaṃ na imaṃ somaṃ rājānam āhareti sā tathety abravīt tāṃ vai mā sarveṇa svastyayanenānumantrayadhvam iti tatheti sodapatat tāṃ devāḥ sarveṇa svastyayanenānvamantrayanta preti ceti cety etad vai sarvaṃ svastyayanaṃ yat preti ceti ceti tad yo 'sya priyaḥ syāt tam etenānumantrayeta preti ceti ceti svasty eva gacchati svasti punar āgacchati ||
children.translated_text: The gods said to <s>Gāyatrī</s>, "Bring us this king <s>Soma</s>." "So be it," she said. "But address me with every benediction for safe going." "So be it," they said. She flew up, and the gods addressed her with every benediction for safe going: "Go forth, and come back, and come back." This, indeed, is every benediction for safe going, namely, "Go forth, and come back, and come back." Whoever is dear to him, he should address that one with this: "Go forth, and come back, and come back." He goes safely and returns safely.

children.text: sā patitvā somapālān bhīṣayitvā padbhyāṃ ca mukhena ca somaṃ rājānaṃ samagṛbhṇād yāni cetare chandasī akṣarāṇy ajahitāṃ tāni copasamagṛbhṇāt ||
children.translated_text: After flying there, she frightened the guardians of <s>Soma</s> and seized king <s>Soma</s> with her feet and her mouth; and she also gathered up the syllables that the other two meters had abandoned.

children.text: tasyā anuvisṛjya kṛśānuḥ somapālaḥ savyasya pado nakham achidat tacchalyako 'bhavat tasmāt sa nakham iva yad vaśam asravat sā vaśābhavat tasmāt sā havir ivātha yaḥ śalyo yad anīkam āsīt sa sarpo nirdaṃśy abhavat sahasaḥ svajo yāni parṇāni te manthāvalā yāni snāvāni te gaṇḍūpadā yat tejanaṃ so 'ndhāhiḥ so sā tatheṣur abhavat ||
children.translated_text: As she was being released, <s>Kṛśānu</s>, the guardian of <s>Soma</s>, cut off the nail of her left foot. That became the porcupine; therefore it is like a nail. The fluid that flowed became the barren cow; therefore she is like an oblation. And what was the barb, what was the point, became the biting serpent, born of force. The feathers became <s>manthāvalā</s>s; the sinews became earthworms; the shaft became the blind snake. Thus that became the arrow.

children.text: Chapter 98

sā yad dakṣiṇena padā samagṛbhṇāt tat prātaḥsavanam abhavat tad gāyatrī svam āyatanam akuruta tasmāt tat samṛddhatamaṃ manyante sarveṣāṃ savanānām agriyo mukhyo bhavati śreṣṭhatām aśnute ya evaṃ vedātha yat savyena padā samagṛbhṇāt tan mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam abhavat tad visraṃsata tad visrastaṃ nānvāpnot pūrvaṃ savanaṃ te devāḥ prājijñāsanta tasmiṃs triṣṭubhaṃ chandasām adadhur indraṃ devatānāṃ tena tat samāvadvīryam abhavat pūrveṇa savanenobhābhyāṃ savanābhyāṃ samāvadvīryābhyāṃ samāvajjāmībhyāṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ vedātha yan mukhena samagṛbhṇāt tat tṛtīyasavanam abhavat ||
children.translated_text: When she grasped it with her right foot, that became the morning pressing. <s>Gāyatrī</s> made that her own seat. Therefore they regard that as the most successful of all the pressings. He becomes foremost and chief; he attains preeminence, who knows thus. Then when she grasped it with her left foot, that became the midday pressing. It slipped loose. Having slipped loose, it did not equal the earlier pressing. The gods investigated it. Among the metres they placed <s>Triṣṭubh</s> in it, and among the deities <s>Indra</s>; by that it became equal in power to the earlier pressing. With the earlier pressing, with both pressings equal in power and equal in kinship, he prospers who knows thus. Then when she grasped it with her mouth, that became the third pressing.

children.text: tasya patantī rasam adhayat taddhītarasaṃ nānvāpnot pūrve savane te devāḥ prājijñāsanta tat paśuṣv apaśyaṃs tad yad āśiram avanayanty ājyena paśunā caranti tena tat samāvadvīryam abhavat pūrvābhyāṃ savanābhyām ||
children.translated_text: As it was falling, she drew off its sap. Having lost its sap, it did not equal the earlier pressings. The gods investigated it. They saw that sap among the cattle. Therefore, when they pour in the <s>āśira</s> (milk-mixture) and proceed with ghee as the animal offering, by that it became equal in power to the two earlier pressings.

children.text: sarvaiḥ savanaiḥ samāvadvīryaiḥ samāvajjāmibhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: With all the pressings equal in power and equal in kinship, he prospers who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 99

te vā ime itare chandasī gāyatrīm abhyavadetāṃ vittaṃ nāv akṣarāṇy anuparyāgur iti nety abravīd gāyatrī yathāvittam eva na iti te deveṣu praśnam aitāṃ te devā abruvan yathāvittam eva va iti tasmāddhāpy etarhi vittyāṃ vyāhur yathāvittam eva na iti tato vā aṣṭākṣarā gāyatry abhavat tryakṣarā triṣṭub ekākṣarā jagatī ||
children.translated_text: Now these two other metres addressed <s>Gāyatrī</s>: 'The syllables have gone around for us according to what was found.' 'No,' said <s>Gāyatrī</s>, 'they are just according to what was found for us.' They went to the gods with this question. The gods said, 'They are just according to what was found for you.' Therefore even now, in a distribution, people say, 'It is just according to what was found for us.' From that, <s>Gāyatrī</s> became eight-syllabled, <s>Triṣṭubh</s> three-syllabled, and <s>Jagatī</s> one-syllabled.

children.text: sāṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī prātaḥsavanam udayacchan nāśaknot triṣṭup tryakṣarā mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam udyantuṃ tāṃ gāyatry abravīd āyāny api me 'trāstv iti sā tathety abravīt triṣṭup tāṃ vai maitair aṣṭābhir akṣarair upasaṃdhehīti tatheti tām upasamadadhād etad vai tad gāyatryai madhyaṃdine yan marutvatīyasyottare pratipado yaś cānucaraḥ saikādaśākṣarā bhūtvā mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam udayacchat ||
children.translated_text: That eight-syllabled <s>Gāyatrī</s> raised the morning pressing. <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, three-syllabled, was not able to raise the midday pressing. <s>Gāyatrī</s> said to her, 'Let me come; let there be a share for me here too.' <s>Triṣṭubh</s> said, 'So be it.' 'Join me with these eight syllables,' she said. 'So be it,' she replied, and joined her to herself. That indeed is <s>Gāyatrī</s>'s share at midday: the later opening verses of the <s>Marutvatīya</s> and the following verse. Having become eleven-syllabled, she raised the midday pressing.

children.text: nāśaknoj jagaty ekākṣarā tṛtīyasavanam udyantuṃ tāṃ gāyatry abravīd āyāny api me 'trāstv iti sā tathety abravīj jagatī tāṃ vai maitair ekādaśabhir akṣarair upasaṃdhehīti tatheti tām upasamadadhād etad vai tad gāyatryai tṛtīyasavane yad vaiśvadevasyottare pratipado yaś cānucaraḥ sā dvādaśākṣarā bhūtvā tṛtīyasavanam udayacchat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jagatī</s>, one-syllabled, was not able to raise the third pressing. <s>Gāyatrī</s> said to her, 'Let me come; let there be a share for me here too.' <s>Jagatī</s> said, 'So be it.' 'Join me with these eleven syllables,' she said. 'So be it,' she replied, and joined her to herself. That indeed is <s>Gāyatrī</s>'s share in the third pressing: the later opening verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> and the following verse. Having become twelve-syllabled, she raised the third pressing.

children.text: tato vā aṣṭākṣarā gāyatry abhavad ekādaśākṣarā triṣṭub dvādaśākṣarā jagatī ||
children.translated_text: From that, <s>Gāyatrī</s> became eight-syllabled, <s>Triṣṭubh</s> eleven-syllabled, and <s>Jagatī</s> twelve-syllabled.

children.text: sarvaiś chandobhiḥ samāvadvīryaiḥ samāvajjāmibhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: With all the metres equal in power and equal in kinship, he prospers who knows thus.

children.text: ekaṃ vai sat tat tredhābhavat tasmād āhur dātavyam evaṃ viduṣa ity ekaṃ hi sat tat tredhābhavat ||
children.translated_text: Being one, it became threefold. Therefore they say, 'A gift should be given to one who knows thus,' for being one, it became threefold.

children.text: Chapter 100
te devā abruvann ādityān yuṣmābhir idaṃ savanam udyacchāmeti tatheti tasmād ādityārambhaṇaṃ tṛtīyasavanam ādityagrahaḥ purastāt tasya ||
children.translated_text: The gods said to the <s>Ādityas</s>, 'With you let us raise this pressing.' 'So be it,' they replied. Therefore the third pressing has the <s>Ādityas</s> as its support, and the <s>Āditya</s> cup is before it.

children.text: yajaty ādityāso aditir mādayantām iti madvatyā rūpasamṛddhayā madvad vai tṛtīyasavanasya rūpam ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices with the verse, 'May the <s>Ādityas</s>, may <s>Aditi</s>, be gladdened,' with a verse containing gladness and complete in form; for gladness is the form of the third pressing.

children.text: nānuvaṣaṭkaroti na bhakṣayati saṃsthā vā eṣā yad anuvaṣaṭkāraḥ saṃsthā bhakṣaḥ prāṇā ādityā net prāṇān saṃsthāpayānīti ||
children.translated_text: He does not make the after-<s>vaṣaṭ</s>, and he does not consume the portion. The after-<s>vaṣaṭ</s> is a conclusion, and consumption is a conclusion. The <s>Ādityas</s> are the vital breaths; lest he bring the vital breaths to a conclusion.

children.text: ta ādityā abruvan savitāraṃ tvayedaṃ saha savanam udyacchāmeti tatheti tasmāt sāvitrī pratipad bhavati vaiśvadevasya sāvitragrahaḥ purastāt tasya yajati damūnā devaḥ savitā vareṇya iti madvatyā rūpasamṛddhayā madvad vai tṛtīyasavanasya rūpaṃ nānuvaṣaṭkaroti na bhakṣayati saṃsthā vā eṣā yad anuvaṣaṭkāraḥ saṃsthā bhakṣaḥ prāṇaḥ savitā net prāṇaṃ saṃsthāpayānīti ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>Ādityas</s> said to <s>Savitṛ</s>, 'With you let us raise this pressing.' 'So be it,' he replied. Therefore a <s>Sāvitrī</s> verse is the opening verse of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, and the <s>Sāvitra</s> cup is before it. He sacrifices with the verse, 'The household god <s>Savitṛ</s>, worthy of choice,' with a verse containing gladness and complete in form; for gladness is the form of the third pressing. He does not make the after-<s>vaṣaṭ</s>, and he does not consume the portion. The after-<s>vaṣaṭ</s> is a conclusion, and consumption is a conclusion. <s>Savitṛ</s> is the vital breath; lest he bring the vital breath to a conclusion.

children.text: ubhe vā eṣa ete savane vipibati yat savitā prātaḥsavanaṃ ca tṛtīyasavanaṃ ca tad yat pibavat sāvitryai nividaḥ padam purastād bhavati madvad upariṣṭād ubhayor evainaṃ tat savanayor ābhajati prātaḥsavane ca tṛtīyasavane ca ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Savitṛ</s> drinks both these pressings fully, the morning pressing and the third pressing. Therefore, because a word meaning 'drinking' stands before in the <s>nivid</s> of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, and a word containing gladness stands after, by that he apportions him to both pressings, to the morning pressing and to the third pressing.

children.text: bahvyaḥ prātar vāyavyāḥ śasyanta ekā tṛtīyasavane tasmād ūrdhvāḥ puruṣasya bhūyāṃsaḥ prāṇā yaccāvāñcaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Many <s>Vāyavya</s> verses are recited in the morning, but one at the third pressing. Therefore the upward vital breaths of a person are more numerous than those that go downward.

children.text: dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ śaṃsati dyāvāpṛthivī vai pratiṣṭhe iyam eveha pratiṣṭhāsāv amutra tad yad dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ śaṃsati pratiṣṭhayor evainaṃ tat pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Dyāvāpṛthivīya</s>. Heaven and earth are the two foundations: this one is the foundation here, that one there. When he recites the <s>Dyāvāpṛthivīya</s>, he thereby establishes him on the two foundations.

children.text: Chapter 101
ārbhavaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Ārbhava</s>.

children.text: ṛbhavo vai deveṣu tapasā somapītham abhyajayaṃs tebhyaḥ prātaḥsavane vācikalpayiṣaṃs tān agnir vasubhiḥ prātaḥsavanād anudata tebhyo mādhyaṃdine savane vācikalpayiṣaṃs tān indro rudrair mādhyaṃdināt savanād anudata tebhyas tṛtīyasavane vācikalpayiṣaṃs tān viśve devā anonudyanta neha pāsyanti neheti sa prajāpatir abravīt savitāraṃ tava vā ime 'ntevāsās tvam evaibhiḥ saṃpibasveti sa tathety abravīt savitā tān vai tvam ubhayataḥ paripibeti tān prajāpatir ubhayataḥ paryapibat ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṛbhus</s>, by austerity, won the right to drink Soma among the gods. When they wished to arrange a place for them at the morning pressing, <s>Agni</s>, together with the <s>Vasus</s>, drove them away from the morning pressing. When they wished to arrange a place for them at the midday pressing, <s>Indra</s>, together with the <s>Rudras</s>, drove them away from the midday pressing. When they wished to arrange a place for them at the third pressing, the <s>Viśve Devas</s> kept driving them away, saying, 'They shall not drink here, not here.' Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said to <s>Savitṛ</s>, 'These are your pupils; drink together with them yourself.' He said, 'So be it.' They said, 'But you must drink around them on both sides, O <s>Savitṛ</s>.' <s>Prajāpati</s> then drank around them on both sides.

children.text: te ete dhāyye anirukte prājāpatye śasyete abhita ārbhavaṃ surūpakṛtnum ūtaye 'yaṃ venaś codayat pṛśnigarbhā iti prajāpatir evaināṃs tad ubhayataḥ paripibati tasmād u śreṣṭhī pātre rocayaty eva yaṃ kāmayate tam ||
children.translated_text: These two <s>dhāyyā</s> verses, undefined and belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>, are recited on both sides of the <s>Ārbhava</s>: 'surūpakṛtnum ūtaye' and 'ayaṃ venaś codayat pṛśnigarbhāḥ.' By that <s>Prajāpati</s> drinks around them on both sides. Therefore a superior man too makes the one whom he wishes pleasing in the vessel.

children.text: tebhyo vai devā apaivābībhatsanta manuṣyagandhāt ta ete dhāyye antaradadhata yebhyo mātaivā pitra iti ||
children.translated_text: The gods were indeed disgusted with them because of the smell of human beings. These two <s>dhāyyā</s> verses hid them away: 'for whom mother indeed, and father,' and so on.

children.text: Chapter 102
vaiśvadevaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.

children.text: yathā vai prajā evaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ tad yathāntaraṃ janatā evaṃ sūktāni yathāraṇyāny evaṃ dhāyyās tad ubhayato dhāyyām paryāhvayate tasmāt tāny araṇyāni santy anaraṇyāni mṛgaiś ca vayobhiś ceti ha smāha ||
children.translated_text: As creatures are, so is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>; as the population in between is, so are the hymns; as the forests are, so are the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses. Therefore he calls upon a <s>dhāyyā</s> on both sides. Hence those forests are both forest and not forest, with beasts and birds, so he used to say.

children.text: yathā vai puruṣa evaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ tasya yathāvantaram aṅgāny evaṃ sūktāni yathā parvāṇy evaṃ dhāyyās tad ubhayato dhāyyām paryāhvayate tasmāt puruṣasya parvāṇi śithirāṇi santi dṛﾱhāni brahmaṇā hi tāni dhṛtāni ||
children.translated_text: As a man is, so is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>; as his inner limbs are, so are the hymns; as the joints are, so are the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses. Therefore he calls upon a <s>dhāyyā</s> on both sides. Hence a man's joints are loose and yet firm, for they are held by sacred formulation.

children.text: mūlaṃ vā etad yajñasya yad dhāyyāś ca yājyāś ca tad yad anyā anyā dhāyyāś ca yājyāś ca kuryur unmūlam eva tad yajñaṃ kuryus tasmāt tāḥ samānya eva syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the root of the sacrifice, namely the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses and the offering verses. If they were to make the <s>dhāyyā</s> verses and the offering verses different from one another, they would make the sacrifice uprooted. Therefore they should be the same.

children.text: pāñcajanyaṃ vā etad ukthaṃ yad vaiśvadevaṃ sarveṣāṃ vā etat pañcajanānām uktham devamanuṣyāṇāṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ sarpāṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ caiteṣāṃ vā etat pañcajanānām uktham ||
children.translated_text: This <s>uktha</s>, the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, belongs to the five peoples. It is the <s>uktha</s> of all these five peoples: of gods and human beings, of <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>, of serpents, and of the Fathers; it is the <s>uktha</s> of these five peoples.

children.text: sarva enam pañcajanā vidur ainam pañcinyai janatāyai havino gacchanti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: All the five peoples know him; oblations go to him from the fivefold population, who knows thus.

children.text: sarvadevatyo vā eṣa hotā yo vaiśvadevaṃ śaṃsati sarvā diśo dhyāyecchaṃsiṣyan sarvāsv eva tad dikṣu rasaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>hotṛ</s> who recites the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> belongs to all deities. When about to recite, he should meditate upon all the directions; thereby he places sap in all the directions.

children.text: yasyām asya diśi dveṣyaḥ syān na tāṃ dhyāyed anuhāyaivāsya tad vīryam ādatte ||
children.translated_text: In whatever direction there may be an enemy of his, he should not meditate upon that direction. By omitting it, he takes away that man's vital power.

children.text: aditir dyaur aditir antarikṣam ity uttamayā paridadhātīyaṃ vā aditir iyaṃ dyaur iyaṃ antarikṣam ||
children.translated_text: He encloses it with the final verse, 'Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the midspace.' This world indeed is <s>Aditi</s>; this is heaven; this is the midspace.

children.text: aditir mātā sa pitā sa putra itīyaṃ vai māteyam piteyam putraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Aditi is mother, she is father, she is son.' This world indeed is mother; this is father; this is son.

children.text: viśve devā aditiḥ pañca janā ity asyāṃ vai viśve devā asyām pañcajanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Viśve Devas</s> are <s>Aditi</s>; the five peoples are <s>Aditi</s>.' In this world indeed are the <s>Viśve Devas</s>; in this world are the five peoples.

children.text: aditir jātam aditir janitvam itīyaṃ vai jātam iyaṃ janitvam ||
children.translated_text: 'Aditi is what has been born; Aditi is birth.' This world indeed is what has been born; this is birth.

children.text: dviḥ pacchaḥ paridadhāti catuṣpādā vai paśavaḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai sakṛd ardharcaśaḥ pratiṣṭhāyā eva dvipratiṣṭho vai puruṣaś catuṣpādāḥ paśavo yajamānam eva tad dvipratiṣṭhaṃ catuṣpātsu paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He encloses it twice, foot by foot, for cattle are four-footed, for the securing of cattle; once by half-verses, for foundation. A man is two-footed, and cattle are four-footed. Thereby he establishes the sacrificer, who is two-footed, among four-footed cattle.

children.text: sadaiva pañcajanīyayā paridadhyāt tad upaspṛśan bhūmim paridadhyāt tad yasyām eva yajñaṃ saṃbharati tasyām evainaṃ tad antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He should always enclose with the <s>Pañcajanīya</s> verse. He should enclose while touching the earth. In whatever earth he gathers the sacrifice, in that very earth he thereby establishes it at the end.

children.text: viśve devāḥ śṛṇutemaṃ havam ma iti vaiśvadevam ukthaṃ śastvā vaiśvadevyā yajati yathābhāgaṃ tad devatāḥ prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: Having recited the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> <s>uktha</s>, he sacrifices with the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> verse, 'O <s>Viśve Devas</s>, hear this call of mine.' Thereby he satisfies the deities according to their shares.

children.text: Chapter 103
āgneyī prathamā ghṛtayājyā saumī saumyayājyā vaiṣṇavī ghṛtayājyā tvaṃ soma pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidāna iti saumyasya pitṛmatyā yajati ||
children.translated_text: The first is an <s>Āgneyī</s>, an offering verse with ghee; the <s>Saumī</s> is an offering verse for Soma; the <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> is an offering verse with ghee. With 'You, O Soma, in accord with the Fathers,' he sacrifices for Soma with an offering verse connected with the Fathers.

children.text: ghnanti vā etat somaṃ yad abhiṣuṇvanti tasyaitām anustaraṇīṃ kurvanti yat saumyaḥ pitṛbhyo vā anustaraṇī tasmāt saumyasya pitṛmatyā yajati ||
children.translated_text: They do in effect strike Soma when they press him. For him they make this under-spreading, namely the verse for Soma. The under-spreading belongs to the Fathers; therefore he sacrifices for Soma with an offering verse connected with the Fathers.

children.text: avadhiṣur vā etat somaṃ yad abhyasuṣavus tad enam punaḥ saṃbhāvayanti ||
children.translated_text: They have in effect slain Soma when they have pressed him. Then they bring him back into being again.

children.text: punar āpyāyayanty upasadāṃ rūpeṇopasadāṃ kila vai tad rūpaṃ yad etā devatā agniḥ somo viṣṇur iti ||
children.translated_text: They make him swell again in the form of the <s>upasads</s>. For it is indeed the form of the <s>upasads</s> that these deities are: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: pratigṛhya saumyaṃ hotā pūrvaś chandogebhyo 'vekṣeta ||
children.translated_text: After accepting the Soma portion, the <s>hotṛ</s> should look first, before the <s>chandogas</s>.

children.text: taṃ haike pūrvaṃ chandogebhyo haranti tat tathā na kuryād vaṣaṭkartā prathamaḥ sarvabhakṣān bhakṣayatīti ha smāha tenaiva rūpeṇa tasmād vaṣaṭkartaiva pūrvo 'vekṣetāthainaṃ chandogebhyo haranti ||
children.translated_text: Some carry it first to the <s>chandogas</s>. He should not do that. The maker of the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> is the first to partake of all enjoyments, so he used to say. Therefore, in that very form, the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-maker himself should look first; then they carry it to the <s>chandogas</s>.

children.text: Chapter 104

prajāpatir vai svāṃ duhitaram abhyadhyāyad divam ity anya āhur uṣasam ity anye tām ṛśyo bhūtvā rohitam bhūtām abhyait taṃ devā apaśyann akṛtaṃ vai prajāpatiḥ karotīti te tam aicchan ya enam āriṣyaty etam anyonyasmin nāvindaṃs teṣāṃ yā eva ghoratamās tanva āsaṃs tā ekadhā samabharaṃs tāḥ saṃbhṛtā eṣa devo 'bhavat tad asyaitad bhūtavan nāma ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, indeed, desired his own daughter. Some say she was <s>Dyau</s> (Sky), others say she was <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn). Becoming a stag, he went toward her when she had become a red doe. The gods saw him: '<s>Prajāpati</s> is doing what has not been done.' They sought the one who would injure him, but they did not find him among one another. Whatever bodies of theirs were most terrible, those they brought together in one place; when they had been gathered, this god came into being. Therefore this is his name <s>Bhūtavān</s> ('possessing being').

children.text: bhavati vai sa yo 'syaitad evaṃ nāma veda ||
children.translated_text: He truly comes to be, who knows this name of his in this way.

children.text: taṃ devā abruvann ayaṃ vai prajāpatir akṛtam akar imaṃ vidhyeti sa tathetyabravīt sa vai vo varaṃ vṛṇā iti vṛṇīṣveti sa etam eva varam avṛṇīta paśūnām ādhipatyaṃ tad asyaitat paśuman nāma ||
children.translated_text: The gods said to him, 'This <s>Prajāpati</s> has done what has not been done; pierce him.' He said, 'So be it. But I choose a boon from you.' 'Choose,' they said. He chose this very boon, lordship over animals. Therefore this is his name <s>Paśumān</s> ('possessing animals').

children.text: paśumān bhavati yo 'syaitad evaṃ nāma veda ||
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of animals, who knows this name of his in this way.

children.text: tam abhyāyatyāvidhyat sa viddha ūrdhva udaprapatat tam etam mṛga ity ācakṣate ya u eva mṛgavyādhaḥ sa u eva sa yā rohit sā rohiṇī yo eveṣus trikāṇḍā so eveṣus trikāṇḍā ||
children.translated_text: He went up to him and pierced him. Pierced, he sprang upward. They call him <s>Mṛga</s> (the Beast); and the one who is the <s>Mṛgavyādha</s> (hunter of the beast) is just he. She who was red is <s>Rohiṇī</s>; the three-jointed arrow is just that three-jointed arrow.

children.text: tad vā idam prajāpate retaḥ siktam adhāvat tat saro 'bhavat te devā abruvan medam prajāpate reto duṣad iti yad abruvan medam prajāpate reto duṣad iti tan māduṣam abhavat tan māduṣasya māduṣatvam māduṣaṃ ha vai nāmaitad yan mānuṣaṃ tan māduṣaṃ san mānuṣam ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then this spilled seed of <s>Prajāpati</s> ran away; it became a pool. The gods said, 'May this seed of <s>Prajāpati</s> not be spoiled.' Because they said, 'May this seed of <s>Prajāpati</s> not be spoiled,' it became <s>māduṣa</s>; that is the <s>māduṣa</s>-nature of <s>māduṣa</s>. For this which is <s>mānuṣa</s> (human) is indeed named <s>māduṣa</s>. Though it is <s>māduṣa</s>, they call it <s>mānuṣa</s> indirectly, for the gods are, as it were, fond of the indirect.

children.text: Chapter 105

tad agninā paryādadhus tan maruto 'dhūnvaṃs tad agnir na prācyāvayat tad agninā vaiśvānareṇa paryādadhus tan maruto 'dhūnvaṃs tad agnir vaiśvānaraḥ prācyāvayat tasya yad retasaḥ prathamam udadīpyata tad asāv ādityo 'bhavad yad dvitīyam āsīt tad bhṛgur abhavat taṃ varuṇo nyagṛhṇīta tasmāt sa bhṛgur vāruṇir atha yat tṛtīyam adīded iva ta ādityā abhavan ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan yad aṅgārāḥ punar avaśāntā udadīpyanta tad bṛhaspatir abhavat ||
children.translated_text: They enclosed it with <s>Agni</s>; the <s>Maruts</s> shook it. <s>Agni</s> did not set it in motion. Then they enclosed it with <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>; the <s>Maruts</s> shook it, and <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> set it in motion. Of that seed, what first flared up became yonder <s>Āditya</s> (Sun); what was second became <s>Bhṛgu</s>. <s>Varuṇa</s> seized him, and therefore he is <s>Bhṛgu Vāruṇi</s>. What third glowed, as it were, became the <s>Ādityas</s>; the embers became the <s>Aṅgirases</s>; and when the embers, having quieted down again, flared up, that became <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: yāni parikṣāṇāny āsaṃs te kṛṣṇāḥ paśavo 'bhavan yā lohinī mṛttikā te rohitā atha yad bhasmāsīt tat paruṣyaṃ vyasarpad gauro gavaya ṛśya uṣṭro gardabha iti ye caite 'ruṇāḥ paśavas te ca ||
children.translated_text: The burnt-out remains became black animals; the reddish clay became red animals; and what was ash spread out as rough-colored beasts: the <s>gaura</s>, the <s>gavaya</s>, the <s>ṛśya</s>, the camel, the donkey, and also those tawny animals.

children.text: tān vā eṣa devo 'bhyavadata mama vā idaṃ mama vai vāstuham iti tam etayarcā niravādayanta yaiṣā raudrī śasyate ||
children.translated_text: This god addressed them, saying, 'This is mine indeed; this is my own dwelling-place.' They made him desist with this verse, the one that is recited as the <s>Raudrī</s>.

children.text: ā te pitar marutāṃ sumnam etu mā naḥ sūryasya saṃdṛśo yuyothās tvaṃ no vīro arvati kṣamethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'May your favor come to us, O father of the <s>Maruts</s>; do not separate us from the sight of the sun; may you, a hero, be gracious to us in the contest.'

children.text: iti brūyān nābhi na ity anabhimānuko haiṣa devaḥ prajā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He should say it in this form, not with 'against us'; for this god is not directly favorable, and offspring comes into being.

children.text: pra jāyemahi rudriya prajābhir iti brūyān na rudrety etasyaiva nāmnaḥ parihṛtyai ||
children.translated_text: He should say, 'May we be born forth, O <s>Rudriya</s>, with offspring, with offspring,' not 'O <s>Rudra</s>,' in order to avoid that very name of his.

children.text: tad u khalu śaṃ naḥ karatīty eva śaṃsec cham iti pratipadyate sarvasmā eva śāntyai nṛbhyo nāribhyo gava iti pumāṃso vai naraḥ striyo nāryaḥ sarvasmā eva śāntyai ||
children.translated_text: But he should recite only, 'May he make peace for us,' and he enters upon the word 'peace,' for peace from everything. 'For men, for women, for cows': males are men, females are women; this is for peace from everything.

children.text: so 'niruktā raudrī śāntā sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Raudrī</s> is unexpressed, pacified, and full-life-giving, for the attainment of the full span of life.

children.text: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He reaches the full span of life, who knows thus.

children.text: so gāyatrī brahma vai gāyatrī brahmaṇaivainaṃ tan namasyati ||
children.translated_text: It is in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>brahman</s>; with <s>brahman</s> he thereby pays homage to him.

children.text: Chapter 106
vaiśvānarīyeṇāgnimārutam pratipadyate vaiśvānaro vā etad retaḥ siktam prācyāvayat tasmād vaiśvānarīyeṇāgnimārutam pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> he enters upon the <s>Agnimāruta</s>. <s>Vaiśvānara</s> set this spilled seed in motion; therefore with the <s>Vaiśvānarīya</s> he enters upon the <s>Agnimāruta</s>.

children.text: anavānam prathamark śaṃstavyāgnīn vā eṣo 'rcīṃṣy aśāntān prasīdann eti ya āgnimārutaṃ śaṃsati prāṇenaiva tad agnīṃs tarati ||
children.translated_text: The first verse should be recited without taking breath. For the one who recites the <s>Agnimāruta</s> goes toward the unpacified flames of the fires as they are becoming calm; by breath he thereby crosses over the fires.

children.text: adhīyann upahanyād anyaṃ vivaktāram icchet tam eva tatsetuṃ kṛtvā tarati ||
children.translated_text: If, while reciting, he should be harmed, he should seek another <s>vivaktṛ</s> (ritual divider/reciter). Making that one his bridge, he crosses over.

children.text: tasmād āgnimārute na vyucyam eṣṭavyo vivaktā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>Agnimāruta</s>, a <s>vivaktṛ</s> should not be sought when the recitation has been broken off.

children.text: mārutaṃ śaṃsati maruto ha vā etad retaḥ siktaṃ dhūnvantaḥ prācyāvayaṃs tasmān mārutaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Māruta</s>. For the <s>Maruts</s>, shaking this spilled seed, set it in motion; therefore he recites the <s>Māruta</s>.

children.text: yajñā yajñā vo agnaye devo vo draviṇodā iti madhye yoniṃ cānurūpaṃ ca śaṃsati tad yan madhye yoniṃ cānurūpam ca śaṃsati tasmān madhye yonir dhṛtā ||
children.translated_text: He recites 'Sacrifice after sacrifice for your <s>Agni</s>' and 'The god, bestower of wealth, for you' in the middle, both the <s>yoni</s> (source verse) and the <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse). Because he recites the <s>yoni</s> and the <s>anurūpa</s> in the middle, therefore the womb is placed in the middle.

children.text: yad u dve sūkte śastvā śaṃsati pratiṣṭhayor eva tad upariṣṭāt prajananaṃ dadhāti prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: When, after reciting two hymns, he recites, he thereby places procreation above the two foundations, for the sake of begetting.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is born forth with offspring and with cattle, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 107
jātavedasyaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Jātavedasya</s>.

children.text: prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ parācya evāyan na vyāvartanta tā agninā paryagacchat tā agnim upāvartanta tam evādyāpy upāvṛttāḥ so 'bravīj jātā vai prajā anenāvidam iti yad abravīj jātā vai prajā anenāvidam iti taj jātavedasyam abhavat taj jātavedaso jātavedastvam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> created creatures. Once created, they went away eastward and did not turn back. He went around them with <s>Agni</s>; they turned back to <s>Agni</s>. To him they have turned back even today. He said, 'The creatures have been born; through this one I have found them.' Because he said, 'The creatures have been born; through this one I have found them,' that became the <s>Jātavedasya</s>. That is the <s>Jātavedas</s>-nature of <s>Jātavedas</s>.

children.text: tā agninā parigatā niruddhāḥ śocantyaḥ dīdhyatyo 'tiṣṭhaṃs tā adbhir abhyaṣiñcat tasmād upariṣṭāj jātavedasyasyāpohiṣṭhīyam śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: Surrounded by fire, confined, they stood grieving and blazing. He sprinkled them with waters. Therefore, after the <s>Jātavedasya</s>, he recites the <s>Āpo hi ṣṭhīya</s> verse.

children.text: tasmāt tacchamayateva śaṃstavyaṃ tā adbhir abhiṣicya nijāsyaivāmanyata ||
children.translated_text: Therefore that is to be recited as if pacifying them. Having sprinkled them with waters, he thought that he had made them his own.

children.text: tāsu vā ahinā budhnyena parokṣāt tejo 'dadhād eṣa ha vā ahir budhnyo yad agnir gārhapatyo 'gninaivāsu tadgārhapatyena parokṣāt tejo dadhāti tasmād āhur juhvad evājuhvato vasīyān iti ||
children.translated_text: In them, by means of <s>Ahi Budhnya</s>, he placed brilliance indirectly. This indeed is <s>Ahi Budhnya</s>, namely <s>Agni</s> as the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire. With <s>Agni</s>, with that <s>Gārhapatya</s>, he thereby places brilliance in them indirectly. Therefore they say, 'One who offers is better than one who does not offer.'

children.text: Chapter 108
devānām patnīḥ śaṃsaty anūcīr agniṃ gṛhapatiṃ tasmād anūcī patnī gārhapatyam āste ||
children.translated_text: He recites the verses to the wives of the gods, following <s>Agni</s> the house-lord. Therefore the wife sits following the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire.

children.text: tad āhū rākām pūrvāṃ śaṃsej jāmyai vai pūrvapeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'Should he recite <s>Rākā</s> first? For the first drink belongs to a female kinswoman.'

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyaṃ devānām eva patnīḥ pūrvāḥ śaṃsed eṣa ha vā etat patnīṣu reto dadhāti yad agnir gārhapatyo 'gninaivāsu tad gārhapatyena patnīṣu pratyakṣād reto dadhāti prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: He should not heed that. He should recite the wives of the gods first. This indeed places seed among the wives, namely <s>Agni</s> as the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire. With <s>Agni</s>, with that <s>Gārhapatya</s>, he thereby places seed visibly among the wives, for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is born with offspring and cattle who knows thus.

children.text: tasmāt samānodaryā svasānyodaryāyai jāyāyā anujīvinī jīvati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a sister from the same womb lives as one dependent on a wife from another womb.

children.text: rākāṃ śaṃsati rākā ha vā etām puruṣasya sevanīṃ sīvyati yaiṣā śiśne 'dhi ||
children.translated_text: He recites to <s>Rākā</s>. <s>Rākā</s> indeed sews this seam of a man, the one that is on the penis.

children.text: pumāṃso 'sya putrā jāyante ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Male sons are born to him who knows thus.

children.text: pāvīravīṃ śaṃsati vāg vai sarasvatī pāvīravī vācy eva tad vācaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Pāvīravī</s> verse. Speech indeed is <s>Sarasvatī Pāvīravī</s>; in speech itself he thereby places speech.

children.text: tad āhur yāmīm pūrvāṃ śaṃset pitryām iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'Should he recite the <s>Yāmī</s> verse first, since it belongs to the Fathers?'

children.text: yāmīm eva pūrvāṃ śaṃsed imaṃ yama prastaram ā hi sīdeti rājño vai pūrvapeyaṃ tasmād yāmīm eva pūrvāṃ śaṃset ||
children.translated_text: He should recite the <s>Yāmī</s> verse first: 'Come, O <s>Yama</s>, sit upon this strewn grass.' For the first drink belongs to the king; therefore he should recite the <s>Yāmī</s> verse first.

children.text: mātalī kavyair yamo aṅgirobhir iti kāvyānām anūcīṃ śaṃsaty avareṇaiva vai devān kāvyāḥ pareṇaiva pitṝṃs tasmāt kāvyānām anūcīṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: 'Mātalī with the <s>Kavyas</s>, <s>Yama</s> with the <s>Aṅgirases</s>': he recites the verse following the <s>Kavyas</s>. The <s>Kavyas</s> are below the gods and above the Fathers; therefore he recites the verse following the <s>Kavyas</s>.

children.text: ud īratām avara ut parāsa iti pitryāḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the ancestral verse, 'Let the lower ones arise, and let the higher ones arise.'

children.text: un madhyamāḥ pitaraḥ somyāsa iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Let the middle Fathers, the Soma-drinkers, arise,' so it says.

children.text: ye caivāvamā ye ca paramā ye ca madhyamās tān sarvān anantarāyam pṛṇāti ||
children.translated_text: Those who are lowest, those who are highest, and those who are middle: he satisfies all of them without interruption.

children.text: āham pitṝn suvidatrāṁ avitsīti dvitīyāṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the second verse, 'I have found the Fathers with good guidance.'

children.text: barhiṣado ye svadhayā sutasyety etaddha vā eṣām priyaṃ dhāma yad barhiṣada iti priyeṇaivaināṃs tad dhāmnā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: 'Those who sit on the sacred grass, with the pressed offering according to <s>svadhā</s>': this indeed is their dear abode, namely that they sit on the sacred grass. By their dear abode he thereby brings them to prosperity.

children.text: priyeṇa dhāmnā samṛdhyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers through a dear abode who knows thus.

children.text: idam pitṛbhyo namo astv adyeti namaskāravatīm antataḥ śaṃsati tasmād antataḥ pitṛbhyo namaskriyate ||
children.translated_text: At the end he recites the verse containing homage, 'Let this homage be to the Fathers today.' Therefore homage is made to the Fathers at the end.

children.text: tad āhur vyāhāvam pitryāḥ śaṃset avyāhāvām iti vyāhāvam eva śaṃsed asaṃsthitaṃ vai pitṛyajñasya sādhv asaṃsthitaṃ vā eṣa pitṛyajñaṃ saṃsthāpayati yo 'vyāhāvaṃ śaṃsati tasmād vyāhāvam eva śaṃstavyam ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'Should he recite the ancestral verses with <s>vyāhāva</s> or without <s>vyāhāva</s>?' He should recite them with <s>vyāhāva</s>. For the <s>pitṛyajña</s> is proper when it is unfinished; but one who recites without <s>vyāhāva</s> brings the <s>pitṛyajña</s> to completion. Therefore it should be recited with <s>vyāhāva</s>.

children.text: Chapter 109
svāduṣ kilāyam madhumāṁ utāyam itīndrasyaindrīr anupānīyāḥ śaṃsaty etābhir vā indras tṛtīyasavanam anvapibat tad anupānīyānām anupānīyatvam ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Indra</s>-verses that serve as after-drinks, beginning 'Sweet indeed is this one, and honeyed is this one.' With these <s>Indra</s> drank after the third pressing; that is why they are after-drink verses.

children.text: mādyantīva vai tarhi devatā yad etā hotā śaṃsati tasmād etāsu madvat pratigīryam ||
children.translated_text: At that time the deities are, as it were, exhilarated when the <s>hotṛ</s> recites these. Therefore, in these verses, the response should be given as if intoxicated.

children.text: yayor ojasā skabhitā rajāṃsīti vaiṣṇuvāruṇīm ṛcaṃ śaṃsati viṣṇur vai yajñasya duriṣṭam pāti varuṇaḥ sviṣṭaṃ tayor ubhayor eva śāntyai ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Vaiṣṇava-Vāruṇī</s> verse, 'By the strength of whom the realms are propped up.' <s>Viṣṇu</s> guards what is badly sacrificed in the sacrifice, and <s>Varuṇa</s> guards what is well sacrificed; it is for the appeasement of both of them.

children.text: viṣṇor nu kaṃ vīryāṇi pra vocam iti vaiṣṇavīṃ śaṃsati yathā vai matyam evaṃ yajñasya viṣṇus tad yathā duṣkṛṣṭaṃ durmatīkṛtaṃ sukṛṣṭaṃ sumatīkṛtaṃ kurvann iyād evam evaitad yajñasya duṣṭutaṃ duḥśastaṃ suṣṭutaṃ suśastaṃ kurvann eti yad etāṃ hotā śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> verse, 'Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' As thought is for a mortal, so <s>Viṣṇu</s> is for the sacrifice. Just as one might go along making what is badly ploughed and badly thought into what is well ploughed and well thought, so the <s>hotṛ</s>, when he recites this verse, goes along making what is badly praised and badly recited in the sacrifice into what is well praised and well recited.

children.text: tantuṃ tanvan rajaso bhānum anv ihīti prājāpatyāṃ śaṃsati prajā vai tantuḥ prajām evāsmā etat saṃtanoti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Prājāpatya</s> verse, 'Stretching the thread, follow the light of the atmosphere.' Offspring indeed are the thread; he thereby extends offspring for him.

children.text: jyotiṣmataḥ patho rakṣa dhiyā kṛtān iti devayānā vai jyotiṣmantaḥ panthānas tān evāsmā etad vitanoty anulbaṇaṃ vayata joguvām apo manur bhava janayā daivyaṃ janam ity evainaṃ tan manoḥ prajayā saṃtanoti prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: 'Guard the luminous paths made by insight': the paths of the gods are luminous paths, and he thereby stretches them out for him. 'Weave without a knot; call attentively. O waters, become <s>Manu</s>; generate the divine people': with that he extends him through the offspring of <s>Manu</s>, for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evam veda ||
children.translated_text: He is born with offspring and cattle who knows thus.

children.text: evā na indro maghavā virapśīty uttamayā paridadhātīyaṃ vā indro maghavā virapśī ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse he encloses it: 'Thus for us may <s>Indra Maghavan</s>, the far-reaching one...' This earth indeed is <s>Indra Maghavan</s>, the far-reaching one.

children.text: karat satyā carṣaṇīdhṛd anarvetīyaṃ vai satyā carṣaṇīdhṛd anarvā ||
children.translated_text: 'May she make it true, supporter of peoples, unhindered': this earth indeed is true, supporter of peoples, and unhindered.

children.text: tvaṃ rājā januṣāṃ dhehy asme itīyaṃ vai rājā januṣām ||
children.translated_text: 'You, as king of generations, place it for us': this earth indeed is king of generations.

children.text: adhi śravo māhinaṃ yaj jaritra itīyaṃ vai māhinaṃ yajñaḥ śravo yajamāno jaritā yajamānāyaivaitām āśiṣam āśāste ||
