children.translated_text: 'Bestow great fame upon the singer': this earth indeed is greatness; the sacrifice is fame, and the sacrificer is the singer. He thereby invokes this blessing for the sacrificer.

children.text: tad upaspṛśan bhūmim paridadhyāt tad yasyām eva yajñaṃ saṃbharati tasyām evainaṃ tad antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: Touching the ground, he should enclose it. On the very earth on which he gathers the sacrifice, on that same earth he finally establishes it.

children.text: agne marudbhiḥ śubhayadbhir ṛkvabhir ity āgnimārutam ukthaṃ śastvāgnimārutyā yajati yathābhāgaṃ tad devatāḥ prīṇāti prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: Having recited the <s>Agnimāruta</s> <s>uktha</s>, 'O <s>Agni</s>, with the splendid <s>Maruts</s>, rich in verses,' he sacrifices with the <s>Agnimārutīya</s> verse. Thereby he pleases the deities according to their shares; he pleases them.

children.text: Chapter 110

devā vā asurair yuddham upaprāyan vijayāya tān agnir nānvakāmayataituṃ taṃ devā abruvann api tvam ehy asmākaṃ vai tvameko 'sīti sa nāstuto 'nveṣyāmīty abravīt stuta nu meti taṃ te samutkramyopanivṛtyāstuvaṃs tān stuto 'nuprait ||
children.translated_text: The gods went forth against the <s>Asuras</s> in battle for victory. <s>Agni</s> did not wish to go along after them. The gods said to him, "Come along too; surely you alone are ours." He said, "I will not go along unpraised. Praise me now." Then, having risen up together and turned back toward him, they praised him. Being praised, he went along after them.

children.text: sa triḥśreṇir bhūtvā tryanīko 'surān yuddham upaprāyad vijayāya triḥśreṇir iti chandāṃsy eva śreṇīr akuruta tryanīka iti savanāny evānīkāni tān asaṃbhāvyam parābhāvayat tato vai devā abhavan parāsurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having become three-ranked and three-fronted, he went forth against the <s>Asuras</s> in battle for victory. "Three-ranked" means that he made the metres into ranks; "three-fronted" means that he made the pressings into fronts. He defeated them irresistibly. Then indeed the gods became victorious and the <s>Asuras</s> were defeated.

children.text: bhavaty ātmanā parāsya dviṣan pāpmā bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers in his own person; his hating enemy, evil, his rival, is defeated, who knows thus.

children.text: sā vā eṣā gāyatry eva yad agniṣṭomaś caturviṃśatyakṣarā vai gāyatrī caturviṃśatiragniṣṭomasya stutaśastrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, namely the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has twenty-four syllables, and the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> has twenty-four praises and recitations.

children.text: tad vai yad idam āhuḥ sudhāyāṃ ha vai vājī suhito dadhātīti gāyatrī vai tan na ha vai gāyatrī kṣamā ramata ūrdhvā ha vā eṣā yajamānamādāya svar etīty agniṣṭomo vai tan na ha vā agniṣṭomaḥ kṣamā ramata ūrdhvo ha vā eṣa yajamānam ādāya svar eti ||
children.translated_text: As to what people say, "A well-fed racer sets one on a good course," that is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. The <s>Gāyatrī</s> does not delight in staying on the earth; upright, indeed, she takes up the sacrificer and goes to heaven. That is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. The <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> does not delight in staying on the earth; upright, indeed, it takes up the sacrificer and goes to heaven.

children.text: sa vā eṣa saṃvatsara eva yad agniṣṭomaś caturviṃśatyardhamāso vai saṃvatsaraś caturviṃśatir agniṣṭomasya stutaśastrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is the year, namely the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. The year has twenty-four half-months, and the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> has twenty-four praises and recitations.

children.text: taṃ yathā samudraṃ srotyā evaṃ sarve yajñakratavo 'piyanti ||
children.translated_text: As streams flow into the ocean, so all sacrificial rites enter into it.

children.text: Chapter 111
dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭis tāyate tām evānu yāḥ kāśceṣṭayas tāḥ sarvā agniṣṭomam apiyanti ||
children.translated_text: The initiation offering is performed. Following that very offering, whatever offerings there are, all of them enter into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: iﾱām upahvayata iﾱāvidhā vai pākayajñā iﾱām evānu ye keca pākayajñās te sarve 'gniṣṭomam apiyanti ||
children.translated_text: They call upon <s>Iḍā</s>. The cooked offerings are indeed of the <s>Iḍā</s>-type. Following <s>Iḍā</s> herself, whatever cooked offerings there are, all of them enter into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: sāyamprātar agnihotraṃ juhvati sāyamprātar vratam prayacchanti svāhākāreṇāgnihotraṃ juhvati svāhākāreṇa vratam prayacchanti svāhākāram evānv agnihotram agniṣṭomam apyeti ||
children.translated_text: They offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> evening and morning; they present the vow-offering evening and morning. With the cry <s>svāhā</s> they offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>; with the cry <s>svāhā</s> they present the vow-offering. Following the <s>svāhā</s>-cry, the <s>Agnihotra</s> enters into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: pañcadaśa prāyaṇīye sāmidhenīr anvāha pañcadaśa darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ prāyaṇīyam evānu darśapūrṇamāsāv agniṣṭomam apītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the opening rite he recites fifteen kindling verses; there are fifteen at the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices. Following the opening rite itself, the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices enter into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: somaṃ rājānaṃ krīṇanty auṣadho vai somo rājauṣadhibhis tam bhiṣajyanti yam bhiṣajyanti somam eva rājānaṃ krīyamāṇam anu yāni kānica bheṣajāni tāni sarvāṇy agniṣṭomam apiyanti ||
children.translated_text: They buy King <s>Soma</s>. King <s>Soma</s> is the plants. With plants they heal the one whom they heal. Following King <s>Soma</s> as he is being bought, whatever medicines there are, all of them enter into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: agnim ātithye manthanty agniṃ cāturmāsyeṣv ātithyam evānu cāturmāsyāny agniṣṭomam apiyanti ||
children.translated_text: At the guest-offering they churn <s>Agni</s>; there is <s>Agni</s> in the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> rites. Following the guest-offering itself, the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> rites enter into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: payasā pravargye caranti payasā dākṣāyaṇayajñe pravargyam evānu dākṣāyaṇayajño 'gniṣṭomam apyeti ||
children.translated_text: At the <s>Pravargya</s> they proceed with milk; at the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice they proceed with milk. Following the <s>Pravargya</s> itself, the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> sacrifice enters into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: paśur upavasathe bhavati tam evānu ye keca paśubandhās te sarve 'gniṣṭomamapiyanti ||
children.translated_text: On the fast-day there is an animal. Following that very animal, whatever animal sacrifices there are, all of them enter into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: iﾱādadho nāma yajñakratus taṃ dadhnā caranti dadhnā dadhigharme dadhigharmam evānv iﾱādadho 'gniṣṭomam apyeti ||
children.translated_text: There is a sacrificial rite named <s>Iḍādadha</s>; they proceed with it by means of curds, and with curds at the <s>Dadhigharma</s>. Following the <s>Dadhigharma</s> itself, the <s>Iḍādadha</s> enters into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: Chapter 112

iti nu purastād athopariṣṭāt pañcadaśokthyasya stotrāṇi pañcadaśa śastrāṇi sa māso māsadhā saṃvatsaro vihitaḥ saṃvatsaro 'gnir vaiśvānaro 'gnir agniṣṭomaḥ saṃvatsaram evānūkthyo 'gniṣṭomam apyety ukthyam apiyantam anu vājapeyo 'pyety ukthyo hi sa bhavati ||
children.translated_text: So much for what comes before; now for what comes after. The <s>Ukthya</s> has fifteen chants and fifteen recitations. That is the month; month by month the year is arranged. The year is <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>; <s>Agni</s> is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. Following the year, the <s>Ukthya</s> enters into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; following the <s>Ukthya</s> as it enters, the <s>Vājapeya</s> enters, for it is an <s>Ukthya</s>.

children.text: dvādaśa rātreḥ paryāyāḥ sarve pañcadaśās te dvau dvau sampadya triṃśad ekaviṃśaṃ ṣoﾱaśi sāma trivṛt saṃdhiḥ sā triṃśat sa māsas triṃśan māsasya rātrayo māsadhā saṃvatsaro vihitaḥ saṃvatsaro 'gnir vaiśvānaro 'gnir agniṣṭomaḥ saṃvatsaram evānv atirātro 'gniṣṭomam apyety atirātram apiyantam anv aptoryāmo 'pyety atirātro hi sa bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The twelve rounds of the night are all fifteen-fold. When they are combined two by two, they amount to thirty. The <s>Ekaviṃśa</s>, the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> <s>sāman</s>, and the <s>Trivṛt</s> form the junction. That thirty is the month, for the month has thirty nights; month by month the year is arranged. The year is <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>; <s>Agni</s> is the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. Following the year, the <s>Atirātra</s> enters into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; following the <s>Atirātra</s> as it enters, the <s>Aptoryāma</s> enters, for it is an <s>Atirātra</s>.

children.text: etad vai ye ca purastād ye copariṣṭād yajñakratavas te sarve 'gniṣṭomam apiyanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus all the sacrificial rites, those that come before and those that come after, enter into the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>.

children.text: tasya saṃstutasya navatiśataṃ stotriyāḥ sā yā navatis te daśa trivṛto 'tha yā navatis te daśātha yā daśa tāsām ekā stotriyodeti trivṛt pariśiṣyate so 'sāvekaviṃśo 'dhyāhitas tapati viṣuvān vā eṣa stomānāṃ daśa vā etasmād arvāñcas trivṛto daśa parāñco madhya eṣa ekaviṃśa ubhayato 'dhyāhitas tapati tad yāsau stotriyodeti saitasminn adhyūﾱhā sa yajamānas tad daivaṃ kṣatraṃ saho balam ||
children.translated_text: Of it, when it has been fully praised, there are one hundred and ninety <s>stotriya</s> verses. The ninety are ten <s>Trivṛt</s>s; then the other ninety are ten; and from the remaining ten, one <s>stotriya</s> rises up, while the <s>Trivṛt</s> remains over. That is yonder <s>Ekaviṃśa</s>, set upon both sides, shining. This is the midpoint of the <s>stoma</s>s: ten <s>Trivṛt</s>s are on this side of it, ten are beyond it, and in the middle this <s>Ekaviṃśa</s>, set upon both sides, shines. The <s>stotriya</s> that rises up is mounted upon this; that is the sacrificer, the divine ruling power, force, and strength.

children.text: aśnute ha vai daivaṃ kṣatraṃ saho balam etasya ha sāyujyaṃ sarūpatāṃ salokatām aśnute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He obtains divine ruling power, force, and strength; he obtains union with it, likeness to it, and the same world as it, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 113

devā vā asurair vijigyānā ūrdhvāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyan so 'gnir divispṛg ūrdhva udaśrayata sa svargasya lokasya dvāram avṛṇod agnir vai svargasya lokasyādhipatis taṃ vasavaḥ prathamā āgacchaṃs ta enam abruvann ati no 'rjasy ākāśaṃ naḥ kurv iti sa nāstuto 'tisrakṣya ity abravīt stuta nu meti tatheti taṃ te trivṛtā stomenāstuvaṃs tān stuto 'tyārjata te yathālokam agacchan ||
children.translated_text: The gods, having conquered the <s>Asuras</s>, went upward to the heavenly world. That <s>Agni</s>, touching heaven, stood up above; he closed the door of the heavenly world. <s>Agni</s> is indeed the overlord of the heavenly world. The <s>Vasus</s> came to him first. They said to him, 'You are blocking us from passing beyond; make an opening for us.' He said, 'Unless I am praised, I will not let you pass beyond. Praise me now.' 'So be it,' they said. They praised him with the <s>Trivṛt</s> stoma. When praised, he let them pass beyond. They went to their proper world.

children.text: taṃ rudrā āgacchaṃs ta enam abruvann ati no 'rjasy ākāśaṃ naḥ kurv iti sa nāstuto 'tisrakṣya ity abravīt stuta nu meti tatheti taṃ te pañcadaśena stomenāstuvaṃs tān stuto 'tyārjata te yathālokam agacchan ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Rudras</s> came to him. They said to him, 'You are blocking us from passing beyond; make an opening for us.' He said, 'Unless I am praised, I will not let you pass beyond. Praise me now.' 'So be it,' they said. They praised him with the fifteenfold stoma. When praised, he let them pass beyond. They went to their proper world.

children.text: tam ādityā āgacchaṃs ta enam abruvann ati no 'rjasy ākāśaṃ naḥ kurv iti sa nāstuto 'tisrakṣya ity abravīt stuta nu meti tatheti taṃ te saptadaśena stomenāstuvaṃs tān stuto 'tyārjata te yathālokam agacchan ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s> came to him. They said to him, 'You are blocking us from passing beyond; make an opening for us.' He said, 'Unless I am praised, I will not let you pass beyond. Praise me now.' 'So be it,' they said. They praised him with the seventeenfold stoma. When praised, he let them pass beyond. They went to their proper world.

children.text: taṃ viśve devā āgacchaṃs ta enam abruvann ati no 'rjasy ākāśaṃ naḥ kurv iti sa nāstuto 'tisrakṣya ity abravīt stuta nu meti tatheti taṃ ta ekaviṃśena stomenāstuvaṃs tān stuto 'tyārjata te yathālokam agacchan ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Viśve Devas</s> came to him. They said to him, 'You are blocking us from passing beyond; make an opening for us.' He said, 'Unless I am praised, I will not let you pass beyond. Praise me now.' 'So be it,' they said. They praised him with the twenty-onefold stoma. When praised, he let them pass beyond. They went to their proper world.

children.text: ekaikena vai taṃ devāḥ stomenāstuvaṃs tān stuto 'tyārjata te yathālokam agacchan ||
children.translated_text: The gods praised him with each single stoma in turn. When praised, he let them pass beyond. They went to their proper world.

children.text: atha hainam eṣa etaiḥ sarvaiḥ stomaiḥ stauti yo yajate ||
children.translated_text: Now the one who sacrifices praises him with all these stomas.

children.text: yaś cainam evaṃ vedātī tu tam arjātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And whoever knows him in this way, those stomas indeed carry him beyond.

children.text: ati ha vā enam arjate svargaṃ lokam abhi ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus indeed passes beyond, toward the heavenly world.

children.text: Chapter 114
sa vā eṣo 'gnir eva yad agniṣṭomas taṃ yad astuvaṃs tasmād agnistomas tam agnistomaṃ santam agniṣṭoma ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Agni</s> is precisely what the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is. Because they praised him, therefore it is <s>agnistoma</s>; though it is <s>agnistoma</s>, they call it <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> indirectly, for the gods are, as it were, fond of the indirect.

children.text: taṃ yac catuṣṭayā devāś caturbhiḥ stomair astuvaṃs tasmāccatustomas taṃ catustomaṃ santaṃ catuṣṭoma ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the gods praised him fourfold, with four stomas, therefore it is <s>catustoma</s>; though it is <s>catustoma</s>, they call it <s>Catuṣṭoma</s> indirectly, for the gods are, as it were, fond of the indirect.

children.text: atha yad enam ūrdhvaṃ santaṃ jyotir bhūtam astuvaṃs tasmāj jyotistomas taṃ jyotistomaṃ santaṃ jyotiṣṭoma ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And because they praised him when he was raised upward and had become light, therefore it is <s>jyotistoma</s>; though it is <s>jyotistoma</s>, they call it <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> indirectly, for the gods are, as it were, fond of the indirect.

children.text: sa vā eṣo 'pūrvo 'naparo yajñakratur yathā rathacakram anantam evaṃ yad agniṣṭomas tasya yathaiva prāyaṇaṃ tathodayanam ||
children.translated_text: This sacrificial rite has no earlier and no later; it is endless, like a chariot wheel, namely the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. As its <s>prāyaṇa</s> (opening course) is, so is its <s>udayana</s> (closing rise).

children.text: tad eṣābhi yajñagāthā gīyate yad asya pūrvam aparaṃ tad asya yad v asyāparaṃ tad v asya pūrvam aher iva sarpaṇaṃ śākalasya na vijānanti yatarat parastād iti ||
children.translated_text: About this a sacrificial verse is sung: 'What of it is earlier, that is its later part; and what of it is later, that is its earlier part. Like the movement of a serpent, they do not know which side is beyond <s>Śākala</s>.'

children.text: yathā hy evāsya prāyaṇam evam udayanam asad iti ||
children.translated_text: For its <s>udayana</s> should be just as its <s>prāyaṇa</s> is.

children.text: tad āhur yat trivṛt prāyaṇam ekaviṃśam udayanaṃ kena te same iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'Since the <s>prāyaṇa</s> is <s>Trivṛt</s> and the <s>udayana</s> is twenty-onefold, by what are those two equal?'

children.text: yo vā ekaviṃśas trivṛd vai so 'tho yad ubhau tṛcau tṛcināv iti brūyāt teneti ||
children.translated_text: One should say, 'The twenty-onefold is indeed <s>Trivṛt</s>; or else, because both <s>tṛcas</s> are triadic, by that they are equal.'

children.text: Chapter 115
yo vā eṣa tapaty eṣo 'gniṣṭoma eṣa sāhnas taṃ sahaivāhnā saṃsthāpayeyuḥ sāhno vai nāma ||
children.translated_text: The one who shines there is this <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; this is the <s>Sāhna</s>. They should complete it together with the day itself, for its name is <s>sāhna</s> (belonging to one day).

children.text: tena saṃtvaramāṇāś careyur yathaiva prātaḥsavana evam mādhyaṃdina evaṃ tṛtīyasavana evam u ha yajamāno 'pramāyuko bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they should perform it without hurrying: as at the morning pressing, so at the midday pressing, and so at the third pressing. In this way the sacrificer does not become short-lived.

children.text: yaddha vā idam pūrvayoḥ savanayor asaṃtvaramāṇāś caranti tasmāddhedam prācyo grāmatā bahulāviṣṭā atha yaddhedaṃ tṛtīyasavane saṃtvaramāṇaś caranti tasmāddhedam pratyañci dīrghāraṇyāni bhavanti tathā ha yajamānaḥ pramāyuko bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Because, in the first two pressings, they perform it without hurrying, therefore the eastern village lands here are densely inhabited. But because, at the third pressing, they perform it in haste, therefore the western regions here become long stretches of forest. In that way the sacrificer becomes short-lived.

children.text: tenāsaṃtvaramāṇāś careyur yathaiva prātaḥsavana evam mādhyaṃdina evaṃ tṛtīyasavana evam u ha yajamāno 'pramāyuko bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they should perform it without hurrying: as at the morning pressing, so at the midday pressing, and so at the third pressing. In this way the sacrificer does not become short-lived.

children.text: sa etam eva śastreṇānuparyāvarteta yadā vā eṣa prātar udety atha mandraṃ tapati tasmān mandrayā vācā prātaḥsavane śaṃsed atha yadābhyety atha balīyas tapati tasmād balīyasyā vācā madhyaṃdine śaṃsed atha yadābhitarām ety atha baliṣṭhatamaṃ tapati tasmād baliṣṭhatamayā vācā tṛtīyasavane śaṃsed evaṃ śaṃsed yadi vāca īśīta vāgghi śastraṃ yayā tu vācottarottariṇyotsaheta samāpanāya tayā pratipadyetaitat suśastatamam iva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He should follow this very one around with the <s>śastra</s> (recitation). When he rises in the morning, he gives a low heat; therefore at the morning pressing one should recite with a low voice. When he advances, he gives stronger heat; therefore at midday one should recite with a stronger voice. When he comes still farther in, he gives the strongest heat; therefore at the third pressing one should recite with the strongest voice. Thus should one recite, if he has command of his voice, for speech is the <s>śastra</s>. But with whatever voice he can rise higher and higher toward completion, with that voice he should begin. This becomes, as it were, the best-recited.

children.text: sa vā eṣa na kadācanāstam eti nodeti ||
children.translated_text: This one, indeed, never sets and never rises.

children.text: taṃ yad astam etīti manyante 'hna eva tad antam itvāthātmānaṃ viparyasyate rātrīm evāvastāt kurute 'haḥ parastāt ||
children.translated_text: When they think that he sets, he has merely gone to the end of the day and then turns himself around; he makes the night below and the day beyond.

children.text: atha yad enam prātar udetīti manyante rātrer eva tad antam itvāthātmānaṃ viparyasyate 'har evāvastāt kurute rātrīm parastāt ||
children.translated_text: And when they think that he rises in the morning, he has merely gone to the end of the night and then turns himself around; he makes the day below and the night beyond.

children.text: sa vā eṣa na kadācana nimrocati ||
children.translated_text: This one, indeed, never sinks down.

children.text: na ha vai kadācana nimrocaty etasya ha sāyujyaṃ sarūpatām salokatām aśnute ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: It never sets. He attains union with it, likeness of form with it, and its world, who knows thus, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 116

yajño vai devebhyo 'nnādyam udakrāmat te devā abruvan yajño vai no 'nnādyam udakramīd anv imaṃ yajñam anna anvicchāmeti te 'bruvan katham anvicchāmeti brāhmaṇena ca chandobhiś cety abruvaṃs te brāhmaṇaṃ chandobhir adīkṣayaṃs tasyāntaṃ yajñam atanvatāpi patnīḥ samayājayaṃs tasmāddhāpyetarhi dīkṣaṇīyāyām iṣṭāv āntam eva yajñaṃ tanvate 'pi patnīḥ saṃyājayanti tam anu nyāyam anvavāyan ||
children.translated_text: The <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), the food of the gods, went away from the gods. The gods said, 'The sacrifice, our food, has gone away. Come, let us seek after this sacrifice, this food.' They said, 'How shall we seek after it?' They said, 'With the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and with the metres.' They consecrated the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> with the metres. For it they extended the sacrifice to its end, and they also made the wives join in the sacrifice. Therefore even now, at the initiatory offering, they extend the sacrifice to its end, and also make the wives join in the sacrifice. They followed that procedure.

children.text: te prāyaṇīyam atanvata tam prāyaṇīyena nedīyo 'nvāgacchaṃs te karmabhiḥ samatvaranta tac chaṃyvantam akurvaṃs tasmāddhāpyetarhi prāyaṇīyaṃ śaṃyvantam eva bhavati tam anu nyāyam anvavāyan ||
children.translated_text: They extended the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> rite. By the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> they came nearer to it. They hastened through the rites. They made it end with the <s>śaṃyu</s>. Therefore even now the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> has the <s>śaṃyu</s> as its end. They followed that procedure.

children.text: ta ātithyam atanvata tam ātithyena nedīyo 'nvāgacchaṃs te karmabhiḥ samatvaranta tad iﾱāntam akurvaṃs tasmāddhāpyetarhyātithyam iﾱāntam eva bhavati tam anu nyāyam anvavāyan ||
children.translated_text: They extended the guest-offering. By the guest-offering they came nearer to it. They hastened through the rites. They made it end with the <s>iḍā</s>. Therefore even now the guest-offering has the <s>iḍā</s> as its end. They followed that procedure.

children.text: ta upasado 'tanvata tam upasadbhir nedīyo 'nvāgacchaṃs te karmabhiḥ samatvaranta te tisraḥ sāmidhenīr anūcya tisro devatā ayajaṃs tasmāddhāpyetarhyupasatsu tisra eva sāmidhenīr anūcya tisro devatā yajanti tam anu nyāyam anvavāyan ||
children.translated_text: They extended the <s>upasads</s>. By the <s>upasads</s> they came nearer to it. They hastened through the rites. After reciting three kindling-verses, they sacrificed to three deities. Therefore even now, in the <s>upasads</s>, after reciting just three kindling-verses, they sacrifice to three deities. They followed that procedure.

children.text: ta upavasatham atanvata tam upavasathye 'hany āpnuvaṃs tam āptvāntaṃ yajñam atanvatāpi patnīḥ samayājayaṃs tasmāddhāpyetarhy upavasatha āntam eva yajñaṃ tanvate 'pi patnīḥ saṃyājayanti ||
children.translated_text: They extended the <s>upavasatha</s>. On the <s>upavasatha</s> day they reached it. Having reached it, they extended the sacrifice to its end, and also made the wives join in the sacrifice. Therefore even now, at the <s>upavasatha</s>, they extend the sacrifice to its end, and also make the wives join in the sacrifice.

children.text: tasmād eteṣu pūrveṣu karmasu śanaistarāṃ śanaistarām ivānubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in these preceding rites, he should recite more and more slowly, as it were.

children.text: anūtsāram iva hi te tam āyāṃs tasmād upavasathe yāvatyā vācā kāmayīta tāvatyānubrūyād āpto hi sa tarhi bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: For they came to it as if without haste. Therefore at the <s>upavasatha</s> he should recite with as much voice as he wishes, for at that time it has been reached.

children.text: tam āptvābruvaṃs tiṣṭhasva no'nnādyāyeti sa nety abravīt kathaṃ vas tiṣṭheyeti tān īkṣataiva tam abruvan brāhmaṇena ca naś chandobhiś ca sayug bhūtvānnādyāya tiṣṭhasveti tatheti tasmāddhāpyetarhi yajñaḥ sayug bhūtvā devebhyo havyaṃ vahati brāhmaṇena ca chandobhiś ca ||
children.translated_text: Having reached it, they said, 'Stand for us, for the sake of food.' It said, 'No.' 'How should I stand for you?' It looked at them. They said to it, 'Having become yoked together with our <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and with the metres, stand for the sake of food.' 'So be it,' it said. Therefore even now the sacrifice, having become yoked together with the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and with the metres, carries the oblation to the gods.

children.text: Chapter 117
trīṇi ha vai yajñe kriyante jagdhaṃ gīrṇaṃ vāntam ||
children.translated_text: Three things, indeed, are done in the sacrifice: what is eaten, what is swallowed, and what is vomited.

children.text: taddhaitad eva jagdhaṃ yad āśaṃsamānam ārtvijyaṃ kārayata uta vā me dadyād uta vā mā vṛṇīteti taddha tat parāṅ eva yathā jagdhaṃ na haiva tad yajamānam bhunakti ||
children.translated_text: Of these, this is what is eaten: when one makes a man perform priestly service while hoping, 'Perhaps he may give me something, or perhaps he may choose me.' That, like food eaten, has gone away; it does not benefit the sacrificer.

children.text: atha haitad eva gīrṇaṃ yad bibhyad ārtvijyaṃ kārayata uta vā mā na bādhetota vā me na yajñaveśasaṃ kuryād iti taddha tat parāṅ eva yathā gīrṇaṃ na haiva tad yajamānam bhunakti ||
children.translated_text: Then this is what is swallowed: when one makes a man perform priestly service out of fear, thinking, 'Perhaps he may not injure me, or perhaps he may not cause me damage in the sacrifice.' That, like what is swallowed, has gone away; it does not benefit the sacrificer.

children.text: atha haitad eva vāntaṃ yad abhiśasyamānam ārtvijyaṃ kārayate yathā ha vā idaṃ vāntān manuṣyā bībhatsanta evam tasmād devās taddha tat parāṅ eva yathā vāntaṃ na haiva tad yajamānam bhunakti ||
children.translated_text: Then this is what is vomited: when one makes a man perform priestly service while he is under reproach. Just as people are disgusted by vomit here, so the gods are disgusted by that. That, like what is vomited, has gone away; it does not benefit the sacrificer.

children.text: sa eteṣāṃ trayāṇām āśām neyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not direct his hope toward any of these three.

children.text: taṃ yady eteṣāṃ trayāṇām ekaṃ cid akāmam abhyābhavet tasyāsti vāmadevyasya stotre prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, against his will, even one of these three should befall him, there is an expiation for it in the <s>Vāmadevya</s> stotra.

children.text: idaṃ vā idaṃ vāmadevyaṃ yajamānaloko 'mṛtalokaḥ svargo lokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Vāmadevya</s> is indeed this world of the sacrificer, the immortal world, the heavenly world.

children.text: tat tribhir akṣarair nyūnaṃ tasya stotra upasṛpya tredhātmānaṃ vigṛhṇīyāt pu ru ṣa iti ||
children.translated_text: It is short by three syllables. In its stotra, having approached it, he should divide himself threefold: 'pu-ru-ṣa.'

children.text: sa eteṣu lokeṣv ātmānaṃ dadhāty asmin yajamānaloke 'sminn amṛtaloke 'smin svarge loke sa sarvāṃ duriṣṭim atyeti ||
children.translated_text: He thereby places himself in these worlds: in this world of the sacrificer, in this immortal world, in this heavenly world. He passes beyond every badly performed sacrifice.

children.text: api yadi samṛddhā iva ṛtvijaḥ syur iti ha smāhātha haitaj japed eveti ||
children.translated_text: Even if the officiating priests should seem successful, so he used to say, still he should recite this formula.

children.text: Chapter 118
chandāṃsi vai devebhyo havyam ūḍhvā śrāntāni jaghanārdhe yajñasya tiṣṭhanti yathāśvo vāśvataro vohivāṃs tiṣṭhed evaṃ tebhya etam maitrāvaruṇam paśupuroﾱāśam anu devikāhavīṃṣi nirvapet ||
children.translated_text: The metres, having carried the oblation for the gods, stand tired in the rear part of the sacrifice, as a horse or a mule that has carried a load would stand. For them he should offer this <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> animal-cake and the <s>Devikā</s> oblations.

children.text: dhātre puroﾱāśaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ yo dhātā sa vaṣaṭkāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Dhātṛ</s>, a cake on twelve potsherds; what is <s>Dhātṛ</s> is the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>.

children.text: anumatyai caruṃ yānumatiḥ sā gāyatrī ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Anumati</s>, a <s>caru</s> (porridge offering); she who is <s>Anumati</s> is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: rākāyai caruṃ yā rākā sā triṣṭup ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Rākā</s>, a <s>caru</s>; she who is <s>Rākā</s> is the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: sinīvālyai caruṃ yā sinīvālī sā jagatī kuhvai caruṃ yā kuhūḥ sānuṣṭup ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Sinīvālī</s>, a <s>caru</s>; she who is <s>Sinīvālī</s> is the <s>Jagatī</s>. For <s>Kuhū</s>, a <s>caru</s>; she who is <s>Kuhū</s> is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: etāni vāva sarvāṇi chandāṃsi gāyatraṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ jāgatam ānuṣṭubham anv anyāny etāni hi yajñe pratamām iva kriyante ||
children.translated_text: These indeed are all the metres: the <s>Gāyatra</s>, the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s>, the <s>Jāgata</s>, and the <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s>. The others follow after them, for these are the ones first employed, as it were, in the sacrifice.

children.text: etair ha vā asya chandobhir yajataḥ sarvaiś chandobhir iṣṭam bhavāti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For the man who sacrifices with these metres, the sacrifice has been performed with all the metres, who knows thus.

children.text: tad vai yad idam āhuḥ sudhāyāṃ ha vai vājī suhito dadhātīti chandāṃsi vai tat sudhāyāṃ ha vā enaṃ chandāṃsi dadhati ||
children.translated_text: Now when they say, 'The well-fed racer places him in good fodder,' the metres are that good fodder; the metres indeed place him in good fodder.

children.text: ananudhyāyinaṃ lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He wins a world in which no one broods against him, who knows thus.

children.text: taddhaika āhur dhātāram eva sarvāsām purastāt purastād ājyena pariyajet tad āsu sarvāsu mithunaṃ dadhātīti ||
children.translated_text: Concerning this, some say: he should worship <s>Dhātā</s> alone before all of them, before each one, with ghee; thereby he places a male counterpart among all these goddesses.

children.text: tad u vā āhur jāmi vā etad yajñe kriyate yatra samānībhyām ṛgbhyāṃ samāne 'han yajatīti ||
children.translated_text: But others say: this is a close pairing made in the sacrifice, when one sacrifices on the same day with two identical verses.

children.text: yadi ha vā api bahvya iva jāyāḥ patir vāva tāsām mithunaṃ tad yad āsāṃ dhātāram purastād yajati tad āsu sarvāsu mithunaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Yet even if the wives are many, the husband is indeed the male counterpart of them all; therefore, when he sacrifices to <s>Dhātā</s> before them, he places a male counterpart among all these goddesses.

children.text: iti nu devikānām ||
children.translated_text: So much, then, for the <s>Devikās</s>.

children.text: Chapter 119
atha devīnām ||
children.translated_text: Now for the <s>Devīs</s>.

children.text: sūryāya puroﾱāśam ekakapālaṃ yaḥ sūryaḥ sa dhātā sa u eva vaṣaṭkāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Sūrya</s> there is a cake on one potsherd; the one who is <s>Sūrya</s> is <s>Dhātā</s>, and he himself is the vaṣaṭ-call.

children.text: dive caruṃ yā dyauḥ sānumatiḥ so eva gāyatry uṣase caruṃ yoṣāḥ sā rākā so eva triṣṭub gave caruṃ yā gauḥ sā sinīvālī so eva jagatī pṛthivyai caruṃ yā pṛthivī sā kuhūḥ so evānuṣṭup ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Dyauḥ</s> there is a caru: she who is <s>Dyauḥ</s> is <s>Anumati</s>, and that same one is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. For <s>Uṣas</s> there is a caru: she who is <s>Uṣas</s> is <s>Rākā</s>, and that same one is the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. For the Cow there is a caru: she who is the Cow is <s>Sinīvālī</s>, and that same one is the <s>Jagatī</s>. For <s>Pṛthivī</s> there is a caru: she who is <s>Pṛthivī</s> is <s>Kuhū</s>, and that same one is the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: etāni vāva sarvāṇi chandāṃsi gāyatraṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ jāgatam ānuṣṭubham anv anyāny etāni hi yajñe pratamām iva kriyanta etair ha vā asya chandobhir yajataḥ sarvaiś chandobhir iṣṭam bhavati ya evaṃ veda tad vai yad idam āhuḥ sudhāyāṃ ha vai vājī suhito dadhātīti chandāṃsi vai tat sudhāyāṃ ha vā enaṃ chandāṃsi dadhaty ananudhyāyinaṃ lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda taddhaika āhuḥ sūryam eva sarvāsām purastāt purastād ājyena pariyajet tad āsu sarvāsu mithunaṃ dadhātīti tad u vā āhur jāmi vā etad yajñe kriyate yatra samānībhyām ṛgbhyāṃ samāne 'han yajatīti yadi ha vā api bahvya iva jāyāḥ patir vāva tāsām mithunaṃ tad yad āsāṃ sūryam purastād yajati tad āsu sarvāsu mithunaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: These indeed are all the metres: the Gāyatra, the Traiṣṭubha, the Jāgata, and the Ānuṣṭubha; the others follow after them, for these are performed as the foremost ones in the sacrifice. For him who sacrifices with these metres, the sacrifice has been performed with all the metres, who knows thus. As to what people say, 'A well-fed racer sets one upon a good course,' that refers to the metres: the metres set him upon a good course. He wins a world in which no one broods against him, who knows thus. Concerning this, some say: he should worship <s>Sūrya</s> alone before all of them, before each one, with ghee; thereby he places a male counterpart among all these goddesses. But others say: this is a close pairing made in the sacrifice, when one sacrifices on the same day with two identical verses. Yet even if the wives are many, the husband is indeed the male counterpart of them all; therefore, when he sacrifices to <s>Sūrya</s> before them, he places a male counterpart among all these goddesses.

children.text: tā yā imās tā amūr yā amūs tā imā anyatarābhir vāva taṃ kāmam āpnoti ya etāsūbhayīṣu ||
children.translated_text: Those that are these here are those yonder, and those that are yonder are these here; by either set he obtains that desire which belongs to both of these sets.

children.text: tā ubhayīr gataśriyaḥ prajātikāmasya saṃnirvapet ||
children.translated_text: He should offer both sets together for a man whose prosperity has departed and who desires offspring.

children.text: na tv eṣiṣyamāṇasya ||
children.translated_text: But not for one who is still seeking to prosper.

children.text: yad enā eṣiṣyamāṇasya saṃnirvaped īśvaro hāsya vitte devā arantor yad vā ayam ātmane 'lam amaṃsteti ||
children.translated_text: For if he were to offer them together for one who is still seeking to prosper, the gods might turn away from his wealth, thinking, 'This man has considered himself sufficient for himself.'

children.text: tā ha śucivṛkṣo gaupalāyano vṛddhadyumnasyābhipratāriṇasyobhayīr yajñe saṃniruvāpa tasya ha rathagṛtsaṃ gāhamānaṃ dṛṣṭvovācettham aham asya rājanyasya devikāś ca devīś cobhayīr yajñe samamādayaṃ yad asyetthaṃ rathagṛtso gāhata iti catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ kavacinaḥ śaśvaddhāsya te putranaptāra āsuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śucivṛkṣa Gaupalāyana</s> offered both sets together in the sacrifice for <s>Vṛddhadyumna Abhipratārin</s>. Seeing <s>Rathagṛtsa</s> plunging in, he said, 'In just this way I have gladdened together for this royal man both the <s>Devikās</s> and the <s>Devīs</s> in the sacrifice, since <s>Rathagṛtsa</s> plunges in like this.' Sixty-four armored men, so they say, were always his sons and grandsons.

children.text: Chapter 120
agniṣṭomaṃ vai devā aśrayantokthāny asurās te samāvadvīryā evāsan na vyāvartanta tān bharadvāja ṛṣīṇām apaśyad ime vā asurā uktheṣu śritās tān eṣāṃ na kaścana paśyatīti so 'gnim udahvayat ||
children.translated_text: The gods resorted to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, and the <s>Asuras</s> to the <s>ukthas</s>. They were of equal strength and did not separate from one another. <s>Bharadvāja</s>, among the seers, saw them: 'These <s>Asuras</s> are lodged in the <s>ukthas</s>, and no one sees them.' Then he called upon <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: ehy ū ṣu bravāṇi te 'gna itthetarā gira iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Come here; let me now speak to you, O <s>Agni</s>, words different from these.'

children.text: asuryā ha vā itarā giraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The other words are indeed Asuric.

children.text: so 'gnir upottiṣṭhann abravīt kiṃ svid eva mahyaṃ kṛśo dīrghaḥ palito vakṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Agni</s>, rising up, said, 'What exactly will this thin, tall, grey-haired man say to me?'

children.text: bharadvājo ha vai kṛśo dīrghaḥ palita āsa ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharadvāja</s> was indeed thin, tall, and grey-haired.

children.text: so 'bravīd ime vā asurā uktheṣu śritās tān vo na kaścana paśyatīti ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'These <s>Asuras</s> are lodged in the <s>ukthas</s>, and no one among you sees them.'

children.text: tān agnir aśvo bhūtvābhyatyadravad yad agnir aśvo bhūtvābhyatyadravat tat sākamaśvaṃ sāmābhavat tat sākamaśvasya sākamaśvatvam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, becoming a horse, ran upon them. Because <s>Agni</s>, becoming a horse, ran upon them, that <s>sāman</s> became the <s>Sākamaśva</s>; that is why the <s>Sākamaśva</s> has the name <s>Sākamaśva</s>.

children.text: tad āhuḥ sākamaśvenokthāni praṇayed apraṇītāni vāva tāny ukthāni yāny anyatra sākamaśvād iti ||
children.translated_text: They say: one should lead forth the <s>ukthas</s> with the <s>Sākamaśva</s>; those <s>ukthas</s> that are led otherwise than with the <s>Sākamaśva</s> are, in effect, not led forth.

children.text: pramaṃhiṣṭhīyena praṇayed ity āhuḥ pramaṃhiṣṭhīyena vai devā asurān ukthebhyaḥ prāṇudanta ||
children.translated_text: They say: one should lead them forth with the <s>Pramaṃhiṣṭhīya</s>; for with the <s>Pramaṃhiṣṭhīya</s> the gods drove the <s>Asuras</s> out of the <s>ukthas</s>.

children.text: tat prāhaiva pramaṃhiṣṭhīyena nayet pra sākamaśvena ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he should indeed lead them with the <s>Pramaṃhiṣṭhīya</s>, and lead them forth with the <s>Sākamaśva</s>.

children.text: Chapter 121

te vā asurā maitrāvaruṇasyoktham aśrayanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaś cāhaṃ cemān ito 'surān notsyāvahā ity ahaṃ cety abravīd varuṇas tasmād aindrāvaruṇam maitrāvaruṇas tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīndraś ca hi tān varuṇaś ca tato 'nudetām ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>Asuras</s> then resorted to the <s>uktha</s> of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>. <s>Indra</s> said, 'Who, together with me, will drive these <s>Asuras</s> away from here?' 'I will,' said <s>Varuṇa</s>. Therefore the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites the <s>Aindrāvaruṇa</s> at the third pressing, for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> drove them away from there.

children.text: te vai tato 'pahatā asurā brāhmaṇācchaṃsina uktham aśrayanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaścāhaṃ cemān ito 'surān notsyāvahā ity ahaṃ cety abravīd bṛhaspatis tasmād aindrābārhaspatyam brāhmaṇācchaṃsī tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīndraś ca hi tān bṛhaspatiś ca tato'nudetām ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>Asuras</s>, beaten away from there, resorted to the <s>uktha</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. <s>Indra</s> said, 'Who, together with me, will drive these <s>Asuras</s> away from here?' 'I will,' said <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. Therefore the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites the <s>Aindrābārhaspatya</s> at the third pressing, for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> drove them away from there.

children.text: te vai tato 'pahatā asurā achāvākasyoktham aśrayanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaś cāhaṃ cemān ito 'surān notsyāvahā ity ahaṃ cety abravīd viṣṇus tasmād aindrāvaiṣṇavam achāvākas tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīndraś ca hi tān viṣṇuś ca tato 'nudetām ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>Asuras</s>, beaten away from there, resorted to the <s>uktha</s> of the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. <s>Indra</s> said, 'Who, together with me, will drive these <s>Asuras</s> away from here?' 'I will,' said <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Therefore the <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites the <s>Aindrāvaiṣṇava</s> at the third pressing, for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> drove them away from there.

children.text: dvandvam indreṇa devatāḥ śasyante dvandvaṃ vai mithunaṃ tasmād dvandvān mithunam prajāyate prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: The deities are recited in pairs with <s>Indra</s>. A pair is indeed a mating pair; therefore from a pair a mating pair is born, for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is born with offspring and cattle who knows thus.

children.text: atha haite potrīyāś ca neṣṭrīyāś ca catvāra ṛtuyājāḥ ṣaﾱ ṛcaḥ sā virāḍ daśinī tad virāji yajñaṃ daśinyām pratiṣṭhāpayanti pratiṣṭhāpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Now these, the <s>Potṛ</s>'s and the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>'s, are four seasonal offering verses and six verses: that is the tenfold <s>Virāj</s>. Thereby they establish the sacrifice in the <s>Virāj</s>, the tenfold one; they establish it.

children.text: Chapter 122
devā vai prathamenāhnendrāya vajraṃ samabharaṃs taṃ dvitīyenāhnāsiñcaṃs taṃ tṛtīyenāhnā prāyacchaṃs taṃ caturthe 'han prāharat tasmāccaturthe 'han ṣoﾱaśinaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: The gods, on the first day, gathered the vajra (thunderbolt) for <s>Indra</s>; on the second day they consecrated it; on the third day they gave it to him; on the fourth day he struck with it. Therefore on the fourth day he recites the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>.

children.text: vajro vā eṣa yat ṣoﾱaśī tad yac caturthe 'han ṣoﾱaśinaṃ śaṃsati vajram eva tat praharati dviṣate bhrātṛvyāya vadhaṃ yo 'sya stṛtyas tasmai startavai ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is the vajra, namely the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>. Since on the fourth day he recites the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, he thereby hurls the vajra, a blow against the hateful rival, in order to strike down whoever is to be struck down by him.

children.text: vajro vai ṣoﾱaśī paśava ukthāni tam parastād ukthānām paryasya śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is indeed the vajra, and the <s>uktha</s>s are cattle. He recites it by placing it after the <s>uktha</s>s.

children.text: taṃ yat parastād ukthānām paryasya śaṃsati vajreṇaiva tat ṣoﾱaśinā paśūn parigacchati tasmāt paśavo vajreṇaiva ṣoﾱaśinā parigatā manuṣyān abhy upāvartante tasmād aśvo vā puruṣo vā gaur vā hastī vā parigata eva svayam ātmaneta eva vācābhiṣiddha upāvartate vajram eva ṣoﾱaśinam paśyan vajreṇaiva ṣoﾱaśinā parigato vāgghi vajro vāk ṣoﾱaśī ||
children.translated_text: Since he recites it by placing it after the <s>uktha</s>s, with the vajra, the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, he thereby encloses the cattle. Therefore cattle, enclosed by the vajra, the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, turn back toward men. Therefore a horse, or a man, or a cow, or an elephant, once enclosed, turns back of its own accord when checked merely by voice, seeing the vajra as the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> and being enclosed by the vajra, the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>; for speech is the vajra, speech is the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>.

children.text: tad āhuḥ kiṃ ṣoﾱaśinaḥ ṣoﾱaśitvam iti ṣoﾱaśaḥ stotrāṇāṃ ṣoﾱaśaḥ śastrāṇāṃ ṣoﾱaśabhir akṣarair ādatte ṣoﾱaśibhiḥ praṇauti ṣoﾱaśapadāṃ nividaṃ dadhāti tat ṣoﾱaśinaḥ ṣoﾱaśitvam ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'What is the sixteenness of the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>?' It is the sixteenth among the <s>stotra</s>s and the sixteenth among the <s>śastra</s>s; he takes it up with sixteen syllables, praises with sixteenfold elements, and sets down a <s>nivid</s> of sixteen words. That is the sixteenness of the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>.

children.text: dve vā akṣare atiricyete ṣoﾱaśino 'nuṣṭubham abhisaṃpannasya vāco vāva tau stanau satyānṛte vāva te ||
children.translated_text: Two syllables exceed when the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> has attained the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. These are precisely the two breasts of speech; they are truth and untruth.

children.text: avaty enaṃ satyaṃ nainam anṛtaṃ hinasti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Truth protects him; untruth does not injure him, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 123
gaurivītaṃ ṣoﾱaśi sāma kurvīta tejaskāmo brahmavarcasakāmas tejo vai brahmavarcasaṃ gaurivītaṃ tejasvī brahmavarcasī bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān gaurivītaṃ ṣoﾱaśi sāma kurute ||
children.translated_text: One who desires brilliance and desires brahminical lustre should make the <s>Gaurivīta</s> the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> <s>sāman</s>. Brilliance, indeed, is brahminical lustre; the <s>Gaurivīta</s> is brilliance. He becomes brilliant and possessed of brahminical lustre who, knowing thus, makes the <s>Gaurivīta</s> the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: nānadaṃ ṣoﾱaśi sāma kartavyam ity āhur indro vai vṛtrāya vajram udayacchat tam asmai prāharat tam abhyahanat so 'bhihato vyanadad yad vyanadat tan nānadaṃ sāmābhavat tan nānadasya nānadatvam abhrātṛvyaṃ vā etad bhrātṛvyahā sāma yan nānadam ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'The <s>Nānada</s> should be made the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> <s>sāman</s>.' <s>Indra</s> raised the vajra against <s>Vṛtra</s>, hurled it at him, and struck him. Struck, he cried out. Because he cried out, that became the <s>Nānada</s> <s>sāman</s>; that is the Nānada-ness of the <s>Nānada</s>. The <s>Nānada</s> is indeed a rival-removing and rival-slaying <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: abhrātṛvyo bhrātṛvyahā bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān nānadaṃ ṣoﾱaśi sāma kurute ||
children.translated_text: He becomes without a rival and a slayer of rivals who, knowing thus, makes the <s>Nānada</s> the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tad yadi nānadaṃ kuryur avihṛtaḥ ṣoﾱaśī śaṃstavyo 'vihṛtāsu hi tāsu stuvate yadi gaurivītaṃ vihṛtaḥ ṣoﾱaśī śaṃstavyo vihṛtāsu hi tāsu stuvate ||
children.translated_text: If they should use the <s>Nānada</s>, the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is to be recited without separation, for they chant it on those chants when they are unseparated. If they should use the <s>Gaurivīta</s>, the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is to be recited with separation, for they chant it on those chants when they are separated.

children.text: Chapter 124

athātaś chandāṃsy eva vyatiṣajaty ā tvā vahantu haraya upo ṣu śṛṇuhī gira iti gāyatrīś ca paṅktīś ca vyatiṣajati gāyatro vai puruṣaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavaḥ puruṣam eva tat paśubhir vyatiṣajati paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati yad u gāyatrī ca paṅktiś ca te dve anuṣṭubhau teno vāco rūpād anuṣṭubho rūpād vajrarūpān naiti ||
children.translated_text: Now, then, he interweaves the metres themselves. With 'May the bay steeds carry you hither' and 'Now listen to the songs,' he interweaves <s>Gāyatrī</s>s and <s>Paṅkti</s>s. Man is <s>Gāyatra</s>, and cattle are <s>Pāṅkta</s>; he thereby interweaves man with cattle and establishes him among cattle. Since <s>Gāyatrī</s> and <s>Paṅkti</s> are together two <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>s, by that he does not depart from the form of speech, from the form of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, from the form of the vajra.

children.text: yadindra pṛtanājye 'yaṃ te astu haryata ity uṣṇihaś ca bṛhatīś ca vyatiṣajaty auṣṇiho vai puruṣo bārhatāḥ paśavaḥ puruṣam eva tat paśubhir vyatiṣajati paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati yad uṣṇik ca bṛhatī ca te dve anuṣṭubhau teno vāco rūpād anuṣṭubho rūpād vajrarūpān naiti ||
children.translated_text: With 'When, O <s>Indra</s>, in the prize-winning battle' and 'Let this desirable one be yours,' he interweaves <s>Uṣṇih</s>s and <s>Bṛhatī</s>s. Man is <s>Auṣṇiha</s>, and cattle are <s>Bārhata</s>; he thereby interweaves man with cattle and establishes him among cattle. Since <s>Uṣṇih</s> and <s>Bṛhatī</s> are together two <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>s, by that he does not depart from the form of speech, from the form of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, from the form of the vajra.

children.text: ā dhūrṣu asmai brahman vīra brahmakṛtiṃ juṣāṇa iti dvipadāṃ ca triṣṭubhaṃ ca vyatiṣajati dvipād vai puruṣo vīryaṃ triṣṭup puruṣam eva tad vīryeṇa vyatiṣajati vīrye pratiṣṭhāpayati tasmāt puruṣo vīrye pratiṣṭhitaḥ sarveṣām paśūnāṃ vīryavattamo yad u dvipadā ca viṃśatyakṣarā triṣṭup ca te dve anuṣṭubhau teno vāco rūpād anuṣṭubho rūpād vajrarūpānnaiti ||
children.translated_text: With 'Upon the yoke-poles for him, O <s>Brahman</s>' and 'O hero, delighting in the work of sacred formulation,' he interweaves a <s>Dvipadā</s> and a <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. Man is two-footed, and virility is the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; he thereby interweaves man with virility and establishes him in virility. Therefore man, established in virility, is the most virile of all cattle. Since the <s>Dvipadā</s> has twenty syllables and the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> together are two <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>s, by that he does not depart from the form of speech, from the form of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, from the form of the vajra.

children.text: eṣa brahmā pra te mahe vidathe śaṃsiṣaṃ harī iti dvipadāś ca jagatīś ca vyatiṣajati dvipād vai puruṣo jāgatāḥ paśavaḥ puruṣam eva tat paśubhir vyatiṣajati paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati tasmāt puruṣaḥ paśuṣu pratiṣṭhito 'tti cainān adhi ca tiṣṭhati vaśe cāsya yad u dvipadā ca ṣoﾱaśākṣarā jagatī ca te dve anuṣṭubhau teno vāco rūpād anuṣṭubho rūpād vajrarūpān naiti ||
children.translated_text: With 'This <s>Brahman</s>' and 'For you, for the great assembly, I would proclaim the two bay steeds,' he interweaves <s>Dvipadā</s>s and <s>Jagatī</s>s. Man is two-footed, and cattle are <s>Jāgata</s>; he thereby interweaves man with cattle and establishes him among cattle. Therefore man, established among cattle, both eats them and stands over them, and they are under his control. Since the <s>Dvipadā</s> has sixteen syllables and the <s>Jagatī</s> together are two <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>s, by that he does not depart from the form of speech, from the form of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, from the form of the vajra.

children.text: trikadrukeṣu mahiṣo yavāśiram pro ṣv asmai puroratham ity aticchandasaḥ śaṃsati chandasāṃ vai yo raso 'tyakṣarat so 'ticchandasam abhy atyakṣarat tad aticchandaso 'ticchandastvaṃ sarvebhyo vā eṣa chandobhyaḥ saṃnirmito yat ṣoﾱaśī tad yad aticchandasaḥ śaṃsati sarvebhya evainaṃ tac chandobhyaḥ saṃnirmimīte ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Trikadruka</s> verses he recites the <s>Aticchandas</s> verse, 'The mighty one, mixed with barley, at the head of the chariot for him.' The essence of the metres, which overflowed, overflowed into the <s>Aticchandas</s>; that is the aticchandas-character of the <s>Aticchandas</s>. This <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is made up from all the metres. Therefore, when he recites an <s>Aticchandas</s> verse, he thereby constructs it from all the metres.

children.text: sarvebhyaś chandobhyaḥ saṃnirmitena ṣoﾱaśinā rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> constructed from all the metres, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 125
mahānāmnīnām upasargān upasṛjati ||
children.translated_text: He adds the introductory additions of the <s>Mahānāmnī</s> verses.

children.text: ayaṃ vai lokaḥ prathamā mahānāmny antarikṣaloko dvitīyāsau lokas tṛtīyā sarvebhyo vā eṣa lokebhyaḥ saṃnirmito yatṣoﾱaśī tad yan mahānāmnīnām upasargān upasṛjati sarvebhya evainaṃ tal lokebhyaḥ saṃnirmimīte ||
children.translated_text: This world is the first <s>Mahānāmnī</s>; the midspace-world is the second; that world yonder is the third. This <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is made up from all the worlds. Therefore, when he adds the introductory additions of the <s>Mahānāmnī</s> verses, he thereby constructs it from all the worlds.

children.text: sarvebhyo lokebhyaḥ saṃnirmitena ṣoﾱaśinā rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> constructed from all the worlds, who knows thus.

children.text: pra pra vas triṣṭubham iṣam arcata prārcata yo vyatīṁr aphāṇayad iti prajñātā anuṣṭubhaḥ śaṃsati tad yatheha ceha cāpathena caritvā panthānam paryaveyāt tādṛk tad yat prajñātā anuṣṭubhaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites recognized <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> verses, 'Sing forth, sing forth nourishment for you in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; sing forth him who made the overpassing one swell.' This is like someone who, having gone here and there by a wrong path, should finally reach the road. Such is it when he recites recognized <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> verses.

children.text: sa yo vyāpto gataśrīr iva manyetāvihṛtaṃ ṣoﾱaśinaṃ śaṃsayen nec chandasāṃ kṛcchrād avapadyā ity atha yaḥ pāpmānam apajighāṃsuḥ syād vihṛtaṃ ṣoﾱaśinaṃ śaṃsayed vyatiṣakta iva vai puruṣaḥ pāpmanā vyatiṣaktam evāsmai tat pāpmānaṃ śamalaṃ hanti ||
children.translated_text: If one should think himself encompassed, as if his prosperity had departed, he should have the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> recited without separation, lest he fall into distress among the metres. But if he should wish to strike away evil, he should have the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> recited in separated form. For a man is, as it were, entangled with evil; he thereby strikes away from him that entangled evil, that impurity.

children.text: apa pāpmānaṃ hate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He strikes away evil, who knows thus.

children.text: ud yad bradhnasya viṣṭapam ity uttamayā paridadhāti svargo vai loko bradhnasya viṣṭapam svargam eva tal lokaṃ yajamānaṃ gamayati ||
children.translated_text: With the final verse, 'When the height of the ruddy one rises up,' he encloses it. The height of the ruddy one is the heavenly world. He thereby causes the sacrificer to go to that heavenly world.

children.text: apāḥ pūrveṣāṃ harivaḥ sutānām iti yajati ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices with the verse, 'You have drunk of the former pressed draughts, O bay-horsed one.'

children.text: sarvebhyo vā eṣa savanebhyaḥ saṃnirmito yat ṣoﾱaśī tad yad apāḥ pūrveṣāṃ harivaḥ sutānām iti yajati pītavad vai prātaḥsavanam prātaḥsavanād evainaṃ tat saṃnirmimīte ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is made up from all the pressings. Therefore, when he sacrifices with the verse, 'You have drunk of the former pressed draughts, O bay-horsed one,' the morning pressing has indeed the character of being drunk; he thereby constructs it from the morning pressing.

children.text: atho idaṃ savanaṃ kevalaṃ ta iti mādhyaṃdinaṃ vai savanaṃ kevalam mādhyaṃdinād evainaṃ tat savanāt saṃnirmimīte ||
children.translated_text: And with 'But this pressing is yours alone': the midday pressing is indeed alone; he thereby constructs it from the midday pressing.

children.text: mamaddhi somam madhumantam indreti madvad vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ tṛtīyasavanād evainaṃ tat saṃnirmimīte ||
children.translated_text: With 'Drink the sweet soma, O <s>Indra</s>': the third pressing indeed has the character of intoxication; he thereby constructs it from the third pressing.

children.text: satrā vṛṣañ jaṭhara ā vṛṣasveti vṛṣaṇvad vai ṣoﾱaśino rūpaṃ sarvebhyo vā eṣa savanebhyaḥ saṃnirmito yat ṣoﾱaśī tad yad apāḥ pūrveṣāṃ harivaḥ sutānām iti yajati sarvebhya evainaṃ tat savanebhyaḥ saṃnirmimīte ||
children.translated_text: With 'Together, O bull, swell in your belly': the form of the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> indeed has the character of the bull. This <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is made up from all the pressings. Therefore, when he sacrifices with 'You have drunk of the former pressed draughts, O bay-horsed one,' he thereby constructs it from all the pressings.

children.text: sarvebhyaḥ savanebhyaḥ saṃnirmitena ṣoﾱaśinā rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> constructed from all the pressings, who knows thus.

children.text: mahānāmnīnām pañcākṣarān upasargān upasṛjaty ekādaśākṣareṣu pādeṣu sarvebhyo vā eṣa chandobhyaḥ saṃnirmito yat ṣoﾱaśī tad yan mahānāmnīnām pañcākṣarān upasargān upasṛjaty ekādaśākṣareṣu pādeṣu sarvebhya evainaṃ tac chandobhyaḥ saṃnirmimīte ||
children.translated_text: He adds five-syllable introductory additions of the <s>Mahānāmnī</s> verses in eleven-syllable feet. This <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> is made up from all the metres. Therefore, when he adds five-syllable introductory additions of the <s>Mahānāmnī</s> verses in eleven-syllable feet, he thereby constructs it from all the metres.

children.text: sarvebhyaś chandobhyaḥ saṃnirmitena ṣoﾱaśinā rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers with the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s> constructed from all the metres, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 126

ahar vai devā aśrayanta rātrīm asurās te samāvadvīryā evāsan na vyāvartanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaś cāhaṃ cemān ito 'surān rātrīm anv aveṣyāva iti sa deveṣu na pratyavindad abibhayū rātres tamaso mṛtyos tasmāddhāpy etarhi naktaṃ yāvanmātram ivaivāpakramya bibheti tama iva hi rātrir mṛtyur iva ||
children.translated_text: The gods took refuge in the day, the <s>Asuras</s> in the night. They were just equal in strength and were not separated. Then <s>Indra</s> said, 'Who and I will follow these <s>Asuras</s> from here into the night?' He found no one among the gods; they were afraid of night, of darkness, of death. Therefore even now, at night, after going only a little way off, one becomes afraid, for night is like darkness, like death.

children.text: taṃ vai chandāṃsy evānvavāyaṃs taṃ yacchandāṃsy evānvavāyaṃstasmād indraścaiva chandāṃsi ca rātrīṃ vahanti na nivicchasyate na puroruṅ na dhāyyā nānyā devatendraśca hyevachandāṃsi ca rātrīṃ vahanti ||
children.translated_text: The metres alone followed him. Because the metres alone followed him, therefore <s>Indra</s> and the metres carry the night. No <s>nivic</s>, no <s>puroruc</s>, no <s>dhāyyā</s>, and no other deity is assigned, for <s>Indra</s> and the metres alone carry the night.

children.text: tān vai paryāyair eva paryāyam anudanta yat paryāyaiḥ paryāyam anudanta tat paryāyāṇām paryāyatvam ||
children.translated_text: They drove them from round to round by means of the rounds. Because they drove them from round to round by means of the rounds, that is the round-character of the rounds.

children.text: tān vai prathamenaiva paryāyeṇa pūrvarātrād anudanta madhyamena madhyarātrād uttamenāpararātrāt ||
children.translated_text: By the first round they drove them from the early night, by the middle one from midnight, and by the last one from the latter part of the night.

children.text: api śarvaryā anusmasīty abruvann apiśarvarāṇi khalu vā etāni chandāṃsīti ha smāhaitāni hīndraṃ rātres tamaso mṛtyor bibhyatam atyapārayaṃs tad apiśarvarāṇām apiśarvaratvam ||
children.translated_text: They said, 'We are after even the night.' These metres, they say, are indeed <s>Apiśarvara</s> verses, for they carried <s>Indra</s>, who was afraid of night, darkness, and death, across beyond them. That is the apiśarvara-character of the <s>Apiśarvara</s> verses.

children.text: Chapter 127
pāntam ā vo andhasa ity andhasvatyānuṣṭubhā rātrīm pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> verse containing the word andhas, 'Drink for yourselves of the soma-juice,' he enters upon the night.

children.text: ānuṣṭubhī vai rātrir etad rātrirūpam ||
children.translated_text: The night is indeed <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; this is the form of night.

children.text: andhasvatyaḥ pītavatyo madvatyas triṣṭubho yājyā bhavanty abhirūpā yad yajñe 'bhirūpaṃ tat samṛddham ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> offering-verses contain andhas, have the character of being drunk, and have the character of intoxication; they are fitting. What is fitting in the sacrifice is successful.

children.text: prathamena paryāyeṇa stuvate prathamāny eva padāni punar ādadate yad evaiṣām aśvā gāva āsaṃs tad evaiṣāṃ tenādadate ||
children.translated_text: They chant with the first round; they take up the first words again. Whatever horses and cattle belonged to them, by that they take them back from them.

children.text: madhyamena paryāyeṇa stuvate madhyamāny eva padāni punar ādadate yad evaiṣām manorathā āsaṃs tad evaiṣāṃ tenādadate ||
children.translated_text: They praise with the middle round; they take up again the middle words. Whatever desires of theirs there had been, those very desires they thereby take up for them.

children.text: uttamena paryāyeṇa stuvata uttamāny eva padāni punar ādadate yad evaiṣāṃ vāso hiraṇyam maṇir adhyātmam āsīt tad evaiṣāṃ tenādadate ||
children.translated_text: They praise with the highest round; they take up again the highest words. Whatever clothing, gold, gem, and personal possession of theirs there had been, that very thing they thereby take up for them.

children.text: ā dviṣato vasu datte nir enam ebhyaḥ sarvebhyo lokebhyo nudate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He takes wealth from the hating enemy and drives him away from all these worlds, who knows thus.

children.text: pavamānavad ahar ity āhur na rātriḥ pavamānavatī katham ubhe pavamānavatī bhavataḥ kena te samāvadbhājau bhavata iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "The day has <s>pavamāna</s> (purifying Soma chants), but the night is not furnished with <s>pavamāna</s>; how do both become furnished with <s>pavamāna</s>? By what do the two have equal shares?"

children.text: yad evendrāya madvane sutam idaṃ vaso sutam andha idaṃ hy anv ojasā sutam iti stuvanti ca śaṃsanti ca tena rātriḥ pavamānavatī tenobhe pavamānavatī bhavatas tena te samāvadbhājau bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that they both chant and recite, "Pressed for <s>Indra</s>, for exhilaration," "This, O <s>Vasu</s>, has been pressed," and "This draught has indeed been pressed with power," by that the night is furnished with <s>pavamāna</s>; by that both are furnished with <s>pavamāna</s>; by that the two have equal shares.

children.text: pañcadaśastotram ahar ity āhur na rātriḥ pañcadaśastotrā katham ubhe pañcadaśastotre bhavataḥ kena te samāvadbhājau bhavata iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "The day has fifteenfold <s>stotra</s>s (chants), but the night does not have fifteenfold <s>stotra</s>s; how do both become furnished with fifteenfold <s>stotra</s>s? By what do the two have equal shares?"

children.text: dvādaśa stotrāṇy apiśarvarāṇi tisṛbhir devatābhiḥ saṃdhinā rāthaṃtareṇa stuvate tena rātriḥ pañcadaśastotrā tenobhe pañcadaśastotre bhavatas tena te samāvadbhājau bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are twelve <s>stotra</s>s belonging to the whole night; with three deities, at the junction, they praise with the <s>Rāthaṃtara</s>. By that the night has fifteenfold <s>stotra</s>s; by that both have fifteenfold <s>stotra</s>s; by that the two have equal shares.

children.text: parimitaṃ stuvanty aparimitam anuśaṃsati parimitaṃ vai bhūtam aparimitam bhavyam aparimitasyāvaruddhyā iti ||
children.translated_text: They chant what is limited, and he recites in response what is unlimited. The past is limited, while the future is unlimited; this is for the securing of the unlimited.

children.text: atiśaṃsati stotram ati vai prajātmānam ati paśavas tad yat stotram atiśaṃsati yad evāsyāty ātmānaṃ tad evāsyaitenāvarunddhe 'varunddhe ||
children.translated_text: He recites beyond the <s>stotra</s>. Offspring and cattle are indeed beyond one's own self. Thus, when he recites beyond the <s>stotra</s>, whatever is beyond his self, that he thereby secures for him; he secures it.

children.text: Chapter 128

prajāpatir vai somāya rājñe duhitaram prāyacchat sūryāṃ sāvitrīṃ tasyai sarve devā varā āgacchaṃs tasyā etat sahasraṃ vahatum anvākarod yad etad āśvinam ity ācakṣate 'nāśvinaṃ haiva tad yad arvāksahasraṃ tasmāt tat sahasraṃ vaiva śaṃsed bhūyo vā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> gave his daughter, <s>Sūryā Sāvitrī</s>, to King <s>Soma</s>. All the gods came to her as suitors. For her he prescribed this thousand as the bridal gift, namely what they call the <s>Āśvina</s>. What is short of a thousand is indeed not <s>Āśvina</s>. Therefore he should recite a thousand, or more than that.

children.text: prāśya ghṛtaṃ śaṃsed yathā ha vā idam ano vā ratho vākto vartata evaṃ haivākto vartate ||
children.translated_text: Having tasted ghee, he should recite. Just as here a wagon or a chariot, when greased, keeps rolling, so indeed, when greased, it keeps rolling.

children.text: śakunir ivotpatiṣyann āhvayīta ||
children.translated_text: He should call out like a bird about to fly up.

children.text: tasmin devā na samajānata mamedam astu mamedam astv iti te saṃjānānā abruvann ājim asyāyāmahai sa yo na ujjeṣyati tasyedam bhaviṣyatīti te 'gner evādhi gṛhapater ādityaṃ kāṣṭhām akurvata tasmād āgneyī pratipad bhavaty āśvinasyāgnir hotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājeti ||
children.translated_text: The gods did not agree about her, each saying, "Let this be mine, let this be mine." Coming to an agreement, they said, "Let us run a race for her; whichever of us wins, this shall belong to him." From <s>Agni</s> the householder onward they made the <s>Āditya</s> the goal. Therefore the opening verse of the <s>Āśvina</s> is addressed to <s>Agni</s>: "<s>Agni</s> is the <s>hotṛ</s>, the householder; he is king."

children.text: taddhaika āhur agnim manye pitaram agnim āpim ity etayā pratipadyeta ||
children.translated_text: Some say about this that he should begin with this verse: "I regard <s>Agni</s> as father, <s>Agni</s> as kinsman."

children.text: divi śukraṃ yajataṃ sūryasyeti prathamayaiva ṛcā kāṣṭhām āpnotīti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "With the very first verse, 'The bright, worshipful one of the sun in heaven,' he reaches the goal."

children.text: tattan nādṛtyaṃ ya enaṃ tatra brūyād agnim agnim iti vai pratyapādy agnim āpatsyatīti śaśvat tathā syāt ||
children.translated_text: That is not to be heeded. If someone should say of him there, "He has been set back to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Agni</s>; he will come to <s>Agni</s>," it would always be so.

children.text: tasmād agnir hotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājety etayaiva pratipadyeta gṛhapativatī prajātimatī śāntā sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he should begin with this very verse, "<s>Agni</s> is the <s>hotṛ</s>, the householder; he is king." It contains the householder, contains progeny, is peaceful, and possesses the full span of life, for the sake of the full span of life.

children.text: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He attains the full span of life, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 129

tāsāṃ vai devatānām ājiṃ dhāvantīnām abhisṛṣṭānām agnir mukham prathamaḥ pratyapadyata tam aśvināv anvāgacchatāṃ tam abrūtām apodihy āvāṃ vā idaṃ jeṣyāva iti sa tathety abravīt tasya vai mamehāpyastv iti tatheti tasmā apy atrākurutāṃ tasmād āgneyam āśvine śasyate ||
children.translated_text: When those deities had been released and were running the race, <s>Agni</s> first reached the front, the opening. The <s>Aśvins</s> came up after him. They said to him, "Move aside; we two shall win this." He said, "So be it. But let there be a share for me here too." "So be it," they said, and they made a share for him there too. Therefore an <s>Āgneya</s> (Agni-addressed verse) is recited in the <s>Āśvina</s>.

children.text: tā uṣasam anvāgacchatāṃ tām abrūtām apodihy āvāṃ vā idaṃ jeṣyāva iti sā tathety abravīt tasyai vai mamehāpyastv iti tatheti tasyā apy atrākurutāṃ tasmād uṣasyam āśvine śasyate ||
children.translated_text: They came up after <s>Uṣas</s>. They said to her, "Move aside; we two shall win this." She said, "So be it. But let there be a share for me here too." "So be it," they said, and they made a share for her there too. Therefore an <s>Uṣasya</s> (Dawn-addressed verse) is recited in the <s>Āśvina</s>.

children.text: tāv indram anvāgacchatāṃ tam abrūtām āvāṃ vā idam maghavañ jeṣyāva iti na ha taṃ dadhṛṣatur apodihīti vaktuṃ sa tathety abravīt tasya vai mamehāpyastv iti tatheti tasmā apy atrākurutāṃ tasmād aindram āśvine śasyate ||
children.translated_text: They came up after <s>Indra</s>. They said to him, "<s>Maghavan</s>, we two shall win this." They did not dare say to him, "Move aside." He said, "So be it. But let there be a share for me here too." "So be it," they said, and they made a share for him there too. Therefore an <s>Aindra</s> (Indra-addressed verse) is recited in the <s>Āśvina</s>.

children.text: tad aśvinā udajayatām aśvināv āśnuvātāṃ yad aśvinā udajayatām aśvināv āśnuvātāṃ tasmād etad āśvinam ity ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Aśvins</s> won it; the <s>Aśvins</s> obtained it. Because the <s>Aśvins</s> won it and the <s>Aśvins</s> obtained it, therefore this is called the <s>Āśvina</s>.

children.text: aśnute yad yat kāmayate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He obtains whatever he desires, who knows thus.

children.text: tad āhur yacchasyata āgneyaṃ śasyata uṣasyam śasyata aindram atha kasmād etad āśvinam ity ācakṣata ity aśvinau hi tad udajayatām aśvināv āśnuvātāṃ yad aśvinā udajayatām aśvināv āśnuvātāṃ tasmād etad āśvinam ity ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since an <s>Āgneya</s> is recited, an <s>Uṣasya</s> is recited, and an <s>Aindra</s> is recited, why then is this called the <s>Āśvina</s>?" Because the <s>Aśvins</s> won it and the <s>Aśvins</s> obtained it. Because the <s>Aśvins</s> won it and the <s>Aśvins</s> obtained it, therefore this is called the <s>Āśvina</s>.

children.text: aśnute yad yat kāmayate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He obtains whatever he desires, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 130
aśvatarīrathenāgnir ājim adhāvat tāsām prājamāno yonim akūﾱayat tasmāt tā na vijāyante ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> ran the race with a mule-mare chariot. As he drove them forward, he damaged their womb; therefore they do not give birth.

children.text: gobhir aruṇair uṣā ājim adhāvat tasmād uṣasy āgatāyām aruṇam ivaiva prabhāty uṣaso rūpam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uṣas</s> ran the race with reddish cows; therefore, when <s>Uṣas</s> has arrived, it shines as if reddish: that is the form of <s>Uṣas</s>.

children.text: aśvarathenendra ājim adhāvat tasmāt sa uccairghoṣa upabdimān kṣatrasya rūpam aindro hi sa ||
children.translated_text: With a horse-chariot <s>Indra</s> ran the race. Therefore it is loud-voiced and clamorous, the form of <s>kṣatra</s> (royal power), for it belongs to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: gardabharathenāśvinā udajayatām aśvināv āśnuvātāṃ yad aśvinā udajayatām aśvināv āśnuvātāṃ tasmāt sa sṛtajavo dugdhadohaḥ sarveṣām etarhi vāhanānām anāśiṣṭho retasas tv asya vīryaṃ nāharatāṃ tasmāt sa dviretā vājī ||
children.translated_text: With a donkey-chariot the two <s>Aśvins</s> won; the two <s>Aśvins</s> attained their goal. Because the two <s>Aśvins</s> won and attained their goal, therefore it is of released speed and milk-yielding, yet among all vehicles now the least blessed. But they did not carry off the strength of its seed; therefore it is a two-seeded racer.

children.text: tad āhuḥ sapta sauryāṇi chandāṃsi śaṃsed yathaivāgneyaṃ yathoṣasyaṃ yathāśvinaṃ sapta vai devalokāḥ sarveṣu devalokeṣu rādhnotīti ||
children.translated_text: They say: one should recite seven solar metres, just as there is an Agni verse, a Dawn verse, and an Aśvin verse. There are indeed seven divine worlds; thereby he prospers in all the divine worlds.

children.text: tattan nādṛtyaṃ trīṇy eva śaṃset trayo vā ime trivṛto lokā eṣām eva lokānām abhijityai ||
children.translated_text: That is not to be heeded. He should recite only three; for these three worlds are threefold, and this is for the conquest of these very worlds.

children.text: tad āhur ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam iti sauryāṇi pratipadyeteti ||
children.translated_text: They say: he should begin the solar verses with 'Up has arisen that <s>Jātavedas</s>.'

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyaṃ yathaiva gatvā kāṣṭhām aparādhnuyāt tādṛk tat ||
children.translated_text: That is not to be heeded. It would be just as if, having gone, one missed the goal-post.

children.text: sūryo no divas pātv ity etenaiva pratipadyeta yathaiva gatvā kāṣṭhām abhipadyeta tādṛk tat ||
children.translated_text: He should begin with this verse, 'May <s>Sūrya</s> protect us from heaven.' That is just as if, having gone, one reached the goal-post.

children.text: ud u tyaṃ jātavedasam iti dvitīyaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites second, 'Up has arisen that <s>Jātavedas</s>.'

children.text: citraṃ devānām ud agād anīkam iti traiṣṭubham asau vāva citraṃ devānām udeti tasmād etacchaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, 'The bright face of the gods has arisen.' That yonder one indeed rises as the bright face of the gods; therefore he recites this.

children.text: namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣasa iti jāgataṃ tadvāśīḥpadam āśiṣam evaitenāśāsta ātmane ca yajamānāya ca ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Jagatī</s>, 'Homage to the eye of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.' That is a place of blessing; with it he asks blessing for himself and for the sacrificer.

children.text: Chapter 131
tad āhuḥ sūryo nātiśasyo bṛhatī nātiśasyā yat sūryam atiśaṃsed brahmavarcasam atipadyeta yad bṛhatīm atiśaṃset prāṇān atipadyeteti ||
children.translated_text: They say: <s>Sūrya</s> must not be over-recited, and the <s>Bṛhatī</s> must not be over-recited. If he were to over-recite <s>Sūrya</s>, he would overstep <s>brahmavarcasa</s> (sacred lustre); if he were to over-recite the <s>Bṛhatī</s>, he would overstep the breaths.

children.text: indra kratuṃ na ā bharety aindram pragāthaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Aindra</s> pragātha, 'O <s>Indra</s>, bring us inspired power.'

children.text: śikṣā ṇo asmin puruhūta yāmani jīvā jyotir aśīmahīti ||
children.translated_text: 'Teach us in this course, O much-invoked one; may we, living, attain the light.'

children.text: asau vāva jyotis tena sūryaṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: That yonder one indeed is the light; by this he does not over-recite <s>Sūrya</s>.

children.text: yad u bārhataḥ pragāthas tena bṛhatīṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And since it is a <s>Bārhata</s> pragātha, by this he does not over-recite the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.

children.text: abhi tvā śūra nonuma iti rāthaṃtarīṃ yoniṃ śaṃsati rāthaṃtareṇa vai saṃdhināśvināya stuvate tad yad rāthaṃtarīṃ yoniṃ śaṃsati rathaṃtarasyaiva sayonitvāya ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Rāthaṃtarī</s> source-verse, 'To you, O hero, we call out.' With a <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> connection they chant for the <s>Aśvin</s> rite; therefore, when he recites a <s>Rāthaṃtarī</s> source-verse, it is so that the <s>Rathantara</s> may have its own source.

children.text: īśānam asya jagataḥ svardṛśam ity asau vāva svardṛk tena sūryaṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: 'The lord of this moving world, seeing heaven'--that yonder one indeed sees heaven; by this he does not over-recite <s>Sūrya</s>.

children.text: yad u bārhataḥ pragāthas tena bṛhatīṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And since it is a <s>Bārhata</s> pragātha, by this he does not over-recite the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.

children.text: bahavaḥ sūracakṣasa iti maitrāvaruṇam pragāthaṃ śaṃsaty ahar vai mitro rātrir varuṇa ubhe vā eṣo 'horātre ārabhate yo 'tirātram upaiti tad yan maitrāvaruṇam pragāthaṃ śaṃsaty ahorātrayor evainaṃ tat pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> pragātha, 'Many are sun-eyed.' Day is <s>Mitra</s>, night is <s>Varuṇa</s>. The one who enters upon the <s>Atirātra</s> undertakes both, day and night. Therefore, when he recites the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> pragātha, he thereby establishes him in day and night.

children.text: sūracakṣasa iti tena sūryaṃ nātiśaṃsati yad u bārhataḥ pragāthas tena bṛhatīṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: 'Sun-eyed'--by this he does not over-recite <s>Sūrya</s>; and since it is a <s>Bārhata</s> pragātha, by this he does not over-recite the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.

children.text: mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca nas te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuveti dyāvāpṛthivīye śaṃsati dyāvāpṛthivī vai pratiṣṭhe iyam eveha pratiṣṭhāsāv amutra tad yad dyāvāpṛthivīye śaṃsati pratiṣṭhayor evainaṃ tat pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites verses belonging to Heaven and Earth: 'Great heaven and earth are ours, for these two, heaven and earth, are all-beneficent.' Heaven and earth are indeed the two foundations: this one is the foundation here, that one the foundation there. Therefore, when he recites verses belonging to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>, he thereby establishes him upon the two foundations.

children.text: devo devī dharmaṇā sūryaḥ śucir iti tena sūryaṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: 'The god <s>Sūrya</s>, pure by the law, with the goddess'--by this he does not over-recite <s>Sūrya</s>.

children.text: yad u gāyatrī ca jagatī ca te dve bṛhatyau tena bṛhatīṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And since they are a <s>Gāyatrī</s> and a <s>Jagatī</s>, and those two make two <s>Bṛhatī</s>s, by this he does not over-recite the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.

children.text: viśvasya devī mṛcayasya janmano na yā roṣāti na grabhad iti dvipadām śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the two-footed verse, 'Of the goddess, of every vulnerable birth, whom neither rage nor seizure harms.'

children.text: citaidham uktham iti ha sma vā etad ācakṣate yad etad āśvinaṃ nirṛtir ha sma pāśiny upāste yadaiva hotā paridhāsyaty atha pāśān pratimokṣyāmīti tato vā etām bṛhaspatir dvipadām apaśyan na yā roṣāti na grabhad iti tayā nirṛtyāḥ pāśinyā adharācaḥ pāśān apāsyat tad yad etāṃ dvipadāṃ hotā śaṃsati nirṛtyā eva tat pāśinyā adharācaḥ pāśān apāsyati svasty eva hotonmucyate sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya ||
children.translated_text: They used to call this <s>Aśvina</s> uktha 'Citaidha.' <s>Nirṛti</s>, bearing a noose, sits near it, thinking, 'When the <s>Hotṛ</s> is about to conclude, then I will fasten the nooses.' Then <s>Bṛhaspati</s> saw this two-footed verse, 'whom neither rage nor seizure harms.' With it he cast downward the nooses of noose-bearing <s>Nirṛti</s>. Therefore, when the <s>Hotṛ</s> recites this two-footed verse, he casts downward the nooses of noose-bearing <s>Nirṛti</s>; the <s>Hotṛ</s> is released in safety, for the full span of life and for full-livedness.

children.text: sarvam āyur eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus reaches the full span of life.

children.text: mṛcayasya janmana ity asau vāva marcayatīva tena sūryaṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: 'Of the vulnerable birth'--that yonder one indeed seems to scorch; by this he does not over-recite <s>Sūrya</s>.

children.text: yad u dvipadā puruṣachandasaṃ sā sarvāṇi chandāṃsy abhyāptā tena bṛhatīṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And since the two-footed verse is a human metre and has encompassed all the metres, by this he does not over-recite the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.

children.text: Chapter 132
brāhmaṇaspatyayā paridadhāti brahma vai bṛhaspatir brahmaṇy evainaṃ tad antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He concludes with a verse addressed to <s>Brāhmaṇaspati</s>. <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is indeed <s>brahman</s>; thereby, at the end, he establishes him in <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: evā pitre viśvadevāya vṛṣṇa ity etayā paridadhyāt prajākāmaḥ paśukāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who desires offspring and desires cattle should conclude with this verse: 'Thus to the father, to the all-divine, the bull.'

children.text: bṛhaspate suprajā vīravanta iti prajayā vai suprajā vīravān ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, rich in good offspring, rich in heroes'--through offspring one is indeed rich in good offspring and rich in heroes.

children.text: vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'May we be lords of riches.'

children.text: prajāvān paśumān rayimān vīravān bhavati yatraivaṃ vidvān etayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of offspring, possessed of cattle, possessed of wealth, and possessed of heroes, when, knowing thus, he concludes with this verse.
