children.text: bṛhaspate ati yad aryo arhād ity etayā paridadhyāt tejaskāmo brahmavarcasakāmo 'tīva vānyān brahmavarcasam arhati ||
children.translated_text: One who desires brilliance and desires <s>brahmavarcasa</s> should conclude with this verse: 'O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, when you surpassed what the stranger deserves.' For he greatly surpasses others in <s>brahmavarcasa</s>.

children.text: dyumad iti dyumad iva vai brahmavarcasaṃ vibhātīti vīva vai brahmavarcasam bhāti ||
children.translated_text: 'Luminous'--for <s>brahmavarcasa</s> shines as if luminous; indeed <s>brahmavarcasa</s> shines distinctly.

children.text: yad dīdayac chavasa ṛtaprajāteti dīdāyeva vai brahmavarcasam ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "what shone with might, born of <s>ṛta</s>," <s>brahmavarcas</s> (sacred brilliance) indeed shines.

children.text: tad asmāsu draviṇaṃ dhehi citram iti citram iva vai brahmavarcasam ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "Place in us that wondrous wealth," <s>brahmavarcas</s> is indeed, as it were, wondrous.

children.text: brahmavarcasī brahmayaśasī bhavati yatraivaṃ vidvān etayā paridadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of <s>brahmavarcas</s> and of <s>brahmayaśas</s> (the renown of sacred power), who, knowing thus, encloses with this verse.

children.text: tasmād evaṃ vidvān etayaiva paridadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one who knows thus should enclose with this very verse.

children.text: brāhmaṇaspatyā tena sūryaṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>Brāhmaṇaspatya</s> verse he thereby does not over-recite the <s>Sūrya</s> verse.

children.text: yad u triṣṭubhaṃ triḥ śaṃsati sā sarvāṇi chandāṃsy abhyāptā tena bṛhatīṃ nātiśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: And since he recites the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> three times, it has reached all the metres; thereby he does not over-recite the <s>Bṛhatī</s>.

children.text: gāyatryā ca triṣṭubhā ca vaṣaṭkuryāt ||
children.translated_text: He should make the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: brahma vai gāyatrī vīryam triṣṭub brahmaṇaiva tad vīryaṃ saṃdadhāti ||
children.translated_text: For the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>brahman</s> (sacred formulation), and the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is vigor; by <s>brahman</s> he thereby joins vigor to it.

children.text: brahmavarcasī brahmayaśasī vīryavān bhavati yatraivaṃ vidvān gāyatryā ca triṣṭubhā ca vaṣaṭkaroti ||
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of <s>brahmavarcas</s>, possessed of <s>brahmayaśas</s>, and vigorous, who, knowing thus, makes the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: aśvinā vāyunā yuvaṃ sudakṣobhā pibatam aśvineti ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Aśvins</s>, together with <s>Vāyu</s>, you two of good skill, drink, O <s>Aśvins</s>."

children.text: gāyatryā ca virājā ca vaṣaṭkuryād brahma vai gāyatry annaṃ virāḍ brahmaṇaiva tad annādyaṃ saṃdadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He should make the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the <s>Virāj</s>. For the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>brahman</s>, and the <s>Virāj</s> is food; by <s>brahman</s> he thereby joins food and eating to it.

children.text: brahmavarcasī brahmayaśasī bhavati brahmādyam annam atti yatraivaṃ vidvān gāyatryā ca virājā ca vaṣaṭkaroti ||
children.translated_text: He becomes possessed of <s>brahmavarcas</s> and possessed of <s>brahmayaśas</s>; he eats food fit for sacred power, who, knowing thus, makes the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the <s>Virāj</s>.

children.text: tasmād evaṃ vidvān gāyatryā caiva virājā ca vaṣaṭkuryāt pra vām andhāṃsi madyāny asthur ubhā pibatam aśvinety etābhyām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one who knows thus should make the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the <s>Virāj</s>, with these two verses: "Your intoxicating draughts have gone forth; drink both of them, O <s>Aśvins</s>."

children.text: Chapter 133
caturviṃśam etad ahar upayanty ārambhaṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: They enter upon this twenty-fourth day, the day of beginning.

children.text: etena vai saṃvatsaram ārabhanta etena stomāṃś ca chandāṃsi caitena sarvā devatā anārabdhaṃ vai tac chando 'nārabdhā sā devatā yad etasminn ahani nārabhante tad ārambhaṇīyasyārambhaṇīyatvam ||
children.translated_text: By this, indeed, they began the year, and by this the <s>stoma</s>s, the metres, and all the deities. That metre is unbegun, that deity is unbegun, which they do not begin on this day. That is why the day of beginning has its character as the day of beginning.

children.text: caturviṃśaḥ stomo bhavati tac caturviṃśasya caturviṃśatvam ||
children.translated_text: There is the twenty-fourfold <s>stoma</s>; that is the twenty-fourness of the twenty-fourfold.

children.text: caturviṃśatir vā ardhamāsā ardhamāsaśa eva tat saṃvatsaram ārabhante ||
children.translated_text: There are twenty-four half-months; half-month by half-month they thereby begin the year.

children.text: ukthyo bhavati paśavo vā ukthāni paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: It is an <s>Ukthya</s>. The <s>uktha</s>s are cattle; it is for the winning of cattle.

children.text: tasya pañcadaśa stotrāṇi bhavanti pañcadaśa śastrāni sa māso māsaśa eva tat saṃvatsaram ārabhante ||
children.translated_text: It has fifteen <s>stotra</s>s and fifteen <s>śastra</s>s. That is the month; month by month they thereby begin the year.

children.text: tasya ṣaṣṭiś ca trīṇi ca śatāni stotriyās tāvanti saṃvatsarasyāhāny ahaśśa eva tat saṃvatsaram ārabhante ||
children.translated_text: It has three hundred and sixty <s>stotriyā</s> verses; so many are the days of the year. Day by day they thereby begin the year.

children.text: agniṣṭoma etad ahaḥ syād ity āhur agniṣṭomo vai saṃvatsaro na vā etad anyo 'gniṣṭomād ahar dādhāra na vivyāceti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "This day should be an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, for the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> is the year; no other day than an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> has held or encompassed this."

children.text: sa yady agniṣṭomaḥ syād aṣṭācatvāriṃśās trayaḥ pavamānāḥ syuś caturviṃśānītarāṇi stotrāṇi tad u ṣaṣṭiś caiva trīṇi ca śatāni stotriyās tāvanti saṃvatsarasyāhāny ahaśśa eva tat saṃvatsaram ārabhante ||
children.translated_text: If it were an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, the three <s>pavamāna</s>s would be forty-eightfold, and the other <s>stotra</s>s twenty-fourfold; thus there would be three hundred and sixty <s>stotriyā</s> verses, so many as the days of the year. Day by day they thereby begin the year.

children.text: ukthya eva syāt paśusamṛddho yajñaḥ paśusamṛddhaṃ satraṃ sarvāṇi caturviṃśāni stotrāṇi pratyakṣāddhyetad ahaś caturviṃśaṃ tasmād ukthya eva syāt ||
children.translated_text: But it should be an <s>Ukthya</s> alone: the sacrifice is rich in cattle, the <s>satra</s> is rich in cattle, and all the <s>stotra</s>s are twenty-fourfold. This day is visibly the twenty-fourth; therefore it should be an <s>Ukthya</s> alone.

children.text: Chapter 134
bṛhadrathaṃtare sāmanī bhavata ete vai yajñasya nāvau sampāriṇyau yad bṛhadrathaṃtare tābhyām eva tat saṃvatsaraṃ taranti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathaṃtara</s> sāmans are used. These two, the <s>Bṛhat</s> and the <s>Rathaṃtara</s>, are the two boats of the sacrifice that carry one fully across; by them they cross the year.

children.text: pādau vai bṛhadrathaṃtare śira etad ahaḥ pādābhyām eva tacchriyaṃ śiro 'bhyāyanti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathaṃtara</s> are the feet, and this day is the head. With the feet they thereby reach the head, the splendor.

children.text: pakṣau vai bṛhadrathaṃtare śira etad ahaḥ pakṣābhyām eva tacchriyaṃ śiro 'bhyāyuvate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathaṃtara</s> are the two wings, and this day is the head. With the wings they thereby reach the head, the splendor.

children.text: te ubhe na samavasṛjye ya ubhe samavasṛjeyur yathaiva chinnā naur bandhanāt tīraṃ tīram ṛcchantī plavetaivam eva te satriṇas tīraṃ tīram ṛcchantaḥ plaveran ya ubhe samavasṛjeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should not let both of them go. If they were to let both go, then, just as a cut boat, freed from its fastening and reaching one bank after another, would drift, so those <s>sattra</s>-performers, reaching one bank after another, would drift, if they were to let both go.

children.text: tad yadi rathaṃtaram avasṛjeyur bṛhataivobhe anavasṛṣṭe atha yadi bṛhad avasṛjeyū rathaṃtareṇaivobhe anavasṛṣṭe ||
children.translated_text: If they were to let the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> go, both would remain unlet-go by means of the <s>Bṛhat</s>; but if they were to let the <s>Bṛhat</s> go, both would remain unlet-go by means of the <s>Rathaṃtara</s>.

children.text: yad vai rathaṃtaraṃ tad vairūpaṃ yad bṛhat tad vairājam yad rathaṃtaraṃ tacchākvaraṃ yad bṛhat tad raivatam evam ete ubhe anavasṛṣṭe bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is <s>Rathaṃtara</s> is <s>Vairūpa</s>; what is <s>Bṛhat</s> is <s>Vairāja</s>. What is <s>Rathaṃtara</s> is <s>Śākvara</s>; what is <s>Bṛhat</s> is <s>Raivata</s>. Thus these two remain unlet-go.

children.text: ye vā evaṃ vidvāṃsa etad ahar upayanty āptvā vai te 'haśśaḥ saṃvatsaram āptvārdhamāsaśa āptvā māsaśa āptvā stomāṃś ca chandāṃsi cāptvā sarvā devatās tapa eva tapyamānāḥ somapītham bhakṣayantaḥ saṃvatsaram abhiṣuṇvanta āsate ||
children.translated_text: Those who, knowing thus, enter upon this day, having obtained the year day by day, having obtained it half-month by half-month, having obtained it month by month, and having obtained the <s>stoma</s>s, the metres, and all the deities, sit practicing austerity, consuming the soma-drink, and pressing soma through the year.

children.text: ye vā ata ūrdhvaṃ saṃvatsaram upayanti guruṃ vai te bhāram abhinidadhate saṃ vai gurur bhāraḥ śṛṇāty atha ya enam parastāt karmabhir āptvāvastād upaiti sa vai svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute ||
children.translated_text: But those who enter upon the year after this lay a heavy burden upon themselves. A heavy burden indeed crushes. But the one who, having attained it from beyond by the rites, enters upon it from below, he safely reaches the far shore of the year.

children.text: Chapter 135

yad vai caturviṃśaṃ tan mahāvratam bṛhaddivenātra hotā retaḥ siñcati tad ado mahāvratīyenāhnā prajanayati saṃvatsare saṃvatsare vai retaḥ siktaṃ jāyate tasmāt samānam bṛhaddivo niṣkevalyam bhavaty eṣa ha vā enam parastāt karmabhir āptvāvastād upaiti ya evaṃ vidvān etad ahar upaiti ||
children.translated_text: What is twenty-fourfold is the <s>Mahāvrata</s>. Here, with the <s>Bṛhaddiva</s>, the <s>hotṛ</s> pours seed; then he generates that with the <s>Mahāvrata</s> day. What seed is poured in the year is born in the year; therefore the <s>niṣkevalya</s> of the <s>Bṛhaddiva</s> is the same. He indeed enters upon it from below after having attained it from beyond by the rites, who, knowing thus, enters upon this day.

children.text: svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He safely reaches the far side of the year, who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai saṃvatsarasyāvāraṃ ca pāraṃ ca veda sa vai svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute 'tirātro vā asya prāyaṇīyo 'vāram udayanīyaḥ pāram ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the near side and the far side of the year safely reaches the far side of the year. The <s>Atirātra</s> is his opening rite, the near side; the <s>Udayanīya</s> is the far side.

children.text: svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He safely reaches the far side of the year, who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai saṃvatsarasyāvarodhanaṃ codrodhanaṃ ca veda sa vai svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute 'tirātro vā asya prāyaṇīyo 'varodhanam udayanīya udrodhanam ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the holding down and the lifting up of the year safely reaches the far side of the year. The <s>Atirātra</s> is his opening rite, the holding down; the <s>Udayanīya</s> is the lifting up.

children.text: svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He safely reaches the far side of the year, who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai saṃvatsarasya prāṇodānau veda sa vai svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute 'tirātro vā asya prāyaṇīyaḥ prāṇa udāna udayanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>udāna</s> of the year safely reaches the far side of the year. The <s>Atirātra</s> is his opening rite, the <s>prāṇa</s>; the <s>Udayanīya</s> is the <s>udāna</s>.

children.text: svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He safely reaches the far side of the year, who knows thus, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 136
jyotir gaur āyur iti stomebhir yanty ayaṃ vai loko jyotir antarikṣaṃ gaur asau loka āyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They proceed with the <s>stoma</s>s called <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaur</s>, and <s>Āyus</s>. This world is <s>Jyotis</s>; the midspace is <s>Gaur</s>; that world yonder is <s>Āyus</s>.

children.text: sa evaiṣa uttaras tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is the later three-day sequence.

children.text: jyotir gaur āyur iti trīṇy ahāni gaur āyur jyotir iti trīṇi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Gaur</s>, and <s>Āyus</s>: these are three days; <s>Gaur</s>, <s>Āyus</s>, and <s>Jyotis</s>: these are three.

children.text: ayaṃ vai loko jyotir asau loko jyotis te ete jyotiṣī ubhayataḥ saṃlokete ||
children.translated_text: This world is <s>Jyotis</s>, and that world yonder is <s>Jyotis</s>; these two lights are visible to one another from both sides.

children.text: tenaitenobhayatojyotiṣā ṣaﾱahena yanti tad yad etenobhayatojyotiṣā ṣaﾱahena yanty anayor eva tal lokayor ubhayataḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanty asmiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś cobhayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this six-day sequence that has light on both sides they proceed. In that they proceed by this six-day sequence that has light on both sides, they proceed while establishing themselves on both sides in these two worlds, in this world and in that yonder, in both.

children.text: pariyad vā etad devacakraṃ yad abhiplavaḥ ṣaﾱahas tasya yāv abhito 'gniṣṭomau tau pradhī ye catvāro madhya ukthyās tan nabhyam ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day sequence is a turning divine wheel. Of it the two <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>s on either side are the rims, and the four <s>Ukthya</s>s in the middle are the nave.

children.text: gacchati vai vartamānena yatra kāmayate tat svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: By means of what is turning one goes wherever one desires. He safely reaches the far side of the year, who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai tad veda yat prathamaḥ ṣaﾱahaḥ sa vai svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute yas tad veda yad dvitīyo yas tad veda yat tṛtīyo yas tad veda yac caturtho yas tad veda yat pañcamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows what the first six-day sequence is safely reaches the far side of the year; so too whoever knows what the second is, whoever knows what the third is, whoever knows what the fourth is, and whoever knows what the fifth is.

children.text: Chapter 137
prathamaṃ ṣaﾱaham upayanti ṣaﾱ ahāni bhavanti ṣaḍ vā ṛtava ṛtuśa eva tat saṃvatsaram āpnuvanty ṛtuśaḥ saṃvatsare pratitiṣṭhanto yanti ||
children.translated_text: They enter upon the first six-day sequence; there are six days. There are six seasons; thereby they obtain the year season by season, and proceed while establishing themselves in the year season by season.

children.text: dvitīyaṃ ṣaﾱaham upayanti dvādaśāhāni bhavanti dvādaśa vai māsā māsaśa eva tat saṃvatsaram āpnuvanti māsaśaḥ saṃvatsare pratitiṣṭhanto yanti ||
children.translated_text: They enter upon the second six-day sequence; there are twelve days. There are twelve months; thereby they obtain the year month by month, and proceed while establishing themselves in the year month by month.

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ ṣaﾱaham upayanty aṣṭādaśāhāni bhavanti tāni dvedhā navānyāni navānyāni nava vai prāṇā nava svargā lokāḥ prāṇāṃś caiva tat svargāṃś ca lokān āpnuvanti prāṇeṣu caiva tat svargeṣu ca lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanto yanti ||
children.translated_text: They enter upon the third six-day sequence; there are eighteen days. These are two sets of nine and nine. There are nine vital breaths, and nine heavenly worlds. Thereby they obtain the vital breaths and the heavenly worlds, and proceed while establishing themselves in the vital breaths and in the heavenly worlds.

children.text: caturthaṃ ṣaﾱaham upayanti caturviṃśatir ahāni bhavanti caturviṃśatir vā ardhamāsā ardhamāsaśa eva tat saṃvatsaram āpnuvanty ardhamāsaśaḥ saṃvatsare pratitiṣṭhanto yanti ||
children.translated_text: They enter upon the fourth six-day sequence; there are twenty-four days. There are twenty-four half-months; thereby they obtain the year half-month by half-month, and proceed while establishing themselves in the year half-month by half-month.

children.text: pañcamaṃ ṣaﾱaham upayanti triṃśad ahāni bhavanti triṃśadakṣarā vai virāḍ virāﾱ annādyaṃ virājam eva tan māsi māsy abhisaṃpādayanto yanti ||
children.translated_text: They enter upon the fifth six-day sequence; there are thirty days. The <s>Virāj</s> has thirty syllables, and the <s>Virāj</s> is food to be eaten. Thereby they proceed while bringing the <s>Virāj</s> to completion month by month.

children.text: annādyakāmāḥ khalu vai satram āsata tad yad virājam māsi māsy abhisaṃpādayanto yanty annādyam eva tan māsi māsy avarundhānā yanty asmai ca lokāyāmuṣmai cobhābhyām ||
children.translated_text: Those who sit through a <s>sattra</s> do indeed desire food to be eaten. In that they proceed while bringing the <s>Virāj</s> to completion month by month, they proceed while securing food to be eaten month by month for this world and for that yonder, for both.

children.text: Chapter 138
gavām ayanena yanti gāvo vā ādityā ādityānām eva tad ayanena yanti ||
children.translated_text: They proceed by the <s>Gavām Ayana</s>, the Course of the Cows. The cows are the <s>Ādityas</s>; therefore they proceed by the course of the <s>Ādityas</s>.

children.text: gāvo vai satram āsata śaphāñchṛṅgāṇi siṣāsantyas tāsāṃ daśame māsi śaphāḥ śṛṅgāṇy ajāyanta tā abruvan yasmai kāmāyādīkṣāmahy āpāma tam uttiṣṭhāmeti tā yā udatiṣṭhaṃs tā etāḥ śṛṅgiṇyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The cows sat through a <s>sattra</s>, wishing to obtain hooves and horns. In their tenth month hooves and horns were born for them. They said, 'We have obtained the desire for which we underwent consecration; let us rise.' Those which rose are these horned ones.

children.text: atha yāḥ samāpayiṣyāmaḥ saṃvatsaram ity āsata tāsām aśraddhayā śṛṅgāṇi prāvartanta tā etās tūparā ūrjaṃ tv asunvaṃs tasmād u tāḥ sarvān ṛtūn prāptvottaram uttiṣṭhanty ūrjaṃ hy asunvan sarvasya vai gāvaḥ premāṇaṃ sarvasya cārutāṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But those which sat on, saying, 'We shall complete the year,' had their horns turn away through lack of faith. They are these <s>tūpara</s> cattle, yet they pressed out nourishment. Therefore, after reaching all the seasons, they rise later, for they pressed out nourishment. Cows have attained the dearness of everything and the beauty of everything.

children.text: sarvasya premāṇaṃ sarvasya cārutāṃ gacchati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He attains the dearness of everything and the beauty of everything, who knows thus.

children.text: ādityāś ca ha vā aṅgirasaś ca svarge loke 'spardhanta vayam pūrva eṣyāmo vayam iti te hādityāḥ pūrve svargaṃ lokaṃ jagmuḥ paścevāṅgirasaḥ ṣaṣṭyāṃ vā varṣeṣu ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Aṅgirases</s> competed for the heavenly world, saying, 'We shall go first; we shall.' The <s>Ādityas</s> went first to the heavenly world, and only afterward the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, in sixty years.

children.text: yathā vā prāyaṇīyo 'tirātraś caturviṃśa ukthyaḥ sarve 'bhiplavāḥ ṣaﾱahā ākṣyanty anyāny ahāni tad ādityānām ayanam ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, the opening <s>Atirātra</s>, the twenty-fourfold <s>Ukthya</s>, and all the <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day sequences exhaust the other days: that is the course of the <s>Ādityas</s>.

children.text: prāyaṇīyo 'tirātraś caturviṃśa ukthyaḥ sarve pṛṣṭhyāḥ ṣaﾱahā ākṣyanty anyāny ahāni tad aṅgirasām ayanam ||
children.translated_text: The opening <s>Atirātra</s>, the twenty-fourfold <s>Ukthya</s>, and all the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day sequences exhaust the other days: that is the course of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>.

children.text: sā yathā srutir añjasāyany evam abhiplavaḥ ṣaﾱahaḥ svargasya lokasyātha yathā mahāpathaḥ paryāṇa evam pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaﾱahaḥ svargasya lokasya tad yad ubhābhyāṃ yanty ubhābhyāṃ vai yan na riṣyaty ubhayoḥ kāmayor upāptyai yaś cābhiplave ṣaﾱahe yaś ca pṛṣṭhye ||
children.translated_text: As a narrow path is straight-going, so the <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite is for the heavenly world; and as a great road is a circuitous way, so the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite is for the heavenly world. Since they go by both, for when one goes by both one does not come to harm, this is for the attainment of both desires, the one in the <s>Abhiplava</s> six-day rite and the one in the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s>.

children.text: Chapter 139
ekaviṃśam etad ahar upayanti viṣuvantam madhye saṃvatsarasya ||
children.translated_text: They approach this twenty-first day, the <s>Viṣuvant</s>, in the middle of the year.

children.text: etena vai devā ekaviṃśenādityaṃ svargāya lokāyodayacchan ||
children.translated_text: By this twenty-first one the gods raised <s>Āditya</s> up to the heavenly world.

children.text: sa eṣa ita ekaviṃśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This here is that twenty-first one.

children.text: tasya daśāvastād ahāni divākīrtyasya bhavanti daśa parastān madhya eṣa ekaviṃśa ubhayato virāji pratiṣṭhita ubhayato hi vā eṣa virāji pratiṣṭhitas tasmād eṣo 'ntaremāṃllokān yan na vyathate ||
children.translated_text: Of it there are ten days of the <s>Divākīrtya</s> before, and ten after; this twenty-first is in the middle, established in the <s>Virāj</s> on both sides. For it is established in the <s>Virāj</s> on both sides; therefore this one does not tremble between these worlds.

children.text: tasya vai devā ādityasya svargāl lokād avapātād abibhayus taṃ tribhiḥ svargair lokair avastāt pratyuttabhnuvan stomā vai trayaḥ svargā lokās tasya parāco 'tipātād abibhayus taṃ tribhiḥ svargair lokaiḥ parastāt pratyastabhnuvan stomā vai trayaḥ svargā lokās tat trayo 'vastāt saptadaśā bhavanti trayaḥ parastān madhya eṣa ekaviṃśa ubhayataḥ svarasāmabhir dhṛta ubhayato hi vā eṣa svarasāmabhir dhṛtas tasmād eṣo 'ntaremāṃllokān yan na vyathate ||
children.translated_text: The gods feared that <s>Āditya</s> would fall down from the heavenly world. They propped him up from below with three heavenly worlds; the three <s>stoma</s>s are heavenly worlds. They feared that he would fall away forward; they propped him from above with three heavenly worlds; the three <s>stoma</s>s are heavenly worlds. Thus there are three seventeenfold ones below, three above, and this twenty-first in the middle, held on both sides by <s>svarasāman</s>s. For this one is held on both sides by <s>svarasāman</s>s; therefore this one does not tremble between these worlds.

children.text: tasya vai devā ādityasya svargāl lokād avapātād abibhayus tam paramaiḥ svargair lokair avastāt pratyuttabhnuvan stomā vai paramāḥ svargā lokās tasya parāco 'tipātād abibhayus tam paramaiḥ svargair lokaiḥ parastāt pratyastabhnuvan stomā vai paramāḥ svargā lokās tat trayo 'vastāt saptadaśā bhavanti trayaḥ parastāt te dvau dvau sampadya trayaś catustriṃśā bhavanti catustriṃśo vai stomānām uttamas teṣu vā eṣa etad adhyāhitas tapati teṣu hi vā eṣa etad adhyāhitas tapati ||
children.translated_text: The gods feared that <s>Āditya</s> would fall down from the heavenly world. They propped him up from below with the highest heavenly worlds; the <s>stoma</s>s are the highest heavenly worlds. They feared that he would fall away forward; they propped him from above with the highest heavenly worlds; the <s>stoma</s>s are the highest heavenly worlds. Thus there are three seventeenfold ones below and three above; combining two by two, they become three thirty-fourfold ones. The thirty-fourfold is the highest of the <s>stoma</s>s. Set upon them, this one shines; for set upon them, this one indeed shines.

children.text: sa vā eṣa uttaro 'smāt sarvasmād bhūtād bhaviṣyataḥ sarvam evedam atirocate yad idaṃ kiṃcottaro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: This one is higher than all this, than everything that has become and will become; whatever here is higher, it outshines all of it.

children.text: yasmād uttaro bubhūṣati tasmād uttaro bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Higher than whatever he wishes to become higher than, higher than that he becomes, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 140
svarasāmna upayantīme vai lokāḥ svarasāmāna imān vai lokān svarasāmabhir aspṛṇvaṃs tat svarasāmnāṃ svarasāmatvaṃ tad yat svarasāmna upayanty eṣv evainaṃ tallokeṣv ābhajanti ||
children.translated_text: They approach with <s>svarasāman</s>s. These worlds are indeed <s>svarasāman</s>s; with <s>svarasāman</s>s they strengthened these worlds. That is the <s>svarasāman</s>-nature of the <s>svarasāman</s>s. Therefore, when they approach with <s>svarasāman</s>s, they thereby apportion him among these worlds.

children.text: teṣāṃ vai devāḥ saptadaśānām pravlayād abibhayuḥ samā iva vai stomā avigūﾱhā iveme ha na pravliyerann iti tān sarvaiḥ stomair avastāt paryārṣan sarvaiḥ pṛṣṭhaiḥ parastāt tad yad abhijit sarvastomo 'vastād bhavati viśvajit sarvapṛṣṭhaḥ parastāt tat saptadaśān ubhayataḥ paryṛṣanti dhṛtyā apravlayāya ||
children.translated_text: The gods feared the collapse of those seventeenfold ones: 'The <s>stoma</s>s are, as it were, alike and not concealed; let these not collapse.' They enclosed them below with all the <s>stoma</s>s and above with all the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s. Therefore, because the <s>Abhijit</s>, possessing all <s>stoma</s>s, is below, and the <s>Viśvajit</s>, possessing all <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s, is above, they enclose the seventeenfold ones on both sides, for steadiness and against collapse.

children.text: tasya vai devā ādityasya svargāl lokād avapātād abibhayus tam pañcabhī raśmibhir udavayan raśmayo vai divākīrtyāni mahādivākīrtyaṃ pṛṣṭham bhavati vikarṇam brahmasāma bhāsam agniṣṭomasāmobhe bṛhadrathaṃtare pavamānayor bhavatas tad ādityam pañcabhī raśmibhir udvayanti dhṛtyā anavapātāya ||
children.translated_text: The gods feared that <s>Āditya</s> would fall down from the heavenly world. They raised him up with five rays. The <s>Divākīrtya</s>s are rays: the <s>Mahādivākīrtya</s> is a <s>pṛṣṭha</s>, the <s>Vikarṇa</s> is the <s>brahmasāman</s>, the <s>Bhāsa</s> is the <s>Agniṣṭoma-sāman</s>, and both <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> occur in the <s>pavamāna</s> chants. Thus they raise <s>Āditya</s> up with five rays, for steadiness and against falling down.

children.text: udita āditye prātaranuvākam anubrūyāt sarvaṃ hy evaitad ahar divākīrtyam bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Āditya</s> has risen, he should recite the morning litany, for this entire day is <s>Divākīrtya</s>.

children.text: sauryam paśum anyaṅgaśvetaṃ savanīyasyopālambhyam ālabheran sūryadevatyaṃ hy etad ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should take as the pressing-day victim a solar animal, white on one side, to be offered in place of the pressing victim, for this day has <s>Sūrya</s> as its deity.

children.text: ekaviṃśatiṃ sāmidhenīr anubrūyāt pratyakṣāddhyetad ahar ekaviṃśam ||
children.translated_text: He should recite twenty-one <s>sāmidhenī</s> verses, for this day is manifestly the twenty-first.

children.text: ekapañcāśataṃ dvipañcāśataṃ vā śastvā madhye nividaṃ dadhāti tāvatīr uttarāḥ śaṃsati śatāyur vai puruṣaḥ śatavīryaḥ śatendriya āyuṣy evainaṃ tad vīrya indriye dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: After reciting fifty-one or fifty-two, he places the <s>nivid</s> in the middle; he recites as many following verses. A man is indeed one whose life is a hundred, whose vigor is a hundred, whose powers are a hundred. Thereby he places him in life, in vigor, and in power.

children.text: Chapter 141
dūrohaṇaṃ rohati svargo vai loko dūrohaṇam ||
children.translated_text: He ascends the <s>Dūrohaṇa</s>; the heavenly world is the <s>Dūrohaṇa</s>.

children.text: svargam eva tal lokaṃ rohati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He ascends that very heavenly world, who knows thus.

children.text: yad eva dūrohaṇam asau vai dūroho yo 'sau tapati kaścid vā atra gacchati sa yad dūrohaṇaṃ rohaty etam eva tad rohati ||
children.translated_text: As for that <s>Dūrohaṇa</s>, that shining one up there is indeed the difficult ascent; and someone does go there. Therefore, when he ascends the <s>Dūrohaṇa</s>, he ascends that very one.

children.text: haṃsavatyā rohati ||
children.translated_text: He ascends with the <s>Haṃsavatī</s> verse.

children.text: haṃsaḥ śuciṣad ity eṣa vai haṃsaḥ śuciṣat ||
children.translated_text: 'The swan sitting in purity': this indeed is the swan sitting in purity.

children.text: vasur antarikṣad ity eṣa vai vasur antarikṣasat ||
children.translated_text: 'The good one dwelling in the midspace': this indeed is the good one dwelling in the midspace.

children.text: hotā vediṣad ity eṣa vai hotā vediṣat ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>hotṛ</s> dwelling at the altar': this indeed is the <s>hotṛ</s> dwelling at the altar.

children.text: atithir duroṇasad ity eṣa vā atithir duroṇasat ||
children.translated_text: 'The guest dwelling in the house': this indeed is the guest dwelling in the house.

children.text: nṛṣad ity eṣa vai nṛṣat ||
children.translated_text: 'Dwelling among men': this indeed is the one dwelling among men.

children.text: varasad ity eṣa vai varasad varaṃ vā etat sadmanāṃ yasminn eṣa āsannas tapati ||
children.translated_text: 'Dwelling in the best': this indeed is the one dwelling in the best. For this is the best of abodes, where this one sits and shines.

children.text: ṛtasad ity eṣa vai satyasat ||
children.translated_text: 'Dwelling in truth': this indeed is the one dwelling in truth.

children.text: vyomasad ity eṣa vai vyomasad vyoma vā etat sadmanāṃ yasminn eṣa āsannas tapati ||
children.translated_text: 'Dwelling in the sky': this indeed is the one dwelling in the sky. For the sky is this among abodes, where this one sits and shines.

children.text: abjā ity eṣa vā abjā adbhyo vā eṣā prātar udety apaḥ sāyam praviśati ||
children.translated_text: 'Water-born': this indeed is water-born; for she rises in the morning from the waters and enters the waters in the evening.

children.text: gojā ity eṣa vai gojāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Cow-born': this indeed is cow-born.

children.text: ṛtajā ity eṣa vai satyajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Born of ṛta': this indeed is born of truth.

children.text: adrijā ity eṣa vā adrijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Stone-born': this indeed is stone-born.

children.text: ṛtam ity eṣa vai satyam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Ṛta</s>': this indeed is truth.

children.text: eṣa etāni sarvāṇy eṣā ha vā asya chandassu pratyakṣatamād iva rūpam ||
children.translated_text: This is all these; this indeed is, as it were, his most directly visible form among the metres.

children.text: tasmād yatra kva ca dūrohaṇaṃ roheddhaṃsavatyaiva rohet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, wherever he should ascend the <s>dūrohaṇa</s> (difficult ascent), he should ascend with the <s>Haṃsavatī</s> verse.

children.text: tārkṣye svargakāmasya rohet ||
children.translated_text: For one who desires heaven, he should ascend with the <s>Tārkṣya</s> verse.

children.text: tārkṣyo ha vā etam pūrvo 'dhvānam aid yatrādo gāyatrī suparṇo bhūtvā somam āharat tad yathā kṣetrajñam adhvanaḥ puraetāraṃ kurvīta tādṛk tad yad eva tārkṣye 'yaṃ vai tārkṣyo yo 'yam pavata eṣa svargasya lokasyābhivoﾱhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tārkṣya</s> indeed went this path formerly, when <s>Gāyatrī</s>, having become a winged one, brought <s>Soma</s>. As one would make a knower of the road go in front as guide on a journey, so is that which is done with the <s>Tārkṣya</s>. This wind that blows here is <s>Tārkṣya</s>; he is the conveyer to the heavenly world.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam ity eṣa vai vājī devajūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'That swift steed, urged by the gods': this indeed is the steed urged by the gods.

children.text: sahāvānaṃ tarutāraṃ rathānām ity eṣa vai sahāvāṃs tarutaiṣa hīmāṃllokān sadyas tarati ||
children.translated_text: 'Powerful, overcoming, foremost among chariots': this indeed is powerful and overcoming, for he immediately crosses these worlds.

children.text: ariṣṭanemim pṛtanājam āśum ity eṣa vā ariṣṭanemiḥ pṛtanājid āśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'With uninjured felly, battle-winning, swift': this indeed is with uninjured felly, battle-winning, and swift.

children.text: svastaya iti svastitām āśāste ||
children.translated_text: 'For well-being': he thereby wishes for well-being.

children.text: tārkṣyam ihā huvemeti hvayaty evainam etat ||
children.translated_text: 'We call here upon <s>Tārkṣya</s>': by this he indeed calls upon him.

children.text: indrasyeva rātim ājohuvānāḥ svastaya iti svastitām evāśāste ||
children.translated_text: 'Calling upon a gift like <s>Indra</s>'s, for well-being': he thereby wishes precisely for well-being.

children.text: nāvam ivā ruhemeti sam evainam etad adhirohati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai sampattyai saṃgatyai ||
children.translated_text: 'Let us mount him as one mounts a ship': by this he fully mounts upon him, for the complete attainment, obtaining, and conjunction with the heavenly world.

children.text: urvī na pṛthvī bahule gabhīre mā vām etau mā paretau riṣāmetīme evaitad anumantrayata ā ca parā ca meṣyan ||
children.translated_text: 'Broad as earth, wide, deep: may we not come to harm from you two, neither coming hither nor going beyond.' With this he addresses these two, as he is about to go both toward and away.

children.text: sadyaś cid yaḥ śavasā pañca kṛṣṭīḥ sūrya iva jyotiṣāpas tatāneti pratyakṣaṃ sūryam abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: 'He who at once, by his might, stretched out the five peoples, like <s>Sūrya</s> with light the waters': he speaks directly to the sun.

children.text: sahasrasāḥ śatasā asya raṃhir na smā varante yuvatiṃ na śaryām ity āśiṣam evaitenāśāsta ātmane ca yajamānebhyaś ca ||
children.translated_text: 'His rush wins thousands and hundreds; they do not check him, as they do not check a young woman or an arrow.' By this he wishes a blessing for himself and for the sacrificers.

children.text: Chapter 142
āhūya dūrohaṇaṃ rohati svargo vai loko dūrohaṇaṃ vāg āhāvo brahma vai vāk sa yad āhvayate tad brahmaṇāhāvena svargaṃ lokaṃ rohati ||
children.translated_text: Having called out, he ascends the <s>dūrohaṇa</s>. The heavenly world indeed is the <s>dūrohaṇa</s>; speech is the call; speech indeed is <s>brahman</s>. When he calls out, then by <s>brahman</s>, by the call, he ascends to the heavenly world.

children.text: sa pacchaḥ prathamaṃ rohatīmaṃ tal lokam āpnoty athārdharcaśo 'ntarikṣaṃ tad āpnoty atha tripadyāmuṃ tallokam āpnoty atha kevalyā tad etasmin pratitiṣṭhati ya eṣa tapati ||
children.translated_text: He first ascends foot by foot; by that he obtains this world. Then, by half-verses, he obtains the midspace. Then, by the three-footed verse, he obtains that world yonder. Then, by the single complete verse, he is established in that one who burns.

children.text: tripadyā pratyavarohati yathā śākhāṃ dhārayamāṇas tad amuṣmiṃlloke pratitiṣṭhaty ardharcaśo 'ntarikṣe paccho 'smiṃlloka āptvaiva tat svargaṃ lokaṃ yajamānā asmiṃlloke pratitiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: He descends with the three-footed verse, as one holding a branch; by that he is established in that world yonder. By half-verses he is established in the midspace, and foot by foot in this world. Having thereby attained the heavenly world, the sacrificers are established in this world.

children.text: atha ya ekakāmāḥ syuḥ svargakāmāḥ parāñcam eva teṣāṃ rohet te jayeyur haiva svargaṃ lokam ||
children.translated_text: But those who are of a single desire, who desire heaven, for them he should ascend facing away only; they would indeed win the heavenly world.

children.text: na tv evāsmiṃlloke jyog iva vaseyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But they would not dwell for long in this world.

children.text: mithunāni sūktāni śasyante traiṣṭubhāni ca jāgatāni ca mithunaṃ vai paśavaḥ paśavaś chandāṃsi paśūnāṃ avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Paired hymns are recited, both <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s>. Cattle indeed are a pair; the metres are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: Chapter 143

yathā vai puruṣa evaṃ viṣuvāṃs tasya yathā dakṣiṇo 'rdha evam pūrvo 'rdho viṣuvato yathottaro 'rdha evam uttaro 'rdho viṣuvatas tasmād uttara ity ācakṣate prabāhuk sataḥ śira eva viṣuvān bidalasaṃhita iva vai puruṣas taddhāpi syūmeva madhye śīrṣṇo vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: As a man is, so is the <s>Viṣuvant</s>. As his right half is, so is the former half of the <s>Viṣuvant</s>; as his left half is, so is the later half of the <s>Viṣuvant</s>. Therefore they call it 'later.' Though he stands with arms extended, the <s>Viṣuvant</s> is the head. A man is, as it were, joined in two halves; even so a seam is perceived in the middle of the head.

children.text: tad āhur viṣuvaty evaitad ahaḥ śaṃsed viṣuvān vā etad ukthānām ukthaṃ viṣuvān viṣuvān iti ha viṣuvanto bhavanti śreṣṭhatām aśnuvata iti ||
children.translated_text: They say: 'On the <s>Viṣuvant</s> itself he should recite this day; for this <s>uktha</s> is the <s>Viṣuvant</s> among <s>uktha</s>s. Saying "<s>Viṣuvant</s>, <s>Viṣuvant</s>," they become possessed of <s>Viṣuvant</s>; they attain excellence.'

children.text: tat tan nādṛtyaṃ saṃvatsara eva śaṃsed reto vā etat saṃvatsaraṃ dadhato yanti ||
children.translated_text: That is not to be heeded. He should recite it in the year itself, for they go placing seed in the year.

children.text: yāni vai purā saṃvatsarād retāṃsi jāyante yāni pañcamāsyāni yāni ṣaṇmāsyāni srīvyanti vai tāni na vai tair bhuñjate ||
children.translated_text: Those seeds that are born before a year, those of five months and those of six months, are indeed lost; one does not make use of them.

children.text: atha yāny eva daśamāsyāni jāyante yāni sāṃvatsarikāṇi tair bhuñjate tasmāt saṃvatsara evaitad ahaḥ śaṃset ||
children.translated_text: But those that are born at ten months, those that are yearly, by them one makes use. Therefore he should recite this day in the year itself.

children.text: saṃvatsaro hy etad ahar āpnoti saṃvatsaraṃ hy etad ahar āpnuvanty eṣa ha vai saṃvatsareṇa pāpmānam apahata eṣa viṣuvatāṅgebhyo haiva māsaiḥ pāpmānam apahate śīrṣṇo viṣuvatā ||
children.translated_text: For the year reaches this day, and they reach this day through the year. This one indeed, by means of the year, strikes away evil. This one, by the <s>Viṣuvant</s>, from the limbs, with the months, strikes away evil; from the head, with the <s>Viṣuvant</s>.

children.text: apa saṃvatsareṇa pāpmānaṃ hate 'pa viṣuvatā ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He strikes away evil by the year and by the <s>Viṣuvant</s>, who knows thus.

children.text: vaiśvakarmaṇam ṛṣabhaṃ savanīyasyopālambhyam ālabheran dvirūpam ubhayata etam mahāvratīye 'hani ||
children.translated_text: On this <s>Mahāvrata</s> day they should take, as the offering animal for the pressing, the <s>Vaiśvakarmaṇa</s> bull, to be bound as victim, two-formed on both sides.

children.text: indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā viśvakarmābhavat prajāpatiḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā viśvakarmābhavat saṃvatsaro viśvakarmendram eva tadātmānam prajāpatiṃ saṃvatsaraṃ viśvakarmāṇam āpnuvantīndra eva tadātmani prajāpatau saṃvatsare viśvakarmaṇy antataḥ pratitiṣṭhanti pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, having slain <s>Vṛtra</s>, became <s>Viśvakarman</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created creatures, became <s>Viśvakarman</s>. The year is <s>Viśvakarman</s>. Thereby they attain <s>Indra</s> himself, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the year, <s>Viśvakarman</s>; at the end they are established in <s>Indra</s> himself, in <s>Prajāpati</s>, in the year, in <s>Viśvakarman</s>. He is established who knows thus, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 144

prajāpatir akāmayata prajāyeya bhūyān syām iti sa tapo 'tapyata sa tapas taptvemaṃ dvādaśāham apaśyad ātmana evāṅgeṣu ca prāṇeṣu ca tam ātmana evāṅgebhyaś ca prāṇebhyaś ca dvādaśadhā niramimīta tam āharat tenāyajata tato vai so 'bhavad ātmanā pra prajayā paśubhir ajāyata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> desired, 'May I be propagated; may I become more numerous.' He performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity). Having performed <s>tapas</s>, he saw this <s>Dvādaśāha</s> (twelve-day rite) in his own limbs and breaths. He fashioned it twelvefold from his own limbs and breaths. He brought it forth; with it he sacrificed. Then indeed he became; by himself he was propagated, and he was born forth with offspring and cattle.

children.text: bhavaty ātmanā pra prajayā paśubhir jāyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He becomes through himself, and he is born forth with offspring and cattle, who knows thus.

children.text: so 'kāmayata kathaṃ nu gāyatryā sarvato dvādaśāham paribhūya sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnuyām iti taṃ vai tejasaiva purastāt paryabhavac chandobhir madhyato 'kṣarair upariṣṭād gāyatryā sarvato dvādaśāham paribhūya sarvām ṛddhim ārdhnot ||
children.translated_text: He desired, 'How now may I, by means of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, encompass the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> on every side and attain all prosperity?' He encompassed it in front with splendor, in the middle with the metres, and above with syllables. By means of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, encompassing the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> on every side, he attained all prosperity.

children.text: sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He attains all prosperity, who knows thus.

children.text: yo vai gāyatrīṃ pakṣiṇīṃ cakṣuṣmatīṃ jyotiṣmatīm bhāsvatīṃ veda gāyatryā pakṣiṇyā cakṣuṣmatyā jyotiṣmatyā bhāsvatyā svargaṃ lokam ety eṣā vai gāyatrī pakṣiṇī cakṣuṣmatī jyotiṣmatī bhāsvatī yad dvādaśāhas tasya yāv abhito 'tirātrau tau pakṣau yāv antarāgniṣṭomau te cakṣuṣī ye 'ṣṭau madhya ukthyāḥ sa ātmā ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the <s>Gāyatrī</s> as winged, possessing eyes, possessing light, and shining, goes to the heavenly world by means of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> that is winged, possessing eyes, possessing light, and shining. This <s>Gāyatrī</s>, winged, possessing eyes, possessing light, and shining, is indeed the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>. Its two <s>Atirātra</s>s on either side are the two wings; the two intervening <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>s are the two eyes; the eight <s>Ukthya</s>s in the middle are the body.

children.text: gāyatryā pakṣiṇyā cakṣuṣmatyā jyotiṣmatyā bhāsvatyā svargaṃ lokam eti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He goes to the heavenly world by means of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> that is winged, possessing eyes, possessing light, and shining, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 145
trayaś ca vā ete tryahā ā daśamam ahar ā dvāv atirātrau yad dvādaśāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are three three-day periods up to the tenth day, and two <s>Atirātra</s>s: that is the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>.

children.text: dvādaśāhāni dīkṣito bhavati yajñiya eva tair bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He remains consecrated for twelve days; by those days he becomes fit for the sacrifice.

children.text: dvādaśa rātrīr upasada upaiti śarīram eva tābhir dhūnute ||
children.translated_text: He attends the <s>upasad</s>s for twelve nights; by them he shakes off the body.

children.text: dvādaśāham prasutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He has been set in motion for the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>.

children.text: bhūtvā śarīraṃ dhūtvā śuddhaḥ pūto devatā apyeti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Having become, having shaken off the body, purified and cleansed, he goes to the deities, who knows thus.

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśadaho vā eṣa yad dvādaśāhaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadakṣarā vai bṛhatī bṛhatyā vā etad ayanaṃ yad dvādaśāho bṛhatyā vai devā imāṃllokān āśnuvata te vai daśabhir evākṣarair imaṃ lokam āśnuvata daśabhir antarikṣam daśabhir divaṃ caturbhiś catasro diśo dvābhyām evāsmiṃlloke pratyatiṣṭhan ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Dvādaśāha</s> is in truth a thirty-six-day rite. The <s>Bṛhatī</s> has thirty-six syllables. This course which is the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> belongs to the <s>Bṛhatī</s>. By the <s>Bṛhatī</s> the gods reached these worlds: with ten syllables they reached this world, with ten the midspace, with ten heaven, with four the four directions, and with two they stood firm in this world.

children.text: pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He stands firm, who knows thus.

children.text: tad āhur yad anyāni chandāṃsi varṣīyāṃsi bhūyo 'kṣaratarāṇy atha kasmād etām bṛhatīty ācakṣata iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, 'Since the other metres are longer and have more syllables, why then do they call this one <s>Bṛhatī</s>?'

children.text: etayā hi devā imāṃllokān āśnuvata te vai daśabhir evākṣarair imaṃ lokam āśnuvata daśabhir antarikṣaṃ daśabhir divaṃ caturbhiś catasro diśo dvābhyām evāsmiṃlloke pratyatiṣṭhaṃs tasmād etām bṛhatīty ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: For by this one the gods reached these worlds: with ten syllables they reached this world, with ten the midspace, with ten heaven, with four the four directions, and with two they stood firm in this world. Therefore they call this one <s>Bṛhatī</s>.

children.text: aśnute yadyat kāmayate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He reaches whatever he desires, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 146

prajāpatiyajño vā eṣa yad dvādaśāhaḥ prajāpatir vā etenāgre 'yajata dvādaśāhena so 'bravīd ṛtūṃśca māsāṃśca yājayata mā dvādaśāheneti taṃ dīkṣayitvānapakramaṃ gamayitvābruvan dehi nu no 'tha tvā yājayiṣyāma iti tebhya iṣam ūrjam prāyacchat saiṣorg ṛtuṣu ca māseṣu ca nihitā dadataṃ vai te tam ayājayaṃs tasmād dadad yājyaḥ pratigṛhṇanto vai te tam ayājayaṃs tasmāt pratigṛhṇatā yājyam ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Dvādaśāha</s> is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>'s sacrifice. In the beginning <s>Prajāpati</s> sacrificed with this, with the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>. He said, 'Have the seasons and the months sacrifice for me with the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>.' Having consecrated him and made him go without departing, they said, 'Give to us now, and then we shall sacrifice for you.' He gave them refreshment and strength. This refreshment is deposited in the seasons and in the months. Giving, indeed, they sacrificed for him; therefore a giver is one for whom sacrifice should be performed. Receiving, indeed, they sacrificed for him; therefore sacrifice should be performed by one who receives.

children.text: ubhaye rādhnuvanti ya evaṃ vidvāṃso yajante ca yājayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Both prosper, those who, knowing thus, sacrifice and also officiate at sacrifice.

children.text: te vā ima ṛtavaś ca māsāś ca gurava ivāmanyanta dvādaśāhe pratigṛhya te 'bruvan prajāpatiṃ yājaya no dvādaśāheneti sa tathety abravīt te vai dīkṣadhvam iti te pūrvapakṣāḥ pūrve 'dīkṣanta te pāpmānam apāhata tasmāt te diveva diveva hy apahatapāpmāno 'parapakṣā apare 'dīkṣanta te natarām pāpmānam apāhata tasmāt te tama iva tama iva hy anapahatapāpmānas tasmād evaṃ vidvān dīkṣamāṇeṣu pūrvaḥ pūrva eva didīkṣiṣeta ||
children.translated_text: These seasons and months, after receiving in the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>, thought themselves weighty, as it were. They said, 'Sacrifice for us, <s>Prajāpati</s>, with the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>.' He said, 'So be it. Consecrate yourselves.' The waxing half-months were consecrated first; they drove evil away. Therefore they are like day after day, for their evil has been driven away. The waning half-months were consecrated later; they did not drive evil away so much. Therefore they are like darkness after darkness, for their evil has not been driven away. Therefore one who knows thus, when people are being consecrated, should desire to be consecrated first of all.

children.text: apa pāpmānaṃ hate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He drives evil away, who knows thus.

children.text: sa vā ayam prajāpatiḥ saṃvatsara ṛtuṣu ca māseṣu ca pratyatiṣṭhat te vā ima ṛtavaś ca māsāś ca prajāpatāv eva saṃvatsare pratyatiṣṭhaṃs ta ete 'nyonyasmin pratiṣṭhitā evaṃ ha vāva sa ṛtviji pratitiṣṭhati yo dvādaśāhena yajate tasmād āhur na pāpaḥ puruṣo yājyo dvādaśāhena ned ayam mayi pratitiṣṭhād iti ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Prajāpati</s>, the year, stood firm in the seasons and in the months. These seasons and months stood firm in <s>Prajāpati</s>, the year. They are thus established in one another. In just this way he who sacrifices with the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> becomes established in the officiating priest. Therefore they say, 'A bad man should not be one for whom sacrifice is performed with the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>, lest this man become established in me.'

children.text: jyeṣṭhayajño vā eṣa yad dvādaśāhaḥ sa vai devānāṃ jyeṣṭho ya etenāgre 'yajata śreṣṭhayajño vā eṣa yad dvādaśāhaḥ sa vai devānāṃ śreṣṭho ya etenāgre 'yajata ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Dvādaśāha</s> is indeed the eldest sacrifice. He who sacrificed with it in the beginning is the eldest of the gods. This <s>Dvādaśāha</s> is indeed the best sacrifice. He who sacrificed with it in the beginning is the best of the gods.

children.text: jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭho yajeta kalyāṇīha samā bhavati na pāpaḥ puruṣo yājyo dvādaśāhena ned ayam mayi pratitiṣṭhād iti ||
children.translated_text: The eldest and best man should sacrifice. A propitious year comes to be here. A bad man should not be one for whom sacrifice is performed with the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>, lest this man become established in me.

children.text: indrāya vai devā jyaiṣṭhyāya śraiṣṭhyāya nātiṣṭhanta so 'bravīd bṛhaspatiṃ yājaya mā dvādaśāheneti tam ayājayat tato vai tasmai devā jyaiṣṭhyāya śraiṣṭhyāyātiṣṭhanta ||
children.translated_text: The gods did not stand by <s>Indra</s> for superiority and supremacy. He said to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, "Sacrifice for me with the twelve-day rite." He sacrificed for him; then indeed the gods stood by him for superiority and supremacy.

children.text: tiṣṭhante 'smai svā jyaiṣṭhyāya śraiṣṭhyāya sam asmin svāḥ śreṣṭhatāyāṃ jānate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: His own people stand by him for superiority and supremacy; his own people recognize him as established in supremacy, who knows thus.

children.text: ūrdhvo vai prathamas tryahas tiryaṅ madhyamo 'rvāṅ uttamaḥ sa yad ūrdhvaḥ prathamas tryahas tasmād ayam agnir ūrdhva uddīpyata ūrdhvā hy etasya dig yat tiryaṅ madhyamas tasmād ayaṃ vāyus tiryaṅ pavate tiraścīr āpo vahanti tiraścī hy etasya dig yad arvāṅ uttamas tasmād asāv arvāṅ tapaty arvāṅ varṣaty arvāñci nakṣatrāṇy arvācī hy etasya dik samyañco vā ime lokāḥ samyañca ete tryahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first three-day sequence is upward, the middle one is across, and the last is downward. Because the first three-day sequence is upward, this fire here blazes upward, for its direction is upward. Because the middle one is across, this wind blows across, and the waters flow across, for its direction is transverse. Because the last one is downward, that sun yonder heats downward, rains downward, and the stars are turned downward, for its direction is downward. These worlds are aligned, and these three-day sequences are aligned.

children.text: samyañco 'smā ime lokāḥ śriyai dīdyati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: These worlds shine in alignment for him, for prosperity, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 147

dīkṣā vai devebhyo 'pākrāmat tāṃ vāsantikābhyām māsābhyām anvayuñjata tāṃ vāsantikābhyām māsābhyāṃ nodāpnuvaṃs tāṃ graiṣmābhyāṃ tāṃ vārṣikābhyāṃ tāṃ śāradābhyāṃ tāṃ haimantikābhyām māsābhyām anvayuñjata tāṃ haimantikābhyām māsābhyāṃ nodāpnuvaṃs tāṃ śaiśirābhyām māsābhyām anvayuñjata tāṃ śaiśirābhyām māsābhyām āpnuvan ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dīkṣā</s> (consecration) slipped away from the gods. They pursued it with the two spring months, but they did not obtain it with the two spring months; then with the two summer months, then with the two rainy-season months, then with the two autumn months, then they pursued it with the two early-winter months, but they did not obtain it with the two early-winter months. They pursued it with the two late-winter months, and with the two late-winter months they obtained it.

children.text: āpnoti yam īpsati nainaṃ dviṣann āpnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He obtains what he seeks; one who hates him does not overtake him, who knows thus.

children.text: tasmād yaṃ sattriyā dīkṣopanamed etayor eva śaiśirayor māsayor āgatayor dīkṣeta sākṣād eva tad dīkṣāyām āgatāyām dīkṣate pratyakṣād dīkṣām parigṛhṇāti tasmād etayor eva śaiśirayor māsayor āgatayor ye caiva grāmyāḥ paśavo ye cāraṇyā aṇimānam eva tat paruṣimāṇaṃ niyanti dīkṣārūpam eva tad upaniplavante ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when <s>dīkṣā</s> approaches those engaged in a <s>sattra</s> (long sacrificial session), they should consecrate themselves only when these two late-winter months have arrived. Thus, with consecration visibly arrived, one consecrates oneself; one takes hold of consecration directly. Therefore, when these two late-winter months have arrived, both domestic animals and wild animals come to leanness and roughness; they approach the very form of consecration.

children.text: sa purastād dīkṣāyāḥ prājāpatyam paśum ālabhate ||
children.translated_text: Before the consecration he immolates an animal belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: tasya saptadaśa sāmidhenīr anubrūyāt saptadaśo vai prajāpatiḥ prajāpater āptyai ||
children.translated_text: For it he should recite seventeen <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling) verses. <s>Prajāpati</s> is seventeenfold; this is for the attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: tasyāpriyo jāmadagnyo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Its <s>āpri</s> verses are the <s>Jāmadagnya</s> verses.

children.text: tad āhur yad anyeṣu paśuṣu yathaṛṣy āpriyo bhavanty atha kasmād asmin sarveṣāṃ jāmadagnya eveti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since in the case of other animals the <s>āpri</s> verses are according to the seer, why then in this case are all of them specifically <s>Jāmadagnya</s>?"

children.text: sarvarūpā vai jāmadagnyaḥ sarvasamṛddhāḥ sarvarūpa eṣa paśuḥ sarvasamṛddhas tad yajjāmadagnyo bhavanti sarvarūpatāyai sarvasamṛddhyai ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Jāmadagnya</s> verses are of every form and furnished with every success. This animal is of every form and furnished with every success. Therefore, when the <s>Jāmadagnya</s> verses are used, it is for every-formedness and for complete success.

children.text: tasya vāyavyaḥ paśupuroﾱāśo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Its animal cake is one belonging to <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: tad āhur yad anyadevatya uta paśur bhavaty atha kasmād vāyavyaḥ paśupuroﾱāśaḥ kriyata iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If the animal belongs to another deity, why is the animal cake made as one belonging to <s>Vāyu</s>?"

children.text: prajāpatir vai yajño yajñasyāyātayāmatāyā iti brūyād yad u vāyavyas tena prajāpater naiti vāyur hy eva prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should say, "<s>Prajāpati</s> is the sacrifice, and this is for the sacrifice's unwearied freshness." And as for its being one belonging to <s>Vāyu</s>, by that it does not depart from <s>Prajāpati</s>, for <s>Vāyu</s> is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: tad uktam ṛṣiṇā pavamānaḥ prajāpatir iti ||
children.translated_text: This has been said by the seer: "The purifying one is <s>Prajāpati</s>."

children.text: satram u cet saṃnyupyāgnīn yajeran sarve dīkṣeran sarve sunuyur vasantam abhyudavasyaty ūrg vai vasanta iṣam eva tad ūrjam abhyudavasyati ||
children.translated_text: If, having brought the fires together, they were to sacrifice in a <s>sattra</s>, all should be consecrated and all should press Soma. It comes to its completion toward spring. Spring is nourishment; thereby it comes to completion toward food and nourishment.

children.text: Chapter 148

chandāṃsi vā anyonyasyāyatanam abhyadhyāyan gāyatrī triṣṭubhaś ca jagatyai cāyatanam abhyadhyāyat triṣṭub gāyatryai ca jagatyai ca jagatī gāyatryai ca triṣṭubhaś ca tato vā etam prajāpatir vyūﾱhachandasaṃ dvādaśāham apaśyat tam āharat tenāyajata tena sa sarvān kāmāṃś chandāṃsy agamayat ||
children.translated_text: The metres studied one another's support: the <s>Gāyatrī</s> studied the support of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and of the <s>Jagatī</s>, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> that of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and of the <s>Jagatī</s>, and the <s>Jagatī</s> that of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. Then <s>Prajāpati</s> saw this twelve-day rite with its metres distributed. He brought it forth and sacrificed with it; by it he caused the metres to reach all desires.

children.text: sarvān kāmān gacchati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He reaches all desires, who knows thus.

children.text: chandāṃsi vyūhaty ayātayāmatāyai ||
children.translated_text: He distributes the metres for unwearied freshness.

children.text: chandāṃsy eva vyūhati tad yathādo 'śvair vānaﾱudbhir vānyair anyair aśrāntatarair aśrāntatarair upavimokaṃ yānty evam evaitac chandobhir anyair anyair aśrāntatarair aśrāntatarair upavimokaṃ svargaṃ lokam yanti yacchandāṃsi vyūhati ||
children.translated_text: He distributes the metres themselves. Just as, with horses or with draught oxen or with other teams, one goes to the unyoking place by using others that are more and more unwearied, so too, by means of different metres that are more and more unwearied, they go to the unyoking place, the heavenly world, when he distributes the metres.

children.text: imau vai lokau sahāstāṃ tau vyaitāṃ nāvarṣan na samatapat te pañcajanā na samajānata tau devāḥ samanayaṃs tau saṃyantāv etaṃ devavivāhaṃ vyavahetāṃ rathaṃtareṇaiveyam amūṃ jinvati bṛhatāsāv imām ||
children.translated_text: These two worlds were together. They separated; they did not rain, and they did not heat together. The five peoples did not understand them. The gods brought them together, and as they came together they celebrated this divine marriage. With the <s>Rathantara</s>, this world invigorates that one yonder; with the <s>Bṛhat</s>, that one yonder invigorates this world.

children.text: naudhasenaiveyam amūṃ jinvati śyaitenāsāv imāṃ dhūmenaiveyam amūṃ jinvati vṛṣṭyāsāv imāṃ devayajanam eveyam amuṣyām adadhāt paśūn asāv asyām ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>Naudhasa</s>, this world invigorates that one yonder; with the <s>Śyaita</s>, that one yonder invigorates this world. With smoke, this world invigorates that one yonder; with rain, that one yonder invigorates this world. This world placed a divine sacrificial ground in that one yonder, and that one placed animals in this world.

children.text: etad vā iyam amuṣyāṃ devayajanam adadhād yad etaccandramasi kṛṣṇam iva ||
children.translated_text: What this world placed in that one yonder as a divine sacrificial ground is that which appears dark on the moon.

children.text: tasmād āpūryamāṇapakṣeṣu yajanta etad evopepsantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they sacrifice during the waxing fortnights, seeking to obtain just that.

children.text: ūṣān asāv asyāṃ taddhāpi turaḥ kāvaṣeya uvācoṣaḥ poṣo janamejayaketi tasmāddhāpyetarhi gavyam mīmāṃsamānāḥ pṛcchanti santi tatroṣāḥ iti ūṣo hi poṣo 'sau vai loka imaṃ lokam abhiparyāvartata ||
children.translated_text: That world placed saline soil in this one. Thus even <s>Tura Kāvaṣeya</s> said, "Saline soil is nourishment, O <s>Janamejayaka</s>." Therefore even now, when people are examining land for cattle, they ask, "Are there saline patches there?" For saline soil is nourishment. That world yonder turns around this world.

children.text: tato vai dyāvāpṛthivī abhavatāṃ na dyāvāntarikṣān nāntarikṣād bhūmiḥ ||
children.translated_text: From that, indeed, <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>, Heaven and Earth, came to be: heaven was not from the midspace, nor was earth from the midspace.

children.text: Chapter 149

bṛhac ca vā idam agre rathaṃtaraṃ cāstāṃ vāk ca vai tan manaś cāstāṃ vāg vai rathaṃtaram mano bṛhat tad bṛhat pūrvaṃ sasṛjānaṃ rathaṃtaram atyamanyata tad rathaṃtaraṃ garbham adhatta tad vairūpam asṛjata ||
children.translated_text: In the beginning this was <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>; speech and mind indeed were that. Speech is <s>Rathantara</s>, and mind is <s>Bṛhat</s>. That <s>Bṛhat</s>, being created first, thought itself superior to <s>Rathantara</s>. Then <s>Rathantara</s> conceived an embryo; it created <s>Vairūpa</s>.

children.text: te dve bhūtvā rathaṃtaraṃ ca vairūpaṃ ca bṛhad atyamanyetāṃ tad bṛhad garbham adhatta tad vairājam asṛjata ||
children.translated_text: Those two, <s>Rathantara</s> and <s>Vairūpa</s>, having become two, thought themselves superior to <s>Bṛhat</s>. Then <s>Bṛhat</s> conceived an embryo; it created <s>Vairāja</s>.

children.text: te dve bhūtvā bṛhac ca vairājaṃ ca rathaṃtaraṃ ca vairūpam cātyamanyetāṃ tad rathaṃtaraṃ garbham adhatta tacchākvaram asṛjata ||
children.translated_text: Those two, <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Vairāja</s>, having become two, thought themselves superior to <s>Rathantara</s> and <s>Vairūpa</s>. Then <s>Rathantara</s> conceived an embryo; it created <s>Śākvara</s>.

children.text: tāni trīṇi bhūtvā rathaṃtaraṃ ca vairūpam ca śākvaraṃ ca bṛhac ca vairājaṃ cātyamanyanta tad bṛhad garbham adhatta tad raivatam asṛjata ||
children.translated_text: Those three, <s>Rathantara</s>, <s>Vairūpa</s>, and <s>Śākvara</s>, having become three, thought themselves superior to <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Vairāja</s>. Then <s>Bṛhat</s> conceived an embryo; it created <s>Raivata</s>.

children.text: tāni trīṇy anyāni trīṇy anyāni ṣaṭ pṛṣṭhāny āsan ||
children.translated_text: Those three on one side and those three on the other became the six <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s.

children.text: tāni ha tarhi trīṇi chandāṃsi ṣaṭ pṛṣṭhāni nodāpnuvan sā gāyatrī garbham adhatta sānuṣṭubham asṛjata triṣṭub garbham adhatta sā paṅktim asṛjata jagatī garbham adhatta sātichandasam asṛjata tāni trīṇy anyāni trīṇy anyāni ṣaṭ chandāṃsy āsan ṣaṭ pṛṣṭhāni tāni tathākalpanta kalpate yajño 'pi ||
children.translated_text: At that time those three meters did not attain the six <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s. <s>Gāyatrī</s> conceived an embryo; she created <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. <s>Triṣṭubh</s> conceived an embryo; she created <s>Paṅkti</s>. <s>Jagatī</s> conceived an embryo; she created <s>Atichandas</s>. Those three on one side and those three on the other became six meters and six <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s. They were arranged in that way; the sacrifice too is arranged.

children.text: tasyai janatāyai kalpate yatraivam etāṃ chandasāṃ ca pṛṣṭhānāṃ ca kﾱptiṃ vidvān dīkṣate dīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: For that community the rite is arranged, wherever one who knows this arrangement of the meters and the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s is consecrated, whenever he is consecrated.

children.text: Chapter 150
agnir vai devatā prathamam ahar vahati trivṛt stomo rathaṃtaraṃ sāma gāyatrī chandaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is the deity who carries the first day; the <s>Trivṛt</s> is the <s>stoma</s>, <s>Rathantara</s> the <s>sāman</s>, and <s>Gāyatrī</s> the meter.

children.text: yathādevatam enena yathāstomaṃ yathāsāma yathāchandasaṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: By this he prospers according to the deity, according to the <s>stoma</s>, according to the <s>sāman</s>, and according to the meter, who knows thus.

children.text: yad vā eti ca preti ca tat prathamasyāhno rūpaṃ yad yuktavad yad rathavad yad āśumad yat pibavad yat prathame pade devatā nirucyate yad ayaṃ loko 'bhyudito yad rāthaṃtaraṃ yad gāyatraṃ yat kariṣyad etāni vai prathamasyāhno rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has 'goes' and 'goes forth' is the form of the first day; whatever has yoking, whatever has a chariot, whatever has swiftness, whatever has drinking, whatever names the deity in the first verse-foot, whatever proclaims this world, whatever is <s>Rāthaṃtara</s>, whatever is <s>Gāyatra</s>, whatever is about to act: these indeed are the forms of the first day.

children.text: upaprayanto adhvaram iti prathamasyāhna ājyam bhavati ||
children.translated_text: 'They approach the rite' is the <s>ājya</s> chant of the first day.

children.text: preti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: It has 'goes forth' on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: vāyav ā yāhi darśateti praugam eti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, come, visible one' proceeds as the <s>praüga</s> on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaya idaṃ vaso sutam andha iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucarau rathavac ca pibavac ca prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: 'To you, as to a chariot, for aids' and 'This, O good one, is the pressed, intoxicating drink' are the opening and following verses of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>; they have a chariot and have drinking, on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: indra nedīya ed ihītīndranihavaḥ pragāthaḥ prathame pade devatā nirucyate prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Indra</s>, come nearer here' is the <s>Indranihava</s> <s>pragātha</s>. The deity is specified in the first verse-foot, on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: praitu brahmaṇaspatir iti brāhmaṇaspatyaḥ preti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: 'Let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth' is addressed to <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>; it has 'goes forth' on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: agnir netā tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinvanty apa iti dhāyyāḥ prathameṣu padeṣu devatā nirucyante prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Agni</s> is the leader,' 'you, O <s>Soma</s>,' 'with powers of resolve,' and 'the waters swell' are <s>dhāyyā</s> verses. The deities are specified in the first verse-feet, on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: pra vā indrāya bṛhata iti marutvatīyaḥ pragāthaḥ preti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: 'Forth for great <s>Indra</s>' is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>pragātha</s>; it has 'forth' on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: ā yātv indro 'vasa upa na iti sūktam eti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn 'May <s>Indra</s> come to us with aid' proceeds on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: abhi tvā śūra nonumo 'bhi tvā pūrvapītaya iti rathaṃtaram pṛṣṭham bhavati rāthaṃtare 'hani prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: 'We praise you, hero' and 'We praise you for the first drinking' are the <s>Rathantara</s> <s>pṛṣṭha</s>. On the <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> day, on the first day, that is the form of the first day.

children.text: yad vāvāna purutamam purāṣāﾱ iti dhāyyā vṛtrahendro nāmāny aprā ity eti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>dhāyyā</s> verse beginning 'When, much-invoked, most abundant ...' and the line '<s>Indra</s>, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, has filled the names' have 'goes' on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: pibā sutasya rasina iti sāmapragāthaḥ pibavān prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: 'Drink of the juicy pressed soma' is the <s>sāma-pragātha</s>; it has drinking, on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam iti tārkṣyam purastāt sūktasya śaṃsati svastyayanaṃ vai tārkṣyaḥ svastitāyai ||
children.translated_text: He recites '<s>Tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam</s>' to <s>Tārkṣya</s> before the hymn. <s>Tārkṣya</s> is indeed safe passage, for the sake of safety.

children.text: svastyayanam eva tat kurute svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Thereby he makes safe passage itself. He safely reaches the far side of the year, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 151
ā na indro dūrād ā na āsād iti sūktam eti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn '<s>Indra</s>, come to us from afar; come to us from nearby' proceeds on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: sampātau bhavato niṣkevalyamarutvatīyayor nividdhāne vāmadevo vā imāṃllokān apaśyat tān sampātaiḥ samapatad yat sampātaiḥ samapatat tat sampātānāṃ sampātatvaṃ tad yat sampātau prathame 'hani śaṃsati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai sampattyai saṃgatyai ||
children.translated_text: There are two <s>Sampāta</s> verses at the placing of the <s>nivid</s> in the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> and <s>Marutvatīya</s>. <s>Vāmadeva</s> saw these worlds; with the <s>Sampāta</s>s he flew together to them. Because he flew together with the <s>Sampāta</s>s, that is the <s>Sampāta</s>-nature of the <s>Sampāta</s>s. Therefore, when he recites the two <s>Sampāta</s>s on the first day, it is for the complete attainment of the heavenly world, for success, for coming together.

children.text: tat savitur vṛṇīmahe 'dyā no deva savitar iti vaiśvadevasya pratipadanucarau rāthaṃtare 'hani prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: 'That of <s>Savitṛ</s> we choose' and 'Today, O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, for us' are the opening and following verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. On the <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> day, on the first day, that is the form of the first day.

children.text: yuñjate mana uta yuñjate dhiya iti sāvitraṃ yuktavat prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: 'They yoke the mind, and they yoke the thoughts' is addressed to <s>Savitṛ</s>; it has yoking, on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī ṛtāvṛdheti dyāvāpṛthivīyam preti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: 'Forth may Heaven and Earth, strengthened by truth, through sacrifices' is addressed to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>; it has 'forth' on the first day; that is the form of the first day.

children.text: iheha vo manasā bandhutā nara ity ārbhavaṃ yad vā eti ca preti ca tat prathamasyāhno rūpaṃ tad yat preti sarvam abhaviṣyat praiṣyann evāsmāllokād yajamānā iti tad yad iheha vo manasā bandhutā nara ity ārbhavam prathame 'hani śaṃsaty ayaṃ vai loka ihehāsminn evaināṃs tal loke ramayati ||
children.translated_text: "Here, here among you, O men, is kinship in mind" is a verse belonging to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>. That which both comes hither and goes away is the form of the first day. If it merely went away, everything would have come to an end; the sacrificers would indeed have departed from this world. Therefore, when on the first day he recites the <s>Ṛbhu</s> verse, "Here, here among you, O men, is kinship in mind," this world is indeed "here, here"; in this very world he thereby makes them take delight.

children.text: devān huve bṛhacchravasaḥ svastaya iti vaiśvadevam prathame pade devatā nirucyante prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "I call the gods of great fame for well-being" is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse. In the first foot the deities are named; on the first day this is the form of the first day.

children.text: mahāntaṃ vā ete 'dhvānam eṣyanto bhavanti ye saṃvatsaraṃ vā dvādaśāhaṃ vāsate tad yad devān huve bṛhacchravasaḥ svastaya iti vaiśvadevam prathame 'hani śaṃsati svastitāyai ||
children.translated_text: Those who sit through a year or through a twelve-day rite are about to travel a great road. Therefore, when on the first day he recites the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse, "I call the gods of great fame for well-being," it is for safe welfare.

children.text: svastyayanam eva tat kurute svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute ya evaṃ veda yeṣāṃ caivaṃ vidvān etaddhotā devān huve bṛhacchravasaḥ svastaya iti vaiśvadevam prathame 'hani śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He thereby makes an auspicious going. He safely reaches the far side of the year, who knows thus, and so do those for whom a <s>hotṛ</s> who knows thus recites this <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse, "I call the gods of great fame for well-being," on the first day.

children.text: vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase vipa ity āgnimārutasya pratipat prathame pade devatā nirucyate prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "For <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, broad-bright, O inspired ones" is the opening verse of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. In the first foot the deity is named; on the first day this is the form of the first day.

children.text: pratvakṣaso pratavaso virapśina iti mārutam preti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Of forward-driving, very mighty, wide-shining ones" is addressed to the <s>Maruts</s> and has the forward-going form; on the first day this is the form of the first day.

children.text: jātavedase sunavāma somam iti jātavedasyām purastāt sūktasya śaṃsati svastyayanaṃ vai jātavedasyāḥ svastitāyai ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse, "For <s>Jātavedas</s> let us press the Soma," before the hymn. The <s>Jātavedasī</s> is an auspicious going, for safe welfare.

children.text: svastyayanam eva tat kurute svasti saṃvatsarasya pāram aśnute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He thereby makes an auspicious going. He safely reaches the far side of the year, who knows thus.

children.text: pra tavyasīṃ navyasīṃ dhītim agnaya iti jātavedasyam preti prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Forth a mightier, newer thought for Agni" is a <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse with the forward-going form; on the first day this is the form of the first day.

children.text: samānam āgnimārutam bhavati yac cāgniṣṭome yad vai yajñe samānaṃ kriyate tat prajā anusamananti tasmāt samānam āgnimārutam bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Āgnimāruta</s> is the same as in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. Whatever is done as the same in the sacrifice, the creatures conform to it in the same way; therefore the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> is the same.

children.text: Chapter 152
indro vai devatā dvitīyam ahar vahati pañcadaśaḥ stomo bṛhat sāma triṣṭup chandaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> is the deity that carries the second day; the <s>stoma</s> is fifteenfold, the <s>sāman</s> is <s>Bṛhat</s>, and the meter is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: yathādevatam enena yathāstomaṃ yathāsāma yathāchandasaṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: By this he succeeds according to the deity, according to the <s>stoma</s>, according to the <s>sāman</s>, and according to the meter, who knows thus.

children.text: yad vai neti na preti yat sthitaṃ tad dvitīyasyāhno rūpaṃ yad ūrdhvavad yat prativad yad antarvad yad vṛṣaṇvad yad vṛdhanvad yan madhyame pade devatā nirucyate yad antarikṣam abhyuditaṃ yad bārhataṃ yat traiṣṭubhaṃ yat kurvad etāni vai dvitīyasyāhno rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Whatever neither comes hither nor goes away, whatever is stationary, whatever has an upward form, whatever has a counter-form, whatever has an inner form, whatever has a bull-form, whatever has a growth-form, whatever names the deity in the middle foot, whatever is uttered toward the midspace, whatever belongs to <s>Bṛhat</s>, whatever is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, and whatever has an action-form: these are the forms of the second day.

children.text: agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmaha iti dvitīyasyāhna ājyam bhavati kurvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "We choose Agni as messenger" is the <s>ājya</s> verse of the second day. It has an action-form; on the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: vāyo ye te sahasriṇa iti praugaṃ sutaḥ soma ṛtāvṛdheti vṛdhanvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Vāyu</s>, those thousandfold ones of yours" is the <s>praüga</s> hymn; "the Soma has been pressed for the increaser of truth" has the growth-form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: viśvānarasya vas patim indra it somapā eka iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucarau vṛdhanvaccāntarvacca dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "For you, the lord of <s>Viśvānara</s>" and "<s>Indra</s> alone is the Soma-drinker" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>; they have both the growth-form and the inner form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: indra nedīya ed ihītyacyutaḥ pragātha ut tiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata iti brāhmaṇaspatya ūrdhvavān dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Indra</s>, come here nearer" is an unshifted <s>pragātha</s>; "Rise up, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>" is addressed to <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> and has the upward form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: agnir netā tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinvanty apa iti dhāyyā acyutā ||
children.translated_text: "Agni is the leader," "You, Soma, by your powers," and "the waters swell" are fixed <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.

children.text: bṛhad indrāya gāyateti marutvatīyaḥ pragātho yena jyotir ajanayann ṛtāvṛdha iti vṛdhanvān dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Sing the <s>Bṛhat</s> for <s>Indra</s>" is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>pragātha</s>; "by which they generated light, increasing truth" has the growth-form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: indra somaṃ somapate pibemam iti sūktam sajoṣā rudrais tṛpad ā vṛṣasveti vṛṣaṇvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Indra</s>, lord of Soma, drink this Soma" is the hymn; "together with the <s>Rudras</s> be satisfied; swell like a bull" has the bull-form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: tvām iddhi havāmahe tvaṃ hy ehi cerava iti bṛhatpṛṣṭham bhavati bārhate 'hani dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "It is you indeed whom we call; for you, come here, O active one" is the <s>Bṛhatpṛṣṭha</s>. It belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s> day, to the second day; this is the form of the second day.

children.text: yad vāvāneti dhāyyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "What, being eager, he has won" is a fixed <s>dhāyyā</s> verse.

children.text: ubhayaṃ śṛṇavac ca na iti sāmapragātho yac cedam adya yad u ca hya āsīd iti bārhate 'hani dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "And may he hear both of us" is the <s>sāman-pragātha</s>; "what this is today and what was yesterday" belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s> day, to the second day; this is the form of the second day.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam iti tārkṣyo 'cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "That strong steed, impelled by the gods" is the fixed verse to <s>Tārkṣya</s>.

children.text: Chapter 153
yā ta ūtir avamā yā parameti sūktaṃ jahi vṛṣṇyāni kṛṇuhī parāca iti vṛṣaṇvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Whichever aid of yours is nearest, whichever is farthest" is the hymn; "strike down the bull-powers; make them turn away" has the bull-form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.
