children.text: viśvo devasya netus tat savitur vareṇyam ā viśvadevaṃ satpatim iti vaiśvadevasya pratipadanucarau bārhate 'hani dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "All belongs to the divine leader," "that desirable thing of <s>Savitṛ</s>," and "to the all-god, the true lord" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. They belong to the <s>Bṛhat</s> day, to the second day; this is the form of the second day.

children.text: ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayeti sāvitram ūrdhvavad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Up has that god <s>Savitṛ</s> risen with his golden one" is the <s>Sāvitra</s> verse and has the upward form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuveti dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ sujanmanī dhiṣaṇe antar īyata ity antarvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "For these two, Heaven and Earth, bring good to all" is the verse addressed to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>; "the well-born two <s>Dhiṣaṇās</s> move within" has the inner form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: takṣan rathaṃ suvṛtaṃ vidmanāpasa ity ārbhavaṃ takṣan harī indravāhā vṛṣaṇvasū iti vṛṣaṇvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "They fashioned the well-rolling chariot, with skillful work" is the verse belonging to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>; "they fashioned the two bay steeds, bearers of <s>Indra</s>, rich in bull-strength" has the bull-form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: yajñasya vo rathyaṃ viśpatiṃ viśām iti vaiśvadevaṃ vṛṣā ketur yajato dyām aśāyateti vṛṣaṇvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "For you the charioteer of the sacrifice, lord of clans among clans" is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse; "the bull, the signal of worship, has lain upon heaven" has the bull-form. On the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: tad u śāryātam aṅgiraso vai svargāya lokāya satram āsata te ha sma dvitīyaṃ dvitīyam evāhar āgatya muhyanti tān vā etac chāryāto mānavo dvitīye 'hani sūktam aśaṃsayat tato vai te pra yajñam ajānan pra svargaṃ lokaṃ tad yad etat sūktaṃ dvitīye 'hani śaṃsati yajñasya prajñātyai svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai ||
children.translated_text: Now there is the <s>Śāryāta</s>. The <s>Aṅgirases</s> sat through a <s>satra</s> (session) for the heavenly world. They used to become bewildered again and again when they had come to the second day. Then <s>Śāryāta Mānava</s> caused them to recite this hymn on the second day. From that, indeed, they came to understand the sacrifice and the heavenly world. Therefore, when one recites this hymn on the second day, it is for understanding the sacrifice and for proclaiming the heavenly world.

children.text: pṛkṣasya vṛṣṇo aruṣasya nū saha ity āgnimārutasya pratipad vṛṣaṇvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Now with the strength of the mottled, bull-like one rich in food" is the opening verse of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. It has the bull-form; on the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: vṛṣṇe śardhāya sumakhāya vedhasa iti mārutaṃ vṛṣaṇvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "For the bull-like host, liberal and wise" is addressed to the <s>Maruts</s>. It has the bull-form; on the second day this is the form of the second day.

children.text: jātavedase sunavāma somam iti jātavedasyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "For <s>Jātavedas</s> let us press the <s>Soma</s>" is the fixed <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse.

children.text: yajñena vardhata jātavedasam iti jātavedasyaṃ vṛdhanvad dvitīye 'hani dvitīyasyāhno rūpam ahno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "With sacrifice strengthen <s>Jātavedas</s>" is a <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse with the growth-form. On the second day this is the form of the second day, the form of the day.

children.text: Chapter 154
viśve vai devā devatās tṛtīyam ahar vahanti saptadaśaḥ stomo vairūpaṃ sāma jagatī chandaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are the deities that carry the third day; the <s>stoma</s> is seventeenfold, the <s>sāman</s> is <s>Vairūpa</s>, and the meter is <s>Jagatī</s>.

children.text: yathādevatam enena yathāstomaṃ yathāsāma yathāchandasaṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: By this he succeeds according to the deity, according to the <s>stoma</s>, according to the <s>sāman</s>, and according to the meter, who knows thus.

children.text: yad vai samānodarkaṃ tat tṛtīyasyāhno rūpaṃ yad aśvavad yad antavad yat punarāvṛttaṃ yat punarninṛttaṃ yad ratavad yat paryastavad yat trivad yad antarūpaṃ yad uttame pade devatā nirucyate yad asau loko 'bhyudito yad vairūpaṃ yaj jāgataṃ yat kṛtam etāni vai tṛtīyasyāhno rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has the same ending, whatever has a horse-form, whatever has an end-form, whatever is repeated, whatever is turned back again, whatever has a treasure-form, whatever has a casting-around form, whatever is threefold, whatever has an inner form, whatever names the deity in the last foot, whatever proclaims that world above, whatever is <s>Vairūpa</s>, whatever is <s>Jāgata</s>, and whatever has been done: these indeed are the forms of the third day.

children.text: yukṣvā hi devahūtamāṁ aśvāṁ agne rathīr iveti tṛtīyasyāhna ājyam bhavati ||
children.translated_text: "Yoke, O <s>Agni</s>, the steeds most called by the gods, as charioteers do" is the <s>ājya</s> verse of the third day.

children.text: devā vai tṛtīyenāhnā svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs tān asurā rakṣāṃsy anvavārayanta te virūpā bhavata virūpā bhavateti bhavanta āyaṃs te yad virūpā bhavata virūpā bhavateti bhavanta āyaṃs tad vairūpaṃ sāmābhavat tad vairūpasya vairūpatvam ||
children.translated_text: The gods went to the heavenly world by the third day. The <s>Asuras</s> and <s>Rakṣases</s> tried to block them. As they went, they kept saying, "Become various, become various." Because, as they went, they kept saying, "Become various, become various," that became the <s>Vairūpa</s> <s>sāman</s>. That is the <s>Vairūpa</s>-nature of the <s>Vairūpa</s>.

children.text: virūpaḥ pāpmanā bhūtvā pāpmānam apahate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Having become various in relation to evil, he strikes evil away, who knows thus.

children.text: tān ha smānv evāgacchanti sam eva sṛjyante tān aśvā bhūtvā padbhir apāghnata yad aśvā bhūtvā padbhir apāghnata tad aśvānām aśvatvam ||
children.translated_text: They kept coming after them and rushing together against them. Having become horses, they struck them away with their feet. Because, having become horses, they struck them away with their feet, that is the horsehood of horses.

children.text: aśnute yad yat kāmayate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He obtains whatever he desires, who knows thus.

children.text: tasmād aśvaḥ paśūnāṃ javiṣṭhas tasmād aśvaḥ pratyaṅ padā hinasti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the horse is the swiftest of animals; therefore the horse strikes backward with its foot.

children.text: apa pāpmānaṃ hate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He strikes evil away, who knows thus.

children.text: tasmād etad aśvavad ājyam bhavati tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this <s>ājya</s> verse has the horse-form on the third day. It is the form of the third day.

children.text: vāyav ā yāhi vītaye vāyo yāhi śivā diva indraś ca vāyav eṣāṃ sutānām ā mitre varuṇe vayam aśvināv eha gacchatam ā yāhy adribhiḥ sutaṃ sajūr viśvebhir devebhir uta naḥ priyā priyāsv ity auṣṇiham praugaṃ samānodarkaṃ tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Vāyu</s>, come for the drinking," "O <s>Vāyu</s>, come from the bright heaven," "O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, of these pressed libations," "We, with <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>," "O two <s>Aśvins</s>, come here," "Come to the pressed Soma with the pressing-stones, together with all the gods," and "also our dear ones among the dear" form the <s>Auṣṇiha</s> <s>praüga</s>. It has the same ending; on the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: taṃ tam id rādhase mahe traya indrasya somā iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucarau ninṛttavat trivat tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "This very one, this one, for bounty, we greatly..." and "the three Somas of <s>Indra</s>" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. They have the turned-back form and are threefold; on the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: indra nedīya ed ihīty acyutaḥ pragāthaḥ pra nūnam brahmaṇaspatir iti brāhmaṇaspatyo ninṛttavāṃs tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Indra</s>, come here nearer" is a fixed <s>pragātha</s>; "Forth now, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>" is addressed to <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> and has the turned-back form. On the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: agnir netā tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinvanty āpa iti dhāyyā acyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Agni</s> is the leader," "you, O <s>Soma</s>," "with powers of resolve," and "the waters swell" are fixed <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.

children.text: nakiḥ sudāso ratham pary āsa na rīramad iti marutvatīyaḥ pragāthaḥ paryastavāṃs tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "No one checked <s>Sudās</s>' chariot, nor stopped it from going around" is the <s>Marutvatīya</s> <s>pragātha</s>. It has the casting-around form; on the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: try aryamā manuṣo devatāteti sūktaṃ trivat tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "Threefold is <s>Aryaman</s> in the divine office of man" is threefold. On the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: yad dyāva indra te śataṃ yad indra yāvatas tvam iti vairūpam pṛṣṭham bhavati rāthaṃtare 'hani tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "If, O <s>Indra</s>, your heavens are a hundred" and "As far as you, O <s>Indra</s>..." are the <s>Vairūpa</s> <s>pṛṣṭha</s>. On the <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> day, on the third day, this is the form of the third day.

children.text: yad vāvāneti dhāyyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>dhāyyā</s> verse beginning "When he has won..." is fixed.

children.text: abhi tvā śūra nonuma iti rathaṃtarasya yonim anu nivartayati rāthaṃtaraṃ hy etad ahar āyatanena ||
children.translated_text: With "We praise you, O hero" he turns back to the source of the <s>Rathantara</s>, for this day is <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> by its basis.

children.text: indra tridhātu śaraṇam iti sāmapragāthas trivāṃs tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Indra</s>, threefold shelter" is the <s>sāma-pragātha</s>. It is threefold; on the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam iti tārkṣyo 'cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "That vigorous one, impelled by the gods" is the fixed verse to <s>Tārkṣya</s>.

children.text: Chapter 155
yo jāta eva prathamo manasvān iti sūktaṃ samānodarkaṃ tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "He who, as soon as born, was first, thoughtful" has the same ending. On the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: tad u sajanīyam etad vā indrasyendriyaṃ yat sajanīyam etasmin vai śasyamāna indram indriyam āviśati ||
children.translated_text: Now there is the <s>Sajanīya</s>. This, indeed, is <s>Indra</s>'s <s>indriya</s> (power), namely the <s>Sajanīya</s>. When it is being recited, <s>Indra</s>'s <s>indriya</s> enters him.

children.text: taddhāpyāhuś chandogās tṛtīye 'hani bahvṛcā indrasyendriyam śaṃsantīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Chandogas</s> even say, "On the third day the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> recite <s>Indra</s>'s <s>indriya</s>."

children.text: tad u gārtsamadam etena vai gṛtsamada indrasya priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchat sa paramaṃ lokam ajayat ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is the <s>Gārtsamada</s>. By this <s>Gṛtsamada</s> approached the beloved abode of <s>Indra</s>; he won the highest world.

children.text: upendrasya priyaṃ dhāma gacchati jayati paramaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He approaches the beloved abode of <s>Indra</s> and wins the highest world, who knows thus.

children.text: tat savitur vṛṇīmahe 'dyā no deva savitar iti vaiśvadevasya pratipadanucarau rāthaṃtare 'hani tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "That of <s>Savitṛ</s> we choose" and "Today for us, O god <s>Savitṛ</s>" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. On the <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> day, on the third day, this is the form of the third day.

children.text: tad devasya savitur vāryam mahad iti sāvitram ||
children.translated_text: "That great desirable thing of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>" is the <s>Sāvitra</s> verse.

children.text: anto vai mahad antas tṛtīyam ahas tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The great is indeed an end; the third day is an end. On the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī abhīvṛte iti dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ ghṛtaśriyā ghṛtapṛcā ghṛtāvṛdheti punarāvṛttam punarninṛttaṃ tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Heaven and Earth are enveloped with ghee" is addressed to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>; "with ghee-splendor, touching ghee, increasing by ghee" is repeated and turned back. On the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: anaśvo jāto anabhīśur ukthya ity ārbhavam rathas tricakra iti trivat tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Born horseless, without reins, fit for praise" is the <s>Ārbhava</s> verse. "The chariot has three wheels" is threefold. On the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: parāvato ye didhiṣanta āpyam iti vaiśvadevam anto vai parāvato 'ntas tṛtīyam ahas tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Those from afar who desire kinship" is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse. What is far away is indeed an end; the third day is an end. On the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: tad u gāyam etena vai gayaḥ plāto viśveṣāṃ devānām priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchat sa paramaṃ lokam ajayat ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is the <s>Gāya</s>. By this <s>Gaya Plāta</s> approached the beloved abode of all the gods; he won the highest world.

children.text: upa viśveṣāṃ devānām priyaṃ dhāma gacchati jayati paramaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He approaches the beloved abode of all the gods and wins the highest world, who knows thus.

children.text: vaiśvānarāya dhiṣaṇām ṛtāvṛdha ity āgnimārutasya pratipad anto vai dhiṣaṇāntas tṛtīyam ahas tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "For <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the inspired speech that increases truth" is the opening verse of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. <s>Dhiṣaṇā</s> is indeed an end; the third day is an end. On the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: dhārāvarā maruto dhṛṣṇvojasa iti mārutam bahvabhivyāhṛtyam anto vai bahv antas tṛtīyam ahas tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "The streams, O <s>Maruts</s> of bold strength" is addressed to the <s>Maruts</s>; it has many utterances. Much is indeed an end; the third day is an end. On the third day this is the form of the third day.

children.text: jātavedase sunavāma somam iti jātavedasyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "For <s>Jātavedas</s> let us press Soma" is the fixed <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse.

children.text: tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣir iti jātavedasyam purastādudarkaṃ tṛtīye 'hani tṛtīyasyāhno rūpaṃ tvaṃ tvam ity uttaraṃ tryaham abhivadati saṃtatyai ||
children.translated_text: "You, O <s>Agni</s>, were the first <s>Aṅgiras</s> seer" is a <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse with its conclusion placed first. On the third day this is the form of the third day. By saying "you, you" he addresses the following three-day period, for continuity.

children.text: saṃtatais tryahair avyavacchinnair yanti ya evaṃ vidvāṃso yanti ||
children.translated_text: With continuous, uninterrupted three-day periods they go, those who know thus.

children.text: Chapter 156
āpyante vai stomā āpyante chandāṃsi tṛtīye 'hany etad eva tata ucchiṣyate vāg ity eva tad etad akṣaraṃ tryakṣaraṃ vāg ity ekam akṣaram akṣaram iti tryakṣaram ||
children.translated_text: The <s>stomas</s> are filled up, and the meters are filled up on the third day. Then this alone remains over: speech, this very syllable. "Vāc" is one syllable; "akṣara" is three syllables.

children.text: sa evaiṣa uttaras tryaho vāg ekaṃ gaur ekaṃ dyaur ekam ||
children.translated_text: This, indeed, is the following three-day period: speech is one, cow is one, heaven is one.

children.text: tato vai vāg eva caturtham ahar vahati ||
children.translated_text: From that point speech itself carries the fourth day.

children.text: tad yac caturtham ahar nyūṅkhayanty etad eva tad akṣaram abhyāyacchanty etad vardhayanty etat prabibhāvayiṣanti caturthasyāhna udyatyai ||
children.translated_text: When they perform the <s>nyūṅkha</s> on the fourth day, they make this very syllable full, they increase it, and they will make it manifest, for the rising of the fourth day.

children.text: annaṃ vai nyūṅkho yadelavā abhigeṣṇāś caranty athānnādyam prajāyate tad yaccaturtham ahar nyūṅkhayanty annam eva tat prajanayanty annādyasya prajātyai tasmāccaturtham ahar jātavad bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nyūṅkha</s> is food. When the <s>elavā</s> and <s>abhigeṣṇā</s> syllables are performed, then eatable food is produced. Therefore, when they perform the <s>nyūṅkha</s> on the fourth day, they generate food itself, for the production of eatable food. Therefore the fourth day has the character of something born.

children.text: caturakṣareṇa nyūṅkhayed ity āhuś catuṣpādā vai paśavaḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: They say, "He should perform the <s>nyūṅkha</s> with four syllables." Four-footed indeed are the animals; it is for securing the animals.

children.text: tryakṣareṇa nyūṅkhayed ity āhus trayo vā ime trivṛto lokā eṣām eva lokānām abhijityai ||
children.translated_text: They say, "He should perform the <s>nyūṅkha</s> with three syllables." These three worlds are threefold; it is for the conquest of these very worlds.

children.text: ekākṣareṇa nyūṅkhayed iti ha smāha lāṅgalāyano brahmā maudgalya ekākṣarā vai vāg eṣa vāva samprati nyūṅkhaṃ nyūṅkhayati ya ekākṣareṇa nyūṅkhayatīti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lāṅgalāyana Brahmā Maudgalya</s> used to say, "He should perform the <s>nyūṅkha</s> with one syllable. Speech is indeed one syllable. He, in truth, performs the <s>nyūṅkha</s> at the present moment who performs it with one syllable."

children.text: dvyakṣareṇaiva nyūṅkhayet pratiṣṭhāyā eva dvipratiṣṭho vai puruṣaś catuṣpādāḥ paśavo yajamānam eva tad dvipratiṣṭhaṃ catuṣpātsu paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati tasmād dvyakṣareṇaiva nyūṅkhayet ||
children.translated_text: He should perform the <s>nyūṅkha</s> with two syllables only, for firm standing. Man is two-footed, and animals are four-footed. Thereby he establishes the two-footed sacrificer among the four-footed animals. Therefore he should perform the <s>nyūṅkha</s> with two syllables only.

children.text: mukhataḥ prātaranuvāke nyūṅkhayati mukhato vai prajā annam adanti mukhata eva tad annādyasya yajamānaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He performs the <s>nyūṅkha</s> at the beginning in the morning recitation. Creatures indeed eat food with the mouth; thereby he places the sacrificer in possession of food from the mouth.

children.text: madhyata ājye nyūṅkhayati madhyato vai prajā annaṃ dhinoti madhyata eva tad annādyasya yajamānaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He performs the <s>nyūṅkha</s> in the middle during the <s>ājya</s> chant. Food indeed sustains creatures from the middle; thereby he places the sacrificer in possession of food from the middle.

children.text: mukhato madhyaṃdine nyūṅkhayati mukhato vai prajā annam adanti mukhata eva tad annādyasya yajamānaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He performs the <s>nyūṅkha</s> at the beginning at the midday pressing. Creatures indeed eat food with the mouth; thereby he places the sacrificer in possession of food from the mouth.

children.text: tad ubhayato nyūṅkham parigṛhṇāti savanābhyām annādyasya parigṛhītyai ||
children.translated_text: Thus he encloses the <s>nyūṅkha</s> on both sides by the two pressings, for enclosing the possession of food.

children.text: Chapter 157
vāg vai devatā caturtham ahar vahaty ekaviṃśaḥ stomo vairājaṃ sāmānuṣṭup chando yathādevatam enena yathāstomaṃ yathāsāma yathāchandasaṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Speech is the deity that carries the fourth day; the <s>stoma</s> is twenty-onefold, the <s>sāman</s> is <s>Vairāja</s>, and the meter is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. By this he succeeds according to the deity, according to the <s>stoma</s>, according to the <s>sāman</s>, and according to the meter, who knows thus.

children.text: yad vā eti ca preti ca taccaturthasyāhno rūpaṃ yaddhyeva prathamam ahas tad etat punar yac caturthaṃ yad yuktavad yad rathavad yad āśumad yat pibavad yat prathame pade devatā nirucyate yad ayaṃ loko 'bhyudito yaj jātavad yaddhavavad yacchukravad yad vāco rūpaṃ yad vaimadaṃ yad viriphitaṃ yad vichandā yad ūnātiriktaṃ yad vairājaṃ yad ānuṣṭubhaṃ yat kariṣyad yat prathamasyāhno rūpam etāni vai caturthasyāhno rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Whatever both comes and goes forth is the form of the fourth day; for precisely what the first day is, that again is the fourth. Whatever has yoking, whatever has a chariot, whatever has swiftness, whatever has drinking, whatever names the deity in the first foot, whatever proclaims this world, whatever has birth, whatever has invocation, whatever has brightness, whatever is the form of speech, whatever is <s>vaimada</s>, whatever is <s>viriphita</s>, whatever is irregular in meter, whatever is deficient or excessive, whatever is <s>vairāja</s>, whatever is <s>ānuṣṭubha</s>, whatever is about to act, whatever is the form of the first day: these indeed are the forms of the fourth day.

children.text: āgniṃ na svavṛktibhir iti caturthasyāhna ājyam bhavati vaimadaṃ viriphitaṃ viriphitasya ṛṣeś caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Agni</s>, as with good invocations" is the <s>ājya</s> chant of the fourth day. It is <s>vaimada</s> and <s>viriphita</s>; it belongs to the seer <s>Viriphita</s>. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: aṣṭarcam pāṅktam pāṅkto yajñaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavaḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: It has eight verses and is <s>pāṅkta</s>; the sacrifice is <s>pāṅkta</s>, and the animals are <s>pāṅkta</s>, for the securing of animals.

children.text: tā u daśa jagatyo jagatprātaḥsavana eṣa tryahas tena caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are ten <s>Jagatī</s> verses. This three-day rite has a <s>Jagatī</s> morning pressing; thereby it is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tā u pañcadaśānuṣṭubha ānuṣṭubhaṃ hy etad ahas tena caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are fifteen <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> verses; for this day is <s>ānuṣṭubha</s>. Thereby it is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tā u viṃśatir gāyatryaḥ punaḥ prāyaṇīyaṃ hy etad ahas tena caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are twenty <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses; for this day is again a <s>prāyaṇīya</s> day. Thereby it is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tad etad astutam aśastam ayātayāma sūktaṃ yajña eva sākṣāt tad yad etac caturthasyāhna ājyam bhavati yajñād eva tad yajñaṃ tanvate vācam eva tat punar upayanti saṃtatyai ||
children.translated_text: This hymn is unpraised, unrecited, and fresh; it is the sacrifice itself directly. Since this is the <s>ājya</s> chant of the fourth day, from the sacrifice itself they extend the sacrifice; they approach speech again, for continuity.

children.text: saṃtatais tryahair avyavacchinnair yanti ya evaṃ vidvāṃso yanti ||
children.translated_text: With continuous, unbroken three-day periods they proceed, those who proceed knowing thus.

children.text: vāyo śukro ayāmi te vihi hotrā avītā vāyo śataṃ harīṇām indraś ca vāyav eṣāṃ somānām ā cikitāna sukratū ā no viśvābhir ūtibhis tyam u vo aprahaṇam apa tyaṃ vṛjinaṃ ripum ambitame nadītama ity ānuṣṭubham praugam eti ca preti ca śukravac caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Vāyu</s>, bright one, I come to you; appoint the priestly offices as helper. O <s>Vāyu</s>, of the hundred bays. <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, aware of these Soma draughts, O wise ones. Come to us with all aids. That unassailable one of yours. Drive away that crooked enemy. O best mother, best river" proceeds as the <s>ānuṣṭubha praüga</s>. It both comes and goes forth; it has brightness. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: taṃ tvā yajñebhir īmaha iti marutvatīyasya pratipad īmaha ity abhyāyāmyam ivaitad ahas tena caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "We approach you with sacrifices" is the opening verse of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. The word "we approach" is, as it were, "I come near" for this day. Thereby it is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: idaṃ vaso sutam andha indra nedīya ed ihi praitu brahmaṇaspatir agnir netā tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinvanty apaḥ pra va indrāya bṛhata iti prathamenāhnā samāna ātānaś caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "This pressed drink, O <s>Vasu</s>, O <s>Indra</s>; come quite near. Let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth. <s>Agni</s> is the leader. You, O <s>Soma</s>, by your powers. The waters swell. Forth for great <s>Indra</s>" has the same <s>ātāna</s> as on the first day. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: śrudhī havam indra mā riṣaṇya iti sūktaṃ havavac caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Hear the invocation, O <s>Indra</s>; do not do harm" is a hymn with invocation. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: marutvān indra vṛṣabho raṇayeti sūktam ugraṃ sahodām iha taṃ huvemeti havavac caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>, bull, make roar" is a hymn. It is fierce and strength-giving; "him here I call" has invocation. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With that firmly placed foot he supports the pressing; by this he does not slip from its base.

children.text: imaṃ nu māyinaṃ huva iti paryāso havavāṃś caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Now I call this wonder-working one" is the concluding <s>paryāsa</s>, having invocation. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tā u gāyatryo gāyatryo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses; for <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day rite.

children.text: tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nividdhīyate tasmād gāyatrīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: That meter carries the rite in which the <s>nivid</s> is placed. Therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses.

children.text: pibā somam indra mandatu tvā śrudhī havaṃ vipipānasyādrer iti vairājam pṛṣṭham bhavati bārhate 'hani caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Drink Soma, O <s>Indra</s>; let it gladden you. Hear the invocation of the drinking stone" is the <s>Vairāja pṛṣṭha</s>. On the <s>Bārhata</s> day, on the fourth day, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: yad vāvāneti dhāyyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "When, having won richly" is a fixed <s>dhāyyā</s> verse.

children.text: tvām iddhi havāmaha iti bṛhato yonim anu nivartayati bārhataṃ hy etad ahar āyatanena ||
children.translated_text: With "You indeed we call" he turns back according to the womb of the <s>Bṛhat</s>; for this is a <s>Bārhata</s> day by its base.

children.text: tvam indra pratūrtiṣv iti sāmapragātho 'śastihā janiteti jātavāṃś caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "You, O <s>Indra</s>, in the onrushes" is the <s>sāma-pragātha</s>; "the slayer of curses, the begetter" has birth. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam iti tārkṣyo 'cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "That swift steed, impelled by the gods" is the fixed verse to <s>Tārkṣya</s>.

children.text: Chapter 158
kuha śruta indraḥ kasminn adyeti sūktaṃ vaimadaṃ viriphitaṃ viriphitasya ṛṣeś caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Where is <s>Indra</s> heard of? In what place today?" is a hymn that is <s>vaimada</s> and <s>viriphita</s>; it belongs to the seer <s>Viriphita</s>. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: yudhmasya te vṛṣabhasya svarāja iti sūktam ugraṃ gabhīraṃ januṣābhy ugram iti jātavac caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Of you, the warlike bull, the self-ruler" is a hymn, fierce and deep; "fierce by birth" has birth. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With that firmly placed foot he supports the pressing; by this he does not slip from its base.

children.text: tyam u vaḥ satrāsāham iti paryāso viśvāsu gīrṣv āyatam ity abhyāyāmyam ivaitad ahas tena caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "That battle-conquering one of yours" is the concluding <s>paryāsa</s>; "extended in all songs" is, as it were, "I come near" for this day. Thereby it is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tā u gāyatryo gāyatryo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinam vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nividdhīyate tasmād gāyatrīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses; for <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day rite. That meter carries the rite in which the <s>nivid</s> is placed. Therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses.

children.text: viśvo devasya netus tat savitur vareṇyam ā viśvadevaṃ satpatim iti vaiśvadevasya pratipadanucarau bārhate 'hani caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "All belongs to the divine leader," "that desirable thing of <s>Savitṛ</s>," and "to the all-god, the true lord" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. On the <s>Bārhata</s> day, on the fourth day, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: ā devo yātu savitā suratna iti sāvitram eti caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "May the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, rich in good treasures, come" proceeds as the <s>Sāvitra</s> verse. On the fourth day this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī namobhir iti dyāvāpṛthivīyam preti caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Forth may Heaven and Earth, with sacrifices, with reverences" is the verse addressed to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>; it has "forth." On the fourth day, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: pra ṛbhubhyo dūtam iva vācam iṣya ity ārbhavam preti ca vācam iṣya iti ca caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Forth to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, send speech as if it were a messenger" is the verse belonging to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>; it has both "forth" and "send speech forth." On the fourth day, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: pra śukraitu devī manīṣeti vaiśvadevam preti ca śukravac ca caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Forth let the bright divine thought go" is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse; it has "forth" and it has the word "bright." On the fourth day, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tā u vichandasaḥ santi dvipadāḥ santi catuṣpadās tena caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: These are in irregular meters; there are two-footed and four-footed verses. By that, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāmety āgnimārutasya pratipad ito jāta iti jātavac caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "May we be in the favor of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>" is the opening verse of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>; "born from here" has the word "born." On the fourth day, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: ka īṃ vyaktā naraḥ sanīﾱā iti mārutaṃ nakir hy eṣāṃ janūṃṣi vedeti jātavac caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Who have manifested them, the men, sanī[?]ā" is a verse to the <s>Maruts</s>; "for no one knows their births" has the birth-form. On the fourth day, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tā u vichandasaḥ santi dvipadāḥ santi catuṣpadās tena caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: These are in irregular meters; there are two-footed and four-footed verses. By that, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: jātavedase sunavāma somam iti jātavedasyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "For <s>Jātavedas</s> let us press the soma" is the fixed <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse.

children.text: agniṃ naro dīdhitibhir araṇyor iti jātavedasyaṃ hastacyutī janayanteti jātavac caturthe 'hani caturthasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Men, with their flames, from the two fire-sticks, [generated] Agni" is a <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse; "generating him by movements of the hands" has the birth-form. On the fourth day, this is the form of the fourth day.

children.text: tā u vichandasaḥ santi virājaḥ santi triṣṭubhas tena caturthasyāhno rūpam ahno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: These are in irregular meters; there are <s>Virāj</s> and <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses. By that, this is the form of the fourth day, the form of the day.

children.text: Chapter 159
gaur vai devatā pañcamam ahar vahati triṇavaḥ stomaḥ śākvaraṃ sāma paṅktiś chando yathādevatam enena yathāstomaṃ yathāsāma yathāchandasaṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The cow is the deity that carries the fifth day; the <s>stoma</s> is twenty-sevenfold, the <s>sāman</s> is <s>Śākvara</s>, and the meter is <s>Paṅkti</s>. By this he succeeds according to the deity, according to the <s>stoma</s>, according to the <s>sāman</s>, and according to the meter, who knows thus.

children.text: yad vai neti na preti yat sthitaṃ tat pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever neither comes hither nor goes forth, whatever is stationary, that is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: yaddhyeva dvitīyam ahas tad etat punar yat pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: For what is the second day, that again is this, namely the fifth.

children.text: yad ūrdhvavad yat prativad yad antarvad yad vṛṣaṇvad yad vṛdhanvad yan madhyame pade devatā nirucyate yad antarikṣam abhyuditam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has an upward form, whatever has a counter-form, whatever has an inner form, whatever has a bull-form, whatever has a growth-form, whatever names the deity in the middle verse-foot, whatever is proclaimed toward the midspace,

children.text: yad dugdhavad yad ūdhavad yad dhenumad yat pṛśnimad yan madvad yat paśurūpaṃ yad adhyāsavad vikṣudrā iva hi paśavo yaj jāgataṃ jāgatā hi paśavo yad bārhatam bārhatā hi paśavo yat pāṅktam pāṅktā hi paśavo yad vāmaṃ vāmam hi paśavo yaddhaviṣmaddhavir hi paśavo yad vapuṣmad vapur hi paśavo yacchākvaraṃ yat pāṅktaṃ yat kurvad yad dvitīyasyāhno rūpam etāni vai pañcamasyāhno rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: whatever has milk, whatever has an udder, whatever has a milch cow, whatever has <s>Pṛśni</s>, whatever has exhilaration, whatever has the form of cattle, whatever has an overlying form, for cattle are like small creatures; whatever is <s>Jagatī</s>, for cattle are <s>Jagatī</s>; whatever is <s>Bārhata</s>, for cattle are <s>Bārhata</s>; whatever is <s>Pāṅkta</s>, for cattle are <s>Pāṅkta</s>; whatever is pleasant, for cattle are pleasant; whatever has oblation, for cattle are oblation; whatever has beauty, for cattle are beauty; whatever is <s>Śākvara</s>, whatever is <s>Pāṅkta</s>, whatever has action, whatever is the form of the second day: these indeed are the forms of the fifth day.

children.text: imam ū ṣu vo atithim uṣarbudham iti pañcamasyāhna ājyam bhavati jāgatam adhyāsavat paśurūpam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "This guest of yours, awakening at dawn" is the <s>ājya</s> verse of the fifth day. It is <s>Jagatī</s>, has an overlying form, and has the form of cattle. On the fifth day, this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: ā no yajñaṃ divispṛśam ā no vāyo mahe tane rathena pṛthupājasā bahavaḥ sūracakṣasa imā u vāṃ diviṣṭayaḥ pibā sutasya rasino devaṃ devaṃ vo 'vase devaṃ devam bṛhad u gāyiṣe vaca iti bārhatam praugam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "To us may the sacrifice that touches heaven," "to us, O <s>Vāyu</s>, for great offspring," "with a broad-ribbed chariot," "many are the sun-eyed ones," "these ascents to heaven of you two," "drink of the juicy pressed soma," "god after god for your aid," and "for god after god I will sing the lofty song" are the <s>Bārhata</s> <s>praüga</s>. On the fifth day, this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: yat pāñcajanyayā viśeti marutvatīyasya pratipat pāñcajanyayeti pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "With the fivefold people" is the opening verse of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>; because it has "fivefold people," on the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: indra it somapā eka indra nedīya ed ihy ut tiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate 'gnir netā tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinvanty apo bṛhad indrāya gāyateti dvitīyenāhnā samāna ātānaḥ pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Indra</s> alone is the soma-drinker," "<s>Indra</s>, come here nearer," "Rise up, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>," "<s>Agni</s> is the leader," "you, O <s>Soma</s>, by your powers," "the waters swell," and "sing the <s>Bṛhat</s> for <s>Indra</s>" have the same extension as on the second day. On the fifth day, this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: avitāsi sunvato vṛktabarhiṣa iti sūktam madvat pāṅktam pañcapadam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "You are the helper of the soma-presser whose barhis is cut" has exhilaration, is <s>Pāṅkta</s>, and has five feet. On the fifth day, this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: itthā hi soma in mada iti sūktam madvat pāṅktam pañcapadam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "Thus indeed, O <s>Soma</s>, in exhilaration" has exhilaration, is <s>Pāṅkta</s>, and has five feet. On the fifth day, this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: indra piba tubhyaṃ suto madāyeti sūktam madvat traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "<s>Indra</s>, drink; for you it has been pressed for exhilaration" has exhilaration and is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With its firmly established foot it has supported the pressing; by this he does not fall away from his own place.

children.text: marutvāṁ indra mīḍhva iti paryāso neti na preti pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Indra</s> with the <s>Maruts</s>, bountiful one" is the closing turn; it has neither "comes" nor "goes forth." On the fifth day, this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: tā u gāyatryo gāyatryo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nividdhīyate tasmād gāyatrīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: These are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses. <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day sequence. That meter indeed carries that in which the <s>nivid</s> is inserted; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among the <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses.

children.text: Chapter 160
mahānāmnīṣv atra stuvate śākvareṇa sāmnā rāthaṃtare 'hani pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: Here they chant among the <s>Mahānāmnī</s> verses with the <s>Śākvara</s> <s>sāman</s>, on the <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> day, on the fifth day. This is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: indro vā etābhir mahān ātmānaṃ niramimīta tasmān mahānāmnyo 'tho ime vai lokā mahānāmnya ime mahāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With these, <s>Indra</s>, being great, fashioned himself; therefore they are called <s>Mahānāmnī</s>. Moreover, these worlds are the <s>Mahānāmnī</s> verses, for these are great.

children.text: imān vai lokān prajāpatiḥ sṛṣṭvedaṃ sarvam aśaknod yad idam kiṃca yad imāṃllokān prajāpatiḥ sṛṣṭvedaṃ sarvam aśaknod yad idaṃ kiṃca tac chakvaryo 'bhavaṃs tac chakvarīṇāṃ śakvarītvam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created these worlds, was able to do all this, whatever there is here. Since <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created these worlds, was able to do all this, whatever there is here, those became <s>Śakvarī</s> verses. That is the <s>Śakvarī</s>-nature of the <s>Śakvarī</s> verses.

children.text: tā ūrdhvāḥ sīmno 'bhyasṛjata yad ūrdhvāḥ sīmno 'bhyasṛjata tat simā abhavaṃs tat simānāṃ simātvam ||
children.translated_text: He sent them forth upward beyond the boundary. Since he sent them forth upward beyond the boundary, they became boundaries. That is the boundary-nature of boundaries.

children.text: svādor itthā viṣūvata upa no haribhiḥ sutam indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhann ity anurūpo vṛṣaṇvān pṛśnimān madvān vṛdhanvān pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The corresponding verse is '<s>Svādor itthā viṣūvata</s>, <s>upa no haribhiḥ sutam</s>, all have made <s>Indra</s> grow.' It contains a bull, a speckled one, intoxication, and growth; on the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: yad vāvāneti dhāyyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>dhāyyā</s> verse beginning '<s>Yad vāvāna</s>' is fixed in place.

children.text: abhi tvā śūra nonuma iti rathaṃtarasya yonim anu nivartayati rāthaṃtaraṃ hy etad ahar āyatanena ||
children.translated_text: With '<s>Abhi tvā śūra nonuma</s>' he turns back toward the source of the <s>Rathantara</s>, for this day is <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> by its support.

children.text: mo ṣu tvā vāghataś caneti sāmapragātho 'dhyāsavān paśurūpam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Mo ṣu tvā vāghataś cana</s>' is the <s>sāma-pragātha</s>; it has an <s>adhyāsa</s> and the form of cattle. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam iti tārkṣyo 'cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam</s>' is the fixed verse to <s>Tārkṣya</s>.

children.text: Chapter 161
predam brahma vṛtratūryeṣv āvitheti sūktam pāṅktam pañcapadam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn '<s>Predam brahma vṛtratūryeṣv āvitā</s>' is in the <s>Paṅkti</s> meter and has five feet. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: indro madāya vāvṛdha iti sūktam madvat pāṅktam pañcapadam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn '<s>Indro madāya vāvṛdha</s>' contains intoxication, is in the <s>Paṅkti</s> meter, and has five feet. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: satrā madāsas tava viśvajanyā iti sūktam madvat traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: The hymn '<s>Satrā madāsas tava viśvajanyāḥ</s>' contains intoxication and is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter. With its firmly established foot he supports the pressing; by this he does not slip from the support.

children.text: tam indraṃ vājayāmasīti paryāsaḥ sa vṛṣā vṛṣabho bhuvad iti paśurūpam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Tam indraṃ vājayāmasi</s>' is the closing formula; '<s>Sa vṛṣā vṛṣabho bhuvat</s>' has the form of cattle. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: tā u gāyatryo gāyatryo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nividdhīyate tasmād gāyatrīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Those are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses. <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day sequence. That meter indeed carries in which the <s>nivid</s> is placed; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among the <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses.

children.text: tat savitur vṛṇīmahe 'dyā no deva savitar iti vaiśvadevasya pratipadanucarau rāthaṃtare 'hani pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Tat savitur vṛṇīmahe</s>' and '<s>Adyā no deva savitar</s>' are the opening and following verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. On the <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> day, on the fifth day, this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā damūnā iti sāvitram ā dāśuṣe suvati bhūri vāmam iti vāmam paśurūpam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā damūnāḥ</s>' is the verse to <s>Savitṛ</s>; '<s>Ā dāśuṣe suvati bhūri vāmam</s>' contains what is desirable and has the form of cattle. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: mahī dyāvāpṛthivī iha jyeṣṭhe iti dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ ruvaddhokṣeti paśurūpam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Mahī dyāvāpṛthivī iha jyeṣṭhe</s>' is addressed to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>; '<s>ruvad dhokṣā</s>' has the form of cattle. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: ṛbhur vibhvā vāja indro no acchety ārbhavaṃ vājo vai paśavaḥ paśurūpam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Ṛbhur vibhvā vāja indro no accheti</s>' belongs to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>. <s>Vāja</s> means cattle; it has the form of cattle. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: stuṣe janaṃ suvrataṃ navyasībhir iti vaiśvadevam adhyāsavat paśurūpam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Stuṣe janaṃ suvrataṃ navyasībhiḥ</s>' is a <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse; it has an <s>adhyāsa</s> and the form of cattle. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: haviṣpāntam ajaraṃ svarvidīty āgnimārutasya pratipaddhaviṣmat pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Haviṣpāntam ajaraṃ svarvid</s>' is the opening verse of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>; it contains oblation. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: vapur nu tac cikituṣe cid astv iti mārutaṃ vapuṣmat pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Vapur nu tac cikituṣe cid astu</s>' is addressed to the <s>Maruts</s> and contains bodily form. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: jātavedase sunavāma somam iti jātavedasyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Jātavedase sunavāma somam</s>' is the fixed <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse.

children.text: agnir hotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājeti jātavedasyam adhyāsavat paśurūpam pañcame 'hani pañcamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Agnir hotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājā</s>' is a <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse; it has an <s>adhyāsa</s> and the form of cattle. On the fifth day this is the form of the fifth day.

children.text: Chapter 162
devakṣetraṃ vā etad yat ṣaṣṭham ahar devakṣetraṃ vā eta āgacchanti ye ṣaṣṭham ahar āgacchanti ||
children.translated_text: This, namely the sixth day, is a field of the gods. Those who come to the sixth day come to a field of the gods.

children.text: na vai devā anyonyasya gṛhe vasanti nartur ṛtor gṛhe vasatīty āhus tad yathāyatham ṛtvija ṛtuyājān yajanty asaṃpradāyaṃ tad yathartv ṛtūn kalpayanti yathāyathaṃ janatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods do not dwell in one another's houses; nor does one season dwell in the house of another season, they say. Therefore the priests perform the seasonal offerings each in its proper way, without interchange; according to the season they arrange the seasons, and according to their kinds the peoples.

children.text: tad āhur nartupraiṣaiḥ preṣitavyaṃ nartupraiṣair vaṣaṭkṛtyaṃ vāg vā ṛtupraiṣā āpyate vai vāk ṣaṣṭhe 'hanīti ||
children.translated_text: They say: one should not give the summons with season-summons, and one should not utter <s>vaṣaṭ</s> with season-summons. Speech itself is the season-summons; speech is fully reached on the sixth day.

children.text: yad ṛtupraiṣaiḥ preṣyeyur yad ṛtupraiṣair vaṣaṭkuryur vācam eva tad āptāṃ śrāntām ṛkṇavahīṃ vaharāviṇīm ṛccheyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If they were to summon with season-summons, or if they were to utter <s>vaṣaṭ</s> with season-summons, they would run into speech already reached, wearied, impaired in its carrying and bearing.

children.text: yad v ebhir na preṣyeyur yad v ebhir na vaṣaṭkuryur acyutād yajñasya cyaveran yajñāt prāṇāt prajāpateḥ paśubhyo jihmā īyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if they were not to summon with these, or if they were not to utter <s>vaṣaṭ</s> with these, they would be shaken from the fixed sacrifice; they would go crookedly away from the sacrifice, from breath, from <s>Prajāpati</s>, and from the cattle.

children.text: tasmād ṛgmebhya evādhi preṣitavyam ṛgmebhyo 'dhi vaṣaṭkṛtyaṃ tan na vācam āptāṃ śrāntām ṛkṇavahīṃ vaharāviṇīm ṛcchanti nācyutād yajñasya cyavante na yajñāt prāṇāt prajāpateḥ paśubhyo jihmā yanti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the summons should be made on the basis of the <s>ṛgma</s> verses, and the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> should be uttered on the basis of the <s>ṛgma</s> verses. Then they do not run into speech already reached, wearied, impaired in its carrying and bearing; nor are they shaken from the fixed sacrifice, nor do they go crookedly away from the sacrifice, from breath, from <s>Prajāpati</s>, or from the cattle.

children.text: Chapter 163
pārucchepīr upadadhati pūrvayoḥ savanayoḥ purastāt prasthitayājyānāṃ rohitaṃ vai nāmaitac chando yat pārucchepam etena vā indraḥ sapta svargāṃllokān arohat ||
children.translated_text: They insert the <s>Pārucchepī</s> verses before the <s>prasthita-yājyā</s> verses at the first two pressings. This meter, namely the <s>Pārucchepa</s>, is called <s>Rohita</s>; with it <s>Indra</s> ascended the seven heavenly worlds.

children.text: rohati sapta svargāṃllokān ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He ascends the seven heavenly worlds, who knows thus.

children.text: tad āhur yat pañcapadā eva pañcamasyāhno rūpaṃ ṣaṭpadāḥ ṣaṣṭhasyātha kasmāt saptapadāḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hañchasyanta iti ||
children.translated_text: They say: since five-footed verses are the form of the fifth day and six-footed verses of the sixth, why then are seven-footed verses recited on the sixth day?

children.text: ṣaḍbhir eva padaiḥ ṣaṣṭham ahar āpnuvanty apacchidyevaitad ahar yat saptamaṃ tad eva saptamena padenābhyārabhya vasanti vācam eva tat punar upayanti saṃtatyai ||
children.translated_text: With six feet they attain the sixth day. That day which is the seventh would be cut off; taking hold of it with the seventh foot, they remain. Thereby they return again to speech, for continuity.

children.text: saṃtatais tryahair avyavacchinnair yanti ya evaṃ vidvāṃso yanti ||
children.translated_text: Those who go knowing thus go by continuous, unbroken three-day sequences.

children.text: Chapter 164

devāsurā vā eṣu lokeṣu samayatanta te vai devāḥ ṣaṣṭhenaivāhnaibhyo lokebhyo 'surān prāṇudanta teṣāṃ yāny antarhastīnāni vasūny āsaṃs tāny ādāya samudram praupyanta ta etenaiva chandasānuhāyāntarhastīnāni vasūny ādadata tad yad etat padam punaḥpadaṃ sa evāṅkuśa āsañjanāya ||
children.translated_text: The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> were contending over these worlds. By the sixth day the gods drove the <s>Asuras</s> away from these worlds. Taking the goods that were in their hands, they plunged into the ocean. Following after with this very meter, they seized the goods that were in their hands. And the repeated foot here was the goad for hooking them on.

children.text: adviṣato vasu datte nir enam ebhyaḥ sarvebhyo lokebhyo nudate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He takes wealth from the enemy; he drives him out from all these worlds, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 165
dyaur vai devatā ṣaṣṭham ahar vahati trayastriṃśaḥ stomo raivataṃ sāmātichandāś chando yathādevatam enena yathāstomaṃ yathāsāma yathāchandasaṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Heaven is the deity that carries the sixth day; the <s>stoma</s> is thirty-threefold, the <s>sāman</s> is <s>Raivata</s>, and the meter is <s>Atichandas</s>. By this he prospers according to the deity, according to the <s>stoma</s>, according to the <s>sāman</s>, and according to the meter, who knows thus.

children.text: yad vai samānodarkaṃ tat ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ yaddhyeva tṛtīyam ahas tad etat punar yat ṣaṣṭhaṃ yad aśvavad yad antavad yat punarāvṛttaṃ yat punarninṛttaṃ yad ratavad yat paryastavad yat trivad yad antarūpaṃ yad uttame pade devatā nirucyate yad asau loko 'bhyuditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has the same conclusion is the form of the sixth day. For what is the third day, that again is this, namely the sixth: whatever has a horse, whatever has an ending, whatever is repeated, whatever is turned back again, whatever has a chariot, whatever has an overturning, whatever is threefold, whatever has an inner form, whatever names the deity in the last foot, and whatever is proclaimed upward as that world above.

children.text: yat pārucchepaṃ yat saptapadaṃ yan nārāśaṃsaṃ yan nābhānediṣṭhaṃ yad raivataṃ yad atichandā yat kṛtaṃ yat tṛtīyasyāhno rūpaṃ etāni vai ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is <s>Pārucchepa</s>, whatever is seven-footed, whatever is <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s>, whatever is <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>, whatever is <s>Raivata</s>, whatever is <s>Atichandas</s>, whatever is performed, and whatever is the form of the third day: these indeed are the forms of the sixth day.

children.text: ayaṃ jāyata manuṣo dharīmaṇīti ṣaṣṭhasyāhna ājyam bhavati pārucchepam atichandāḥ saptapadaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "This one was born in the support of <s>Manuṣa</s>" is the <s>ājya</s> verse of the sixth day. It is <s>Pārucchepa</s>, <s>Atichandas</s>, and seven-footed; on the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: stīrṇam barhir upa no yāhi vītaya ā vāṃ ratho niyutvān vakṣad avase suṣumā yātam adribhir yuvāṃ stomebhir devayanto aśvinā var maha indra vṛṣann indrāstu śrauṣaﾱ o ṣū ṇo agne śṛṇuhi tvam īﾱito ye devāso divy ekādaśa stheyam adadād rabhasam ṛṇacyutam iti praugam pārucchepam atichandāḥ saptapadaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "The <s>barhis</s> has been strewn; come to us for the feast. May your chariot with its teams bring you two here for aid. Come well pressed by the stones. Worshipping with hymns, O <s>Aśvins</s>, you two. We choose great <s>Indra</s>, the bull. Let <s>Indra</s> listen. O <s>Agni</s>, hear us, you who are invoked. The gods who are eleven in heaven. <s>Stheya</s> gave the impetuous debt-removing one" is the <s>praüga</s>. It is <s>Pārucchepa</s>, <s>Atichandas</s>, and seven-footed; on the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: sa pūrvyo mahānām iti marutvatīyasya pratipad anto vai mahad antaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "He, the ancient one among the great" is the opening verse of the <s>Marutvatīya</s>. The word "great" is an end, and the sixth day is an end. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: traya indrasya somā indra nedīya ed ihi pra nūnam brahmaṇaspatir agnir netā tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinvanty apo nakiḥ sudāso ratham iti tṛtīyenāhnā samāna ātānaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "The three Soma draughts of <s>Indra</s>; O <s>Indra</s>, come nearer; now let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth; <s>Agni</s> is the leader; you, O <s>Soma</s>, by your powers; the waters swell; no one the chariot of <s>Sudās</s>" have the same extension as on the third day. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: yaṃ tvaṃ ratham indra medhasātaya iti sūktam pārucchepam atichandāḥ saptapadaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "The chariot which you, O <s>Indra</s>, for the winning of wisdom" is <s>Pārucchepa</s>, <s>Atichandas</s>, and seven-footed; on the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: sa yo vṛṣā vṛṣṇyebhiḥ samokā iti sūktaṃ samānodarkaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "He who, a bull, together with the virile ones, shares one home" has the same conclusion. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: indra marutva iha pāhi somam iti sūktaṃ tebhiḥ sākam pibatu vṛtrakhāda ity anto vai khādo 'ntaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "O <s>Indra</s> with the <s>Maruts</s>, drink the Soma here" ends with "Let him drink together with them, the devourer of <s>Vṛtra</s>." Devouring is an end, and the sixth day is an end. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With that firmly placed foot he supports the pressing; by this he does not fall away from its base.

children.text: ayaṃ ha yena vā idam iti paryāsaḥ svar marutvatā jitam ity anto vai jitam antaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "This indeed, by which this" is the concluding <s>paryāsa</s>; it ends with "the heavenly world has been won by the one accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>." Winning is an end, and the sixth day is an end. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: tā u gāyatryo gāyatryo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nivid dhīyate tasmād gāyatrīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses. <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day sequence. That meter indeed carries that in which the <s>nivid</s> is inserted; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among the <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses.

children.text: revatīr naḥ sadhamāde revāṁ id revata stoteti raivatam pṛṣṭham bhavati bārhate 'hani ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "May the wealthy ones be with us at the common feast; praise the wealthy, wealth-giving one" is the <s>Raivata pṛṣṭha</s>. On the <s>Bārhata</s> day, on the sixth day, this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: yad vāvāneti dhāyyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "Whatever has indeed been won" is a fixed <s>dhāyyā</s> verse.

children.text: tvām iddhi havāmaha iti bṛhato yonim anu nivartayati bārhataṃ hy etad ahar āyatanena ||
children.translated_text: With "You indeed we call" he turns back according to the womb of the <s>Bṛhat</s>; for this is a <s>Bārhata</s> day by its base.

children.text: indram id devatātaya iti sāmapragātho ninṛttavān ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Indra</s> indeed, for divine help" is the <s>sāma-pragātha</s>; it has turning back. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam iti tārkṣyo 'cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "That swift steed, impelled by the gods" is the fixed verse to <s>Tārkṣya</s>.

children.text: Chapter 166
endra yāhy upa naḥ parāvata iti sūktam pārucchepam atichandāḥ saptapadaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "O <s>Indra</s>, come here to us from afar" is <s>Pārucchepa</s>, <s>Atichandas</s>, and seven-footed; on the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: pra ghā nv asya mahato mahānīti sūktaṃ samānodarkaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "Now indeed, of this great one, the greatness" has the same conclusion. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: abhūr eko rayipate rayīṇām iti sūktaṃ ratham ā tiṣṭha tuvinṛmṇa bhīmam ity anto vai sthitam antaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "You became the sole lord of riches, O lord of wealth" ends with "Mount the chariot, terrible one of many powers." Standing is an end, and the sixth day is an end. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With that firmly placed foot he supports the pressing; by this he does not fall away from its base.

children.text: upa no haribhiḥ sutam iti paryāsaḥ samānodarkaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Come to our pressed Soma with your bay horses" is the concluding <s>paryāsa</s>; it has the same conclusion. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: tā u gāyatryo gāyatryo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nivid dhīyate tasmād gāyatrīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses. <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day sequence. That meter indeed carries that in which the <s>nivid</s> is inserted; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among the <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses.

children.text: abhi tyaṃ devaṃ savitāram oṇyor iti vaiśvadevasya pratipad atichandāḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Toward that god <s>Savitṛ</s> on the two laps" is the opening verse of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>; it is <s>Atichandas</s>. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: tat savitur vareṇyaṃ doṣo āgād ity anucaro 'nto vai gatam antaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "That desirable thing of <s>Savitṛ</s>," and "evening has come" are the following verse and the end. What has gone to the end is the end; the sixth day is an end. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā savāyeti sāvitraṃ śaśvattamaṃ tadapā vahnir asthād ity anto vai sthitam antaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Up has that god <s>Savitṛ</s> risen to impel," is the <s>Sāvitra</s> verse, most constant; "then <s>Vahni</s> stood away" is the end. What has stood is the end; the sixth day is an end. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: katarā pūrvā katarāparāyor iti dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ samānodarkaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Which of the two is earlier, which is later?" is the verse to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>, having the same conclusion. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kiṃ yaviṣṭho na ājagann upa no vājā adhvaram ṛbhukṣā ity ārbhavaṃ nārāśaṃsaṃ trivat ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Who is best, who youngest, has come to us? Come to our sacrifice, O strength-bringing <s>Ṛbhus</s>," is the <s>Ārbhava</s> <s>Nārāśaṃsa</s>, threefold. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: idam itthā raudraṃ gūrtavacā ye yajñena dakṣiṇayā samaktā iti vaiśvadevam ||
children.translated_text: "This, just thus, is the <s>Raudra</s>, with weighty speech," and "those who are united by sacrifice and by the sacrificial gift" form the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.

children.text: Chapter 167
nābhānediṣṭhaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>.

children.text: nābhānediṣṭhaṃ vai mānavam brahmacaryaṃ vasantam bhrātaro nirabhajan so 'bravīd etya kim mahyam abhāktety etam eva niṣṭhāvam avavaditāram ity abruvaṃs tasmāddhāpyetarhi pitaram putrā niṣṭhāvo 'vavaditety evācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: Now the brothers excluded <s>Nābhānediṣṭha Mānava</s> while he was living as a student. He said, when he had come back, "What have they allotted to me?" They said, "This very <s>niṣṭhāva</s>, the reprover." Therefore even now sons call a father simply "the <s>niṣṭhāva</s>, the reprover."

children.text: sa pitaram etyābravīt tvāṃ ha vāva mahyam tatābhākṣur iti tam pitābravīn mā putraka tad ādṛthā aṅgiraso vā ime svargāya lokāya satram āsate te ṣaṣṭhaṃ ṣaṣṭham evāhar āgatya muhyanti tān ete sūkte ṣaṣṭhe 'hani śaṃsaya teṣāṃ yat sahasraṃ satrapariveṣaṇaṃ tat te svar yanto dāsyantīti tatheti ||
children.translated_text: He went to his father and said, "Father, they have in fact allotted you to me." His father said to him, "Do not take that to heart, my dear son. These <s>Aṅgirases</s> are sitting in a <s>sattra</s> for the heavenly world. Coming to each sixth day, each sixth day, they become confused. Have them recite these two hymns on the sixth day. The thousand that is the attendance-gift for the <s>sattra</s>, they will give to you as they go to heaven." "So be it," he said.

children.text: tān upait prati gṛbhṇīta mānavaṃ sumedhasa iti tam abruvan kiṃkāmo vadasītīdam eva vaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ prajñāpayānīty abravīd atha yad va etat sahasraṃ satrapariveṣaṇaṃ tan me svar yanto datteti tatheti tān ete sūkte ṣaṣṭhe 'hani aśaṃsayat tato vai te pra yajñam ajānan pra svargaṃ lokam ||
children.translated_text: He approached them with, "Accept the <s>Mānava</s>, the wise one." They said to him, "With what desire do you speak?" He said, "I will make this sixth day known to you. Then, as for that thousand of yours, the attendance-gift for the <s>sattra</s>, give it to me as you go to heaven." "So be it," they said. He had them recite these two hymns on the sixth day; then indeed they understood the sacrifice and the heavenly world.

children.text: tad yad ete sūkte ṣaṣṭhe 'hani śaṃsati yajñasya prajñātyai svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when he recites these two hymns on the sixth day, it is for the recognition of the sacrifice and for the disclosure of the heavenly world.

children.text: taṃ svar yanto 'bruvann etat te brāhmaṇa sahasram iti tad enaṃ samākurvāṇam puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇaśavāsy uttarata upotthāyābravīn mama vā idam mama vai vāstuham iti so 'bravīn mahyaṃ vā idam adur iti tam abravīt tad vai nau tavaiva pitari praśna iti sa pitaram ait tam pitābravīn nanu te putrakādūr ity adur eva ma ity abravīt tat tu me puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇaśavāsy uttarata upodatiṣṭhan mama vā idam mama vai vāstuham ity āditeti tam pitābravīt tasyaiva putraka tat tat tu sa tubhyaṃ dāsyatīti sa punar etyābravīt tava ha vāva kila bhagava idam iti me pitāheti so 'bravīt tad ahaṃ tubhyam eva dadāmi ya eva satyam avādīr iti ||
children.translated_text: As they were going to heaven, they said to him, "This thousand is yours, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>." As he was gathering it together, a man clothed in a black hide rose up from the north and said, "This is mine; this indeed is my dwelling-place." He said, "But they gave this to me." The man replied, "Then this question of ours is for your father alone." He went to his father. His father said to him, "Did they not give it to you, my dear son?" "They did give it to me," he said, "but a man clothed in a black hide stood up beside me from the north, saying, 'This is mine; this indeed is my dwelling-place.'" His father said to him, "That, my dear son, belongs to him alone, but he will give it to you." He went back again and said, "My father says that this truly is yours, lord." The man said, "Then I give it to you alone, because you have spoken the truth."

children.text: tasmād evaṃ viduṣā satyam eva vaditavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one who knows thus should speak only the truth.

children.text: sa eṣa sahasrasanir mantro yan nābhānediṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the thousand-winning mantra, namely the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>.

children.text: upainaṃ sahasraṃ namati pra ṣaṣṭhenāhnā svargaṃ lokaṃ jānāti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: A thousand bends toward him; through the sixth day he knows the heavenly world, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 168
tāny etāni sahacarāṇy ity ācakṣate nābhānediṣṭhaṃ vālakhilyā vṛṣākapim evayāmarutaṃ tāni sahaiva śaṃset ||
children.translated_text: These are called the accompanying ones: the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>, the <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses, the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, and the <s>Evayāmaruta</s>. He should recite them together.

children.text: yad eṣām antariyāt tad yajamānasyāntariyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he were to separate one of them, he would separate something belonging to the sacrificer.

children.text: yadi nābhānediṣṭhaṃ reto 'syāntariyād yadi vālakhilyāḥ prāṇān asyāntariyād yadi vṛṣākapim ātmānam asyāntariyād yady evayāmarutam pratiṣṭhāyā enaṃ cyāvayed daivyai ca mānuṣyai ca ||
children.translated_text: If he were to separate the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>, he would separate his seed; if the <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses, he would separate his vital breaths; if the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, he would separate his self; if the <s>Evayāmaruta</s>, he would make him fall from his foundation, both divine and human.

children.text: nābhānediṣṭhenaiva reto 'siñcat tad vālakhilyābhir vyakarot sukīrtinā kākṣīvatena yoniṃ vyahāpayad urau yathā tava śarman mademeti tasmāj jyāyān san garbhaḥ kanīyāṃsaṃ santam yoniṃ na hinasti brahmaṇā hi sa kﾱpta evayāmarutaitavai karoti tenedaṃ sarvam etavai kṛtam eti yad idaṃ kiṃca ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> he poured in seed; with the <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses he distributed it; with the <s>Sukīrtin Kākṣīvata</s> he made the womb open, with "as in your wide shelter may we rejoice." Therefore an embryo, though greater, does not injure the womb, though it is smaller, for it has been fitted by <s>brahman</s>. With the <s>Evayāmaruta</s> he sets this in motion; by it all this, whatever exists here, has been made to move.

children.text: ahaś ca kṛṣṇam ahar arjunaṃ cety āgnimārutasya pratipad ahaś cāhaś ceti punarāvṛttam punarninṛttaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "The day and the black one, and the day and the bright one" is the opening verse of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>; "day after day" is repeated and turned back. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: madhvo vo nāma mārutaṃ yajatrā iti mārutam bahvabhivyāhṛtyam anto vai bahv antaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Your name is honey-sweet, O worshipful <s>Maruts</s>," is the <s>Māruta</s> verse, rich in repeated utterance. The end is indeed abundant; the sixth day is an end. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: jātavedase sunavāma somam iti jātavedasyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "For <s>Jātavedas</s> let us press Soma" is the fixed <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse.

children.text: sa pratnathā sahasā jāyamāna iti jātavedasyaṃ samānodarkaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Born with force in the ancient way" is the <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse, having the same conclusion. On the sixth day this is the form of the sixth day.

children.text: dhārayan dhārayann iti śaṃsati prasraṃsād vā antasya bibhāya tad yathā punarāgrantham punarnigrantham antam badhnīyān mayūkhaṃ vāntato dhāraṇāya nihanyāt tādṛk tad yad dhārayan dhārayann iti śaṃsati saṃtatyai ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "holding, holding." Fearing that the end might slip down, it is as though one were to tie the end again with an upper knot and again with a lower knot, or were to drive in a peg at the end for holding it. Such is this. When he recites, "holding, holding," it is for continuity.

children.text: saṃtatais tryahair avyavacchinnair yanti ya evaṃ vidvāṃso yanti yanti ||
children.translated_text: With continuous, uninterrupted three-day periods they proceed, those who proceed knowing thus; they proceed.

children.text: Chapter 169
yad vā eti ca preti ca tat saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever both comes and goes forth, that is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: yaddhyeva prathamam ahas tad evaitat punar yat saptamam ||
children.translated_text: For what is the first day, that again is this, namely the seventh.

children.text: yad yuktavad yad rathavad yad āśumad yat pibavad yat prathame pade devatā nirucyate yad ayaṃ loko 'bhyuditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has the word "yoked," whatever has the word "chariot," whatever has the word "swift," whatever has the word "drink," whatever names the deity in the first foot, and whatever is proclaimed toward this world,

children.text: yaj jātavad yad aniruktam ||
children.translated_text: whatever has the word "born," whatever is not explicitly defined,

children.text: yat kariṣyad yat prathamasyāhno rūpam etāni vai saptamasyāhno rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: whatever has the word "will do," and whatever is the form of the first day: these indeed are the forms of the seventh day.

children.text: samudrād ūrmir madhumāṁ ud ārad iti saptamasyāhna ājyam bhavaty aniruktam saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "From the ocean the honeyed wave has risen" is the <s>ājya</s> verse of the seventh day. It is undefined; on the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: vāg vai samudro na vai vāk kṣīyate na samudraḥ kṣīyate tad yad etat saptamasyāhna ājyam bhavati yajñād eva tad yajñaṃ tanvate vācam eva tat punar upayanti saṃtatyai ||
children.translated_text: Speech is the ocean. Speech is not exhausted, and the ocean is not exhausted. When this is the <s>ājya</s> verse of the seventh day, thereby they extend the sacrifice from the sacrifice itself; they return to speech itself, for continuity.

children.text: saṃtatais tryahair avyavacchinnair yanti ya evaṃ vidvāṃso yanti ||
children.translated_text: With continuous, uninterrupted three-day periods they proceed, those who proceed knowing thus.

children.text: āpyante vai stomā āpyante chandāṃsi ṣaṣṭhe 'hani tad yathaivāda ājyenāvadānāni punaḥ pratyabhighārayanty ayātayāmatāyā evam evaitat stomāṃś ca chandāṃsi ca punaḥ pratyupayanty ayātayāmatāyai yad etat saptamasyāhna ājyam bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>stomas</s> are filled up, and the meters are filled up on the sixth day. Just as, in that case, they pour clarified butter again over the cut portions so that they remain fresh, so here they return again to the <s>stomas</s> and the meters so that they remain fresh, when this is the <s>ājya</s> verse of the seventh day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ triṣṭupprātaḥsavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, that is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; this three-day rite has a <s>Triṣṭubh</s> morning pressing.

children.text: ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ pra yābhir yāsi dāśvāṃsam acchā no niyudbhiḥ śatinībhir adhvaraṃ pra sotā jīro adhvareṣv asthād ye vāyava indramādanāso yā vāṃ śataṃ niyuto yāḥ sahasraṃ pra yad vām mitrāvaruṇā spūrdhann ā gomatā nāsatyā rathenā no deva śavasā yāhi śuṣmin pra vo yajñeṣu devayanto arcan pra kṣodasā dhāyasā sasra eṣeti praugam eti ca preti ca saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpaṃ tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ triṣṭupprātaḥsavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Vāyu</s>, come adorned, drinker of the pure draught, near to us; with the aids by which you go to the worshipper; toward our rite with your hundreds of teams; the swift presser has stood at the rites; those of <s>Vāyu</s> that gladden <s>Indra</s>; your hundred teams and your thousand; when <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> contend for you; with a cow-rich chariot, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>; come to us, god, with might, O powerful one; the god-loving ones have praised you in the sacrifices; it has flowed forth with nourishment and sustenance" proceeds as the <s>praüga</s>. It both comes and goes forth. On the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day. Moreover, it is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; this three-day rite has a <s>Triṣṭubh</s> morning pressing.

children.text: ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaya idaṃ vaso sutam andha indra nedīya ed ihi praitu brahmaṇaspatir agnir netā tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinvanty apaḥ pra va indrāya bṛhata iti prathamenāhnā samāna ātānaḥ saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "To you, as to a chariot for aid; this pressed drink, O <s>Vasu</s>; come nearer, O <s>Indra</s>; let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> go forth; <s>Agni</s> is the leader; you, O <s>Soma</s>, by your powers; the waters swell; forth for great <s>Indra</s>" has the same extension as on the first day. On the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīﾱā iti sūktaṃ na jāyamāno naśate na jāta iti jātavat saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "With what bright aid, companions of the same age, sanī[corrupt]ā" and "Not being born, he perishes; not born" has the word "born." On the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: tad u kayāśubhīyam etad vai saṃjñānaṃ saṃtani sūktaṃ yat kayāśubhīyam etena ha vā indro 'gastyo marutas te samajānata tad yat kayāśubhīyaṃ śaṃsati saṃjñātyā eva ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is the <s>Kayāśubhīya</s>. This <s>Kayāśubhīya</s> is indeed a hymn of recognition and continuity. By it <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agastya</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s> came to mutual understanding. Therefore, when he recites the <s>Kayāśubhīya</s>, it is precisely for mutual recognition.

children.text: tad v āyuṣyaṃ tad yo 'sya priyaḥ syāt kuryād evāsya kayāśubhīyam ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is life-giving. Therefore, if someone should be dear to him, he should perform the <s>Kayāśubhīya</s> for him.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, that is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With that firmly established foot he has supported the pressing; by this he does not fall away from its base.

children.text: tyaṃ su meṣam mahayā svarvidam iti sūktam atyaṃ na vājaṃ havanasyadaṃ ratham iti rathavat saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "Praise that ram, finder of light" and "Like a racehorse eager for the call, the chariot" has the word "chariot." On the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: tad u jāgataṃ jagatyo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nividdhīyate tasmāj jagatīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, that is <s>Jagatī</s>. <s>Jagatī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day rite. That meter indeed carries the rite in which the <s>nivid</s> is placed; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among <s>Jagatī</s> verses.

children.text: mithunāni sūktāni śasyante traiṣṭubhāni ca jāgatāni ca mithunaṃ vai paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Paired hymns are recited, both <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s>. Cattle are a pair, and the <s>chandomas</s> are cattle; this is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: tvām iddhi havāmahe tvaṃ hy ehi cerava iti bṛhatpṛṣṭham bhavati saptame 'hani ||
