children.translated_text: "You indeed we call; for you, come hither, O <s>Cerava</s>" is the <s>Bṛhatpṛṣṭha</s> on the seventh day.

children.text: yad eva ṣaṣṭhasyāhnas tat ||
children.translated_text: It is just what belongs to the sixth day.

children.text: yad vai rathaṃtaraṃ tad vairūpaṃ yad bṛhat tad vairājaṃ yad rathaṃtaraṃ tacchākvaraṃ yad bṛhat tad raivatam ||
children.translated_text: What is <s>Rathantara</s>, that is <s>Vairūpa</s>; what is <s>Bṛhat</s>, that is <s>Vairāja</s>; what is <s>Rathantara</s>, that is <s>Śākvara</s>; what is <s>Bṛhat</s>, that is <s>Raivata</s>.

children.text: tad yad bṛhatpṛṣṭham bhavati bṛhataiva tad bṛhat pratyuttabhnuvanty astomakṛntatrāya ||
children.translated_text: When it is the <s>Bṛhatpṛṣṭha</s>, they thereby prop up the <s>Bṛhat</s> with the <s>Bṛhat</s> itself, so that the <s>stoma</s> may not be cut off there.

children.text: yad rathaṃtaraṃ syāt kṛntatraṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: If it were the <s>Rathantara</s>, there would be a cutting off.

children.text: tasmād bṛhad eva kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Bṛhat</s> alone is to be performed.

children.text: yad vāvāneti dhāyyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "What indeed has won" is the unfailing <s>dhāyyā</s> verse.

children.text: abhi tvā śūra nonuma iti rathaṃtarasya yonim anu nivartayati rāthaṃtaraṃ hy etad ahar āyatanena ||
children.translated_text: With "We praise you, O hero," he turns back according to the womb of the <s>Rathantara</s>, for this is a <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> day by its base.

children.text: pibā sutasya rasina iti sāmapragāthaḥ pibavān saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Drink of the juicy pressed draught" is the <s>sāma-pragātha</s>; it has the word "drink." On the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam iti tārkṣyo 'cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "That swift steed, impelled by the gods" is the unfailing verse to <s>Tārkṣya</s>.

children.text: Chapter 170
indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam iti sūktam preti saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>" has "goes forth." On the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With that firmly established foot he supports the pressing; by this he does not fall away from its base.

children.text: abhi tyam meṣam puruhūtam ṛgmiyam iti sūktaṃ yad vāva preti tad abhīti saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Toward that ram, much-invoked, worthy of praise" is a hymn. What indeed goes forth is expressed by "toward"; on the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: tad u jāgataṃ jagatyo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nivid dhīyate tasmāj jagatīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Jagatī</s>. <s>Jagatī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day rite. That meter indeed carries that in which the <s>nivid</s> is inserted; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among <s>Jagatī</s> verses.

children.text: mithunāni sūktāni śasyante traiṣṭubhāni ca jāgatāni ca mithunaṃ vai paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Paired hymns are recited, both <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s>. Cattle are paired; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: tat savitur vṛṇīmahe 'dyā no deva savitar iti vaiśvadevasya pratipadanucarau rāthaṃtare 'hani saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "That desirable thing of <s>Savitṛ</s> we choose" and "today, O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, for us" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, on the <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> day, on the seventh day. This is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: abhi tvā deva savitar iti sāvitraṃ yad vāva preti tad abhīti saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Toward you, O god <s>Savitṛ</s>" is the <s>Sāvitra</s> verse. What indeed goes forth is expressed by "toward"; on the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: pretāṃ yajñasya śambhuveti dyāvāpṛthivīyam preti saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Let them go forth for the sacrifice, for blessing" is the verse addressed to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>. It has "go forth"; on the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: ayaṃ devāya janmana ity ārbhavaṃ jātavat saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "This one for divine birth" belongs to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>; it has birth. On the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: ā yāhi vanasā saheti dvipadāḥ śaṃsati dvipād vai puruṣaś catuṣpādāḥ paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai tad yad dvipadāḥ śaṃsati yajamānam eva tad dvipratiṣṭhaṃ catuṣpātsu paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: With "Come here together with strength" he recites two-footed verses. Man is two-footed, and cattle are four-footed; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle. When he recites two-footed verses, he thereby establishes the sacrificer, as two-footed, among the four-footed cattle.

children.text: aibhir agne duvo gira iti vaiśvadevam eti saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "With these songs of service, O <s>Agni</s>" is the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse. It goes; on the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: tāny u gāyatrāṇi gāyatratṛtīyasavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses; this three-day rite has a <s>Gāyatrī</s> third pressing.

children.text: vaiśvānaro ājījanad ity āgnimārutasya pratipaj jātavat saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Vaiśvānara</s> has generated" is the opening verse of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>. It has birth; on the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: pra yat vas triṣṭubham iṣam iti mārutaṃ preti saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "When for you, O <s>Maruts</s>, nourishment in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>" is a hymn to the <s>Maruts</s>. It has "forth"; on the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: jātavedase sunavāma somam iti jātavedasyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "For <s>Jātavedas</s> let us press Soma" is the unfailing <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse.

children.text: dūtaṃ vo viśvavedasam iti jātavedasyam aniruktaṃ saptame 'hani saptamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Your messenger, the all-knowing one" is an undefined <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse. On the seventh day this is the form of the seventh day.

children.text: tāny u gāyatrāni gāyatratṛtīyasavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses; this three-day rite has a <s>Gāyatrī</s> third pressing.

children.text: Chapter 171
yad vai neti na preti yat sthitaṃ tad aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever neither comes here nor goes forth, whatever is stationary, that is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: yaddhy eva dvitīyam ahas tad evaitat punar yad aṣṭamam ||
children.translated_text: For what is the second day is again this very one, namely the eighth.

children.text: yad ūrdhvavad yat prativad yad antarvad yad vṛṣaṇvad yad vṛdhanvad yan madhyame pade devatā nirucyate yad antarikṣam abhyuditam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has an upward form, whatever has a counter-form, whatever has an inner form, whatever has a bull-form, whatever has a growth-form, whatever names the deity in the middle foot, whatever is proclaimed toward the midspace,

children.text: yad dvyagni yan mahadvad yad dvihūtavad yat punarvad yat kurvat ||
children.translated_text: whatever has two <s>Agnis</s>, whatever has the word "great," whatever has two invocations, whatever has "again," whatever has action,

children.text: yad dvitīyasyāhno rūpam etāni vā aṣṭamasyāhno rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: whatever is the form of the second day: these indeed are the forms of the eighth day.

children.text: agniṃ vo devam agnibhiḥ sajoṣā ity aṣṭamasyāhna ājyam bhavati dvyagny aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Agni</s>, your god, together with the <s>Agnis</s>" is the <s>ājya</s> verse of the eighth day. It has two <s>Agnis</s>; on the eighth day this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ triṣṭupprātaḥsavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; this three-day rite has a <s>Triṣṭubh</s> morning pressing.

children.text: kuvid aṅga namasā ye vṛdhāsaḥ pīvoannāṁ rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhā ucchann uṣasaḥ sudinā ariprā uśantā dūtā na dabhāya gopā yāvat taras tanvo yāvad ojaḥ prati vāṃ sūra udite sūktair dhenuḥ pratnasya kāmyaṃ duhānā brahmā ṇā indropa yāhi vidvān ūrdhvo agniḥ sumatiṃ vasvo aśred uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇeti praugam prativad antarvad dvihūtavad ūrdhvavad aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Can it be that those grown by reverence, rich in food, increasing wealth, wise; the shining dawns, bright days, free from harm; the eager messengers, like guardians against deceit; as much as is your vigor, as much as the body's strength; at the sun's rising, with hymns, the milch cow, milking the ancient desired thing; O <s>Indra</s>, come near to the priests, knowing; <s>Agni</s> stands upright toward the good favor of wealth; [corrupt word]; and may <s>Sarasvatī</s> be pleased with us" is the <s>praüga</s>. It has a counter-form, an inner form, two invocations, and an upward form. On the eighth day this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ triṣṭupprātaḥsavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; this three-day rite has a <s>Triṣṭubh</s> morning pressing.

children.text: viśvānarasya vas patim indra it somapā eka indra nedīya ed ihy uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate 'gnir netā tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinvanty apo bṛhad indrāya gāyateti dvitīyenāhnā samāna ātāno 'ṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "The lord of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>'s goods," "<s>Indra</s> alone is the Soma-drinker," "<s>Indra</s>, come here nearer," "Rise up, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>," "<s>Agni</s> is the leader," "you, O <s>Soma</s>, by your powers," "the waters swell," and "sing the <s>Bṛhat</s> for <s>Indra</s>" have the same extension as on the second day. On the eighth day this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: śaṃsā mahām indraṃ yasmin viśvā iti sūktam mahadvad aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Praise great <s>Indra</s>, in whom are all things" is a hymn. It has the word "great"; on the eighth day this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: mahaś cit tvam indra yata etān iti sūktam mahadvad aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Great indeed are you, O <s>Indra</s>, from whom these" is a hymn. It has the word "great"; on the eighth day this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: pibā somam abhi yam ugra tarda iti sūktam ūrvaṃ gavyam mahi gṛṇāna indreti mahadvad aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Drink the Soma, O fierce one; break through against him" is a hymn. "Wide in cattle, great, singing, O <s>Indra</s>" has the word "great"; on the eighth day this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: mahāṁ indro nṛvad ā carṣaṇiprā iti sūktam mahadvad aṣṭame 'hani aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Great <s>Indra</s>, manly, filling the peoples" is a hymn. It has the word "great"; on the eighth day this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With that firmly established foot he supports the pressing; by this he does not fall away from its base.

children.text: tam asya dyāvāpṛthivī sacetaseti sūktaṃ yad ait kṛṇvāno mahimānam indriyam iti mahadvad aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Heaven and Earth, of one mind, [attend] this one of his" is a hymn. "When he went, fashioning greatness and lordly power" has the word "greatness"; on the eighth day this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: tad u jāgataṃ jagatyo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nivid dhīyate tasmājjagatīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Jagatī</s>. <s>Jagatī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day rite. That meter indeed carries that in which the <s>nivid</s> is inserted; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among <s>Jagatī</s> verses.

children.text: mithunāni sūktāni śasyante traiṣṭubhāni ca jāgatāni ca mithunaṃ vai paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Paired hymns are recited, both <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s>. Cattle are paired; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: mahadvanti sūktāni śasyante mahad vā antarikṣam antarikṣasyāptyai ||
children.translated_text: Hymns containing greatness are recited. The midspace is indeed great; this is for the attainment of the midspace.

children.text: pañca sūktāni śasyante pañcapadā paṅktiḥ pāṅkto yajñaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Five hymns are recited. <s>Paṅkti</s> has five feet; the sacrifice is <s>Pāṅkta</s>; cattle are <s>Pāṅkta</s>; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: abhi tvā śūra nonumo 'bhi tvā pūrvapītaya iti rathaṃtaraṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavaty aṣṭame 'hani ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ</s>" and "<s>Abhi tvā pūrvapītaye</s>" form the <s>Rathantara</s> <s>pṛṣṭha</s> on the eighth day.

children.text: yad vāvāneti dhāyyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Yad vāvāna</s>" is the fixed <s>dhāyyā</s> verse.

children.text: tvām iddhi havāmaha iti bṛhato yonim anu nivartayati bārhataṃ hy etad ahar āyatanena ||
children.translated_text: With "<s>Tvām id dhi havāmahe</s>" he turns back toward the source of the <s>Bṛhat</s>, for this day is <s>Bārhata</s> by its support.

children.text: ubhayaṃ śṛṇavacca na iti sāmapragātho yac cedam adya yad u ca hya āsīd iti bārhate 'hany aṣṭame 'hani aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Ubhayaṃ śṛṇavac ca naḥ</s>" is the <s>sāma-pragātha</s>; "<s>Yac cedam adya yad u ca hya āsīt</s>" occurs on the <s>Bārhata</s> day, on the eighth day. This is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam iti tārkṣyo 'cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam</s>" is the fixed verse to <s>Tārkṣya</s>.

children.text: Chapter 172

apūrvyā purutamāny asmā iti sūktam mahe vīrāya tavase turāyeti mahadvad aṣṭame 'hani aṣṭamasyāhno rūpaṃ tāṃ su te kīrtim maghavan mahitveti sūktam mahadvad aṣṭame 'hani aṣṭamasyāhno rūpaṃ tvam mahāṁ indra yo ha śuṣmair iti sūktam mahadvad aṣṭame 'hani aṣṭamasyāhno rūpaṃ tvam mahāṁ indra tubhyaṃ ha kṣā iti sūktam mahadvad aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "<s>Apūrvyā purutamāny asmā</s>," with "<s>Mahe vīrāya tavase turāya</s>," contains greatness on the eighth day; this is the form of the eighth day. The hymn "<s>Tāṃ su te kīrtim maghavan mahitvā</s>" contains greatness on the eighth day; this is the form of the eighth day. The hymn "<s>Tvam mahāṃ indra yo ha śuṣmaiḥ</s>" contains greatness on the eighth day; this is the form of the eighth day. The hymn "<s>Tvam mahāṃ indra tubhyaṃ ha kṣāḥ</s>" contains greatness on the eighth day; this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: That is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter. With it, by a firmly established foot, he has supported the pressing; by this he does not fall away from his own support.

children.text: divaś cid asya varimā vi papratha iti sūktam indraṃ na mahneti mahadvad aṣṭame 'hani aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The hymn "<s>Divaś cid asya varimā vi papratha</s>," with "<s>Indraṃ na mahna</s>," contains greatness on the eighth day; this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: tad u jāgataṃ jagatyo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tacchando vahati yasmin nividdhīyate tasmājjagatīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: That is in the <s>Jagatī</s> meter. The <s>Jagatī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day sequence. That meter indeed carries the rite in which the <s>nivid</s> is inserted; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among the <s>Jagatī</s> verses.

children.text: mithunāni sūktāni śasyante traiṣṭubhāni ca jāgatāni ca mithunaṃ vai paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Paired hymns are recited, both <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s>. Cattle are paired; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: mahadvanti sūktāni śasyante mahad vā antarikṣam antarikṣasyāptyai pañca pañca sūktāni śasyante pañcapadā paṅktiḥ pāṅkto yajñaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Hymns containing greatness are recited. The midspace is indeed great; this is for the attainment of the midspace. Five and five hymns are recited. <s>Paṅkti</s> has five feet; the sacrifice is <s>Pāṅkta</s>; cattle are <s>Pāṅkta</s>; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: tāni dvedhā pañcānyāni pañcānyāni daśa sampadyante sā daśinī virāﾱ annam virāﾱ annam paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: These, divided in two, five on one side and five on the other, come to be ten. That tenfold <s>Virāj</s> is food; <s>Virāj</s> is food; cattle are food; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: viśvo devasya netus tat savitur vareṇyam ā viśvadevaṃ satpatim iti vaiśvadevasya pratipadanucarau bārhate 'hani aṣṭame 'hani aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Viśvo devasya netuḥ</s>," "<s>Tat savitur vareṇyam</s>," and "<s>Ā viśvadevaṃ satpatim</s>" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. On the <s>Bārhata</s> day, on the eighth day, this is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaya iti sāvitram ūrdhvavad aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaye</s>" is the verse to <s>Savitṛ</s>; it has an upward form on the eighth day. This is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivīyam mahadvad aṣṭame 'hani aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ</s>" is addressed to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>; it contains greatness on the eighth day. This is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: yuvānā pitarā punar ity ārbhavam punarvad aṣṭame 'hani aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Yuvānā pitarā punaḥ</s>" belongs to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>; it contains return on the eighth day. This is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: imā nu kam bhuvanā sīṣadhāmeti dvipadāḥ śaṃsati dvipād vai puruṣaś catuṣpādāḥ paśavaḥ paśavaśchandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai tad yad dvipadāḥ śaṃsati yajamānam eva tad dvipratiṣṭhaṃ catuṣpātsu paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the two-footed verses beginning "<s>Imā nu kam bhuvanā sīṣadhāma</s>." Man is two-footed, while cattle are four-footed; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle. In that he recites two-footed verses, he thereby establishes the sacrificer, who has two supports, among the four-footed cattle.

children.text: devānām id avo mahad iti vaiśvadevam mahadvad aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Devānām id avo mahat</s>" is a <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse; it contains greatness on the eighth day. This is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: tāny u gāyatrāṇi gāyatratṛtīyasavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. This three-day sequence has a third pressing carried by <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: ṛtāvānaṃ vaiśvānaram ity āgnimārutasya pratipad agnir vaiśvānaro mahān iti mahadvad aṣṭame 'hanyaṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Ṛtāvānaṃ vaiśvānaram</s>" is the opening verse of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>; "<s>Agnir vaiśvānaro mahān</s>" contains greatness on the eighth day. This is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: krīﾱaṃ vaḥ śardho mārutam iti mārutaṃ jambhe rasasya vāvṛdha iti vṛdhanvad aṣṭame 'hany aṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Krīḍaṃ vaḥ śardho mārutam</s>" is addressed to the <s>Maruts</s>; "<s>Jambhe rasasya vāvṛdhe</s>" contains growth on the eighth day. This is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: jātavedase sunavāma somam iti jātavedasyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Jātavedase sunavāma somam</s>" is the fixed <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse.

children.text: agne mṛﾱa mahāṁ asīti jātavedasyam mahadvad aṣṭame 'hanyaṣṭamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Agne mṛḍa mahāṃ asi</s>" is a <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse; it contains greatness on the eighth day. This is the form of the eighth day.

children.text: tāny u gāyatrāṇi gāyatratṛtīyasavana eṣa tryaha eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. This three-day sequence has a third pressing carried by <s>Gāyatrī</s>; this is the three-day sequence.

children.text: Chapter 173
yad vai samānodarkaṃ tan navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has the same conclusion, that is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: yaddhyeva tṛtīyam ahas tad evaitat punar yannavamam ||
children.translated_text: For what is the third day is precisely this again, namely the ninth.

children.text: yad aśvavad yad antavad yat punarāvṛttaṃ yat punarninṛttaṃ yad ratavad yat paryastavad yat trivad yad antarūpaṃ yad uttame pade devatā nirucyate yad asau loko 'bhyuditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever has a horse, whatever has an end, whatever is repeated, whatever is turned back again, whatever has a chariot, whatever has an overlying form, whatever is threefold, whatever has an inner form, whatever names the deity in the last foot, whatever is proclaimed toward that world above,

children.text: yacchucivad yat satyavad yat kṣetivad yad gatavad yad okavat ||
children.translated_text: whatever contains brightness, whatever contains truth, whatever contains a field, whatever contains going, whatever contains a dwelling,

children.text: yat kṛtaṃ yat tṛtīyasyāhno rūpam etāni vai navamasyāhno rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: whatever is accomplished, whatever is the form of the third day: these indeed are the forms of the ninth day.

children.text: aganma mahā namasā yaviṣṭham iti navamasyāhna ājyaṃ bhavati gatavan navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Aganma mahā namasā yaviṣṭham</s>" is the <s>ājya</s> verse of the ninth day. It contains going on the ninth day; this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ triṣṭupprātaḥsavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter. This three-day sequence has a morning pressing carried by <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: pra vīrayā śucayo dadrire te te satyena manasā dīdhyānā divi kṣayantā rajasaḥ pṛthivyām ā viśvavārāśvinā gataṃ no 'yaṃ soma indra tubhyaṃ sunva ā tu pra brahmāṇo aṅgiraso nakṣanta sarasvatīṃ devayanto havanta ā no divo bṛhataḥ parvatād ā sarasvaty abhi no neṣi vasya iti praugaṃ śucivat satyavat kṣetivad gatavad okavan navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "With heroic power the pure ones have shown themselves; they, shining with true mind, dwelling in heaven, in the expanse, upon earth; come to us, O all-desired <s>Aśvins</s>; this <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, is being pressed for you; here the priests, the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, reach <s>Sarasvatī</s>, desiring the gods; they call; from heaven, from the great mountain, may <s>Sarasvatī</s> lead us to good" is the <s>praüga</s>. It has purity, truth, a field, going, and a dwelling; on the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ triṣṭupprātaḥsavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. In the morning pressing there is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; this is the three-day rite.

children.text: taṃ tam id rādhase mahe traya indrasya somā indra nedīya ed ihi pra nūnam brahmaṇaspatir agnir netā tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ pinvanty apo nakiḥ sudāso ratham iti tṛtīyenāhnā samāna ātāno navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "For that very boon, O great one," "the three <s>Somas</s> of <s>Indra</s>," "<s>Indra</s>, come here nearer," "now <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>," "<s>Agni</s> is the leader," "you, O <s>Soma</s>, by your powers," "the waters swell," and "no one [checks] the chariot of <s>Sudās</s>" have the same extension as on the third day. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: indraḥ svāhā pibatu yasya soma iti sūktam anto vai svāhākāro 'nto navamam ahar navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Let <s>Indra</s> drink with svāhā, he whose <s>Soma</s>..." is a hymn. The svāhā-call is indeed an end, and the ninth day is an end. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: gāyat sāma nabhanyaṃ yathā ver iti sūktam arcāma tad vāvṛdhānaṃ svarvad ity anto vai svar anto navamam ahar navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Sing the <s>Nabhanya</s> sāman, as one should" is a hymn. "Let us worship him, as he has grown, possessing svar" is its end; svar is indeed an end, and the ninth day is an end. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: tiṣṭhā harī ratha ā yujyamāneti sūktam anto vai sthitam anto navamam ahar navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Stand, O bay steeds, at the chariot as it is being yoked" is a hymn. What is standing is indeed an end, and the ninth day is an end. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: imā u tvā purutamasya kāror iti sūktaṃ dhiyo ratheṣṭhām ity anto vai sthitam anto navamam ahar navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "These songs for you of the most abundant poet" is a hymn. Its end is "the thoughts set upon the chariot"; what is standing is indeed an end, and the ninth day is an end. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubhaṃ tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With that firmly established foot he supports the pressing; by this he does not fall away from its base.

children.text: pra mandine pitumad arcatā vaca iti sūktaṃ samānodarkaṃ navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Sing forth speech for the exhilarated one, rich in drink" is a hymn, having the same conclusion. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: tad u jāgataṃ jagatyo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nividdhīyate tasmāj jagatīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Jagatī</s>. <s>Jagatī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day rite. That metre indeed carries that in which the <s>nivid</s> is inserted; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among <s>Jagatī</s> verses.

children.text: mithunāni sūktāni śasyante traiṣṭubhāni ca jāgatāni ca mithunaṃ vai paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Paired hymns are recited, both <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s>. Cattle are paired; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: pañca sūktāni śasyante pañcapadā paṅktiḥ pāṅkto yajñaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Five hymns are recited. <s>Paṅkti</s> has five feet; the sacrifice is <s>Paṅkti</s>-like, and cattle are <s>Paṅkti</s>-like. The <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: tvām iddhi havāmahe tvaṃ hy ehi cerava iti bṛhatpṛṣṭham bhavati navame 'hani ||
children.translated_text: "We call upon you indeed" and "for you indeed, come, O <s>Cerava</s>" form the <s>Bṛhatpṛṣṭha</s> on the ninth day.

children.text: yad vāvāneti dhāyyācyutābhi tvā śūra nonuma iti rathaṃtarasya yonim anu nivartayati rāthaṃtaraṃ hy etad ahar āyatanenendra tridhātu śaraṇam iti sāmapragāthas trivān navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpaṃ tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtam iti tārkṣyo 'cyutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "When he has won" is the inserted verse. With "We praise you, O hero, with unfailing ones" he turns back according to the womb of the <s>Rathaṃtara</s>, for this day belongs to the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> by its base. "O <s>Indra</s>, threefold refuge" is the <s>sāmapragātha</s>, threefold on the ninth day; this is the form of the ninth day. "That swift courser, impelled by the gods" is <s>Tārkṣya</s>, unfailing.

children.text: Chapter 174
saṃ ca tve jagmur gira indra pūrvīr iti sūktaṃ gatavan navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Together toward you many songs have gone, O <s>Indra</s>" is a hymn. It has going; on the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: kadā bhuvan rathakṣayāṇi brahmeti sūktaṃ kṣetivad antarūpaṃ kṣetīva vā antaṃ gatvā navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "When shall the brahman become chariot-winning?" is a hymn. It has a field and an inner form; having gone to the end, as it were, one dwells. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: ā satyo yātu maghavāṁ ṛjīṣīti sūktaṃ satyavan navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Let the true bountiful one come to the pressed Soma" is a hymn. It has truth; on the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: tat ta indriyam paramam parācair iti sūktam anto vai paramam anto navamam ahar navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "That highest power of yours, turned away by those from afar" is a hymn. The highest is indeed an end, and the ninth day is an end. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: tad u traiṣṭubham tena pratiṣṭhitapadena savanaṃ dādhārāyatanād evaitena na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>. With that firmly established foot he supports the pressing; by this he does not fall away from its base.

children.text: aham bhuvaṃ vasunaḥ pūrvyas patir iti sūktam ahaṃ dhanāni saṃjayāmi śaśvata ity anto vai jitam anto navamam ahar navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "I became the former lord of wealth" is a hymn. Its end is "I win lasting riches." What has been won is indeed an end, and the ninth day is an end. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: tad u jāgataṃ jagatyo vā etasya tryahasya madhyaṃdinaṃ vahanti tad vai tac chando vahati yasmin nivid dhīyate tasmājjagatīṣu nividaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: That, moreover, is <s>Jagatī</s>. <s>Jagatī</s> verses carry the midday pressing of this three-day rite. That metre indeed carries that in which the <s>nivid</s> is inserted; therefore he places the <s>nivid</s> among <s>Jagatī</s> verses.

children.text: mithunāni sūktāni śasyante traiṣṭubhāni ca jāgatāni ca mithunaṃ vai paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai pañca pañca sūktāni śasyante pañcapadā paṅktiḥ pāṅkto yajñaḥ pāṅktāḥ paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai tāni dvedhā pañcānyāni pañcānyāni daśa sampadyante sā daśinī virāﾱ annam virāﾱ annaṃ paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Paired hymns are recited, both <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s>. Cattle are paired; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle. Five and five hymns are recited. <s>Paṅkti</s> has five feet; the sacrifice is <s>Paṅkti</s>-like, and cattle are <s>Paṅkti</s>-like. The <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle. These, divided in two, five on one side and five on the other, make ten. That is the tenfold <s>Virāj</s>. Food is <s>Virāj</s>; cattle are food. The <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: tat savitur vṛṇīmahe 'dyā no deva savitar iti vaiśvadevasya pratipadanucarau rāthaṃtare 'hani navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "That of <s>Savitṛ</s> we choose" and "today, O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, for us" are the opening and following verses of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> on the <s>Rāthaṃtara</s> day, on the ninth day. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: doṣo āgād iti sāvitram anto vai gatam anto navamam ahar navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Evening has come" is the <s>Sāvitra</s> verse. What has gone is indeed an end, and the ninth day is an end. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: pra vām mahi dyavī abhīti dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ śucī upa praśastaya iti śucivan navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Forth to you two, great Heaven-and-Earth" is the verse addressed to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>. "Pure ones, toward the praises" has purity; on the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: indra iṣe dadātu nas te no ratnāni dhattanety ārbhavaṃ trir ā sāptāni sunvata iti trivan navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: With "May <s>Indra</s> give us refreshment; place your treasures upon us" he recites the <s>Ārbhava</s> verse, and three times "to the sevenfold ones for the soma-presser." It is threefold on the ninth day; this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: babhrur eko viṣuṇaḥ sūnaro yuveti dvipadāḥ śaṃsati dvipād vai puruṣaś catuṣpādāḥ paśavaḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai tad yad dvipadāḥ śaṃsati yajamānam eva tad dvipratiṣṭhaṃ catuṣpātsu paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: With "The one brown, separate, good-guiding youth" he recites two-footed verses. Man is two-footed, and cattle are four-footed; the <s>Chandomas</s> are cattle. This is for the securing of cattle. When he recites two-footed verses, he thereby establishes the sacrificer, as two-footed, among four-footed cattle.

children.text: ye triṃśati trayas para iti vaiśvadevaṃ trivan navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: With "Those thirty, and three beyond" he recites the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> verse. It is threefold on the ninth day; this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: tāny u gāyatrāṇi gāyatratṛtīyasavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses; this three-day rite has a <s>Gāyatrī</s> third pressing.

children.text: vaiśvānaro na ūtaya ity āgnimārutasya pratipad ā pra yātu parāvata ity anto vai parāvato 'nto navamam ahar navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "May <s>Vaiśvānara</s> be for our aids" is the opening verse of the <s>Āgnimāruta</s>; "let him go forth from afar" is the end. The far distance is an end, and the ninth day is an end. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: maruto yasya hi kṣaya iti mārutaṃ kṣetivad antarūpaṃ kṣetīva vā antaṃ gatvā navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Maruts</s>, because his dwelling" is a <s>Māruta</s> verse, having the word "dwelling" as an inner form. For having gone to the end, one seems to dwell. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: jātavedase sunavāma somam iti jātavedasyācyutā ||
children.translated_text: "For <s>Jātavedas</s> let us press Soma" is the unfailing <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse.

children.text: prāgnaye vācam īrayeti jātavedasyaṃ samānodarkaṃ navame 'hani navamasyāhno rūpam ||
children.translated_text: "Send forth speech for <s>Agni</s>" is a <s>Jātavedasī</s> verse with the same conclusion. On the ninth day this is the form of the ninth day.

children.text: sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣaḥ sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣa iti śaṃsati bahu vā etasmin navarātre kiṃca kiṃca vāraṇaṃ kriyate śāntyā eva tad yat sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣaḥ sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣa iti śaṃsati sarvasmād evaināṃs tad enasaḥ pramuñcati ||
children.translated_text: He recites, "May he carry us beyond hatreds, may he carry us beyond hatreds." In this nine-night rite many different wardings-off are performed. That is for appeasement. When he recites, "May he carry us beyond hatreds, may he carry us beyond hatreds," he thereby releases them from every sin.

children.text: tāny u gāyatrāṇi gāyatratṛtīyasavana eṣa tryahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These, moreover, are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses; this three-day rite has a <s>Gāyatrī</s> third pressing.

children.text: Chapter 175

pṛṣṭhyaṃ ṣaﾱaham upayanti yathā vai mukham evam pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaﾱahas tad yathāntaram mukhasya jihvā tālu dantā evaṃ chandomā atha yenaiva vācaṃ vyākaroti yena svādu cāsvādu ca vijānāti tad daśamam ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They approach the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite. As the mouth is, so is the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; as the tongue, palate, and teeth are inside the mouth, so are the <s>Chandomas</s>. And that by which one articulates speech, and by which one recognizes what is tasty and not tasty, is the tenth day.

children.text: yathā vai nāsike evam pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaﾱahas tad yathāntaram nāsikayor evaṃ chandomā atha yenaiva gandhān vijānāti tad daśamam ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the two nostrils are, so is the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; as what is within the nostrils is, so are the <s>Chandomas</s>. And that by which one recognizes smells is the tenth day.

children.text: yathā vā akṣy evam pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaﾱahas tad yathāntaram akṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇam evaṃ chandomā atha yaiva kanīnikā yena paśyati tad daśamam ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the eye is, so is the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; as the black of the eye is within the eye, so are the <s>Chandomas</s>. And the pupil itself, by which one sees, is the tenth day.

children.text: yathā vai karṇa evam pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaﾱahas tad yathāntaraṃ karṇasyaivaṃ chandomā atha yenaiva śṛṇoti tad daśamam ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the ear is, so is the <s>Pṛṣṭhya</s> six-day rite; as what is within the ear is, so are the <s>Chandomas</s>. And that by which one hears is the tenth day.

children.text: śrīr vai daśamam ahaḥ śriyaṃ vā eta āgacchanti ye daśamam ahar āgacchanti tasmād daśamam ahar avivākyam bhavati mā śriyo 'vavādiṣmeti duravavadaṃ hi śreyasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The tenth day is prosperity. Those who reach the tenth day indeed come to prosperity. Therefore the tenth day is not to be spoken against, lest we speak against prosperity; for what is superior is hard to speak against.

children.text: te tataḥ sarpanti ||
children.translated_text: From there they creep forward.

children.text: te mārjayante ||
children.translated_text: They cleanse themselves.

children.text: te patnīśālāṃ samprapadyante ||
children.translated_text: They enter the wives' hall.

children.text: teṣāṃ ya etām āhutiṃ vidyāt sa brūyāt samanvārabhadhvam iti sa juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Of them, the one who knows this oblation should say, "Take hold together." He should offer it.

children.text: iha rameha ramadhvam iha dhṛtir iha svadhṛtir agne vāṭ svāhā vāﾱ iti ||
children.translated_text: He offers with, "Rejoice here; take delight here. Here is firmness; here is self-firmness. O <s>Agni</s>, vāṭ, svāhā, vāṭ."

children.text: sa yad iha ramety āhāsminn evaināṃs tal loke ramayatīha ramadhvam iti yad āha prajām evaiṣu tad ramayatīha dhṛtir iha svadhṛtir iti yad āha prajāṃ caiva tad vācaṃ ca yajamāneṣu dadhāty agne vāﾱ iti rathaṃtaram svāhā vāﾱ iti bṛhat ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "Rejoice here," he thereby makes them rejoice in this very world. When he says, "Take delight here," he thereby makes offspring delight among them. When he says, "Here is firmness; here is self-firmness," he thereby places both offspring and speech among the sacrificers. "O <s>Agni</s>, vāṭ" is the <s>Rathaṃtara</s>; "svāhā, vāṭ" is the <s>Bṛhat</s>.

children.text: devānāṃ vā etan mithunaṃ yad bṛhadrathaṃtare devānām eva tan mithunena mithunam avarundhate devānām mithunena mithunam prajāyante prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: That pair of the gods is the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathaṃtara</s>. By that divine pair they secure a pair; by that divine pair they are propagated as a pair, for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus is propagated with offspring and cattle.

children.text: te tataḥ sarpanti te mārjayante ta āgnīdhraṃ samprapadyante teṣāṃ ya etām āhutiṃ vidyāt sa brūyāt samanvārabhadhvam iti sa juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: From there they creep forward; they cleanse themselves; they enter the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>. Of them, the one who knows this oblation should say, "Take hold together." He should offer it.

children.text: upasṛjan dharuṇam mātaraṃ dharuṇo dhayan rāyas poṣam iṣam ūrjam asmāsu dīdharat svāheti ||
children.translated_text: He offers with, "Sending forth the support, the mother, the supporter sucking, may he sustain among us increase of wealth, refreshment, strength, and vigor. Svāhā."

children.text: rāyas poṣam iṣam ūrjam avarunddha ātmane ca yajamānebhyaś ca yatraivaṃ vidvān etām āhutiṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: He secures increase of wealth, refreshment, strength, and vigor for himself and for the sacrificers, wherever one who knows thus offers this oblation.

children.text: Chapter 176
te tataḥ sarpanti te sadaḥ samprapadyante yathāyatham anya ṛtvijo vyutsarpanti saṃsarpanty udgātāras te sarparājñyā ṛkṣu stuvate ||
children.translated_text: From there they creep forward; they enter the sitting-hall. The other priests go out and come in, each according to his proper place; the <s>Udgātṛs</s> chant upon the <s>Sarparājñī</s> verses.

children.text: iyaṃ vai sarparājñīyaṃ hi sarpato rājñīyaṃ vā alomikevāgra āsīt saitam mantram apaśyad āyaṃ gauḥ pṛśnir akramīd iti tām ayam pṛśnir varṇa āviśan nānārūpo yaṃ yaṃ kāmam akāmayata yad idaṃ kiṃcauṣadhayo vanaspatayaḥ sarvāṇi rūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: This earth is the <s>Sarparājñī</s>; for this earth is queen of those who creep. This earth, as it were, was hairless in the beginning. She saw this mantra, "This speckled cow has stepped forward." Then the speckled color entered her, becoming manifold, each desire that she desired: whatever plants and trees there are here, all forms.

children.text: pṛśnir enaṃ varṇa āviśati nānārūpo yaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The speckled color enters him, becoming manifold, each desire that he desires, who knows thus.

children.text: manasā prastauti manasodgāyati manasā pratiharati vācā śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: With the mind he performs the preliminary chant; with the mind he sings the <s>udgītha</s>; with the mind he performs the response; with speech he recites.

children.text: vāk ca vai manaś ca devānām mithunaṃ devānām eva tan mithunena mithunam avarundhate devānām mithunena mithunam prajāyante prajātyai prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Speech and mind indeed are a pair belonging to the gods. With the pair belonging to the gods they secure the pair itself; with the pair belonging to the gods they generate the pair, for procreation. He is born with offspring and cattle who knows this.

children.text: atha caturhotṝn hotā vyācaṣṭe tad eva tat stutam anuśaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Hotṛ</s> explains the <s>Caturhotṛ</s> formulae; that very thing he recites in response to what has been praised.

children.text: devānāṃ vā etad yajñiyaṃ guhyaṃ nāma yac caturhotāras tad yac caturhotṝn hotā vyācaṣṭe devānām eva tad yajñiyaṃ guhyaṃ nāma prakāśaṃ gamayati tad enam prakāśaṃ gatam prakāśam gamayati ||
children.translated_text: This is the sacrificial secret name of the gods, namely the <s>Caturhotṛs</s>. When the <s>Hotṛ</s> explains the <s>Caturhotṛ</s> formulae, he brings the sacrificial secret name of the gods to the light. Having gone to the light, it brings him to the light.

children.text: gacchati prakāśaṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He goes to the light who knows this.

children.text: yam brāhmaṇam anūcānaṃ yaśo narcched iti ha smāhāraṇyam paretya darbhastambān udgrathya dakṣiṇato brahmāṇam upaveśya caturhotṝn vyācakṣīta ||
children.translated_text: If fame should fail to reach a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, so they used to say, he should go to the wilderness, pull up clumps of darbha grass, seat the <s>Brahman</s> priest to the south, and explain the <s>Caturhotṛ</s> formulae.

children.text: devānāṃ vā etad yajñiyaṃ guhyaṃ nāma yac caturhotāras tad yac caturhotṝn vyācakṣīta devānām eva tad yajñiyaṃ guhyaṃ nāma prakāśaṃ gamayati tad enam prakāśaṃ gatam prakāśaṃ gamayati gacchati prakāśaṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: This is the sacrificial secret name of the gods, namely the <s>Caturhotṛs</s>. When he explains the <s>Caturhotṛ</s> formulae, he brings the sacrificial secret name of the gods to the light. Having gone to the light, it brings him to the light. He goes to the light who knows this.

children.text: Chapter 177
athaudumbarīṃ samanvārabhante ||
children.translated_text: Then they take hold of the udumbara implement.

children.text: iṣam ūrjam anvārabha iti ||
children.translated_text: He says, "I take hold of refreshment and strength."

children.text: ūrg vā annādyam udumbaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The udumbara is strength, the eating of food.

children.text: yad vai tad devā iṣam ūrjaṃ vyabhajanta tata udumbaraḥ samabhavat tasmāt sa triḥ saṃvatsarasya pacyate ||
children.translated_text: When the gods divided refreshment and strength, from that the udumbara came into being. Therefore it ripens three times in the year.

children.text: tad yad audumbarīm samanvārabhanta iṣam eva tad ūrjam annādyaṃ samanvārabhante ||
children.translated_text: When they take hold of the udumbara implement, they thereby take hold of refreshment, strength, and the eating of food.

children.text: vācaṃ yacchanti vāg vai yajño yajñam eva tad yacchanti ||
children.translated_text: They restrain speech. Speech is the sacrifice; thus they restrain the sacrifice itself.

children.text: ahar niyacchanty ahar vai svargo lokaḥ svargam eva tal lokaṃ niyacchanti ||
children.translated_text: They restrain the day. The day is the heavenly world; thus they restrain that heavenly world itself.

children.text: na divā vācaṃ visṛjeran yad divā vācaṃ visṛjerann ahar bhrātṛvyāya pariśiṃṣyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should not release speech by day. If they were to release speech by day, they would leave the day as a remainder for the rival.

children.text: na naktaṃ vācaṃ visṛjeran yan naktaṃ vācaṃ visṛjeran rātrīm bhrātṛvyāya pariśiṃṣyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should not release speech at night. If they were to release speech at night, they would leave the night as a remainder for the rival.

children.text: samayāviṣitaḥ sūryaḥ syād atha vācaṃ visṛjeraṃs tāvantam eva tad dviṣate lokam pariśiṃṣanti ||
children.translated_text: The sun should be half set; then they may release speech. They leave only that much world as a remainder for the hating enemy.

children.text: atho khalv astamita eva vācaṃ visṛjeraṃs tamobhājam eva tad dviṣantam bhrātṛvyaṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, they should release speech only when the sun has set. They thereby make the hating rival one whose share is darkness.

children.text: āhavanīyam parītya vācaṃ visṛjeran yajño vā āhavanīyaḥ svargo loka āhavanīyo yajñenaiva tat svargeṇa lokena svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti ||
children.translated_text: After going around the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, they should release speech. The <s>Āhavanīya</s> is the sacrifice; the <s>Āhavanīya</s> is the heavenly world. By the sacrifice, by the heavenly world, they thereby go to the heavenly world.

children.text: yad ihonam akarma yad atyarīricāma prajāpatiṃ tat pitaram apyetv iti vācaṃ visṛjante ||
children.translated_text: With the words, "Whatever here we have done deficiently, whatever we have overdone, may that go to <s>Prajāpati</s>, the father," they release speech.

children.text: prajāpatiṃ vai prajā anuprajāyante prajāpatir ūnātiriktayoḥ pratiṣṭhā nainān ūnaṃ nātiriktaṃ hinasti ||
children.translated_text: Creatures are propagated after <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> is the foundation of what is deficient and what is excessive. Neither deficiency nor excess harms them.

children.text: prajāpatim evonātiriktāny abhyatyarjanti ya evaṃ vidvāṃsa etena vācaṃ visṛjante ||
children.translated_text: Those who, knowing thus, release speech with this formula consign the deficient and excessive things to <s>Prajāpati</s> himself.

children.text: tasmād evaṃ vidvāṃsa etenaiva vācaṃ visṛjeran ||
children.translated_text: Therefore those who know thus should release speech with this very formula.

children.text: Chapter 178
adhvaryo ity āhvayate caturhotṛṣu vadiṣyamāṇas tad āhāvasya rūpam ||
children.translated_text: He calls, "O <s>Adhvaryu</s>!" when he is about to speak among the <s>Caturhotṛ</s> formulae. That is the form of the summons.

children.text: oṃ hotas tathā hotar ity adhvaryuḥ pratigṛṇāty avasite 'vasite daśasu padeṣu ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Adhvaryu</s> responds, "Om, O <s>Hotṛ</s>; so it is, O <s>Hotṛ</s>," whenever each set of ten words has been completed.

children.text: teṣāṃ cittiḥ srug āsīt ||
children.translated_text: Their thought was the sacrificial ladle.

children.text: cittam ājyam āsīt ||
children.translated_text: Mind was the clarified butter.

children.text: vāg vedir āsīt ||
children.translated_text: Speech was the altar.

children.text: ādhītam barhir āsīt ||
children.translated_text: What had been studied was the sacrificial grass.

children.text: keto agnir āsīt ||
children.translated_text: Intention was the fire.

children.text: vijñātam agnīd āsīt ||
children.translated_text: What was known was the <s>Agnīdh</s> priest.

children.text: prāṇo havir āsīt ||
children.translated_text: Breath was the oblation.

children.text: sāmādhvaryur āsīt ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Sāman</s> was the <s>Adhvaryu</s>.

children.text: vācaspatir hotāsīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vācaspati</s> was the <s>Hotṛ</s>.

children.text: mana upavaktāsīt ||
children.translated_text: Mind was the assistant speaker.

children.text: te vā etaṃ graham agṛhṇata vācaspate vidhe nāman vidhema te nāma vidhes tvam asmākaṃ nāmnā dyāṃ gaccha yāṃ devāḥ prajāpatigṛhapataya ṛddhim arādhnuvaṃs tām ṛddhiṃ rātsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They took this cup-offering: "O <s>Vācaspati</s>, O Disposer, by name, let us serve your name, O Disposer. With our name go to heaven. The prosperity that the gods, with <s>Prajāpati</s> as house-lord, attained, that prosperity shall we attain."

children.text: atha prajāpates tanūr anudravati brahmodyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Then follows a body of <s>Prajāpati</s>, and a <s>brahmodya</s> (theological riddle).

children.text: annādā cānnapatnī cānnādā tad agnir annapatnī tad ādityaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Food-eating" and "mistress of food": food-eating is <s>Agni</s>; mistress of food is <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: bhadrā ca kalyāṇī ca bhadrā tat somaḥ kalyāṇī tat paśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Auspicious" and "fortunate": auspicious is <s>Soma</s>; fortunate is the cattle.

children.text: anilayā cāpabhayā cānilayā tad vāyur na hy eṣa kadācanelayaty apabhayā tan mṛtyuḥ sarvaṃ hy etasmād bībhāya ||
children.translated_text: "Unsettling" and "fear-removing": unsettling is <s>Vāyu</s>, for he never settles at all; fear-removing is <s>Mṛtyu</s>, for everything fears him.

children.text: anāptā cānāpyā cānāptā tat pṛthivy anāpyā tad dyauḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Unattained" and "unattainable": unattained is the earth; unattainable is heaven.

children.text: anādhṛṣyā cāpratidhṛṣyā cānādhṛṣyā tad agnir apratidhṛṣyā tad ādityaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Unassailable" and "irresistible": unassailable is <s>Agni</s>; irresistible is <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: apūrvā cābhrātṛvyā cāpūrvā tan mano 'bhrātṛvyā tat saṃvatsaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Unprecedented" and "without a rival": unprecedented is mind; without a rival is the year.

children.text: etā vāva dvādaśa prajāpates tanva eṣa kṛtsnaḥ prajāpatis tat kṛtsnam prajāpatim āpnoti daśamam ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These indeed are the twelve bodies of <s>Prajāpati</s>. This is the whole <s>Prajāpati</s>; on the tenth day he obtains <s>Prajāpati</s> whole.

children.text: atha brahmodyam vadanty agnir gṛhapatir iti haika āhuḥ so 'sya lokasya gṛhapatir vāyur gṛhapatir iti haika āhuḥ so 'ntarikṣalokasya gṛhapatir asau vai gṛhapatir yo 'sau tapaty eṣa patir ṛtavo gṛhā yeṣāṃ vai gṛhapatiṃ devaṃ vidvān gṛhapatir bhavati rādhnoti sa gṛhapatī rādhnuvanti te yajamānā yeṣāṃ vā apahatapāpmānaṃ devaṃ vidvān gṛhapatir bhavaty apa sa gṛhapatiḥ pāpmānaṃ hate 'pa te yajamānāḥ pāpmānaṃ ghnate 'dhvaryo arātsmārātsma ||
children.translated_text: Then they speak the <s>brahmodya</s> (ritual riddle). Some say, "<s>Agni</s> is the householder"; he is the householder of this world. Some say, "<s>Vāyu</s> is the householder"; he is the householder of the midspace-world. But the one who shines yonder is indeed the householder. He is the lord; the seasons are the houses. For those among whom a man becomes householder knowing the god who is the householder, that householder prospers, and those sacrificers prosper. For those among whom a man becomes householder knowing the god whose evil has been beaten away, that householder beats away evil, and those sacrificers beat away evil. "O <s>adhvaryu</s>, we have attained success, we have attained success."

children.text: Chapter 179
uddharāhavanīyam ity aparāhṇa āha yad evāhnā sādhu karoti tad eva tat prāṅ uddhṛtya tadabhaye nidhatte ||
children.translated_text: In the afternoon he says, "Lift out the <s>āhavanīya</s>." Whatever good he does by day, that very thing, having lifted it out eastward, he places in what is free from danger.

children.text: uddharāhavanīyam iti prātar āha yad eva rātryā sādhu karoti tad eva tat prāṅ uddhṛtya tadabhaye nidhatte ||
children.translated_text: In the morning he says, "Lift out the <s>āhavanīya</s>." Whatever good he does by night, that very thing, having lifted it out eastward, he places in what is free from danger.

children.text: yajño vā āhavanīyaḥ svargo loka āhavanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>āhavanīya</s> is the sacrifice; the <s>āhavanīya</s> is the heavenly world.

children.text: yajña eva tat svarge loke svargaṃ lokaṃ nidhatte ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Thereby, in the sacrifice itself and in the heavenly world, he places the heavenly world, he who knows thus.

children.text: yo vā agnihotraṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ṣoﾱaśakalam paśuṣu pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda vaiśvadevenāgnihotreṇa ṣoﾱaśakalena paśuṣu pratiṣṭhitena rādhnoti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the <s>agnihotra</s> as Vaiśvadeva, sixteenfold, established among cattle, prospers through the Vaiśvadeva <s>agnihotra</s>, sixteenfold and established among cattle.

children.text: raudraṃ gavi sad vāyavyam upāvasṛṣṭam āśvinaṃ duhyamānaṃ saumyaṃ dugdhaṃ vāruṇam adhiśritam pauṣṇaṃ samudantam mārutaṃ viṣyandamānaṃ vaiśvadevam binduman maitraṃ śarogṛhītaṃ dyāvāpṛthivīyam udvāsitaṃ sāvitram prakrāntaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ hriyamāṇam bārhaspatyam upasannam agneḥ pūrvāhutiḥ prajāpater uttaraindraṃ hutam ||
children.translated_text: It is Rudra's while abiding in the cow; Vāyu's when let near; the <s>Aśvins'</s> when being milked; <s>Soma's</s> when milked; <s>Varuṇa's</s> when set over the fire; <s>Pūṣan's</s> when rising up; the <s>Maruts'</s> when streaming; the <s>Viśve Devāḥ's</s> when drop-filled; <s>Mitra's</s> when taken with the śara; <s>Heaven-and-Earth's</s> when taken off; <s>Savitṛ's</s> when set forth; <s>Viṣṇu's</s> when being carried; <s>Bṛhaspati's</s> when brought near; <s>Agni's</s> as the former oblation; <s>Prajāpati's</s> as the latter; <s>Indra's</s> when offered.

children.text: etad vā agnihotraṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ṣoﾱaśakalam paśuṣu pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: This, indeed, is the Vaiśvadeva <s>agnihotra</s>, sixteenfold, established among cattle.

children.text: vaiśvadevenāgnihotreṇa ṣoﾱaśakalena paśuṣu pratiṣṭhitena rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers through the Vaiśvadeva <s>agnihotra</s>, sixteenfold and established among cattle, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 180
yasyāgnihotry upāvasṛṣṭā duhyamānopaviśet kā tatra prāyaścittir iti tām abhimantrayeta ||
children.translated_text: If someone's agnihotra cow, having been let near, sits down while being milked, one asks, "What is the expiation there?" He should address her with this formula:

children.text: yasmād bhīṣā niṣīdasi tato no abhayaṃ kṛdhi paśūn naḥ sarvān gopāya namo rudrāya mīﾱhuṣa iti ||
children.translated_text: "From the fear because of which you sit down, make safety for us from that. Protect all our cattle. Homage to <s>Rudra</s> the bountiful."

children.text: tām utthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: He should make her rise.

children.text: udasthād devy aditir āyur yajñapatāv adhāt indrāya kṛṇvatī bhāgam mitrāya varuṇāya ceti ||
children.translated_text: "The goddess <s>Aditi</s> has stood up; she has placed life in the lord of the sacrifice, making a portion for <s>Indra</s>, and for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>."

children.text: athāsyā udapātram ūdhasi ca mukhe copagṛhṇīyād athainām brāhmaṇāya dadyāt sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he should take up a water-vessel at her udder and at her mouth. Then he should give her to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. That is the expiation there.

children.text: yasyāgnihotry upāvasṛṣṭā duhyamānā vāśyeta kā tatra prāyaścittir ity aśanāyāṃ ha vā eṣā yajamānasya pratikhyāya vāśyate tām annam apy ādayecchāntyai śāntir vā annaṃ sūyavasād bhagavatī hi bhūyā iti sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If someone's agnihotra cow, having been let near and being milked, should bellow, one asks, "What is the expiation there?" Because of hunger, indeed, she bellows in reproach against the sacrificer. He should have her eat food, for appeasement. Food, indeed, is appeasement. "May she be rich in good pasture." That is the expiation there.

children.text: yasyāgnihotry upāvasṛṣṭā duhyamānā spandeta kā tatra prāyaścittir iti sā yat tatra skandayet tad abhimṛśya japet ||
children.translated_text: If someone's agnihotra cow, having been let near and being milked, should tremble, one asks, "What is the expiation there?" Whatever she spills there, he should touch it and murmur:

children.text: yad adya dugdham pṛthivīm asṛpta yad oṣadhīr atyasṛpad yad āpaḥ payo gṛheṣu payo aghnyāyāṃ payo vatseṣu payo astu tan mayīti ||
children.translated_text: "Whatever milk today has slipped onto the earth, whatever has slipped among the plants, whatever into the waters: may there be milk in the houses, milk in the inviolate cow, milk among the calves; may that milk be mine."

children.text: tatra yat pariśiṣṭaṃ syāt tena juhuyād yad alaṃ homāya syāt ||
children.translated_text: There, if anything should remain that is sufficient for an oblation, he should sacrifice with that.

children.text: yady u vai sarvaṃ siktaṃ syād athānyām āhūya tāṃ dugdhvā tena juhuyād ā tveva śraddhāyai hotavyaṃ sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if all of it should be spilled, then he should call another cow, milk her, and sacrifice with that. Yet for the sake of faith the offering must be made. That is the expiation there.

children.text: sarvaṃ vā asya barhiṣyaṃ sarvam parigṛhītaṃ ya evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Everything of his is placed on the sacred grass; everything is encompassed, for one who, knowing thus, offers the <s>agnihotra</s>.

children.text: Chapter 181
asau vā asyādityo yūpaḥ pṛthivī vedir oṣadhayo barhir vanaspataya idhmā āpaḥ prokṣaṇyo diśaḥ paridhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yonder sun is his sacrificial post; the earth is the altar; the plants are the sacred grass; the trees are the fuel-sticks; the waters are the sprinkling waters; the directions are the enclosing sticks.

children.text: yaddha vā asya kiṃca naśyati yan mriyate yad apājanti sarvaṃ haivainaṃ tad amuṣmiṃlloke yathā barhiṣi dattam āgacched evam āgacchati ya evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever of his is lost, whatever dies, whatever goes away, all that comes to him in that world just as something placed on the sacred grass would come, for one who, knowing thus, offers the <s>agnihotra</s>.

children.text: ubhayān vā eṣa devamanuṣyān viparyāsaṃ dakṣiṇā nayati sarvaṃ cedaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃca ||
children.translated_text: This gift leads both gods and humans, by reversal, and all this, whatever there is.

children.text: manuṣyān vā eṣa sāyamāhutyā devebhyo dakṣiṇā nayati sarvaṃ cedaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃca ta ete pralīnā nyokasa iva śere manuṣyā devebhyo dakṣiṇā nītāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the evening oblation, it leads humans as a gift to the gods, and all this, whatever there is. These humans, led as a gift to the gods, lie as if absorbed, as if dwelling low.

children.text: devān vā eṣa prātarāhutyā manuṣyebhyo dakṣiṇā nayati sarvaṃ cedaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃca ta ete vividānā ivotpatanty ado 'haṃ kariṣye 'do 'haṃ gamiṣyāmīti vadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the morning oblation, it leads the gods as a gift to humans, and all this, whatever there is. These, as if becoming manifest, leap up, saying, "I will do this; I will go there."

children.text: yāvantaṃ ha vai sarvam idaṃ dattvā lokaṃ jayati tāvantaṃ ha lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: As great a world as one wins by giving all this, just so great a world he wins who, knowing thus, offers the <s>agnihotra</s>.

children.text: agnaye vā eṣa sāyamāhutyāśvinam upākaroti tad vāk pratigṛṇāti vāg vāg iti ||
children.translated_text: By the evening oblation to <s>Agni</s>, he sets in motion what belongs to the <s>Aśvins</s>. Speech receives that, saying, "Speech, speech."

children.text: agninā hāsya rātryāśvinaṃ śastam bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Through <s>Agni</s>, what belongs to the <s>Aśvins</s> becomes recited for him during the night, for one who, knowing thus, offers the <s>agnihotra</s>.

children.text: ādityāya vā eṣa prātarāhutyā mahāvratam upākaroti tat prāṇaḥ pratigṛṇāty annam annam ity ādityena hāsyāhnā mahāvrataṃ śastam bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: For with the morning oblation he undertakes the <s>Mahāvrata</s> for <s>Āditya</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> receives it as "food, food." For him who, knowing thus, offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>, the <s>Mahāvrata</s> has been recited by means of a day belonging to <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: tasya vā etasyāgnihotrasya sapta ca śatāni viṃśatiś ca saṃvatsare sāyamāhutayaḥ sapta co eva śatāni viṃśatiś ca saṃvatsare prātarāhutayas tāvatyo 'gner yajuṣmatya iṣṭakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of this <s>Agnihotra</s> there are seven hundred and twenty evening oblations in a year, and exactly seven hundred and twenty morning oblations in a year; that many are the formula-bearing bricks of <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: saṃvatsareṇa hāsyāgninā cityeneṣṭam bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: For him who, knowing thus, offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>, sacrifice has been performed within the year with <s>Agni</s> as a piled fire-altar.

children.text: Chapter 182
vṛṣaśuṣmo ha vātāvata uvāca jātūkarṇyo vaktā smo vā idaṃ devebhyo yad vai tad agnihotram ubhayedyur ahūyatānyedyur vāva tad etarhi hūyata iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣaśuṣma Vātāvata</s>, a <s>Jātūkarṇya</s>, said, "We are to speak this for the gods: that <s>Agnihotra</s> which used to be offered on both days is now in fact offered only on one day."

children.text: etad u hovāca kumārī gandharvagṛhītā vaktā smo vā idam pitṛbhyo yad vai tad agnihotram ubhayedyur ahūyatānyedyur vāva tad etarhi hūyata iti ||
children.translated_text: A maiden possessed by a <s>Gandharva</s> said this: "We are to speak this for the Fathers: that <s>Agnihotra</s> which used to be offered on both days is now in fact offered only on one day."

children.text: etad vā agnihotram anyedyur hūyate yad astamite sāyaṃ juhoty anudite prātar athaitad agnihotram ubhayedyur hūyate yad astamite sāyaṃ juhoty udite prātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Agnihotra</s> offered on one day: when one offers in the evening after sunset and in the morning before sunrise. But this is the <s>Agnihotra</s> offered on both days: when one offers in the evening after sunset and in the morning after sunrise.

children.text: tasmād udite hotavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it should be offered after sunrise.

children.text: caturviṃśe ha vai saṃvatsare 'nuditahomī gāyatrīlokam āpnoti dvādaśa uditahomī sa yadā dvau saṃvatsarāv anudite juhoty atha hāsyaiko huto bhavaty atha ya udite juhoti saṃvatsareṇaiva saṃvatsaram āpnoti ya evaṃ vidvān udite juhoti tasmād udite hotavyam ||
children.translated_text: In the twenty-fourth year the one who offers before sunrise reaches the world of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; in the twelfth, the one who offers after sunrise. When he offers before sunrise for two years, then only one has been offered for him; but one who offers after sunrise reaches the year by the year itself. Whoever, knowing thus, offers after sunrise does so; therefore it should be offered after sunrise.

children.text: eṣa ha vā ahorātrayos tejasi juhoti yo 'stamite sāyaṃ juhoty udite prātar agninā vai tejasā rātris tejasvaty ādityena tejasāhas tejasvat ||
children.translated_text: He who offers in the evening after sunset and in the morning after sunrise offers into the radiance of day and night. By the radiance of <s>Agni</s> the night is radiant; by the radiance of <s>Āditya</s> the day is radiant.

children.text: ahorātrayor hāsya tejasi hutaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān udite juhoti ||
children.translated_text: For him who, knowing thus, offers after sunrise, the offering has been made into the radiance of day and night.

children.text: tasmād udite hotavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it should be offered after sunrise.

children.text: Chapter 183

ete ha vai saṃvatsarasya cakre yad ahorātre tābhyām eva tat saṃvatsaram eti sa yo 'nudite juhoti yathaikataścakreṇa yāyāt tādṛk tad atha ya udite juhoti yathobhayataścakreṇa yān kṣipram adhvānaṃ samaśnuvīta tādṛk tat ||
children.translated_text: Day and night are the two wheels of the year; by means of them he reaches the year. He who offers before sunrise is like one who would travel with a wheel on one side only. But he who offers after sunrise is like one who, traveling with wheels on both sides, would quickly cover the road.

children.text: tad eṣābhi yajñagāthā gīyate ||
children.translated_text: On this a sacrificial verse is sung.

children.text: bṛhadrathaṃtarābhyām idam eti yuktaṃ yad bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac cāpi sarvaṃ tābhyām iyād agnīn ādhāya dhīro divaivānyaj juhuyān naktam anyad iti ||
children.translated_text: "Harnessed with the <s>Bṛhat</s> and the <s>Rathantara</s>, this goes on: whatever has been, whatever will be, and all besides. By them the wise man, having established the fires, should go; he should offer one oblation by day and another by night."

children.text: rāthaṃtarī vai rātry ahar bārhatam agnir vai rathaṃtaram ādityo bṛhad ete ha vā enaṃ devate bradhnasya viṣṭapaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayato ya evaṃ vidvān udite juhoti tasmād udite hotavyam ||
children.translated_text: The night belongs to the <s>Rathantara</s>; the day belongs to the <s>Bṛhat</s>. <s>Agni</s> is the <s>Rathantara</s>, and <s>Āditya</s> is the <s>Bṛhat</s>. These two deities make him go to the summit of <s>Bradhna</s>, to the heavenly world, he who, knowing thus, offers after sunrise. Therefore it should be offered after sunrise.

children.text: tad eṣābhi yajñagāthā gīyate ||
children.translated_text: On this a sacrificial verse is sung.

children.text: yathā ha vā sthūriṇaikena yāyād akṛtvānyad upayojanāya evaṃ yanti te bahavo janāsaḥ purodayāj juhvati ye 'gnihotram iti ||
children.translated_text: "Just as one would travel with a single support, without making another ready for yoking, so go the many people who offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> before sunrise."

children.text: tāṃ vā etāṃ devatām prayatīṃ sarvam idam anupraiti yad idaṃ kiṃcaitasyai hīdaṃ devatāyā anucaraṃ sarvaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃca saiṣānucaravatī devatā ||
children.translated_text: All this follows that deity as she goes forward, whatever there is here. For all this, whatever there is here, is attendant upon that deity. That deity is therefore attended by a retinue.

children.text: vindate ha vā anucaram bhavaty asyānucaro ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He obtains an attendant; one becomes his attendant, who knows thus.

children.text: sa vā eṣa ekātithiḥ sa eṣa juhvatsu vasati ||
children.translated_text: He is this single guest; he dwells among those who offer.

children.text: tad yad ado gāthā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: That is why there is this verse:

children.text: anenasam enasā so 'bhiśastād enasvato vāpaharād enaḥ ekātithim apa sāyaṃ ruṇaddhi bisāni steno apa so jahāreti ||
children.translated_text: "From the guiltless one accused through guilt, or from the guilty one, may he remove the guilt. In the evening he shuts out the single guest; like a thief, he has stolen the lotus-fibres."

children.text: eṣa ha vai sa ekātithiḥ sa eṣa juhvatsu vasaty etāṃ vāva sa devatām aparuṇaddhi yo 'lam agnihotrāya san nāgnihotraṃ juhoti tam eṣā devatāparoddhāparuṇaddhy asmāc ca lokād amuṣmāc cobhābhyāṃ yo 'lam agnihotrāya san nāgnihotraṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is that single guest; he dwells among those who offer. The man who, though able for the <s>Agnihotra</s>, does not offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>, shuts out precisely this deity. This deity, as one who shuts out, shuts him out from this world and from yonder world, from both, the man who, though able for the <s>Agnihotra</s>, does not offer the <s>Agnihotra</s>.

children.text: tasmād yo 'lam agnihotrāya syāj juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore whoever is able for the <s>Agnihotra</s> should offer it.

children.text: tasmād āhur na sāyam atithir aparudhya iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they say, "An evening guest should not be shut out."

children.text: etaddha sma vai tad vidvān nagarī jānaśruteya uditahominam aikādaśākṣam mānutantavyam uvāca prajāyām enaṃ vijñātā smo yadi vidvān vā juhoty avidvān veti tasyo haikādaśākṣe rāṣṭram iva prajā babhūva rāṣṭram iva ha vā asya prajā bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān udite juhoti tasmād udite hotavyam ||
children.translated_text: Knowing this, <s>Nagarī Jānaśruteya</s> said to <s>Aikādaśākṣa Mānutantavya</s>, an offerer after sunrise, "We have come to know him in his offspring, whether he offers knowingly or unknowingly." For <s>Aikādaśākṣa</s>, his offspring became like a kingdom. Like a kingdom, indeed, his offspring become, who, knowing thus, offers after sunrise. Therefore it should be offered after sunrise.

children.text: Chapter 184

udyann u khalu vā āditya āhavanīyena raśmīn saṃdadhāti sa yo 'nudite juhoti yathā kumārāya vā vatsāya vājātāya stanam pratidadhyāt tādṛk tad atha ya udite juhoti yathā kumārāya vā vatsāya vā jātāya stanam pratidadhyāt tādṛk tat tam asmai pratidhīyamānam ubhayor lokayor annādyam anu pratidhīyate 'smāc ca lokād amuṣmāc cobhābhyām ||
children.translated_text: Now as he rises, <s>Āditya</s> joins his rays with the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. He who offers before sunrise is like one who would present the breast to a child or a calf not yet born; but he who offers after sunrise is like one who would present the breast to a child or a calf already born. As it is being presented to him, food and eating are presented to him in both worlds, in this world and in yonder world, in both.

children.text: sa yo 'nudite juhoti yathā puruṣāya vā hastine vāprayate hasta ādadhyāt tādṛk tad atha ya udite juhoti yathā puruṣāya vā hastine vā prayate hasta ādadhyāt tādṛk tat tam eṣa etenaiva hastenordhvaṃ hṛtvā svarge loka ādadhāti ya evaṃ vidvān udite juhoti tasmād udite hotavyam ||
children.translated_text: He who offers before the sun has risen is like one who would put his hand on a man or on an elephant when it is not ready; such is that act. But he who offers after the sun has risen is like one who would put his hand on a man or on an elephant when it is ready; such is that act. This one, taking him upward with that very hand, places him in the heavenly world, the man who, knowing thus, offers after sunrise. Therefore one should offer after sunrise.

children.text: udyann u khalu vā ādityaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni praṇayati tasmād enam prāṇa ity ācakṣate prāṇe hāsya samprati hutam bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān udite juhoti tasmād udite hotavyam ||
children.translated_text: For when rising, the <s>Āditya</s> leads onward all beings. Therefore they call him <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath, life-force). The offering of the man who, knowing thus, offers after sunrise has in fact been offered in <s>Prāṇa</s>. Therefore one should offer after sunrise.

children.text: eṣa ha vai satyaṃ vadan satye juhoti yo 'stamite sāyaṃ juhoty udite prātar bhūr bhuvaḥ svar aum agnir jyotir jyotir agnir iti sāyaṃ juhoti bhūr bhuvaḥ svar auṃ sūryo jyotir jyotiḥ sūrya iti prātaḥ satyaṃ hāsya vadataḥ satye hutaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān udite juhoti tasmād udite hotavyam ||
children.translated_text: The man who offers in the evening when the sun has set and in the morning when it has risen, speaking truth, indeed offers in truth. In the evening he offers with, "<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>, <s>aum</s>; <s>Agni</s> is light, light is <s>Agni</s>." In the morning he offers with, "<s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>, <s>aum</s>; <s>Sūrya</s> is light, light is <s>Sūrya</s>." For him, speaking truth, the oblation has in fact been offered in truth, the man who, knowing thus, offers after sunrise. Therefore one should offer after sunrise.

children.text: tad eṣābhi yajñagāthā gīyate ||
children.translated_text: On this matter this sacrificial verse is sung:

children.text: prātaḥ prātar anṛtaṃ te vadanti purodayāj juhvati ye 'gnihotraṃ divā kīrtyam adivā kīrtayantaḥ sūryo jyotir na tadā jyotir eṣām iti ||
children.translated_text: "Morning after morning they speak falsehood for you, those who offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> before sunrise, proclaiming as not-day what should be proclaimed by day: 'The sun is light'; at that time it is not light for them."

children.text: Chapter 185

prajāpatir akāmayata prajāyeya bhūyān syām iti sa tapo 'tapyata sa tapas taptvemāṃllokān asṛjata pṛthivīm antarikṣaṃ divaṃ tāṃllokān abhyatapat tebhyo 'bhitaptebhyas trīṇi jyotīṃṣy ajāyantāgnir eva pṛthivyā ajāyata vāyur antarikṣād ādityo divas tāni jyotīṃṣy abhyatapat tebhyo 'bhitaptebhyas trayo vedā ajāyanta ṛgveda evāgner ajāyata yajurvedo vāyoḥ sāmaveda ādityāt tān vedān abhyatapat tebhyo 'bhitaptebhyas trīṇi śukrāṇy ajāyanta bhūr ity eva ṛgvedād ajāyata bhuva iti yajurvedāt svar iti sāmavedāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> desired, "May I be propagated; may I become more numerous." He practiced austerity. Having practiced austerity, he created these worlds: earth, midspace, and heaven. He heated those worlds. From them, when heated, three lights were born: <s>Agni</s> was born from the earth, <s>Vāyu</s> from the midspace, and <s>Āditya</s> from heaven. He heated those lights. From them, when heated, the three Vedas were born: the <s>Ṛgveda</s> was born from <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s> from <s>Vāyu</s>, and the <s>Sāmaveda</s> from <s>Āditya</s>. He heated those Vedas. From them, when heated, three bright essences were born: <s>bhūr</s> was born from the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s> from the <s>Yajurveda</s>, and <s>svar</s> from the <s>Sāmaveda</s>.

children.text: tāni śukrāṇy abhyatapat tebhyo 'bhitaptebhyas trayo varṇā ajāyantākāra ukāro makāra iti tān ekadhā samabharat tad etad aum iti tasmād om om iti praṇauty om iti vai svargo loka om ity asau yo 'sau tapati ||
children.translated_text: He heated those bright essences. From them, when heated, three sounds were born: the sound <s>a</s>, the sound <s>u</s>, and the sound <s>m</s>. He brought them together into one. That is this <s>aum</s>. Therefore one utters in praise, "<s>om</s>, <s>om</s>." For <s>om</s> is the heavenly world; <s>om</s> is that yonder one who burns.

children.text: sa prajāpatir yajñam atanuta tam āharat tenāyajata sa ṛcaiva hautram akarod yajuṣādhvaryavaṃ sāmnodgīthaṃ yad etat trayyai vidyāyai śukraṃ tena brahmatvam akarot ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Prajāpati</s> extended the sacrifice, took it up, and sacrificed with it. With the <s>ṛc</s> verse he made the office of <s>Hotṛ</s>; with the <s>yajus</s> formula, the office of <s>Adhvaryu</s>; with the <s>sāman</s> chant, the <s>udgītha</s>. With that bright essence of the threefold knowledge he made the office of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: sa prajāpatir yajñaṃ devebhyaḥ samprāyacchat te devā yajñam atanvata tam āharanta tenāyajanta ta ṛcaiva hautram akurvan yajuṣādhvaryavaṃ sāmnodgīthaṃ yad evaitat trayyai vidyāyai śukraṃ tena brahmatvam akurvan ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Prajāpati</s> handed the sacrifice over to the gods. The gods extended the sacrifice, took it up, and sacrificed with it. With the <s>ṛc</s> verse they made the office of <s>Hotṛ</s>; with the <s>yajus</s> formula, the office of <s>Adhvaryu</s>; with the <s>sāman</s> chant, the <s>udgītha</s>. With that very bright essence of the threefold knowledge they made the office of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: te devā abruvan prajāpatiṃ yadi no yajña ṛkta ārtiḥ syād yadi yajuṣṭo yadi sāmato yady avijñātā sarvavyāpad vā kā prāyaścittir iti sa prajāpatir abravīd devān yadi vo yajña ṛkta ārtir bhavati bhūr iti gārhapatye juhavātha yadi yajuṣṭo bhuva ity āgnīdhrīye 'nvāhāryapacane vā haviryajñeṣu yadi sāmataḥ svar ity āhavanīye yady avijñātā sarvavyāpad vā bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti sarvā anudrutyāhavanīya eva juhavātheti ||
children.translated_text: The gods said to <s>Prajāpati</s>, "If an injury should occur in our sacrifice with respect to the <s>ṛc</s>, or with respect to the <s>yajus</s>, or with respect to the <s>sāman</s>, or if there should be an unknown fault or one pervading the whole, what is the expiation?" <s>Prajāpati</s> said to the gods, "If an injury occurs in your sacrifice with respect to the <s>ṛc</s>, offer 'bhūr' in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire. If with respect to the <s>yajus</s>, offer 'bhuvaḥ' in the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s>, or in the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> in oblation-sacrifices. If with respect to the <s>sāman</s>, offer 'svar' in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. If there is an unknown fault or one pervading the whole, then, having run through all, offer 'bhūr bhuvaḥ svar' in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> alone."
