children.text: etāni ha vai vedānām antaḥśleṣaṇāni yad etā vyāhṛtayas tad yathātmanātmānaṃ saṃdadhyād yathā parvaṇā parva yathā śleṣmaṇā carmaṇyaṃ vānyad vā viśliṣṭam saṃśleṣayed evam evaitābhir yajñasya viśliṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti saiṣā sarvaprāyaścittir yad etā vyāhṛtayas tasmād eṣaiva yajñe prāyaścittiḥ kartavyā ||
children.translated_text: These <s>vyāhṛtis</s> are indeed the inner joinings of the Vedas. As one might join self to self, joint to joint, or with an adhesive mend what has come apart in a hide or anything else, just so with these he joins what has come apart in the sacrifice. These <s>vyāhṛtis</s> are the expiation for everything. Therefore this very expiation is to be performed in the sacrifice.

children.text: Chapter 186
tad āhur mahāvadāḥ yad ṛcaiva hautraṃ kriyate yajuṣādhvaryavaṃ sāmnodgīthaṃ vyārabdhā trayī vidyā bhavaty atha kena brahmatvaṃ kriyata iti trayyā vidyayeti brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: On this point the great disputants say, "Since the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s work is done with the <s>ṛc</s>, the <s>Adhvaryu</s>'s work with the <s>yajus</s>, and the <s>udgītha</s> with the <s>sāman</s>, the threefold knowledge has been divided up. Then by what is the office of <s>Brahman</s> performed?" One should answer, "By the threefold knowledge."

children.text: ayaṃ vai yajño yo 'yaṃ pavate tasya vāk ca manaś ca vartanyau vācā ca hi manasā ca yajño vartata iyaṃ vai vāg ado manas tad vācā trayyā vidyayaikam pakṣaṃ saṃskurvanti manasaiva brahmā saṃskaroti ||
children.translated_text: This sacrifice is that one which blows. Speech and mind are its two tracks, for the sacrifice proceeds by speech and by mind. This is speech; that is mind. With speech, as the threefold knowledge, they perfect one wing; the <s>Brahman</s> perfects the other by mind alone.

children.text: te haike brahmāṇa upākṛte prātaranuvāke stomabhāgāñ japitvā bhāṣamāṇā upāsate taddhaitad uvāca brāhmaṇa upākṛte prātaranuvāke brahmāṇam bhāṣamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvārdham asya yajñasyāntaragur iti tad yathaikapāt puruṣo yann ekataścakro vā ratho vartamāno bhreṣaṃ nyety evam eva sa yajño bhreṣaṃ nyeti yajñasya bhreṣam anu yajamāno bhreṣaṃ nyeti ||
children.translated_text: Some <s>Brahman</s> priests, when the morning recitation has been begun, sit speaking after having murmured the <s>stomabhāgas</s>. A certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, seeing a <s>Brahman</s> priest speaking when the morning recitation had begun, said this: "Half of this sacrifice has gone astray." Just as a one-footed man, or a chariot moving with one wheel, falls into a breakdown, so that sacrifice falls into a breakdown; after the breakdown of the sacrifice, the sacrificer falls into a breakdown.

children.text: tasmād brahmopākṛte prātaranuvāke vācaṃyamaḥ syād opāṃśvantaryāmayor homād upākṛteṣu pavamāneṣv odṛco 'tha yāni stotrāṇi saśastrāṇy ā teṣāṃ vaṣaṭkārād vācaṃyama eva syāt tad yathobhayataḥpāt puruṣo yann ubhayataścakro vā ratho vartamāno na riṣyaty evam eva sa yajño na riṣyati yajñasyāriṣṭim anu yajamāno na riṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the morning recitation has been begun under the supervision of the <s>Brahman</s>, he should keep silence from the offering of the <s>Upāṃśu</s> and <s>Antaryāma</s> cups until the end of the verses in the <s>Pavamāna</s> chants; then, for those stotras that have their śastras, he should keep silence until their <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>. Just as a man guarded on both sides, or a chariot moving with wheels on both sides, is not injured, so that sacrifice is not injured. Following the freedom from injury of the sacrifice, the sacrificer is not injured.

children.text: Chapter 187

tad āhur yad grahān me 'grahīt prācārīn ma āhutīr me 'hauṣīd ity adhvaryave dakṣiṇā nīyanta udagāsīn ma ity udgātre 'nvavocan me 'śaṃsīn me 'yākṣīn ma iti hotre kiṃ svid eva cakruṣe brahmaṇe dakṣiṇā nīyante 'kṛtvāho svid eva haratā iti ||
children.translated_text: They say: gifts are brought to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> because "he has taken the cups for me, he has gone forward for me, he has offered my oblations for me"; to the <s>Udgātṛ</s> because "he has sung for me"; to the <s>Hotṛ</s> because "he has recited after me, praised for me, sacrificed for me." But for what, indeed, that the <s>Brahman</s> has done are gifts brought to him? Or do they carry them off to him though he has done nothing?

children.text: yajñasya haiṣa bhiṣag yad brahmā yajñāyaiva tad bheṣajaṃ kṛtvā harati ||
children.translated_text: This one, namely the <s>Brahman</s>, is indeed the physician of the sacrifice. Having prepared a remedy for the sacrifice itself, he takes it.

children.text: atho yad bhūyiṣṭhenaiva brahmaṇā chandasāṃ rasenārtvijyaṃ karoti yad brahmā tasmād brahmārdhabhāggha vā eṣa itareṣām ṛtvijām agra āsa yad brahmārdham eva brahmaṇa āsārdham itareṣām ṛtvijām ||
children.translated_text: And further, because the <s>Brahman</s> performs his priestly office chiefly with <s>brahman</s>, the essence of the metres, therefore the <s>Brahman</s> is a half-sharer. Formerly the <s>Brahman</s> was the foremost of the other priests as a half-sharer: one half belonged to the <s>Brahman</s>, and one half to the other priests.

children.text: tasmād yadi yajña ṛkta ārtiḥ syād yadi yajuṣṭo yadi sāmato yady avijñātā sarvavyāpad vā brahmaṇa eva nivedayante tasmād yadi yajña ṛkta ārtir bhavati bhūr iti brahmā gārhapatye juhuyād yadi yajuṣṭo bhuva ity āgnīdhrīye 'nvāhāryapacane vā haviryajñeṣu yadi sāmataḥ svar ity āhavanīye yady avijñātā sarvavyāpad vā bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti sarvā anudrutyāhavanīya eva juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, if in the sacrifice there should be a mishap arising from the <s>ṛc</s>, or from the <s>yajus</s>, or from the <s>sāman</s>, or if it is unknown or affects everything, they report it to the <s>Brahman</s> alone. Therefore, if a mishap in the sacrifice arises from the <s>ṛc</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> should offer with "bhūr" in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire; if from the <s>yajus</s>, with "bhuvaḥ" in the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> fire, or in the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s> in oblation-sacrifices; if from the <s>sāman</s>, with "svar" in the <s>Āhavanīya</s>. If it is unknown or affects everything, after running around all the fires, he should offer with "bhūr bhuvaḥ svar" in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> alone.

children.text: sa prastotopākṛte stotra āha brahman stoṣyāmaḥ praśāstar iti sa bhūr iti brahmā prātaḥsavane brūyād indravantaḥ studhvam iti bhuva iti mādhyaṃdine savane brūyād indravantaḥ studhvam iti svar iti tṛtīyasavane brūyād indravantaḥ studhvam iti bhūr bhuvaḥ svar ity ukthe vātirātre vā brūyād indravantaḥ studhvam iti ||
children.translated_text: When the stotra has been begun, the <s>Prastotṛ</s> says, "O <s>Brahman</s>, O <s>Praśāstar</s>, shall we sing praise?" At the morning pressing the <s>Brahman</s> should say, "bhūr; chant with <s>Indra</s>." At the midday pressing he should say, "bhuvaḥ; chant with <s>Indra</s>." At the third pressing he should say, "svar; chant with <s>Indra</s>." At the <s>Uktha</s> or at the <s>Atirātra</s> he should say, "bhūr bhuvaḥ svar; chant with <s>Indra</s>."

children.text: sa yad āhendravantaḥ studhvam ity aindro vai yajña indro yajñasya devatā sendram eva tad udgīthaṃ karotīndrān mā gād indravantaḥ studhvam iti evaināṃs tad āha tad āha ||
children.translated_text: When he says, "Chant with <s>Indra</s>," the sacrifice indeed belongs to <s>Indra</s>; <s>Indra</s> is the deity of the sacrifice. He thereby makes the <s>udgītha</s> possessed of <s>Indra</s>. "Let it not go away from <s>Indra</s>; chant with <s>Indra</s>": this is what he says to them. This he says.

children.text: Chapter 188

devā ha vai sarvacarau satraṃ niṣedus te ha pāpmānaṃ nāpajaghnire tān hovācārbudaḥ kādraveyaḥ sarpaṛṣir mantrakṛd ekā vai vo hotrākṛtā tāṃ vo 'haṃ karavāṇy atha pāpmānam apahaniṣyadhva iti te ha tathety ūcus teṣāṃ ha sma sa madhyaṃdine madhyaṃdina evopodāsarpan grāvṇo 'bhiṣṭauti ||
children.translated_text: The gods once sat down for an all-ranging <s>sattra</s>. They did not drive away evil. <s>Arbuda Kādraveya</s>, a serpent seer and maker of mantras, said to them, "One priestly function of yours has not been performed. I shall perform it for you; then you will drive away evil." They said, "So be it." For them, at midday, precisely at midday, he used to creep up to the pressing stones and praise them.

children.text: tasmān madhyaṃdine madhyaṃdina eva grāvṇo 'bhiṣṭuvanti tadanukṛti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore at midday, precisely at midday, they praise the pressing stones. This is in imitation of that.

children.text: sa ha yenopodāsarpat taddhāpy etarhy arbudodāsarpaṇī nāma prapad asti ||
children.translated_text: The path by which he crept up is still even now called the <s>Arbudodāsarpaṇī</s>.

children.text: tān ha rājā madayāṃcakāra te hocur āśīviṣo vai no rājānam avekṣate hantāsyoṣṇīṣeṇākṣyāv apinahyāmeti tatheti tasya hoṣṇīṣeṇākṣyāv apinehus tasmād uṣṇīṣam eva paryasya grāvṇo 'bhiṣṭuvanti tadanukṛti ||
children.translated_text: The king kept making them intoxicated. They said, "A venomous serpent is looking at our king. Come, let us bind up his eyes with a turban." "So be it," they said. They bound up his eyes with a turban. Therefore, having wrapped on a turban, they praise the pressing stones. This is in imitation of that.

children.text: tān ha rājā madayām eva cakāra te hocuḥ svena vai no mantreṇa grāvṇo 'bhiṣṭautīti hantāsyānyābhir ṛgbhir mantram āpṛṇacāmeti tatheti tasya hānyābhir ṛgbhir mantram āpapṛcus tato hainān na madayāṃcakāra tad yad asyānyābhir ṛgbhir mantram āpṛñcanti śāntyā eva ||
children.translated_text: The king kept making them intoxicated all the same. They said, "He praises the pressing stones with his own mantra. Come, let us mix his mantra with other <s>ṛc</s> verses." "So be it," they said. They mixed his mantra with other <s>ṛc</s> verses. After that he did not make them intoxicated. When they mix his mantra with other <s>ṛc</s> verses, it is for appeasement.

children.text: te ha pāpmānam apajaghnire teṣām anv apahatiṃ sarpāḥ pāpmānam apajaghnire ta ete 'pahatapāpmāno hitvā pūrvāṃ jīrṇāṃ tvacaṃ navayaiva prayanti ||
children.translated_text: They drove away evil. Following their driving it away, serpents drove away evil. These serpents, having driven away evil and having abandoned their former old skin, go forth with a new one.

children.text: apa pāpmānaṃ hate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus strikes away evil.

children.text: Chapter 189
tad āhuḥ kiyatībhir abhiṣṭuyād iti śatenety āhuḥ śatāyur vai puruṣaḥ śatavīryaḥ śatendriya āyuṣy evainaṃ tad vīrya indriye dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "With how many verses should one praise?" "With a hundred," they say. Man indeed has a hundred years of life, a hundredfold vigor, and a hundred faculties. Thereby he places him in life, vigor, and faculty.

children.text: trayastriṃśatā vety āhus trayastriṃśato vai sa devānām pāpmano 'pāhaṃs trayastriṃśad vai tasya devā iti ||
children.translated_text: Or, they say, with thirty-three. For he drove away evil from the thirty-three gods, and the gods belonging to him were thirty-three.

children.text: aparimitābhir abhiṣṭuyād aparimito vai prajāpatiḥ prajāpater vā eṣā hotrā yad grāvastotrīyā tasyāṃ sarve kāmā avarudhyante sa yad aparimitābhir abhiṣṭauti sarveṣāṃ kāmānām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: One should praise with an unlimited number. <s>Prajāpati</s> is unlimited, and this priestly function, namely the <s>Grāvastotrīyā</s>, belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>. In it all desires are secured. When he praises with an unlimited number, it is for the securing of all desires.

children.text: sarvān kāmān avarunddhe ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus secures all desires.

children.text: tasmād aparimitābhir evābhiṣṭuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should praise with an unlimited number.

children.text: tad āhuḥ katham abhiṣṭuyād ity akṣaraśaḥ caturakṣaraśaḥ pacchaḥ ardharcaśaḥ ṛkśaḥ iti tad yad ṛkśo na tad avakalpate 'tha yat paccho no eva tad avakalpate 'tha yad akṣaraśaś caturakṣaraśo vi tathā chandāṃsi lupyeran bahūni tathākṣarāṇi hīyerann ardharcaśa evābhiṣṭuyāt pratiṣṭhāyā eva ||
children.translated_text: They say, "How should he praise them: syllable by syllable, four syllables at a time, by verse-foot, by half-verse, or by whole ṛc?" What is done by whole ṛc is not suitable; what is done by verse-foot is not suitable either. If it were syllable by syllable or four syllables at a time, the meters would be broken apart in that way, and many syllables would be lost. He should praise only by half-verse, for the sake of firm establishment.

children.text: dvipratiṣṭho vai puruṣaś catuṣpādāḥ paśavo yajamānam eva tad dvipratiṣṭhaṃ catuṣpātsu paśuṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati tasmād ardharcaśa evābhiṣṭuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Man is two-footed, and the animals are four-footed. Thus he establishes the sacrificer, who is two-footed, among the four-footed animals. Therefore he should praise only by half-verse.

children.text: tad āhur yan madhyaṃdine madhyaṃdina eva grāvṇo 'bhiṣṭauti katham asyetarayoḥ savanayor abhiṣṭutam bhavatīti yad eva gāyatrībhir abhiṣṭauti gāyatraṃ vai prātaḥsavanaṃ tena prātaḥsavane 'tha yaj jagatībhir abhiṣṭauti jāgataṃ vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ tena tṛtīyasavane ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since at the midday pressing he praises the pressing stones only at midday, how is praise accomplished for him at the other two pressings?" In that he praises with <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, the morning pressing is <s>Gāyatra</s>; by that it is done at the morning pressing. And in that he praises with <s>Jagatī</s> verses, the third pressing is <s>Jāgata</s>; by that it is done at the third pressing.

children.text: evam u hāsya madhyaṃdine madhyaṃdina eva grāvṇo 'bhiṣṭuvataḥ sarveṣu savaneṣv abhiṣṭutam bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when he praises the pressing stones at midday, only at midday, praise has been accomplished for him at all the pressings, who knows thus.

children.text: tad āhur yad adhvaryur evānyān ṛtvijaḥ saṃpreṣyaty atha kasmād eṣa etām asampreṣitaḥ pratipadyata iti mano vai grāvastotrīyāsampreṣitaṃ vā idaṃ manas tasmād eṣa etām asampreṣitaḥ pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since the <s>adhvaryu</s> gives directions to the other priests, why does this one undertake this without being directed?" The pressing-stone praise is mind; this mind is indeed undirected. Therefore this one undertakes it without being directed.

children.text: Chapter 190
vāg vai subrahmaṇyā tasyai somo rājā vatsaḥ some rājani krīte subrahmaṇyām āhvayanti yathā dhenum upahvayet tena vatsena yajamānāya sarvān kāmān duhe ||
children.translated_text: Speech is <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s>, and King <s>Soma</s> is her calf. When King <s>Soma</s> has been bought, they call out the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s>, as one would call a cow by means of her calf. By means of that calf she milks all desires for the sacrificer.

children.text: sarvān hāsmai kāmān vāg duhe ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Speech milks all desires for him, who knows thus.

children.text: tad āhuḥ kiṃ subrahmaṇyāyai subrahmaṇyātvam iti vāg eveti brūyād vāg vai brahma ca subrahma ceti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "What is the Subrahmaṇyā-ness of <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s>?" One should say, "Speech itself." For speech is both <s>brahma</s> and <s>subrahma</s>.

children.text: tad āhur atha kasmād enam pumāṃsaṃ santaṃ strīm ivācakṣata iti vāgghi subrahmaṇyeti brūyāt teneti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Then why, though he is male, do they refer to him as if to a female?" One should say, "Because speech is <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s>; for that reason."

children.text: tad āhur yad antarvedītara ṛtvija ārtvijyaṃ kurvanti bahirvedi subrahmaṇyā katham asyāntarvedy ārtvijyaṃ kṛtam bhavatīti veder vā utkaram utkiranti yad evotkare tiṣṭhann āhvayatīti brūyāt teneti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since the other priests perform their priestly work inside the altar, while <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> is outside the altar, how has her priestly work been done inside the altar?" One should say, "They throw up the altar's mound; by standing on the mound and calling out, it is done."

children.text: tad āhur atha kasmād utkare tiṣṭhan subrahmaṇyām āhvayatīty ṛṣayo vai satram āsata teṣāṃ yo varṣiṣṭha āsīt tam abruvan subrahmaṇyām āhvaya tvaṃ no nediṣṭhād devān hvayiṣyasīti varṣiṣṭham evainaṃ tat kurvanty atho vedim eva tat sarvām prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Then why does he stand on the mound and call out the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s>?" The seers once sat in a sacrificial session. They said to the one among them who was tallest, "Call out the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s>; from nearest at hand you will call the gods for us." Thus they make him the tallest, and further, by that he gratifies the whole altar.

children.text: tad āhuḥ kasmād asmā ṛṣabhaṃ dakṣiṇām abhyājantīti vṛṣā vā ṛṣabho yoṣā subrahmaṇyā tan mithunaṃ tasya mithunasya prajātyā iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Why do they drive a bull to him as the sacrificial gift?" The bull is male, and <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> is female. That is a pair; it is for the procreation of that pair.

children.text: upāṃśu pātnīvatasyāgnīdhro yajati reto vai pātnīvata upāṃśv iva vai retasaḥ siktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Agnīdhra</s> sacrifices the <s>Pātnīvata</s> silently. The <s>Pātnīvata</s> is seed; the emission of seed is, as it were, silent.

children.text: nānuvaṣaṭkaroti saṃsthā vā eṣā yad anuvaṣaṭkāro nedretaḥ saṃsthāpayānīty asaṃsthitaṃ vai retasaḥ samṛddhaṃ tasmān nānuvaṣaṭkaroti ||
children.translated_text: He does not make the after-<s>vaṣaṭ</s>. The after-<s>vaṣaṭ</s> is a completion, and he thinks, "Let me not bring the seed to completion." Seed prospers when it is not brought to completion; therefore he does not make the after-<s>vaṣaṭ</s>.

children.text: neṣṭur upastha āsīno bhakṣayati patnībhājanaṃ vai neṣṭāgniḥ patnīṣu reto dadhāti prajātyā agninaiva tat patnīṣu reto dadhāti prajātyai ||
children.translated_text: Sitting in the lap of the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>, he consumes the portion. The <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> is the receptacle belonging to the wives. <s>Agni</s> places seed in the wives for procreation; by <s>Agni</s> alone, then, he places seed in the wives for procreation.

children.text: prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He is propagated with offspring and with animals, who knows thus.

children.text: dakṣiṇā anu subrahmaṇyā saṃtiṣṭhate vāg vai subrahmaṇyānnaṃ dakṣiṇānnādya eva tad vāci yajñam antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayanti pratiṣṭhāpayanti ||
children.translated_text: The sacrificial gift comes to rest after the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s>. Speech is <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s>; food is the sacrificial gift. From food and eating, they finally establish the sacrifice in speech. They establish it indeed.

children.text: Chapter 191

devā vai yajñam atanvata tāṃs tanvānān asurā abhyāyan yajñaveśasam eṣāṃ kariṣyāma iti tān dakṣiṇata upāyan yata eṣāṃ yajñasya taniṣṭham amanyanta te devāḥ pratibudhya mitrāvaruṇau dakṣiṇataḥ paryauhaṃs te mitrāvaruṇābhyām eva dakṣiṇataḥ prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apāghnata tathaivaitad yajamānā mitrāvaruṇābhyām eva dakṣiṇataḥ prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apaghnate tasmān maitrāvaruṇam maitrāvaruṇaḥ prātaḥsavane śaṃsati mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ hi devā dakṣiṇataḥ prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apāghnata ||
children.translated_text: The gods once stretched out the sacrifice. As they were stretching it out, the <s>Asuras</s> came upon them, saying, "We will make ruin of their sacrifice." They came upon them from the south, from where they thought the sacrifice was thinnest. The gods, becoming aware, set <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> around on the south. With <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> they drove away the asura-demons from the south at the morning pressing. In the same way, these sacrificers drive away the asura-demons from the south at the morning pressing with <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>. Therefore the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> priest recites the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> at the morning pressing, for with <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> the gods drove away the asura-demons from the south at the morning pressing.

children.text: te vai dakṣiṇato 'pahatā asurā madhyato yajñam prāviśaṃs te devāḥ pratibudhyendram madhyato 'dadhus ta indreṇaiva madhyataḥ prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apāghnata tathaivaitad yajamānā indreṇaiva madhyataḥ prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apaghnate tasmād aindram brāhmaṇācchaṃsī prātaḥsavane śaṃsatīndreṇa hi devā madhyataḥ prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apāghnata ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>Asuras</s>, beaten off from the south, entered the sacrifice from the middle. The gods, becoming aware, placed <s>Indra</s> in the middle. With <s>Indra</s> they drove away the asura-demons from the middle at the morning pressing. In the same way, these sacrificers drive away the asura-demons from the middle at the morning pressing with <s>Indra</s>. Therefore the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites the <s>Aindra</s> at the morning pressing, for with <s>Indra</s> the gods drove away the asura-demons from the middle at the morning pressing.

children.text: te vai madhyato 'pahatā asurā uttarato yajñam prāviśaṃs te devāḥ pratibudhyendrāgnī uttarataḥ paryauhaṃs ta indrāgnibhyāṃ evottarataḥ prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apāghnata tathaivaitad yajamānā indrāgnibhyām evottarataḥ prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apaghnate tasmād aindrāgnam achāvākaḥ prātaḥsavane śaṃsatīndrāgnibhyāṃ hi devā uttarataḥ prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apāghnata ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>Asuras</s>, struck away from the middle, entered the sacrifice from the north. The gods, becoming aware of them, arrayed <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> around it on the north. With <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> alone, from the north, at the morning pressing, they drove away the Asura-Rākṣasas. In just the same way these sacrificers, with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> alone, from the north, at the morning pressing, drive away the Asura-Rākṣasas. Therefore the <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites an Aindrāgna hymn at the morning pressing, for with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> the gods drove away the Asura-Rākṣasas from the north at the morning pressing.

children.text: te vā uttarato 'pahatā asurāḥ purastāt paryadravan samanīkatas te devāḥ pratibudhyāgnim purastāt prātaḥsavane paryauhaṃs te 'gninaiva purastāt prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apāghnata tathaivaitad yajamānā agninaiva purastāt prātaḥsavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apaghnate tasmād āgneyam prātaḥsavanam ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>Asuras</s>, struck away from the north, ran around to the east in battle array. The gods, becoming aware of them, arrayed <s>Agni</s> around it in front at the morning pressing. With <s>Agni</s> alone, from the front, at the morning pressing, they drove away the Asura-Rākṣasas. In just the same way these sacrificers, with <s>Agni</s> alone, from the front, at the morning pressing, drive away the Asura-Rākṣasas. Therefore the morning pressing is Āgneya, belonging to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: apa pāpmānaṃ hate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He drives away evil, who knows thus.

children.text: te vai purastād apahatā asurāḥ paścāt parītya prāviśaṃs te devāḥ pratibudhya viśvān devān ātmānaṃ paścāt tṛtīyasavane paryauhaṃs te viśvair eva devair ātmabhiḥ paścāt tṛtīyasavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apāghnata tathaivaitad yajamānā viśvair eva devair ātmabhiḥ paścāt tṛtīyasavane 'surarakṣāṃsy apaghnate tasmād vaiśvadevaṃ tṛtīyasavanam ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>Asuras</s>, struck away from the front, went around behind and entered. The gods, becoming aware of them, arrayed all the gods, their own selves, around it behind at the third pressing. With all the gods, with their own selves, from behind, at the third pressing, they drove away the Asura-Rākṣasas. In just the same way these sacrificers, with all the gods, with their own selves, from behind, at the third pressing, drive away the Asura-Rākṣasas. Therefore the third pressing is Vaiśvadeva, belonging to all the gods.

children.text: apa pāpmānaṃ hate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He drives away evil, who knows thus.

children.text: te vai devā asurān evam apāghnata sarvasmād eva yajñāt tato vai devā abhavan parāsurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the gods drove the <s>Asuras</s> away from the whole sacrifice. Thereafter the gods came into being, and the <s>Asuras</s> were defeated.

children.text: bhavaty ātmanā parāsya dviṣan pāpmā bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He comes into being in his own person, and his hateful evil rival is defeated, who knows thus.

children.text: te devā evaṃ kﾱptena yajñenāpāsurān pāpmānam aghnatājayan svargaṃ lokam ||
children.translated_text: With the sacrifice thus arranged, the gods drove away the <s>Asuras</s>, evil, and won the heavenly world.

children.text: apa ha vai dviṣantam pāpmānam bhrātṛvyaṃ hate jayati svargaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān savanāni kalpayati ||
children.translated_text: He indeed drives away the hating evil rival, and wins the heavenly world, who knows thus and who, knowing thus, arranges the pressings.

children.text: Chapter 192
stotriyaṃ stotriyasyānurūpaṃ kurvanti prātaḥsavane 'har eva tad ahno 'nurūpaṃ kurvanty avareṇaiva tad ahnā param ahar abhyārabhante ||
children.translated_text: At the morning pressing they make the stotriya correspond to the stotriya. Thus they make the day correspond to the day. With the lower day they lay hold of the higher day.

children.text: atha tathā na madhyaṃdine śrīr vai pṛṣṭhāni tāni tasmai na tasthānāni yat stotriyaṃ stotriyasyānurūpaṃ kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But not so at midday. The pṛṣṭhas are splendor, and these would not be firmly established for him if they were to make the stotriya correspond to the stotriya.

children.text: tayaiva vibhaktyā tṛtīyasavane na stotriyaṃ stotriyasyānurūpaṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: By that same division, at the third pressing, they do not make the stotriya correspond to the stotriya.

children.text: Chapter 193
athāta ārambhaṇīyā eva ||
children.translated_text: Now, then, there are the opening verses.

children.text: ṛjunītī no varuṇa iti maitrāvaruṇasya mitro nayatu vidvān iti praṇetā vā eṣa hotrakāṇāṃ yan maitrāvaruṇas tasmād eṣā praṇetṛmatī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: "With straight guidance for us, O <s>Varuṇa</s>," is for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; "let <s>Mitra</s>, knowing, lead," it says. For the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is the leader of the Hotraka priests. Therefore this verse contains a leader.

children.text: indraṃ vo viśvatas parīti brāhmaṇācchaṃsino havāmahe janebhya itīndram evaitayāhar ahar nihvayante ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Indra</s> for you on every side," is for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>; "we call from among the people," it says. With this they call <s>Indra</s> day by day.

children.text: na haiṣāṃ vihave 'nya indraṃ vṛṅkte yatraivaṃ vidvān brāhmaṇācchaṃsy etām ahar ahaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: In their invocation no other person wins <s>Indra</s> away, where a <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> who knows thus recites this day by day.

children.text: yat soma ā sute nara ity achāvākasyendrāgnī ajohavur itīndrāgnī evaitayāhar ahar nihvayante na haiṣāṃ vihave 'nya indrāgnī vṛṅkte yatraivaṃ vidvān achāvāka etām ahar ahaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: "When <s>Soma</s> is pressed, O men," is for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>; "they called on <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>," it says. With this they call <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> day by day. In their invocation no other person wins <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> away, where an <s>Acchāvāka</s> who knows thus recites this day by day.

children.text: tā vā etāḥ svargasya lokasya nāvaḥ sampāriṇyaḥ svargam evaitābhir lokam abhisaṃtaranti ||
children.translated_text: These, indeed, are boats to the heavenly world, carrying one completely across. By means of these they cross over to the heavenly world.

children.text: Chapter 194
athātaḥ paridhānīyā eva ||
children.translated_text: Now, then, there are the closing verses.

children.text: te syāma deva varuṇeti maitrāvaruṇasyeṣaṃ svaś ca dhīmahīty ayaṃ vai loka iṣam ity asau lokaḥ svar ity ubhāv evaitayā lokāv ārabhante ||
children.translated_text: "May we be yours, O god <s>Varuṇa</s>," is for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; "may we set our thought on refreshment and on <s>svar</s>," it says. This world is refreshment; yonder world is <s>svar</s>. With this they lay hold of both worlds.

children.text: vy antarikṣam atirad iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsino vivattṛcaṃ svargam evaibhya etayā lokaṃ vivṛṇoti ||
children.translated_text: "He has opened wide the midspace," is for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, a vivattṛcā verse. With this he opens the heavenly world for them.

children.text: made somasya rocanā indro yad abhinad valamiti ||
children.translated_text: "In the exhilaration of <s>Soma</s>, the lights, when <s>Indra</s> broke open <s>Vala</s>," it says.

children.text: siṣāsavo vā ete yad dīkṣitās tasmād eṣā valavatī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: These consecrated sacrificers are desirous of winning; therefore this verse contains <s>Vala</s>.

children.text: ud gā ājad aṅgirobhya āviṣkṛṇvan guhā satīḥ arvāñcaṃ nunude valam iti sanim evaibhya etayāvarunddhe ||
children.translated_text: "He drove out the cows for the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, revealing them though they were hidden; he thrust <s>Vala</s> down hither," it says. With this he secures gain for them.

children.text: indreṇa rocanā diva iti svargo vai loka indreṇa rocanā divaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "By <s>Indra</s>, the lights of heaven," it says. The heavenly world is, indeed, the lights of heaven by <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: dṛﾱhāni dṛṃhitāni ca sthirāṇi na parāṇuda iti ||
children.translated_text: "The firm things, strengthened and stable, he did not drive away," it says.

children.text: svarga evaitayā loke 'harahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti ||
children.translated_text: With this they go, establishing themselves day by day in the heavenly world.

children.text: āhaṃ sarasvatīvator ity achāvākasya vāg vai sarasvatī vāgvator iti haitad āhendrāgnyor avo vṛṇa ity etaddha vā indrāgnyoḥ priyaṃ dhāma yad vāg iti priyeṇaivainau tad dhāmnā samardhayati ||
children.translated_text: "I call upon the two rich in <s>Sarasvatī</s>," is for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>. Speech is <s>Sarasvatī</s>; thus he really says, "the two rich in speech." "I choose the aid of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>," it says. This indeed is the dear abode of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, namely speech. By that dear abode he prospers them.

children.text: priyeṇa dhāmnā samṛdhyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He prospers by a dear abode, who knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 195
ubhayyaḥ paridhānīyā bhavanti hotrakāṇām prātaḥsavane ca mādhyaṃdine cāhīnāś caikāhikāś ca ||
children.translated_text: There are both kinds of closing verses for the Hotraka priests, at the morning pressing and at the midday pressing: both ahīna verses and ekāhika verses.

children.text: tata aikāhikābhir eva maitrāvaruṇaḥ paridadhāti tenāsmāllokānna pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> closes with the ekāhika verses alone. Thereby he does not fall away from this world.

children.text: ahīnābhir achāvākaḥ svargasya lokasyāptyā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Acchāvāka</s> closes with the ahīna verses, for the attainment of the heavenly world.

children.text: ubhayībhir brāhmaṇācchaṃsī teno sa ubhau vyanvārabhamāṇa etīmaṃ cāmuṃ ca lokam atho maitrāvaruṇaṃ cāchāvākaṃ cātho ahīnaṃ caikāham cātho saṃvatsaraṃ cāgniṣṭomaṃ caivam u sa ubhau vyanvārabhamāṇa eti ||
children.translated_text: With both sets the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> proceeds, thereby taking hold of both worlds, this one and yonder one; and likewise of the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> and the <s>Acchāvāka</s>, of the <s>ahīna</s> and the <s>ekāha</s>, and of the year and the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>. In this way he proceeds, taking hold of both.

children.text: atha tata aikāhikā eva tṛtīyasavane hotrakāṇām paridhānīyā bhavanti pratiṣṭhā vā ekāhaḥ pratiṣṭhāyām eva tad yajñam antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayanti ||
children.translated_text: After that, at the third pressing, the concluding verses of the <s>Hotraka</s> priests are precisely those belonging to the <s>ekāha</s>. The <s>ekāha</s> is a foundation; at the very end they thereby establish the sacrifice upon a foundation.

children.text: anavānam prātaḥsavane yajet ||
children.translated_text: At the morning pressing he should sacrifice without taking breath.

children.text: ekāṃ dve na stomam atiśaṃset tad yathābhiheṣate pipāsate kṣipram prayacchet tādṛk tad atho kṣipraṃ devebhyo 'nnādyaṃ somapītham prayacchānīti kṣipraṃ hāsmiṃlloke pratitiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: He should not overpraise the <s>stoma</s> beyond one or two. Just as one would quickly give drink to one that is neighing and thirsty, such is this. And further, thinking, 'May I quickly present food and eating, the Soma-drink, to the gods,' he quickly becomes established in this world.

children.text: aparimitābhir uttarayoḥ savanayor aparimito vai svargo lokaḥ svargasya lokasyāptyai ||
children.translated_text: At the two later pressings he should use an unlimited number of verses, for the heavenly world is unlimited; this is for the attainment of the heavenly world.

children.text: kāmaṃ taddhotā śaṃsed yaddhotrakāḥ pūrvedyuḥ śaṃseyur yad vā hotā taddhotrakāḥ prāṇo vai hotāṅgāni hotrakāḥ samāno vā ayam prāṇo 'ṅgāny anusaṃcarati tasmāt tat kāmaṃ hotā śaṃsed yaddhotrakāḥ pūrvedyuḥ śaṃseyur yad vā hotā taddhotrakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s> may recite at will what the <s>Hotraka</s> priests would recite on the preceding day, or the <s>Hotraka</s> priests may recite what the <s>Hotṛ</s> would recite. The <s>Hotṛ</s> is breath, and the <s>Hotraka</s> priests are the limbs; this same breath moves through the limbs. Therefore the <s>Hotṛ</s> may recite at will what the <s>Hotraka</s> priests would recite on the preceding day, or the <s>Hotraka</s> priests what the <s>Hotṛ</s> would recite.

children.text: sūktāntair hotā paridadhad ety atha samānya eva tṛtīyasavane hotrakāṇām paridhānīyā bhavanty ātmā vai hotāṅgāni hotrakāḥ samānā vā ime 'ṅgānām antās tasmāt samānya eva tṛtīyasavane hotrakāṇām paridhānīyā bhavanti bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s> proceeds, enclosing with the endings of hymns. Then, at the third pressing, the concluding verses of the <s>Hotraka</s> priests are common ones. The <s>Hotṛ</s> is the self, and the <s>Hotraka</s> priests are the limbs; the ends of these limbs are alike. Therefore at the third pressing the concluding verses of the <s>Hotraka</s> priests are common ones; they are so.

children.text: Chapter 196
ā tvā vahantu haraya iti prātaḥsavana unnīyamānebhyo 'nvāha vṛṣaṇvatīḥ pītavatīḥ sutavatīr madvatī rūpasamṛddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the Soma cups are being drawn at the morning pressing, he recites over them the verse beginning, 'May the tawny steeds bring you.' They contain the words 'bull,' 'drunk,' 'pressed,' and 'intoxicating'; they are complete in form.

children.text: aindrīr anvāhaindro vai yajñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites verses addressed to <s>Indra</s>, for the sacrifice indeed belongs to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: gāyatrīr anvāha gāyatraṃ vai prātaḥsavanam ||
children.translated_text: He recites verses in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre, for the morning pressing is connected with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: nava nyūnāḥ prātaḥsavane 'nvāha nyūne vai retaḥ sicyate ||
children.translated_text: At the morning pressing he recites nine, a deficient number; for seed is emitted into what is deficient.

children.text: daśa madhyaṃdine 'nvāha nyūne vai retaḥ siktam madhyaṃ striyai prāpya sthaviṣṭham bhavati ||
children.translated_text: At midday he recites ten. Seed emitted into what is deficient, when it reaches the middle of the woman, becomes thickest.

children.text: nava nyūnās tṛtīyasavane 'nvāha nyūnād vai prajāḥ prajāyante ||
children.translated_text: At the third pressing he recites nine, a deficient number; for from what is deficient offspring are born.

children.text: tad yad etāni kevalasūktāny anvāha yajamānam eva tad garbham bhūtam prajanayati yajñād devayonyai ||
children.translated_text: When he recites these independent hymns, he thereby brings the sacrificer to birth from the sacrifice, from the divine womb, as an embryo.

children.text: te haike sapta saptānvāhuḥ sapta prātaḥsavane sapta mādhyaṃdine sapta tṛtīyasavane yāvatyo vai puronuvākyās tāvatyo yājyāḥ sapta vai prāñco yajanti sapta vaṣaṭkurvanti tāsām etāḥ puronuvākyā iti vadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some recite seven and seven: seven at the morning pressing, seven at midday, and seven at the third pressing, saying, 'As many as the invitatory verses are, so many are the offering verses. Seven sacrifice facing east, and seven utter the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>; these are their invitatory verses.'

children.text: tat tathā na kuryād yajamānasya ha te reto vilumpanty atho yajamānam eva yajamāno hi sūktam ||
children.translated_text: One should not do it in that way. They tear away the sacrificer's seed, and also the sacrificer himself, for the sacrificer is the hymn.

children.text: navabhir vā etam maitrāvaruṇo 'smāl lokād antarikṣalokam abhi pravahati daśabhir antarikṣalokād amuṃ lokam abhy antarikṣaloko hi jyeṣṭho navabhir amuṣmāl lokāt svargaṃ lokam abhi ||
children.translated_text: With nine verses the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> carries him from this world toward the midspace-world; with ten, from the midspace-world toward yonder world, for the midspace-world is the greatest; and with nine, from yonder world toward the heavenly world.

children.text: na ha vai te yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokam abhi voﾱhum arhanti ye sapta saptānvāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who recite seven and seven are certainly not able to carry the sacrificer toward the heavenly world.

children.text: tasmāt kevalaśa eva sūktāny anubrūyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should recite the hymns only as independent whole hymns.

children.text: Chapter 197

athāha yad aindro vai yajño 'tha kasmād dvāveva prātaḥsavane prasthitānām pratyakṣād aindrībhyāṃ yajato hotā caiva brāhmaṇācchaṃsī cedaṃ te somyam madhviti hotā yajatīndra tvā vṛṣabhaṃ vayaṃ iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsī nānādevatyābhir itare kathaṃ teṣām aindryo bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: Now he says: if the sacrifice indeed belongs to <s>Indra</s>, why, at the morning pressing, do only two of those who have set out sacrifice with verses directly addressed to <s>Indra</s>, namely the <s>Hotṛ</s> and the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>? The <s>Hotṛ</s> sacrifices with, 'This sweet Soma is for you,' and the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> with, '<s>Indra</s>, we choose you, the bull.' The others use verses addressed to different deities; how, then, are their verses Indra-verses?

children.text: mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmaha iti maitrāvaruṇo yajati varuṇaṃ somapītaya iti yad vai kiṃca pītavat padaṃ tad aindraṃ rūpaṃ tenendram prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> sacrifices with, 'We call <s>Mitra</s>,' and with, '<s>Varuṇa</s>, for the drinking of Soma.' Whatever word contains the idea of drinking is a form of <s>Indra</s>; by it he pleases <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: maruto yasya hi kṣaya iti potā yajati sa sugopātamo jana itīndro vai gopās tad aindraṃ rūpaṃ tenendram prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Potṛ</s> sacrifices with, 'The <s>Maruts</s>, whose dwelling is indeed,' and with, 'He is the best guardian of the people.' <s>Indra</s> is the guardian; that is a form of <s>Indra</s>, and by it he pleases <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: agne patnīr ihā vaheti neṣṭā yajati tvaṣṭāraṃ somapītaya itīndro vai tvaṣṭā tad aindraṃ rūpaṃ tenendram prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> sacrifices with, '<s>Agni</s>, bring the wives here,' and with, '<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, for the drinking of Soma.' <s>Indra</s> is <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>; that is a form of <s>Indra</s>, and by it he pleases <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: ukṣānnāya vaśānnāyety āgnīdhro yajati somapṛṣṭhāya vedhasa itīndro vai vedhās tad aindraṃ rūpaṃ tenendram prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> sacrifices with, 'For the bull-eater, for the cow-eater,' and with, 'For the wise one whose back is Soma.' <s>Indra</s> is the wise one; that is a form of <s>Indra</s>, and by it he pleases <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: prātaryāvabhir ā gataṃ devebhir jenyāvasū indrāgnī somapītaya iti svayaṃ samṛddhāchāvākāsya ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Acchāvāka</s>'s verse is complete in itself: 'Come with those who travel in the morning, with the gods, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, possessors of victorious wealth, for the drinking of Soma.'

children.text: evam u haitā aindryo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed these become verses addressed to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: yan nānādevatyās tenānyā devatāḥ prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: In that they are addressed to various deities, by that he pleases the other deities.

children.text: yad u gāyatryas tenāgneyyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that they are in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre, by that they are connected with <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: etad u haitābhis trayam upāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: With these verses, then, he obtains these three things.

children.text: Chapter 198
asāvi devaṃ goṛjīkam andha iti madhyaṃdina unnīyamānebhyo 'nvāha vṛṣaṇvatīḥ pītavatīḥ sutavatīr madvatī rūpasamṛddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At midday, when the Soma cups are being drawn, he recites over them the verse beginning, 'The Soma-draught has been pressed for the god, rich in cattle.' They contain the words 'bull,' 'drunk,' 'pressed,' and 'intoxicating'; they are complete in form.

children.text: aindrīr anvāhaindro vai yajñas triṣṭubho 'nvāha traiṣṭubham vai mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam ||
children.translated_text: He recites verses addressed to <s>Indra</s>, for the sacrifice indeed belongs to <s>Indra</s>. He recites verses in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> metre, for the midday pressing is connected with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: tad āhur yat tṛtīyasavanasyaiva rūpam madvad atha kasmān madhyaṃdine madvatīr anu cāha yajanti cābhir iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since it is really the form of the third pressing that is Madvat, why then at midday does he recite Madvatī verses and sacrifice with them?"

children.text: mādyantīva vai madhyaṃdine devatāḥ sam eva tṛtīyasavane mādayante tasmān madhyaṃdine madvatīr anu cāha yajanti cābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: At midday the deities are, as it were, intoxicated; at the third pressing he makes them intoxicated altogether. Therefore at midday he recites Madvatī verses and sacrifices with them.

children.text: te vai khalu sarva eva mādhyaṃdine prasthitānām pratyakṣād aindrībhir yajanti ||
children.translated_text: Now all of them, when the midday cups have been set forth, sacrifice directly with verses belonging to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: abhitṛṇṇavatībhir eke ||
children.translated_text: Some do so with verses containing the word <s>abhitṛṇṇa</s>.

children.text: pibā somam abhi yam ugra tarda iti hotā yajati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s> sacrifices with, "Drink the soma, you fierce one, pierce through him."

children.text: sa īṃ pāhi ya ṛjīṣī tarutra iti maitrāvaruṇo yajati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> sacrifices with, "Protect him, you who are <s>Ṛjīṣin</s>, who overcome."

children.text: evā pāhi pratnathā mandatu tveti brāhmaṇācchaṃsī yajati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> sacrifices with, "Protect in this way, as of old; let it exhilarate you."

children.text: arvāṅ ehi somakāmaṃ tvāhur iti potā yajati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Potṛ</s> sacrifices with, "Come hither; they say that you desire soma."

children.text: tavāyaṃ somastvam ehy arvāṅ iti neṣṭā yajati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> sacrifices with, "This soma is yours; come hither."

children.text: indrāya somāḥ pradivo vidānā ity achāvāko yajati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Acchāvāka</s> sacrifices with, "The somas, known from ancient days, are for <s>Indra</s>."

children.text: āpūrṇo asya kalaśaḥ svāhety āgnīdhro yajati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> sacrifices with, "His bowl is full; svāhā."

children.text: tāsām etā abhitṛṇṇavatyo bhavantīndro vai prātaḥsavane na vyajayata sa etābhir eva mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam abhyatṛṇad yad abhyatṛṇat tasmād etā abhitṛṇṇavatyo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Of these, these are the verses containing <s>abhitṛṇṇa</s>. At the morning pressing <s>Indra</s> did not win distinctly; with these very verses he pierced through the midday pressing. Because he pierced through it, therefore these are verses containing <s>abhitṛṇṇa</s>.

children.text: Chapter 199
ihopa yāta śavaso napāta iti tṛtīyasavana unnīyamānebhyo 'nvāha vṛṣaṇvatīḥ pītavatīḥ sutavatīr madvatī rūpasamṛddhās tā aindrārbhavyo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: When the third pressing is being drawn up, he recites for the cups that are being lifted, "Come here, offspring of strength," verses containing <s>vṛṣan</s>, containing drinking, containing pressing, and containing exhilaration, complete in their proper form; they belong to <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Ṛbhus</s>.

children.text: tad āhur yan nārbhavīṣu stuvate 'tha kasmād ārbhavaḥ pavamāna ity ācakṣata iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Since they do not chant in the <s>Arbhavī</s> hymns, why then do they call it the <s>Ārbhava Pavamāna</s>?"

children.text: prajāpatir vai pitarbhūn martyān sato 'martyān kṛtvā tṛtīyasavana ābhajat tasmān nārbhavīṣu stuvate 'thārbhavaḥ pavamāna ity ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, having made the ancestors, who were mortal beings, immortal, assigned them to the third pressing. Therefore they do not chant in the <s>Arbhavī</s> hymns, yet they call it the <s>Ārbhava Pavamāna</s>.

children.text: athāha yad yathāchandasam pūrvayoḥ savanayor anvāha gāyatrīḥ prātaḥsavane triṣṭubho mādhyaṃdine 'tha kasmāj jāgate sati tṛtīyasavane triṣṭubho 'nvāheti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says, "Since in the two earlier pressings he recites according to the meter, Gāyatrī verses at the morning pressing and Triṣṭubh verses at midday, why then, when the third pressing is Jāgata, does he recite Triṣṭubh verses?"

children.text: dhītarasaṃ vai tṛtīyasavanam athaitad adhītarasaṃ śukriyaṃ chando yat triṣṭup savanasya sarasatāyā iti brūyād atho indraṃ evaitat savane 'nvābhajatīti ||
children.translated_text: One should say, "The third pressing is one whose sap has been drunk away, and this Triṣṭubh meter is bright and has not had its sap drunk away, for the juiciness of the pressing." And also, "Thereby he assigns <s>Indra</s> himself to the pressing."

children.text: athāha yad aindrārbhavaṃ vai tṛtīyasavanam atha kasmād eṣa eva tṛtīyasavane prasthitānām pratyakṣād aindrārbhavyā yajatīndra ṛbhubhir vājavadbhiḥ samukṣitam iti hotaiva nānādevatyābhir itare kathaṃ teṣām aindrārbhavyo bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says, "Since the third pressing belongs to <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, why is it that among those whose cups have been set forth at the third pressing only this one sacrifices directly with verses belonging to <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, namely the <s>Hotṛ</s> with, 'For <s>Indra</s>, sprinkled together with the strength-giving <s>Ṛbhus</s>'; but the others use verses having different deities? How do their verses belong to <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Ṛbhus</s>?"

children.text: indrāvaruṇā sutapāv imaṃ sutam iti maitrāvaruṇo yajati yuvo ratho adhvaraṃ devavītaya iti bahūni vāha tad ṛbhūṇām rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> sacrifices with, "O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, drinkers of the pressed soma, drink this pressed soma"; and with, "Your chariot goes to the rite for the divine feast." It conveys plurality, and that is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>.

children.text: indraś ca somam pibatam bṛhaspata iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsī yajaty ā vāṃ viśantv indavaḥ svābhuva iti bahūni vāha tad ṛbhūṇāṃ rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> sacrifices with, "O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, drink the soma"; and with, "Let the drops enter you two, self-born ones." It conveys plurality, and that is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>.

children.text: ā vo vahantu saptayo raghuṣyada iti potā yajati raghupatvānaḥ pra jigāta bāhubhir iti bahūni vāha tad ṛbhūṇāṃ rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Potṛ</s> sacrifices with, "Let your swift horses bring you here, moving lightly"; and with, "With quick flight come forth with your arms." It conveys plurality, and that is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>.

children.text: ameva naḥ suhavā ā hi gantaneti neṣṭā yajati gantaneti bahūni vāha tad ṛbhūṇāṃ rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> sacrifices with, "Come hither to us, readily invoked ones"; the word "come" conveys plurality, and that is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>.

children.text: indrāviṣṇū pibatam madhvo asyety achāvāko yajaty ā vām andhāṃsi madirāṇy agmann iti bahūni vāha tad ṛbhūṇāṃ rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Acchāvāka</s> sacrifices with, "O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, drink of this sweetness"; and with, "The exhilarating draughts have come to you two." It conveys plurality, and that is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>.

children.text: imaṃ stomam arhate jātavedasa ity āgnīdhro yajati ratham iva saṃ mahemā manīṣayeti bahūni vāha tad ṛbhūṇāṃ rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Āgnīdhra</s> sacrifices with, "This praise-song for the worthy <s>Jātavedas</s>"; and with, "May we fit it together with thought, like a chariot." It conveys plurality, and that is the form of the <s>Ṛbhus</s>.

children.text: evam u haitā aindrārbhavyo bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed these verses belong to <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Ṛbhus</s>.

children.text: yan nānādevatyās tenānyā devatāḥ prīṇāti ||
children.translated_text: Insofar as they have various deities, he thereby satisfies other deities.

children.text: yad u jagatprāsāhā jāgataṃ vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ tṛtīyasavanasyaiva samṛddhyai ||
children.translated_text: And insofar as they have the Jāgata refrain, the third pressing is Jāgata; this is for the prosperity of the third pressing itself.

children.text: Chapter 200
athāha yad ukthinyo 'nyā hotrā anukthā anyāḥ katham asyaitā ukthinyaḥ sarvāḥ samāḥ samṛddhā bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says, "Since some Hotṛ offices are Ukthya and others are without an uktha, how do all these Ukthya offices of his become equal and complete?"

children.text: yad evaināḥ saṃpragīrya hotrā ity ācakṣate tena samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because they call them Hotṛ offices after gathering them together in recitation: by that they are equal.

children.text: yad ukthinyo 'nyā hotrā anukthā anyās teno viṣamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because some Hotṛ offices are Ukthya and others are without an uktha: by that, on the other hand, they are unequal.

children.text: evam u hāsyaitā ukthinyaḥ sarvāḥ samāḥ samṛddhā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus indeed all these Ukthya offices of his become equal and complete.

children.text: athāha śaṃsanti prātaḥsavane śaṃsanti mādhyaṃdine hotrakāḥ katham eṣāṃ tṛtīyasavane śastam bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says, "They recite at the morning pressing, and the Hotṛ assistants recite at midday; how is the recitation of these men accomplished at the third pressing?"

children.text: yad eva mādhyaṃdine dve dve sūkte śaṃsantīti brūyāt teneti ||
children.translated_text: One should say, "Because at midday they recite two hymns each; by that it is accomplished."

children.text: athāha yad dvyuktho hotā kathaṃ hotrakā dvyukthā bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says, "Since the <s>Hotṛ</s> has two ukthas, how do the Hotṛ assistants have two ukthas?"

children.text: yad eva dvidevatyābhir yajantīti brūyāt teneti ||
children.translated_text: One should say, "Because they sacrifice with verses addressed to two deities; by that they have them."

children.text: Chapter 201
athāha yad etās tisra ukthinyo hotrāḥ katham itarā ukthinyo bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says, "Since these three Hotṛ offices are Ukthya, how do the others become Ukthya?"

children.text: ājyam evāgnīdhrīyāyā uktham marutvatīyam potrīyāyai vaiśvadevaṃ neṣṭrīyāyai tā vā etā hotrā evaṃnyaṅgā eva bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ājya</s> itself is the uktha of the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> office, the <s>Marutvatīya</s> of the <s>Potṛ</s>'s office, and the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> of the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>'s office. These Hotṛ offices are, in this way, just so furnished with their limbs.

children.text: athāha yad ekapraiṣā anye hotrakā atha kasmād dvipraiṣaḥ potā dvipraiṣo neṣṭeti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says, "Since the other Hotṛ assistants have a single summons, why are the <s>Potṛ</s> and the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> summoned twice?"

children.text: yatrādo gāyatrī suparṇo bhūtvā somam āharat tad etāsāṃ hotrāṇām indra ukthāni parilupya hotre pradadau yūyam mābhyahvayadhvaṃ yūyam asyāvediṣṭeti te hocur devā vāceme hotre prabhāvayāmeti tasmāt te dvipraiṣe bhavata ṛcāgnīdhrīyām prabhāvayāṃcakrus tasmāt tasyaikayarcā bhūyasyo yājyā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Where formerly the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, having become a <s>suparṇa</s>, brought the soma, there <s>Indra</s>, having stripped away the ukthas from these Hotṛ-offices, gave them to the <s>Hotṛ</s>: "You shall call upon me; you know this most nearly." They, the gods, said, "Let us empower speech here for the <s>Hotṛ</s>." Therefore those two have a double summons. They empowered the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> with an ṛc verse; therefore its yājyā verses with a single ṛc are the more numerous.

children.text: athāha yaddhotā yakṣaddhotā yakṣad iti maitrāvaruṇo hotre preṣyaty atha kasmād ahotṛbhyaḥ sadbhyo hotrāśaṃsibhyo hotā yakṣaddhotā yakṣad iti preṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says: since the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> gives the command to the <s>Hotṛ</s>, "Let the <s>Hotṛ</s> sacrifice, let the <s>Hotṛ</s> sacrifice," why does he give the command, "Let the <s>Hotṛ</s> sacrifice, let the <s>Hotṛ</s> sacrifice," to the Hotrāśaṃsins, though they are not <s>Hotṛ</s>s?

children.text: prāṇo vai hotā prāṇaḥ sarva ṛtvijaḥ prāṇo yakṣat prāṇo yakṣad ity eva tad āha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed the <s>Hotṛ</s>; <s>Prāṇa</s> is all the officiating priests. Thus he is saying precisely, "Let <s>Prāṇa</s> sacrifice, let <s>Prāṇa</s> sacrifice."

children.text: athāhāsty udgātṝṇām praiṣaḥ nāṁ iti astīti brūyād yad evaitat praśāstā japaṃ japitvā studhvam ity āha sa eṣām praiṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he says: "Is there a summons for the <s>Udgātṛ</s>s, or not?" One should say, "There is." When the <s>Praśāstar</s>, after muttering the muttering, says, "Sing praise," that is their summons.

children.text: athāhāsty achāvākasya pravarāḥ nāṁ iti astīti brūyād yad evainam adhvaryur āhāchāvāka vadasva yat te vādyam ity eṣo 'sya pravaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he says: "Are there pravaras for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>, or not?" One should say, "There are." When the <s>Adhvaryu</s> says to him, "<s>Acchāvāka</s>, speak what is yours to be spoken," that is his pravara.

children.text: athāha yad aindrāvaruṇam maitrāvaruṇas tṛtīyasavane śaṃsaty atha kasmād asyāgneyau stotriyānurūpau bhavata ity agninā vai mukhena devā asurān ukthebhyo nirjaghnus tasmād asyāgneyau stotriyānurūpau bhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he says: since the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites an Aindrāvaruṇa hymn at the third pressing, why are his stotriya and anurūpa verses Agneya? With <s>Agni</s> as their mouth, the gods drove the Asuras out from the ukthas; therefore his stotriya and anurūpa verses are Agneya.

children.text: athāha yad aindrābārhaspatyam brāhmaṇācchaṃsī tṛtīyasavane śaṃsaty aindrāvaiṣṇavam achāvākaḥ katham enayor aindrāḥ stotriyānurūpā bhavantītīndro ha sma vā asurān ukthebhyaḥ prajigāya so 'bravīt kaś cāhaṃ cety ahaṃ cāhaṃ ceti ha sma devatā anvavayanti sa yad indraḥ pūrvaḥ prajigāya tasmād enayor aindrāḥ stotriyānurūpā bhavanti yad v ahaṃ cāhaṃ ceti ha sma devatā anvavayus tasmān nānādevatyāni śaṃsataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he says: since the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites an Aindrabārhaspatya hymn at the third pressing, and the <s>Acchāvāka</s> an Aindrāvaiṣṇava one, how are the stotriya and anurūpa verses of these two Aindra? <s>Indra</s>, it is said, won the Asuras away from the ukthas. He said, "Who, and I?" The deities, it is said, followed after saying, "I too, I too." Because <s>Indra</s> won first, therefore the stotriya and anurūpa verses of these two are Aindra. But because the deities followed after saying, "I too, I too," therefore they recite hymns having different deities.

children.text: Chapter 202

athāha yad vaiśvadevaṃ vai tṛtīyasavanam atha kasmād etāny aindrāṇi jāgatāni sūktāni tṛtīyasavana ārambhaṇīyāni śasyanta itīndram evaitair ārabhya yantīti brūyād atho yaj jāgataṃ vai tṛtīyasavanaṃ taj jagatkāmyaiva tad yat kiṃcāta ūrdhvaṃ chandaḥ śasyate taddha sarvaṃ jāgatam bhavaty etāni ced aindrāṇi jāgatāni sūktāni tṛtīyasavana ārambhaṇīyāni śasyante ||
children.translated_text: Then he says: since the third pressing is Vaiśvadeva, why are these Aindra Jagatī hymns recited at the third pressing as opening hymns? One should say, "With these they proceed after taking hold of <s>Indra</s>." And further, since the third pressing is Jagatī, that is done with desire for the world of moving beings. Whatever metre is recited after that becomes altogether Jagatī, provided these Aindra Jagatī hymns are recited at the third pressing as opening hymns.

children.text: atha traiṣṭubham achāvāko 'ntataḥ śaṃsati saṃ vāṃ karmaṇeti yad eva panāyyaṃ karma tad etad abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites a Triṣṭubh verse at the end, beginning "saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā"; he thereby declares that very praiseworthy act.

children.text: sam iṣety annaṃ vā iṣo 'nnādyasyāvaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: "Together with nourishment": nourishment is food; this is for the securing of food and eating.

children.text: ariṣṭair naḥ pathibhiḥ pārayanteti svastitāyā evaitad aharahaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: "May they carry us across by unharmed paths": he recites this day by day precisely for well-being.

children.text: athāha yaj jāgataṃ vai tṛtīyasavanam atha kasmād eṣāṃ triṣṭubhaḥ paridhānīyā bhavantīti vīryaṃ vai triṣṭub vīrya eva tad antataḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says: since the third pressing is Jagatī, why are their enclosing verses Triṣṭubh? The Triṣṭubh is vigor. Thus, standing finally upon vigor, they go forth.

children.text: iyam indraṃ varuṇam aṣṭa me gīr iti maitrāvaruṇasya bṛhaspatir naḥ pari pātu paścād iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsina ubhā jigyathur ity achāvākasya ||
children.translated_text: "This song of mine has invoked <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>" belongs to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; "May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> protect us from behind" belongs to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>; "You both have conquered" belongs to the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.

children.text: ubhau hi tau jigyatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those two both conquered.

children.text: na parā jayethe na parā jigya iti ||
children.translated_text: "You two were not beaten back; you two were not defeated."

children.text: na hi tayoḥ kataraś cana parājigye ||
children.translated_text: For neither of those two was defeated.

children.text: indraś ca viṣṇo yad apaspṛdhethāṃ tredhā sahasraṃ vi tad airayethām iti ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, when you strove, you drove the thousand apart threefold."

children.text: indraś ca ha vai viṣṇuś cāsurair yuyudhāte tān ha sma jitvocatuḥ kalpāmahā iti te ha tathety asurā ūcuḥ so 'bravīd indro yāvad evāyaṃ viṣṇus trir vikramate tāvad asmākam atha yuṣmākam itarad iti sa imāṃllokān vicakrame 'tho vedān atho vācaṃ tad āhuḥ kiṃ tat sahasram itīme lokā ime vedā atho vāg iti brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, it is said, fought with the Asuras. Having defeated them, they said, "Let us make an arrangement." The Asuras said, "So be it." <s>Indra</s> said, "As much as this <s>Viṣṇu</s> strides in three steps, that much is ours; the rest is yours." He strode across these worlds, and also the Vedas, and also speech. They ask, "What was that thousand?" One should answer, "These worlds, these Vedas, and speech."

children.text: airayethām airayethām ity achāvāka ukthye 'bhyasyati sa hi tatrāntyo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Acchāvāka</s> repeats "airayethām, airayethām" in the Ukthya rite, for there he is the last.

children.text: agniṣṭome hotātirātre ca sa hi tatrāntyo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: At the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> the <s>Hotṛ</s> does so, and at the <s>Atirātra</s>; for there he is the last.

children.text: abhyasyet ṣoﾱaśini nābhyasyait iti abhyasyed ity āhuḥ katham anyeṣv ahaḥsv abhyasyati katham atra nābhyasyed iti tasmād abhyasyet ||
children.translated_text: "Should he repeat in the <s>Ṣoḍaśin</s>, or should he not repeat?" "He should repeat," they say. "How can he repeat on the other days and not repeat here?" Therefore he should repeat.

children.text: Chapter 203
athāha yan nārāśaṃsaṃ vai tṛtīyasavanam atha kasmād achāvāko 'ntataḥ śilpeṣv anārāśaṃsīḥ śaṃsatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then he says: since the third pressing is Nārāśaṃsa, why does the <s>Acchāvāka</s>, at the end, recite non-Nārāśaṃsī verses among the śilpas?

children.text: vikṛtir vai nārāśaṃsaṃ kim iva ca vai kim ivaca reto vikriyate tat tadā vikṛtam prajātam bhavaty athaitan mṛdv iva chandaḥ śithiraṃ yan nārāśaṃsam athaiṣo 'ntyo yad achāvākas tad dṛﾱhatāyai dṛﾱhe pratiṣṭhāsyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: The Nārāśaṃsa is transformation. Just as this or that seed is transformed, then, when transformed, it is born as that transformed thing. But this Nārāśaṃsa metre is as it were soft and slack. Now the <s>Acchāvāka</s> is the last one; that is for firmness: "We shall stand upon firmness, upon the firm."

children.text: tasmād achāvāko 'ntataḥ śilpeṣv anārāśaṃsīḥ śaṃsati dṛﾱhatāyai dṛﾱhe pratiṣṭhāsyāma iti dṛﾱhe pratiṣṭhāsyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Acchāvāka</s>, at the end, recites non-Nārāśaṃsī verses among the śilpas, for firmness: "We shall stand upon firmness, upon the firm; we shall stand upon the firm."

children.text: Chapter 204
yaḥ śvaḥstotriyas tam anurūpaṃ kurvanti prātaḥsavane 'hīnasaṃtatyai ||
children.translated_text: What is the stotriya for the following day they make the anurūpa at the morning pressing, for the continuity of the <s>ahīna</s>.

children.text: yathā vā ekāhaḥ suta evam ahīnas tad yathaikāhasya sutasya savanāni saṃtiṣṭhamānāni yanty evam evāhīnasyāhāni saṃtiṣṭhamānāni yanti tad yacchvaḥstotriyam anurūpaṃ kurvanti prātaḥsavane 'hīnasaṃtatyā ahīnameva tat saṃtanvanti ||
children.translated_text: For just as a one-day rite, when its soma has been pressed, proceeds with its pressings established, so an <s>ahīna</s> proceeds with its days established. Therefore, when they make the next day's stotriya the anurūpa at the morning pressing, it is for the continuity of the <s>ahīna</s>; thereby they extend the <s>ahīna</s> itself.

children.text: te vai devāś ca ṛṣayaś cādriyanta samānena yajñaṃ saṃtanavāmeti ta etat samānaṃ yajñasyāpaśyan samānān pragāthān samānīḥ pratipadaḥ samānāni sūktāni ||
children.translated_text: The gods and the seers were concerned: "Let us extend the sacrifice by means of something common." They saw this common element of the sacrifice: common pragāthas, common opening verses, and common hymns.

children.text: okaḥsārī vā indro yatra vā indraḥ pūrvaṃ gacchaty aiva tatrāparaṃ gacchati yajñasyaiva sendratāyai ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> is one who goes to his accustomed place. Wherever <s>Indra</s> goes first, there indeed the later one goes also, for the sacrifice's possession of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: Chapter 205

tān vā etān sampātān viśvāmitraḥ prathamam apaśyat tān viśvāmitreṇa dṛṣṭān vāmadevo 'sṛjataiva tvām indra vajrinn atra yan na indro jujuṣe yacca vaṣṭi kathā mahām avṛdhat kasya hotur iti tān kṣipraṃ samapatad yat kṣipraṃ samapatat tat sampātānāṃ sampātatvam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāmitra</s> first saw these sampātas. <s>Vāmadeva</s> created those that had been seen by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>: "Thus you, O <s>Indra</s>, wielder of the bolt, here," "What <s>Indra</s> has favored for us and what he desires," and "How has the great one grown? Of which Hotṛ?" They fell together quickly; because they fell together quickly, that is the sampāta-character of the sampātas.

children.text: sa hekṣāṃcakre viśvāmitro yān vā ahaṃ sampātān apaśyaṃ tān vāmadevo 'sṛṣṭa kāni nv ahaṃ sūktāni sampātāṃs tatpratimān sṛjeyeti sa etāni sūktāni sampātāṃs tatpratimān asṛjata sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ kanīna indraḥ pūrbhid ātirad dāsam arkair imām ū ṣu prabhṛtiṃ sātaye dhā icchanti tvā somyāsaḥ sakhāyaḥ śāsad vahnir duhitur naptyaṃ gād abhi taṣṭeva dīdhayā manīṣām iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāmitra</s> considered: "The sampātas that I saw, <s>Vāmadeva</s> has created. What hymns, corresponding to those sampātas, should I create?" He created these hymns as sampātas corresponding to them: "Born at once, a young bull," "<s>Indra</s>, breaker of forts, overcame the Dāsa with songs," "Set forth this offering for winning," "Your soma-loving friends seek you," "The carrier, ruling, has gone to the daughter's offspring," and "I shape my inspired thought like a craftsman with skill."

children.text: ya eka iddhavyaś carṣaṇīnām iti bharadvājo yas tigmaśṛṅgo vṛṣabho na bhīma ud u brahmāṇy airata śravasyeti vasiṣṭho 'smā id u pra tavase turāyeti nodhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He alone is to be invoked among peoples" is <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s; "He who, sharp-horned, like a fearsome bull" and "He has raised up the prayers for fame" are <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s; "To him indeed, for strength and overcoming" is <s>Nodhās</s>'s.

children.text: ta ete prātaḥsavane ṣaﾱahastotriyāñchastvā mādhyaṃdine 'hīnasūktāni śaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: After reciting the six-day stotriyas at the morning pressing, they recite the <s>ahīna</s> hymns at the midday pressing.

children.text: tāny etāny ahīnasūktāny ā satyo yātu maghavān ṛjīṣīti satyavan maitrāvaruṇo 'smā id u pra tavase turāyendrāya brahmāṇi rātatamā indra brahmāṇi gotamāso akrann iti brahmaṇvad brāhmaṇācchaṃsī śāsad vahnir janayanta vahnim iti vahnivad achāvākaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are those <s>ahīna</s> hymns: "May the truthful, bountiful one go to the pressed Soma," containing the word "truth," is for the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; "To him indeed, for strength and overcoming," "The prayers, most lavish for <s>Indra</s>," and "The <s>Gotamas</s> have made prayers for <s>Indra</s>," containing the word "prayer," are for the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>; "The carrier ruled, generating the carrier," containing the word "carrier," is for the <s>Acchāvāka</s>.

children.text: tad āhuḥ kasmād achāvāko vahnivad etat sūktam ubhayatra śaṃsati parāñciṣu caivāhaḥsv abhyāvartiṣu ceti ||
children.translated_text: They say: "Why does the <s>Acchāvāka</s> recite this hymn containing the word 'carrier' in both situations, both on the forward-going days and on the returning days?"

children.text: vīryavān vā eṣa bahvṛco vahnivad etat sūktaṃ vahati ha vai vahnir dhuro yāsu yujyate tasmād achāvāko vahnivad etat sūktam ubhayatra śaṃsati parāñciṣu caivāhaḥsv abhyāvartiṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: This Bahvṛca is vigorous; he carries this hymn containing the word "carrier." For the carrier does carry the loads to which he is yoked. Therefore the <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites this hymn containing the word "carrier" in both situations, both on the forward-going days and on the returning days.

children.text: tāni pañcasv ahaḥsu bhavanti caturviṃśe 'bhijiti viṣuvati viśvajiti mahāvrate 'hīnāni ha vā etāny ahāni na hy eṣu kiṃcana hīyate parāñcīni ha vā etāny ahāny anabhyāvartīni tasmād enāny eteṣv ahaḥsu śaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: They occur on five days: the <s>Caturviṃśa</s>, the <s>Abhijit</s>, the <s>Viṣuvat</s>, the <s>Viśvajit</s>, and the <s>Mahāvrata</s>. These days are indeed <s>ahīna</s> days, for nothing at all is lacking in them. These days are forward-going and not returning; therefore they recite these hymns on those days.

children.text: yad enāni śaṃsanty ahīnān svargāṃllokān sarvarūpān sarvasamṛddhān avāpnavāmeti ||
children.translated_text: When they recite these hymns, they do so thinking, "May we obtain the <s>ahīna</s> heavenly worlds, possessing every form and every prosperity."

children.text: yad evaināni śaṃsantīndram evaitair nihvayante yatharṣabhaṃ vāśitāyai ||
children.translated_text: When they recite these hymns, they thereby call upon <s>Indra</s> himself, as one calls a bull for a cow in heat.

children.text: yad v evaināni śaṃsanty ahīnasya saṃtatyā ahīnam eva tat saṃtanvanti ||
children.translated_text: And when they recite these hymns, it is for the continuity of the <s>ahīna</s>; thereby they extend the <s>ahīna</s> itself.

children.text: Chapter 206
tato vā etāṃs trīn sampātān maitrāvaruṇo viparyāsam ekaikam ahar ahaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites these three sampātas in reverse order, one on each successive day.

children.text: evā tvām indra vajrinn atreti prathame 'hani yan na indro jujuṣe yac ca vaṣṭīti dvitīye kathā mahām avṛdhat kasya hotur iti tṛtīye ||
children.translated_text: "Thus you, O <s>Indra</s>, wielder of the bolt, here" is on the first day; "What <s>Indra</s> has favored for us and what he desires" is on the second; "How has the great one grown? Of which Hotṛ?" is on the third.

children.text: trīn eva sampātān brāhmaṇācchaṃsī viparyāsam ekaikam ahar ahaḥ śaṃsatīndraḥ pūrbhid ātirad dāsam arkair iti prathame 'hani ya eka iddhavyaś carṣaṇīnām iti dvitīye yas tigmaśṛṅgo vṛṣabho na bhīma iti tṛtīye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> likewise recites three sampātas in reverse order, one on each successive day: "<s>Indra</s>, breaker of forts, overcame the Dāsa with songs" on the first day; "He alone is to be invoked among peoples" on the second; "He who, sharp-horned, like a fearsome bull" on the third.

children.text: trīn eva sampātān achāvāko viparyāsam ekaikam ahar ahaḥ śaṃsatīmām ū ṣu prabhṛtiṃ sātaye dhā iti prathame 'hanīcchanti tvā somyāsaḥ sakhāya iti dvitīye śāsad vahnir duhitur naptyaṃ gād iti tṛtīye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Acchāvāka</s> likewise recites three sampātas in reverse order, one on each successive day: "Set forth this offering for winning" on the first day; "Your soma-loving friends seek you" on the second; "The carrier, ruling, has gone to the daughter's offspring" on the third.

children.text: tāni vā etāni nava ||
children.translated_text: These are nine.

children.text: trīṇi cāhar ahaḥ śasyāni ||
children.translated_text: And three are to be recited on each day.

children.text: tāni dvādaśa sampadyante dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatir yajñas tat saṃvatsaram prajāpatiṃ yajñam āpnuvanti tat saṃvatsare prajāpatau yajñe 'har ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti ||
children.translated_text: They amount to twelve. Twelve months are a year; the year is <s>Prajāpati</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s> is the sacrifice. Thus they obtain the year, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the sacrifice. Thus they go on, establishing themselves day by day in the year, in <s>Prajāpati</s>, and in the sacrifice.

children.text: tāny antareṇāvāpam āvaperan ||
children.translated_text: Between them they should insert an insertion.

children.text: anyūṅkhyā virājo vaimadīś caturthe 'hani paṅktīḥ pañcame pārucchepīḥ ṣaṣṭhe ||
children.translated_text: On the fourth day they should insert the Anyūṅkhyā Virāj verses and the Vaimadī verses, on the fifth the Paṅkti verses, and on the sixth the Pārucchepī verses.

children.text: atha yāny ahāni mahāstomāni syuḥ ko adya naryo devakāma iti maitrāvaruṇa āvapeta vane na vā yo ny adhāyi cākann iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsy ā yāhy arvāṅ upa vandhureṣṭhā ity achāvākaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, on the days that are <s>mahāstoma</s>s, the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> should insert, 'Who today, heroic one, desirous of the gods?'; the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, 'In the wood, or he who was set down elsewhere, they delighted'; the <s>Acchāvāka</s>, 'Come hither, sitting near on the chariot-seat.'

children.text: etāni vā āvapanāny etair vā āvapanair devāḥ svargam lokam ajayann etair ṛṣayas tathaivaitad yajamānā etair āvapanaiḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ jayanti ||
children.translated_text: These, indeed, are the insertions. With these insertions the gods won the <s>svarga</s> world; with these the seers did so. In just the same way, the patrons win the <s>svarga</s> world with these insertions.

children.text: Chapter 207
sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ kanīna iti maitrāvaruṇaḥ purastāt sūktānām ahar ahaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites before the hymns, day by day, 'Born at once, the young bull.'

children.text: tad etat sūktaṃ svargyam etena vai sūktena devāḥ svargaṃ lokam ajayann etena ṛṣayas tathaivaitad yajamānā etena sūktena svargaṃ lokaṃ jayanti ||
children.translated_text: That hymn is a means to <s>svarga</s>. With this hymn the gods won the <s>svarga</s> world; with it the seers did so. In just the same way, the patrons win the <s>svarga</s> world with this hymn.

children.text: tad u vaiśvāmitraṃ viśvasya ha vai mitraṃ viśvāmitra āsa ||
children.translated_text: It is a hymn of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>; for <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was indeed a friend of all.

children.text: viśvaṃ hāsmai mitram bhavati ya evaṃ veda yeṣāṃ caivaṃ vidvān etan maitrāvaruṇaḥ purastāt sūktānām ahar ahaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: Everything becomes friendly to the one who knows this, and to those for whom the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, knowing this, recites it before the hymns day by day.

children.text: tad ṛṣabhavat paśumad bhavati paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: It has bulls and cattle; this is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: tat pañcarcam bhavati pañcapadā paṅktiḥ paṅktir vā annam annādyasyāvaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: It consists of five verses. The <s>Paṅkti</s> has five feet; and <s>Paṅkti</s> is food. This is for the securing of food and eating.

children.text: ud u brahmāṇy airata śravasyeti brāhmaṇācchaṃsī brahmaṇvat samṛddhaṃ sūktam ahar ahaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites day by day the hymn, 'The sacred formulations have raised up fame,' a hymn possessed of <s>brahman</s> and complete.

children.text: tad etat sūktaṃ svargyam etena vai sūktena devāḥ svargaṃ lokam ajayann etena ṛṣayas tathaivaitad yajamānā etena sūktena svargaṃ lokaṃ jayanti ||
children.translated_text: That hymn is a means to <s>svarga</s>. With this hymn the gods won the <s>svarga</s> world; with it the seers did so. In just the same way, the patrons win the <s>svarga</s> world with this hymn.

children.text: tad u vāsiṣṭham etena vai vasiṣṭha indrasya priyaṃ dhāmopāgacchat sa paramaṃ lokam ajayat ||
children.translated_text: It is a hymn of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. With this, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> reached <s>Indra</s>'s beloved abode, and he won the highest world.

children.text: upendrasya priyaṃ lokaṃ gacchati jayati paramaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this goes to <s>Indra</s>'s beloved world and wins the highest world.

children.text: tad vai ṣaﾱṛcaṃ ṣaḍ vā ṛtava ṛtūnām āptyai ||
children.translated_text: It consists of six verses. There are six seasons; this is for the attainment of the seasons.

children.text: tad upariṣṭāt sampātānāṃ śaṃsaty āptvaiva tat svargaṃ lokaṃ yajamānā asmiṃlloke pratitiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: He recites it after the <s>sampāta</s> verses. Having thereby attained the <s>svarga</s> world, the patrons stand firmly in this world.

children.text: abhi taṣṭeva dīdhayā manīṣām ity achāvāko 'har ahaḥ śaṃsaty abhivat tatyai rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites day by day, 'Like a carpenter, with vision, I shape my thought'; that has the form of approach toward the goal.

children.text: abhi priyāṇi marmṛśat parāṇīti yāny eva parāṇy ahāni tāni priyāṇi tāny eva tad abhimarmṛśato yanty abhyārabhamāṇāḥ paro vā asmāl lokāt svargo lokas tam eva tad abhivadati ||
children.translated_text: 'May he touch the dear things, the distant ones': whatever later days there are, they are the dear things; setting out and taking hold, they go on touching those very days. The <s>svarga</s> world is beyond this world; he thereby speaks toward that very world.

children.text: kavīṃr icchāmi saṃdṛśe sumedhā iti ||
children.translated_text: 'I desire to see the poets, being wise.'

children.text: ye vai te na ṛṣayaḥ pūrve pretās te vai kavayas tān eva tad abhyativadati ||
children.translated_text: Those former seers who have departed are the poets; he thereby speaks beyond, toward them.

children.text: tad u vaiśvāmitraṃ viśvasya ha vai mitraṃ viśvāmitra āsa viśvaṃ hāsmai mitram bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: It is a hymn of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>; for <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was indeed a friend of all. Everything becomes friendly to the one who knows this.

children.text: tad aniruktam prājāpatyaṃ śaṃsaty anirukto vai prajāpatiḥ prajāpater āptyai ||
children.translated_text: He recites it as undefined and as belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> is undefined; this is for the attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: sakṛd indraṃ nirāha tenaindrād rūpān na pracyavate ||
children.translated_text: Once he expressly utters <s>Indra</s>; by that he does not fall away from the form belonging to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: tad vai daśarcaṃ daśākṣarā virāﾱ annaṃ virāﾱ annādyasyāvaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: It consists of ten verses. The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables; <s>Virāj</s> is food. This is for the securing of food and eating.

children.text: yad eva daśarcaṃ daśa vai prāṇāḥ prāṇān eva tad āpnuvanti prāṇān ātman dadhate ||
children.translated_text: Because it consists of ten verses: there are ten vital breaths. They thereby obtain the vital breaths and place the vital breaths in themselves.

children.text: tad upariṣṭāt sampātānāṃ śaṃsaty āptvaiva tat svargaṃ lokaṃ yajamānā asmiṃlloke pratitiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: He recites it after the <s>sampāta</s> verses. Having thereby attained the <s>svarga</s> world, the patrons stand firmly in this world.

children.text: Chapter 208
kas tam indra tvāvasuṃ kan navyo atasīnāṃ kad ū nv asyākṛtam iti kadvantaḥ pragāthā ārambhaṇīyā ahar ahaḥ śasyante ||
children.translated_text: The <s>pragātha</s>s containing the word <s>kad</s>, beginning 'Who, O <s>Indra</s> rich in aid, who is newer among those who sit? When now is his deed done?' are recited day by day as opening verses.

children.text: ko vai prajāpatiḥ prajāpater āptyai ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ka</s> is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>; this is for the attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: yad eva kadvantaḥ annaṃ vai kam annādyasyāvaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: Because they contain <s>kad</s>: <s>ka</s> is food; this is for the securing of food and eating.
