children.text: yad v eva kadvantaḥ ahar ahar vā ete śāntāny ahīnasūktāny upayuñjānā yanti tāni kadvadbhiḥ pragāthaiḥ śamayanti tāny ebhyaḥ śāntāni kam bhavanti tāny enāñchāntāni svargaṃ lokam abhi vahanti ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, because they contain <s>kad</s>: day after day they proceed using these pacified <s>ahīna</s> hymns. With the <s>pragātha</s>s containing <s>kad</s> they pacify them; pacified, they become <s>ka</s> for them. Pacified, they carry them to the <s>svarga</s> world.

children.text: triṣṭubhaḥ sūktapratipadaḥ śaṃseyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should recite <s>Triṣṭubh</s> opening verses for the hymns.

children.text: tā haike purastāt pragāthānāṃ śaṃsanti dhāyyā iti vadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some recite them before the <s>pragātha</s>s, saying, 'They are <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.'

children.text: tat tathā na kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: One should not do it in that way.

children.text: kṣatraṃ vai hotā viśo hotrāśaṃsinaḥ kṣatrāyaiva tad viśam pratyudyāminīṃ kuryuḥ pāpavasyasam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s> is the ruling power; the Hotṛ-assistants are the people. They would thereby make the people rise up against the ruling power, which would be more evil and worse.

children.text: triṣṭubho ma imāḥ sūktapratipada ity eva vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: Rather, one should understand, 'These are my <s>Triṣṭubh</s> opening verses for the hymns.'

children.text: tad yathā samudram praplaverann evaṃ haiva te praplavante ye saṃvatsaraṃ vā dvādaśāhaṃ vāsate tad yathā sairāvatīṃ nāvam pārakāmāḥ samāroheyur evam evaitās triṣṭubhaḥ samārohanti ||
children.translated_text: Just as they might set sail into the ocean, so indeed those who sit through the year-long rite or the twelve-day rite set sail. Just as men wishing for the far shore would board a boat with oars, so they board these <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses.

children.text: na ha vā etac chando gamayitvā svargaṃ lokam upāvartate vīryavattamaṃ hi ||
children.translated_text: This meter, having led them to the <s>svarga</s> world, does not turn back, for it is the most vigorous.

children.text: tābhyo na vyāhvayīta samānaṃ hi chando 'tho ned dhāyyāḥ karavāṇīti ||
children.translated_text: One should not call out separately from them, for the meter is the same; and also, 'lest I make them <s>dhāyyā</s> verses.'

children.text: yad enāḥ śaṃsanti prajñātābhiḥ sūktapratipadbhiḥ sūktāni samārohāmeti ||
children.translated_text: When they recite these with recognized hymn-opening verses, they do so thinking, 'Let us mount the hymns.'

children.text: yad evaināḥ śaṃsantīndram evaitābhir nihvayante yatharṣabhaṃ vāśitāyai yad v evaināḥ śaṃsanty ahīnasya saṃtatyā ahīnam eva tat saṃtanvanti ||
children.translated_text: When they recite these, they summon <s>Indra</s> with them, as one summons a bull for a cow in heat. Or rather, when they recite these, it is for the continuity of the <s>ahīna</s>; they thereby extend the <s>ahīna</s>.

children.text: Chapter 209
apa prāca indra viśvāṁ amitrān iti maitrāvaruṇaḥ purastāt sūktānām ahar ahaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites day after day before the hymns: "Drive away, O <s>Indra</s>, all hostile powers in front."

children.text: apāpāco abhibhūte nudasva apodīco apa śūrādharāca urau yathā tava śarman mademeti ||
children.translated_text: "Drive away those behind, overpowering them; drive away those to the north, O hero, and those below. May we rejoice in your broad shelter."

children.text: abhayasya rūpam abhayam iva hi yann icchati ||
children.translated_text: This is the form of fearlessness, for what he desires is, as it were, fearlessness.

children.text: brahmaṇā te brahmayujā yunajmīti brāhmaṇācchaṃsy ahar ahaḥ śaṃsati yunajmīti yuktavatī yukta iva hy ahīno 'hīnasya rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites day after day: "With sacred formulation, yoked to sacred formulation, I yoke you." The phrase "I yoke" contains yoking; for the <s>ahīna</s> is as though yoked. This is the form of the <s>ahīna</s>.

children.text: uruṃ no lokam anu neṣi vidvān ity achāvāko 'harahaḥ śaṃsaty anu neṣīty etīva hy ahīno 'hīnasya rūpam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites day after day: "Knowing, you lead us along to a broad world." The phrase "you lead along" is as though "you go"; for the <s>ahīna</s> is as though going. This is the form of the <s>ahīna</s>.

children.text: neṣīti sattrāyaṇarūpam ||
children.translated_text: The word "you lead" is the form of the <s>sattrāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: tā vā etā ahar ahaḥ śasyante ||
children.translated_text: These, then, are recited day after day.

children.text: samānībhiḥ paridadhyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should enclose the rite with the same verses.

children.text: okaḥsārī haiṣām indro yajñam bhavatī3ṃ yatharṣabho vāśitāṃ yathā vā gauḥ prajñātaṃ goṣṭham evaṃ haiṣām indro yajñam aiva gacchati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> becomes one who goes to their own place, to their sacrifice: just as a bull goes to a cow in heat, or as a cow goes to a known cowshed, so indeed <s>Indra</s> goes to their sacrifice.

children.text: na śunaṃhuvīyayāhīnasya paridadhyāt kṣatriyo ha rāṣṭrāccyavate yo haiva paro bhavati tam abhihvayati ||
children.translated_text: One should not enclose the <s>ahīna</s> with the <s>Śunaṃhuvīya</s> verse. The kṣatriya who is superior falls from the kingdom, for one calls upon precisely the one who is other and superior.

children.text: Chapter 210
athāto 'hīnasya yuktiś ca vimuktiś ca ||
children.translated_text: Now, then, the yoking and the release of the <s>ahīna</s>.

children.text: vy antarikṣam atirad ity ahīnaṃ yuṅkta eved indram iti vimuñcati ||
children.translated_text: With "He has stretched apart the midspace" he indeed yokes the <s>ahīna</s>; with "indeed <s>Indra</s>" he releases it.

children.text: āhaṃ sarasvatīvator nūnaṃ sā ta ity ahīnaṃ yuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: With the two <s>Sarasvatīvat</s> verses, beginning "I now ..." and "that now is yours," he yokes the <s>ahīna</s>.

children.text: te syāma deva varuṇa nū ṣṭuta iti vimuñcati ||
children.translated_text: With "May we be yours, O god <s>Varuṇa</s>, now that you have been praised" he releases it.

children.text: eṣa ha vā ahīnaṃ tantum arhati ya enaṃ yoktuṃ ca vimoktuṃ ca veda ||
children.translated_text: He indeed is worthy of the thread of the <s>ahīna</s> who knows how to yoke it and how to release it.

children.text: tad yac caturviṃśe 'han yujyante sā yuktir atha yat purastād udayanīyasyātirātrasya vimucyante sa vimuktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That they are yoked on the twenty-fourth day is the yoking; and that they are released before the concluding <s>Atirātra</s> is the release.

children.text: tad yac caturviṃśe 'hann aikāhikābhiḥ paridadhyur atrāhaiva yajñaṃ saṃsthāpayeyur nāhīnakarma kuryur atha yad ahīnaparidhānīyābhiḥ paridadhyur yathā śrānto 'vimucyamāna utkṛtyetaivaṃ yajamānā utkṛtyerann ubhayībhiḥ paridadhyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, on the twenty-fourth day, they were to enclose with one-day verses, they would complete the sacrifice right there on that day and would not perform the work of an <s>ahīna</s>. But if they were to enclose with <s>ahīna</s>-enclosing verses, then, just as a tired man who is not released would be torn apart, so the sacrificers would be torn apart. They should enclose with both kinds.

children.text: tad yathā dīrghādhva upavimokaṃ yāyāt tādṛk tat ||
children.translated_text: That is like going on a long road toward a place of release.

children.text: saṃtato haiṣāṃ yajño bhavatīṃ vy ū muñcante ||
children.translated_text: Their sacrifice is continuous, and yet they release it.

children.text: ekāṃ dve na dvayoḥ savanayoḥ stomam atiśaṃset ||
children.translated_text: One should not over-recite the <s>stoma</s> by one or two at two pressings.

children.text: dīrghāraṇyāni ha vai bhavanti yatra bahvībhiḥ stomo 'tiśasyate ||
children.translated_text: Long wildernesses, indeed, arise where the <s>stoma</s> is over-recited with many verses.

children.text: aparimitābhiḥ tṛtīyasavane 'parimito vai svargo lokaḥ svargasya lokasyāptyai ||
children.translated_text: At the third pressing he may use an unlimited number, for the heavenly world is unlimited; this is for the attainment of the heavenly world.

children.text: saṃtato hāsyābhyārabdho 'visrasto 'hīno bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān ahīnaṃ tanute ||
children.translated_text: For the one who, knowing thus, extends the <s>ahīna</s>, the <s>ahīna</s> is continuous, firmly begun, and not fallen apart.

children.text: Chapter 211

devā vai vale gāḥ paryapaśyaṃs tā yajñenaivepsaṃs tāḥ ṣaṣṭhenāhnāpnuvaṃs te prātaḥsavane nabhākena valam anabhayaṃs taṃ yad anabhayān aśrathayann evainaṃ tat ta u tṛtīyasavane vajreṇa vālakhilyābhir vācaḥ kūṭenaikapadayā valaṃ virujya gā udājan ||
children.translated_text: The gods saw the cows enclosed in <s>Vala</s>. They sought to obtain them by sacrifice, and they obtained them on the sixth day. At the morning pressing they shook <s>Vala</s> with the <s>Nabhāka</s>; when they shook him, they thereby loosened him. Then, at the third pressing, with the thunderbolt, with the <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses, with the summit of speech, and with the one-footed verse, they broke open <s>Vala</s> and drove out the cows.

children.text: tathaivaitad yajamānāḥ prātaḥsavane nabhākena valaṃ nabhayanti taṃ yan nabhayantīṃ śrathayanty evainaṃ tat tasmāddhotrakāḥ prātaḥsavane nābhākāṃs tṛcāñchaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: In just the same way, these sacrificers at the morning pressing shake <s>Vala</s> with the <s>Nabhāka</s>; when they shake him, they thereby loosen him. Therefore the Hotṛ-assistants recite the <s>Nabhāka</s> triplets at the morning pressing.

children.text: yaḥ kakubho nidhāraya iti maitrāvaruṇaḥ pūrvīṣṭa indropamātaya iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsī tā hi madhyam bharāṇām ity achāvākaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> first recites "He who supports the quarters"; the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> recites "The ancient invocations near <s>Indra</s>"; the <s>Acchāvāka</s> recites "For they are in the middle of the bearers."

children.text: ta u tṛtīyasavane vajreṇa vālakhilyābhir vācaḥ kūṭenaikapadayā valaṃ virujya gā āpnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: Then, at the third pressing, with the thunderbolt, with the <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses, with the summit of speech, and with the one-footed verse, they break open <s>Vala</s> and obtain the cows.

children.text: pacchaḥ prathamaṃ ṣaḍ vālakhilyānāṃ sūktāni viharaty ardharcaśo dvitīyam ṛkśas tṛtīyaṃ sa paccho viharan pragāthe pragātha evaikapadāṃ dadhyāt sa vācaḥ kūṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He divides the first six hymns of the <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses foot by foot, the second set by half-verses, and the third by whole verses. While dividing foot by foot, at the <s>pragātha</s>, precisely in the <s>pragātha</s>, he should place the one-footed verse. That is the summit of speech.

children.text: tā etāḥ pañcaikapadāś catasro daśamād ahna ekā mahāvratāt ||
children.translated_text: These are the five one-footed verses: four from the tenth day and one from the <s>Mahāvrata</s>.

children.text: athāṣṭākṣarāṇi māhānāmanāni padāni teṣāṃ yāvadbhiḥ saṃpadyeta tāvanti śaṃsen netarāṇy ādriyeta ||
children.translated_text: Then there are the eight-syllabled <s>Māhānāmana</s> feet. He should recite as many of them as are needed to complete the set, and should pay no attention to the others.

children.text: athārdharcaśo viharaṃs tāś caivaikapadāḥ śaṃset tāni caivāṣṭākṣarāṇi māhānāmanāni padāni ||
children.translated_text: Then, while dividing by half-verses, he should recite both those same one-footed verses and those same eight-syllabled <s>Māhānāmana</s> feet.

children.text: atha ṛkśo viharaṃs tāś caivaikapadāḥ śaṃset tāni caivāṣṭākṣarāṇi māhānāmanāni padāni ||
children.translated_text: Then, while dividing by whole verses, he should recite both those same one-footed verses and those same eight-syllabled <s>Māhānāmana</s> feet.

children.text: sa yat prathamaṃ ṣaḍ vālakhilyānāṃ sūktāni viharati prāṇaṃ ca tad vācaṃ ca viharati yad dvitīyaṃ cakṣuś ca tan manaś ca viharati yat tṛtīyaṃ śrotraṃ ca tad ātmānaṃ ca viharati tad upāpto vihāre kāma upāpto vajre vālakhilyāsūpāpto vācaḥ kūṭa ekapadāyām upāptaḥ prāṇakﾱptyām ||
children.translated_text: When he first divides the six hymns of the <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses, he thereby divides breath and speech; when he divides the second set, he thereby divides sight and mind; when he divides the third, he thereby divides hearing and the self. Thus the desire has been attained in the division; the thunderbolt has been attained in the <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses; the summit of speech has been attained in the one-footed verse; and attainment has been made in the arrangement of breath.

children.text: avihṛtān eva caturtham pragāthāñchaṃsati paśavo vai pragāthāḥ paśūnām avaruddhyai ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>pragātha</s>s a fourth time without dividing them. The <s>pragātha</s>s are cattle; this is for the securing of cattle.

children.text: nātraikapadāṃ vyavadadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not insert a one-footed verse there.

children.text: yad atraikapadāṃ vyavadadhyād vācaḥ kūṭena yajamānāt paśūn nirhaṇyād ya enaṃ tatra brūyād vācaḥ kūṭena yajamānāt paśūn niravadhīr apaśum enam akar iti śaśvat tathā syāt ||
children.translated_text: If he were to insert a one-footed verse there, he would strike away the cattle from the sacrificer with the summit of speech. If someone were to say of him, "With the summit of speech you have struck the cattle away from the sacrificer; you have made him cattleless," it would certainly be so.

children.text: tasmāt tatraikapadāṃ na vyavadadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore he should not insert a one-footed verse there.

children.text: vy evottame sūkte paryasyati sa eva tayor vihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He separates them only in the last hymn; that indeed is the arrangement of the two.

children.text: tad etat saubalāya sarpir vātsiḥ śaśaṃsa sa hovāca bhūyiṣṭhān ahaṃ yajamāne paśūn paryagrahaiṣam akaniṣṭhā u mām āgamiṣyantīti tasmai ha yathā mahadbhya ṛtvigbhya evaṃ nināya tad etat paśavyaṃ ca svargyaṃ ca śastraṃ tasmād etacchaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Sarpir Vātsiḥ</s> proclaimed to <s>Saubalāya</s>. He said, "I have gathered in the greatest number of cattle for the sacrificer; the least ones will come to me." To him he assigned a share just as to the great officiating priests. This recitation is both conducive to cattle and conducive to heaven; therefore he recites it.

children.text: Chapter 212
dūrohaṇaṃ rohati tasyoktam brāhmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: He ascends the <s>dūrohaṇa</s>; its brāhmaṇa explanation has been stated.

children.text: aindre paśukāmasya rohed aindrā vai paśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one desiring cattle he should ascend with an Aindra hymn, for cattle belong to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: taj jāgataṃ syāj jāgatā vai paśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be Jāgata, for cattle are Jāgata.

children.text: tan mahāsūktaṃ syād bhūyiṣṭheṣv eva tat paśuṣu yajamānam pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: It should be a <s>mahāsūkta</s>; thereby he establishes the sacrificer among the greatest number of cattle.

children.text: barau rohet tan mahāsūktaṃ ca jāgataṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: He should ascend with the <s>Barau</s>; that is both a <s>mahāsūkta</s> and Jāgata.

children.text: aindrāvaruṇe pratiṣṭhākāmasya rohed etaddevatā vā eṣā hotraitatpratiṣṭhā yad aindrāvaruṇā tad enat svāyām eva pratiṣṭhāyām antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: For one desiring firm establishment he should ascend with an Aindrāvaruṇa hymn. This Hotṛ-office has those deities, and that which is Aindrāvaruṇa is this establishment; therefore, at the end, he establishes him in his own firm establishment.

children.text: yad evaindrāvaruṇaiṣā ha vā atra nivin nividā vai kāmā āpyante sa yady aindrāvaruṇe rohet sauparṇe rohet tad upāpta aindrāvaruṇe kāma upāptaḥ sauparṇe ||
children.translated_text: As to its being Aindrāvaruṇa: here indeed there is a <s>nivid</s>; by a <s>nivid</s> desires are obtained. If he should ascend with the Aindrāvaruṇa hymn, he should ascend with the Sauparṇa hymn: the desire obtained in the Aindrāvaruṇa is obtained in the Sauparṇa.

children.text: Chapter 213
tad āhuḥ saṃśaṃset ṣaṣṭhe 'hān na samśaṃsait iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "Should he recite them together on the sixth day, or should he not recite them together?"

children.text: saṃśaṃsed ity āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He should recite them together," they say.

children.text: katham anyeṣv ahaḥsu saṃśaṃsati katham atra na saṃśaṃsed iti ||
children.translated_text: "How does he recite them together on the other days, and how should he not recite them together here?"

children.text: atho khalv āhur naiva saṃśaṃset ||
children.translated_text: But others say, "He should certainly not recite them together."

children.text: svargo vai lokaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahar asamāyī vai svargo lokaḥ kaścid vai svarge loke sametīti sa yat saṃśaṃset samānaṃ tat kuryād atha yan na saṃśaṃsatīṁ tat svargasya lokasya rūpaṃ tasmān na saṃśaṃsed yad eva na saṃśaṃsatīṁ ||
children.translated_text: The sixth day is the heavenly world. The heavenly world is not a place of coming together; does anyone come together in the heavenly world? If he were to recite them together, he would make that a coming together. But when he does not recite them together, that is the form of the heavenly world. Therefore he should not recite together what is not to be recited together.

children.text: ātmā vai stotriyaḥ prāṇā vālakhilyāḥ sa yat saṃśaṃsed etābhyāṃ devatābhyāṃ yajamānasya prāṇān vīyād ya enaṃ tatra brūyād etābhyāṃ devatābhyāṃ yajamānasya prāṇān vyagāt prāṇa enaṃ hāsyatīti śaśvat tathā syāt tasmān na saṃśaṃset ||
children.translated_text: The stotriya is the self; the Vālakhilyā verses are the breaths. If he were to recite them together, he would separate the sacrificer's breaths by means of these two deities. If someone there were to say of him, "By these two deities he has made the sacrificer's breaths depart; breath will abandon him," it would surely be so. Therefore he should not recite them together.

children.text: sa yad īkṣetāśaṃsiṣaṃ vālakhilyā hanta purastād dūrohaṇasya saṃśaṃsānīti no eva tasyāśām iyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he should think, "I have recited the Vālakhilyā verses; come, I will recite them together before the <s>dūrohaṇa</s>," he should not go after that wish.

children.text: taṃ yadi darpa eva vinded upariṣṭād dūrohaṇasyāpi bahūni śatāni śaṃsed yasyo tat kāmāya tathā kuryād atraiva tad upāptam ||
children.translated_text: But if pride should take hold of him, he may recite even many hundreds after the <s>dūrohaṇa</s>, for whatever desire he would act in that way; that desire is obtained right here.

children.text: aindryo vālakhilyās tāsāṃ dvādaśākṣarāṇi padāni tatra sa kāma upāpto ya aindre jāgate 'thedam aindrāvaruṇaṃ sūktam aindrāvaruṇī paridhānīyā tasmān na saṃśaṃset ||
children.translated_text: The Vālakhilyā verses belong to <s>Indra</s>; their padas have twelve syllables. There the desire is obtained which belongs to the Aindra Jāgata. And this is an Aindrāvaruṇa hymn, with an Aindrāvaruṇī concluding verse; therefore he should not recite them together.

children.text: tad āhur yathā vāva stotram evaṃ śastraṃ vihṛtā vālakhilyāḥ śasyante vihṛtāṃ stotrām avihṛtām iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "As the stotra is, so is the śastra. The Vālakhilyā verses are recited divided; is the stotra divided or undivided?"

children.text: vihṛtam iti brūyād aṣṭākṣareṇa dvādaśākṣaram iti ||
children.translated_text: One should say, "It is divided: the twelve-syllabled one by means of the eight-syllabled one."

children.text: tad āhur yathā vāva śastram evaṃ yājyā tisro devatāḥ śasyante 'gnirindro varuṇa ity athaindrāvaruṇyā yajati katham agnir anantarita iti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "As the śastra is, so is the yājyā. Three deities are recited: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>. But then he sacrifices with an Aindrāvaruṇī verse. How is <s>Agni</s> not interrupted?"

children.text: yo vā agniḥ sa varuṇas tad apy etad ṛṣiṇoktaṃ tvam agne varuṇo jāyase yad iti tad yad evaindrāvaruṇyā yajati tenāgnir anantarito 'nantaritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is <s>Agni</s> is <s>Varuṇa</s>. This too has been spoken by a seer: "You, <s>Agni</s>, are born as <s>Varuṇa</s>." Therefore, when he sacrifices with the Aindrāvaruṇī verse, <s>Agni</s> is thereby uninterrupted, uninterrupted.

children.text: Chapter 214
śilpāni śaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: They recite the <s>śilpas</s>.

children.text: devaśilpāny eteṣām vai śilpānām anukṛtīha śilpam adhigamyate hastī kaṃso vāso hiraṇyam aśvatarīrathaḥ śilpam ||
children.translated_text: These are divine crafts. Through imitation of these crafts, craft is obtained here: an elephant, a bronze vessel, a garment, gold, and a mule-drawn chariot are craft.

children.text: śilpaṃ hāsminn adhigamyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Craft is indeed obtained by the one who knows this thus.

children.text: yad eva śilpānīn ||
children.translated_text: That indeed is why they are the <s>śilpas</s>.

children.text: ātmasaṃskṛtir vāva śilpāni chandomayaṃ vā etair yajamāna ātmānaṃ saṃskurute ||
children.translated_text: The <s>śilpas</s> are truly a cultivation of the self. By these, made of metres, the sacrificer cultivates his own self.

children.text: nābhānediṣṭhaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the Nābhānediṣṭha.

children.text: reto vai nābhānediṣṭho retas tat siñcati ||
children.translated_text: The Nābhānediṣṭha is semen; thereby he pours semen.

children.text: tam aniruktaṃ śaṃsaty aniruktaṃ vai reto guhā yonyāṃ sicyate ||
children.translated_text: He recites it indistinctly; semen is poured indistinctly, in secret, into the womb.

children.text: sa retomiśro bhavati kṣmayā retaḥ saṃjagmāno niṣiñcad iti retaḥsamṛddhyā eva ||
children.translated_text: It becomes mixed with semen, for he says, "pouring the semen, coming together with the earth"; this is precisely for the prosperity of semen.

children.text: taṃ sanārāśaṃsaṃ śaṃsati prajā vai naro vāk śaṃsaḥ prajāsv eva tad vācaṃ dadhāti tasmād imāḥ prajā vadantyo jāyante ||
children.translated_text: He recites it together with the Nārāśaṃsa. Offspring are men, and speech is praise; thereby he places speech among offspring. Therefore these offspring are born speaking.

children.text: taṃ haike purastāc chaṃsanti purastādāyatanā vāg iti vadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some recite it beforehand, saying, "Speech has its seat in front."

children.text: upariṣṭād eka upariṣṭādāyatanā vāg iti vadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some recite it afterward, saying, "Speech has its seat afterward."

children.text: madhya eva śaṃsen madhyāyatanā vā iyaṃ vāk ||
children.translated_text: He should recite it in the middle, for this speech has its seat in the middle.

children.text: upariṣṭānnedīyasīvopariṣṭān nedīyasīva vā iyaṃ vāk ||
children.translated_text: It is, as it were, nearer to what comes afterward; for this speech is, as it were, nearer to what comes afterward.

children.text: taṃ hotā retobhūtaṃ siktvā maitrāvaruṇāya samprayacchaty etasya tvam prāṇān kalpayeti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Hotṛ</s>, having poured it as semen, hands it over to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, saying, "Set his breaths in order."

children.text: Chapter 215
vālakhilyāḥ śaṃsati prāṇā vai vālakhilyāḥ prāṇān evāsya tat kalpayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the Vālakhilyā verses. The Vālakhilyā verses are the breaths; thereby he sets his breaths in order.

children.text: tā vihṛtāḥ śaṃsati vihṛtā vā ime prāṇāḥ prāṇenāpāno 'pānena vyānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites them divided. These breaths are divided: the out-breath by the in-breath, and the diffused breath by the out-breath.

children.text: sa pacchaḥ prathame sūkte viharaty ardharcaśo dvitīye ṛkśas tṛtīye ||
children.translated_text: In the first hymn he divides them by padas, in the second by half-verses, and in the third by individual ṛcs.

children.text: sa yat prathame sūkte viharati prāṇaṃ ca tad vācaṃ ca viharati yad dvitīye cakṣuśca tan manaś ca viharati yat tṛtīye śrotraṃ ca tad ātmānaṃ ca viharati ||
children.translated_text: When he separates them in the first hymn, he thereby separates breath and speech; when in the second, he separates sight and mind; when in the third, he separates hearing and the self.

children.text: te haike saha bṛhatyau saha satobṛhatyau viharanti tad upāpto vihāre kāmo net tu pragāthāḥ kalpante ||
children.translated_text: Some perform the Bṛhatī verses together and the Satobṛhatī verses together. In that case the desired alternation is attained, but the <s>pragāthas</s> do not fit.

children.text: atimarśam eva viharet tathā vai pragāthāḥ kalpante pragāthā vai vālakhilyās tasmād atimarśam eva vihared yad evātimarśām ||
children.translated_text: One should perform the alternation only by <s>atimarśa</s> (overlapping contact). In that way the <s>pragāthas</s> do fit. The <s>Vālakhilyas</s> are <s>pragāthas</s>; therefore one should perform the alternation only by <s>atimarśa</s>, precisely as <s>atimarśa</s>.

children.text: ātmā vai bṛhatī prāṇāḥ satobṛhatī sa bṛhatīm aśaṃsīt sa ātmātha satobṛhatīṃ te prāṇā atha bṛhatīm atha satobṛhatīṃ tad ātmānam prāṇaiḥ paribṛhann eti tasmād atimarśam eva viharet ||
children.translated_text: The Bṛhatī is the self, and the Satobṛhatī is the breaths. He recited a Bṛhatī: that was the self. Then a Satobṛhatī: those were the breaths. Then a Bṛhatī, then a Satobṛhatī. Thus he goes along enclosing the self with the breaths. Therefore one should perform the alternation only by <s>atimarśa</s>.

children.text: yad v evātimarśām ātmā vai bṛhatī paśavaḥ satobṛhatī sa bṛhatīm aśaṃsīt sa ātmātha satobṛhatīṃ te paśavo 'tha bṛhatīm atha satobṛhatīṃ tad ātmānam paśubhiḥ paribṛhann eti tasmād atimarśam eva viharet ||
children.translated_text: Or rather, because it is <s>atimarśa</s>: the Bṛhatī is the self, and the Satobṛhatī is the animals. He recited a Bṛhatī: that was the self. Then a Satobṛhatī: those were the animals. Then a Bṛhatī, then a Satobṛhatī. Thus he goes along enclosing the self with animals. Therefore one should perform the alternation only by <s>atimarśa</s>.

children.text: vy evottame sūkte paryasyati sa eva tayor vihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the final hymn he does separate them apart; that is the alternation of the two.

children.text: tasya maitrāvaruṇaḥ prāṇān kalpayitvā brāhmaṇācchaṃsine samprayacchaty etaṃ tvam prajanayeti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, after arranging the breaths for him, hands him over to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, saying, "Do you generate this one."

children.text: Chapter 216
sukīrtiṃ śaṃsati devayonir vai sukīrtis tad yajñād devayonyai yajamānam prajanayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Sukīrti</s>. The <s>Sukīrti</s> is a divine womb; thereby, from the sacrifice, he generates the sacrificer from a divine womb.

children.text: vṛṣākapiṃ śaṃsaty ātmā vai vṛṣākapir ātmānam evāsya tat kalpayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>. The <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> is the self; thereby he arranges the self for him.

children.text: taṃ nyūṅkhayaty annaṃ vai nyūṅkhas tad asmai jātāyānnādyam pratidadhāti yathā kumārāya stanam ||
children.translated_text: He makes it a <s>nyūṅkha</s> chant. Food is the <s>nyūṅkha</s>; thereby he gives food and eating to him when he has been born, as one gives the breast to a child.

children.text: sa pāṅkto bhavati pāṅkto 'yam puruṣaḥ pañcadhā vihito lomāni tvaṅ māṃsam asthi majjā sa yāvān eva puruṣas tāvantaṃ yajamānaṃ saṃskaroti ||
children.translated_text: It is Pāṅkta. This person is Pāṅkta, arranged fivefold: hairs, skin, flesh, bone, and marrow. As great as a person is, so great a sacrificer he thereby prepares.

children.text: tam brāhmaṇācchaṃsī janayitvāchāvākāya samprayacchaty etasya tvam pratiṣṭhāṃ kalpayeti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>, after generating him, hands him over to the <s>Acchāvāka</s>, saying, "Do you arrange a foundation for this one."

children.text: Chapter 217
evayāmarutaṃ śaṃsati pratiṣṭhā vā evayāmarut pratiṣṭhām evāsya tat kalpayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Evayāmaruta</s>. The <s>Evayāmaruta</s> is a foundation; thereby he arranges a foundation for him.

children.text: taṃ nyūṅkhayaty annaṃ vai nyūṅkho 'nnādyam evāsmiṃs tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He makes it a <s>nyūṅkha</s> chant. Food is the <s>nyūṅkha</s>; thereby he places food and eating in him.

children.text: sa jāgato vātijāgato vā sarvaṃ vā idaṃ jāgataṃ vātijāgataṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: It is Jāgata or Vātijāgata, for all this is Jāgata or Vātijāgata.

children.text: sa u māruta āpo vai maruta āpo 'nnam abhipūrvam evāsmiṃs tad annādyaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: And it is Māruta. The <s>Maruts</s> are waters, and the waters are food; thereby, in due order, he places food and eating in him.

children.text: tāny etāni sahacarāṇīty ācakṣate nābhānediṣṭhaṃ vālakhilyā vṛṣākapim evayāmarutaṃ tāni saha vā śaṃset saha vā na śaṃset ||
children.translated_text: These are called the companions: the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>, the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, and the <s>Evayāmaruta</s>. One may recite them together, or one may not recite them together.

children.text: yad enāni nānā śaṃsed yathā puruṣaṃ vā reto vā vicchindyāt tādṛk tat tasmād enāni saha vā śaṃset saha vā na śaṃset ||
children.translated_text: If he were to recite them separately, that would be like cutting apart a person or seed. Therefore one should either recite them together or not recite them together.

children.text: sa ha bulila āśvatara āśvir vaiśvajito hotā sann īkṣāṃcakra eṣāṃ vā eṣāṃ śilpānāṃ viśvajiti sāṃvatsarike dve madhyaṃdinam abhi pratyetor hantāham ittham evayāmarutaṃ śaṃsayānīti taddha tathā śaṃsayāṃcakāra ||
children.translated_text: Now <s>Bulila Āśvatara</s>, the Āśvi, while serving as <s>Hotṛ</s> at the year-long <s>Viśvajit</s>, considered the midday pressing in relation to these śilpas: "Come, I will have the <s>Evayāmaruta</s> recited in just this way." And he did have it recited in that way.

children.text: taddha tathā śasyamāne gauśla ājagāma sa hovāca hotaḥ kathā te śastraṃ vicakram plavata iti ||
children.translated_text: While it was being recited in that way, <s>Gauśla</s> came up. He said, "<s>Hotṛ</s>, how is your recitation leaping apart and floating away?"

children.text: kiṃ hy abhūd iti ||
children.translated_text: "What has happened?" he asked.

children.text: evayāmarud ayam uttarataḥ śasyata iti sa hovācaindro vai madhyaṃdinaḥ kathendram madhyaṃdinān ninīṣasīti ||
children.translated_text: "This <s>Evayāmaruta</s> is being recited afterward," he said. He said, "The midday pressing belongs to <s>Indra</s>; how do you wish to lead <s>Indra</s> away from the midday pressing?"

children.text: nendram madhyaṃdinān ninīṣāmīti hovāca ||
children.translated_text: "I do not wish to lead <s>Indra</s> away from the midday pressing," he said.

children.text: chandas tv idam amadhyaṃdinasācy ayaṃ jāgato vātijāgato vā sarvaṃ vā idaṃ jāgataṃ vātijāgataṃ vā sa u māruto maiva śaṃsiṣṭeti ||
children.translated_text: "But this meter is not connected with the midday pressing. This is Jāgata or Vātijāgata, for all this is Jāgata or Vātijāgata, and it is Māruta. Do not have it recited."

children.text: sa hovācāramāchāvākety atha hāsminn anuśāsanam īṣe ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Enough, <s>Acchāvāka</s>." Then he sought instruction about this.

children.text: sa hovācaindram eṣa viṣṇunyaṅgaṃ śaṃsatv atha tvam etaṃ hotar upariṣṭād raudryai dhāyyāyai purastān mārutasyāpy asyāthā iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, "Let him recite this <s>Indra-Viṣṇu</s> verse-section. Then you, <s>Hotṛ</s>, should insert this one above, before the Raudrī Dhāyyā and also before the Māruta."

children.text: taddha tathā śaṃsayāṃcakāra tad idam apy etarhi tathaiva śasyate ||
children.translated_text: He had it recited in that way, and this is recited in just that way even now.

children.text: Chapter 218

tad āhur yad asmin viśvajity atirātra evaṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani kalpate yajñaḥ kalpate yajamānasya prajātiḥ katham atrāśasta eva nābhānediṣṭho bhavaty atha maitrāvaruṇo vālakhilyāḥ śaṃsati te prāṇā reto vā agre 'tha prāṇā evam brāhmaṇācchaṃsy aśasta eva nābhānediṣṭho bhavaty atha vṛṣākapiṃ śaṃsati sa ātmā reto vā agre 'thātmā katham atra yajamānasya prajātiḥ katham prāṇā avikﾱptā bhavantīti ||
children.translated_text: They say: "Since in this <s>Viśvajit Atirātra</s> the sacrifice is arranged in this way on the sixth day, and the sacrificer's generation is arranged, how here does the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> remain unrecited, while the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> recites the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>? Those are the breaths. Seed comes first, then the breaths. In the same way, how does the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> leave the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s> unrecited, while he recites the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>? That is the self. Seed comes first, then the self. How, then, is the sacrificer's generation here? How do the breaths not remain improperly arranged?"

children.text: yajamānaṃ ha vā etena sarveṇa yajñakratunā saṃskurvanti sa yathā garbho yonyām antar evaṃ sambhavañchete na vai sakṛd evāgre sarvaḥ sambhavaty ekaikaṃ vā aṅgaṃ sambhavataḥ sambhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: By this whole sacrificial rite they prepare the sacrificer. Just as an embryo, coming into being, lies within the womb, so he lies there. Not indeed all at once, at the beginning, does he come into being complete; rather, as he is coming into being, one limb after another comes into being.

children.text: sarvāṇi cet samāne 'han kriyeran kalpata eva yajñaḥ kalpate yajamānasya prajātir athaitaṃ hotaivayāmarutaṃ tṛtīyasavane śaṃsati tad yāsya pratiṣṭhā tasyām evainaṃ tad antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: If all of them were performed on the same day, the sacrifice would indeed be properly arranged, and the sacrificer's procreation would be properly arranged. Now the <s>Hotṛ</s> recites this <s>Aivayāmaruta</s> at the third pressing. Whatever is its foundation, upon that very foundation he finally establishes him.

children.text: Chapter 219

chandasāṃ vai ṣaṣṭhenāhnāptānāṃ raso 'tyanedat sa prajāpatir abibhet parāṅ ayaṃ chandasāṃ raso lokān atyeṣyatīti tam parastāc chandobhiḥ paryagṛhṇān nārāśaṃsyā gāyatryā raibhyā triṣṭubhaḥ pārikṣityā jagatyāḥ kāravyayānuṣṭubhas tat punaś chandassu rasam adadhāt ||
children.translated_text: When the metres had been obtained by the sixth day, their sap flowed beyond. <s>Prajāpati</s> feared, thinking, "This sap of the metres will turn away and go beyond the worlds." He enclosed it from behind with metres: the <s>Nārāśaṃsī</s> with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the <s>Raibhī</s> from the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the <s>Pārikṣitī</s> from the <s>Jagatī</s>, and the <s>Kāravyā</s> from the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. That put the sap back among the metres.

children.text: sarasair hāsya chandobhir iṣṭam bhavati sarasaiś chandobhir yajñaṃ tanute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For him, the offering is made with sap-filled metres; with sap-filled metres he stretches out the sacrifice, who knows thus.

children.text: nārāśaṃsīḥ śaṃsati prajā vai naro vāk śaṃsaḥ prajāsv eva tad vācaṃ dadhāti tasmād imāḥ prajā vadantyo jāyante ya evaṃ veda yad eva nārāśaṃsīḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Nārāśaṃsī</s> verses. Men are progeny, and utterance is speech; thereby he places speech among progeny. Therefore these creatures are born speaking, who knows thus. That is the reason for the <s>Nārāśaṃsī</s> verses.

children.text: śaṃsanto vai devāś ca ṛṣayaś ca svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānāḥ śaṃsanta eva svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti ||
children.translated_text: By reciting praise, the gods and the seers went to the heavenly world. In just the same way these sacrificers, precisely by reciting praise, go to the heavenly world.

children.text: tāḥ pragrāhaṃ śaṃsati yathā vṛṣākapiṃ vārṣākapaṃ hi vṛṣākapes tan nyāyam eti ||
children.translated_text: He recites them with a <s>pragrāha</s>, as in the case of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>; for what belongs to <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> is <s>Vārṣākapa</s>. That follows the proper rule.

children.text: tāsu na nyūṅkhayen nīvaiva nardet sa hi tāsāṃ nyūṅkhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In them he should not make the <s>nyūṅkha</s>; he should simply roar downward, for that is their <s>nyūṅkha</s>.

children.text: raibhīḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Raibhī</s> verses.

children.text: rebhanto vai devāś ca ṛṣayaś ca svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānā rebhanta eva svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti ||
children.translated_text: By roaring, the gods and the seers went to the heavenly world. In just the same way these sacrificers, precisely by roaring, go to the heavenly world.

children.text: tāḥ pragrāhaṃ śaṃsati yathā vṛṣākapiṃ vārṣākapaṃ hi vṛṣākapes tan nyāyam eti tāsu na nyūṅkhayen nīvaiva nardet sa hi tāsāṃ nyūṅkhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites them with a <s>pragrāha</s>, as in the case of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>; for what belongs to <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> is <s>Vārṣākapa</s>. That follows the proper rule. In them he should not make the <s>nyūṅkha</s>; he should simply roar downward, for that is their <s>nyūṅkha</s>.

children.text: pārikṣitīḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Pārikṣitī</s> verses.

children.text: agnir vai parikṣid agnir hīmāḥ prajāḥ parikṣety agniṃ hīmāḥ prajāḥ parikṣiyanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is indeed <s>Parikṣit</s>, for <s>Agni</s> surrounds these creatures, and these creatures settle around <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: agner eva sāyujyaṃ sarūpatāṃ salokatām aśnute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He obtains union with <s>Agni</s>, sameness of form with him, and dwelling in his world, who knows thus.

children.text: yad eva pārikṣitīḥ ||
children.translated_text: That, then, is the reason for the <s>Pārikṣitī</s> verses.

children.text: saṃvatsaro vai parikṣit saṃvatsaro hīmāḥ prajāḥ parikṣeti saṃvatsaraṃ hīmāḥ prajāḥ parikṣiyanti ||
children.translated_text: The year is indeed <s>Parikṣit</s>, for the year surrounds these creatures, and these creatures settle around the year.

children.text: saṃvatsarasyaiva sāyujyaṃ sarūpatāṃ salokatām aśnute ya evaṃ veda tāḥ pragrāhaṃ śaṃsati yathā vṛṣākapiṃ vārṣākapaṃ hi vṛṣākapes tan nyāyam eti tāsu na nyūṅkhayen nīvaiva nardet sa hi tāsāṃ nyūṅkhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He obtains union with the year, sameness of form with it, and dwelling in its world, who knows thus. He recites them with a <s>pragrāha</s>, as in the case of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>; for what belongs to <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> is <s>Vārṣākapa</s>. That follows the proper rule. In them he should not make the <s>nyūṅkha</s>; he should simply roar downward, for that is their <s>nyūṅkha</s>.

children.text: kāravyāḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Kāravyā</s> verses.

children.text: devā vai yat kiṃca kalyāṇaṃ karmākurvaṃs tat kāravyābhir āpnuvaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānā yat kiṃca kalyāṇaṃ karma kurvanti tat kāravyābhir āpnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever auspicious work the gods performed, they attained it through the <s>Kāravyā</s> verses. In just the same way, whatever auspicious work these sacrificers perform, they attain it through the <s>Kāravyā</s> verses.

children.text: tāḥ pragrāhaṃ śaṃsati yathā vṛṣākapiṃ vārṣākapaṃ hi vṛṣākapes tan nyāyam eti tāsu na nyūṅkhayet nīvīva nardet sa hi tāsāṃ nyūṅkhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites them with a <s>pragrāha</s>, as in the case of <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>; for what belongs to <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> is <s>Vārṣākapa</s>. That follows the proper rule. In them he should not make the <s>nyūṅkha</s>; he should roar as if downward, for that is their <s>nyūṅkha</s>.

children.text: diśāṃ kﾱptīḥ śaṃsati diśa eva tat kalpayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the verses on the arrangement of the directions; thereby he arranges the directions themselves.

children.text: tāḥ pañca śaṃsati pañca vā imā diśaś catasras tiraścya ekordhvā ||
children.translated_text: He recites five of them, for these directions are five: four crosswise and one upward.

children.text: tāsu na nyūṅkhayen nevaiva ca ninarden ned imā diśo nyūṅkhayānīti ||
children.translated_text: In them he should not make the <s>nyūṅkha</s>, nor should he make a roar, lest he make these directions into a <s>nyūṅkha</s>.

children.text: tā ardharcaśaḥ śaṃsati pratiṣṭhāyā eva ||
children.translated_text: He recites them half-verse by half-verse, for the sake of a foundation.

children.text: janakalpāḥ śaṃsati prajā vai janakalpā diśa eva tat kalpayitvā tāsu prajāḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Janakalpa</s> verses. The <s>Janakalpa</s> verses are progeny; having thereby arranged the directions, he establishes progeny in them.

children.text: tāsu na nyūṅkhayen nevaiva ca ninarden ned imāḥ prajā nyūṅkhayānīti tā ardharcaśaḥ śaṃsati pratiṣṭhāyā eva ||
children.translated_text: In them he should not make the <s>nyūṅkha</s>, nor should he make a roar, lest he make these creatures into a <s>nyūṅkha</s>. He recites them half-verse by half-verse, for the sake of a foundation.

children.text: indragāthāḥ śaṃsatīndragāthābhir vai devā asurān abhigāyāthainān atyāyaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānā indragāthābhir evāpriyam bhrātṛvyam abhigāyāthainam atiyanti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Indragāthā</s> verses. With the <s>Indragāthā</s> verses the gods, having sung against the Asuras, then passed beyond them. In just the same way these sacrificers, with the <s>Indragāthā</s> verses, having sung against an unwelcome rival, pass beyond him.

children.text: tā ardharcaśaḥ śaṃsati pratiṣṭhāyā eva ||
children.translated_text: He recites them half-verse by half-verse, for the sake of a foundation.

children.text: Chapter 220
aitaśapralāpaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Aitaśapralāpa</s>.

children.text: aitaśo ha vai munir agner āyur dadarśa yajñasyāyātayāmam iti haika āhuḥ so 'bravīt putrān putrakā agner āyur adarśaṃ tad abhilapiṣyāmi yat kiṃca vadāmi tan me mā parigāteti sa pratyapadyataitā aśvā āplavante pratīpam prātisatvanam iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aitaśa</s> the seer once saw the life-span of <s>Agni</s>; some say it was the unexhausted vitality of the sacrifice. He said to his sons, "Sons, dear sons, I have seen the life-span of <s>Agni</s>. I am going to utter it. Whatever I say, do not interrupt me." He began, "These horses plunge forth, upstream, against the current."

children.text: tasyābhyagnir aitaśāyana etyākāle 'bhihāya mukham apyagṛhṇād adṛpan naḥ piteti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Abhyagni Aitaśāyana</s>, coming at the wrong time, cried out over him and seized his mouth, saying, "Our father has become delirious."

children.text: taṃ hovācāpehy alaso 'bhūr yo me vācam avadhīḥ śatāyuṃ gām akariṣyaṃ sahasrāyum puruṣam pāpiṣṭhāṃ te prajāṃ karomi yo mettham asakthā iti ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, "Go away. You have become useless, you who cut off my speech. I would have made a cow live a hundred years and a man live a thousand years. I make your offspring most wicked, because you have thwarted me in this way."

children.text: tasmād āhur abhyagnaya aitaśāyanā aurvāṇām pāpiṣṭhā iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they say that the <s>Abhyagni Aitaśāyana</s>s are the most wicked among the <s>Aurva</s>s.

children.text: taṃ haike bhūyāṃsaṃ śaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: Some recite it in a fuller form.

children.text: sa na niṣedhed yāvatkāmaṃ śaṃsety eva brūyād āyur vā aitaśapralāpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should not forbid him. He should simply say, "Recite as much as you wish," for the <s>Aitaśapralāpa</s> is life-span.

children.text: āyur eva tad yajamānasya pratārayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: Thereby he extends the sacrificer's life-span, who knows thus.

children.text: yad evaitaśapralāpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: That, then, is the reason for the <s>Aitaśapralāpa</s> verses.

children.text: chandasāṃ haiṣa raso yad aitaśapralāpaś chandassv eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is the sap of the metres, namely the <s>Aitaśapralāpa</s>; thereby he places sap among the metres themselves.

children.text: sarasair hāsya chandobhir iṣṭam bhavati sarasaiś chandobhir yajñaṃ tanute ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: For him, the offering is made with sap-filled metres; with sap-filled metres he stretches out the sacrifice, who knows thus.

children.text: yad v evaitaśapralāpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, as for these <s>Aitaśapralāpas</s>:

children.text: ayātayāmā vā akṣitir aitaśapralāpo 'yātayāmā me yajñe 'sad akṣitir me yajñe 'saditi ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Aitaśapralāpa</s> is indeed unwearied and inexhaustible: "May it be unwearied in my sacrifice; may there be inexhaustibility in my sacrifice."

children.text: taṃ vā etam aitaśapralāpaṃ śaṃsati padāvagrāhaṃ yathā nividam ||
children.translated_text: He recites this <s>Aitaśapralāpa</s> with separation of words, like a <s>nivid</s>.

children.text: tasyottamena padena praṇauti yathā nividaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With its final word he gives praise, as with the <s>nivids</s>.

children.text: pravalhikāḥ śaṃsati pravalhikābhir vai devā asurān pravalhyāthainān atyāyaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānāḥ pravalhikābhir evāpriyam bhrātṛvyam pravalhyāthainam atiyanti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Pravalhikās</s>. With the <s>Pravalhikās</s> the gods crushed the <s>Asuras</s> and then passed beyond them. In just the same way these sacrificers, with the <s>Pravalhikās</s>, crush the hostile rival who is displeasing and then pass beyond him.

children.text: tā ardharcaśaḥ śaṃsati pratiṣṭhāyā eva ||
children.translated_text: He recites them by half-verses, for the sake of firm foundation.

children.text: ājijñāsenyāḥ śaṃsaty ājijñāsenyābhir vai devā asurān ājñāyāthainān atyāyaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānā ājijñāsenyābhir evāpriyam bhrātṛvyam ājñāyāthainam atiyanti tā ardharcaśaḥ śaṃsati pratiṣṭhāyā eva ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Ājijñāsenyās</s>. With the <s>Ājijñāsenyās</s> the gods discerned the <s>Asuras</s> and then passed beyond them. In just the same way these sacrificers, with the <s>Ājijñāsenyās</s>, discern the hostile rival who is displeasing and then pass beyond him. He recites them by half-verses, for the sake of firm foundation.

children.text: pratirādhaṃ śaṃsati pratirādhena vai devā asurān pratirādhyāthainān atyāyaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānāḥ pratirādhenaivāpriyam bhrātṛvyam pratirādhyāthainam atiyanti ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Pratirādha</s>. With the <s>Pratirādha</s> the gods overcame the <s>Asuras</s> and then passed beyond them. In just the same way these sacrificers, with the <s>Pratirādha</s>, overcome the hostile rival who is displeasing and then pass beyond him.

children.text: ativādaṃ śaṃsaty ativādena vai devā asurān atyudyāthainān atyāyaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānā ativādenaivāpriyam bhrātṛvyam atyudyāthainam atiyanti tam ardharcaśaḥ śaṃsati pratiṣṭhāyā eva ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Ativāda</s>. With the <s>Ativāda</s> the gods spoke beyond the <s>Asuras</s> and then passed beyond them. In just the same way these sacrificers, with the <s>Ativāda</s>, speak beyond the hostile rival who is displeasing and then pass beyond him. He recites it by half-verses, for the sake of firm foundation.

children.text: Chapter 221
deyanīthaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Deyanītha</s>.

children.text: ādityāś ca ha vā aṅgirasaś ca svarge loke 'spardhanta vayam pūrva eṣyāmo vayam iti te hāṅgirasaḥ pūrve śvaḥsutyāṃ svargasya lokasya dadṛśus te 'gnim prajighyur aṅgirasāṃ vā eko 'gniḥ parehy ādityebhyaḥ śvaḥsutyāṃ svargasya lokasya prabrūhīti te hādityā agnim eva dṛṣṭvā sadyaḥsutyāṃ svargasya lokasya dadṛśus tān etyābravīc chvaḥsutyāṃ vaḥ svargasya lokasya prabrūma iti te hocur atha vayaṃ tubhyaṃ sadyaḥsutyāṃ svargasya lokasya prabrūmas tvayaiva vayaṃ hotrā svargaṃ lokam eṣyāma iti sa tathety uktvā pratyuktaḥ punar ājagāma ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s> and the <s>Aṅgirases</s> were competing in the heavenly world, saying, "We shall go first, we shall." The <s>Aṅgirases</s> first saw the heavenly world by means of a pressing on the following day. They sent <s>Agni</s>: "<s>Agni</s> is one of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>; go, announce to the <s>Ādityas</s> a pressing on the following day for the heavenly world." When the <s>Ādityas</s> saw <s>Agni</s>, they at once saw the heavenly world by means of a pressing on the same day. He came to them and said, "We announce to you a pressing on the following day for the heavenly world." They said, "Then we announce to you a pressing on the same day for the heavenly world. With you yourself as <s>Hotṛ</s> we shall go to the heavenly world." Saying "So be it," and having been answered in return, he came back again.

children.text: te hocuḥ prāvocāḥ iti prāvocam iti hovācātho me pratiprāvocann iti no hi na pratyajñāsthāḥ iti prati vā ajñāsam iti hovāca ||
children.translated_text: They said, "Did you announce it?" "I announced it," he said, "and then they announced it back to me." "Surely you did not acknowledge it in return?" they said. "I did acknowledge it in return," he said.

children.text: yaśasā vā eṣo 'bhyaiti ya ārtvijyena taṃ yaḥ pratirundhed yaśaḥ sa pratirundhet tasmān na pratyarautsīti ||
children.translated_text: One who approaches by priestly service approaches with glory. Whoever should obstruct him would obstruct glory. Therefore you did not obstruct it in return.

children.text: yadi tv asmād apojjigāṃsed yajñenāsmād apodiyāt yadi yadi tv ayājyaḥ svayam apoditaṃ tasmāt ||
children.translated_text: But if one should wish to drive him away from this, one should drive him away from this by a sacrifice. But if he is himself one unfit for sacrifice, he is thereby driven away of himself.

children.text: Chapter 222

te hādityān aṅgiraso 'yājayaṃs tebhyo yājayadbhya imām pṛthivīm pūrṇāṃ dakṣiṇānām adadus tān iyam pratigṛhītātapat tāṃ nyavṛñjan sā siṃhī bhūtvā vijṛmbhantī janān acarat tasyāḥ śocatyā ime pradarāḥ prādīryanta ye 'syā ime pradarāḥ sameva haiva tataḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Aṅgirases</s> performed sacrifice for the <s>Ādityas</s>. To them, as they were performing sacrifice, the <s>Ādityas</s> gave this earth filled with sacrificial fees. This earth, once accepted, burned them. They turned her back. Becoming a lioness, stretching herself out, she moved among people. As she burned, these fissures of hers split open; before that, these fissures of hers were wholly joined together.

children.text: tasmād āhur na nivṛttadakṣiṇām pratigṛhṇīyān nenmā śucā viddhā śucā vidhyād iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they say, "One should not accept a returned <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, lest she, pierced by heat and grief, pierce me with heat and grief."

children.text: yadi tv enām pratigṛhṇīyād apriyāyainām bhrātṛvyāya dadyāt parā haiva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But if one were to accept her, one should give her to a hostile rival who is displeasing; he becomes utterly overcome.

children.text: atha yo 'sau tapatīṁ eṣo 'śvaḥ śveto rūpaṃ kṛtvāśvābhidhānyapihitenātmanā praticakrama imaṃ vo nayāma iti sa eṣa devanītho 'nūcyate ||
children.translated_text: Then that one who burns yonder, this white horse, having made a form for himself and with his body covered by horse-trappings, went back, saying, "We are leading this to you." This is recited as the <s>Devanītha</s>.

children.text: ādityā ha jaritar aṅgirobhyo dakṣiṇām anayan ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s>, O singer, led the sacrificial fee to the <s>Aṅgirases</s>.

children.text: tāṃ ha jaritar na pratyāyann iti na hi ta imām pratyāyan ||
children.translated_text: They did not come back to that, O singer; for they did not come back to this one.

children.text: tām u ha jaritaḥ pratyāyann iti prati hi te 'mum āyan ||
children.translated_text: They did come back to that, O singers; for they came back to that one.

children.text: tāṃ ha jaritar na pratyagṛbhṇann iti na hi ta imām pratyagṛbhṇan ||
children.translated_text: They did not take that back, O singer; for they did not take this one back.

children.text: tām u ha jaritaḥ pratyagṛbhṇann iti prati hi te 'mum agṛbhṇan ||
children.translated_text: They did take that back, O singers; for they took that one back.

children.text: ahā ned asann avicetanānīty eṣa ha vā ahnāṃ vicetayitā ||
children.translated_text: "Lest the days become without discernment"; for this one is indeed the discerner of the days.

children.text: yajñā ned asann apurogavāsa iti dakṣiṇā vai yajñānām purogavī yathā ha vā idam ano 'purogavaṃ riṣyaty evaṃ haiva yajño 'dakṣiṇo riṣyati tasmād āhur dātavyaiva yajñe dakṣiṇā bhavaty apy alpikāpi ||
children.translated_text: "Lest the sacrifices become without a leader"; for the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is the leader of sacrifices. Just as a wagon without a leader is wrecked, so a sacrifice without <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is wrecked. Therefore they say, "A <s>dakṣiṇā</s> must indeed be given in the sacrifice, even if it is only a small one."

children.text: uta śveta āśupatvā ||
children.translated_text: And the white one, by his swiftness,

children.text: uto padyābhir javiṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the swiftest with his feet,

children.text: utem āśu mānam piparti ||
children.translated_text: and this swift one fills out the measure.

children.text: ādityā rudrā vasavas tveﾱate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and the <s>Vasus</s> are impelled toward you.

children.text: idaṃ rādhaḥ pratigṛbhṇīhy aṅgira iti pratigraham eva tad rādhasa aicchan ||
children.translated_text: "Receive this gift, O <s>Aṅgiras</s>"; by that they sought the acceptance of the gift.

children.text: idaṃ rādho bṛhat pṛthu ||
children.translated_text: This gift is great and broad.

children.text: devā dadatv ā varam ||
children.translated_text: Let the gods give it as an excellent boon.

children.text: tad vo astu sucetanam ||
children.translated_text: May that be well-minded for you.

children.text: yuṣme astu dive dive ||
children.translated_text: May it be yours day by day.

children.text: praty eva gṛbhāyateti praty evainaṃ tad ajagrabhaiṣan ||
children.translated_text: "Do take it back"; by that they sought to have him take it back.

children.text: taṃ vā etaṃ devanīthaṃ śaṃsati padāvagrāhaṃ yathā nividaṃ tasyottamena padena praṇauti yathā nividaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He recites this <s>Devanītha</s> with separation of words, like a <s>nivid</s>; with its final word he gives praise, as with the <s>nivids</s>.

children.text: Chapter 223
bhūtechadaḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the <s>Bhūtechada</s>.

children.text: bhūtechadbhir vai devā asurān upāsacantoteva yuddhenoteva māyayā teṣāṃ vai devā asurāṇām bhūtechadbhir eva bhūtaṃ chādayitvāthainān atyāyaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānā bhūtechadbhir evāpriyasya bhrātṛvyasya bhūtaṃ chādayitvāthainam atiyanti ||
children.translated_text: With concealments of what had come into being the gods approached the Asuras, both with battle and with stratagem. Of those Asuras, the gods, having concealed what had come into being precisely with concealments of what had come into being, then passed beyond them. In just the same way these sacrificers, having concealed what has come into being for the hateful rival precisely with concealments of what has come into being, then pass beyond him.

children.text: tā ardharcaśaḥ śaṃsati pratiṣṭhāyā eva ||
children.translated_text: He recites them by half-verses, precisely for firm establishment.

children.text: ahanasyāḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites what belongs to the <s>āhanasya</s>.

children.text: āhanasyād vai retaḥ sicyate retasaḥ prajāḥ prajāyante prajātim eva tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>āhanasya</s> semen is poured; from semen offspring are born. Thereby he establishes procreation.

children.text: tā daśa śaṃsati daśākṣarā virāﾱ annaṃ virāﾱ annād retaḥ sicyate retasaḥ prajāḥ prajāyante prajātim eva tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He recites ten of them. The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables; food is the <s>Virāj</s>. From food semen is poured; from semen offspring are born. Thereby he establishes procreation.

children.text: tā nyūṅkhayaty annaṃ vai nyūṅkho 'nnād retaḥ sicyate retasaḥ prajāḥ prajāyante prajātim eva tad dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He makes them a <s>nyūṅkha</s> chant. Food indeed is the <s>nyūṅkha</s>. From food semen is poured; from semen offspring are born. Thereby he establishes procreation.

children.text: dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣam iti dādhikrīṃ śaṃsati devapavitraṃ vai dadhikrā idaṃ vā idaṃ vyāhanasyāṃ vācam avādīt tad devapavitreṇa vācam punīte ||
children.translated_text: He recites the Dādhikrī verse, 'Dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣam.' <s>Dadhikrā</s> is a divine purifier. This one here, in the <s>vyāhanasya</s>, had uttered speech; therefore he purifies speech with a divine purifier.

children.text: sānuṣṭub bhavati vāg vā anuṣṭup tat svena chandasā vācam punīte ||
children.translated_text: It is in the Anuṣṭubh metre. Speech indeed is Anuṣṭubh. Thereby he purifies speech with its own metre.

children.text: sutāso madhumattamā iti pāvamānīḥ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the Pāvamānī verses, 'sutāso madhumattamā.'

children.text: devapavitraṃ vai pāvamānya idaṃ vā idaṃ vyāhanasyāṃ vācam avādīt tad devapavitreṇaiva vācam punīte tā anuṣṭubho bhavanti vāg vā anuṣṭup tat svenaiva chandasā vācam punīte ||
children.translated_text: The Pāvamānī verses are divine purifiers. This one here, in the <s>vyāhanasya</s>, had uttered speech; therefore he purifies speech with a divine purifier. They are Anuṣṭubh verses. Speech indeed is Anuṣṭubh. Thereby he purifies speech with its own metre.

children.text: ava drapso aṃśumatīm atiṣṭhad ity aindrābārhaspatyaṃ tṛcaṃ śaṃsati ||
children.translated_text: He recites the three-verse hymn belonging to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, 'ava drapso aṃśumatīm atiṣṭhat.'

children.text: viśo adevīr abhy ācarantīr bṛhaspatinā yujendraḥ sasāha iti ||
children.translated_text: 'The godless clans, advancing against him, <s>Indra</s>, yoked with <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, overcame.'

children.text: asuraviśaṃ ha vai devān abhy udācārya āsīt sa indro bṛhaspatinaiva yujāsuryaṃ varṇam abhidāsantam apāhaṃs tathaivaitad yajamānā indrābṛhaspatibhyām eva yujāsuryaṃ varṇam abhidāsantam apaghnate ||
children.translated_text: The Asura clan had indeed advanced against the gods. <s>Indra</s>, yoked with <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, struck away the Asuric color that was assailing them. In just the same way these sacrificers, yoked with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, strike away the Asuric color that assails them.

children.text: tad āhuḥ saṃśaṃset ṣaṣṭhe 'hān na saṃśaṃsait iti saṃśaṃsed ity āhuḥ katham anyeṣv ahassu saṃśaṃsati katham atra na saṃśaṃsed ity atho khalv āhur naiva saṃśaṃset svargo vai lokaḥ ṣaṣṭham ahar asamāyī vai svargo lokaḥ kaścid vai svarge loke sametīti sa yat saṃśaṃset samānaṃ tat kuryād atha yan na saṃśaṃsatīṁ tat svargasya lokasya rūpaṃ tasmān na saṃśaṃsed yad eva na saṃśaṃsatīṁ ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, 'Should he recite together on the sixth day, or should he not recite together?' Some say, 'He should recite together. How does he recite together on the other days, and how would he not recite together here?' But others say, 'He should certainly not recite together. The sixth day is the heavenly world, and the heavenly world is not a place of meeting. Does anyone meet together in the heavenly world? If he were to recite together, he would make it a meeting; but when he does not recite together, that is the form of the heavenly world. Therefore he should not recite together, precisely because he does not recite together.'

children.text: etāni vā atrokthāni nābhānediṣṭho vālakhilyā vṛṣākapir evayāmarut sa yat saṃśaṃsed apaiva sa eteṣu kāmaṃ rādhnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: These here are the <s>ukthas</s>: the <s>Nābhānediṣṭha</s>, the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, and the <s>Evayāmaruta</s>. If he were to recite them together, he would attain his desire among these only in a scattered way.

children.text: aindro vṛṣākapiḥ sarvāṇi chandāṃsy aitaśapralāpas tatra sa kāma upāpto ya aindre jāgate 'thedam aindrābārhaspatyaṃ sūktam aindrābārhaspatyā paridhānīyā tasmān na saṃśaṃsen na saṃśaṃset ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> belongs to <s>Indra</s>; the <s>Aitaśapralāpa</s> contains all the metres, and there the desire is obtained that is in the Indra-related Jagatī. But this hymn belongs to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and the concluding verse belongs to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. Therefore he should not recite together, he should not recite together.

children.text: Chapter 224
athātaḥ paśor vibhaktis tasya vibhāgaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now then, the division of the sacrificial animal. We shall state its distribution.

children.text: hanū sajihve prastotuḥ śyenaṃ vakṣa udgātuḥ kaṇṭhaḥ kākudraḥ pratihartur dakṣiṇā śroṇir hotuḥ savyā brahmaṇo dakṣiṇaṃ sakthi maitrāvaruṇasya savyam brāhmaṇācchaṃsino dakṣiṇam pārśvaṃ sāṃsam adhvaryoḥ savyam upagātṝṇāṃ savyo'ṃsaḥ pratiprasthātur dakṣiṇaṃ dor neṣṭuḥ savyam potur dakṣiṇa ūrur achāvākasya savya āgnīdhrasya dakṣiṇo bāhur ātreyasya savyaḥ sadasyasya sadaṃ cānūkaṃ ca gṛhapater dakṣiṇau pādau gṛhapater vratapradasya savyau pādau gṛhapater bhāryāyai vratapradasyauṣṭha enayoḥ sādhāraṇo bhavati taṃ gṛhapatir eva praśiṃṣyāj jāghanīm patnībhyo haranti tām brāhmaṇāya dadyuḥ skandhyāś ca maṇikās tisraś ca kīkasā grāvastutas tisraś caiva kīkasā ardhaṃ ca vaikartasyonnetur ardhaṃ caiva vaikartasya klomā ca śamitus tad brāhmaṇāya dadyād yady abrāhmaṇaḥ syāc chiraḥ subrahmaṇyāyai yaḥ śvaḥsutyām prāha tasyājinam iﾱā sarveṣāṃ hotur vā ||
children.translated_text: The two jaws with the tongue belong to the <s>Prastotṛ</s>; the breast, as a hawk, to the <s>Udgātṛ</s>; the neck and hump to the <s>Pratihartṛ</s>; the right haunch to the <s>Hotṛ</s>; the left to the <s>Brahman</s>; the right thigh to the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>; the left to the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>; the right flank, with the shoulder, to the <s>Adhvaryu</s>; the left to the assistant singers; the left shoulder to the <s>Pratiprasthātṛ</s>; the right foreleg to the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>; the left to the <s>Potṛ</s>; the right upper thigh to the <s>Acchāvāka</s>; the left to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>; the right upper arm to the <s>Ātreya</s>; the left to the <s>Sadasya</s>; the rump and the back belong to the householder; the two right feet belong to the householder who gives the vow-food; the two left feet belong to the householder's wife who gives the vow-food. The upper lip is common to these two; the householder himself should assign it. They carry the rump-piece to the wives; they should give it to a Brahmin. The shoulder-blades, the vertebrae, and three ribs belong to the stone-praiser; three ribs likewise and half of the cut-off piece to the <s>Unnetṛ</s>; the other half of the cut-off piece and the lungs to the slaughterer. He should give that to a Brahmin if the slaughterer is not a Brahmin. The head belongs to the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s>; the hide belongs to the one who announces the next day's Soma pressing; the <s>iḍā</s> belongs to all, or else to the <s>Hotṛ</s>.

children.text: tā vā etāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśatam ekapadā yajñaṃ vahanti ṣaṭtriṃśadakṣarā vai bṛhatī bārhatāḥ svargā lokāḥ prāṇāṃś caiva tat svargāṃś ca lokān āpnuvanti prāṇeṣu caiva tat svargeṣu ca lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanto yanti ||
children.translated_text: These, then, are thirty-six one-footed portions that carry the sacrifice. The <s>Bṛhatī</s> has thirty-six syllables; the Bārhata worlds are heavenly worlds. Thereby they obtain both the breaths and the heavenly worlds, and they go on established both in the breaths and in the heavenly worlds.

children.text: sa eṣa svargyaḥ paśur ya enam evaṃ vibhajanti ||
children.translated_text: This is the animal that leads to heaven, when they divide it in this way.

children.text: atha ye 'to 'nyathā tad yathā selagā vā pāpakṛto vā paśuṃ vimathnīraṃs tādṛk tat ||
children.translated_text: But those who divide it otherwise are like thieves or evil-doers tearing an animal apart; such is that act.

children.text: tāṃ vā etām paśor vibhaktiṃ śrautaṛṣir devabhāgo vidāṃcakāra tām u hāprocyaivāsmāllokād uccakrāmat ||
children.translated_text: This division of the sacrificial animal was discovered by <s>Devabhāga Śrautarṣi</s>. Having taught it, he departed upward from this world.

children.text: tām u ha girijāya bābhravyāyāmanuṣyaḥ provāca tato hainām etadarvāṅ manuṣyā adhīyate 'dhīyate ||
children.translated_text: A superhuman being taught it to <s>Girija Bābhravya</s>. From then onward, on this side of that time, human beings study it; they study it.

children.text: Chapter 225
tad āhur ya āhitāgnir upavasathe mriyeta katham asya yajñaḥ syād iti nainaṃ yājayed iti āhur anabhiprāpto hi yajñam bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If an <s>āhitāgni</s> (one who has established the sacred fires) dies on the upavasatha day, how should his sacrifice be?" They say, "One should not make him sacrifice, for he has not reached the sacrifice."

children.text: tad āhur ya āhitāgnir adhiśrite 'gnihotre sāṃnāyye vā haviṣṣu vā mriyeta kā tatra prāyaścittir ity atraivaināny anuparyādadhyād yathā sarvāṇi saṃdahyeran sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If an <s>āhitāgni</s> dies when the <s>agnihotra</s>, the <s>sāṃnāyya</s>, or the oblations have been set on the fire, what is the expiation there?" One should lay these very offerings around there in such a way that they are all burned up. That is the expiation there.

children.text: tad āhur ya āhitāgnir āsanneṣu haviṣṣu mriyeta kā tatra prāyaścittir iti yābhya eva tāni devatābhyo havīṃṣi gṛhītāni bhavanti tābhyaḥ svāhety evaināny āhavanīye sarvahunti juhuyāt sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If an <s>āhitāgni</s> dies when the oblations are ready at hand, what is the expiation there?" For whatever deities those oblations have been taken, one should offer them as a whole-offering in the <s>āhavanīya</s>, saying only, "Svāhā to those deities." That is the expiation there.

children.text: tad āhur ya āhitāgniḥ pravasan mriyeta katham asyāgnihotraṃ syād ity abhivānyavatsāyāḥ payasā juhuyād anyad ivaitat payo yad abhivānyavatsāyā anyad ivaitad agnihotraṃ yat pretasya ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If an <s>āhitāgni</s> dies while away from home, how should his <s>agnihotra</s> be?" One should offer with the milk of an <s>abhivānyavatsā</s> cow; that milk of an <s>abhivānyavatsā</s> cow is, as it were, different, and that <s>agnihotra</s> of one who has died is, as it were, different.

children.text: api vā yata eva kutaśca payasā juhuyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else they may offer with milk from wherever it can be obtained.

children.text: athāpy āhur evam evainān ajasrān ajuhvata indhīrann ā śarīrāṇām āhartor iti ||
children.translated_text: But some also say, "In just this way they should keep them constantly kindled, without offering, until the bodies have been brought."

children.text: yadi śarīrāṇi na vidyeran parṇaśaraḥ ṣaṣṭiṃ trīṇi ca śatāny āhṛtya teṣām puruṣarūpakam iva kṛtvā tasmiṃs tām āvṛtaṃ kuryur athaināñcharīrair āhṛtaiḥ saṃsparśyodvāsayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the bodies are not found, they should bring three hundred and sixty <s>parṇa</s>-reeds, make from them something like a human form, and perform that procedure upon it. Then, when the bodies have been brought, they should touch these reeds to the bodies and remove them.

children.text: adhyardhaśataṃ kāye sakthinī dvipañcāśe ca viṃśe corū dvipañcaviṃśe śeṣaṃ tu śirasy upari dadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should place a hundred and a half on the trunk, two fifties on the haunches, two twenties on the thighs, two twenty-fives, and the remainder above on the head.

children.text: sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is the expiation there.

children.text: Chapter 226
tad āhur yasyāgnihotry upāvasṛṣṭā duhyamānopaviśet kā tatra prāyaścittir iti tām abhimantrayeta ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If a man's <s>agnihotra</s> cow, after being let near, sits down while being milked, what is the expiation there?" He should address her with a mantra.

children.text: yasmād bhīṣā niṣīdasi tato no abhayaṃ kṛdhi paśūn naḥ sarvān gopāya namo rudrāya mīﾱhuṣa iti tām utthāpayed udasthād devy aditir āyur yajñapatāv adhāt indrāya kṛṇvatī bhāgam mitrāya varuṇāya cety athāsyā udapātram ūdhasi ca mukhe copagṛhṇīyād athainām brāhmaṇāya dadyāt sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "From whatever fear you sit down, from that make us fearless; guard all our cattle; homage to <s>Rudra</s> the bounteous." With this he should make her rise: "The goddess <s>Aditi</s> has risen; she has placed life in the lord of the sacrifice, making a share for <s>Indra</s> and for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>." Then he should hold a vessel of water near her udder and mouth, and then he should give her to a Brāhmaṇa. That is the expiation there.

children.text: tad āhur yasyāgnihotry upāvasṛṣṭā duhyamānā vāśyeta kā tatra prāyaścittir ity aśanāyāṃ ha vā eṣā yajamānasya pratikhyāya vāśyate tām annam apy ādayec chāntyai śāntir vā annaṃ sūyavasād bhagavatī hi bhūyā iti sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If a man's <s>agnihotra</s> cow, after being let near, lows while being milked, what is the expiation there?" She lows as though announcing hunger on the part of the sacrificer. He should make her take food for appeasement; for food is appeasement. "May she, blessed, have good fodder." That is the expiation there.

children.text: tad āhur yasyāgnihotry upāvasṛṣṭā duhyamānā syandeta kā tatra prāyaścittir iti sā yat tatra skandayet tad abhimṛśya japed yad adya dugdham pṛthivīm asṛpta yad oṣadhīr atyasṛpad yad āpaḥ payo gṛheṣu payo aghnyāyām payo vatseṣu payo astu tan mayīti tatra yat pariśiṣṭaṃ syāt tena juhuyād yady alaṃ homāya syād yady u vai sarvaṃ siktaṃ syād athānyām āhūya tāṃ dugdhvā tena juhuyād ā tv eva śraddhāyai hotavyaṃ sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If a man's <s>agnihotra</s> cow, after being let near, lets milk spill while being milked, what is the expiation there?" Whatever she spills there, he should touch it and murmur, "Whatever milk today has slipped onto the earth, whatever has passed over the plants, whatever has gone to the waters: milk in the houses, milk in the inviolable cow, milk in the calves; may that milk be in me." With whatever remains there he should offer, if it is enough for the oblation. But if all of it has been spilled, then, after summoning another cow and milking her, he should offer with that. For the sake of faith, at any rate, the offering must be made. That is the expiation there.

children.text: Chapter 227
tad āhur yasya sāyaṃdugdhaṃ sāṃnāyyaṃ duṣyed vāpahared vā kā tatra prāyaścittir iti prātardugdhaṃ dvaidhaṃ kṛtvā tasyānyatarām bhaktim ātacya tena yajeta sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If a man's evening-milked <s>sāṃnāyya</s> is spoiled or carried off, what is the expiation there?" Having divided the morning-milked portion in two and prepared one of its portions, he should sacrifice with that. That is the expiation there.

children.text: tad āhur yasya prātardugdhaṃ sāṃnāyyaṃ duṣyed vāpahared vā kā tatra prāyaścittir ity aindraṃ vā māhendraṃ vā puroﾱāśaṃ tasya sthāne nirupya tena yajeta sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If a man's morning-milked <s>sāṃnāyya</s> is spoiled or carried off, what is the expiation there?" Having prepared in its place a cake for <s>Indra</s> or for great <s>Indra</s>, he should sacrifice with that. That is the expiation there.

children.text: tad āhur yasya sarvam eva sāṃnāyyaṃ duṣyed vāpahared vā kā tatra prāyaścittir ity aindraṃ vā māhendraṃ veti samānaṃ sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If all of a man's <s>sāṃnāyya</s> is spoiled or carried off, what is the expiation there?" The same procedure applies: for <s>Indra</s> or for great <s>Indra</s>. That is the expiation there.

children.text: tad āhur yasya sarvāṇy eva havīṃṣi duṣyeyur vāpahareyur vā kā tatra prāyaścittir ity ājyasyaināni yathādevatam parikalpya tayājyahaviṣeṣṭyā yajetāto 'nyām iṣṭim anulbaṇāṃ tanvīta yajño yajñasya prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If all of a man's oblations are spoiled or carried off, what is the expiation there?" Having prepared these out of ghee according to the proper deities, he should sacrifice with that iṣṭi whose oblation is ghee. After that he should extend another, unobtrusive iṣṭi. Sacrifice is the expiation for sacrifice.

children.text: Chapter 228

tad āhur yasyāgnihotram adhiśritam amedhyam āpadyeta kā tatra prāyaścittir iti sarvam evainat srucy abhiparyāsicya prāṅ udetyāhavanīye haitāṃ samidham abhyādadhāty athottarata āhavanīyasyoṣṇam bhasma nirūhya juhuyān manasā vā prājāpatyayā varcā taddhutaṃ cāhutaṃ ca sa yady ekasmin unnīte yadi dvayor eṣa eva kalpas tac ced vyapanayituṃ śaknuyān niṣṣicyaitad duṣṭam aduṣṭam abhiparyāsicya tasya yathonnītī syāt tathā juhuyāt sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If an impure thing befalls a man's <s>agnihotra</s> after it has been set on the fire, what is the expiation there?" Having poured all of it over into the sacrificial spoon, he goes eastward and lays this fuel-stick upon the <s>āhavanīya</s>. Then, having drawn out hot ashes to the north of the <s>āhavanīya</s>, he should offer, either mentally or with a <s>Prajāpati</s> formula. That is both offered and not offered. If one ladling has been lifted out, or if two have been, this same procedure applies. But if he is able to remove the contaminated part, then, having poured away that spoiled portion and poured over the unspoiled portion, he should offer it according to the way it had been lifted out. That is the expiation there.

children.text: tad āhur yasyāgnihotram adhiśritaṃ skandati vā viṣyandate vā kā tatra prāyaścittir iti tad adbhir upaninayec chāntyai śāntir vā āpo 'thainad dakṣiṇena pāṇinābhimṛśya japati ||
children.translated_text: They say, "If a man's <s>agnihotra</s>, after being set on the fire, spills or runs over, what is the expiation there?" He should bring it back together with water, for appeasement; for water is appeasement. Then, having touched it with his right hand, he murmurs the mantra.

children.text: divaṃ tṛtīyaṃ devān yajño 'gāt tato mā draviṇam āṣṭāntarikṣaṃ tṛtīyam pitṝn yajño 'gāt tato mā draviṇam āṣṭa pṛthivīṃ tṛtīyam manuṣyān yajño 'gāt tato mā draviṇam āṣṭa ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice went a third time to heaven, to the gods; from there may it obtain wealth for me. The sacrifice went a third time to the atmosphere, to the Fathers; from there may it obtain wealth for me. The sacrifice went a third time to the earth, to human beings; from there may it obtain wealth for me.

children.text: yayor ojasā skabhitā rajāṃsīti vaiṣṇuvāruṇīm ṛcaṃ japati viṣṇur vai yajñasya duriṣṭam pāti varuṇaḥ sviṣṭaṃ tayor ubhayor eva śāntyai ||
children.translated_text: He murmurs the Vaiṣṇava-Vāruṇa verse beginning, <s>yayor ojasā skabhitā rajāṃsi</s>. <s>Viṣṇu</s> protects what has been badly sacrificed in the sacrifice, and <s>Varuṇa</s> protects what has been well sacrificed; this is for the appeasement of both of them.

children.text: sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is the expiation in that case.

children.text: tad āhur yasyāgnihotram adhiśritam prāṅ udāyan skhalate vāpi vā bhraṃśate kā tatra prāyaścittir iti sa yady upanivartayet svargāl lokād yajamānam āvartayed atraivāsmā upaviṣṭāyaitam agnihotraparīśeṣam āhareyus tasya yathonnītī syāt tathā juhuyāt sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say: When a man's <s>Agnihotra</s>, having been set on the fire, slips as it is being carried eastward, or else falls down, what is the expiation in that case? If he were to turn back, he would turn the sacrificer back from the heavenly world. The remainder of that <s>Agnihotra</s> should be brought to him right there as he sits, and he should make the offering according to the way in which it had been ladled out. That is the expiation in that case.

children.text: tad āhur atha yadi srug bhidyeta kā tatra prāyaścittir ity anyām srucam āhṛtya juhuyād athaitāṃ srucam bhinnām āhavanīye 'bhyādadhyāt prāgdaṇḍām pratyakpuṣkarāṃ sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say: Now if the <s>sruc</s> ladle should break, what is the expiation in that case? Having brought another <s>sruc</s>, he should make the offering; then he should lay that broken <s>sruc</s> upon the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire, with its handle to the east and its bowl to the west. That is the expiation in that case.

children.text: tad āhur yasyāhavanīye hāgnir vidyetātha gārhapatya upaśāmyet kā tatra prāyaścittir iti sa yadi prāñcam uddharet prāyatanāc cyaveta yat pratyañcam asuravad yajñaṃ tanvīta yan manthed bhrātṛvyaṃ yajamānasya janayed yad anugamayet prāṇo yajamānaṃ jahyāt sarvam evainaṃ sahabhasmānam samopya gārhapatyāyatane nidhāyātha prāñcam āhavanīyam uddharet sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say: When a man's fire is present in the <s>āhavanīya</s>, but the <s>gārhapatya</s> has gone out, what is the expiation in that case? If he were to carry it out eastward, he would fall away from the starting place; if westward, he would stretch out the sacrifice in the manner of the Asuras; if he were to churn fire, he would produce an enemy for the sacrificer; if he were to make it follow after, breath would abandon the sacrificer. He should gather all of it together with its ashes, place it on the site of the <s>gārhapatya</s>, and then carry out the <s>āhavanīya</s> eastward. That is the expiation in that case.

children.text: Chapter 229

tad āhur yasyāgnāv agnim uddhareyuḥ kā tatra prāyaścittir iti sa yady anupaśyed udūhya pūrvam aparaṃ nidadhyād yady u nānupaśyet so 'gnaye 'gnivate 'ṣṭākapālam puroﾱāśaṃ nirvapet tasya yājyānuvākye agnināgniḥ samidhyate tvaṃ hy agne agninety āhutiṃ vāhavanīye juhuyād agnaye 'gnivate svāheti sā tatra prāyaścittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They say: When they have carried out a fire into a man's fire, what is the expiation in that case? If he should notice it, after removing the earlier one he should set down the later one. But if he should not notice it, he should prepare an eight-cup <s>puroḍāśa</s> cake for <s>Agni Agnivat</s>. Its <s>yājyā</s> and <s>anuvākyā</s> verses are those beginning <s>agnināgniḥ samidhyate</s> and <s>tvaṃ hy agne agninā</s>; or he should make an oblation in the <s>āhavanīya</s>, saying, <s>agnaye agnivate svāhā</s>. That is the expiation in that case.
